hearer, witness, judge', rel. to Umbr. afputrali,
'by arbitration'; prob. formed fr. ad, 'to' (see
ad-), and baetere, bitere, bltere, 'to go', and lit.
meaning 'one who goes to Something'. For the
change of ad to ar in arbiter cp. Marsian L.
apor — L. apud, 'at, near, by'.

## arbitrable
arbitrable, adj. — Formed with suff. -able fr. L.
arbitrari. See arbitrate.

## arbitrage
arbitrage, п., arbitration. — F., fr. arbitrer, 'to
arbitrate, judge', fr. L. arbitrari. See orbitrata
and -age.

## arbitrament
arbitrament, n. — F. arbitrement, fr. arbitrer. See
prec. word and -ment

## arbitrary
arbitrary, adj.—L. arbitrarius, 'of arbitration,
depending on the will, arbitrary', fr. arbiter. See
arbiter and adj. suff. -ary.
Derivatives: arbilrari-ly, adv., arbitrari-ness, n.

## arbitrate
arbitrate, intr. v. — L. arbitral us, pp. of
arbitrari, 4o make a decision, be of opinion', fr.
arbiter. See arbiter and verbal Suff. -ate.
Derivatives: arbitration (q.v.), arbilrat-ive, adj.,
arbitrator (q.v.)

## arbitration
arbitration, n. — OF. arbttracion, arbitration (F.
arbitration), fr. L. arbitratidnem, ace. of
arbitration 'judgement, will', fr. arbitratus, п., of
s.m., fr. arbitratus, pp. of arbitrari. See prec.
word and -ion.
Derivative: arbitration-al, adj.

## arbitrator
arbitrator, n. — L., 'a spectator, hearer, witness,
judge', fr. arbitratus, pp. of arbitrari. See
arbitrate and agential suff. -or.

## arbor
arbor, arbour, п., a shady retreat. — Fr. earlier
arber, fr. ME. herbier, 'a garden of herbs', fr.
OF. (= F.) herbier, fr. L. herbarium, of s.m.,
fr. herba, 'herb'. See herb and cp. herbarium.
For the change of e (in ME. herbier) to a (in
arber) cp. carve, harbor. The change of arber
to arbor, arbour is due to a confusion with L.
arbor, 'tree*.

## arbor
arbor, п., tree. — L., of uncertain origin. Cp.
arborescent, arboretum, urbuscle, arbuscule, ar-
bustum.

## arboraceous
arboraceous, adj., treelike; wooded. — Formed
with suff. -aceous fr. L. arbor, 'tree'. See prec.
word.

## arboreal
arboreal, adj., 1) of a tree or trees; z) living in
trees. — Formed with adj. suff. -ul fr. L. ar-
boreus, 'pertaining to a tree or trees', fr. arbor.
See arbor, 'tree'.

## nrborean
nrborean, adj., arboreal. — Formed fr. orbor,
'tree', with suff. -ean.

## arboreous
arboreous, adj., l) abounding in trees; z) living
in trees. — L. arboreus, 'pertaining to a tree or
trees', fr. arbor. See arbor, 'tree'. For E.-ous,
as equivalent to L. -us, see -ous.

## nrborescence
nrborescence, n. — Formed fr. next word with
suff. -ce.

## arborescent
arborescent, adj., l) treelike; z) branching. — L.
arborescins, gen. -entis, pres. part, of arboris-
cere, 'to grow into a tree', formed fr. arbor,
'tree', with the inchoative suffix -escere. See
arbor, 'tree', and -escent.

## arboretum
arboretum, п., a garden of trees. — L. arboretum,
'a place grown with trees', fr. arbor, 'tree'. See
arbor, 'tree'.

## arboriculture
arboriculture, п., cultivation of trees. —
Compounded of L. arbor, 'tree', and cultura,
'cultivation'. See arbor, 'tree', and culture.
Derivatives: arboricultur-al, adj., arboricultur-ist.

## arborize
arborize, tr. v., to give a treelike appearance;
intr. v., to assume a treelike appearance. —
Formed fr. arbor, 'tree', with suff. -ize.
Derivative: arboriz-ation, n.

## arbor vltae
arbor vltae, п., an evergreen tree of the genus
Thuja. — L., 'tree of life'; a name given by the
French physician and botanist Charles de Le-
cluse, latinized into Carolus Clusius (1525-

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:74 COLUMN:2 -->
1609), to trees of the genus Thuja. See arboreal
and vital,

## arbuscle
arbuscle, п., a dwarf tree. — Late L. arbuscula,
dimin. of L. arbor, 'tree'. See arbor, 'tree', and
-cle.

## arbuscule
arbuscule, п., a tuft of hairs (zool.) — See prec.
word and -cule.

## arbustum
arbustum, п., a copse; an orchard. — L., 'a place
where trees are planted; an orchard', prop. neut.
of arbustus, 'planted with trees', used as a noun,
which stands for *arbos-to-s, fr. arbos, arbor,
'tree'. See arbor, 'tree'.

## Arbutus
Arbutus, п., 1) a genus of evergreen trees of the
heath family; 2) (not cap.) a tree of this genus.
— L., 'the strawberry tree', of obscure origin.

## arc
arc, n. — OF. (— F.) arc, fr. L. arcus, 'bow, arch',
which is cogn. with Goth, arhazna, 'arrow', OE.
earh, ON. 6r, of s.m.; but Russ. rakita, Czech
rokyla, 'willow', and Gk. αρκυς, 'net', are not
cognate. Cp. arcade, arch, arrow, and the first
element in arbalest, arciform, arcuate, arculite,
arquebus.

## area
area, п., a chest. — L., fr. arcire, 'to enclose'.
See arcanum and cp. Arcella.

## arcade
arcade, n. — F., fr. It. areata, a derivative of arco,
'arc*, fr. L. arcus, of s.m. See arc and -ade.
Derivative: arcad-ed, adj.

## Arcadia
Arcadia, п., a district in ancient Greece,
proverbial for the rural life of its inhabitants. —
L., fr. Gk. 'Αρκαδία, fr. 'Αρκάς, gen. 'Αρκάδος
= Areas, the founder of Arcadia.

## Arcadian
Arcadian, adj., and n. — Formed with suff. -an
fr. L. Arcadia. See prec. word.

## arcanum
arcanum, п., secret, mystery. — L. arcanum, prop,
subst. use of the neut. of arcanus, 'shut up,
secret', orig. 'enclosed in a chest', fr. area, 'chest,
coffin', which is rel. to arcire, 'to enclose, keep
away, ward off', and cogn. with Gk. άρκεϊν, 'to
keep off', Άρχος, 'defense', £ρκιος, 'safe, sure'.
Arm. argel, 'obstacle', argelum, Ί lock in', and
possibly also with Lith. rSktas, 'key', rakinti, 'to
shut lock'. These words stand in gradational
relationship to Orcus, name of the god of the
infernal regions in Roman mythology. Cp. area,
Arcella, ark, coerce, exercise, Orcus. Cp. also
askari, lascar, autarchy, 'self sufficiency'.

## Arcella
Arcella, п., a genus of protozoans (zool.) —
ModL., dimin. of area, 'chest, box' (see area);
so called from the boxlike shape of the shell.

## Arceuthobium
Arceuthobium, п., a genus of parasitic plants
(bot.) — ModL., compounded of Gk. αρκευ&ος,
'the juniper', and βίος, 'life'; so called from
its parasitism on conifers. Gk. ϋρκευθος is prob.
rel. to £ρκυς, 'net'. For the etymol. of βίος see
bio-

## arch
arch, п., a curved structure. — OF. (= F.) arche,
fr. VL. *arca, fr. L. arcus, 'bow'. See arc.
Derivative: arch, tr. v.

## arch
arch, adj., chief, principal. — See pref. arch-.
Derivatives: arch-ly, adv., arch-ness, n.

## arch-
arch-, pref. meaning 'chief, principal', as in
archduke, archbishop. — ME. arche-, fr. OE. arce-,
-erce, fr. L. archi-, arch-, fr. Gk. άρχι-, άρχ-,
which is rel. to άρχος, 'leader, chief, ruler', from
the stem of αρχειν, 'to begin, rule' (whence
also αρχή, 'beginning, first cause, origin, first
principle, office'), and in gradational
relationship to ορχαμος, 'leader, chief. Cp. arch, 'chief',
-arch. Cp. also archaeo-, archaic, archaism,
arche, architect, archon, -archy.

## -arch
-arch, suff. meaning 'a ruler', as in ethnarch,
oligarch. — See pref, arch-.

## Archaean
Archaean, also Archean, pertaining to the oldest
geological period. — Formed with suff. -an fr.
Gk. αρχαίος, 'ancient', fr. αρχή, 'beginning'. See
arch- and cp. archaic.

## archaeo-
archaeo-, before a vowel archae-; also archeo-,
resp. arche-, combining fotm meaning 'ancient,
primeval, primitive. — Gk. άρχαιο-, άρχαι-, fr.
αρχαίος, 'ancient', lit. 'from the beginning*, fr.
αρχή, 'beginning'. See arch-,

## archaeological
archaeological, archeological, adj. — Formed
with adj. suff. -al fr. Gk. αρχαιολογικός,
'pertaining to archaeology', fr. αρχαιολογία. See
next word.
Derivative: archaeological-ly, archeologkal-ly,
adv.

## archaeology
archaeology, also archeology, n. — Gk.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:74 COLUMN:3 -->
αρχαιολογία, 'the study of ancient things',
compounded of άρχαιο- (see archaeo-) and Gk. -λογία, fr.
-λόγος, 'one who speaks (in a certain manner);
one who deals (with a certain topic)'. See -logy.
Derivatives: archaeological (q.v.), archaeolog-ist
or archeolog-isl, n.

## Archaeopteryx
Archaeopteryx, also Archeopteryx, п., a genus of
extinct reptilian birds (paleontol.) — ModL.,
compounded ofarchaeo-and Gk. πτέρης, 'wing'.
— See pterygo-, ptero-.

## archaic
archaic, adj., old-fashioned, antiquated,
obsolete. — Gk. αρχαϊκός, 'old-fashioned,
antiquated', fr. αρχαίος, 'ancient', fr. αρχή,
'beginning'. See arch- and cp. Archaean.
Derivative: archaic-al-ly, adv.

## arcbaism
arcbaism, п., use of an obsolete word. — Gk.
αρχαϊσμός, fr. άρχαΐζειν, 'to be old-fashioned,
copy the ancients in language', fr. αρχαίος,
'ancient'. See prec. word and -ism.

## archaist
archaist, п., one fond of using archaisms. —
Formed with suff, -ist fr. Gk. αρχαίος, 'ancient'.
See archaic.
Derivative: archaist-ic, adj.

## archaize
archaize, tr. v., to make archaic; intr. v., to use
archaisms.— Gk. άρχαΛζειν. See archaism and
-ize.

## archangel
archangel, n. — Late L. archangelus, fr. Gk.
αρχάγγελος, 'chief angel', fr. άρχ- (see arch-)
and άγγελος, 'angel'. See angel,

## archaugelic
archaugelic, adj. — Late L. archangelicus, fr. Gk.
άρχαγγελικός, fr. αρχάγγελος. See ρ с. word
and -ic

## archbishop
archbishop, n. — ME. archebischop, fr. OE. arce-
biscop, fr. Eccles. L. archiepiscopus, fr. Eccles.
Gk. αρχιεπίσκοπος, lit. 'chief bishop', fr. Gk.
άρχι- (see archi-) and επίσκοπος, 'bishop'. See
bishop.

## urchbishopric
urchbishopric,n.—ME. archebischopriche,fi.OE.
arcebiscoprice. See arch· and bishopric and cp.
prec. word.

## archdeacon
archdeacon, n. — OE. arcediacon, fr. Eccles. L.
archidiaconus, fr. Eccles. Gk. άρχιδιάκονος, lit.
'chief deacon', fr. άρχι- (see archi-) and διάκονος,
'servant, minister of a church'. See dencos.

## arche
arche, п., the first principle (Greek philos.) — Gk.
αρχή, 'beginning, first cause, origin, first
principle*. See arch-.
Archean. — See Archaean,

## archegonium
archegonium, п., the female sex organ in ferns
and mosses (bot.) — ModL., fr. Gk. αρχέγονος,
'first of a race', fr. άρχ- (see arch-) and -γόνος,
which is rel. to γονή, Offspring, race, family,
generation', fr. I.-E. base *ien-, 'to produce,
beget'. See genus.

## Archelon
Archelon, п., a genus of extinct turtles. — ModL.,
shortened fr. Gk. άρχ (ων χ)ελώνη, 'ruler
tortoise'. Gk. άρχων, 'ruler', is pres. part, of αρχειν,
'to rule'; see arch- and cp. archon. Gk. χελώνη
is rel. to χελός, 'tortoise', lit. 'the yellow animal',
fr. I.-E. base *ghel-, 'yellow'; see yellow,

## arcbenteroa
arcbenteroa, п., the primitive enteron of a gas-
trula (zool.)—Formed fr. arch- and Gk. έντερον,
'intestine'. See enteric,

## archer
archer, n. — OF. archier (F. archer), fr. L. ar·
curius, fr. arcus, 'bow'. See arc and subst. suff.
-er.

## archery
archery, n. — OF. archerie, fr. archier, 'archer'.
See prec. word and -y (representing OF. -ie).

## archetype
archetype, n. — L. archelypum, fr. Gk. άρχέτυπον,
'pattern, model', prop. neut. of the adjective
αρχέτυπος, 'stamped first', used as a noun, fr.
άρχε- (= άρχι-), 'first', and τύπος, 'a blow, mark
of a blow'. See arch- and type,

## archi-
archi-, pref. meaning 1) 'chief, as in archidia-
conal; 2) 'primitive, original' as in archiplasm. —
Gk. άρχι-, rel. to άρχος, 'leader, chief, ruler',
* αρχειν, 'to begin, to rule'. See arch-,

## archiater
archiater, п., the chief physician at the court of a
Greek king or Roman emperor (Greek and
Roman hist.) — Gk. αρχίατρος, 'court
physician', fr. άρχι- (see archi-) and ιατρός,
'physician'. See iatric.

## archidiaconal
archidiaconal, adj., 1) of an archdeacon; 2) of an
archdeaconry. — Compounded of archi- and
diacoiml.

## archil
archil, orchil, п., dyestuff obtained from lichen.
— ME. orchell, fr. AF. orchel, which is rel. to
earlier F. orsolle, F. orseille, It. orcella; of un-

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:75 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: ARCHIMANDRITE | 48 -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:75 COLUMN:1 -->
certain origin. Cp. Roccella.

## archimandrite
archimandrite, п., in the Greek Church, head of
a monastery or of a group of monasteries. —'
ML. archimandrita, fr. MGk. αρχιμανδρίτης,
fr. άρχι-, 'chief (see archi-), and μάνδρα, 'fold,
stable', which is prob. cogn. with OI. mandurd,
'stable', mandirdm, 'room, house, palace,
temple'.

## Archimedean
Archimedean, adj., pertaining to Archimedes. —
Formed with suff. -an fr. L. Archimedeus, 'of
Archimedes', fr. Gk. 'Αρχιμήδης, Archimedes, the
celebrated mathematician (2877-212 B.C.E.).

## archipelago
archipelago, п., l) the Aegean Sea; 2) a sea
studded with many islands; 3) a group of islands. —
It. arcipelago, lit. 'the chief sea', compounded of
ατά-, 'chief, fr. Gk. άρχι- (see archi-), and Gk.
πέλαγος, 'sea' (see pelagic). In ancient and
mediaeval Greek, the word αρχιπέλαγος does not
occur, in modern Greek it is an Italian loanword.
The fact that archipelago orig. denoted the
Aegean Sea may help us And the origin of this word,
which is a real crux etymologorum. It. arcipelago
very probably arose from a mistaking of Gk.
ΑΕγαΐον πέλαγος, 'the Aegean Sea', for
αρχιπέλαγος, 'the chief sea', a confusion suggested by
the numerous Greek words beginning with άρχι-.

## archipinsm
archipinsm, п., I) primitive protoplasm; 2) ar-
choplasm.—Compounded of archi- and -plasm.
Derivative: archiplasm-ic, adj.

## architect
architect, n. — F. architecte, fr. L. architectus, fr.
Gk. αρχιτέκτων, 'master builder', fr. άρχι-,
'chief, and τέκτων, 'carpenter, builder', which
is rel. to τέχνη, 'art, skill, craft'. See archi- and
text and cp. technic, tectonic.

## architectonic
architectonic, adj. — L. archiiectonicus, fr. Gk.
αρχιτεκτονικός, 'pertaining to a master builder',
fr. αρχιτέκτων. See prec. word and -ic

## architectonics
architectonics, n. — See prec. word and -ics.

## architecture
architecture, n. — F., fr. L. architectural fr. ar-
chitectus. See architect and -ore.
Derivatives: archilectur-al, adj., architectur-al-
ly, adv.

## architrave
architrave, п., the lowest part of the entablature
(archil.) — It. architrave, fr. archi- and trave,
'beam', fr. L. trabem, ace. oitrabs. See trabeate.

## archive
archive, п., generally used in the pi. — F. archives,
fr. L. archivum, archium, 'the archives',
transliteration of Gk. άρχεϊον, 'official building', pi.
τά αρχεία, 'public records, archives', fr. αρχή,
'beginning, origin, first place, office'. See arch-
and cp. arche.
Derivatives: archive, tr. v., archiv-al, adj.,
archiv-ist, n.

## archirolt
archirolt, п., a curved molding on the face of an
arch (archil.) — It. archivolto, lit. 'an arched
vault', fr. arco, 'arch', and volta, 'vault'. See
arch and vault.

## archo-
archo-, combining form meaning 'rectal' (med.)
— Fr. Gk. αρχάς, 'rectum', which is of
uncertain origin.

## archon
archon, п., one of the nine chief magistrates in
Athens (Ancient Greek hist.) — Gk. ίρχων,
'ruler', prop. pres. part, of ίρχειν, 'to rale'.
See arch- and cp. the first element in Archelon.

## -archy
-archy, combining form meaning 'rule', as in
anarchy, monarchy. — L. -archia, fr. Gk. -αρχία,
'rule', fr. άρχος, 'leader, chief, ruler'. See -arch
and -y (representing Gk. -ία).

## arciform
arciform, adj., having the torm of an arch. —
Compounded of L. arcus, 'bow', and forma,
'form, shape'. See arc and form, n.

## arctic
arctic, adj., pertaining to the North Pole or the
regions near it. — L. arcticus, fr. Gk. αρκτικός,
'of a bear; of the Great Bear; northern', fr.
ίρκτος (also ίρκος), 'bear'; the constellation
of the Great Bear; the north', which is cogn.
with OI. fksah, Avestic ar'shd. Arm. arj. Alb.
arl, 'bear', L. ursus (for *urksos), Olr., Gael.
art, W. arth (for *arkt), 'bear'. Cp. Ursus. Cp.
also Arctium, arcto-, Arcturus, antarctic, Arthar,
Nearctic.

## Arctium
Arctium, п., a genus of plants of the thistle family,
the burdock (bot.) — ModL., fr. Gk. ίρκτος,
'bear'. See prec. word.

## arcto-
arcto-, before a vowel arct-, combining form
meaning 'bear', or 'the north'. — Gk. άοκτο-,
άρκτ-, fr. ίρκτος, 'bear; the north'. See arctic.

## Arctogaen
Arctogaen, Arctogen, п., a zoogeographical

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:75 COLUMN:2 -->
realm, comprising North America, Europe, Asia
and Africa. — ModL., compounded of arcto-
and Gk. γη, 'earth'. See geo- and cp. Neogaea,
Notogaea.
Derivatives: Arctogae-al or Arctoge-al, Arcto-
gae-an or Arctoge-an, Arclogae-ic or Arcloge-
ic, adjs.

## Arctostaphylos
Arctostaphylos, п., a genus of plants of the heath
family, the bear berry (bot.) — ModL.,
compounded of Gk. ίρκτος, 'bear' and σταφυλή,
'bunch of grapes'. See arctic and staphylo-,

## Arcturus
Arcturus, п., the brightest star in the
constellation Bo6tes (aslron.) — L., fr. Gk. Άρκτοϋρος,
lit. 'the Bearguard', fr. ίρκτος, 'bear' and ουρος,
'watcher, guard, ward'. See arctic and ware,
'alert'.

## arcuate
arcuate, arcuated, adj., bent like a bow. — L.
arcuatus, pp. of arcuare, 'to bend like a bow',
fr. arcus, 'bow'. See arc.
Derivative: arcuate-ly, adv.

## arcuation
arcuation, n. — L. arcualio, gen. -Snis, fr. arcuatus
pp. of arcuare. See prec. word and -ion.

## arculite
arculite, п., a bow-shaped crystallite (mineral.) —
Compounded of L. arcus, 'bow' (see arc), and
combining form -lite.

## -ard
-ard, -art, suff. It orig. had an intensive force;
now it is often used in a pejorative sense. —
OF., fr. OHG. -harl, which is rel. to OHG. har-
li, 'hard'. See bard. For the force of this suff.
cp. coward, dastard, dotard, drunkard, sluggard.

## Arden
Arden, п., a genus of herons (ornilhol.) — L. ar-
dea, 'heron', cogn. with Gk. ερωδιός, 'heron',
Serb., Croat, rada 'stork', ON. aria, OSwed.
aria, 'creek duck'. Cp. Erodium.

## ardeb
ardeb, п., a measure of capacity used in Egypt! —
Arab, irdabb, in vulgar pronunciation ardabb,
ardebb, fr. Gk. άρτάβη, name of a Persian
measure. See artaba.

## ardella
ardella, п., any of the small apothecia of some
lichens (bot.) — ModL., fr. Gk. ίρδειν, 'to
water, pour forth', a word of unknown etymology.
Cp. Arethusa.

## ardency
ardency, n. — Formed fr. next word with suff. -cy.

## ardent
ardent, adj. — ME. ardaunt, fr. OF. ardanl (F.
ardent), fr. L. ardentem, ace. of ardins, pres. part,
of ardire, 'to burn', which stands for *aridire,
fr. aridus, 'parched, dry', and is rel. to arire,
'to be dry', fr. *asire, fr. I.-E. base *is-, 'to
burn, glow', whence also OI. asah, 'ashes, dust',
Tech. A asar, 'dry', Arm. azazem, Ί dry up',
aliun, 'ashes', Gk. ίζειν (for 'azdfein), 'to dry
up, parch', ίζα, 'dryness; dirt, mold', άζαλέος,
'dry, parched', Czech ozd, 'malt drier', ozditi,
'to dry (malt)', Goth, azgd, OE. asce, &sce,
'ashes'. See ash, 'powdery substance', and cp.
ara, ardor, area, arid, arson, asbollte, Azalea.
Cp. aiso the second element in aguardiente.
Derivatives: ardent-ly, adv., ardent-ness, n.

## ardennite
ardennite, п., a vanadosilicate of aluminum and
manganese (mineral.) — Named after Ardennes
in Belgium. For the ending see subst. suff. -Ite.

## ardnanari
ardnanari, п., a form of Siva in which he is
represented as half male and half female (Hindu
mylhol.) — OI. ardha-ndri-, 'half woman', fr.
ardhah-, 'half, part, side', and nan-, 'woman'.
OI. ardhah- is rel. to OI. fdhak, 'especially',
Avestic ar'da-, 'side', OI. fii, 'besides, except', fr.
I.-E. base *er-, *(e)ri-, 'loose; to split, separate,
be rare', whence also L. rarus, 'thin, loose', see
rare, 'thin'. OI. nari-, 'woman', prop, means
'pertaining to a man', and is rel. to OI. ndram
(ace.), 'man', and cogn. with Gk. άνήρ, 'man';
see andro-.

## arditi
arditi, n. pi., Italian volunteers serving in storm
troops in World War I. — It., pi. of ardito,
'brave, audacious', fr. F. hardi, prop. pp. of OF.
*hardir, 'to render courageous', lit. 'to make
hard', fr. Frankish *hardjan, fr. *hart, 'hard',
which is rel. to OHG. hard. OE. heard, 'hard'.
See hard.

## ardor
ardor, ardour, n. — ME. ardeur, fr. OF. ardour
(F. ardeur), fr. L. ardorem, ace. of ardor, 'heat',
fr. ardgre, 'to burn'. See ardent and -or.

## arduialte
arduialte, п., a zeolite (mineral.) — Named after
the Venetian geologist Giovanni Arduino. For
the ending see subst. suff. -ite.

## arduous
arduous, adj. — L. arduus, 'high, lofty, steep', fr.
I.-E. base *eredh-, *erdh-, 'to grow; high'.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:75 COLUMN:3 -->
whence also Avestic· *r*dva-, 'high', Olr. ard,
'high', Alb. rit, OSlav. rastq, Ί grow'. Cp. I.-E.
base 'weredh-, 'to grow; high', whence OI.
urdhvdh, 'high', vdrdhati, 'causes to grow,
increases', Gk. όρ&ός (for */ορθΓός; ср. Dor.
βορ&ό-), 'straight, right, erect'. See ortbo- and
cp. vriddhi. For E. -ous, as equivalent to L. -us,
see-ous.
Derivatives: arduous-ly, adv., arduous-ness, n.

## arc
arc, v., pres. pi. indicative of be. — ME. aren,
later are, fr. OE. (Northumbrian) aron, rel. to
ON. eru, '(they) are', for I.-E. *es-en, whence
also Dor. έντί, Att. είσί, ΟΙ. sdnti, L. sunt,
Umbr. ie/i/»Goth., OE. sind. All these words
are derivatives of I.-E. base *es-, 'to be'. See
esse and cp. apt. art. is.

## are
are, п., a square unit. — F., formed in 1795 by a
decree of the French National Convention, fr.
L. area, 'vacant piece of ground'. See next word
* and cp. the second element in hectare.

## area
area, n. — L., 'vacant piece of ground, building,
plot', rel. to arire, 'to become dry', hence area
orig. meant 'a place burned down, a dry, bare
place' ; see ardent and cp. areola,deboualr. For sense
development cp. G. Esse, 'chimney, forge',
which also derives fr. I.-E. base *<Xs-, 'to burn'.

## Areca
Areca,n., a genus of palms of Asia and the Malay
Archipelago (bot.) — ModL., fr. Port, areca, fr.
Malayalam cidakka, fr. Tamil ddaikay, lit.
'having close clusters of nuts', fr. ddai, 'close
arrangement of the cluster', and kay, 'nut'. See
OED. and Yule-Burnell, Hobson-Jobson, p. 35.

## Arecaceae
Arecaceae, n. pi., a family of plants, the palm
family (bot.) — ModL., formed fr. prec. word
with suff. -aceae.

## arecaceous
arecaceous, adj. — See prec. word and -aceous.

## arena
arena, n. — L. harina, arena, 'sand, sandy place,
seashore; place of.combat (lit. 'place strewn
with sand'), prob. of Etruscan origin. Cp.
Arenaria.

## arenaceous
arenaceous, adj., sandy. — L. arindceus, 'sandy'.
See prec. word and -aceous.

## Arenaria
Arenaria, п., a genus of herbs of the duckweed
family; the sandwort (bat.) — ModL., lit. 'the
sandwort', fr. Late L. harlnurius, arlndrius, 'of
sand', fr. L. harina, arena (see arena); so called
because many representatives of this species
grow in the sand.

## arend
arend, п., bearded vulture (S. Afr.) — Du.,
'eagle', fr. MDu. arent, reL to ON. От, OE.
earn, OHG. aro, 'eagle'. See ern(e).

## areo- combining form meaning 'of
areo- combining form meaning 'of, or pertaining
to, Ares or Mars', used in astronomy. — Fr.
Gk. "Αρεος or "Αρεως, gen. of "Αρης, 'Ares'.
See Ares and cp. Areopagtte.

## areola
areola, п., a small area; esp. the pigmented ring
surrounding the nipple (anat.) — L. areola,
'small area', dimin. of area, 'a vacant piece of
ground' (see area); introduced into anatomy by
the Swiss anatomist and botanist Caspar Bauhin
(1560-1624)in 1605.
Derivatives: areol-ar, areol-ate, areol-at-ed,
adjs., areol-ation, n.

## areole
areole, п., a small space (bol.) — F. oriole, fr. L.
areola. See areola.

## areolet
areolet, п., a small areola (zool.) — A dimin. of
areola, hence a double dimin. of area. For the
ending see suff. -et.

## areology
areology, п., the study of the planet Mars. —
Compounded of areo- and Gk. -λογία, fr.
-λόγος, 'one who speaks (in a certain manner);
one who deals (with a certain topic)'. See -logy.
Derivatives: areolog-ic, areolag-ic-al, adjs., are-
olog-ic-al-ly, adv.

## areometer
areometer, п., a hydrometer. — Compounded of
Gk. αραιός, 'thin, rare', and μέτρον,
'measure'. The first element is of uncertain origin;
it originally began with digamma (f = w),
henc; cannot be cognate with L. rarus, 'thin,
rare' (see rare, 'thin'). For the second element
see meter, 'poetical rhythm'.
Derivatives: areometr-ic, areometr-ic-al, adjs.,
areometr-y, n.

## Areopagite
Areopagite, п., member of the Areopagus. — Gk.
Άρειοπαγίτης, fr. Άρειόπαγος. See next word.

## Areopagus
Areopagus, п., name of a hill west of the
Acropolis in Athens and of the tribunal situated on
it. — L., fr. Gk. Άρειόπαγος, for Άρειος

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:76 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: 49 | ARISTOTELIAN -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:76 COLUMN:1 -->
πάγος, 'hill of Ares (= Mars)', resp. ή Βουλή
ή έξ 'Αρείου πάγου, 'the council of the hill of
Ares'. See next word. For the etymol. of πάγος,
'rocky hill', see pact

## Ares
Ares, п., the Greek god of war, identified by the
Romans with Mars (Greek mythol.) — L., fr.
Gk. "Αρης (gen. "Αρεος or "Αρεως), lit. 'injurer,
destroyer', fr. άρή, 'bane, ruin', which is rel.
to άρειή, 'a cursing, menacing', and prob.
cogn. with OI. irasya, 'ill will', irasyaii, 'bears
ill will', Arm. her, 'anger, envy', OE. eorre, yrre,
'angry'. Cp. areo-, Areopagus, Airfares.

## arete
arete, п., virtue (Greek philos.) — Gk. αρετή,
'virtue', prop, 'that which is good', rel. to
άρείων, 'better', άριστος, 'best' (whence
αριστοκρατία, 'the rule of the best'), άρέσκειν, 'to
make good, conciliate'. See aristo-.

## arete
arete, п., sharp crest of a mountain. — F.,
'fishbone; ridge', fr. L. arista, 'ear of grain', which
is prob. of Etruscan origin. Cp. arista, Aristida,
arris.

## Arethusa
Arethusa, п., nymph of a fountain near Syracuse
(Greek mythol.) — L., fr. Gk. 'Αρέθουσα, a
collateral form of άροΌυσα, 'waterer', fem. pres.
part, of άρδειν, 'to water'. See ardella.

## Arethusa
Arethusa, п., a genus of orchids (bot.) — ModL.,
named after the nymph Arethusa. See prec. word.

## arfvedsonite
arfvedsonite, п., a basic metasilicate (mineral.) —
Named after the Swedish chemist Johan August
Arfvedson (I J92-184I). For the ending see subst.
sun", -ite.

## argala
argala, п., the adjutant bird. — Hind, harglta.

## argali
argali, п., a large wild sheep of Asia (Ovis am-
mori). — Mongolian.
argand lamp. — Named after its inventor Αίταέ
Argand, a Swiss physicist (1755-1803).

## Argentine
Argentine, п., a genus of plants of the poppy
family (bot.) — Gk. άργεμώνη, 'a kind of
poppy', prob. fr. Heb. argaman, 'purple'. Cp. Ak-
kad. argamannu, of s.m. Cp. also agrimony. For
the ending -ώνη in άργεμώνη, ср. ανεμώνη, 'the
wind flower' (see anemone).

## argent
argent, п., silver (archaic). — F., fr. L. argentum,
'silver', which is cogn. with Gk. άργυρος, 'silver',
prop, 'the white (metal)', fr. αργός (dissimil-
ated fr. 'άργρός), 'shining, bright, white'; fr.
I.-E. base *arg-, 'to shine', whence also OI.
rjrah, 'shining, glowing, bright', rajatam, Aves-
tic 'r'zata, 'silver', OI. arjunah, 'shining, white',
Toch. A arki, 'white' (said of teeth), arkyant,
'silver', В arkwi, of s.m., arkm'rffle, "light color',
Hitt. harkish. 'bright, clear', Thracian άργιλος,
'mouse' (lit. 'the white colored animal'), Arm.
arcaf, 'silver', Olr. argat, W. ariaM.1), Co.,
MBret. argant, Bret, arc'hant, 'silver', L. ar-
guere, 'to make clear, prove'. Cp. argil, Argo,
argue, Argus, argyria, argyrodite, arjun, and the
second element in litharge, Pelargonium, Po-
darge, pygarg.

## argentiferous
argentiferous, adj., containing silver. —
Compounded of L. argentum, 'silver', and the stem
of L. ferre, 'to bear, carry'. See argent and
-ferous.

## argentine
argentine, adj., resembling silver. — L. argen-
tinus, 'of silver', fr. argentum, 'silver'. See argent
and -ine (representing L. -inus).

## argentite
argentite, п., silver sulfid, Ag3S (mineral.) —
Formed with subst. suff. -ite fr. L. argentum,
'silver'. See argent.

## argil
argil, п., potter's clay. — F. argile, 'clay', fr. L.
argilla, 'white clay, potter's earth', fr. Gk.
άργιλλος, of s.m., which is rel. to αργός,
'shining, bright'. See argent

## argillaceous
argillaceous, adj., resembling clay. — L. argilla-
ceus. It. argilla. See prec. word and -aceous.

## argilliferous
argilliferous, adj., rich in clay. — Compounded
of L. argilla, 'white clay' and the stem of ferre,
'to bear, carry'. See argil and -ferous.

## Argive
Argive, adj., of Argos; (by extension) of Greece.
— L. Argivus, fr. Gk. Άργεΐος, 'of Argos', fr.
"Αργός, 'Argos', name of the capital of Argolis
in the Peloponnesus.
Derivative: Argive, n.

## Argo
Argo, п., 1) name of the ship in which the
Argonauts sailed to Colchis, whence z) name of a
constellation. — Gk. 'Αργώ, lit. 'the Swift', fr.
αργός, 'swift'. This word is identical with αργός,
'shining, bright'. Cp. its OI. cognate rjrah, which

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:76 COLUMN:2 -->
also unites these two meanings, and see argent.
Cp. also Argonaut

## argon
argon, п., an inert chemical element. — ModL.,
fr. Gk. ίργόν, neut of αργός, 'idle, inert',
contraction of άεργος, lit. 'not active', fr. ά- (see
priv. pref. a-), and ϊργον, 'work'. See ergon
and cp. the second element in lethargy. This
element, discovered by the British chemists Sir
William Ramsay (1852-1916) and Morris
William Travers (1872-1961) in 1894, was so called
by them because it does not readily unite with
other elements.

## Argonaut
Argonaut, n. pi., one of the heroes led by Jason
in the ship Argo to fetch the golden fleece in
Colchis. — L. Argonauta, fr. Gk. 'Αργοναύτης,
'sailor of the Argo', which is compounded of
Αργώ (see Argo) and ναύτης, 'sailor, seaman'.
See nautical.

## argonaut
argonaut, п., the paper nautilus (zool.) — Fr.
prec. word.

## argosy
argosy, n„ a large ship; a fleet of large ships. —
Earlier ragusye, arguze, lit. 'ship from Ragusa'
fr. It. Ragusea, 'ship of Ragusa'.

## argot
argot, п., slang, esp. the slang of Paris. — F., of
uncertain origin.

## argue
argue, intr. and tr. v. — ME. arguen, fr. OF.
(= F.) arguer, fr. L. argutdre, freq. of arguere,
'to make clear, prove', which is rel. to argentum,
'silver' (arguere orig. meant 'to make as white
as silver'). See argent
Derivatives: argu-able, adj., argu-er, n.

## argument
argument, n. — F.^fr. L. argumentum, fr. arguere,
'to argue'. See prec. word and -ment.

## argumental
argumental, adj. — L. argumentalis, fr.
argumentum. See prec. word and adj. suff. -al.

## argumentation
argumentation, n. — F., fr. L. argumentStionem,
ace. of argumentutie, 'an adducing of proof, pp.
of argumentart, "to argue', fr. argumentum. See
argament and -ation.

## argumeatative
argumeatative, adj. — F. argumentatif (fem.
argumentative), fr. argument. See argument and -ive.
Derivatives: argumentative-ly, adv.,
argumentativeness, n.

## Argus
Argus, п., a giant with a hundred eyes (Greek
mythol.) — L., fr. Gk. "Αργός, lit. 'the bright
one', fr. αργός, 'shining, bright' (see argent);
so called in allusion to his hundred eyes. Cp. his
epithet Πανόπτης, 'all-seeing, all eyes'.

## argute
argute, adj., sharp, quick. — L. argutus, pp. of
arguere, 'to argue'. See argue.
Derivatives: argule-ly, adv., argute-ness, n.

## argyr-
argyr-, form of argyro- before a vowel.

## argyria
argyria, п., discoloration of the skin (med.) —
Medical L., fr. άργυρος, 'silver'. See argyro-
and -ia.

## argyrite
argyrite, п., argentite (mineral) — Formed with
subst. suff. -ite fr. Gk. άργυρος, 'silver'. See
argyro- and cp. argentite.

## argyro-
argyro-, before a vowel argyr-, combining form
meaning 'silver'. — Gk. άργυρο-, άργυρ-, fr.
άργυρος, 'silver', which is cogn. with L.
argentum, 'silver'. See argeat and cp. the second
element in hydrargyrum.

## argyrodite
argyrodite, п., a steel gray mineral containing
silver, geranium and sulfur (mineral.) — G. Ar-
gyrodit, coined by its discoverer the German
chemist Aloys Auer von Welsbach (1858-1929)
fr. Gk. άργυρώδης, 'rich in silver' (fr. άργυρος,
'silver', and -ώδης, 'like'), and suff. -ίτης. See
argyro-, -ode and subst. suff. -ite.

## Argyrol
Argyrol, п., a trademark for silver vitellin
(pharm.) — Coined by its inventor Albert
C. Barnes fr. argyr- and suff. -ol, a var. of -Ые.

## arin
arin, n. (music). — It., 'air'. See air, 'melody',
and cp. arioso.

## -aria
-aria, subst. suff. meaning 'related to', or
'connected with', as in Utricularia (bot. and zool.) —
ModL. -aria, fr. L. fem. sing, or neut. pi. of
-arius. See adj. suff. -ary.

## Ariadne
Ariadne, п., daughter of Minos, king of Crete
(Greek mythol.) — L., fr. Gk. 'Αριάδνη, a name
of uncertain origin.

## Arian
Arian, adj. and n. — L. Ariunus, 'pertaining to
Arius*, fr. Arius = Gk. "Αρειος, presbyter of
Alexandria (died in 336).
Derivatives: Arian-ism, п., Arian-ist-ic, Arian-
ist-ic-al, adjs., Arian-ize, intr. and tr. v., Arian-
iz-er, n.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:76 COLUMN:3 -->

## -arian
-arian, suff. forming adjectives from nouns
ending in -ary. — Compounded of the suffixes -ary
(representing L. -arius) and -an (representing L.
•anus).

## aricine
aricine, п., an alkaloid found in cusco bark. —
Named after Arica, in Peru. For the ending see
subst. suff. -ine.

## arid
arid, adj., dry.—L. aridus, 'parched, dry', whence
ardere, 'to burn'. See ardent
Derivatives: arid-ly, adv., arid-ness, n.

## aridity
aridity, п., dryness. — F. ariditi, fr. L. aridi-
tatem, ace. of ariditas, 'dryness', fr. aridus. See
prec. word and -ity.

## ariel
ariel, п., a gazelle. — Arab, dryil, a vulgar variant
of dyyil, 'stag', which is rel. to Heb. dyil, 'ram',
ayydl, 'stag', Aram.-Syr. aylA, 'stag', Akkad.
ayalu, 'ram', fr. Sem. base '-w-l, 'anything
strong', whence also Heb. e~ydl, 'strength', eld*,
alia", 'terebinth; oak', allon, Akkad. allanu,
'oak', prop, 'a strong tree'.

## Aries
Aries, п., ι) a constellation; 2) the first of the
signs of the zodiac (astron.) — L. arils, gen.
arietis, 'lamb', cogn. with Arm. or-o) (assimil. fr.
*er-oj), 'lamb', Gk. ίρι-φος, 'kind', Olr. heirp,
'kid', MIr. earb, of s.m.

## aright
aright, adv. — Formed fr. a-, 'on', and right

## aril
aril, п., an accessory covering of seeds (bot.) —
Late L. arillus, 'dried grape'.

## arioso
arioso, adj., melodious; adv., in a melodious
way (mus.) — It., formed fr. aria, 'melody', with
suff. -oso (corresponding to L. -dsus). See aria
and adj. suff. -ose.

## Arisaema
Arisaema, п., a genus of plants of the arum family
(bot.). — ModL., lit. 'blood of arum', fr. Gk.
άρίς, 'a kind of arum', which is rel. to άρον,
'cuckoopint', and αίμα, 'blood' (see Arum and
hemal); so called from the red-spotted leaves of
some species.

## arise
arise, intr. v. - - OE. arisan, rel. to OS. arisan,
Goth, urreisan. See a-, 'on', and rise.

## arista
arista, п., an awn. — L. See arete.

## aristarchy
aristarchy, п., government by the best men. —
Gk. άρισταρχίδ, compounded of άριστος, 'best',
and -αρχίά, 'rule', fr. άρχος, 'leader, chief, ruler*.
See aristo- and -archy.

## Aristida
Aristida, п., a genus of grasses (bot.) — ModL.,
fr. L. arista, 'awn'. See arista and -ida.

## aristo-
aristo-, before a vowel arist-, combining form
meaning 'best'. — Gk. άριστο-, άριστ-, fr.
άριστος, 'best', superl. to άρείων, 'better', rel.
to αρετή, 'virtue', άρέσκειν, 'to make good,
conciliate', fr. I.-E. base *ar-, 'to join', whence also
Gk. άρθρον, 'a joint', L. arius, 'joint, limb', ars,
'art', arma (pi.), 'implements of war, weapons'.
See arm, 'weapon', and cp. arete.

## aristocracy
aristocracy, n. — MF. aristocracie (F.
aristocratic), fr. L. aristocratia, fr. Gk. αριστοκρατία,
'government, rule of the best', which is
compounded of άριστος, 'best' and -κρατίδ, 'rule
of, fr. κράτος, 'strength, power, rule'. Seearisto-
and -cracy.

## aristocrat
aristocrat, n. — F. aristocrate, back formation fr.
aristocratic See prec. word.

## aristocratic
aristocratic, adj. — F. aristocratique, fr. Gk.
αριστοκρατικός, 'pertaining to the rule of the
best', fr. αριστοκρατία. See aristocracy and -ic.
Derivatives: aristocratic-al, adj., artistocratic-
al-ly, adv.

## Aristolochln
Aristolochln, п., a genus of plants, the birthwort.
— ModL., fr. Gk. άριστολοχία, 'birthwort', lit.
'that which is the best for childbirth', fr. άριστος,
'best', and λοχεία, 'childbirth', fr. λόχος, of s.m.
See aristo- and lie, 'to recline'.

## aristology
aristology, п., the science of dining. —
Compounded of Gk. άριστον, 'breakfast', and -λογία,
fr. -λόγος, 'one who speaks (in a certain manner);
one who deals (with a certain topic)'. The first
element lit. means 'morning meal'. It is formed
fr. άρι-, which is rel. to ήρι, 'early*, and cogn.
with OE. xr, 'soon, formerly' (see ere, early),
and fr. -στο (for *d-to), кто degree of root έδ-,
'to eat', whence also Gk. ϊδειν, έσ&ίείν, L. edere,
'to eat' (see ent). For the second element in
aristology see -logy.
Derivatives: aristolog-ic-al, adj., arislolog-ist, n.

## Aristotelian
Aristotelian, adj., pertaining to the Greek
philosopher Aristotle (384-322); п., a follower of
Aristotle; an adherent of Aristotle's teachings.—

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:77 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: ARITE | 50 -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:77 COLUMN:1 -->
Formed with suff. -ian fr. Gk. 'Αριστοτέλης,
'Aristotle'.
Derivative: Aristotelian-ism, n.

## ante
ante, п., a variety of niccolite {mineral.) —
Named after montagne d'Ar in the dept. Basses
Pyrenees, in France. For the ending see subst.
suff. -ite.

## arithmetic
arithmetic, n. — ME. arsmetike, fr. OF. aris-
metique, fr. L. arilhmglica, fr. Gk. αριθμητική
(scil. τέχνη), 'the art of counting', fr. &pi&-
μεϊν, 'to number, count, reckon', fr. άρι-θμός,
'number', fr. I.-E. base *W-, 'to count, number',
whence also Gk. νή-ρι-τος, 'numberless', OE.,
OHG. rim, 'number', Olr. rim, 'number', do-
rtmu, Ί count, number, enumerate', L. ritus,
'religious custom, usage, ceremony'. Base *ri-,
'to count, number', is prob. an enlargement of
base *ar-, 'to join', whence L. arma, 'weapons',
ars, 'art', Goth, arms, OE. earm, arm, etc., 'the
upper limb'. See arm, 'the upper limb', arm,
'weapon', and cp. rhyme, rite. The ά- in αριθμός
is prosthetic and due to the fact thai the Greek
(as well as the Armenian) never begins a word
with primary r. Initial ρ in Greek words goes
back either to *sr- or * wr- (see red). The s in OF.
arismetique is the phonetic rendering of L. th =
Gk. &; the ME. forms arismelric, arsmetrik
were developed from ME. arsmetike, which was
associated erroneously with L. ars metrica, 'the
art of measure'. ModF. arithmetique and E.
arithmetic have been refashioned after the Greek.
Cp. aparithmesis and the second element in
logarithm.

## arithmetician
arithmetician, n. — F. arithmiticien, fr.
arithmitique. See arithmetic and -ian.
arithmo- combining form meaning 'number'. —
Gk., fr. άριθμο-, fr. αριθμός, 'number'. See
arithmetic.

## arithmogram
arithmogram, п., the sum of the numerical values
of the letters in a word or phrase. —
Compounded of arithmo- and Gk. γράμμα, 'something
written'. See -gram.

## arithmograph
arithmograph, п., a kind of calculating machine.
— Compounded of arithmo- and Gk. -γράφος,
fr. γράφειν, 'to write'. See -graph.

## arithmography
arithmography, n. — Compounded of arithmo-
and Gk. -γραφιά, fr. γράφειν, 'to write'. See
-graphy.

## arithmometer
arithmometer, п., a calculating machine. —
Compounded of arithmo- and Gk. μέτρον,
'measure'. See meter, 'poetical rhythm'.

## -arium
-arium, subst. suff. meaning 'a place for, or a-
bounding in, something', or 'a thing pertaining
to something'. — L. -arium, prop. neut. of the
adjectival suff. -arius, used to form nouns. The
regular English equivalent of this suff. is -ary

## arizoolte
arizoolte, п., a ferric metatitanate (mineral.) —
Named after Arizona in the U.S.A. For the
ending see subst. suff. -ite.

## arjun
arjun, п., an Asiatic tropical tree (Terminalia ar-
juna). — Hind, arjun, fr. OI. drjunah, 'white',
which is cogn. with Gk. αργός, 'bright, white',
δργυρος, 'silver', L. argentum, 'silver'. See
argent

## ark
ark, n. — OE. arc, earc, 'Noah's ark, box, coffin',
fr. L. area, 'chest', whence also OHG. arahha,
arka (MHG., G. arche), 'ark'. (OSlav. raka,
'burial cave, rakev, 'coffin', are Teut. loan
words.) See arcanum and cp. words there
referred to.

## arles
arles, n. pi., earnest money (Scot.) — OF., fr. L.
*arrhuta, dimin. of arrha, 'pledge'. See arrha
and cp. words there referred to.

## arm
arm, п., the upper limb. — ME., fr. OE. earm,
arm, rel. to OS., Dan., Swed., MDu., Du.,
MHG., G. arm, ON. armr, OFris. erm, OHG.
arm, aram, Goth, arms, 'arm*, and cogn. with
OI. irmah, Avestic ar'ma-, 'arm', Arm. armukn,
'elbow', Osset. arm, 'palm of the hand', Gk.
αρμός, 'a joint', L. armus, 'shoulder', OSlav.
ramo, OPruss. irmo, 'arm'. All these words
derive fr. I.-E. base *ar-, 'to join', and lit. mean
'joint', whence also L. arma (pi.), 'weapons',
prop, 'implements of war', artus, 'joint, limb',
ars, "art', are OI. ardh, 'spoke (of a wheel)',
Avestic ratav-, 'epoch; judge', Toch. ABarwar,
Srwer, 'ready, prepared', Hitt. ara, 'suitable,
good', Arm. y-armar, 'fitting, appropriate',

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:77 COLUMN:2 -->
arnem, Ί make', Gk. Spdpov, 'a joint', άρμα, 'a
chariot', άραρίσχειν, 'to join, fasten,fit together',
άρέσκειν, 'to make good^ conciliate', άρείων,
'better', άριστος, 'best', αρετή, 'virtue', άρμαλίά,
'allotted sustenance', άρμόζειν, 'to fit together,
adapt, accommodate', αρμός, 'a joining',
αρμονία, 'joint, proportion, concord', άρτι,
'just', άρτιος, 'complete, perfect of its kind,
suitable; even' (said of a number), άρτύειν,
άρτύνειν, 'to arrange„prepare, make ready'. Cp.
arm, 'weapon'. Cp. also ambry, arete, arista-,
armilla, art, Artamus, arthro-, article, articulate,
artillery, artisan, artist, artiste, harmony, inert,
inertia, the first element in Artiodactyla and the
second element in Homer. Cp. also arithmetic,
ration, read, reason.

## arm
arm, п., usually in pi. arms, weapon. — ME.
armes (pi.), fr. OF. armes (pi.), fr. L. arma,
'implements of war, weapons', neut. pi. mistaken
in VL. for fem. sing., fr. I.-E. base *ar-, 'to join',
whence also L. armus, 'shoulder', Goth, arms,
OE. earm, arm, 'arm'. See arm, 'upper limb',
and cp. words there referred to. Cp. also alarm,
alarum, armada, armadillo, armament,
armature, armet, army, Inerm and the last element in
gendarme.

## arm
arm, tr. v., to furnish with weapons. — F. armer,
fr. L. armure, fr. arma, 'weapons'. See arm,
'weapon'.
Derivatives: arm-ed, adj., arm-ing, n.

## armada
armada, п., a fleet of warships; specif, the fleet
of warships sent against England by Philip II
of Spain in 1588, called the Spanish or
Invincible Armada. — Sp., 'fleet, navy', fr. L. armdta,
fem. pp. of armare, 'to furnish with weapons',
used as a noun, fr. arma, 'weapons'. See arm,
'weapon', and cp. army.

## armadillo
armadillo, п., an American burrowing mammal.
— Sp., dimin. of armado, 'armed', fr. L. armatus,
pp. of armare (see prec. word); so called in
allusion to its hard bony plates resembling armor.

## Armageddon
Armageddon, п., scene of a great battle. — Late
L. Armagedon, fr. Gk. Άρμαγεδδών, Άρμα-
γεδών, fr. Heb. Наг Megiddd, 'mountain
(district) of Megiddo'.

## armagnac
armagnac,n., a superior kind of brandy.—So
called because it is made in the department of Gets
in France, a district formerly named Armagnac.

## armament
armament, n. — L. armamenlum, 'implement', fr.
armare, 'to furnish with weapons', fr. arma,
'weapons'. See arm, 'weapon', and -ment and
cp. F. armement.

## armature
armature, п., armor. — L. armatura, 'armor', fr.
armatus, pp. of armare. See prec. word and -ure
and cp. armor, which is a doublet of armature.

## armet
armet, п., a medieval steel helmet. — F., dimin.
of arme. See arm, 'weapon', and -et.

## armlger
armlger, п., an esquire. — L., 'a weapon bearer',
compounded of arma, 'weapons', and the stem
of gerere, 'to bear, carry'. See arm, "weapon',
and gerent

## armigerous
armigerous, adj., possessing arms. — Formed fr.
L. armiger (see prec. word) with suff. -ous, on
analogy of adjectives in which this suff.
corresponds to OF. -ous, -eus (F. -eux), representing
L. -osus.

## armilla
armilla, п., a bracelet. — L. dimin. formed fr.
armus, 'shoulder'. See arm, 'the upper limb'.

## armillary
armillary, adj., 1) pertaining to a bracelet; z)
consisting of rings. — Formed with adj. suff. -ary
fr. L. armilla. See prec. word.

## Arminian
Arminian, adj., pertaining to the Dutch
theologian Jacobus Arminius (1560-1609) or his
doctrines. For the ending see suff. -ian. .
Derivative: Arminian-ism, n.

## armipotent
armipotent, adj., mighty in arms. — L. armi-

## potgns
potgns, gen. -entis, compounded of arma,
'weapons', and potins, 'mighty, powerful'. See
arm, 'weapon', and potent

## armistice
armistice, п., truce. — F„ fr. ModL. armistitium,

## lit. 'a standing (still) of arms'
lit. 'a standing (still) of arms', formed, on
analogy of the juridic term justitium, 'suspension of

## jurisdiction'
jurisdiction', fr. L. arma, 'weapons', and -sistere,

## pp. stem -stit-(um) (used only in compounds)
pp. stem -stit-(um) (used only in compounds),

## fr. sislere
fr. sislere, 'to cause to stand still', fr. stare, 4o
stand'. See state and cp. words there referred to.
G. Waffenstillstand, 'armistice', lit. 'a standing
still of weapons', is a loan translation of F.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:77 COLUMN:3 -->
armistice.

## armlet
armlet, n. — Formed fr. arm, 'the upper limb',
with dimin. suff. -let

## armor
armor, armour, n. — ME. armure, fr. OF. or-
meiire, armure (F. armure), fr. L. armatura. See
armature.
Derivative: armored, armoured, adj.

## armorer
armorer, n. — OF. armeurier, armurier (F. ar-
murier), fr. armeiire, armure. See armor and
agential suff. -er.

## armory
armory, п., the science of heraldry. — OF. ar-
moierie, fr. armoier, armoyer, 'to blazon', fr. L.
arma, 'weapons'. See arm, 'weapon', and cp.
next word.
Derivative: armori-al, adj.

## armory
armory, п., armour collectively. — A blend of
OF. armoierie, 'coat of arms', and OF. almarie,
armarie, 'a place where arms are kept'. See
armor and ambry.

## army
army, n. — F. armee, fr. L. armata, fem. pp. of
armare, 'to furnish with weapons'. See armada
and -y (representing F. -ее).
Derivative: armi-ed, adj.

## Arnebin
Arnebin, п., a genus of plants of the borage
family (bot.)—Arab, arnab tya", name of a plant,
lit. 'hare plant', fr. arnab, 'hare', which is rel.
to Heb. arnebheth, Arm. arnabhta, Syr. ar-
n'bha, Ugar. 'nhb. Akkad. annabu, 'hare'.

## arnica
arnica, п., 1) (cap.) a genus of plants of the thistle
family; 2) tincture made from the root of the
plant.— ModL., prob. corruption ofplarmica, fr.
Gk. πταρμική, 'sneezewort', fem. of πταρμικός,
'causing to sneeze', fr. πταρνύναι, πταίρειν, 'to
sneeze', from the I.-E. imitative base *pster-
(eu)-, whence also L. sternuere, 'to sneeze'. See
sternutation.

## Araold
Araold, masc. PN. — G., fr. OHG. Arenwald,
lit. 'having the strength of an eagie', fr. OHG.
aro, 'eagle', and wald, 'power', from the base
of wallan, 'to have power'. For the first element
see era(e) and cp. arend, for the second see
wield and cp. words there referred to.

## Amoseris
Amoseris, п., a genus of plants of the chicory
family (bot.) — ModL., lit. 'lamb chicory',
fr. Gk. άρνός, 'lamb', and σέρις, 'chicory'.
The first element is rel. to άρήν gen. άρνος,
'lamb', and to Homeric and Ion. Gk. είρος,
'wool'; see erio-. The second element is of
uncertain, prob. foreign, origin.

## aroint
aroint, intr. v. (used only in the imper.). begone!
(obsol.) — Of uncertain origin.

## aroma
aroma, п., odor. — L., fr. Gk. ίίρωμα, 'fragrance,
odor, spice', of uncertain origin.

## aromatic
aromatic, adj. — F. aromatique, fr. L. aromaticus,
fr. Gk. αρωματικός, fr. άρωμα, gen. αρώματος,
'fragrance'. See prec. word and -atic

## aromatize
aromatize, tr. v., to render aromatic. — F. aro-
matiser, fr. L. ardmatizare, fr. Gk. αρωμάτιζε»,
fr. άρωμα. See aroma and -ize.

## aromo
aromo, п., the huisache.—Sp. aroma, fr. L. aroma,
fr. Gk. άρωμα, 'fragrance, odor'. See aroma.

## arose
arose, past tense of arise. — ME. aroos, fr. OE.
aras, 'arose' fr. arisan. See arise.

## around
around, adv. and prep. — Formed fr. a- 'on',
and round.
arouse tr. v. — Formed fr. a-, 'on', and rouse.
Derivatives: arous-al, п., arous-er, n.

## n rovescio
n rovescio, a musical direction indicating
imitation by contrary motion. — It., lit. 'upside
down', fr. a (fr. L. ad), 'to', and rovescio,
'reverse, wrong side', fr. L. reversus, 'turned back',
pp. of revertere. See ad- and revert

## arpeggio
arpeggio, п., the playing of the notes of a chord
in rapid succession instead of simultaneously;
a chord on which the notes are so played
(mus.) — It., fr. arpeggiare, 'to play upon the
harp', fr. arpa, 'harp'. See harp.

## arpent
arpent, п., an old French land measure. — F.,
fr. VL. *arependis, alteration of L. arepennis,
a Gaulish word of uncertain origin.

## arquebus
arquebus, n. — See harquebus.

## nrrack
nrrack, in the East, a strong alcoholic drink made
from rice or molasses. — Fr. Arab, 'araq, 'sweat,
juice of fruit'. Cp. rack, 'arrack', and borage.

## arraign
arraign, tr. v., to call to account; to bring before
a law court. — ME. areinen, fr. AF. areiner,
fr. OF. araisnier, aresnier (F. arraisonner), fr.
VL. *arrationure, fr. ad- and -'ralionare, 4o

reason', fr. L. ratio, 'reckoning, calculation;
reason'. See reason and cp. deraign.
Derivatives: arraign, п., arraign-er, п.,
arraignment (q.v.)

## arraignment
arraignment, n. — OF. araisnement, fr. araisnier.
See prec. word and -ment.

## arrange
arrange, tr. and intr. v. — OF. arengier, arangier,
(F. arranger), fr. a, 'to' (see a), and rengier,

Derivatives: arrange-ment, п., arrang-er, n.

## arrant
arrant, adj., 1) wandering (obsol.); 2) unmitigated;
notorious, infamous. — A variant'of errant.
Derivative: arrant-ly, adv.

## arras
arras, п., pictured tapestry. — Fr. Arras,
formerly capital of the province of Artois (now capital

A/rebates, a tribe of the Belgae (whence also the
name Artois. Cp. artesian.

## arras
arras, п., property contributed by the hnsband
to the wife (Sp. law). — Sp., fr. L. arrha, 'earnest
money'. See arrha and cp. earnest, 'pledge', and
words there referred to.

## arrastre
arrastre, п., a drag-stone mill for grinding ores.
— Sp., 'dragging, haulage', fr. arrastrar, 'to
drag along*, fr. ad-, ar- (fr. L. ad), 'to', and
rastrar, 'to drag', fr. rastro, "rake, harrow', fr.
L. rostrum, 'a toothed hoe, a rake', which stands
for *rad-trom, 'instrument to scrape with', fr.
radere, 'to scrape'. See raze.

## array
array, tr. v., 1) to arrange;.2) to dress, clothe. —
ME. arraien, fr. OF. araier, areier, areer, aroier,
fr. VL. *arredare (whence also It. arredare),
which is formed fr. L. ad, 'to', and Teut. *raid-
jan, 'to place in order', whence OE. ride,
'ready, mounted', Goth, garedan, Ίο attend to,
provide for', garaips, 'fixed, appointed,
ordained'. See ad- and ready and cp. raiment.
Derivatives: array-al, п., array-er, п., array-
ment, n.

## array
array, п., 1) order, arrangement; 2) dress,
garments. — ME. arrai, fr. OF. arret, aroi, arroi
(F. arroi), 'array, equipage', fr. OF. areier,
areer. See array, v.

## arrayan
arrayan,n., name of various trees. — Sp. arrayan,
fr. Arab, ar-rayhdn, fr. ar-, assimilated form of
at-, 'the', and rayfran in rayhan al-qubur, 'myrtle'
(lit. 'sweet-smelling plants of the tombs'), a
deriv. of rib, 'odor', which is rel. to Heb. re"fi,
'odor', prop, 'breath', Heb. ra°h, Aram.-Syr.
ruhi, 'breath, wind, spirit', Arab, rub, 'soul,
spirit'.

## arrear
arrear, n. — ME. arere, fr. OF. arere (F. arriire),
'behind', fr. VL. *ad retro (L. = retrS),
'backward'. See ad- and retro- and cp. reredos.

## arrearage
arrearage, n. — ME. arerage, fr. OF. arerage
(F. arrirage). See prec. word and -age.

## arrect
arrect, adj., erect. — L. arrictus, pp. of arrigere,
'to set upright', fr. ad- and regere, 'to keep
straight, stretch'. See regent and cp. erect

## arrest
arrest, tr. v. — ME. aresten, fr. OF. arester (F.
arriler), fr. VL. *arrestdre (whence also It. ar-
restare, Sp., Port, arrestar), fr. ad- and L.
restore, 'to stop', fr. re- and stare, 'to stand'. See
state and cp. rest, 'to remain'.

## arrest
arrest, n. — ME. arest, fr. OF. arest (F. arret),
back formation fr. arester (F. arriter). See
arrest, v.
Derivatives: arrest-er, п., arrest-ing, arrest-ive,
adjs., arrestment (q.v.)

## arrestment
arrestment, n. — OF. arestement, fr. arester. See
prec. word and -ment.

## arrha
arrha, п., earnest money. — L. arrha, arra,
shortened fr. arrhabd, fr. Gk. άρραβών, 'earnest
money', fr. Heb. 'irdbhtn, 'pledge, surety', fr.
'arabh, 'he pledged'. See earnest, 'pledge' and
cp. words there referred to.

## arriba-
arriba-, п., a variety of cacao from Ecuador. —
Sp. arriba, 'up, above', formed fr. ad-, ar- (fr.
L. ad), to' and ripa, 'bank of a stream' (see nd-
and riparian and cp. arrive); so called from an
upland district in Ecuador.

## arride
arride, Ir. v., to please (archaic). — L. arridere,
'to laugh at, laugh with', fr. ad- and ridire, 'to
laugh'. See risible.

## arriere-ban
arriere-ban, п., summons to war issued by the
king to his vassals. — F., fr. OHG. hari-ban,
(whence also G. Heerbann), lit. 'proclamation

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:78 COLUMN:2 -->
to the army', fr. OHG. hari, heri (whence G.
Heer), 'army', and ban (whence G. Bonn),
'proclamation'; see harry and ban. F. arriere-ban
was influenced in form by a confusion with F.
arriire, 'behind' (see next word).

## arriere-pensee
arriere-pensee, п., mental reservation — F., lit.
'a thought behind', fr. arriire, 'behind', and
pensee, 'thought'. For the first word see arrear.
F. pensee is prop. fern. pp. of penser, 'to think',
fr. L. pensdre, 'to weigh out carefully, ponder,
examine'; see pensive and cp. pansy.

## arriero
arriero, a muleteer. — Sp., a collateral form of
harriero, fr. arrear, harrear, 'to drive or push
on', from the interjection harre, fr. Arab, harr,
the cry used to drive on camels.

## arris
arris, п., a sharp ridge, an edge. — OF. areste
(F. arete), fr. L. arista, 'ear of grain'. See arete
and cp. arista, Aristida.

## arrival
arrival, n. — ME. arrivaile, fr. AF. arrivaille, fr.
OF. arriver. See next word and subst. suff. -al.

## arrive
arrive, intr. v. — ME. ariven, fr. OF. arriver,
ariver (F. arriver), 'to arrive', fr. VL. *arripare,
'to touch the shore', fr. ad- and L. ripa, 'shore,
bank'. See river and cp. arriba. Sp. arribar aiso
derives fr. VL. *arripdre, but It. arrivare, is a
French loan word.
Derivatives: arrival (q.v.), arriv-er, n.

## arroba
arroba, п., a Spanish weight. — Sp. and Port.,
fr. Arab, ar-rub', in vulgar pronunciation ar-
rob', 'the quarter' (scil. of the weight al-qintar),
fr. ar-, assimilated form of al-, 'the', and rub'
(rob'), 'quarter', from the stem of arba' (masc),
drba'a" (fem.), which is rel. to Heb. arba'
(masc), arba'a**, (fem.), Aram, arba' (masc.),
arb''a (fem.), Ethiop. arba' (masc.), arbu'tu
(fem.), Akkad. arba'u (masc.), irbitti (fem.),
'four'. (The masc. forms are used with fem.
nouns, the fem. ones with masc. nouns).

## arrogance
arrogance, n. — F., fr. L. arrogantia, fr. arrogans,
gen. -amis. See next word and -ce.

## arrogant
arrogant, adj. — F., fr. L. arrogantem, ace. of
arrogans, pres. part, of arrogare. See next word
and -ant
Derivative: arrogant-ly, adv.

## arrogate
arrogate, tr. v. — L. arrogatus, pp. of arrogare,
'to claim as one's own, to arrogate to oneself,
fr. ad- and rogdre, 'to ask'. See rogation and
verbal suff. -ate and cp. abrogate.
Derivatives: arrogation (q.v.), arrogat-ive, adj.

## arrogation
arrogation, — L., fr. arrogatus, pp. of arrogare.
See prec. word and -ion.

## nrrojndite
nrrojndite, п., a phosphate of natrium, ferrum,
sodium, etc. — Named after the Brazilian
geologist Dr. Miguel Arrojado of Lisbon. For the
ending see subst. suff. -ite.
arroadissement n„ an administrative district of
a department in France. — F., lit. 'a rounding',
fr. arrondir, 'to make round, to round off', fr.
a, 'to' (see a), and rond, 'round'. See round, adj.
and -ment

## arrope
arrope, п., must boiled down to a sirup, — Sp.,
fr. Arab, ar-rubb, ar-, assimilated form of al-,
'the', and rubb, 'juice of the fruit boiled down'.

## arrow
arrow, n. — ME. arewe, fr. OE. arwe, earh, rel.
to ON. or, gen. orvar, Goth, arfvazna, and cogn.
with L. arcus, 'ljow, arch'. See arc
Derivative: arrow-y, adj.

## arroyo
arroyo, п., a watercourse; the dry bed of a
stream. — Sp., 'rivulet, small stream', fr. L. ar-
rugia, 'shaft or pit in a gold mine', which is
prob. formed, fr. ad- and ruga, 'wrinkle'; the
orig. meaning was 'a digging out'. See ruga.

## arse
arse, п., the buttocks (now vulgar). — ME. ars,
ers, fr. OE. ears, mrs, rel. to OS., OHG., MHG.
orj, ON. ars (also metathesized into rass), MDu.
sirs, e(e)rs, Du. (n)aars, G. Arsch, 'buttock',
and cogn. with Gk. δρρος (for I.-E. *orsos),
'tail, rump, base of the spine', ουρά (for *opof &),
'tail', Hitt. arrash. Arm. or, 'buttock', Olr. err
(for *ersd), 'tail'. Cp. uro-, 'tail-'.

## arsenal
arsenal, п., a place for manufacturing and storing
ammunition and weapons. — It. arsenate (Olt.
arzanale), 'dock', borrowed—prob. through the
medium of MGk. άρσηναλης—fr. Arab, dar-
as-sind'a" (whence also Sp. ddrsena and It. dar-
sena, 'dock'), lit. 'house of construction', fr. dar,
'house', as-, assimilated form of al-, 'the', and
sina'a", 'construction, art', fr. sdna'a, 'he made'.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:78 COLUMN:3 -->
- For the ending of arsenal see adj. suff. -al.

## arsenic
arsenic, п., a chemical element. — OF. (= F.)
arsenic,·fr. L. arsenicum, arrhenicum, fr. Gk.
άρσενικάν, άρρενικάν, "yellow orpiment', fr.
MPers. *zarnik, 'gold, golden; orpiment'(whence
ModPers.-Arab. zarntkh, 'orpiment'), through
the medium of a Semitic language; cp. Mish-
naic Heb. zarntkh, Syr. zarnikha, 'orpiment'.
Cp. Avestic zaranya, Pers. zar, 'gold', and the
first element in zermahbub, and see yellow and
words there referred to. Cp. also jargon, 'a
variety of zircon'. Gk. άρσενικόν, άρρενικόν,
'orpiment', was influenced in form by αρσενικός,
άρρενικός, 'male', fr. SpoTjv, δρρην, 'male'. For
the sense development of MPers. "zarnik, cp. L.
auripigmentum, fr. aurum, 'gold' (see orpiment).
Derivatives: arsenic, arsenic-al, adjs.

## arsenious
arsenious, adj., containing arsenic. — See
arsenic and -ons.

## arsis
arsis, п., the unaccented part of a foot in
prosody. — L., fr. Gk. ίρσις, 'a raising, lifting',
fr. άείρειν, αΐρειν, 'to raise, lift'. See artery.

## arson
arson, n. — OF., fr. Late L. arsionem, ace. of
arsid, 'a burning', fr. L. arsus, pp. of ardire, 'to
burn'. See ardent.

## arsonium
arsonium, п., the radical AsH, (chem.) — ModL.,
compounded of arsenic and ammonium.

## art
art, n. — OF. (= F.), fr. L. апет, асе. of ars,
'skill, handicraft, trade, occupation, art', which
is rel. to L. artus, 'joint', and cogn. with OI.
rtih, 'manner, mode', Gk. Жр-ri, 'just', άρτιος,
'complete, perfect of its kind, suitable; even
(said of a number), άρτίζειν, 'to prepare',
άρτύειν, άρτόνειν, 'to arrange, prepare, make
ready', Lith. arti, 'near', MHG., G. art,
'manner, mode'. All these words derive fr. I.-E.
*art-, at- enlargement of base *ar-, 'to join',
whence L. armus, 'shoulder', arma, 'weapons'.
See arm, 'upper limb', and arm, 'weapon', and
cp. Altaians, article, articulate, artifice,
artillery, artisan, artist, artiste, coarctation, inert.
Derivatives: art-ful, adj., artful-ly, adv., art-

## ful-ness
ful-ness, п., art-less, adj., art-less-ly, adv.,
artless- ness, n.

## art
art, 2nd pers. pres. ind. of be. — OE." ear/, fr.
Teut. base *ar-, corresponding to I.-E. base *es-,
'to be'. See are, v., and words there referred to.

## artaha
artaha, artabe, п., a Persian and Egyptian
measure. — Gk. άρτάβη, prob. of Egyptian origin.
Cp. ardeb.

## Artamus
Artamus, п., a genus of oscine birds (ornilhol.) —
ModL., fr. Gk. Йр-ταμος, 'butcher, cook',
which—according to Eusthatios—is a
contraction of εις Sprit* τέμνων, 'he who cuts
artistically'. Accordingly ίίρταμος stands for *άρτί-
ταμος (see haplology), and is compounded of
£ρτι, 'just', orig. 'joining, order', and of the
stem of τέμνειν, 'to cut'. See art, п., and tiune.

## Artemis
Artemis, п., the goddess of hunting in Greek
mythology; identified by the Romans with
Diana. — L., fr. Gk. "Αρτεμις, a name of
uncertain origin. Cp. next word.

## Artemisin
Artemisin, п., a genus of plants of the thistle
family (hot.) — L., 'mugwort', fr. Gk. άρτε-
μιαίϋ, fr. "Αρτεμις, the Greek goddess of
hunting. See prec. word and -ia.

## nrterial
nrterial, adj. — F. arterial (now arlerlel), fr. L.
artiria. See artery and adj. suff. -al.
Derivative: arterial-ly, adv.

## arterialize
arterialize, tr. v. to change into arterial. — F.
artirialiser. See prec. word and -ize.
Derivative: arterializ-ation, n.

## arteriasis
arteriasis, п., degeneration of an artery (med.) —
Medical L., formed with suff. -iasis fr. Gk.
αρτηρία. See artery.

## arterio-
arterio-, combining form meaning 'arterial'. —
Gk. άρτηρίο-, fr. άρτηρίϊ, 'windpipe, artery'.
See artery.

## arteriole
arteriole, п., a small artery. — ModL., dimin.
of L. artiria. See artery and -ole.

## arteriosclerosis
arteriosclerosis, п., thickening of the walls of
the arteries (med.) — Medical L., lit. 'hardening
of the arteries'; compounded of Gk. αρτηρία,
'windpipe, artery', and σκλέρωσις, 'hardening,
induration'. See arterio- and sclerosis.

## arteriosclerotic
arteriosclerotic, adj. — See arterio- and sclerotic

## arteriotomy
arteriotomy, п., the cutting open of an artery
(med.) — Late L. artiriotomia, fr. Gk. άρτηριο-

ταμία, fir. άρτηριατομεΐν, Чо cut an artery*. See

## arterious
arterious, adj., arterial. — Formed with sun*, -ous
fr. L, arteria. See artery.

## arteritis
arteritis, п., inflammation of an artery or of
arteries (med.) — Medical L., formed with suff.
-itis fr. Gk. άρτηρϋ. See next word.

## artery
artery, n. — L. artgria, fr. Gk. αρτηρία,
'windpipe, artery', prob. contracted from *άερτηρίά,
which is a derivative of ίείρειν, αΐρειν, 'to
lift, raise, bear'. See aorta and cp. arsis and the
second element in meteor.

## artesiaa
artesiaa, adj. — F. artesien, 'of Artois'. fr. OF.
Arteis (F. Artois), fr. L. Atrebatls, a people that
lived in the NW. of Gallia. Cp. arras. For the
ending see suff. -ian. — Artesian well owes its
name to the circumstance that the first such
wells were established by Belidor (1698-1761)
in the province of Artois, who therefore called
them puils arlesiens.

## artha
artha, п., purpose (Hindu phiios.) — OI. drtham,
later drthah, 'purpose, aim, work, object', which
is rel. to rnati, rmati, 'rises, moves', rcchati,
'goes toward a thing, reaches', Avestic erlnaoiti,
'moves', and cogn. with Gk. βρνϋμι, όρνύναι,
'to stir up, rouse', L. orior, orlri, 'to rise'. See
orient, and cp. words there referred to.

## arthritic
arthritic, adj., pertaining to arthritis. — L. art-
hrilicus, fr. Gk. αρθριτικός, fr. άρθρΐτις. See
next word and -ic.

## arthritis
arthritis, п., inflammation of a joint (med.) —
Medical L., fr. Gk. άρθρΐτις (scil. νόσος),
'disease of the joints', prop. fem. of the adjective
άρθρίτης, 'pertaining to the joints', fr. άρθρον,
'joint'. See next word and -itis and cp. diar-
throsis, enarthrosis, synarthrosis.

## arthro-
arthro-, before a vowel arthr-, combining form
meaning 'pertaining to the joints'. — Gk.
άρθρο-, άρθρ-, fr. άρθρον, 'joint', which is a
derivative of base *ar-, 'to join'. See arm, 'the
upper limb', and cp. arthritis and words there
referred to. Cp. also article.

## arthrology
arthrology, п., the study of the joints. — Formed
fr. arthro- and Gk. -λογίϋ, fr. -λόγος, 'one who
speaks (in a certain manner); one who deals
(with a certain topic)'. See -logy.

## arthroplasty
arthroplasty, n„ formation of (artificial) joints. —
Formed fr. arthro- and -πλαστίά. See -plasty.

## arthropod
arthropod, adj., pertaining to the Arthropoda;
п., one of the Arthropoda. — See next word.

## Arthropoda
Arthropoda, n. pi., the phylum of invertebrate
animals with jointed limbs (entomol.) — ModL.,
lit. 'those with jointed feet'; coined by the
German anatomist and zoologist Karl Theodor
Ernst von Siebold (1S04-S5) in 1S45 fr. nrthro-
and -poda.

## Arthur
Arthur, п., masc. PN. — ML. Arthurus, Arturus,
fr. W. arth, 'bear', which is rel. to Mir. art, of
s.m. and cogn. with Gk. άρκτος, L. ursus 'bear'.
See arctic and cp. words there referred to.

## artichoke
artichoke, n. — Northern It. articiocco, altered
fr. It. carciofo, fr. Sp. alcarchofa, fr. Arab, al-
karshuf, fr. al-, 'the', and karshuf, 'artichoke'.
F. artichaut, and G. Artischocke are also
borrowed fr. It. articiocco.

## article
article, n. — F., fr. L. articulus, dimin. of artus,
'joint', which is rel. to ars, gen. artis, 'art'. See
art, п., and cp. articular, articulate. For the
ending see suff. -cte.
Derivatives: article, tr. v., arlicl-ed, adj.

## articular
articular, adj. — L. articularis, 'pertaining to the

## joints'
joints', fr. articulus, 'joint'. See prec. word
and -ar.

## Articulate
Articulate, n. pi., a division of animais
comprising invertebrates with jointed limbs (now called
Arthropoda). — ModL., coined by the French
naturalist baron Georges-Leopold-Chretien-
Frfderic-Dagobert Cuvier (1769-1832) fr. L.
articulatus, 'jointed', pp. of articulare. See next
word.

## articulate
articulate, tr. and intr. v. — L. articulatus, pp. of

## articulare
articulare, Чо separate into joints; to utter

## distinctly'
distinctly', fr. articulus, 'joint'. See article and
verbal suff. -ate.
Derivatives: articulat-ed, adj., articulation (q.v.),

## articulat-ive
articulat-ive, adj., articulat-or, п., arliculal-ory,
adj.

## articulate
articulate, Adj. — L. articulatus, pp. of articulare.

See articulate, v.

## articulation
articulation, n. — F., fr. L. articulationem, ace.
of articulatid, 'separation into joints', fr. arfi-
culdtus, pp. of articulare. See articulate, v., and
-ion.

## artifact
artifact, п., anything made by human art (pale-
ont.) — Compounded of L. ars, gen. artis, 'art',
and facere, 'to make, do'. See art and fuct and
cp. next word.

## artifice
artifice, п., ι) skill; 2) trickery. — F., fr. L. arti-
ficium, 'handicraft, skill, ingenuity, dexterity;
craft, cunning, device', fr. artifex, gen. arlificis,
'craftsman', which is formed fr. ars, gen. artis,
'art', and -ficere, fr. facere, 'to make, do'. See
art, п., and fact and cp. artifact. For the change
of Latin й (in fucere) to I (in arti-flc-, the stem
of arti-fex) see abigeat and cp. words there
referred to.
Derivative: artific-er, n.

## artificial
artificial, adj. — L. artificialis, 'pertaining to art*
artificial', fr. artificium. See prec. word and adj.
suff. -al.
Derivatives: artificial, п., artificial-ity, п., arli-
ficialize (q.v.), artificial-ly, adv., artificial-ness, n.

## artillery
artillery, n. — OF. (= F.) artillerie, fr. artillier,
'to provide with engines of war', fr. ML. art!·
cula, 'engine of war', dimin. of L. ars. gen. artis,
'art'. See art, п., and cp. words there referred to.
For sense development cp. engine, fr. L. ingenium,
'nature, disposition, capacity'.
Derivative: artiller-isl, n.

## artinite
artinite, п., a hydrous magnesium carbonate
(mineral.) — Named after the Italian
mineralogist Ettore Artini (1866-1928). For the ending
see subst. suff. -ite.

## Artiodactyla
Artiodactyla, п., an order of mammals (zool.) —
ModL., lit. 'having even-numbered toes', fr. Gk.
άρτιος, 'even', and δάκτυλος, 'finger, toe'. For
the first element see art, for the second see
dactyl.

## artisan
artisan, n. — F., fr. It. artigiano, fr. VL. *arti-
tianus, fr. L. artitus, pp. of artire, 'to instruct
in arts', fr. ars, gen. artis, 'art'. See art. For the
ending cp. partisan.

## artist
artist, n. — F. artiste, fr. It·, artisla, which is
formed fr. L. ars gen. artis, 'art'. See art and -ist.

## artiste
artiste, n. — F. See prec. word.

## artistic
artistic, adj. — F. artistique, fr. artiste. See prec.
word and -ic
Derivative: artistic-al-ly, adv.

## artistry
artistry, n. — Coined by Browning fr. artist and
suff. -ry.

## Arum
Arum, п., a genus of plants; (not cap.) any plant
of this genus (bot.) — L., fr. Gk. άρον, 'the
cuckoopinf, a word of Egyptian origin. See
Plinius, Historia Naturalis, Г9, 96, and cp.
Araceae.

## Aruncus
Aruncus, п., a genus of plants, the goat's beard
(bot.) — L. aruncus (a word used by Pliny), fr.
Gk. ήρυγγος, Dor. ίίρυγγος, 'goatsbeard'. See

## Arundinaria
Arundinaria, п., a genus of bamboo grasses (bot.)
— ModL., fr. L. arundo, gen. -inis, 'reed'. See

## Arundo
Arundo, п., a genus of grasses (bot.) — L. arundd,

агора, adj., without form (Hindu religion). — OI.
arupah, formed fr. priv. pref. a- and rupah,

## ArvaL adj.
ArvaL adj., pertaining to the Fratres Arvales
(Rom. relig.) — L. arvalis, 'pertaining to a

with Gk. άροδν, 'to plow', fipoupa, 'arable land'.

## arvejon
arvejon, п., the chickling vetch. — Sp., fr. arvejo,
'bastard chick-pea', rel. to arveja, 'vetch', fr. L.

## -ary
-ary, adj. suff. meaning 'pertaining to, connected
with', as in arbitrary. — ME. -arie, -arye,
derived fr. L. -artus, fem. -aria, neut. -arium, either
directly or through the medium of OF. -ier,
AF. -er or F. -aire. Cp. adj. suff. -ory.

## -ary
-ary, subst. suff. meaning 'a man belonging to,
or engaged, in something', as in emissary,
notary. — L. -alius, prop, identical with adj. suff.
-drius. See adj. suff. -ary.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:79 COLUMN:3 -->

## -ary
-ary, subst. suff. denoting 'a place for, or
abounding in, something', as in aviary. — L. -arium,
prop. neut. of the adj. suff. -arius, used to form
substantives. See prec. suffixes and cp. -arium,
and -er in the sense 'receptacle for*.

## -ary
-ary, adj. suff., meaning 'pertaining to', as in
exemplary. — L. -arts. The regular English
equivalent of L. -oris is -ar (q.v.)

## Aryan
Aryan, adj. and n. — Formed with suff. -an fr.
OI. iryah, 'noble', which is rel. to OPers. ariya,
'noble' (whence Pers. Iran, 'Persia'). Cp.
Iranian. As a synonym for 'Indo-European' the
term Aryan was introduced by the German
philologist Friederich Max MUller (1823-1900).
Derivatives: Aryan-ism, п., Aryan-ize, tr. v.,
Aryan-iz-ation, n.

## aryballus
aryballus, п., a bottle with a short neck and
globular body (Greek antiq.) — L., fr. Gk. άρόβαλ-
λος, 'bag or purse; globular bottle for
holding oil', prob. a North Balkanic loan word. See
Frisk, GEW., I, p. 156.

## arytenoid
arytenoid, adj., pertaining to two small cartilages
in the larynx (anat.)—Gk. apuTotivosio^.'shaped
like a pitcher', coined by Galen fr. άρύταΐνα,
'a pitcher' and -οειδής, 'like', fr. είδος, 'form,
shape'. The first element is rel. to άρυτήρ,
'ladle', fr. άρύειν (Att. άρύτειν), 'to draw' (water,
wine, etc.) which prob. stands for *f αρύειν, and
is rel. to εύρίσκειν, 'tp find'; see heuristic. For
the second element see -old.
Derivatives: arytenoid, п., arytenoid-al, adj.

## as
as, adv. — ME. as(e), als(e), also, al swa, fr. OE.
ealswa, xlswd, alswa, prop, 'all so', rel. to
MHG. als, dlse, also, 'so, as, than', G. als, 'as,
than*. See also.
Derivatives: as, conj., pron., prep.

## us
us, п., Roman copper coin. — L. as (for *ass),
gen. assis, prob. lit. meaning 'square piece of
metal' (such was the original form of the coin),
and orig. identical with assis, axis, 'plank, disc',
which is rel. to asser, 'pole, stake, post'. See
ashlar and cp. the second element in ambsace.

## as-
as-, assimilated form of ad- before s.

## asafetida
asafetida, asafoetida, n. — A ModL. hybrid
coined fr. asa (fr. Pers. aza, 'mastic') and L.
foetida, fem. of foetidus, 'stinking'. See fetid.

## asana
asana, п., seat; sitting. — OI. asanah, formed
from the stem of aste, 'he sits', which is cogn.
with Hitt. esa, esari, 'he sits', eszi, 'he causes
to sit', Gk. ήμαι, 1 sit'.

## asarabacca
asarabacca, п., the wild ginger (bat.) —
Compounded of L. asarum, 'hazelworf, and bacca,
'berry'. See Asarum and baccl-.

## asaron
asaron, п., a crystalline compound, found
especially in the oils of plants of the genus Asarum.
—Gk. άσαρον, 'hazelworf of uncertain, possibly
Sem. origin. Cp. next word.

## Asarum
Asarum, п., a genus of herbs of the family Aristo-
lochiaceae (bot.) — ModL., fr. L. asarum,
•hazelwort, wild spikenard', fr. Gk. ασαρον.
See asaron.

## asbestine
asbestine, adj., pertaining to asbestos. — L. as-
bestinus, fr. Gk. άσβέστινος, fr. άσβεστος. See
next word and adj. suff. -hie (representing L.
-Inus).

## asbestos
asbestos, n. — L. asbestos, fr. Gk. άσβεστος, lit.
'unquenchable, inextinguishable', fr. ά- (see
priv. pref. a-) and σβεστός, verbal adj. of
σβεννύναι, 'to quench, extinguish', which derives
fr. I.-E. base *gKes-, Чо quench, extinguish',
whence also Lith. gestu, gisli, 'to go out, be
extinguished', OSlav. gaSo, gasiti, of s.m., Hitt.
kishlari, 'is being put out', Toch. A kas-, В kes-,
kus-, 'to go out, be extinguished'.

## nsbollte
nsbollte, п., a mineral containing oxide of cobalt
— Formed with subst. suff. ■*** fr. Gk. άσβάλη,
'soot', which is perhaps rel. to Gk. άζα,
'dryness', άζειν, Чо dry up, parch', and cogn. with

## Goth
Goth, azgo, 'ashes', L. arere (for *uslre), 'to be

## dry'
dry', ardlre, 'to burn'. See ardent and cp. ash,
'powdery substance'.

## Ascaridae
Ascaridae, n. pi., a genus of Nematoda or
threadworms. — ModL., fr. Gk. άσκαρίς, hen. -"8ος,
'worm in the intestines', which is rel. to σκα-
ρίζειν, Att. άσκαρ'ζειν, 'to jump', σκαίρειν, 'to

## skip
skip, dance', σκιρτδν (freq. of σκαίρείν), 'to

leap, bound', σκάρος, 'the parrot fish' (lit. 'the

leaping one'), fr. I.-E; base *sqer-, 'to leap,

## ascend
ascend, tr. and intr. v. — L. ascendere, 'to climb
up, mount', fr. ad- and scandere, 'to climb'. See
scan and cp. descend. For the change of Latin
d (in scandere) to ё (in as-cendere) see accent
and cp. words there referred to.

## ascendance
ascendance, ascendence, n. — Formed fr.
ascendant resp. ascendent, with suff. -ce.

## ascendancy
ascendancy, ascendency, n. — Formed from next
word with suff. -cy.

## ascendant
ascendant, ascendent, n. — F. ascendant (adj. and
п.), fr. L. ascendentem, ace. of ascendins, pres.
part, of ascendere. See ascend and -ancy, resp.
-ency.

## ascension
ascension, n. — F., fr. L. ascinsiunem, ace. of as-
censU, 'ascent', fr. ascensus, pp. of ascendere.
See ascend and -ion and cp. descension.
Derivative: ascenlion-al, adj.

## ascensire
ascensire, adj. — Formed with suff. -Ive fr. L.
ascensus, pp..of ascendere. See ascend and cp.

## ascent
ascent, n. — Formed fr. ascend on analogy of

## ascertain
ascertain, tr. v. — OF. acertener, fr. a, 'to' (see a),

Derivatives: ascerlain-able, adj., ascertain-er, п.,
ascertain-ment, n.

## ascetic
ascetic, adj., self-denying, austere. — Gk.
ασκητικός, 'practiced, laborious, athletic', fr.
ασκητής, 'one who practices any art or trade',
fr. άσκεΐν, 'to form by art, to practice
gymnastics, to practice, exercise', which is of
uncertain origin. The word ascetic was introduced
into English by Sir Thomas Brown (1663-1704).
Derivatives: ascetic, п., ascetic-al-ly, adv.,
ascetic-ism, n.

## asddian
asddian, п., a sea squirt (zoo/.) —Gk. άσκίδιον,
dimin. of ασκός, 'leather bag'. See ascus.

## ascites
ascites, п., accumulation of fluid in the peritoneal
cavity (med.) — Gk. άσκίτης, 'a kind of
dropsy', short for άσκίτης ΰορωψ, lit. 'a baglike
dropsy', fr. ασκός. See ascus.

## Asclepindaceae
Asclepindaceae, n. pi., the milkweed family (hot.)
— ModL., formed fr. next word with suff.
-aceae.

## Asclepias
Asclepias, п., a genus of plants, the milkweed. —
L. asclipias, name of a plant, fr. Gk. άσκληπιάς,
fr. 'Ασκληπιός, name of the god of medicine;
see next word and -ad. Asclepias orig. meant
'the plant dedicated to Asclepius'.

## Asclepius
Asclepius, n„ the god of medicine in Greek
mythology. — Gk. 'Ασκληπιός, of uncertain
origin. Cp. Asclepias, Aescidapian.

## asco-
asco-, combining form meaning 'bladder'. —
Gk. άσκο-, fr. ασκός, 'leather bag, wine skin'.
See ascus.

## ascospore
ascospore, п., a spore formed in an ascus (bot.) —
Compounded of asco- and σπόρος, 'a sowing'.
See spore,

## ascribe
ascribe, tr. v. — L. ascrtbere, 'to add to in a
writing', fr. nd- and scribere, 'to write'. See
scribe.
Derivatives: ascrib-able, adj., ascrib-er, n.

## ascription
ascription, n. — L. ascriptid, gen. -dnis, fr. ascrip-
tus, pp. of ascrtbere. See prec. word and -ion.

## ascus
ascus, п., a sac in certain fungi (bot.) — ModL.,
fr. Gk. ασκός, 'leather bag, wine skin'; of
uncertain origin. It is possibly cogn. with OI.
atkah, 'covering garment'. Cp. ascidian, ascites,
askos.

## Ascyrum
Ascyrum, п., a genus of plants (bot.) — ModL.,
fr. Gk. άσκυρον, 'St. John's wort', which is of
unknown origin.
•ase, suff. denoting enzymes (biochemistry). —
The ending of diastase (q.v.), the first enzyme
isolated, became the regular suffix for forming
nouns denoting enzymes. Cp. -ese.

## aseity
aseity, п., being by itself (philos.) — ML. aseitas,
'state of being by itself, fr. L. a se, 'from, or of,
himself'. See a-, 'from', sui and -ity.

## asepsis
asepsis, п., absence of sepsis (med.) — Medical
L., formed fr. priv. pref. a- and sepsis,

## aseptic
aseptic, adj., pertaining to asepsis, not producing
sepsis (med.) — Formed fr. priv. pref. a- and
σηπτικός, 'putrefactive'. See septic
Derivatives: aseptic-al-ly, adv., aseptic-ism, п.,
aseptic-ize, tr. v.

## aseptol
aseptol, п., an antiseptic preparation (pharm.) —
