bdellium, п., ι) a substance mentioned in the
Bible, Gen. 2:12 and Num. 11:7; 2) a gum
resin. — L., fr. Gk. βδέλλιον, 'a fragrant gum',
fr. Heb. b'dolah.

## be
be, intr. v. — ME. been, beon, fr. OE. blon, 'to
be', rel. to Ыот, OS. bium, OHG. bim, OHG.,
MHG., G. bin, Ί am', and cogn. with L. ful,
*] have been', fueram, Ί had been', fuero, Ί shall
have been', fu-turus, 'about to be', Oscan fust,
'will be', L. fid, Ί become', Gk. φύειν, 'to make
to grow', φύσις, 'nature', Ol. bhavati,
'becomes, happens', bhutah, 'been', bhavitram,
world', bhumih, bhaman-, 'earth, world', Alb.
bttj, Ί dwell, spend the night', bote, 'earth,
world', ban(e), 'dwelling place', OSlav. byti, 'to
be', bylu, 'was', Lith. butt, 'to be', buvo, 'was',
Olr. biu, Ί am', buith, 'to be', boi, 'was', OE.,
OS., OHG. buan, ON. bita, Goth, bauan, 'to
dwell', Dan., Swed. bo, 'to dwell', Lith. bums,
house', bukia, 'dwelling place', Ir. both, 'hut'.
All these words derive fr. I.-E. base "bheu-, "bha-,
'to be, exist, grow'. Cp. bhava, bhumi-devi, blurt,
big, 'to build', bond, 'serf, boor, booth, bound,
adj., bower, 'cottage', bower, 'the knave in
cards', build, busk, 'to prepare', byre, the first
element in bylaw, and the second element in
neighbor. Cp. also fiat, future, phyle, physic,
physio-, -pltyte, and the second element in

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:101 COLUMN:3 -->
dubious, eisteddfod, prabhu, probate, prove, superh,
Symphytum, tribe, tribune, tribute.
be- pref. with transitive or intensifying force. —
OE. be-, toneless form of if (see by); cp. OS. be,
resp. Ы, MHG., G. be-, resp. bei, Goth if,
(used both as a pref. and an adverb; in the
latter case it means 'round about, by'). See by.

## beach
beach, n. — Of uncertain origin.
Derivatives: beach, tr. v., beach-y, adj.

## beacon
beacon, n. — ME. beekne, fr. OE. beacen, becen,
'sign, signal', rel. to OS. bokan, OHG. bouhhan,
MHG. bouchen, OFris. baken [whence MLG.
bake, G. Bake, MDu. baken, Du. baak, baken,
ON. bakn, Dan. bavn, Swed. (fyr)bak], 'beacon',
fr. Teut. "baukna-, which is prob. borrowed fr.
L. bucina, 'a crooked horn or trumpet, signal
horn'; see Kluge-Mitzka, EWDS., p.45 s.v.
Bake. See buccinator and cp. beckon, buoy.
Derivatives: beacon, tr. and intr. v.,beaconage, n.

## bead
bead, n. — ME. bede, 'prayer; prayer bead', fr.
OE. bed, gebed, 'prayer', rel. to OS. beda, gibed,
OHG. beta, 'request', gibet, MHG., G. gebet,
'prayer', Du. bede, 'prayer, request', gebed,
'prayer', G. Bine, 'request, entreaty', Goth, bida,
'prayer, request', OHG., MHG., G. bitten, 'to
ask, request', OHG. beton, MHG., G. beten, 'to
pray', Goth, bidjan, OE. biddan, 'to ask, pray'.
See bid.
Derivatives: bead, tr. and intr. v., bead-ed, adj.,
bead-ing, п., bead-y, adj.

## beadie
beadie, n. — ME. bedel, fr. OF. bedel (F. bedeau),
a Teut. loan word. Cp. OE. bydel, OS. budil,
MLG. bedel, boddel, MDu. buel, Du. beul,
OHG. butil, MHG. butet, G. Biittel, which are
formed fr. OE. biodan, OS. biodan, etc., 'to
announce, proclaim', with agential suff. -el, -il.
See bid and agential suff. -Ie.
Derivatives: beadle-dom, п., beadle-ship, n.

## beagle
beagle, п., a small hound used in hare hunting. —
ME. begle, prob. ft. OF. beegueule, fr. VL.
batata (or badata) gula, 'open throat', fr. fem.
pp. of batare or badare, 'to open,' and gula,
'throat'; so called with reference to its bark.
See bay, 'part in the wall' and gullet.
Derivative: beagl-ing, n.

## beak
beak, n. — ME. bee, fr. OF. (= F.) bee, fr. VL.
beccus (whence a so It. becco) said by Suetonius
(De vita Caesarum, 18) to be of Gaulish origin.
Cp. OE. becca, 'pickax', MHG. bickel, of s.m.,
OHG. bicchan, 'to sting' Cp. also becasse and
the first element in beccafico.
Derivatives: beak-ed, beak-y, adjs.

## beaker
beaker, n. — ME. biker, fr. ON. bikarr, fr. VL.
bicarium [whence also OS. bikeri, OHG. beh-
hari (MHG., G. becher). It. bicchiere], fr. Gk.
βίκος, 'earthen wine vessel'; prob. derived fr.
Syr. buq, 'a two-handled vase or jug', a word of
imitative origin. Cp. Heb. baqbuq, 'bottle' and
see bacbuc. Cp. also pitcher.

## beakjron
beakjron, п., the horn of an anvil; a bickern. —
Folk-etymological alteration of bickern (as if
compounded of beak and iron. See bickiron.

## beam
beam, n. — ME. beem, fr. OE. beam, 'tree, beam,
column of light', rel. to OS. bom, MLG., NLG.
bam, MDu., Du. boom, OHG., MHG. bourn, G.
Baum, 'tree', OFris. bum, 'tree, gallows, beam',
Goth, bagms, OSwed. bagn and prob. also to ON.
badmr, 'tree'; of uncertain etymology. Cp. boom,
'pole', and the first element in bumboat.

## beamish
beamish, adj., beaming. — Coined by Lewis
Carroll (1832-98) fr. beam, in the sense of 'ray of
light', and adj. suff. -ish.

## bean
bean, n. — ME. bene, fr. OE bean, rel. to OS.,
OHG. bona, ON. baun, Dan. балле, Norw.
bauna, Swed. bona, OFris. bane, MLG., MDu.
bone, Du. boon, MHG. bone, G. Bohne; prob.
derived from the child's word bha-, 'something
swelling', whence also Gk. φακός, 'lentil'. Cp.
L. faba, 'bean', OSlav. bobu, Russ. bob, OPruss.
babo, 'bean', which prob. derive from lhe I.-E.
child's word "bhabha, 'bean', reduplication of
*bha-; see Fabaceae.
Derivative: bean, tr. v., to hit on the edge (slang).

## beano
beano, п., beanfeast (slang). — Fr. prec. word.

## bear
bear, п., the animal. — ME. bere, fr. OE. bera,
rel. to MDu. bere, Du. beer, OHG. bero, MHG.
ber, G. Bar, ON. bjorn, lit. 'the brown animal',
fr. I.-E. *bhero-, 'brown', whence also Lith.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:102 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: 75 | BEDOUIN -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:102 COLUMN:1 -->
beras, Lett, ifrs, 'brown', L. fiber, OE. beofor,
'beaver', lit. 'the brown animal'. Cp. beaver, the
animal, and brown. Cp. also the first element in
Bernard.
Derivatives: bear, tr. v., bear-ish, adj., bear-ish-
jiess, n.

## bear
bear, tr. and intr. v., to carry. — ME. beren, fr.
OE. beran, rel. to ON. bera, OFris. bera, Du.
baren, OHG. beran, 'to bear, carry', Goth.
bairan, 'to bear, carry, give birth to', OHG. gi-
beran, MHG. gebern, G. gebaren, Goth, ga-
bairan, 'to give birth to', fr. I.-E. base "bher-,
whence also OI. bharati, 'bears', bharman,
'sustenance, care, burden', Arm. berem, Ί bear,
carry, bring', bern, 'burden', Gk. φέρειν, 'to
bear, carry', φώρ, 'thief, L. ferre, 'to bear,
carry', fur, 'thief, Alb. mbar, bar, Ί carry, drag',
bir, 'son', OSlav. berg, birati (for earlier birti),
'to bring together, collect, take', breme,
'burden', su-boru, 'assembly', Olr. biru, Ί carry',
W. cymeraf, Ί take', Toch. AB par, 'to
bear, bring, fetch', and prob. also Toch. В
prari, 'finger'. Cp. bairn, baron, barrow,
'mountain', barrow, 'handcart', berth, bier, birth, bore,
'tidal wave', borough, burden, 'load', burly. Cp.
also ndiaphoresis, adiaphorous, afferent,
amphora, authropophora, Berenice, bhat, breba,
brehon, cataphora, circumference, confer, cumber,
defer, deference, differ, difference, differentiate,
efferent, -fer, feretory, -ferous, ferret, the animal,
fertile, fortuitous, fortune, furtive, furuncle,
infer, metaphor, offer, opprobrinm, paraphernalia,
periphery, phoradendron, phoresis, Phormium,
-phorous, phosphorous, phosphorus, prefer,
proffer, refer, scirophorion, semaphore, Sobranje,
suffer, transfer, varnish, vernix caseosa,
Veronica, vociferate.
Derivatives: bear-able, adj., bear-er, п.,
bearing, n.

## beard
beard, n. — ME. fr. OE. beard, rel. to OFris. herd,
MDu. baert, Du. board, OHG., MHG. G. ban,
'beard', fr. I.-E. base *bhar-dha, 'beard', whence
also L. barba (assimilated from original *farba,
for *bhardha), OSlav. brada, Russ. boroda,
OPruss. bordus, Lett, barda, Lith. barzda (this
latter was influenced in form by Baltic *barzda,
'furrow'). I.-E. *bhar-dha- prop, means 'bristle'.
Cp. OE. byrsi, 'bristle', and see bristle. Cp. also
barb, 'beard', barbate, barbel, barber, barbet,
barbette, barbicel, barbule and the second
element in halberd, Langobard, lombard.
Derivatives: beard, tr. v., beard-er, п., beard-ing,
п., beard-less, adj., beard-less-ness, п., beard-y,
adj.

## beast
beast, n. — ME. besle, fr. OF. besle (F. bite),
fr. L. beslia, 'beast, wild animal', which is of
uncertain origin. Cp. bestial, bestiary, bicbo, the
first element in becbe-de-mer and the second
element in hartebeest.
Derivatives: beasr-ly, adj. and adv., beast-li-
ness, n.

## beat
beat, tr. and intr. v. — ME. beten, fr. OE. bea-
tan, rel. to ON. bauta, beysia, MLG. bote».
OHG. Ьбззап, MHG. Ьбзеп, 'to beat', and to
the second element in OHG. апаЬоз (whence
MHG. апеЬбз, G. Ambofi), 'anvil', fr. I.-E. base
*bhat-, 'to beat, strike', whence also L. con-
futdre, 'to check, suppress', refutare, 'to repel,
refute', and prob. aisofatuus, 'stupid', lit. struck
silly'. Cp. batter, 'to beat', and words there
referred to. Cp. also baste, 'to beat', beetle,
'mallet', boss, 'protuberance', boterol, boutade, butt,
*to strike', butt, 'the thicker end of anything*.
butt, 'aim', button, and the second element in
ambos.
Derivatives: beat, п., beaten (q.v.), beat-er, п..
beal-ing, n.

## beat
beat, adj., exhausted. — ME. bete, prop, short
form of beten, pp. of beten, 'to beat'. See beat, ν.

## Beata
Beata, fern. PN. — Lit. 'happy', fem. of L.
beatus. See beatitude and cp. Beatrice.

## beaten
beaten, adj., prop. pp. of the verb beat. — ME.
beten, St. OE. beaten, pp. of beatan, 'to beat .
See prec. word.

## beatific
beatific, beatifical, adj., making blessed. — Late
L. beatificus, whence beatificare. See beatify and
-fie, resp. also -al.
Derivatives: beatifical-ly, adv., beatific-ate,\r.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:102 COLUMN:2 -->
v., beatification (q.v.)

## beatification
beatification, п., process of making or becoming
blessed. — F. beatification, fr. beatifier. See
next word and -ation.

## beatify
beatify, tr. v.,— to make blessed;to make happy.
— F. beatifier, 'to beatify', fr. post-classical L.
beatificare, 'to make happy', which is
compounded of L. beatus, 'happy, prosperous', and
-ficare, ir.facere, 'to make, do'. Beatus is prop,
pp. o{ beare, 'to make happy, to bless', which is
prob. rel. to bene, 'well', bonus, 'good'. See
bene-, bonus, and -fy and cp. next word,
beatitude, Beatrice.

## beatille
beatille, п., tidbit, dainties. — F., orig. 'work
done by nuns', fr. beate, fem. of beat, 'blessed,
devout', fr. L. beatus. See beatify.

## beatitude
beatitude, п., blessedness, happiness. — F.
beatitude, fr. L. beatitudinem, ace. of beatitudo,
'happiness, blessedness, coined by Cicero fr. beatus.
See beatify and -ude.

## beatnik
beatnik, п., a person behaving and dressing in an
unconventional manner. — A hybrid coined
from the adj. beat and -nik, a suff. of Yiddish,
ult. Slavic origin (see nudnik).

## Beatrice
Beatrice, fem. PN. — F. Beatrice, fr. L. beatricem,
fem. of beatrix, 'she who makes happy', fr.
beatus, 'happy', prop. pp. of beare, 'to make happy'.
See beatify and cp. Beata.

## beauteous
beauteous, adj., beautiful. — Formed with suff.
-ous fr. OF. beaute (F. beaute). See beauty.

## beaujolais
beaujolais, п., a type of burgundy. — Named
from the Beaujolais district in the department of
the Lyonnais in France.

## beaune
beaune, п., a type of burgundy. — So called fr.
the Beaune district in the department of the
Cote d'Or in France, where it is produced.

## benutiful
benutiful, adj. and n. — A hybrid coined fr.
beauty, a word of French origin, and English full;
first used by Tyndale.
Derivatives: beautiful-ly, adv., beautiful-ness, n.

## beautify
beautify, tr. v. — See beauty and -fy.

## beauty
beauty, n. — ME. bealte, beaute (F. beaute), fr.
L. bellitatem, ace. of bellitas, 'prettiness, charm,
loveliness, beauty', fr. bellus, 'pretty, handsome,
charming, fine, lovely, beautiful', which stands
for *dwenelos, *dwenlos, and is rel. to L. bene,
'well', bonus, earlier *dwenos, 'good', prob. also
to beare, 'to make happy', beatus 'happy' and
cogn. with OI. duvas-, 'gift, honor, respect',
duvas-yati, 'honors, respects'. Cp. bonus, and
words there referred to. Cp. also beatify, bel-
dam(e), belladonna, belle, belles-lettres, Bellis,
belvedere, clarabella, embellish, Christabel, Rosabel,

## beaver
beaver, п., a rodent of the genus Castor. — ME.
bever, fr. OE. beofor, rel. to ON. ton-, OS. bitar,
OHG. bibar, MHG., G. biber, 'beaver', and
cogn. with L. fiber, OSlav. bebru, Lith. bebrus
(also dissimilated into vebrus, debrds), Lett.
bebrs, bebris, OPruss. bebrus, W. befer, Bret.
bieuzr, Avestic bawra, 'beaver'. All these words
lit. denote 'the brown animal'; they derive fr.
I.-E. *bhe-bhru-s, 'very brown', whence also OI.
babhruh, adj., 'brown'; п., 'the larger
ichneumon'. I.-E. *bhe-bhru-s is reduplication of base
'bhero-, 'brown'. Both the bear and the beaver
are called after their color. See bear, п., and
brown.

## beaver
beaver, п., the lower, movable, part of the
helmet.— ME. baviere, fr. OF. baviere, lit. 'a bib',
fr. baver, 'to drivel, slobber', which is of
imitative origin. Cp. bavette.

## beaverite
beaverite, п., a hydrous sulfate of copper, lead,
iron and aluminum (mineral.) — Named after
Beaver County in Utah. For the ending see
subst. suff. -ite.

## becalm
becalm, tr. v. — Formed fr. be- and calm.

## became
became, past tense of become. — See become
and came.

## becasse
becasse, п., the woodcock. — F., formed fr. bee,
'beak', with the augment, suff. -asse. See beak.

## because
because, adv. — ME. Ы cause, fr. Ы, 'by', and
cause, 'cause'. See by and cause.

## beecahco
beecahco, п., any of various migratory birds. —
It., prop, 'fig pecker', compounded of beccare,
'to peck' and fico, 'fig'. It. beccare derives fr.
becco, 'beak', fr. VL. beccus: see benk. It. figo
comes fr. L. ficus; see fig.

## bechamel
bechamel, п., a rich white sauce. — F. bechamel.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:102 COLUMN:3 -->
fr. the name of Louis de Bechamel, a steward
of Louis XIV.

## bechance
bechance, tr. and intr. v. — Formed, fr. be- and
chance.

## beche-de-mer
beche-de-mer, п., sea slug, trepang. — F., altered
fr. Port, bicho-do-mar, lit. "sea worm'. Port, bi-
cho, 'animal, worm', derives fr. VL. bestius,
'animal', whence also Sp. bicho, 'insect'; see
bicho. Port, do, 'of the', is a contraction of de,
'from, of (fr. L. dl, 'from, away from'), and the
masc. def. art. o, fr. earlier lo (fr. L. ilium, ace.
of ilk, 'that'); see de- and ille. Port, mar, 'sea',
derives fr. L. mare, of s.m.; see mare, 'sea'.

## beck
beck, п., sign, nod. — Fr. obsol. beck, v., short-
enend fr. beckon (q.v.)

## beck
beck, п., a vat. — See back, 'vat'.

## beck
beck, п., a small stream, a brook. —· ME. bek,
fr. ON. bekkr, See bache.

## becket
becket, п., a device used for fastening loose ends
of ropes, oars, tackle, etc. (лай/.) — Of uncertain
origin.
Derivative: becket, tr. v.

## beckon
beckon, tr. and intr. v. — ME. beknen, bekenen,
fr. OE. biacnian, 'to mske signs, point out', fr.
beacen, 'a sign'. See beacon.
Derivatives: beckon, п., beckon-ed, п.,
beckoning, п., beckon-ing-ly, adv.

## become
become, intr. and tr. v. — ME. bicumen, becu-
men, fr. OE. becuman, 4o come to, meet with,
happen', rel. to Du. bekomen, MHG. bekomen,
G. bekommen, 'to suit, agree' (in G. said only
of food), Goth, biqiman, 'to come upon one',
and to OE. gecweme, ME. iqueme, queme, OHG.
biquami, MHG. bequseme, G. bequem,
'convenient, fitting, suitable'. See be- and come.

## bed
bed, n. — OE. bedd, bed, rel. to OS. beddi, bed,
ON. bedr, Dan. bed, Swed. badd, MLG., MDu.
bedde, Du. bed, OHG. belli, MHG. belte, bel,
G. Betl, Goth, badi, 'bed', prop, 'a couch dug
into the ground', fr. I.-E. base *bhedh, *bhod-,
'to dig, pierce', whence also Hitt. beda-, 'to
pierce, prick', Gk. βό&υρος, 'pit', L. fodere, 'to dig',
fossa, 'ditch', Lith. badau, badyti, 'to pierce,
prick*, bedd, bisii, 'to dig', Lett, badu, badtl, 'to
pierce, prick', Lith. bidre, Lett, bedu, best, 'to"
dig', bedre, 'pit', OPruss. boadis, 'prick', OSlav.
bodp, bosti, 'to prick', bodlt, 'thorn', W. bedd,
Co. bedh, Bret, bez, 'grave'. G. Beet, 'garden-
bed', is a variant of Betl, 'bed'. Cp. bothrium,
fosse, fossil.

## bed
bed, tr. v. — ME. beddien, bedden, fr. OE. beddian,
'to place in a bed, to bed', fr. bedd, 'bed'. See
bed, n.
Derivatives: bedd-ed, adj. bedd-er, n.

## bedding
bedding, n. — OE., fr. bedd. See bed, η., and subst.
suff. -ing.

## bedeck
bedeck, tr. v. — Formed fr. be- and deck, v.

## bedeguar
bedeguar, bedegar, п., a mossy growth on
rosebushes. — F. bedeguar, bedegar, fr. Pers. bSda-
ward, lit. 'wind rose', fr. bad, 'wind', and ward,
'rose'. The first element is rel. to Avestic νάια-,
'wind', vaiti, 'blows', OI. valah, 'wind', vaiti,
'blows'; see wind, n. For the second element
see rose.

## bedel
bedel, bedell, n. — Variants of beadle.

## bedevil
bedevil, tr. v. — Formed fr. be- and devil.

## bedew
bedew, tr. v. — Formed fr. be- and dew.

## bedight
bedight, v., to adorn. — Formed fr. be- and dight.

## bedikah
bedikah, п., examination, required by Jewish
religious law. — MishnaicHeb.
b*dhiqah,'examination, inspection, search', verbal noun of
bddhdq, 'he examined, tested, scrutinized', fr.
Biblical Hebrew, badhdq, 'he mended, repaired',
which is rel. to Biblical Hebrew bedheq, 'fissure,
rent, breach', Aram, b'dhdq, 'he examined,
explored', bidhqa, 'fissure, rent, breach'.

## bedhn
bedhn, tr. v. — Formed fr. be- and dim.

## bedizen
bedizen, tr. v. — Formed fr. be- and dizen.

## bedlam
bedlam, п., a lunatic asylum. — From Bedlam,
fr. ME. Bedlem, fr. earlier Bethlem, fr. Betle-
hem (q.v.); originally name of a hospital in "Urn-
don, converted later into a lunatic asylum.
Derivatives: bedlam-ism, п., bedbm-ite, п., bed-
lam-ize, tr. v.

## Bedlington terrier
Bedlington terrier, bedlington, n. — From Bed-
lingion, town in Northumberland, England,
where it was first bred.

## Bedouin
Bedouin, n. — F. bedouin, fr. Arab, badawfn, lit.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:103 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: BEDRAGGLE | 76 -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:103 COLUMN:1 -->
'desert dwellers', pi.of badawf,ir.badw (in vulgar
pronunciation bedu), 'camp; desert'. The plural
suff. -in in Arab, badawtn was mistaken for part
of the word. Cp. assassin.

## bedraggle
bedraggle, tr. v. — Formed fr. be- and draggle.

## bedridden
bedridden, adj. — ME. bedrede, fr. OE. bedrida,
lit. 'bed rider' (in contradistinction to a 'horse
rider'), formed fr. bed and ridan, 'to ride'. See
bed, п., and ride.

## bee
bee, n. — ME. bee, fr. OE. Ьёо, rel. to OS.,
OSwed. if, ON. by, Dan., Swed. Ы, MDu. bie,
Du. if/, OHG. bia, OS. bini, OHG. bina, MHG.
bin, G. Biene, fr. I.-E. base *bi-, whence also
OSlav. bKela, Lith. bite, bills, Lett, bile, OPruss.
bitte, 'bee', OW. bydaf, 'beehive'.

## beech
beech, n. — ME. beche, fr. OE. bece, rel. to hoc,
bdc-trio, 'beech tree', OS. bake, ON. bdk, Norw.
bek, Swed. bok, Dan. b0g, MDu. boeke, Du.
beuk, OHG. buohha, MHG. buoche, G. Buche,
and cogn. with Gk. φηγός, 'oak', L. fagus
'beech*, Russ. buzina, 'elder'. Cp. Kurdish buz,
'elm'. Cp. also book, buckwheat. Cp also Fagas
and the first element in Fagopyrum and in
Phegopteris.
Derivatives: beech, beech-en, beech-y, adjs.

## beef
beef, n. — ME. boef, beef, fr. OF. boef, buef(F.
bauf), fr. L. bovem, ace. of bos, *ox'. See boviae
and cp. next word. Cp. also biffin.
Derivatives: beef-ish, adj., beef-ish-ness, п., beef-
y, adj., beef-i-ness, n.

## beefeater
beefeater, n. — Compounded of beef and eater
and lit. meaning 'one who eats another's beef.
For sense development cp. OE. hlaf-xta,
'servant', lit. 'loaf eater'.

## Beelzebub
Beelzebub, п., ι) a Philistine god worshiped at
Ekron; 2) the chief devil. — L., used in the
Vulgate to render Heb. bd'al z'bhubh, god of the
Ekronites (II Kings ι: 2), lit. 'lord of flies', fr.
Heb. bd'al, 'lord' and z'bhubh, 'fly'. See Baal
and zimb.

## been
been, pp. of be. — ME. ben, fr. OE. bion, 'been',
pp. of beon, 'to be', See be.

## beer
beer, n. — OE. beor, rel. to OS., OHG. bior, ON.
iiOTT,OFris.iiar,MLG.,MDu. ier.Du., MHG.,
G. bier, fr. Eccles. L. biber (pi. biberes), 'drink,
beverage', fr. L. bibere, 'to drink'. See beverage.
Derivatives: beer-ish, adj., beerish-ly, adv., beer-
y, adj., beer-i-ly, adv., beer-i-ness, n.

## beestings
beestings, biestings, п., first milk of a cow after
calving. — ME. bestinge, fr. OE. bysting, fr.
bysl, beosl, which is rel. to OS., OHG. biost,
MDu., Du., MHG., G. biest, 'beestings', and in
vowel gradation to Norw. budda (for *buzda),
'beestings', fr. I.-E. base *bhou-, 'bhu-, 'to swell'.
See belly.

## beet
beet, n. — ME. bete, fr. OE. bete, fr. L. beta,
'beet'; which is of Celtic origin. See Ettmayer
in Zeitschrift fur neufranzOsische Sprache und
Literatur, vol.32, pp. 153гг. Ср. Beta.

## beetle
beetle, п., any insect of the order Coleoptera. —
ME. betel, fr. OE. bitula, prop, 'little biter',
formed from the base of bitan, 'to bite', with
suff, -el. See bite and dimin. suff. -le.

## beetle
beetle, п., a heavy wooden mallet. — ME. betylie,
fr. OE. betel, bitel, 'mallet', rel. to LG. hotel,
of s.m., MHG. boejel, 'cudgel'. These words lit.
mean 'beater'. They are formed fr. Teut. base
'haul-, 'to beat, strike', with instrumental suff.
-el, -le. See beat and instrumental suff. -le.
Derivatives: beetle, tr. v., beetl-er, n.

## beetie
beetie, intr. v., to project; adj., projecting. — Of
uncertain origin; possibly rel. to beetle,'insect'.
Cp. next word.

## beetle-browed
beetle-browed, adj. having projecting eyebrows.
— ME. bitelbrowed, compounded of bitel,
'projecting' (see prec. word), and the adj. browed,
which is formed fr. brow with suff. -ed.

## befall
befall, intr. and tr. v. — ME. bifallen, fr. OE.
befeallan, 'to fall into (a habit)', fr. be- and
feallan, 'to fall'. See fall, v.

## befit
befit, tr. v. — Formed fr. be- and the verb fit.
Derivatives: befitt-ing, adj., befitt-ing-ly, adv.,
befitt-ing-ness, n.

## befog
befog, tr. v. — Formed fr. be- and fog.

## befool
befool, tr. v. — ME. befolen, formed fr. be- and
fol, 'fool', See fool.

## before
before, prep. adv. and conj. — ME. before», Ы-
foren, fr. OE. beforan, biforan, fr. be-, 'by' and

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:103 COLUMN:2 -->
adv. foran, 'in front', fr. fore, 'before'. See be-
and fore and cp. former.

## befoul
befoul,.tr. v. — Formed fr. be- and foul.

## befriend
befriend, tr. v. — Formed fr. be- and friend.

## befurred
befurred, adj. — Formed fr. be- and pp. of the
verb fur.

## beg
beg, tr. and intr. v. — ME. beggen, back
formation fr. AF. begger, fr. OF. begard, began,
beggar', fr. MDu. beggaert, 'mendicant'. Cp.
beggar. Cp. also Beguine, biggin, 'cap'.
Derivatives: begg-ing, n. and adj., begg-ing-ly,
adv.

## beg
beg, п., a bey. — The same as bey. Cp. beglerbeg.
and begum.

## began
began, past tense of begin. — ME. began, vr. OE.
begann, fr. beginnan. See begin.

## beget
beget, tr. v. — ME. bigiten, fr. OE. begitan, be-
gietan, 'to get', fr. be- and gitan', rel. to Goth.
bigitan, OHG. pigetfan, 'to get, obtain'. See get.
Derivative: begett-er, n.

## beggar
beggar, n. — ME. beggar, beggere, fr. OF.
begard, began. See beg, v.
Derivatives: beggar, tr. v., beggar-ly, adj., beg-
gnr-li-ness, п., beggar-y, n.

## begin
begin, tr. and intr. v. — ME. beginnen, fr. OE.
beginnan, rel. to OS., OHG. beginnan, MDu. be-
ghinnen, MLG., Du., MHG., G. beginnen, OFris.
bijenna, Goth, du-ginnan, 'to begin', fr. Teut.
*bi-ginnan, fr. bi- (see be) and *ginnan, which
is prob. cogn. with Alb. ζε and zq, 'to touch,
begin'. Cp. gin, 'to begin'.
Derivatives: beginn-er, п., begirm-ing, n.

## begird
begird, tr. v. — ME. begyrden, fr. OE. begyrdan,
fr. be- and gyrdan, 'to gird'. See gird, 'to
encircle'.

## beglerbeg
beglerbeg, п., formerly, governor of a province in
the Ottoman empire. — Turk., lit. 'bey of beys',
fr. begler, pi. of beg, 'bey', and beg, 'bey'. See
bey and cp. beg, п., begum.

## begnaw
begnaw, tr. v. — OE. begnagan, fr. be- and gna-
gan, 'to gnaw'. See gnaw.

## begone
begone, intr. v. and interj. — Prop, two words:
be gone [i.e. the imper. be (see be) and the pp.
of go].

## begonia
begonia, n. — F., named by the botanist Plumier
(1646-1706) after Michel Begon (1638-1710),
governor of Santo Domingo, a patron of
botanical sludy. For the ending see suff. -ia.

## begot
begot, past tense of beget.

## begotten
begotten, pp. of beget.

## begrime
begrime, tr. v. — Of LG. origin; cp. MDu. be-
griemen, begremen. See be- and grime, v.

## begrudge
begrudge, tr. v. — Formed fr. be- and grudge.
Derivative: begrudg-ing-ly, adv.

## beguile
beguile, tr. v. — Formed fr. be- and guile.
Derivatives: beguile-ment, п., beguil-er, п., be-
giiil-ing-iy, adv.

## Beguine
Beguine, п., name of the members of certain lay
sisterhoods founded in the 13th cent. — F.
beguine, prob. fern, of beguin, 'monk, friar', a var.
of begard, fr. MDu. beggaert, 'mendicant'. See
beg, v.

## begum
begum, n. — Turk., a hybrid coined fr. beg and
Arab, umm, 'mother', and orig. meaning
'mother of the bey'. For the first element see bey. The
second element is rel. to Heb. em, Aram.-Syr.
■ em, Elhiop. em, Akkad. ummu, 'mother'.

## begun
begun, pp. of begin.

## behalf
behalf, n. — ME., in the phrase on mibehalfe, 'on
my side', fr. OE. be healfe, 'by the side', fr. be,
'by', and healfe, 'half, part, side'. See be- and
half.

## behave
behave, tr. and intr. v. — ME. behaven, fr. OE.
behabban, 'to restrain', formed fr. be- and hahban,
'to have' (see have). The orig. meaning was 'to
have (oneself) under one's control'.

## behavior
behavior, behaviour, n. — Irregular formation fr.
behave, owing to a confusion with havior,
'possession'.

## behaviorism
behaviorism, n. (psychol.) — Coined by the
American psychologist John Broadus Watson 1878-
1958) in 1913 fr. behavior and suff. -ism.

## behaviorist
behaviorist, n. — See prec. word and -ist.
Derivatives: behaviorist-ic, adj., behaviorist-ic-
al-ly, adv.

## behead
behead, tr. v. — ME. bihefden, biheden, fr. OE.
beheafdian, fr. be- and OE. heafod, 'head'. See
head.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:103 COLUMN:3 -->

## beheld
beheld, past tense and pp. of heboid.

## behemoth
behemoth, п., a huge beast, probably the
hippopotamus. — Heb. behem6th, used in the sense
of a plural of intensity of behemah, 'beast' (see
Job 40:15-24). The assumed connection of Heb.
behemoth with Egypt, p-ehe-mau, 'ox of the
water', was justly rejected by W.Max Miiller.

## behen
behen, п., the plant Centaurea behen. — Arab.
bahman, in vulgar pronunciation behmen, fr.
Pers. bahman, a kind of root resembling a large
radish.

## behest
behest, n. — ME. behest, bihest, fr. OE. behxs,
'promise, vow', fr. behatan. See next word and
cp. hest.

## benight
benight, tr. v., to entrust, commit. — The orig.
meaning was 'to promise, vow'; ME. bihaten.
fr. OE. behatan, 'to promise, vow', fr. be- and
hatan, 'to command'. See flight and cp. prec.
word.

## behind
behind, prep, and adv. — ME. behinden, fr. OE.
behindan, fr. be- and hindan, 'behind'. See hind,
adj.
Derivative: behind, n.

## behold
behold, tr. v. — ME. beholden, fr. OE. behealdatr.
beitaldan, 'to hold by, possess', fr. be- andhealdan.
haldan, 'to hold'. See hold, v.
Derivatives: beholden (q.v.), behold-er, n.

## beholden
beholden, adj. — Prop. pp. of behold, used in its
earlier sense as 'held by, attached to'.

## behoof
behoof, n. — ME. Ье/ю/(сЫеИу in the dat. behove
with the prep, to, 'for the use of), fr. OE. behof.
'profit, benefit, advantage, need', rel. to OFris.,
MLG. behof, Du. behoef MHG. behuof, G.
Behuf, 'benefit, use, advantage', Dan. behov,
Swed. behof, 'need,necessity',and in gradational
relationship to E. have and heave.

## behove
behove, tr. and intr. v. — ME. behoven, fr. OE.
behofian, 'to need, require', fr. behof. See prec.
word.

## beige
beige, п., ι) undyed and unbleached wool fabric;
2) its grayish brown color; adj. grayish brown.
— F., 'of natural color, undyed' (said of wool),
of uncertain origin; not fr. It. bambagia,
'cotton'.

## being
being, n. — Formed fr. be with subst. suff. -ing.

## bejewel
bejewel, tr. v. — Formed fr. be- and jewel.

## bekah
bekah, п., half a shekel. — Heb. beqa', lit.
'fraction, part', from the base of baqa', 'he cleaved,
broke through', which is rel. to Aram. №qa\
Syr. peqd\ of s.m., Mishnaic Heb. paqa', 'split,
sprang off', p'qd'ath, 'coil, ball', Arab, fdqa'a,
vulgar faqa'a, ba'aqa, ba'aja, of s.m., Ethiop.
abqdwa, 'he opened wide his mouth'.

## Bel
Bel, п., the god of the earth in Babylonian my-
ihology. — Akkad. Belu (whence Heb. Bel, Gk.
Βήλος), lit. 'owner, master, lord', rel. to Heb.
Bd'al. See Baal.

## bel
bel, п., a unit for determining in logarithms the
ratios of power. — From the name of Alexander
Graham Bell (1847-1922), the inventor of the
telephone.

## belabor
belabor, belabour, tr. v. — Formed fr. be- and
labor.

## Belamcanda
Belamcanda, п., a genus of plants of the iris
family (pot.) — ModL., of East Indian origin.

## belated
belated, adj. — Formed fr. be-, late and suff. -ed.
Derivatives: belated-ly, adv., belated-ness, n.

## belaud
belaud, tr. v. — Formed fr. be- and laud.

## belay
belay, tr. and intr. v. — ME. beleggen, fr. OE.
belecgan, 'to lay round1, fr. be- and lecgan, 'to
lay'. See lay, v.

## belch
belch, intr. and tr. v., to erect. — ME. belchen,
fr. OE. bealcian, prob. rel. to LG. and Du. bal-
ken, 'to shout, bellow'.
Derivative: belch-er, n.

## belcher
belcher, п., a kind of handkerchief. — Named
after the English prizefighter Jim Belcher
(1781-1811).

## beldam(e)
beldam(e), п., an old woman; esp. a hideous old
woman. — OF. beldame (F. belle dame),
'beautiful lady', formerly used in the sense of
'grandmother'. See beauty and dame and cp.
belladonna.

## beleaguer
beleaguer, tr. v. — Du. belegeren, 'to besiege',
formed fr. pref. be-, which corresponds to E.
be-, and leger, 'bed; camp; army'. See leaguer
and cp. words there referred to.
Derivative: beleaguer-er, п., beleaguer-menl, n.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:104 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: 77 | BENEDICK -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:104 COLUMN:1 -->

## belemnite
belemnite, п., name of a tapering fossil of a
cephalopod resembling the cuttlefishes (paleon-
ιοί.) — Formed with subst. stiff, -ite fr. Gk.
βέλεμνον, 'dart', fr. βέλος, 'dart', which stands
in gradational relationship to βάλλειν, 'to
throw'. Accordingly, belemnite prop, means
'dart-shaped'. See ballistic.

## belfry
belfry, п., a bell tower. — ME. berfray, fr. OF.
berfrei, berfroi (F. beffroi), fr. MHG. bercvrit,
'watchtower', fr. OHG. bergfrid, lit. 'that which
watches over peace', fr. OHG. bergan (whence
MHG., G. bergen), 'to save, cover', and OHG.
fridu (whence MHG. vride, G. Frfeii?),'peace\The
first element is rel. to OE. beorgan, 'to save,
preserve'; see bury. The second element is rel. to
OE. fridu, 'peace'; see free. It. battifredo,
'belfry', is a loan word fr. F. beffroi, but was
influenced in form by an association with It.
battere, 'to strike' (s& batter, v.) E. belfry was
influenced by bell, with which, however, it is not
connected derivatively. Cp. the first element in
frankpledge.

## Belial
Belial, п., ι) worthlessness, wickedness; 2)
Satan. — Heb. b'liyya'al, lit. 'uselessness',
compounded of 64/, 'without', and ya'al, 'use,
usefulness'.

## belie
belie, tr. v. — ME. belien, fr. OE. beliogan, fr.
be- and leogan, 'to lie'. See lie, 'to tell an
untruth'.

## belief
belief, n. — ME. bileafe, formed (with change of
pref. ge- into Ы-) fr. OE. geleafa, 'belief, which
is rel. to OS. gildoO, Du. geloof, OHG. gilouho.
MHG. gehube, gloube, G. Glaube, Goth, ga-
laubeins, 'belief, and to E. lief and love (qq.v.)
Cp. next word.

## believe
believe, tr. and intr. v. — ME. bileven, fr. OE.
belTfan, belefan, rel. to gelyfan, gelefan, OS. gi-
Idbian, Du. geloven, OHG. gilouben, MHG.ff-
louben, glouben, G. glauben, Goth, galaubjan,
'to believe', and to OE. geleafa, 'belief. See
prec. word.
Derivatives: believ-able, adj., believ-er, п., be-
liev-ing, adj., believ-ing-ly, adv.

## belike
belike, adv., probably (archaic). — Formed fr.
be- (in the sense of by) and like.

## belirtie
belirtie, tr. v. — Formed fr. be- and little.

## bell
bell, п., a hollow vessel of metal. — ME. belle,
fr. OE. belle, rel. to MLG., MDu. belle, Du. be/,
ON. bjalla, 'bell', and to OE. bellan, 'to bellow,
cry'. See bellow and cp. next word.
Derivatives: bell, tr. v., to furnish with bells,
bell-ing, n.

## bell
bell, intr. v., to bellow (as the stag in the rutting
season); to roar. — ME. belien, fr. OE. bellan.
See bell, n.
Derivative: bell, п., a bellow (as the cry of the
stag in the rutting season); a roar.

## belladonna
belladonna, п., ι) a poisonous plant; 2) a drug
extracted from this plant. — It. (whence F. bella-
done), lit. 'a beautiful woman', from bella, fern,
of bello (fr. L. bellus), 'beautiful', and donna,
'woman, lady' (fr. L. domino) (see beauty and
dame and cp. beldame); so called in allusion to
the cosmetic once made from it.

## Bellatrix
Bellatrix, п., a star in Orion (aslron.) — L. bella-
trix, 'a female warrior', fern, of bellator, fr.
bellure, 'to wage war', fr. bellum, 'war'. See
bellicose and -trix.

## belle
belle, п., a beautiful woman. — F., adj. used as
a noun, fern, of beau, 'beautiful' fr. L. bellus.
See beau, and cp. embellish.

## Belle
Belle, fern. PN. — Fr. prec. word.

## belleric
belleric, п., the fruit of the plant called Terminalia
bellerica. — F. belleric, fr. Arab, balilaj, in
vulgar pronunciation, belilaj, fr. Pers. balilah.

## Bellerophon
Bellerophon, п., a Greek hero, son of Glaucus
and Eurymede (Greek mytltol.) — L., fr. Gk.
Βελλεροφών, more frequently Βελλεροφόυτης,
which prob. means lit. 'the killer of a demon
called Bellerus', fr. Βέλλερος, 'Bellerus', name
of a demon and -φόντης, 'killer of, fr. φόνος,
'murder'; see defend. The identification of the
first element with a king of Corinth supposedly
called Bellerus is folk etymology.

## belles-lettres
belles-lettres, n. pi., literature. — F., lit. 'fine
letters', fr. belles, pi. of belle, fern, of beau, 'fine,
beautiful', and lettres, pi. of lellre, 'letter . See
beauty and letter.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:104 COLUMN:2 -->

## belletrist
belletrist, п., a student of belles-lettres.—Formed
fr. prec. word with suff. -ist.
Derivative: bellelrist-ic, adj.

## bellicose
bellicose, adj., warlike, hostile. — L. bellicosus,
'warlike', fr. bellicus, 'pertaining to war', fr.
bellum, 'war', fr. OL. dvellum, diiellum, which
is of uncertain origin. Duellum in the sense of
'duel' is Medieval Latin (see duel). Cp. Bellona,
rebel, revel. For the ending see adj. suff. -ose.
Derivatives: bellicose-ly, adv., bellicose-ness, n.

## bellicosity
bellicosity, п., hostility. — See prec. word and -ity.

## bellied
bellied, adj. — Formed fr. belly with suff. -ed.

## belligerency
belligerency, n. — Formed fr. next word with
suff. -cy.

## belligerent
belligerent,adj., i)atwar; 2) warlike; п., aperson
or nation engaged in war. — F. beUigirant, fr.
L. belligerantem, ace. of belligerans, pres. part,
of belligerare, 'to wage war', fr. belliger, 'waging
war', fr. bellum, 'war' and gerere, 'to bear,
carry'. See bellicose and gerent.

## Bellis
Bellis, п., the genus of daisies (hot.) — L., 'daisy*,
prop, 'the handsome flower', formed on
analogy of Greek-nouns ending in -ις fr. L. bellus,
'pretty'. See beauty and cp. words there
referred to.

## Bellona
Bellona, п., the goddess of war in Roman
mythology. — L., fr. OL. Duelldna, fr. duellum, 'war'.
See bellicose. For the suff. -na cp. L. Lato-na
(fr. Dor. Λατώ, Gk. Λητώ) and malrd-na,
'matron' (fr. mater, 'mother'); see Latona, matron.

## bellote
bellote, п., the edible acorn of the holm oak. —
Sp. bellota fr. Arab. Ьа11Щак, in vulgar
pronunciation bellata, 'acorn'.

## bellow
bellow, intr. v., to make a loud noise, to roar. —
ME. beh/en, fr. OE. bylgian, rel. to OE. bellan,
'to bellow', MDu. belien, OHG. bellan, MHG.,
G. belien, 'to bark' and E. bell, 'to bellow'; fr.
I.-E. base *bhel-, 'to make a loud noise, to
sound, ring, roar', whence also OI. bhasd-,
'barking', bhasate, 'speaks, talks'. Cp. bawl,
bell, 'metallic vessel', boulder, the first element
in balderdash and in poltergeist, and the second
element in dubash.
Derivatives: bellow, п., bellow-er, n.

## bellows
bellows, n. pi. — ME. bely; prop, a variant of
belly (q.v.)

## belly
belly,n. — ME. bait, bely, fr. OE. bselg, belig, belg,
'bag, belly, bellows', related to ON. belgr, 'bag,
bellows', Swed. balg, 'belly, bellows', Du. balg,
'belly', OHG. balg, MHG. bale, G. Balg,
'bellows', Goth, balgs, 'wineskin', OE. -belg (in
beanbelg, 'bean pod'), OHG. belgan, 'to swell',
ON. bylgja, 'billow', bolstr [for *bul(h)stra],
'bolster', lit. 'something swelled', fr. Teut. base
*belg-, which corresponds to I.-E. base 'bhelgh-,
'to swell', whence OPruss. balsinis (for *bhol-
ghi-nos), 'cushion', Lett, pabalsts, 'pillow',
Serbo-Croat, blaiina (for 'bolzina), 'pillow',
Olr. bolgaim, Ί swell', bolg, 'bag', W. bol, bola,
boly, 'belly', Bret, bolc'h, 'flax pod'. (L. bulga,
'leather knapsack', is a Gaulish loan word.) Cp.
bellows, bilge, billow, bolster, budge, 'fur',
budget, bulge. Base 'bhelgh-, is an enlargement of
base *bhel-, 'to swell'. See bull, 'male of the ox",
and cp. words there referred to.
Derivatives: belly, intr. v., belly-er, п., belly-ful,
adj.

## belong
belong, intr. v. — ME. belongen, fr. longen, 'to
concern', fr. long, long, fr. OE. gelang, 'at hand,
attainable, dependent on', which is rel. to MDu.
belanghen, Du. belangen, G. belangen, 'to
concern; to belong to' (whence Du. belong, resp.
G. Belong, 'concern, interest, importance'), and
to OE. long, etc., 'long'. The orig. meaning of
the above verbs prob. was 'to be alongside of.
See long, adj., and cp. aloag.
Derivatives: belong-er, п., belong-ings, n. pi.

## Belostoma
Belostoma, п., a genus of aquatic bugs (zool.) —
ModL., lit. 'arrow-mouthed', fr. Gk. βέλος,
'arrow, dart', and στόμα, 'mouth'. The first
element stands in gradational relationship to
βάλλειν, 'to throw'; see ballistic. For the
second element see stoma.

## belove
belove, tr. v.; now only in the passive. — ME.
biluven, formed fr. Ы- and luven, 'to love'. See
be- and love, v.

## beloved
beloved, adj. — Prop. pp. of belove.

## below
below, adv. and prep. — Formed fr. be- and the

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:104 COLUMN:3 -->
adj. low.

## Belshazzar
Belshazzar, п., the last Chaldaean king of
Babylon (Bible). — Heb. Behhatztzar, contraction
of Akkad. Bil-shar-usur i.e. 'Bel, protect the
king'.
belt, n. — ME., fr. OE., rel. to ON. belli, OHG.
balz, fr. L. balteus, 'girdle', a word of Etruscan
origin. Cp. balteus, baldric, bauson, bausond,
bauxite.
Derivative: belt, tr. v.

## Beltane
Beltane, п., an ancient Celtic festival on May
Day. — Gael, bealtuinn, a compound lit.
meaning 'blazing fire'. For the first element see
balefire. The second element is rel. to Olr. ten, 'fire'
(for I.-E. *tepnos), and cogn. with L. lepere, 'to
be lukewarm', tepidus, 'lukewarm'. See tepid
and cp. words there referred to.

## beluga
beluga, п., a kind of dolphin. — Russ. beluga, fr.
billy, 'white', which is rel. to OSlav. be~lu, 'white',
Lith. baltas, 'white', Lett, bals, 'pale', and cogn.
with OE. b£l, 'a blazing fire', ON. bal, 'a great
fire'. See balefire and cp. the first element in
Beltane.

## belvedere
belvedere, п., a turret, giving a fine view; a sum-
merhouse. — It., lit. 'a beautiful sight', fr. bello,
bel, 'beautiful, fine', and vedere, fr. L. vidire, 'to
see'. See beanty and vision,

## bema
bema, п., platform, stage (Greek antiq.) — Gk.
βήμα, 'step, platform', from the stemof βαίνειν,
'to go', whence also βάσις, 'a stepping, pedestal,
foot, base'·. See base, n.

## bemonn
bemonn, tr. v. — ME. bimenen, fr. OE. ЬетШпап,
'to lament', fr. be- and msenan, 4o moan'.
See moan,

## bemuse
bemuse, tr. v. — Formed fr. be- and muse.
Derivative: bemus-ed, adj.

## bea
bea, adv., within (Scot.) — OE. binnan (rel. to
OFris. binna, MDu., Du., MHG., G. binneri),
'within'; contraction of bi-innan, be-innan. See
be- and in, prep.

## ben
ben, п., the inner room (Scot.) — From prec.
word.

## ben
ben, п., son. — Heb. ben, 'son', rel. to Arab, ibn,
Aram.-Syr. bar, 'son', Akkad. binbinni,
'grandson'. Cp. Benjamin, B'nai B'rith, boanerges. Cp.
also Barabbas, bar mitzvah, Barnabas,
Bartholomew. For the feminine correspondences Heb.
bath, 'daughter', etc., see hathkol and cp.
Batbsheba.

## Ben
Ben, masc. PN. — Dimin. of Benjamin (q.v.)

## bench
bench, n. — ME., fr. OE. bene, rel. to ON. bekkr,
Dan., Swed. bank, OS., OFris., MLG., Du.,
OHG., G. bank, MHG. banc, 'bench', ON.
bakki, 'elevation'. Cp. bauk, banket, bankrupt,
banquet, charabanc, mountebank, saltimbanco.
Derivatives: bench, tr. and intr. v., bench-ing, n.

## bencher
bencher, п., any of the members of the Inns of
Court. — Formed fr. bench with agential suff.
-er. Cp. disbench.

## bend
bend, tr. and intr. v. — ME. benden, fr. OE.
bendan, 'to stretch a bow; to bend, bind', rel.
to bind (q.v.) Cp. next word and bent
Derivatives: bend, n. (q.v.), bend-ed, adj., bend-er, n.

## bend
bend, п., a knot. — Orig. meaning 'band, bond',
fr. OE. bend, fr. bendan (see bend, v.); prop, a
variant of band, 'a tie' (q.v.)

## bend
bend, п., a diagonal bend (her.) — OF. bende,
bande, 'a bend', a Teut. loan word. See band,
'a tie', and cp. prec. word.

## bendy
bendy, adj., divided by bends (her.) — OF. bende,
bande (F. bande). See bead (her.) and -y
(representing OF. -e, F. -έ).

## bene-
bene-, combining form meaning 'well'. — L. bene,
'well', fr. earlier *dwene, rel. to bonus, earlier
*dwenos, 'good', bellus, earlier 'dwenelos, *dwen-
los, 'beautiful'. See bonus, beauty,

## beneath
beneath, prep, and adv. — ME. benelhe, bene-
olhen, fr. OE. beneopan, fr. be-, 'by', and neopan,
'below, beneath'. See be- and nether and cp.
underneath.

## Benedicite
Benedicite, п., the canticle beginning with the
words 'Benedicite, omnia opera Domini,
Domino' (in English Ό all ye works of the Lord,
bless ye the Lord'). — PI. imper. of benedicere,

## pp. benedict us
pp. benedict us, 'to bless'. See benediction.

## Benedick
Benedick, п., a confirmed bachelor who marries.
— From a character in Shakespeare's Much Ado
About Nothing. For the origin and meaning of

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:105 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: BENEDICT | 78 -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:105 COLUMN:1 -->
the name see benediction.

## Benedict
Benedict, п., masc. PN. — L. benedictus, 'blessed',
pp. of benedicere. See benediction.

## Benedicts
Benedicts, fem. PN. — L. benedicta, fem. of
benedictus, 'blessed'. See prec. word.

## Benedictine
Benedictine, п., a monk of the order founded
in 529 by St. Benedict. — F. benedictin,
fr. Eccles. L. benediclinus, fr. Benedictus (= St.
Benedict), name of the founder of this order,

## benediction
benediction, n. — L. benedictio, gen. -onis, fr.
benedictus, pp. of benedicere, 'to bless', lit. 'to
speak well of, to praise', fr. bene, 'well', and
dicere, 'to say, tell'. See bene- and diction and
cp. benison, which is a doublet of benediction.
Cp. also bennet, bensh.

## benedictory
benedictory, adj., pertaining to a blessing. — ML.
benedictdrius, fr. L. benedictus, pp. oibenedicere.
See prec. word and adj. surf. -ory.

## benefaction
benefaction, п., a good deed, donation. — L.
bene/actio, gen. -onis, fr. bene/actus, better
written in two words bene/actus, fr. bene, 'well', and
/actus, pp. of /acere, 'to make, do'. See bene-
and faction and cp. benefit.

## benefactor
benefactor, п., one who confers a benefit. — L.,
'who performs an act of kindness', fr. bene-
facius. See prec. word and factor.

## benefactress
benefactress, n. — See prec. word and -ess.

## benefice
benefice, п., a church living. — F. benefice, fr. L.
beneficium, 'generosity, kindness, benefit', fr.
beneficus, 'generous, kind, beneficent, obliging',
which is formed fr. bene, 'well' and -ficus, from
the stem of -ficere, unstressed form of /acere,
'to make, do'. See bene- and fact.
Derivative: benefic-ed, adj.

## beneficence
beneficence, п., the quality of being beneficent,
kind, charitable. — Either fr. F. beneficence or
directly fr. L. beneficentia, 'kindness, generosity,
beneficence', back formation fr. beneficentior.
See next word and -ce.

## beneficent
beneficent, adj., doing good, kind, charitable. —
Back formation fr. L. beneficentior, compar. of
beneficus. See benefice and -ent.
Derivative: beneficent-ly, adv.

## beneficial
beneficial, adj., helpful, advantageous. — F.
beneficial, fr. L. beneficidlis, 'pertaining to a favor',
fr. beneficium. See benefice and -ial.
Derivatives: beneficial-ly, adv., beneficial-ness, n.

## benefieiary
benefieiary, п., one who receives benefits. — L.
beneficiarius, 'enjoying a favor, privileged', fr.
beneficium. See benefice and subst. surf. -ary.

## benefit
benefit, n. — ME. bene/et, ben/et, fr. AF. ben/et
(rel. to OF. and F. bien/ait), fr. L. bene/actum,
bene /actum, 'well done'. See benefaction.
Derivatives: benefit, tr. and intr. v., benefit-er,n.

## benevolence
benevolence, п., kindliness. — OF. benivolence,
fr. L. benevolentia, 'good will, kindness', fr.
benevolens, gen. -entis. See next word and -ce.

## benevolent
benevolent, adj. wishing 10 do good, kindly. —
OF. benevolent, fr. L. benevolens, gen. -entis,
'wishing well, benevolent', fr. bene, 'well', and
volens, gen. -entis, pres. part, of void, velle, 'to
will, wish'. See voluntary and -ent and cp.
malevolent
Derivative: benevolent-ly, adv.

## benight
benight, tr. v. (rare) — Formed fr. be- and night.
Derivative: benight-ed, adj.

## benign
benign, adj., kindly. — ME. benigne, fr. OF. be-
nigne (F. benin, fem. benigne), fr. L. benignus,
'kindly, kindhearted, friendly', orig. 'of good
nature', compounded of bene, 'well' and *gno-s
'born, of a certain nature', fr. I.-E. base gn-,
10 beget, bear, bring forth', whence also L.
gignere, 'to beget, bear, bring forth', W. gent,
'to be born'. See bene- and genus and cp. malign.
Derivative: benign-ly, adv.

## benignant
benignant, adj., kindly. — Formed fr. benign on
analogy of malignant. For the ending see suff.
-ant.
Derivative: benignant-ly, adv.

## benignity
benignity, п., kindliness. — ME. benignite, fr. OF.
benignite, fr. L. benignitatem, ace. of benignitds,
fr. benignus. See benign and -ity.

## benison
benison, п., blessing, benediction. — ME., fr. OF.
beneison, fr. L. benedictionem, ace. of benedictio.
See benediction.

## benitoite
benitoite, п., a barium titanosilicate (mineral.) —
Named after San Benito River in California.
For the ending see subst. suff. -ite.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:105 COLUMN:2 -->

## Benjamin
Benjamin, masc. PN.; in the Bible, Jacob's
youngest son. — Heb. Binyamin, lit. 'son of the right
hand', fr. ben 'son', and yamtn, 'right hand';
see Gen. 35:18. For the first element see ben,
'son'. Heb. yamtn means also 'south' (lit. 'the
right hand, the right side', i.e., if one faces east).
It is rel. to Aram.-Syr. yammin, Ugar. ymn,
'right hand', Arab, yaman, 'right hand, right
side, south', ydmana, 'he was happy', lit. 'he
turned or went to the right' (the right side was
regarded as auspicious), Ethiop. yaman, Akkad.
imnu, 'right hand, right side'. Cp. Yemen, mai-
mon, monkey.

## benjamin
benjamin, п., gum benzoin. — Corruption of ben-
join, an earlier form of benzoin (q.v.)

## bennet
bennet, п., a herb. — ME. berbe beneit, 'the
blessed herb', fr. F. benode, prop. fem. pp. of OF.
beneir (F. benir), 'to bless', fr. L. benedicere.
See benediction.

## bensh
bensh, tr. and intr. v., to bless; to say grace. —·
Yiddish benshen, fr. dial. OF. "bencheir (OF.
beneir, F. benir), fr. L. benedicere. See benediction.

## bent
bent, adj., curved. — Pp. of bend.

## bent
bent, п., inclination. — Fr. prec. word.

## bent grass
bent grass, also bent, n. — OE. beonot- (in place
names), rel, to OS. binut, OHG. Ыпиз, MHG.
bin(e)3, bins, 'rush'. G. Binse developed fr. early
MHG. bimz(e), pi. of MHG. Ып(е)з.

## Beathamism
Beathamism, п., utilitarianism, as taught by
Bentham (philos.) — Named after Jeremy Bent-
Лот (1748-1832), founder of the English
Utilitarian School of Philosophy. For the ending
see suff. -ism.

## Benthamite
Benthamite, п., a follower of Bentham. — See
prec. word and subst. suff. -ite.

## benthos
benthos, п., the fauna and flora of the bottom of
lhe sea. — Gk. βένθος, 'depth of the sea', prob.
rel. to βά&ος, 'depth', but influenced in form
by πένΰ-ος, 'grief. See bathos.

## bentonite
bentonite, п., a porous clayey mineral. — Named
after Fort Benton in Wyoming, U.S.A. For the
ending see subst. suff. -ite.

## benumb
benumb, tr. v. — ME. binomen, pp. of biniman,
fr. OE. beniman, 'to deprive', lit., 'to take away',
formed fr. be- and niman, 'to take'. See nimble,
numb.
Derivatives: benumb-ed, adj., benumb-ed-ness,
n„ benumb-ing, adj., benumb-ing-ly, adv.

## benz-
benz-, form of benzo- before a vowel.

## benzene
benzene, n. — Fr. Benzin, a name coined by the
German chemist Eilhardt Mitscherlich (1794-
1863) in 1833; so called by him because he
obtained it through the distillation of benzoic acid
with lime. The spelling benzene is due to A. W.
Hofmann. See benzoin.

## benzine
benzine, benzin, п., a volatile, inflammable liquid.
— See benzene and chem. suff. -ine, -in.

## benzo-
benzo-, before a vowel benz-, combining form
meaning 'relating to benzene'. — See benzene.

## benzoic
benzoic, adj., pertaining to benzoin. — See
benzoin and -ic.

## benzoin
benzoin, п., a balsamic resin. — F. benjoin, fr.
Sp. benjui, which is shortened fr. lo-benjui (the
first syllable having been mistaken for the def.
article), fr. Arab, luban jawt, 'frankincense of
Java' (Java is the former name of Sumatra).
For the etymology of Arabic luban see leban.

## benzol
benzol, п., benzene. — Altered fr. Benzin by the
German chemist Baron Justus von Liebig (1803-
73) in 1834. — See benzene and -ol (representing
L. oleum, 'oil').

## benzoyl
benzoyl, п., a univalent radical, C6H5CO, found
in benzoic acid. — Coined by the German
chemists Baron Justus von Liebig (1803-73) and
Friedrich Wohler (1800-82) fr. benzo- and -yl.

## bepaint
bepaint, tr. v. — Formed fr. pref. be- and paint.

## beplaster
beplaster, tr. v. — Formed fr. pref. be- and
plaster.

## bepowder
bepowder, tr. v. — Formed fr. pref. be- and
powder.

## bequeathe
bequeathe, tr. v. — ME. biquethen, fr. OE.
becwepan, 'to say, bequeathe', which is formed
fr. pref. be- and cwepan, 'to say'. See quoth and
cp. next word.
Derivatives: bequetb-al, п., bequeath-er, n.

## bequest
bequest, n. — ME. biqueste, a blend of ME. Ы-
quide and queste (see quest). ME. biquide is
formed fr. pref. Ы- (see be-) and OE. cwide,

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:105 COLUMN:3 -->
'a saying, declaration', which is rel. to OE.
cwepan, 'to say'. See quoth and cp. prec. word.

## berakah
berakah, п., blessing, benediction. — Heb.
¥rakhdh, 'blessing', from the stem of berdkh,
'he blessed', which is rel. to Aram, bdrekh,
Arab, bdraka, Ethiop. bardka, 'he blessed',
Akkad. kar&bu (a metathesis form), 'to bless',
Ethiop. mekrab (metath.), 'temple'. Cp. cherub,
griffin.

## Berber
Berber, n. — Arab, bdrbar, 'the people of Bar-
bary', perhaps derived fr. Gk. βάρβαρος, 'bar-
bar' (see barbaric).

## Berberidaceae
Berberidaceae, n. pi., the barberry family (hot.)
— Formed fr. Berberis with suff. -aceae.

## berberidaceous
berberidaceous, adj. — See prec. word and
-aceous.

## Berberis
Berberis, п., a genus of plants, the barberry (hot.)
— ML. berberis, barbaris,- 'barberry', fr. Arab.
barbaris, in vulgar pronunciation berberis,
'barberry'. Cp. barberry.

## berceau
berceau, п., cradle; bower. — F., 'cradle', fr.
bercer, 'to rock' (cp. OProvenc. bresar, Catal.
bressar), from the Gaulish base *berta-, 'to
shake'. Cp. Ir. bertaim, Ί shake'.

## bercense
bercense, п., a cradlesong. — F., 'a woman who
rocks an infant; cradlesong', fr. bercer, 'to
rock'. See prec. word.

## Berchemia
Berchemia, a genus of vines of the buckthorn
family (bot.) — ModL., named after M. Berchem,
a French botanist of the 17th century. For the
ending see suff. -ia.

## bereave
bereave, tr. v. — ME. bereven, fr. OE. bereafian,
fr. pref. be- and reafian, 'to plunder, ravage'. See
reave.
Derivatives: bereav-ed, adj., bereave-ment, n.
bereav-ed, n.

## bereft
bereft, adj. — Prop. pp. of bereave.

## berengelite
berengelite, п., a resinous material. — Named
after San Juan de Berengela, a province of Peru.
For the ending see subst. suff. -ite.

## berengena
berengena, п., the eggplant. — Sp., fr. Arab.
badinjan (in vulgar pronunciation bedinjen), ult.
fr. Persian. See aubergine.

## Berenice
Berenice, fem. PN. — L. Berenice, fr. Βερενίκη,
Macedonian var. of Gk. Φερενίκη, lit. 'bringer
of victory', fr. φέρειν, 'to bring', and νίκη,
'victory'. See bear, 'to carry', and Nike, and cp.
Veronica. Cp. also vnrnish,

## Bereshith
Bereshith, п., I) the creation; 2) the first book of
lhe Pentateuch (= Gk. Genesis, lit. 'origin'). —
Heb. B'reshhh, shortened fr. Sepher ma'dse^
b'rishith, 'the Book of the creation'. Since
b'reshhh happens lo be the first word of the
Pentateuch, it was erroneously assumed that
the first book of the Pentateuch was called
Bereshith from the first word of its Hebrew
text. This erroneous belief gave rise to the
custom of naming Hebrew books (also the other
four books of the Pentateuch) from initial
words of the text. — Heb. bereshith lit. means
'in the beginning'. It is formed fr. pref. b*-, 'in',
and reshtth, (for *re'eshtth), 'beginning', a
derivative of rosh, 'head', which is rel. to Aram.
rgsh, Akkad. reshu, Arab, ra's, Ethiop. res,
'head'. Cp. race, 'tribe', rais, reis, resh, Rosh
Hodesh, Rosh Hashanah.

## beret
beret, п., a flat round cap. — F. beret,
occasionally written also berret, fr. berret, a word of the
dialect of Beam, fr. Old Gascon berret, 'cap',
fr. Late L. birrus, also birrum, 'large cloak with
a hood'. See biretta and cp. barret, burnous.

## bergamot
bergamot, п., the tree Citrus bergamia. — Fr.
Bergamo, a city in Lombardy, Italy.

## bergamot
bergamot, п., kind of pear. — F. bergamot, fr. It.
bergamotta, fr. Turk, beg armudi, lit. 'pear of
a bey', influenced in form by the Italian place-
name Bergamo. See bey.

## bergander
bergander, п., sheldrake (obsol.) — Prob. a blend
of Du. bergeend, 'sheldrake', lit. 'mounlain
duck' (see barrow, 'mountain', and Anas), and
E. gander. Cp. goosander.

## berger
berger, п., a long curl hanging down from the
nape of the neck to the shoulder. — F. bergire,
'shepherdess; style of dressing the hair', fem. of
berger, 'shepherd', fr. VL. berbicarius,
'shepherd', fr. berbe», corresponding to L. vervex,
'wether', which is cogn. with Homeric and Ion.
Gk. εΐρος, 'wool', which stands for "ίρΓος, dis-

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:106 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: 79 | BETHEL -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:106 COLUMN:1 -->
similated fr. *f£pfoi. See erio- and cp. nevt
word,

## bergere
bergere, η., ι) a shepherdess; 2) a style of sofa;
a style of armchair (both in vogue iu the i8th
century. — F., 'shepherdess; a large and deep
armchair'. See prec. word

## beri-beri
beri-beri, п., a disease characterized by wasting.
— From intensifying reduplication of
Singhalese beri, 'weakness'.

## berith
berith, η , circumcision of the male child (Jewish
religion). — Heb. b'rith, 'covenant', rel. to Ak-
kad. baru, 'to bind' (whence biriiu, 'fetter,
covenant'. Cp. B'nai B'rith. Beriih in the above
sense is the abbreviation of berith milah,
'covenant of the circumcision', so called in allusion
to Gen. 17: loff. andtoMishnahNedarim,3:H.

## Berkeleian
Berkeleian, adj., pertaining to George Berkeley
or his philosophy. See next word and -ian.

## Berkeleianism
Berkeleianism, n. — The idealistic system of
philosophy taught by George Berkeley (1685-
1753). For the ending see suff. -ism.

## berkelium
berkelium, п., a radioactive element (chem.) —
ModL., named after Berkeley in California,
where it was discovered. For the ending see suff.
-ium.

## berlin
berlin, п., a kind of four-wheeled carriage. —
F. berllne, named after Berlin, Germany,
whence this kind of carriage was imponed
into France in the second half of the 17th
and in the first half of the 18th century.

## berllne
berllne, also berlin, п., an automobile body with
a glass partition at the rear of the driver's seal.
— F. berline. See prec. word.

## berlinite
berlinite, п., a hydrous aluminum phosphate
(mineral.)—Named after N. H. Berlin, Professor
of the University of Lund. For the ending see
subst.'suff. -ite.

## berloque
berloque, brcloque, п., a drumbeat. — F., a word
of imitative origin.

## berm
berm, also berme, п., a narrow ledge. — F. berme,
fr. Du. berm, fr. MDu. baerm, which is rel. to
ON. barmr, 'brim', fr. I.-E. base "bher-, 'edge,
point; to bore, pierce'. Cp. the related base
*bhre-m-, of s.m., whence E. brim (q.v.)

## Bernard
Bernard, masc. PN. — F., fr. G. Bernhard, lit.
'bold as a bear', fr. OHG. bero, 'bear', and
harti, 'hard, bold'. See bear, the animal, and
hard.

## berrugate
berrugate, п., the fish called scientifically Verru-
galo pacificus. — Fr. Sp. verruga, 'wart', fr. L.
verruca. See verruca and cp. words there
referred to.

## berry
berry, n. — ME. bene, fr. OE. berige, berie, rel.
to OS., OHG. beri, ON. ber, Dan. bser, Swed.
bar, MHG. ber, G. Beere, Goth, basi (in weina-
basi 'grape), Du. bes, bezie, 'berry', and prob.
to OE. basu, 'purple', and cogn. with Mir. base,
'red'. Cp. anbury.
Derivatives: berry, intr. v., berri-ed, adj., ber-
ri-er, n.

## bersagliere
bersagliere, n. any of a corps of riflemen in the
Italian army. — It., 'sharpshooter', fr. bersaglio,
'mark', rel. to OF. berser, 'to shoot with the
bow', bersail, bersage, 'target'; of uncertain
origin.

## berserker
berserker, п., a Norse warrior. —· ON. berserkr,
a word lit. meaning 'bear's skin', and referring
to the warrior's garments. For the first element
see bear, the animal, for the second see sark.

## Berteroa
Berteroa, п., a genus of plants of the mustard
family (hot.) — ModL., named after the Italian
botanist Carlo Giuseppe Bertero (1789-1831).

## berth
berth, n. — The orig. meaning of this word was
'convenient sea room'. 11 is formed with subst.
suff. -th from the stem of the verb bear, hence
derivalively identical with birth.
Derivatives: berth, tr. v., berth-er, п.,
berthing, n.

## Bertha
Bertha, fern. PN. — G., fr. OHG. Berahta, Pe-
rahta, name of a female deity, lit. 'the bright
one', fr. OHG. beraht, 'bright,' which is related
to OE. beorht, 'bright'. See bright.

## bertba
bertba, п., a kind of broad collar. — From
Bertha, a woman's name.

## Bertillon system
Bertillon system, a system of anthropometry as
a means of identifying persons. — Named after
ils inventor Alphonse Bertillon, a French
anthropologist and criminologist (1853-1914).

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:106 COLUMN:2 -->

## Bertram
Bertram, masc. PN. — OHG. Berahtram, lit. 'a
bright raven', fr. beraht, 'bright', and hram, a
collateral form oihraban, 'raven'. See bright and
raven and cp. the second element in Ingram,

## bertrandite
bertrandite, п., a beryllium silicate (mineral.) —
Named after the French mineralogist H.Ber-
trand, who first analyzed it. For the ending see
subst. suff. -ite.

## Berula
Berula, п., a genus of plants of the parsley family
(bot.) — L. berula, 'water cress', dissimilated fr.
*beruva, a word of Celtic origin. Cp. W. berwr,
Mir. biror, bilor, 'water cress'.

## beryl
beryl, n. — ME., fr. OF. beryl (F. beryl), fr. L.
beryllus, fr. Gk. βήρυλλος, fr. Prakrit veruliya,
transposed fr. veluriya (whence OI. vaidurya-),
which prob. derives from the name of the city
Velur (now called Belur). Cp. G. Brille,
'spectacles', from the pi. of MHG. bril, of s.m., which
derives fr. MHG. berille, 'beryl', fr. L.
beryllus (the first spectacles were made from beryl).
Cp. also brilliant, the first element in besiclo-
meter and the second element in chrysoberyl.

## beryllium
beryllium, п., a metallic element, called also
glucinum (chem.) — ModL., fr. L. beryllus (see
beryl); so called because it was' first obtained
through isolation from beryl (by the French
chemist Nicolas-Louis Vauquelin in 1797). For
the ending see suff. -ium.

## berzelianite
berzelianite, п., copper selenide (mineral.) —
Named after the Swedish chemist Baron J6ns
Jakob Berzelius (1779-1848), who first analyzed
it. For the ending see subst. suff. -ite.

## berzelite
berzelite, п., arsenate of calcium, magnesium and
manganese (mineral.) — Named after the Swed-
dish chemist Baron J6ns Jakob Berzelius (1779-
1848). For the ending see subst. suff. -ite.

## bescreea
bescreea, tr. v. — Formed fr. be- and screen.

## beseech
beseech, trans, v. — ME. besechen, fr. be-, and
sechen, seken, 'to seek'. See seek and cp. G.
besuchen, 'to visit' (fr. be- and suchen, the
equivalent of E. seek).
Derivatives: beseech-ing, adj., beseech-ing-ly,
adv.

## beseem
beseem, impers. v. — Formed fr. be- and seem.

## beset
beset, tr. v. — ME. besetten, fr. OE. besettan, 'to
set on, adorn', rel. to Du. bezetten, OHG. bi-
sazjan, G. besetzen, Goth, bisatjan. See be- and
the verb set.
Derivatives: besett-er, п., besett-ing, adj.

## beshrew
beshrew, tr. v. — ME. beschrewen, 'to pervert',
fr. be- and schrewen, 'to curse'. See shrew, 'to
curse*.

## besiclometer
besiclometer, п., an instrument for measuring
the forehead to establish the exact size of the
spectacles. — A hybrid coined fr. F. besides
(pi.), 'spectacles', and Gk. μέτρον, 'measure'.
The first element is an alteration of OF. bericle,
fr. L. beryllus, 'beryl'. The ending of OF. bericle
was prob. suggested by the synonym escarboucle,
'carbuncle'; see beryl. For the second element
see meter, 'poetical rhythm'.

## beside
beside, prep. — ME. besiden, beside, fr. OE. be
sidan, 'by the side', fr. be, 'by', and dative of
side, 'side'. See by and side.

## besides
besides, adv. — Formed fr. prec. word with the
adv. gen. suff. -s.
Derivative: besides, prep.

## besiege
besiege, tr. v. — Formed with change of pref. fr.
OF. asegier (F. assieger), fr. VL. 'assedicare,
fr. ad- and *sedicum, 'seat', fr. L. sedire, 'to sit'.
See be- and siege.
Derivatives: besieg-er, п., besieg-ing, п., besieg-
ing-ly, adv.

## beslaver
beslaver, tr. v. — Formed fr. pref. be- and slaver.

## besmear
besmear, tr. v. — Formed fr. pref. be- and smear.

## besmirch
besmirch, tr. v. — Formed fr. pref. be- and smirch.

## besom
besom, n. — ME. besum, fr. OE. besma, besema,
rel. to OS. besmo, OFris. besma, MDu. besem,
bessem, Ou.bezem, OHG. besmo, besamo, MHG.
besme, besem, besen, G. Besen. The original
meaning is 'something bound or twisted', fr.
I.-E. base *bheidh-, 'to bind, twist'. See fisc.
Derivatives: besom, tr. v., besom-er, n.

## besot
besot, tr. v., to make sottish. — Formed fr. be-
and sot.
Derivatives: besott-ed, adj., besotted-ly, adv.,
besott-ed-ness, n.

## besought
besought, past tense and pp. of beseech. — ME.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:106 COLUMN:3 -->
besoht'e), fr. besechen. See beseech and cp.
sought.

## bespangle
bespangle, tr. v. — Formed fr. be- and spangle.
Derivative: bespangl-ed, adj.

## bespatter
bespatter, tr. v. — Formed fr.- be- and spatter.
Derivative: bespatter-er, n.

## bespeak
bespeak, tr. v. — ME. bespeken, fr. OE. be-
sp(r)ecan, 'to speak about', rel. to Du. bespreken,
G. besprechen. See be- and speak.

## besprent
besprent, adj., sprinkled (archaic). — ME. be-
spreynt, pp. of besprengen, fr. OE. besprengan,
'to besprinkle', rel. to Du. and G. besprengen,
of same meaning. See be- and sprinkle and cp.
next word.

## besprinkle
besprinkle, tr. v. — Formed fr. pref. be- and
sprinkle.

## Bessemer process
Bessemer process, Bessemer steel. — So called
after Sir Harry Bessemer, engineer and inventor
(1813-98).

## best
best, adj. — ME., fr. OE. best, dissimilated fr.
betst, rel. to ON. beztr, Du. best, OHG. beijislo,
MHG., G. best, Goth, batists, 'best',OE. batian,
to become better', bot, 'remedy, cure,
improvement, compensation', and possibly cognate with
OI. bhadrab, 'favorable, good', Avestic hubadra-,
'lucky'. Cp. better. Cp. also batten, 'to grow
fat', boot, 'advanlage'. For the dissimilation of
ОБ. betst into best cp. last, adj.

## bestead
bestead, adj. — ME. bestad, 'placed, situated',
formed fr. be- and stad, 'placed', fr. ON.
staddr, 'placed', pp. of stedja, 'to place, fix'. See
stead.

## bestead
bestead, tr. v., to help. — Formed fr. be- and
stead, v., which derives fr. stead, n.

## bestial
bestial, adj. — F., fr. L. bestialis, 'like a beast',
fr. bestia, 'beast'. See beast and adj. suff. -al.
Derivatives: bestial-ly, adv., bestiary (q.v.),
bestial-ize, tr. v.

## bestiality
bestiality, n. — F. bestialite, fr. bestial, fr. L.
bestialis. See prec. word and -ity.

## bestiary
bestiary, п., a medieval collection of fables about
beasts. — ML. bestidrium, 'a treatise on beasts',
prop. neut. of the L. adjective bestiarus,
'pertaining to beasts', and as a noun, fr. bestia,
'beast'. See beast and subst. suff. -ary.

## bestir
bestir, tr. v. — ME. bestiren, fr. OE. bestyrian,
'to heap up', fr. be- and styrian, 'to set in
motion'. See stir.

## bestow
bestow, tr. v. — ME. bestowen, fr. be- and
slowen. See stow.
Derivatives: bestow-al, п., bestow-er, n.

## bestrew
bestrew, tr. v. — ME. bestrowen, fr. OE. be-
streowian, 'to bestrew, cover', fr. be- and
strlowian, 'to strew'. See strew.

## bestrewn
bestrewn, pp. of bestrew.

## bestride
bestride, tr. v. — ME. bestriden, fr. OE. bestridan,
"to mount a horse', fr. be- and stridan, 'to stride'.
See stride.

## bet
bet, n. — Prob. aphetic for the ME. noun abet, fr.
OF. abet, fr. abeter, 'to incite, bait', lit. 'to cause
to bite'. See abet
Derivatives: bet, tr. and intr. v., better, n.
(q.v.), bett-ing, п., beti-or, n.

## beta
beta, п., name of the 2nd letter of the Greek
alphabet. — Gk. βήτα, fr. Heb.-Phoen. beth; see
beth. The m was added because a Greek word
cannot end with a τ; cp. alpha and words there
referred to.

## Beta
Beta, п., a genus of plants of the goosefoot
family (bot.) — L., 'the beet'. See beet.

## betake
betake, reflex, v.—ME. bitaken, 'to entrust', fr. Ы-
(see be-) and taken, 'to take*. See take.

## betatron
betatron, п., a device for accelerating the
velocities of electrons or beta rays. — Coined fr.
beta (rays) and (elec)tron.

## betel
betel, п., the leaf of the pepper called Piper betel.
— Port, betel, beth, betre, fr. Malayal. vettila,
fr. veru ila, 'simple leaf.

## beth
beth, п., name of the 2nd letter of lhe Hebrew
alphabet. — Heb. beth, lit. 'house'; so called
in allusion to the ancient Hebrew form of this
letter. See bethel and cp. beta.

## bethel
bethel, п., a house of worship. — Heb. belh El,
'the house of God'. Beth is the state construct
of bayith, 'house', and rel. to Aram, baytha,
bethd, Ugar. bt, Arab, bayt, Akkad. bitu,
'house'; cp. beth, beta. Cp. also Basque baita,
'house'. For the second element see El. Cp.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:107 COLUMN:1 -->
haetulus, haetyl.

## Bethesda
Bethesda, п., a pool at Jerusalem; a chapel. —
Gk. Βηθεσδά, fr. Aram, blth hesdd, 'house of
mercy'. See bethel and Hasidim and cp. beth,
beta.

## bethink
bethink, reflex, v. — ME. bethenchen, fr. OE.
bebencan, 'to consider', formed fr. be- and pen-
can, 'to think'. See think and cp. Du. and G.
bedenken.

## betide
betide, intr. and tr. v. — ME. betiden, formed fr.
be- and tiden, 'to happen', fr. OE. tidan. See
tide.

## betimes
betimes, adv. — Formed fr. be- and adv. gen. of
OE. lima, 'time'. See time and -s.

## betoken
betoken, tr. v. — ME. betacnien, fr. be- and OE.
tacnian, 'to signify, betoken', for tacn, 'sign,
token'. See token.
Derivative: betoken-er, n.

## beton
beton, п., a kind of concrete. — F., fr. L. bitumen,
'mineral pitch', later used in the sense of 'mud,
sand'. See bitumen.

## Betonica
Betonica, п., a genus of plants of the mint family
(bot.) — L. betonica, 'bettony'. See next word.

## betony
betony, п., a plant of the genus Betonica. — F.
betoine, fr. L. betonica, var. of vettonica, named
from the Vettdnes, Vectdnes (pi.), a tribe living
near the Tagus (now Tajo) in Lusitania (now
Portugal). Vectdnes is prob. a derivative of ve-
here, 'to draw, carry', and lit. means 'carriers'.
See vehicle.

## betray
betray, tr. v. — ME. betraien, a hybrid coined
fr. be- and OF. trair (F. Irahir), 'to betray',
which was formed—with change of
conjugation—fr. L. tradere. Cp. It. tradire, OProv-
eng. trair, 'to betray', and see tradition. Cp.
also traitor, treason.
Derivatives: betrayal, п., betray-er, п., betrav-
ment, n.

## betroth
betroth, tr. v. — ME. betreuthen. See be- and
troth, truth.
Derivatives: betroth-al, п., betroth-ed,adj. andn.

## better
better, adj.—ME.bettere, bettre (adj.), ie((adv.),
fr. OE. betera (adj.), bet (adv.), rel. to ON. betri
(adj.), betr (adv.), Dan. bedre, Swed. baltre, Du.
beter (adj. and adv.), OHG. bessiro (adj.), baj
(adv.) G. besser (adj. and adv.), Goth, batiza
(adj.) See best and cp. words there referred to.
Derivatives: better, v. (q.v.), better, adv.andn.,
belter-ing, п., better-menl, n.

## better
better, tr. and intr. v. — OE. beterian, fr. betera,
'better'. See better, adj.

## better
better, п., one who bets. — Formed fr. bet with
agential suff. -er.

## betty
betty, п., flask of oil; crowbar, etc. — From
Betty, pet name of Elizabeth.

## Betula
Betula, п., the genus of the birches (hot.) — L.
betula, betulla, 'birch tree', fr. Gaulish betu-,
'bitumen' (found in PN.s); cp. Mir. beithe,
'box tree', W. bedwen, 'birch tree'. According
to Pliny the birch tree was called betu-la, i.e.
'bitumen tree', because the Gauls extracted tar
from it; see bitumen.

## between
between, prep, and adv. — ME. bitweonen, bi-
twenen, bitwene. fr. OE. betweowm, fr. be-, 'by',
and tweonum, dative pi. of tweon, 'double,
twain', which is rel. to Goth, tweihnai, 'two
each', fr. twa, 'two'. See be-, twain, two, and
cp. next word.

## betwixt
betwixt, prep, and adv. — ME. betwixe, fr. OE.
betweox, betweohs, betwux, betwyx, fr. pref. be-,
'by', and a form of twa, 'two'; cp. OHG. zwisk,
zwiski, MHG. zwisc, 'twofold', OS. Iwisk,
'between', Du. tussen, G. zwischen, of s.m. See
between. For the final -/ cp. against, amongst,
etc.

## Beulah
Beulah, fern. PN. — Heb. bl4Adh, 'married
woman', fem. pp. of bd'dl, 'he married', rel. to bffal,
'lord, ruler, husband'. See Baal.

## benrre
benrre, п., butter. — F., 'butter', fr. earlier burre,
fr. L. butyrum, fr. Gk. βούτυρον. See butter.

## beurre
beurre, п., any kind of pear with soft flesh. — F.,
pp. of beurrer, 'to butter', fr. beurre, 'butter'.
See prec. word.

## bevel
bevel, п., inclination of a surface. — OF. "balvel
(whence F. beveau, biveau), 'bevel rule', fr. OF.
baif, 'with an open mouth', fr. baer, beer, 'to
gape'. See bay, 'part in the wall', and cp. words
there referred to.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:107 COLUMN:2 -->
Derivatives: bevel, tr. v. bevel(l)-ed, adj.. be-
vel(l)-er, n.

## beverage
beverage, n. — OF. bevrage, bovrage (F. breu-
vage), fr. beivre, boivre (F. boire), 'to drink', fr.
L. bibere. See bibulous and -age and cp. bevy,
abreuvoir.

## bevue
bevue, п., error, blunder. — F. bevue, 'blunder,
mistake, slip', fr. OF. bes-vue, lit. 'an erroneous
vue', fr. pejorative pref. bes-, which derives fr.
L. bis, 'twice' (see bis-; for sense development cp.
OF. bes-torne, 'badly turned', lit. 'twice turned'),
and fr. vue, 'sight', prop. fem. pp. of voir, 'to
see', fr. L. videre, 'to see'. See vision and cp.
words there referred to.

## bevy
bevy, п., ι) a flock of birds; 2) a company, esp. of
women. — F. bevee, 'a flock of larks or quails',
fr. It. beva. The orig. meaning was prob. 'a
company of drinking birds', fr. It. bevere, 'to drink',
fr. L. bibere. See bibulous and cp. prec. word.

## bewail
bewail, tr. v. — Formed fr. be- and wail,

## beware
beware, intr. and tr. v. — Formed fr. be- and
ware, adj.

## bewilder
bewilder, tr. v. — Formed fr. be- and wilder.
Derivatives: bewilder-ed, adj., bewilder-ed-ly,
adv., bewilder-ed-ness, п., bewiider-ing, adj., be-
wilder-ing-ly, adv.

## bewitch
bewitch, tr. v. — Formed fr. be- and witch.
Derivatives: bewitch-ed, adj., bewitch-ing, adj.,
bewitch-ing-ly, adv.

## bewray
bewray, tr. v., to reveal, divulge (archaic) —
ME. bewreien, bewreyen, 'to reveal', fr. be- and
OE. wregan, 'to accuse', which is rel. to OS.
wrogian, OFris. wrogia, OHG. ruogen, MHG.
rtiegen, 'to accuse', G. riigen, 'to censure', Goth.
wrohjan, 'to accuse', ON. ragja, Ίο slander,
defame', Du. wroegen, 'to prick' (said of
conscience), OE., OS. wroht, OFris. wrogie, MHG.
ruoge,ruege, Goth, wrdhs,'accusation'. G. Riige.
'censure', ON. rog, 'quarrel, slander',

## bey
bey, п., l) governor of a district in Turkey; 2) a
Turkish title of honor. — Osmanli equivalent
of Turk. beg. Cp. beg, 'bey', begum,

## beylic
beylic, beylik, n. — Turk., formed fr. bey and
-lik, a suff. expressing quality. Cp. pashalik.

## beyond
beyond, adv. and prep. — ME. biyeonde, biyonde,
fr. OE. begeondan, 'beyond', fr. be- and geond,
'yond, yonder'. See yon, yond, yonder.
Derivative: beyond, n.

## bezant
bezant, п., a gold coin. — Orig. 'coin of
Byzantium', fr. OF. besan, besant, fr. L. byzantius.
short for Byzantius nummus, 'Byzantine coin*.
See Byzantine,

## bezel
bezel, п., a sloping edge. — OF. bezel (F. bisean),
'a sloping edge, bevel, prob. orig. meaning 'a
stone with two angles'; fr. VL. *bis-alus,
'having two angles', fr. L. bis, 'twice', and ala, 'wing,
side'. See bis- and ala.

## bezesteen
bezesteen, п., a bazaar. — Pers. bezestan, formed
fr. bez (whence Arab, bazz), 'flax, linen clothes',
and -stan, a suff. denoting place, which is rel.
to Avestic stana- (in compounds), 'place', lit.
'a place where to stand'. See Hindustani,

## bezetta
bezetta, bezette, п., a dyeing material made by
dipping linen rags into certain coloring matters.
— It. pezzetta, dimin. of pezza, 'piece of cloth',
a word of Gaulish origin. See piece and -ette.

## bezique
bezique, п., a card game. — F. besigue, of
unknown origin.

## bezoar
bezoar, п., orig. a term for antidote; later used
for concoctions found in the stomach or
intestines of certain animals and thought to have
antidotal properties. — F. bezoard, fr. Sp.
bezoar (cp. Port, bezuar), fr. Arab, badizahr, often
shortened into bazahr (see Freytag, Lexicon
Arabico-Latinum, I, 79a and b), ult. fr. Pers.
badzahr, padzahr, 'counterpoison, bezoar stone',
lit. 'protecting (against) poison', fr. pad,
'protecting, guarding; guardian, lord, master', and
zahr, 'poison'. For the first element see padi-
shah. The second element is rel. to Pers. zehre,
'gall, bile', Pahlavi zahr, 'poison', Aveslic zdra-,
'gall, bile', and cogn. with Gk. χολή, 'gall, bile'.
See choler.

## bezonian
bezonian, п., knave, rascal. — Formed with suff.
-ian, fr. It. bisogno, 'want, need', which is rel. to
F. besogne, 'work, task, job', besoin, 'want,
need', OProvenc. bezonh, 'want', bezonha, 'want,
work, task'. These words prob. derive fr. Fran-

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:107 COLUMN:3 -->
kish *bisunnia, which is formed fr. bi-, 'by',
beside' (see be-), and *sunnia (rel. to OS. sunned),
'care', whence Olt. sogna, F. soin, OProvenc.
sonh, sonha, 'care'. See Dauzat, DELF., p. 85
s.v. besogne.

## bezzle
bezzle, tr. v., to plunder, consume; intr. v., to
revel (dial. English). — OF. besillier, 'to
torment', freq. of beser, 'to be scared, be startled'
(said of cows stung by gadflies), fr. OHG. Ы3-
зап, 'to bite, sting'; see bite and cp. embezzle.
See R. Grandsaignes d'Hauterive, Dictionnaire
d'ancien francais, Paris, 1947, p.62 s.v. besillier.

## bezzo
bezzo, п., name of a small Venetian silver coin. —
It., fr. G. Batz, Batzen, name of a small Swiss
coin, orig. meaning 'a thick piece', and rel. to
the verb batzen, 'to be sticky, be adhesive'. See
batz.

## Bhaga
Bhaga, п., a god of wealth (Vedic mythol.) —
OI. Bhagah, lit. 'allotter, distributer, master,
lord', fr. bhdjati, 'assigns, allots, apportions,
enjoys, loves', rel. to Avestic baya, OPers. baga,
'master, lord, god'. See baksheesh and cp. next
word. Cp. also pagoda.

## Bhagavad-Gita
Bhagavad-Gita, the celebrated dialogue between
Krishna and Arjuna inserted in the Maha-
bharata. — OI. Bhagavadgita, 'the song of the
Sublime One', compounded of Bhagn, suff.
■vant (corresponding to Gk. -Fevr-, -εντ-) and
gl-ta, 'song', prop. fem. pp. of gayate, 'sings,
calls', from the I.-E. imitative base *gd-, *gi-,
whence also Avestic ga&S, Pers. gah, 'song',
Lith. giedoti, 'to sing', giesmS, 'song', Lett.
diesma, 'song'.

## bhang
bhang, п., the Indian hemp. — Hind, bhang, fr.
OI. bhanga, 'hemp', which is cogn. with Russ.
penika (whence Pol. pienka), 'hemp'.

## bhat
bhat, п., l) a bard; 2) a title of respect. — Hind.
bhut, fr. OI. bhattah, a title, prob. rel. to bhart-
rih, 'bearer, supporter, master', from the stem
of bharati, 'he bears', fr. I.-E.,base *bher-, 'to
bear, carry'. See bear, 'to carry'.

## bhava
bhava, п., becoming, birth, origin, world, health.
— OI. bhavdh, rel. to bhavitram, 'world', bhtimlh,
bhuman-, 'earth, world', from the stem of bha-
vali, 'becomes, happens', fr. I.-E. base *bheu-,
*bhu-, 'to be, exist', whence also Gk. φύειν, 'to
make to grow', φύσις, 'nature', L. ffo, Ί
become', fui, Ί have been' OE. beon, 'to be'. See
be and words there referred to and cp. esp.
Bhnmi Devi, bhut.

## bheesty
bheesty, п., a water carrier. — Hind, bhisti. fr.
Pers. bihlsti, 'one from Paradise', fr. bihist,
'Paradise', which is rel. to Avestic vahishta-,
Pahlavi vahisht, OI. vasisthah, 'best'.

## Bhrigu
Bhrigu, п., one of the aerial class of gods in Ved ic
mythology. — OI. Bhfguh, lit. 'shining,
resplendent', rel. to bhrajate, 'shines', fr. I.-E.base
*bhleg-, 'to shine', whence also Gk. φλέγε'.ν,
'to burn', φλόξ, gen. φλογός, 'flame of fire', L.
flagrare, 'to burn'. See flagrant and cp. phlegm.

## Bhumi Devi
Bhumi Devi, the earth goddess in Hindu
mythology.—OI. bhamih, 'earth', and devi, 'goddess'.
For the etymology of the first word see bhava,
for that of the second see Devi.

## bhut
bhut, п., a demon, a ghost. — Hind. bhut. fr. OI.
bhutah, lit. 'a being, creature', rel. to bhamih,
bhuman-, 'earth, world'. See bhava.

## bl-
bl-, pref. meaning 'two'. — L. Ы-, 'twice, double',
fr. bis, 'twice', cogn. with. OI. dvi-, Gk. 81-
(for 8J4-), OE. twi-, 'twice, double'. See bis and
Cp. di-, 'two', dis-, twi-, two. Cp. also binary,
combine, barouche, breba.

## biangular
biangular, adj., having two angles. — Formed fr.
bi- and angular.

## biannual
biannual, adj., occurring twice a year. — Formed
fr. bi- and annual.
Derivative: biannual-ly, adv.

## Bianca
Bianca, fem. PN. — it., prop. fem. of bianco
'while', rel. to F. blanc, fem. blanche, 'white'.
See blank and cp. Blanch.

## bias
bias, п., ι) slant; 2) prejudice. — F. biais, 'slope,
obliquity, bias', prob. fr. OProveng. biais, which
prob. derives fr. Gk. έπικάρσιος, 'slanting,
oblique' [through the medium of VL. *(e)bigas-
sius]. Gk. έπιχίρβιος is formed fr. Ιπί, at,
upon' (see epi-), and κάρ, 'head", which is rel.
to κάρϊ, 'head'. See carotid.
Derivative: bias, tr.v.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:108 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: B1 | BIGAME -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:108 COLUMN:1 -->

## biaxial
biaxial, adj., having two axes. — Formed fr.
bland axial.

## bib
bib, п., a piece of linen, worn by children over the
breast. — Prob. fr. bib, 'to drink' Cp. biberon.

## bib
bib, tr. and intr. v. to drink. — L. bibere, 'to
drink'. See bibulous and cp. imbibe.
Derivatives: bibb-er, п., bibb-ing, n.

## biberon
biberon, п., infant's feeding bottle. — F., fr. L.
bibere, 'to drink'. See bibulous and cp. bib,
'piece of linen'.

## bibitory
bibitory, adj., pertaining to drinking (rare). —
ModL. bibitorius, fr. Late L. bibitor, 'drinker,
toper', fr. bibere, 'to drink*. See bibulous and
-ory.

## Bible
Bible, n. — ME. bible, fr. OF. (= F.) bible, fr. L.
biblia, fr. Gk. βιβλία, 'collection of writings',
pi. of βιβλίον, 'paper, scroll, book'. This is the
dimin. of βίβλος, βύβλος, 'the inner bark of
papyrus; book', Λ-.'Βύβλος, Greek name of the
famous Phoen transit port, whence the Greeks
obtained the Egyptian papyrus, Gk. Βύβλος has
been assimilated fr. G'bhal. the Heb.-Phoen.
name of the city (lit. 'frontier town'; cp. Heb.
g'bhal, 'frontier, boundary', Arab, jabal,
'mountain', and see javali). Cp. Jubayl, the actual
Arabic name of ancient Gebhal. (Jubayl prop,
is a dimin. formed from the original name of the
city.) For the sense development of Bible fr.
Byblos cp. parchment.

## Bibllc
Bibllc, adj., Biblical. — See next word.

## Biblical
Biblical, adj. — Formed with adj. suff. -al fr.
ML. biblicus, fr. L. biblia. See Bible.
