camelry, п., — Formed fr. camel with stiff, -ry.

## Camembert
Camembert, п., a soft, rich cheese. — From Ca-
membert, name of a village near Argentan in
Normandy.

## cameo
cameo, п., a carved gem. — It. cammeo, fr. ML.
camahutus, ult. fr. Pers. chumdhdn, 'agate*,
through the medium of the Arabic. Cp. camaieu.
Derivative: cameo, tr. v.

## camera
camera, п., a chamber. — L., 'vault, arched roof,
arch', fr. Gk. καμάρα, which is rel. to κάμϊνος
(whence L. cammus), 'furnace', and cogn. with
L. camur, camurus, 'curved', fr. I.-E. base *qam-,
"qem-, 'to bend, vault'. Cp. It., OProvenc.,
Catal. camera, Sp. camara. Port, camara, F. cham-
bre, OHG. chamara, OS. camara, OSlav. komora,
Cith. kamard, Olr. camra, which all derive fr.
L. camera. Cp. chamber. Cp. also camara,
Cambarus, camber, chimney, comrade, coacamerated.
For derivatives of a -i-enlargement of base *qam-
see change. Cp. cant, 'slope'. Cp. also heavea.

## camerlengo
camerlengo, camerlingo, п., the papal
chamberlain. — It., a hybrid coined fr. camera (see
camera) and the Teut. suff. -ling. Cp. chamberlain.

## Cameroniaa
Cameroniaa, п., a follower of Richard Cameron
(died in 1680). For the ending see suff. -ian.

## Camilla
Camilla, п., a girl of noble birth employed in
religious offices. — L., fern, of camillus (q.v.)

## Camilla
Camilla, fern. PN. — Fr. prec. word.

## camillus
camillus, п., a noble youth employed in religious
offices (Roman antiq.) — L., fr. Etruscan
Camillus, 'Mercury', fr. Gk. Καδμΐλος (whence
Καο-μΐλος), name of one of the Cabiri in Samo-
thrace. Καδμΐλος is prob. related to Κάδμος,
'Cadmus', hence of Hebrew, origin; see
Cadmus. The Hebrew origin of Gk. Καδμΐλος is
supported by the fact that the name Κάβειροι
itself (whence L. Cabiri) also derives from
Hebrew (see Cabiri).

## enmisado
enmisado, camisade, п., a night attack. — F. ca-
misade, fr. OProvenc. *camisada (fr. camiza,
'shirt'), prop, a night attack in which the
attackers wore shirts over their armour, for the
sake of recognizing one another; cp. It. cami-
ciata, 'camisado', fr. camicia, 'shirt'. See
chemise and -ado and cp. next word.

## camise
camise, п., a light shirt. — Arab, qamts, fr.
Late L. camisia. See chemise.

## camisole
camisole, п., a woman's loose jacket. — F., fr.
OProvenc. camisola, 'mantle', dimin. of camisa,
fr. Late L. camisia. See chemise and cp. prec.
word.

## camlet
camlet, п., cloth made of camel's hair and silk
or of wool and silk. — F. camelot, fr. Arab.
khdmlat, 'plush', the stuff having been fabricated
originally in the East. The French form of the
word is due to an erroneous association with the
word chameau, 'camel*. The ending -at (in
Arab, khdmlat) was mistaken for the suff. -at
and substituted by the more frequent French
suff. -ot (in English this latter suff. became -el).
Derivatives: camlet, adj. and tr. v.

## camomile
camomile, п., an aromatic plant. — F. camo-
miile, fr. Late L. camomilla, fr. earlier chamae-
milon, fr. Gk. χαμαίμηλον, lit. 'earth apple', fr.
χαμαί, 'on the ground', and μήλον, 'apple'. See
chamae- and Malus, 'genus of the apple trees',
and cp. Chamomile.

## Camorra
Camorra, п., name of a secret society at Naples.
— It., fr. camorro, 'a person in failing health;
a troublesome person', prob. fr. Port, cha-
morro, 'with shaven head, bald', which is of
uncertain, possibly Basque, origin.
Derivatives: Camorr-ism, п., Camorr-isl, n.

## camouflage
camouflage, п., concealment of troops, ships, etc.,
from the enemy; disguise. — F., fr. camoufler,
'to disguise', fr. It. camuffare, 'to disguise',
contraction of capo muffare, 4o muffle the head'.
See capital, adj., muffle and -age.
Derivatives: camouflage, tr. and intr. v., ca-
mouflag-er, n.

## camp
camp, n. — F., fr. It. campo, 'camp', fr. L.
campus, 'flat space, plain field* (whence also F.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:136 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: 109 | CANCER -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:136 COLUMN:1 -->
champ, 'field, battlefield'), fr. I.-E. base *qamp-,
'to bend', whence also Gk. καμπή, 'bend, turn,
winding of a river*, κάμπτεω, 'to bend, curve,
turn', κάμψις, 'a bending, turning', Lith. kampas,
'corner, region', Lett, kampis, 'a crooked piece
of wood', Lith. kumpas, 'crooked', kumpii, Lett.
kumpt, 'to become bent, to curve', Goth, hamfs,
'mutilated', OHG. hamf, 'crippled' (lit. 'curved),
OE. hofer, 'hump, swelling'. Cp. campaign,
campane, campanile, Campanula, camper,
campion, campo, campus, campylo-, champaign,
champignon, champion, decamp, encamp, gamh,
gamba, schanz, sconce, 'cover', the first element
in Camponotas, Camptosorus, champerty, and
the second element in elecampane, Kalturkampf.
Cp. base ,(s)qamb-, *(s)qemb-, whence Gk.
σκαμβός, 'crooked, bent', Olr. camm, 'crooked,
curved', Mir. cimb, 'tribute', cimbid, 'prisoner',
Gaulish cambita, 'felloe' (whence F. janle, of
a.m.); see change.

## camp
camp, intr. v., to pitch a camp. — F. camper, fr.
camp, 'camp'. See camp, n.
Derivative: camp-er, n.

## campagna
campagna, п., open country. — It., fr. Late L.
campania. See next word.

## campaiga
campaiga, n. — F. campagne, 'open country;
campaign', fr. It. campagna, fr. Late L.
Campania, 'plain, open country' (whence also Sp.
сатрапа, Port, campanha), fr. campanius, a var.
of campaneus, 'pertaining to the open country',
fr. L. campus, 'flat space, plain, open field'. Cp.
L. Campania, name of a province of Italy about
Naples, lit. 'the plain or level country', and see
camp, n. Cp. also campagna, champaign. Cp.
also next word.
Derivative: campaign-er, n.

## campane
campane, п., a bell (her.) — F., fr. Late L.
сатрапа, orig. 'a metal vessel made in Campania',
fr. L. Campania. See prec. word and cp. cam-
panero, campanile, Campanula.

## campanero
campanero, п., the bellbird of South America. —
Sp., lit. 'bellman', fr. сатрапа, 'bell', fr. Late
L. сатрапа. See prec. word.

## campaniform
campaniform, adj., bell-shaped. — Compounded
of Late L. сатрапа 'bell', and L. forma, 'form,
shape'. See campane and form, n.

## campanile
campanile, п., a bell tower. — It., fr. сатрапа,
'bell', fr. Late L. сатрапа (see campane);
introduced into English by the diarist John Evelyn
(1620-1706).

## cumpanist
cumpanist, п., an expert in bells. — A hybrid
coined fr. Late L. сатрапа (see campane) and
-1st, a suff. of Greek origin.

## campanology
campanology, п., the study of bells. — A hybrid
coined fr. Late L. сатрапа and Gk. -λογία, fr.
-λόγος, 'one who speaks (in a certain manner);
one who deals (with a certain topic)'. See cam-
pane and -logy.
Derivative: campanolog-ist, n.

## Campaaula
Campaaula, n„ the bellflower (bot.)— ModL., di-
min. of Late L. сатрапа, 'bell' (see campane and
-uie); so called from the shape of the corolla.

## Campannlaceae
Campannlaceae, n. pi., the bluebell family (bol.)
— Formed fr. prec. word with suff. -aceae.

## campanulaceous
campanulaceous, adj. — See prec. word and
-aceous.

## campanular
campanular, adj., bell-shaped. — Formed with
suff. -ar fr. Late L. campanula, dimin. of
сатрапа, 'bell*. See campane and -ule.

## campanulate
campanulate, campanalous, adj., campanular. —
See prec. word and adj. suff. -ate, resp. -ous.

## Campephagidae
Campephagidae, п., a family of birds, the cuckoo
shrike (ornithol.) — ModL., lit. 'caterpillar
eaters', formed with suff. -idae fr. Gk. κάμπη,
'caterpillar', and the stem of φαγεϊν, 'to eat'. For
the first element see hippocampus, for the second
see -phagous.

## Campephilus
Campephilus, п., a genus of woodpeckers
(ornithol) — ModL., lit. 'lover of caterpillars', fr.
Gk. κάμπη, 'caterpillar', and φίλος, 'lover,
friend*. See hippocampus and philo-.

## camphene
camphene, п., a hydrocarbon, C10H14 (chem.) —
Formed from the abbreviation of camphor and
suff. -ene.

## camphine
camphine, п., purified oil of turpentine (chem.) —
Formed from the abbreviation of camphor and
chem. suff. -ine.

## camphire
camphire,n., 1)camphor(ota>/.ordial.); 2)henna

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:136 COLUMN:2 -->
(see Authorized Version, Song of Songs 1:14).
— A var. of camphor.

## camphor
camphor, n. — F. camphre, fr. ML. camphora, fr.
Arab, kafar, fr. OI. kapparah, assimilated fr.
earlier karpBrab.
Derivatives: camphor, tr. v., camphor-aceous,
adj., camphor-ate, tr. v., camphor-ated, cam-
phor-ic, camphor-y, adjs.

## eampion
eampion, п., any plant of the genus Lychnis. —
Perhaps fr. L. campus, 'field'. See camp, n.

## cumpo
cumpo, п., a field. — It., Sp. and Port., fr. L.
campus. See camp, n.

## Campodea
Campodea, n. pi., a genus of insects (entomol.) —
ModL., compounded of Gk. κάμπη, 'caterpillar',
and -ώδης, 'like'. See hippocampus and -ode.

## Camponotas
Camponotas, п., a genus of ants (entomol.) —
ModL., compounded of Gk. καμπή,'a bending',
and νώτος, 'back'. See camp, п., and noto-.

## campoo
campoo, п., camp (Anglo-Ind.). — Hind, катрй,
fr. Port, campo, 'camp', fr. L. campus, 'field'.
See camp, n.

## Camptosorus
Camptosorus, п., a genus of ferns of the polypody
family, the walking leaf (bot.). — ModL., lit.
'with flexible fruit dots', compounded of Gk.
καμπτός, 'flexible*, verbal adj. of κάμπτειν, 'to
bend', and σωρός, 'heap of corn, heap'. See
camp, п., and sorus.

## campus
campus, п., college grounds. — L., 'field'. See
cump, n.

## campylo-
campylo-, before a vowel campyl-, combining
form meaning 'bent, curved'. — Gk. καμπύλο-,
καμπυλ-, fr. καμπύλος, 'bent, curved', fr. καμπή,
'a bending'. See camp, n.

## camus
camus, camuse, adj., short and flat (said of the
nose) (obsol.) — F. camus, fem. camuse, 'flat-
nosed, snub-nosed', formed from pejorative
pref. ca- and the base of museau, 'muzzle, snout'.
See muzzle.

## camwood
camwood, п., wood of an African tree (Baphia
nitida). — The first element of this compound
is a W. African loan word. For the second
element see wood.

## can
can, aux. ν — ME. cunnen, fr. OE. cunnan, rel.
to ON. kunna, OS. kunnan, Du. kunnen, OHG.
kunnan, MHG. kunnen, kunnen, G. kunnen,
Goth, kunnan, 'to be able', OE. cnawan, OHG.
bi-chnaan, ir-chnaan, 'to know', ON. kna, Ί can*,
fr. I.-E. base *geni-, *gend-, 'to be able
mentally, to know', whence also OI. janati, 'knows',
jnaldh, 'known', Toch. A kna", 'to know', a-
knats, В a-knatsa, 'ignorant', Arm. caneay,
Ί knew', ancan, 'unknown', Gk. γιγνώσκειν, 'to
know*, γνώσις, 'knowledge, wisdom', γνώμη, 'a
means of knowing, judgement, opinion, maxim',
γνωμών, 'one who knows, a judge; the gnomon
or index (of the sundial)', OL. gndscere, L. nos-
cere, 'to know', Alb. heh, 'you know' (sing.),
hoh, Ί know', OSlav. znajg, znati, Lith. zinau,
zinoti, 'to know', OPruss. po-sinna, Ί confess',
Olr. ad-gninim, Ί know, recognize', gndth,
'known, accustomed', W. gnawd, 'custom'. See
know and cp. canny, con, 'to peruse', could,
cunning, keen, ken, 'to know', ken, 'range of
sight', kith, kirhe, uncouth. Cp. also acquaint,
agnoiology, cognition, diagaosis, gnome, 'maxim',
gnomic, gnomon, gnosis, gnostic, ignoble, ignore,
incognito, jnana, narrate, noble, normal, aote,
notice, notion, notorious, quaint, recognize,
reconnoitre.

## can
can, п., vessel. — ME. canne, fr. OE. canne, rel.
to OS., ΟΝ., Swed. karma, MDu. kanne, Du.
кап, OHG. channa, MHG., G. kanne, 'can',
borrowed fr. L. canna, 'reed, cane; small vessel,
tube', which is of Sem. origin. See cane and
cp. canal.
Derivatives: can, tr. v., to put into a can,
canned, adj., cann-er, п., cann-ery, п., carm-ing, n.

## Canaan
Canaan, п., the Promised Land of the Israelites.
— L. Chanaan, fr. Gk. Χαναάν, fr. Heb. K'-
ηά'αη, which is of unknown origin.
Derivatives: Canaan-ite, adj. and п., Сапаап-
it-ic, adj., Canaan-it-ish, adj.

## canaba
canaba, also caanaba, п., a hovel, hut (Roman
antiq.) — L., fr. Gk. κάν(ν)αβος, 'woodenframe-
work', fr. κάννα, 'reed', which is of Sem. origin.
See caae.

## Canada
Canada, п., a Portuguese liquid measure. — Port.

## Canada
Canada, п., a deep valley — Sp., fr. VL. canna,

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:136 COLUMN:3 -->
'canal', fr. L. canna, 'reed, cane; tube'. See cane
and cp. can, 'vessel'.

## canaille
canaille, п., rabble. — F., fr. It. canaglia, lit. 'a
pack of dogs', fr. cane, 'dog'; cp. OF. chiennaille,
which is of the same origin and meaning as It.
canaglia. See caaine.

## canal
canal, n. — F., fr. L. canalis, 'water pipe,
channel, canal', prop, subst. use of an adj. formed fr.
canna, 'reed, cane; small vessel, tube'. The
shortening of the double и is due to the phonetic law,
according to which before a stressed syllable,
a double consonant becomes short. Cp. L.
curulis, 'pertaining to a chariot', fr. currus,
'chariot' (see curule), and mamilla, 'breast',
dimin. of mamma, 'breast' (whence this phonetic
law is called 'mamilla law'; see mammilla). See
cane and adj. suff. -al and cp. channel, caanel,
kennel, 'gutter', which are doublets of canal.
Derivatives: canal, tr. v., canal(l)-er, п.,
canalize, tr. v., canal-iz-ation, n.

## canalicular
canalicular, adj., pertaining to, or like, a
canaliculus or canaliculi. — Formed with adj. suff.
-ar fr. canaliculus (q.v.)

## canaliculate
canaliculate, canaliculated, adj., channeled. —
L. canaliculatus, 'channeled', fr. canaliculus.
Sec next word and adj. suff. -ate, resp. also -ed.

## canaliculus
canaliculus, п., a small canal (anal.) — L., dimin.
of canalis. See caual and -cule.

## Canangium
Canangium, п., a genus of trees of the custard-
apple family (bot.) — ModL., fr. Malay kenan-
ga, prob. a nasalized form of OI. kanakam. For
the ending see suff. -ium.

## canape
canape, п., food served as an appeiizer. — F.,
orig. 'a canopy over a couch to keep off
insects'. See canopy.

## canard
canard, п., a duck; a hoax. — F., 'duck; drake',
fr. OF. canart, fr. OF. caner, 'to cackle', which is
of imitative origin.The suff.-ал? (F.-ard) isdueto
lhe influence of OF. maslart, 'duck; drake', fr.
mask (F. male), 'male'. See -ard and cp. cancan.

## canary
canary, п., — F. canari, canarie, fr. Sp. canario,
'canary bird', lit. 'of the Canary Islands', fr. L.
insula Canada, 'one of the Canary Islands', lit.
'Dog Islands', fr. cam's, 'dog' (see canine). The
islands were so called from their large dogs.

## canasta
canasta, п., a card game originating from
Argentina. — Sp. canasta, 'a basket', fr. canasto,
a secondary form of canaslro, 'a large basket*,
fr. L. canistrum, 'wicker basket', fr. Gk. κάνα-
στρον; see canister. The game was so called
from the basketful of cards used in it.

## canaster
canaster, п., a kind of coarse tobacco. — Sp.
canaslro, 'a large basket'. See prec. word.

## canaut
canaut, also conaut, п., side wall of a tent (Anglo-
Ind.) — Hind, qanat, fr. Pers. qanal, fr. Arab.
qanaf, 'cane'. See cane.

## cancan
cancan, п., a kind of extravagant dance. — F.,
prob. fr. cancan, childish name of the duck
(= F. canard); so called from the waddling gait.
See canard.

## cancel
cancel, tr. and intr. v. — F. canceller, 'to cancel',
fr. L. cancellare, 'to enclose with a lattice',
hence 'to cross out; to cancel', fr. cancelli(pi.),
'enclosure, crossbar, lattice', dimin. of cancer,
'lattice, dissimilated fr. career, 'an enclosed
place; prison'. See incarcerate and cp. career,
chnncel.
Derivatives: cancel, п., cancel-ed, adj., cancell-
ate, adj. (ψν.)

## cancellate
cancellate, adj., marked with crosslines. — L.
cancellatus, pp. of cancellare. See prec. word
and adj. suff. -ate.
Derivatives: cancellat-ed, adj., cancellat-ion, n.

## cancellous
cancellous, adj., having a spongelike structure
(said of the spongy part of bones). — Formed
with suff. -ous fr. L. cancelli (pi.), 'lattice*. See
cnnceL

## cancer
cancer, п., a malignant growth. — L., 'crab,
ulcer, cancer', dissimilated fr. *carcro- and cogn.
with Gk. καρκίνος, 'crab', lit. 'the animal with
the hard shell', fr. I.-E. base *qarq-, *qraq-, 'to
be hard', whence also OI. karkafah, karkah,
'crab', karkarah, 'hard'. Cp. OSlav. raku,
'crayfish', OPruss. rakis, of s.m., which were prob.
dissimilated fr. *krak-; cp. also W. crach, 'crust',
craig, 'rock', Mir. crach, 'hard', fr. *qraq-, Cp.
also I.-E. base 'qar-tu-, 'hard, strong', whence
Gk. κρατύς, 'strong', Goth, /tardus, OE. heard,

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:137 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: CANCRIFORM | 110 -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:137 COLUMN:1 -->
'hard'. See hard and cp. canker, carcinoma,
chancre. Cp. also kunkur.
Derivatives: cancer-ous, adj., cancer-ous-ly, adv.,
cancer-ous-ness, n.

## cancriform
cancriform, adj., crablike. — Compounded of
L. cancer, gen. cancrl, 'crab', and forma, 'form,
shape'. See cancer and form, n.

## cancroid
cancroid, adj., like a crab; like a cancer. — A
hybrid coined fr. L. cancer, gen. cancrl, 'crab',
and Gk. -οειδής, 'like', fr. είδος, 'form, shape'.
See cancer and -oid.

## candelabrum
candelabrum, also candelabra, п., a branched
candlestick. — L. candelabrum, 'candlestick',
fr. candila. See candle and cp. chandelier.

## candent
candent, adj., glowing, white. — L. candens, gen.
-entis, pres. part, of candere. See candescent

## candescence
candescence, n. — Formed fr. next word with suff.
-ce.

## candescent
candescent, adj., glowing. — L. candescent, gen.
-entis, pres. part, of candescere, 'to begin to
glow', inchoative of candire, 'to shine, glow',
whence also candidus, 'glowing, white'. See next
word and -escent, and cp. incandesce.
Derivative: candescent-ly, adv.

## candid
candid, adj., impartial; frank, sincere. — F. can-
dide, 'open, frank, ingenuous, sincere, candid',
fr. L. candidus, 'glowing, white; pure, honest,
upright', fr. candere, 'to shine, glow, be white',
which is cogn. with Gk. κάνδαρος, 'glowing
coal', OI. candrah, 'shining glowing', candana-,
'sandalwood' (lit. 'wood for burning incense'),
Alb. Gheg hqne, Tosk ηεηε, 'moon' (lit. 'the
white one'). All these words derive fr. I.-E. base
*(s)qand-, *(s)qend-, 'to shine, glow'. Cp. W.
cann, 'white, bright', OBret. cant, 'white',
MBret. cann, 'full moon*, which, according to
Pedersen, are not cognate with L. candidus, but
loan words fr. VL. *candus, contraction of
candidus (see haplology). Cp. candle, candelabrum,
candidate, chnndelier, chandler, Cicindelidae,
incandescent, incense, sandalwood, sandarac,
sauders, santal.
Derivatives: candid-ly, adv., candid-ness, n.

## candidate
candidate, п., one who seeks an office, etc. — L.
candidatus, 'one aspiring to office', prop. pp. of
candidare, 'to make bright or white', fr.
candidus, 'glowing, white'; so called because a
candidate for office was clothed in a white toga.
See candid and adj. suff. -ate.
Derivative: candidat-ure, n.

## candle
candle, n. — ME. candel, fr. OE. candel, fr. L.
candela, 'candle made of wax or tallow', fr.
candere, 'to shine, glow, burn'. See candid and
cp. candelabrum, chandelier, chandler.

## Candlemas
Candlemas, n. — ME. candelmasse, fr. OE. can-
delmxsse, compounded of candel, 'candle', and
mxsse, 'Mass'. See candle and Mass.

## candlestick
candlestick, n. — ME. candlestikke, fr. OE.
candelslicca, compounded of candel, 'candle',
and sticca, 'stick'. See candle and stick, n.

## candor
candor, candour, п., impartiality, frankness. —
L. candor, 'whiteness; sincerity, candor', from
the stem of candere, 'to be white'. See candid
and -or.

## candy
candy, п., crystallized sugar. — Shortened fr.
sugar candy, fr. F. (sucre) candi, fr. It. (zucchero)
candi(to), 'sugar candy', fr. Arab, qandi,
'crystallized, candied', adj. formed fr. qand, 'cane
sugar', which, like OI. khandakah, 'candy', is
prob. of Dravidian origin. Cp. Tamil kanfu,
'candy', каци, 'to harden, condense'.

## caady
caady, tr. and intr. v., to crystallize into sugar. —
Formed fr. prec. word, on analogy of F. candir,
'to candy*, back formation fr. candi, 'sugar
candy', which was mistaken for a past participle.
Derivative: can-di-ed, adj.

## candytuft
candytuft, n„ name of a plant. — Compounded
of. Candy, obsolete form of Candia, 'Crete',
and tuft Hence candytuft lit. means 'tuft of
Crete'.

## cane
cane, n. — ME. cane, canne, fr. OF. cane, canne
(F. canne), fr. OProvenc. сапа, fr. L. canna,
'reed, cane, small vessel, tube', fr. Gk. κάννα,
'reed', which is of Sem. origin. Cp. Akkad.
qanu, Heb. gone*, Aram.-Syr. qanya, Arab.
qana* (whence Pers. qanal), 'reed, cane', Ethiop.
qanSt, 'a goad'. Cp. can, 'vessel', canaha, Canada,
canal, canasta, canaster, canaut, canella, can-

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:137 COLUMN:2 -->
ions, canister, Canna, cannel, cannelure,
cannikin, canon, 'rule', canonical, caayon, and the
first element in canephorus, caramel.
Derivatives: cane, tr. v., can-er, п., can-ing, n.

## canella
canella, п., cinnamon. — ML., dimin. of L.
canna, 'reed, cane'. See cane and -ella.

## canephorus
canephorus, п., a basket bearer (Greek antiq.) —
L., fr. Gk. κανηφόρος, 'basket bearing',
compounded of κάνεον, κανοϋν, 'wicker basket'
and -φόρος, 'bearing, carrying'. The first
element is rel. to κάννα, 'reed'; see cane. For the
second element see -pbore.

## canescent
canescent, adj., growing grayish or white. — L.
canescens, gen. -entis, pres. part, of canescere,
'to grow gray or white', inchoative of canere,
'to be gray or white', fr. canus, 'gray, hoary,
white', which stands for *cas-nos, and is rel. to
cascus, 'old', lit. 'gray with age', and cogn. with
OHG. haso, OE. hara, 'hare', lit. 'the gray
animal'. See bare and -escent.

## caague
caague, п., a board worn round the neck by
Chinese criminals. — F., fr. Port, canga, 'yoke', fr.
Annam. gong, of s.m.
Derivative: cangue, tr. v.

## Canicula
Canicula, п., Sirius (astron.) — L. canicula, lit.
'the Dog Star', dimin. of canis, 'dog'. See canine
and -cule.

## caaicular
caaicular, adj., i) pertaining to Sirius; 2)
pertaining to the dog days. — L. canicularis, fr.
canicula. See prec. word and -ar.

## Canidae
Canidae, n. pi., the family of dogs, wolves, foxes
and jackals (zool.) — ModL., formed with suff.
-idae, fr. L. canis, 'dog'. See next woid.

## canine
canine, adj., pertaining to the dog. — L. canimis,
fr. canis, 'dog', which is cogn. with Gk. κύων.
gen. κυνός, Goth, hunds, OE. hund, 'dog'. See
hound and cp. words there referred to. For the
ending see suff. -ine (representing L. -inus).
Derivative: canine, n.

## canions
canions, n. pi., ornamental rolls attached to
breeches. — Sp. canon, in the sense of 'tube'.
See canyon.

## Canis
Canis, п., the genus including the dog, the wolf,
the fox and the jackal (zool.) — L. canis, 'dog'.
See canine.

## Cams Major
Cams Major, Sirius (astron.) — L., 'the larger
dog'. See canine and major.

## Canis Minor
Canis Minor, Procyon (astron.) — L., lit. 'the
lesser dog'. See canine and minor.

## canister
canister, п., a small box. — L. canistrum, 'wicker
basket', fr. Gk. κάναστρον, ft. κάννα, 'reed'.
See cane and cp. canasta, canaster.
Derivative: canister, tr. v.

## canities
canities, п., grayness or whiteness of the hair. —
L., 'grayish white color*, fr. canus. See canescent.

## canker
canker, п., an ulcerous sore. — ONF. cancre
(corresponding to F. chancre), fr. L. cancer, 'crab,
ulcer, cancer*. See cancer and cp. chancre.
Derivatives: canker, tr. and intr. v., canker-ed,
adj., canker-ous, adj.

## Canna
Canna, п., a genus of plants (hot.) — L. canna,
'reed, cane'. See cane.

## cannabic
cannabic, adj., pertaining to hemp. — Formed
with suff. -ic fr. L. cannabis. See next word.

## Cannabis
Cannabis, п., a genus of plants, the hemp (hot.) —
L. cannabis, 'hemp', fr. Gk. κάνναβις. See canvas.

## cannel
cannel, п., a gutter; kennel. — ME. canel, fr.
ONF. canel, fr. L. canalem, ace. of canalis,
'pipe'. See canal and cp. kennel, 'gutter'.

## cannel coal
cannel coal, a bituminous coal. — Corruption of
candle coal.

## cannelure
cannelure, п., a groove. — F., fr. It. cannellatura
(now scannellalura), fr. cannellare, 'to groove',
fr. cannella, 'a small tube', dimin. of canna,
'cane, reed', fr. L. canna. See cane and -ure and
cp. canal.

## cannibal
cannibal, п., a person who eats human flesh. —
Sp. caribe, carlbal, canlbal, fr. Carib. galibi,
'Caribs, Caribbeans', lit. 'strong men'; so called
because the Caribs were eaters of human flesh.
Cp. Carib, Caliban. The word cannibal was
influenced in form by Sp. can, 'dog', fr. L. canis.
Derivatives: cannibal, adj., cannibal-ly, adv.,
cannibal-ic, adj., cannibal-ism, п., cannibal-ist-
ic, adj., cannibal-ist-ic-al-ly, adv.

## cannikin
cannikin, п., a small can. — A hybrid coined fr.
can, 'vessel', and suff. -kin (fr. MDu. -kin,
-kijn).

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:137 COLUMN:3 -->

## cannon
cannon, п., gun. — F. canon, fr. It. cannone, lit.
'a large tube', augment, of canna, 'tube', fr. L.
canna. See cane and cp. canyon.
Derivatives: cannon, intr. v., cannon-ed, adj.,
cannon-ry, n.

## cannon
cannon, п., a stroke in billiards. — Corruption of
carom.

## cannonade
cannonade, п., discharge of artillery. — F. canon-
nade, fr. It. cannonata, fr. cannone. See cannon
and -ade (representing It. -ata).
Derivative: cannonade, tr. and intr. v.

## cannula
cannula, п., a small tube (surg.) — L., 'a small
reed', dimin. of canna. See cane and -ule.
Derivatives: cannul-ar, п., cannul-ate, adj. and
tr. v., cannul-at-ed, adj.

## canny
canny, adj., l) careful; 2) shrewd. — Lit.
'knowing', rel. to the auxiliary verb can (q.v.) Cp.
cunning.

## canoe
canoe, n. — F. canoe, fr. Sp. canoa, a word of
Caribbean origin.
Derivatives: canoe, intr. and tr. v., canoe-ing,
п., canoeist (q.v.)

## canoeist
canoeist, n. — A hybrid coined fr. canoe and
-isf, a suff. of Greek origin.

## canon
canon, п., rule. — ME. canun, canoun, fr. OE.
canon, fr. L. canon, 'a measuring line, rule,
model', in Eccles. L. 'canon', fr. Gk. κανών,
'rod, bar, ruler, rule, model', fr. κάννα, 'reed',
which is of Sem. origin. See cane and cp. words
there referred to.

## canon
canon, п., a dignitary of the church. — ME.
canun, canoun, fr. ONF. canoine, corresponding
to OF. (= F.) chanoine, fr. Eccles. L. canonicus,
lit. 'one subject to the canon', fr. Gk. κανονικός,
'belonging to a rule', fr. κανών, 'rule'. See canon,
'rule', and cp. canonical.

## canon
canon, n. — See canyon.

## canoness
canoness, n. — Formed fr. canon, 'dignitary*,
with suff. -ess.

## canonical
canonical, adj. — ML. canonicdlis, fr.Late L.
canonicus, 'according to rule' (in Eccles. L.
'pertaining to the canon'), fr. canon, 'rule'. See
canon, 'rule', and the suffixes -ic and -al.

## canonicity
canonicity, n. — Formed with suff. -ity fr. L.
canonicus. See prec. word.

## canonist
canonist, п., one skilled in canon law. — Formed
fr. canon, 'rule', with suff. -ist.
Derivatives: canonist-ic, canonist-ic-al, adjs.

## canonize
canonize, tr. v., to put in the canon of saints. —
F. canoniser, fr. Eccles. L. canonizare, fr. canon.
See canon, 'rule', and -ize.
Derivatives: canoniz-ation, п., canoniz-er, n.

## canonry
canonry, п., the office of a canon. — Formed fr.
canon, 'dignitary', with suff. -ry.

## Canopic
Canopic, adj., pertaining to Canopus, a town of
ancient Egypt.

## canopy
canopy, n. — F. canape, fr. ML. canopeum, dis-
similated fr. L. сбпбреит, fr. Gk. κωνωπεΐον, 'a
bed with mosquito curtains', fr. κώνωψ, gen.
κώνωπος, 'gnat, mosquito', a word of uncertain
origin. It. canapi is a French loan word. Cp.
canape and the first element in Conopophagidae.
Derivative: canopy, tr. v.

## canorous
canorous, adj., melodious. — L. canorus,
'melodious, harmonious', fr. canor, 'melody, song',
fr. canere, 'to sing'. See cant, 'slang of beggars'.
For E. -ous, as equivalent to L. -us, see suff.
-«us.
Derivatives: canorous-ly, adv., canorous-ness, n.

## cant
cant, п., slang of beggars. — The word orig.
denoted the whining of beggars. It derives fr.
ONF. cant (corresponding to OF. and F. chant),
fr. L. cantus, 'singing, song', fr. cant-(um), pp.
stem of canere, 'to .sing', whence also carmen
(dissimilated fr. *can-men), 'poem, verse'. L.
canere is cogn. with Toch. кап, 'melody, tune',
Gk. κανάσσειν, 'to give a gurgling or ringing
sound', καναχή, 'a gurgling or ringing sound',
ήΐ-κανός, 'cock', lit. 'singer of the dawn' (the
first element of this word is shortened fr. ήοΐος
(Att. έώος), 'early* (see eo-)t Russ. kanja, 'kite',
Olr. canim, Ί sing*, MIr. cetal, 'song', Goth.
hana, OHG., OS. hano, MLG., MDu., MHG.,
Dan., Swed. hane, Du. haan, G. Hahn, ON. hant,
OE. hana, 'cock', lit. 'the singing bird'. See hen
and cp. accent, baccinator, canorous, cantablle,
cantata, cantatrice, canticle, cantillate, canto,
cantor, cantas, canzone, canzonet, chanson,

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:138 COLUMN:1 -->
chant, chantage, chanter, chanticleer, cbanty,
charm, 'spell', concent, concert, descant, enchant,
diseachant, incantation, incentive, Oscines, pre-
ceator, recant, succentor.
Derivatives: cant, intr. v., to whine, cani-ing,
adj., cant-ing-ly, adv., cant-ing-ness, n.

## cant
cant, п., a slope. — ONF. cant (corresponding to
OF. and F. chant), 'corner', fr. L. cantus, can-
thus, 'the iron ring round a carriage wheel, a
wheel, felloe' (whence Gk. καν&ός, 'tire of a
wheel'), which is of Gaulish origin (cp. Gaulish
kantem,kantena,kanten,quotcdhyG.-O.Oottin,
La langue gauloise, p. 241). Cp. also W. cant,
'bordering (framing, setting) of a circle, tire,
edge', Bret, cant, 'circle', Mir. cite (for *kantya),
'meeting, fair'. Cp. also Gk. κοινθός, 'corner of
the eye', OSlav. "kqtu, Russ. kutu, 'corner'. All
these words prob. derive fr. I.-E. 'qan-t(h)o-, an
enlargement of base *qam-, 'to bend'. See
camera and cp. canthus, cantle, canton, decant, and
the first element in chamfer, conUine.
Derivative: cant, ti. v., to cause to slant; intr. v.,
to slant.

## cantabile
cantabile, adj., melodious. — It., lit. 'singable',
fr. cantare, 'to sing', fr. L. cantare. See cantata
and -able.
Derivative: cantabile, n.

## Cantabrigian
Cantabrigian, adj., pertaining to Cambridge,
England, or its university. — Formed with suff. -an.
fr. ML. Cantabrigia, 'Cambridge'.

## cantaloup
cantaloup, п., a kind of melon. — F., fr. It. canta-
lupo, fr. Cantalupo, name- of a castle in the
province of Ancona, in Italy, where these
melons were first grown.

## cantankerous
cantankerous, adj., ill-natured..— Prob. formed
fr. ME. contekous, fr. contek, contak, 'strife',
but influenced in form by the ending of words
like cankerous, rancorous.
Derivatives: cantankerous-ly, adv., cantanker-
ous-ness, n.

## cantar
cantar, n. — See kantar.

## cantata
cantata, п., a musical composition for solo,
chorus, etc. — It., lit. 'that which is sung', fr. can-
tare, 'to sing', fr. L. cantare, freq. of canere, *to
sing'. See cant, 'slang of beggars', and cp. next
word.

## cantatrice
cantatrice, п., a female singer. — F., fr. It. canla-
trice, 'female singer*, fr. cantare, 'to sing'. See
prec. word.

## canteen
canteen, п., ι) store in a military camp; z) a
small tin vessel. — F. cantine, fr. It. cantina,
'wine cellar, cantine', which is of Gaulish origin.

## canter
canter, n. an easy gallop. — Shortened fr.
Canterbury pace or Canterbury gallop; so called in
allusion to the gait of pilgrims riding to
Canterbury. See next word.
Derivatives: canter, intr. and tr. v., canter-er, n.

## canterbury
canterbury, п., a stand with divisions for music. —
From Canterbury, name of a city in England,
which derives fr. OE. Cantwarabyrig, lit. 'the
fortified town of the Kentish people'. See
Kentish and borough and cp. canter,

## canth-
canth-, form of cantho- before a vowel.

## canthal
canthal, adj., pertaining to a canthus (anat.) —
Formed fr. canthus with adj. suff. -al.

## Cantharellus
Cantharellus, п., a genus of fungi (bot.)—ModL.,
lit. 'a little cup', dimin. of L. cantharus, fr. Gk.
κάν&χρος, 'a kind of beetle worshiped in Egypt;
a drinking cup', which is prob. a pre-Hellenic
word; so called from the shape of these fungi.
Cp. chanterelle.

## cantharides
cantharides, n. pi., dried blister beetles (used in
medicine). — L., pi. of cantharis, a kind of
beetle', fr. Gk. κανθαρίς, gen. -Ιδος, 'blister
beetle', a derivative of κάνθαρος. See prec. word.

## cantho-
cantho-, before a vowel canth-, combining form
denoting the canthus — See next word.

## canthus
canthus, п., either of the corners of the eye (anat.)
— Medical L., fr. Gk. καν&ίς, 'corner of the
eye'. See cant, 'slope'.

## canticie
canticie, п., a short hymn. — L., canliculum, 'a
little song', dimin. of canticum, 'song', fr.
cantus, 'song', fr. cant-(um), pp. stem of canere,
'to sing'. See cant, 'slang of beggars', and -de.

## cantilever
cantilever, п., a projecting bracket. — Prob.
compounded of cant, 'slope', and lever.
Derivative: cantilever, tr. v.

## cantillate
cantillate, tr. v., to chant. — L. cantiUatus, pp. of

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:138 COLUMN:2 -->
cantillare, 'to sing low*, dimin. of cantare, 'to
sing'. See cant, 'slang of beggars', and verbal
suff. -ate.
Derivative: cantillat-ion, n.

## cantie
cantie, п., the hinder part of a saddle. — ONF.
camel, corresponding to OF. chantel, 'corner,
piece' (whence F. chanteau, 'hunch of bread'),
dimin. of ONF. cant (corresponding to OF. and
F. chant), 'corner'. See cant, 'slope'.

## cantlet
cantlet, п., a small cantle. — Formed fr. prec.
word with dimin. suff. -et.

## canto
canto, п., chief division of a long poem. — It.,
'song', fr. L. cantus, 'song', fr. cant-(um), pp.
stem of canere, 'to sing'. See cant, 'slang of
beggars'.

## canton
canton, п., a district. — F., prop, 'corner of land',
fr. It. cantone, augment, of canto, 'corner',
which is rel. to OF. cant, of s.m., whence E.
cant, 'slope' (q.v.)
Derivatives: canton, tr. v. (cp. F. cantonner),
canton-al, adj., canton-ed, adj., cantonment (q.v.)

## cantonment
cantonment, п., a camp for troops. — F. canton-
nement, fr. cantonner, 'to divide into cantons',
fr. canton. See prec. word and -ment.

## cantor
cantor, n. — L., 'singer, precentor', fr. cant-(um)
pp. stem of canere, 'to sing'. See cant, 'slang of
beggars', and agential suff. -or.
Derivatives: cantor-al, cantor-ial, adjs.

## cantas
cantas, п., a song. — L., fr. cant-(um), pp. stem
of canere, 'to sing'. See cant, 'slang of beggars'.

## Canuck
Canuck, п., in Canada: a French Canadian; in
the U.S.A.: a Canadian (slang). — From Indian
corruption of F. Canadien or E. Canadian.

## eanvas
eanvas, n. — OF. (= F.) canevas, prop, a blend
of Picard canevach and OF. chenevas, lit. 'made
of hemp, hempen', fr. OF. chaneve (F. chanvre),
'hemp', fr. L. cannabis, 'hemp', fr. Gk. κάννα-
βις. See hemp and cp. canvass.
Derivative: canvas, tr. v.

## canvass
canvass, tr. v., to discuss; intr. v., to solicit votes.
— Fr. canvus. To canvass orig. meant 'to sift
through canvas'. Cp. OF. canabasser, 'to
examine carefully', lit. 'to sift through canvas', fr.
OProvenc. canabas, 'canvas', which is rel. to
OF. canevas.
Derivative: canvass-er, n.

## canyon
canyon, canon, п., a narrow valley between cliffs.
— Sp. сайоп, 'deep, hollow gorge', augment, of
cano, 'tube', fr. L. canna, 'reed, cane, tube'. See
cane and cp. cnnal, cannon.
Derivative: canyon, canon, tr. and intr. v.

## canzone
canzone, п., a song. — It., fr. L. cantionem, ace.
of cantie, 'song', fr. cant-(um), pp. stem of
canere, 'to sing'. See cant, 'slang of beggars', and
cp. next word. Cp. also cbanson.

## canzonet
canzonet, п., a short song. — It. canzonetta,
dimin. of canzone, 'song'. See prec. word and -et.

## caoha
caoha, п., mahogany. — Sp., fr. a Caribbean
native word.

## caoutchouc
caoutchouc, n. — F., a Tupi loan word (prob.
through the medium of Sp. caucho).

## cap
cap, п., a covering for the head. — ME. cappe, fr.
OE. еяерре, 'hood, cap', fr. Late L. cappa. See
cape, 'cloak', and cp, words there referred to.
Derivatives: cap, tr. v., capp-ed, adj., capp-er,
п., capp-ing, п., capp-y, adj.

## capable
capable, adj. — F., fr. L. capabilis, 'able to grasp
or hold, capable', fr. capere, 'to catch, seize,
hold'. See captive and -able.
Derivatives: capobil-ity, п., capable-ness, п.,
сараЫ-у, adv.

## capacious
capacious, adj., holding much. — Formed with
suff. -ous fr. L. capax, gen capdeis, 'capable to
grasp or hold', fr. capere. See prec. word and
cp. cabbage, 'to pilfer'.
Derivatives: capacious-ly, adv., capacious-ness,n.

## capacitate
capacitate, tr. v., to render capable. — See next
word and verbal suff. -ate.
Derivative: capacitat-ion, n.

## capacity
capacity, п., ability to hold; ability. — F. capa-
cite, fr. L. capacitatem, ace. of capacitas,
'capability of holding much', fr. capax, gen. capacis.
See capacious and -Ity.

## cap-a-pie
cap-a-pie, adv., from head to foot. — OF. (de)

## cap a pie
cap a pie, 'from head to foot', fr. L. caput, 'head',

## ad
ad, 'to', and pedem, ace. of pes, 'foot' (see

## capital
capital, adj., ad-, and pedal). The F. equiv. is

## de pied en cap
de pied en cap, lit. 'from foot to head'.

## caparison
caparison, п., ornamented covering for horses;
outfit, equipment. — OF. caparasson (F. capa-
racon), fr. Sp. caparazon, 'caparison', fr.
OProvenc. caparasso, 'a mantle, with hood', fr. capa,
'hood', fr. Late L. cappa. See cape, 'cloak'.

## caparison
caparison, tr. v., to cover with caparisons. — F.
caparafonner, fr. caparacon. See caparison, n.

## cape
cape, п., a sleeveless cloak. — F., fr. OProvenc.
capa, fr. Late L. cappa, 'hood, mantle', which
is of uncertain origin. Cp. It. cappa, Sp. capa,
'cloak', which also derive fr. Late L. cappa. Cp.
cap, caparison, capeline, capuche, Capuchin,
chape, chapean, chapel, chapelet, chaperon,
chaplet, cope, 'a long cloak', escape, kepi,
schapska.

## cape
cape, п., a promontory. — F. cap, fr. It. capo,
fr. L. caput, 'head'. See eapltal, adj.

## capelin
capelin, п., a fish (Mallotus villosus). — F. cape-
Ian, capelin, lit. 'a beggarly priest', fr. OProvenc.
capelan, 'chaplain; fish'. See chaplain.

## capeline
capeline, п., ι) a small skullcap of iron worn by
soldiers in theMiddle Ages; 2) (med.) a bandage
for the head. — F., fr. It. cappellina, dimin. of
cappella, itself dimin. of cappa, fr. Late L. cappa,
'hood, mantle'. See cape, 'cloak', and cp. words
there referred to.

## Capelia
Capelia, п., name of a star; Alpha in the
Constellation Auriga (astron.) — L., 'she-goat',
dimin. of capra, 'she-goat', fem. of caper, 'goat'.
See cabriolet and cp. Caprella.

## caper
caper, п., a prickly shrub (Capparis spinosa). —
ME, caperis, caperes, fr. L. capparis [whence
also It. cappero [whence OF. caspres, F. capre)
and G. Kaper], tr. Gk. κάππαρις (whence Arab.
kabbar, ModPers. kabar); of unknown
etymology. The -s in ME. was mistaken for the pi.
and was consequently dropped.

## caper
caper, intr. v., to dance about, to prank. —
Shortened fr. capriole (q.v.)
Derivatives: caper, п., caper-er, п., caper-ing,
suff. adj., caper-ing-ly, adv.

## caper
caper, п., a privateer; its captain (hist.) — Du.
kaper, fr. kapen, 'to seize', which prob. derives
fr. Fris. kapia, 'to buy', used euphemistically in
the sense 'to take away', fr. кар, 'purchase', a
euphemistic term for 'piracy'. Fris. кар is rel.
to MDu. coop, Du. koop, OHG. kouf, ON. kaup,
etc., 'purchase'. See cheap, n.

## capa
capa, карп, п., name of the 1 lth letter of the
Hebrew alphabet. — See kaph.

## capercailzie
capercailzie, also capercaillie, n„ the largest
grouse, Tetrao urogallus. — Gael, capulcoille,
lit. 'horse of the woods'! fr. caput, 'horse' and
coille, 'wood'. Gael, capul is borrowed fr. L.
caballus, 'horse'. See cavalry.

## capbar
capbar, η., a toll levied by the Turks upon travelers
for protecting them (obsol.) — Fr. Arab, kha-
fdrah, 'protection', fr. khafara, 'he protected'.

## capias
capias, п., a writ of arrest (Jaw). — L., 'thou
mayest take', 2nd person sing. pres. subjunctive
of capere, 'to catch, seize, hold'. See captive.

## caplllaire
caplllaire, п., the maidenhair fern. — F. capil-
laire, fr. L. herba capillaris, 'the maidenhair', fr.
capillaris, 'pertaining to the hair', fr. capillus.
See capillary.

## capillarity
capillarity, п., the property of exerting capillary

next word and -ity.

## capillary
capillary, adj., hairlike; п., a very thin blood
vessel. — L. capillaris, 'pertaining to the hair',
fr. capillus, 'hair', which is prob. rel. to caput,
gen. capitis, 'head'. See capital, adj.

## enpistrate
enpistrate, adj., hooded. — L. capislratus, pp.
of capistrare, 'to halter', fr. capistrum, 'halter',
fr. capere, 'to catch, seize, hold'. See captive and
adj. suff. -ate and cp. capstan.

## capital
capital, adj. — F., fr. L. capitalis, 'pertaining to
the head, capital, chief, first', formed with suff.
•alis, fr. capul, gen. capitis, 'head', fr. I.-E.
*qap-ul, whence also OI. kaput-, 'head', in ka-
pucchalam, 'hair of the hind part of the head',
Goth, haubip, OE. hiafod, 'head'.· Cp. I.-E.
*qap-elo- in OI. kapalam, 'skull, potsherd, dish,
lid', kapali-, 'mendicant's bowl'. See head and cp.
capital, 'principal', capital, 'head of a column',
and chief. Cp. also achieve, ancipltaL biceps,
cabildo, cabotage, cadet, camail, camouflage,
Capita, cap-a-pie, cape, 'promontory', capitan, ca-

pitation, capitellnm, Cnpito, Capitol, capitulate,

## capital
capital, п., stock of money, principal. —Late L.
capitate, 'property', prop. neut. of the Latin
adjective capitalis, 'pertaining to the head, chief,
first'. Cp. It. capitate, .F. capital, G. Kapital,
'capital, principal', and see capital, adj. For
sense development cp. cattle.
Derivatives: capital-ism, п., capital-ist, п., capi-
tal-ist-ic, adj. ,capital-ize,tr.v.,capital-iz-ation,n.

## capital
capital, п., head of a column. — L. capitellum,
'little head', dimin. of caput, gen: capitis, 'head'.
See capital, adj., and cp. candillo.

## capitan
capitan, п., captain. — It. capitano, fr. Late L.
capitaneus, 'head, chief, fr. L. caput, gen.
capitis, 'head'. See capital, adj., and cp. captain,
chieftain.

## capitate
capitate, adj., head-shaped (бол) — L. capitatus,
fr. caput, gen. capitis, 'head'. See capital, adj.,
and adj. suff. -ate.
Derivative: capitat-ed, adj.

## capitation
capitation,n., tax payable by each person. —Late
L. capitdtio, gen. -dnis, 'poll tax', fr. L. caput,
gen. capitis, 'head'. See capital, adj., and -ation.

## capitellum
capitellum, п., a little head, a knob {anal, and

See capital, adj., and cp. chapter.

## Capito
Capito, п., a genus of fishes, the South American

## Cnpitol
Cnpitol, п., the temple of Jupiter on one of the

— L. Capitdlium, a derivative of caput, gen.
capitis, 'head'. See carrital, adj.

## capitoliae
capitoliae, adj., pertaimng to the Capitol in Rome
or to the hill on wrich it stood. — L. Capito-
llnus, fr. Capitdliur.. See prec. word and adj.
suff. -ine (representing L. -inus).

## capitular
capitular, adj., pertaining to a chapter. — ML.
capitularis, fr. L. capitulum, 'a small head,
chapter', dimin. of caput, gen. capitis, 'head'. See
capital, adj., and -ar and cp. chapter.

## capitulary
capitulary, adj., pertaining to a chapter. — See
prec. word and adj. suff. -ягу.

## capitulary
capitulary, п., a collection of decrees. — ML.
capiluiarium, fr. capilaldris. See capitular and
subst. suff. -ary.

## capitulate
capitulate, intr. v., to surrender on terms. — ML.
capituldtus, pp. of capituldre, 'to draw up the
heads of an agreement', fr. L. caput, gen. capitis,
'head'. See capital, adj., and verbal suff. -ate.
Derivative: capitulat-ion, n.
спроп, п., a castrated cock. — ME., fr. OE. capun,
fr. L. cdpdnem, ace. of capo, 'castrated cock'
(whence also Gk. κάπων, of s.m.), which is cogn.
with Gk. κόπτειν, 'to strike, cut, cut off", κόπος,
'a striking; toil, suffering, pain', κόμμα, 'a piece
cut off; a short clause', κοπίς, 'chopper, cleaver,
billhook', κοπεύς, 'chisel', fr. I.-E. base *(s)qap-,
*(s)qip-, *(s)qdp-, 'to cut', whence also Lith.
kapoju, карой, Lett. kapSju, kapal, 'to hew,
hack', OSlav. kopajg, kopati, Ίο dig', OE. ha-
melian (whence obsol. E. hamble), ON. hamla,
OFris. hfimelia, OHG. hamaldn, 'to mutilate',
OHG. hamal, 'mutilated' (whence MHG. hamel,
G. Hammel, 'wether'), MLG., MDu., Du. hamel,
'wether'. Cp. F. chapon, 'capon', fr. VL. *cappd-
nem, ace. of *cappd, corresponding to classical
L. capo. From the above base—with initial s—
derive also Gk. σκάπτειν, 'to dig out', σκαπάνη,
'spade, hoe', σκάφη, 'boat', lit. 'something dug
out', σκέπαρνος, 'carpenter's ax', σκόπελος, 'high
rock, peak', OSlav. skopiti, 'to castrate', sko-
pict, 'eunuch', Czech skopec, 'wether' (whence
MHG. sc/юрез, G. Schops, of s.m.), Lith. ska-
piCi, skdpti, 'to dig out, hollow out (a spoon)'.
Cp. hatchet Cp. also apocope, comma, Coptis,
kopeck, syncope. Cp. also scabbte, scapho-, scapula,
scopelism, scyphus.
Derivatives: capon, tr. v., caponier (q.v.), capon-
ize, tr. v., capon-iz-er, n.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:139 COLUMN:2 -->

## caponier
caponier, п., a construction placed across a ditch
(fort.) — F. caponniire, fr. Sp. caponera, prop,
'a coop or enclosure to fatten capons', applied
facetiously to a place affording shelter. See
prec. word and -Ier.

## caporal
caporal, a kind of tobacco. — F., lit. 'corporal'
(see corporal, п.); so called because it is superior
in quality to the common soldier's tobacco (as
the corporal is to the common soldier).

## eapot
eapot, п., the winning of all the tricks at the game
of piquet. — F. capot in /aire capot, 'to win all
the tricks at the game of piquet', adopted from
the sea term /aire capot, 'to capsize, upset';
capot prob. derives fr. Provenc. cap, 'head',
(fr. L. caput). For sense development cp. F.
chavirer, 'to capsize, upset', which derives fr.
Proveng. cap virar, 'to turn the head (of a
ship)'. See capital, adj.
Derivative: capot, v.

## Capparidaceae
Capparidaceae, n. pl„ the caper family (bot.) —
Formed fr. next word with suff. -aceae.

## Capparis
Capparis, п., a genus of plants of the caper family
(bot.) — L., fr. Gk. κάππαρις, 'caper'. See caper,
'a prickly plant'.

## Caprella
Caprella, п., a genus of Crustacea (zool.) —
ModL., lit. 'a little she-goat', dimin. of capra,
'she-goat'. See cabriolet and cp. Capella.

## capreol
capreol, capreole, п., a tendril (bot.) — L. capre-
olus, 'wild goat; tendril', fr. caper, 'goat'. See
cabriolet and cp. prec. and next word.
Derivative: capreol-ate, adj.

## Capreolus
Capreolus, п., a genus of mammals, the roe deer
(zool.) — L., 'the wild goat', augmentative
formed fr. caper, 'goat'. See cabriolet and cp. prec.
word.

## capri-
capri-, combining form meaning 'resembling the
goat'. — L. Capri-, fr. caper, gen. capri, 'goat'.
See cabriolet.

## capric
capric, adj., pertaining to a goat. — Formed with
suff. -ic fr. L. capra, 'goat'. See cabriolet.

## capric
capric, adj., pertaining to a fatty acid, QoHjoOj
(chem.) — See prec. word; so called from its
smell. Cp. caproic

## capriccio
capriccio, п., a kind of free composition (mus.) —
It., whence F. caprice. See next word.

## caprice
caprice, п., a whim. — F., fr. It. capriccio, 'a
shiver, sudden start, a whim', which is prob.
compounded of capo (fr. L. caput), 'head' and
riccio (fr. L. ericius), 'hedgehog'. See capital,
adj., and urchin.

## capricious
capricious, adj. — F. capricieux, fr. It. capriccioso,
fr. capriccio. See capriccio, caprice and -ous.
Derivatives: capricious-ly, adv., capricious-
ness, n.

## Capricorn
Capricorn, п., a constellation represented by the
ancients in the form of a goat. — F. capricorne,
fr. L. Capricornus, lit. 'having horns similar to
those of a goat', compounded of caper, 'goat',
and cornu, 'horn', prop, loan translation of
Αιγόκερως, the old Greek name of this
constellation. See eabriolet and horn and cp. corn,
'hardened skin'.

## caprincation
caprincation, п., artificial pollination of figs by
means of the stings of insects. — L. caprificaiid,
gen. -dnis, 'ripening of figs(by thestingingof gall-
insects)', fr. capriftedtus, pp. of caprificare, 'to
ripen figs', fr. caprificus, 'wild fig', lit. 'goat fig', fr.
caper, 'goat', and ficus, 'fig'. See cabriolet, flgand
-arion.

## caprifig
caprifig, п., the wild fig. — A hybrid coined fr. L.
caprificus and E. fig. See prec. word.

## Caprifoliaceae
Caprifoliaceae, n. pi., a family of plants, the
honey-suckle family (bot.) — ModL., formed
with suff. -aceae fr. ML. caprifelium. See
Caprifolium.

## caprifolinceous
caprifolinceous, adj. — See prec. word and
-aceous.

## Caprifolium
Caprifolium, п., a genus of plants (bot.) — ML.,
compounded of L. caper, 'goat', and folium,
'leaf, See cabriolet and folio.

## Caprimulgidae
Caprimulgidae, n. pi., a family of birds, the
goatsuckers (ornithol.) — ModL., formed with suff.
-Jdae, fr. L. caprimulgus. See next word.

## Caprimulgus
Caprimulgus, п., a genus of birds (ornithol.) —-
L. caprimulgus, 'a milker of goats', also the
name of a bird, compounded of caper, 'goat'
(see cabriolet), and mulgire, 'to milk', which is
cogn. with Gk. άμέλγειν, Чо squeeze out, to

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:139 COLUMN:3 -->
milk', Goth, miluks, OE. meolc, 'milk'. See milk,

## caprine
caprine, adj., pertaining to a goat. — L. caprinus,
fr. caper, 'goat'. See cabriolet and adj. suff. -ine
(representing L. -inus) and cp. capric.

## capriole
capriole, п., a leap, caper. — F., cabriole,
capriole, fr. It. capriolare, 'to leap like a goat, to
caper', fr. capriuolo, 'roebuck'. See cabriolet.
Derivative: capriole, intr. v.

## caproic
caproic, adj., pertaining to a fatty acid, QHu03
(chem.) — Formed with suff. -ole fr. L. caper,
'goat'; so called from its smell. See cabriolet,
and cp. capric

## capsa
capsa, п., a repository, a box (esp. for books). —
L. See capsule.

## Capsella
Capsella, п., a genus of plants of the mustard
family (bot.) — ModL., dimin. of L. capsa,
'box, receptacle'. See capsule and -ella.

## Capsicum
Capsicum, п., a genus of plants of the potato
family (bot.) — ModL., irregularly formed, fr. L.
capsa. See case, 'box', and cp. capsa, capsule,

## capsize
capsize, tr. and intr. v., to overturn; to upset. —
Of uncertain origin.
Derivatives: capsize, п., capsiz-al, n.

## capstan
capstan, п., a device for hauling up anchors. —
F. cabestan, fr. OProven?: cabestan, fr. cabe-
stran, pres. part, used as a noun, fr. L. capist-
rare, 'to tie with a halter', fr. capistrum, 'halter',
fr. capere, 'to catch, seize, hold'. Cp. F. chevetre,
'halter', which also derives fr. L. capistrum. See
captive and words there referred to and cp. esp.
capistrate.

## capsule
capsule, n. — L. capsula, 'a small box or chest',
dimin. of capsa, 'repository, box, chest, case'.
See case, 'box', and cp. Capsa, Capsella,
Capsicum. For the ending see suff. -ale.
Derivatives: capsule, tr. v., capsul-ar, capsul-ate,
capsul-at-ed, adjs., capsul-at-ion, п., capsul-er, n.

## captain
captain, n. — ME. capitain, fr. OF. (= F.) capi-
taine, fr. Late L. capitaneus, 'head, chief, fr.
L. caput, gen. capitis, 'head'. See capital, adj.,
and cp. capitan.
Derivatives: captain, tr. and intr. v., captain-cy,
п., captain-ry, п., captain-ship, n.

## captation
captation, п., the reaching after something. — F.,
fr. L. captdtidnem, ace. of captatid, 'a reaching
after, a catching at', fr. captains, pp. of capture,
'to catch, seize; to strive after', freq. of capere
(pp. captus), 'to catch, seize, hold'. See captive
and -ation and cp. next word. Cp. also the
second element in mercaptan.

## caption
caption, п., ι) the act of taking; 2) heading. —
L. captio, gen. -dnis, 'a catching, seizing,
holding', fr. captus, pp. of capere. See captive and
-ion and cp. prec. word. Cp. also usucaption.

## captious
captious, adj., faultfinding, carping. — F. cap·
tieux (fem. caplieuse), fr. L. captidsus,
'fallacious', fr. captio, gen. -dnis, 'a seizing, deception,
fallacious argument, sophism', fr. captus, pp. of
capere. See prec. word and -ous.
Derivatives: captious-ly, adv., captious-ness, n.

## captivate
captivate, tr. v., to capture the attention of; to
fascinate. — Orig. 'to capture', fr. L. captJvdtus, pp.
of captivare, 'to take captive, to capture', fr.
captivus.fiee next word and verbal suff. -ate.
Derivatives: captivat-ing, adj., captivat-ing-ly,
adv., captivat-ion, п., captivat-or, n.

## captive
captive, adj. and n. — F. captif (fem. captive),
fr. L. captivus, 'caught, taken prisoner', fr.
captus, pp. of capere, 'to catch, seize, take hold of,
take, receive, hold, contain', whence L. capsa,
'repository, box, chest, case', capulus,
'sarcophagus, bier'; fr. I.-E. base *qap-, 'to seize, hold,
contain', whence also Gk. κάπτείν, 'to swallow
greedily, gulp down', κάπη, 'manger', κώπη,
'handle, handle of an oar, haft', Alb. кар, Ί
take, seize', kam, Ί have', Lett. kdmp(j)u, kampt,
'to seize', Goth, hafjan, OE. hebban, 'to raise,
lift', Goth, haban, OE. habban, 'to have',
and prob. also OI. kapafi, 'two handfuls'.
See heave and bave and cp. words there referred
to. Cp. also accept, anticipate, apperceive,
apperception, nucupate, cabas, cabbage, 'to pilfer',
cable, cachalot, caisson, caitiff (which is a

## doublet of captive)
doublet of captive), cajn, cajeta, cajole, capable,

## capacious
capacious, capacity, capias, capistrate, capsa,

## Capsella
Capsella, Capsicum, capstan, capsule, captation,

## caption
caption, captious, captor, capture, Carpocapsa,

## case
case, 'box, chest', casement, cash, catch, chara-

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:140 COLUMN:1 -->
banc, chase, conceive, concept, conception, cop,
'to catch', Copepoda, decefpt, deceive, deception,
disciple, discipliae, emancipate, except, excipient,
forceps, imperceptible, incept, inception,
intercept, intussusception, mancipate, mercaptant,
municipal, nuncupative, occupy, participate,
perceive, percept, perception, precept, preceptor,
prince, principal, principle, purchase, recado,
receipt, receive, recept, receptacle, reception,
receptive, recet, recipe, recover, recuperate,
susceptible, usucapion.

## captivity
captivity, n. — F. captiviti, fr. L. caplivildtem,
ace. of captlvitas, fr. captivus. See prec. word
and -ity.

## captor
captor, n. — L., 'a catcher', fr. caplus, pp. of
capere, 'to catch, seize, hold'. See captive and
agential suff. -or.

## capture
capture, n. — L. captura, 'a seizing, taking', fr.
caplus, pp. of capere. See'captive and -иге.
Derivatives: capture, tr. v., captur-er, n.

## capuche
capuche, п., a hood; a cowl. — F. capuche, ca-
puce, fr. It. cappuccio, 'cowl*, dimin. formed fr.
cappa. See cape, 'cloak'.
Derivative: capuch-ed, adj.

## Capuchin
Capuchin,n.,a monk of a Franciscan order
founded in 1526. — F. capucin, earlier also capuchin,
fr. It. cappuccino, dimin. of cappuccio, 'cowl'
(see prec. word); so called from the pointed
cowl worn by the members of this monastic
order.

## capybara
capybara, п., a South American rodent (Hydro-
choerus capybara). — A Tupi word. Cp. Cnvin,
cavy.

## car
car, n. — ME. carre, fr. ONF. carre, fr. VL.
сапа, a word of Celtic origin; ep. Olr., MW.
carr, 'cart, waggon', Bret, karr, 'chariot', L.
carrus, of the same origin and meaning, gave
birth to ONF. car, F. char. L. currus, 'chariot',
is independent cf the above Celtic words, but
cognate with them. See course and cp. career,
cargo, caricature, cariole, cark, caroche, car-
roccio, carry, carriage, charabanc, charge, chariot.
Derivative: car, tr. and intr. v.

## carabao
carabao, п., water buffalo. — Sp., from
Philippine native name.

## Carabidae
Carabidae, n. pi., a family of beetles (entomol.) —
ModL., formed with suff. -Idae fr. Gk. καραβος,
'homed beetle'. See scarab and cp. Caridea.

## carabineer
carabineer, п., a mounted soldier armed with a
carbine. — F. carabinier, fr. carabine, 'carbine*.
See carbine.

## carabinieri
carabinieri, n. pi., the Italian police. — II., pi. of
carabiniere, fr. F. carabinier. See carabineer.

## caracal
caracal, п., a kind of lynx. — F., fr. Turk, qarah
qulak, 'black ear'.

## caracara
caracara, п., a kind of large South American
bird. — A Tupi word of imitative origin.

## carack
carack, n. — See carrack.

## caracole
caracole, п., half-turn in riding. — F., fr. Sp.
caracal, lit. 'snail', which is prob. a blend of
L. scarabaeus, 'a beetle', and conchylium (fr. Gk.
καγχύλιον), 'a shell fish'. See scarab and cockle.

## caracole
caracole, intr. v., to make a caracole. — F. cara-
coler, fr. caracole. See caracole, n.

## carafe
carafe, п., a glass bottle. — F., fr. Sp. garrafa, fr.
Arab, gharraf, 'drinking jug', fr. gharafa, 'he
drew water'.

## carambole
carambole, п., a carom (billiards). — F., fr. Sp.
carambola. See carom.

## caramel
caramel, п., burnt sugar. — F., fr. OSp. caramel
(now carameto), a blend of ML. cannamella,
'sugar cane', (see cane and melliferous) and Sp.
caramillo, 'reed', fr. L. calamellus, dimin. of
calamus, 'reed' (see calamary).

## Carangidae
Carangidae, n. pi., a family of fishes (ichthyol).—
ModL., formed with suff. -idae, fr. ModL.
Caranx, name of the type genus, fr. Sp. caranga,
name of a kind of flatfish, a word of unknown
origin.

## carangold
carangold, adj., pertaining to, or resembling, tne
Carangidae. — A hybrid coined fr. Sp. caranga
(see prec. word) and Gk. -οειδής, 'like', fr. είδος,
'form, shape'. See -oid.

## Caranx
Caranx, п., the type genus of the Carangidae
(ichthyol.) — ModL. See Carangidae.

## carapace
carapace, п., the covering of the back of certain
animals, esp. the upper shell of the turtle, crab
etc. — F., fr. Sp. carapacho, which is of

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:140 COLUMN:2 -->
unknown origin. Cp. calipash, calipee.

## carat
carat, п., unit of weight for precious stones and
pearls. — F., fr. ML. carratus (whence also It.
carato), fr. Arab, ghat, 'fruit of the carob tree;
weight of 4 grains', fr. Gk. κεράτιον, 'a little
horn; fruit of the carob tree; carat', dimin. of
κέρας, gen. κέρατος, 'horn'. See horn and cp.
corn, 'hardened skin'.

## caratch
caratch, п., formerly, a tribute imposed by the
Arabs and Turks upon their non-Mohammedan
subjects. — Arab, khardj, kharj, 'tribute',
borrowed fr. Aram, karga, 'tribute', through the
medium of Persian (Aramaic was the official
language of the Persian kingdom for many
centuries).

## caravan
caravan, n. — F. caravane, fr. Pers. karwdn,
'company of travelers, caravan', which is rel.
to OI. karabhdh, 'camel, young camel, young
elsphant'.
Derivatives: caravan, tr. and intr. v., caravan-
eer, n.

## caravanserai
caravanserai, п., Eastern inn, esp. for caravans.
— F. caravanserai, fr. Pers. karwunsardi, fr.
kibwan (see caravan) and sarat, 'mansion, inn',
which is prob. rel. to Avestic urdyeinti, 'they
protect', Ol. trayate, 'protects'.

## caravel
caravel, carvel, п., any of various kinds of light
vessels. — F. caravelle, fr. Sp. carabela, dimin.
formed fr. carabo, 'a small vessel', fr. Arab.
qurib, 'bark', which is traceable to Gk. κίραβος,
'horned beetle; crayfish; a light ship'. See scarab.

## caraway
caraway,п., a plant with aromatic seeds. — ME
carawai, fr. OSp. (= Sp.) alcaravea (whence
Sp. carvi), fr. Arab. al-karawiya\ fr. al-, 'the',
and karawiya', fr. L. carum, careum, fr. Gk.
κάρον, κάρεον, 'caraway', which is of uncertain
origin. Cp. skirret.
:arb-, form of carbo- before a vowel.

## carbamate
carbamate, п., a salt of carbamic acid (chem.) —
See carbamic and -ate.

## carbamic
carbamic, adj., pertaining to the organic acid
CONH2OH (chem.) — Formed with suff. -ic
from the abbreviation of carbonic and amide.
See carbon and amide.

## carbasus
carbasus, п., lint. — L., fr. Gk. κάρπασος, 'flax,
cotton', which is prob. borrowed fr. OI.
karpasah, . 'cotton brush, cotton', whence also
ModPers. kirpas. Arm. kerpas, Arab, kirbas,
Heb. karpds (Esther г: 6), 'cotton, fine linen'.
See Manfred Mayrhofer, A Concise
Etymological Dictionary, 1, p. 174 s.v. karpasah.
According to Porzig in Zeitschrift fur Indologie
und Iranistik, 5, 272 ff., both OI. karpasah and
Gk. κάρπασος derive from a language of the
Mediterranean or Asia Minor.

## carbide
carbide, п., a compound of carbon with an elec-
tropositiveelement (chem.)—See carbo- and -ide.

## carbine
carbine, п., a short rifle. — F. carabine, 'carbine',
fr. carabin, 'carabineer', fr. MF. calabrim, fr.
ML. Calabrinus, 'of, or pertaining to, Calabria'.
Accordingly the original meaning of F. carabine
is '(rifle) made in Calabria'. For the ending see
adj. suff. -ine (representing L. -inus).

## carbinol
carbinol, п., methanol or any alcohol derived
from it (chem.) — Coined by the German
organic chemist Hermann Kolbe (1818-84) in 1868
fr. carbin (see carbon), a name used by him to
denote the methyl radical, and -ol, a suff.
denoting an alcohol.

## carbo-
carbo-, before a vowel carb-, combining form for
carbon (chem.) — See carbon.

## carbohydrate
carbohydrate, п., (chem.) — Compounded of
carbo- and hydrate.

## carbolate
carbolate, п., a salt of carbolic acid (chem.) —
See carbol- and chem. suff. -ate.

## carbol-
carbol-, combining form denoting the presence
of carbolic acid (chem.) — See next word.

## carbolic
carbolic, adj., pertaining to carbon and oil. —
Compounded of L. carbo, 'coal', and oleum,
'oil'. See carbon, oil and -ic.

## carbolize
carbolize, tr. v., to sterilize with carbolic acid
(chem.) — Formed fr. carbol- and -ize.

## carbon
carbon, п., a nonmetallic element (chem.) — L.
carbo, gen. -dnis, 'coal, charcoal', prob. standing
for "car-dhd and derived fr. I.-E. base *ker-,
'to singe, burn, glow'. See hearth and cp.
cremate. Cp. also carbonado, Carbonari, carbuncle.
Derivatives: carbon-ic, adj., carbon-ize, tr. v.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:140 COLUMN:3 -->

## carbonaceous
carbonaceous, adj., 1) coaly; 2) pertaining to, or
containing, carbon. — Formed with suff. -ace-
ous fr. L. carbo, gen. -dnis, 'coal'. Seeprec. word.

## carbonado
carbonado, п., a broiled piece of meat. — Sp.
carbonado, prop, subst. use of the fem. pp. of car-
bonar. See next word.
Derivative: carbonado, tr. v.

## carbonado
carbonado, п., an opaque kind of diamond. —
Sp., lit. 'carbonated', pp. of carbonar, 'to
carbonate*, fr. carbon, 'coal', fr. L. carbonem, ace.
of carbo. See carbon and -ado.

## carborundum
carborundum, п., silicon carbide (SiC), an
abrasive. — Coined fr. carbon and corundum.

## carboxyl
carboxyl, п., a univalent radical, containing
carbon, oxygen and hydrogen (COOH) (chem.) —
Compounded of carbon, oxygen and -yl.
Derivatives: carboxyl-ate, n. and tr. v., car-
boxyl-ation, n.

## carboy
carboy, п., a large glass bottle. — Pers. qaraba.
Cp. Arab. qirbah, *a large leathern bottle'.

## carbuncle
carbuncle, п., I) formerly, a red gem; now a
garnet with a convex rounded surface; 2) a painful
inflammation under the skin. — ME., fr. ONF.
carbuncle (corresponding to OF. charboncle,
charbucle), fr. L. carbunculus, 'a small coal; a
bright, reddish kind of precious stone; a kind
of tumor', dimin. of carbo, gen. -onis, 'coal*.
See carbon and cp. escarbuncle.
Derivative: carbuncl-ed, adj.

## carbuncular
carbuncular, adj.,— Formed with suff. -ar fr. L.
carbunculus. See prec. word.

## carburet
carburet, tr. v., to combine with carbon (chem.)
— Formed fr. carbon on analogy of sulfuret.
Derivatives: carburet-ant, п., carburet-ion, n.

## carburetor
carburetor, carburettor, п., an apparatus for
carbureting gas or air. — Formed fr. prec. word
with agential suff. -or.

## carcanet
carcanet, п., an ornamental chain. — Dimin. of
F. carcan, 'iron collar; necklace, carcanet;
pillory', fr. ML. carcannum (whence also OProv-
εης. carcan, 'necklace'), which is of uncertain
origin. For the ending see suff. -et.

## carcass
carcass, п., a dead body. — F. carcasse, fr.
earlier Charcots, carcois, of uncertain origin, it. car-
cassa, of s.m., is prob. a French loan word.

## carcel
carcel, п., a French unit of illuminating power. —
Prop, 'the illuminating power of the light of a
Carcel lamp', which is named after the French
clockmaker Bertrand-Guillaume Carcel (1750-
]8t2), its inventor.

## career
career, п., prison. — L. See incarcerate.

## Carcharias
Carcharias, п., a genus of sharks (ichthyol.) —
ModL., fr. Gk. καρχαρίας, 'a kind of shark*,
lit. 'the fish with the sawlike teeth', fr. κάρχαρος,
'sawlike, jagged, pointed, sharp', which is cogn.
with OI. kharah, 'rough, sharp, hard', and prob.
also with Toch. A tsar, 'rough, sharp'.

## Carchariidae
Carchariidae, n. pi., a family of sharks (ichlhyol.)
— ModL., formed from prec. word with suff.
-Idae.

## carcinoma
carcinoma, п., a form of cancer (med.) — L.
carcinoma, fr. Gk. καρκίνωμα, gen. καρκινώματος,
'ulcer, cancer', fr. καρκίνος, 'crab, cancer*. See
cancer and -oma.
Derivative: carcinomat-ous, adj.

## carcinomatoid
carcinomatoid, adj., having the shape of a
carcinoma (med.) — Compounded of Gk.
καρκίνωμα (see prec. word) and -οειδής, 'like', fr.
είδος, 'form, shape*. See -Old.
сагсооп, п., manager, clerk (Anglo-Ind.) — Ma-
rathi karkun, fr. Pers. кйг-кйп, 'manager', lit.
'doer of what is to be done', fr. I.-E. base *q"er-,
'to make, form, shape'. See Sanskrit and cp.
words there referred to.

## card
card, п., a machine for combing hair, wool, etc. —
F. carde, 'chard, teasel, card', fr. OProvenc. car-
do, back formation fr. cardar, 'to card', fr. L.
carduus, 'thistle", which is related to carro, car-
rere, 'to card (wool)', from a basic form *carri-
dus, 'that which scrapes', fr. I.-E. base *qars-,
'to scrape, scratch, rub'. See harsh and cp. car-
doncillo, cardoon, Cardnus, Carex, carline thistle,
carminative, carrizo, chard.

## card
card, tr. v., to comb with a card. — F. carder,
fr. carde. See prec. word.
Derivatives: card-ed, adj., card-er, n.

## card
card, п., a piece of pasteboard for playing. — F.
carte, fr. Late L. carta, 'a leaf of paper; paper',

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:141 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: CARDAMINE | 114 -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:141 COLUMN:1 -->
fr. L. charta, 'a leaf of the Egyptian papyrus;
papyrus; paper', fr. Gk. χάρτης, of s.m., a
foreign word, possibly of Egypt, origin. Cp.
carte blanche, carte de visile, cartel, cartoon,
cartouche, cartridge, cartulary, chart, charter,
ecarte, skat.

## Cardamine
Cardamine, п., a genus of plants of the mustard
family {hot.) — ModL., fr. L. cardamina, fr. Gk.
καρδαμίνη, 'a kind of cress', a word formed by
Dioscorides fr. κάρδαμον, 'cress', which is of
uncertain origin. Cp. next word.

## cardamom
cardamom, cardamum, п., an aromatic fruit. —
F. cardamome, fr. L. cardamomum, fr. Gk. καρ-
δάμωμαν, which is compounded of κάρδαμον,
'cress', and αμωμον, 'a spice plant'. See
Cardamine and Amomus. The contraction of the two
elements into καρδάμωμον from *καρδαμάμω-
μον is due to haplology.

## Cardanic
Cardanic, adj., Cardan joint, Cardan shaft,
Cardan's solution. — Na med after the Italian
mathematician and physician Geronimo Cardano
(1501-76).

## cardiac
cardiac, adj. (anat.), 1) pertaining to the heart;
2) pertaining to the upper part of the stomach.
— F. cardiaque, fr. L. cardiacus, fr. Gk.
καρδιακός, 'pertaining to the heart', fr. καρδία,
'heart'. See cardio- and -ac.
Derivative: cardiac-al, adj.

## cardialgia
cardialgia, n. (med.), 1) pain in the region of the
heart; 2) heartburn. — Medical L.,
compounded of Gk. καρδία, 'heart', and άλγος, 'pain*.
See cardio- and -algia.

## cardigan jacket
cardigan jacket, cnrdigan. — Named after James
Thomas Brudenell, the 7th Earl of Cardigan
(1797-1868).

## cardinal
cardinal, adj. — F., fr. L. cardinalis, 'principal,
chief, fr. cardo, gen. cardinis, 'hinge of a door,
pivot; that on which something turns', which is
of uncertain origin. Perh. it derives fr. 1-Е. base
*(s)qerad-, 'to turn, swing; leap, jump, bound',
whence OI. kardati, 'leaps, hops', Gk. κράδη,
'quivering spray at the end of a branch', κραδάω,
κραδαίνω, I brandish, shake', perh. also κόρδας,
'dance in a comedy'. Base *(s)qerad- is a
-(/-enlargement of base *(s)qer-, 'to leap, jump,
bound', whence Gk. σκαίρω, Ί leap, skip,
bound'. See Scarus and cp. ceruscate, horse,
rathe, rather.
Derivatives: cardinal, n. (q.v.), cardinal-ly, adv.

## cardinal
cardinal, n. — F., fr. Eccles. L. cardinalis (short
for cardinalis ecclesiae Romanae, orig. applied
to various dignitaries of the church), fr. L.
cardinalis, 'principal, chief. See cardinal, adj.

## cardinalate
cardinalate, п., the rank of a cardinal. — F. car-
dinalat, fr. Eccles. L. cardinalatus, fr. cardinalis.
See prec. word and subst. suff. -ate.

## cardio-
cardio-, before a vowel cardi-, combining form
meaning'pertaining to the heart'.—Gk.κάρδιο-,
καρδι-, fr. καρδία, 'heart'. See heart and cp.
cardiac, carditis. Cp. also the second element in
dexiocardia, diplocardiac, endocardium, epi-
cardium, megalocardia, pericardium, myocardia.

## cardiogram
cardiogram, п., the tracing made by the
cardiograph. — Compounded of cardio- and Gk.
γράμμα, 'that which is written'. See -gram.

## cardiograph
cardiograph, п., an instrument for recording the
movement of the heart. — Compounded of
cardio- and Gk. -γράφος, fr. γράφειν, 'to write'.
See -graph.

## cardiology
cardiology, п., the study of the heart. —
Compounded of cardio- and Gk. -λογία, fr. -λόγος1,
'one who speaks (in a certain manner); one who
deals (with a certain topic)'. See -logy.
Derivatives: cardiohg-ical, adj., cardiolog-ist, n.

## Cardiospcrmum
Cardiospcrmum, п., a genus of plants of the
soapberry family (hot.) — ModL., compounded of
cardio- and Gk. σπέρμα, 'seed, sperm'. See sperm.

## carditis
carditis, п., inflammation of the heart (med.) —
Medical L., coined by the French physician Jean-
Nicolas Corvisart (1775-1821) fr. Gk. καρδία,
'heart' (see cardio-), and suff. -itis.

## cardoncillo
cardoncillo, п., a kind of cactus. — Sp., dimin.
of cardan, 'teasel', fr. Late L. cardonem, ace. of
cardo, 'thistle'. See next word.

## cardoon
cardoon, п., the globe artichoke. — F. cardon,
fr. Proven?, cardon, prop, 'thistle', fr. Late L.
cardonem, ace. of cardo, 'thistle', which is rel. to
L. carduus, 'thistle'. See card, 'machine for

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:141 COLUMN:2 -->
combing' and cp. words there referred to.

## Carduus
Carduus, п., a genus of prickly herbs (bot.) —
L. carduus, 'thistle'. See prec. word.

## care
care, n. — ME. care, fr. OE. саги, cearu, 'anxiety,
sorrow, care', rel. to OS. kara, 'sorrow', OHG.
chara, 'lament', Goth, kara, 'sorrow', OS. (mod)
karag, 'anxious, sad, sorrowful', OE. cearig,
MDu. carich, 'sad, sorrowful', Du. karig,
'scanty, frugal', OHG. karag, 'anxious1, MHG.
karc, karg, 'shrewd, clever', G. karg, 'stingy,
scanty'; fr. Teut. *karo, 'sorrow, care'. These
words are cpgn. with Gk. γηρυς. Dor. γίρυς,
'voice, sound', Arm. cicarn, 'swallow', cicafnuk,
'nightingale', Ossetic zar, 'song', zarun, 'to sing',
L. garrire, 'to chat, talk, chatter', W. garm,
Olr. gair, gairm, W. gawr, 'noise, cry', Toch.
karye, 'care'. AH these words derive from the
I.-E. imitative base 'gar-, 'to shout, cry'. The
sense development of Toch. karye, 'care', E. care
and the related Teut. words may be illustrated
by the following stages: cry—lamentation—
grief. Cp. chary, cur, garrulous, Gerygone. Cp.
also German.
Derivatives: care-ful, adj., care-ful-ly, adv., care-
ful-ness, п., care-less, adj., care-less-ly, adv.,
care-less-ness, n.

## care
care, intr. v. — OE. cearian, rel. to OS., Goth.
kardn, 'to sorrow', OHG. charon, 'to lament',
and to OE. гаги, 'anxiety, sorrow, care'. See
care, n.

## careen
careen, tr. and intr. v., to cause (a ship) to turn
aside. — F. cariner, carener, lit. 'to expose a
ship's keel', fr. carine, carine, 'keel of a ship',
fr. dial. It. carena, fr. L. carina, of s.m., orig.
'shell of a nut', which is cogn. with Gk. κάρυον,
'nut, walnut', καρύα, 'the walnut iree', and prob.
also with OI. karakah, 'coconut; water vessel
made from coconut'. Cp. Carya, karyo-, and
the first element in gillyflower. Cp. also carina.
For the sense development of L. carina ср. Е.
hull, 'the body of a ship', prop, figurative use of
hull, 'husk'.
Derivatives: careen, п., careen-age, п., careen-
er, n.

## career
career, п., a running, course; course through life.
— F. carriere, 'racecourse, career*, fr. It. car-
riera, 'wagon', fr. Late L. carraria via, 'road for
vehicles', fr. carrus, 'a four-wheeled wagon'. See
car and cp. chariot, carry, carriage.
Derivatives: career, intr. v., career-er, п.,
careerist (q.v.)

## careerist
careerist, п., a person interested chiefly in his
career. — A hybrid coined fr. career and -ist.
a suff. of Greek origin.

## caress
caress, п., an act of endearment. — F. caresse,
back formation fr. caresser. See caress, v.

## caress
caress, tr. v., 1) to touch endearingly; 2) to
flatter. — F. caresser, fr. It. carezzare, lit. 'to
cherish', fr. caro, 'dear', fr. L. cams, of s.m. See
charity and cp. cherish.
Derivatives: caress-ing, adj., carress-ing-ly, adv.,
carress-ive, adj., carress-ive-ly, adv.

## caret
caret, п., the mark /\ used in writing to show
where something is to be added. — L. caret, 'it
is without, is wanting*, fr. carere, 'to be
without, be wanting, be free from, abstain from*.
See chaste.

## Carex
Carex, п., a genus of plants including the sedge
family (bot.) — L. carex, 'rush, sedge', possibly
rel. to carrere, *cdrere, 'to card', so that carex
would have orig. denoted 'the scratching plant'.
See card, 'machine for combing', and cp. car-
rizo.

## carfax
carfax, п., place where four roads meet. — ME.
carfourkes, fr. OF. carreforcs, pi. of carreforc
(F. carrefour), 'crossroads', fr. Late L. quadri-
furcum, of s.m., prop. neut. of the Latin adj.
quadrifweus, 'having four forks'. See quadri-
and fork.

## cargo
cargo, n. — Sp., 'load, burden', fr. cargar, 'to
load', fr. VL. carricare, fr. L. carrus, 'wagon'.
See charge and cp. car, cark.

## Carib
Carib, п., Caiiban, adj., Caribbean, adj. —
Caribbean galibi, 'strong men'. See cannibal.

## caribou
caribou, п., the N. American reindeer. — A
Canadian F. word of Algonquian origin; cp. Mic-
mac khalibu, lit. 'pawer, scratcher, shoveler'.

## caricature
caricature, n. — F., fr. It. caricalura, 'a load,

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:141 COLUMN:3 -->
overloading', fr. caricare, 'to load, charge', fr.
VL. carricare, 'to load a car', fr. L. carrus, 'car'
(see car and charge, v.) Accordingly caricature
prop, means 'an excess in drawing or painting'.
For the ending see suff. -ure.
Derivatives: caricature, tr. v., caricaturist (q.v.)

## caricaturist
caricaturist, n. — A hybrid coined fr. It. cari-
catura (see caricature) and -ist, a suff. of Greek
origin.

## Caridea
Caridea, п., a group of crustaceans (zool.) —
ModL., formed with suff. -idea fr. Gk. κδρίς,
gen. καρίδος, 'shrimp, prawn', which is prob.
rel. to καραβος, 'horned beetle'. See scarab and
cp. Carabidae. Cp. also Epicarides, Syncarlda.

## caries
caries, п., decay (med.) — L. caries, 'decay,
rottenness', fr. I.-E. base *ker-, 'to hurt, hit',
whence also Gk. κήρ, 'death, destruction',
ακήρατος, 'unhurt', κεραΐζειν (for *κεραΗζειν),
'to lay waste', κεραυνός Ifor "κερα-f (ε)νός],
'thunderbolt, lightning', lit. 'smasher, crusher'.
OI. sjrnati, 'breaks, crushes', stryate, sirydte,
'falls asunder', Olr. ar-a-chrinim, Ί fall to
pieces', irchre, 'fall, ruin', crin, 'withered, faded'.
Cp. cerauno- and the second element in sincere,

## carillon
carillon, п., musical bells. — F., 'peal of bells',
fr. OF. quarregnon, carignon, fr. VL. quadrini-
dnem, ace. of 'quadrinid, refashioned on
analogy of words beginning with quadri- (see qna-
dri-), fr. L. quaternion 'a group of four things'
(here used in the sense of 'a group of four
bells'). See quaternion,

## carina
carina, п., a keel-like part (anat., bot. and zool.)
— L., 'shell of a nut; keel of a ship'. See careen,

## carinate
carinate, adj., shaped like the keel of a ship. —
L. carinatus, pp. of carinare, 'to supply with a
shell', fr. carina, 'shell of a nut, keel of a ship'.
See careen and adj. suff. -ate.
Derivatives: carinate, п., carinat-ion, n.

## cariole
cariole, carriole, п., a small light carriage. — F.
carriole, fr. OProvenc. carriola, dimin. of carri,
fr. VL. 'carrium, fr. L. carrus, 'wagon'. It.
carriola is also borrowed fr. OProvenc. carriola.
See car and -ole.

## carious
carious, adj., decayed. ·— L. cariosus, 'decayed,
rotten', fr. caries. See caries and -ous.
Derivative: carious-ness, n.

## cark
cark, intr. v., to be anxious. — ME. carken, fr.
ONF. carquier, corresponding to OF. chargier
(F. charger), 'to load', fr. VL. carricare, 'to put
a load on'. The orig. meaning of cark was 'to
load'. See charge.
Derivatives: cark-ing, adj., cark-ing-ly, adv.

## cark
cark, п., anxiety. — ME., fr. AF. carque, karke,
fr. ONF. carche, corresponding to OF. (= F.)
charge, fr. ONF. carquier, resp. OF. chargier.
See prec. word.

## carl
carl, п., a fellow (Scot.) — ON. karl, 'a man', rel.
to OE. ceorl, 'a man of low degree'. See churl
and cp. Carl, Charles.

## Carl
Carl, masc. PN. — G. Karl. See Charles and cp.
carl.

## carline
carline, п., an old woman (Scot.) — ON. ker-

## ling
ling, fem. of karl, 'man'. See carl and cp. Carl,
Charles. Cp. also carling.
carline thistle. — F. carline, fr. ML. carlina, for

## cardina
cardina, fr. L. carduus, 'thistle'. See card,
'machine for combing', and cp. words there referred
to. ML. carlina was influenced in form by

## Charlemagne (Carolus Magnus)
Charlemagne (Carolus Magnus), with whom this
plant was associated by legend.

## carling
carling, п., one of the timbers running
lengthwise (naut.) — F. carlingue, fr. ON. kerling, lit.
'an old woman'. See carline, 'an old woman*.

## Carlovingian
Carlovingian, adj.,Carolingian. — F.carlovingien,
a blend of carolingien and merovingien. See
Carolingian and Merovlagiaa.

## carmaguole
carmaguole, п., ι) jacket (worn by the French
Revolutionaries in 1793); 2) a revolutionary
dance. — F., fr. Carmagnola, name of a

## district in Piedmont
district in Piedmont, Italy. The word orig. denoted
a coat worn in Carmagnola and brought to
France by workmen from Piedmont.

## Carmelite
Carmelite, n. and adj. — L. Carmelites, fr. Gk.
Καρμηλίτης, 'an inhabitant of Carmel', fr. Kop-
μι;λος, 'Carmel', fr. Heb. Karmel, '(Mount)

## Carmel'
Carmel', lit. 'garden', derived fr. kerem, 'vineyard'.
The mendicant order of the Carmelites owes
its name to the circumstance that about г 210

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:142 -->

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:142 COLUMN:1 -->
Berthold, a crusader from Calabria, and ten
of his companions, became hermits on Mount
Carmel.

## carminative
carminative, adj., expelling flatulence. — Formed
with suff. -ive fr. L. carminatus, pp. of carmi-
nare, 'to card wool', hence 'to cleanse, purify'.
L. carminare derives fr. carmen, gen. carminis,
'a card for wool or flax', which is re], to carrere,
'to card'. See card, 'machine for combing', and
-ative. (Carmen in the above sense is not rel. to
carmen, gen. carminis, 'song'.)
Derivative: carminative, п., a carminative drug.

## carmine
carmine, п., a purplish-red color; adj., of
purplish-red color. — F. carmin, fr. ML. carminium,
a blend of Arab, qirmiz, 'worm' and L. minium,
'cinnabar, red lead, vermilion', which is of
Iberian origin. See crimson, and miniature.

## carnage
carnage, п., slaughter, massacre. — F., fr. It. car-
naggio, fr. VL. carndricum, fr. L. car6, gen.
carnis, 'flesh, meat'. See carnal and -age and cp.
carrloa, char net.

## carnal
carnal, adj., pertaining to flesh, fleshly, bodily',
of the body; sensual, sexual. — L. carnalis,
'pertaining to the flesh, fleshly, carnal', fr. L. car6,
gen. carnis, 'flesh, meat', orig. 'a piece (of flesh)',
rel. to Umbr. karu, 'part, piece', Oscan earner's
(gen.) 'of a part', fr. I.-E. base *(s)qer-, 'to cut',
whence also L. cortex, 'bark', corium, 'skin,
hide, leather', scortum, 'skin, hide', OI. krnati,
krnati, 'hurts, kills', Gk. κείρειν (for *κέρ4ειν),
'to cut, shear', άκαρής, 'small, tiny' (lit. 'too
short to be cut'), OE. sceran, scieran, 'to cut,
shear'. See shear and adj. suff. -al and cp.
carnage, camiheation, carnivorous, carrion,
caruncle, acharne, acharnement, cenacle, chair,
flesh color', charnel, incarnadine, incarnate. For
derivatives of *(s)qer(e)p-, a -p-enlargement of
base *(s)qer-, see carpel, harvest, scurf, sharp.
Cp. also certain and words there referred to.
Derivatives: carnality (q.v.), carnal-ize, tr. v.,
carnel-ly, adv.

## carnality
carnality, п., fleshliness. — Late L. carnalitas,
fr. L. carnalis. See prec. word and -ity.

## carnation
carnation, п., l) formerly, flesh color; 2) any of
the cultivated varieties of the clove pink. — F.,
'flesh tint, flesh color, carnation', fr. It. car-
nagione, 'flesh, flesh tint', fr. carne, 'flesh, meat',
fr. L. carnem, ace. of caro, of s.m. See carnnl
and -ation.

## camelian
camelian, п., a red variety of chalcedony. — A
blend of cornelian and L. caro, gen. carnis,
'flesh' (see carnal); so called in reference to its
flesh-red color.

## carnification
carnification, п., the act or process of turning
