## charlatan
charlatan, п., a pretender; a quack. — F., fr. It.
ciarlatano, fr. earlier cerretano, of s.m., fr. ML.
ceretanus, lit. 'inhabitant of Cerrelo', a town
near Spoleto in Italy, famous for its quacks and
impostors. It. ciarlatano was influenced in form
by It. ciarlare, 'to prattle'.
Derivatives: charlatan-ic, charlatan-ic-al, adjs.,
charlatan-ic-al-ly, adv., charlatanism (q.v.), char-
latan-ry, n.

## charlatanism
charlatanism, n. — A hybrid coined fr. prec.
word and -ism, a suff. of Greek origin.

## Charles
Charles, masc. PN. — F., derived (possibly
through the medium of ML. Carolus), fr. MHG.
karl, fr. karl, 'man, husband'. See churl and cp.
Carl, carline, 'old woman', carliag, Caroline,
carolus.

## Charles's Wain
Charles's Wain, п., the constellation Ursa Major
(the Great Bear); the Big Dipper (astron.) —
OE. Carles-wxgn, Carles-wxn, lit. 'wain of
Charles', i.e. 'wain of Charlemagne'. The name
of the neighboring star Arctunis (in the
constellation Bootes) having been confused with the
name of King Arthur, the Ursa Major was
associated with the other great hero of medieval
romance, Charlemagne. See Charles and wain.

## Charleston
Charleston, п., a kind of dance. — So called from
Charleston, a seaport in Southern Carolina.

## Charley
Charley, Charlie, п., an obsolete name for a night
watchman. — Prob. so called after Charles I
who introduced a new watch system in London.

## charlock
charlock, п., a wild mustard. — OE. cerlic, cyrlic.

## Charlotte
Charlotte, fem. PN. — F„ fem. of Chariot, dimin.
of Charles. See Charles.

## charlotte
charlotte, п., apple charlotte. — Fr. prec. word.

## charm
charm, п., incantation, spell. — F. charme, fr.
L. carmen, 'song', dissimilated fr. *can-men,
from the stem of canere, 'to sing'. See cant,
'slang of beggars'. For a similar kind of
dissimilation of the consonants nm to rm cp. L.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:155 COLUMN:2 -->
germen, 'germ', dissimilated fr. 'gen-men (see
germ).
Derivatives: charm-ful, adj., charm-fully, adv.,
charm-ful-ness, п., charm-less, adj.

## charm
charm, tr. v. — F. charmer, fr. charme. See prec.
word.
Derivatives: charm-ed-ly, adv., charm-er, п.,
charm-ing, adj., charm-ing-ly, adv., charm-ing-
ness, n.

## charm
charm, п., song of birds (archaic) — ME. chirm,
fr. OE. arm, cerm, of imitative origin. Cp.
chirm.

## charnel
charnel, п., a burial place, charnel house. — ME.,
fr. OF. charnel, from Late L. carnale,
'graveyard, yard', prop. neut. of the Latin adjective
carnalis, 'pertaining to the flesh, fleshly', fr.
card, gen. carnis, 'flesh'. See carnal.

## Charon
Charon, п., theson of Erebus, who ferried the souls
of the dead over the rivers Acheron and Styx
(Greek mylhol.) — L., fr. Gk. Χάρων, which is of
uncertain origin. It possibly is a euphemistic
term lit. meaning 'lovely', and is rel. to χαίρειν
(for *χάρ-ιειν), 'to rejoice'; see Charis.

## charpoy
charpoy, п., the common Indian bedstead. —
Hind, charpai, lit. 'four-footed', fr. Pers. lahar-
pal, 'four-footed', fr. labor, 'four' (which is rel.
to Avestic labwarS, 'four'), and pal, 'foot'
(which is rel. to Avestic pad-, 'foot'). See foar
and foot and cp. the first element in pajama and
the second element in teapoy. Cp. Gk. τετράπους
and L. quadrupes, 'four-footed', which are the
exact etymological equivalents of Pers. iahur-pai.

## charqni
charqni, п., dried meat. — Sp., fr. Peruv. charqui,
'dried meat'. Cp. jerk, 'to dry meat'.

## chart
chart, п., a sea map. — F. carte, fr. Late L. carta,
fr. L. charta. See card, 'a piece of pasteboard',
and cp. next word.
Derivative: chart, tr. v.

## charter
charter, n. — OF. (= F.) chartre, fr. L. chartula,
'a little paper', dimin. of charta. See prec. word
and cp. chartulary.
Derivatives: charter, tr. v., charter-ed, adj.,
charter-er, n.

## charterhouse
charterhouse, п., ι) a Carthusian monastery;
2) (capit.) a charitable foundation. — Formed
by folk etymology fr. F. chartreuse, 'Carthusian
monastery'. See chartreuse.

## charter party
charter party, a written agreement for the hiring
of a ship. — F. chartre-partie or charte-partie,
'a divided chartre' (see charter and part, v.);
so called because the form was made in
duplicate in one sheet, which was divided between
the contracting parties.

## Chartism
Chartism, п., the principles of a political party
of reformers in England (1836-48). — See
charter and -ism j so called from thePeople's Charier,
which contained the principles and demands of
this party.

## Chartist
Chartist, п., an adherent of Chartism. — See prec.
word and -ist.

## Chartreuse
Chartreuse, n„ a Carthusian monastery. — F.,
fr. la Grande-Chartreuse, chief house of the
Carthusians near Grenoble. See Carthusinn and
cp. Charterhouse.

## chartreuse
chartreuse, п., a sweet liqueur. — The word orig.
meant 'liqueur made at la Grande-Chartreuse'.
See prec. word.

## chartulary
chartulary, п., a collection of charters. — ML.
chartularium, fr. L. chartula, 'a little paper',
dimin. of charta. See charter and subst. suff.
-ary and cp. cartulary.

## charwoman
charwoman, n. — Compounded of char, 'a turn
of work', and woman.

## chary
chary, adj., careful. — OE. cearig, 'sorrowful,
careful', fr. cearu, caru, 'sorrow, care'. See
care and -y (representing OE. -ig).
Derivatives: chari-ly, adv., chari-ness, n.

## Charybdis
Charybdis, п., a whirlpool between Italy and
Sicily. — L, fr. Gk. Χάρυβδις, a word of
uncertain etymology.

## chase
chase, tr. and intr. v., to hunt. — ME. chacen,
chosen, fr. OF. chacier (F. chasser), fr. VL. *cap-
tiare, fr. L. capture, 'to strive, to seize', freq. of
capere (pp. captus), 'to catch, seize, hold'. Cp.
It. cacciare, OProvenc., Catal. casar, Sp. cazar,
Port, cagar, 'to chase, hunt', and see catch,
which is a doublet of chase.
Derivatives: chaser (q.v.), chas-ing, n.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:155 COLUMN:3 -->

## chase
chase, п., the act of hunting.— ME. chace, chase,
fr. OE. chace, fr. chacier, 'to hunt'. Cp. It.
caccia, OProvenc., Catal. casa, Sp. caza, Port.
coca, and see prec. word.

## chase
chase, tr. v., to emboss, engrave. — Short for
enchase.

## chase
chase, п., a rectangular, iron frame (print.) —
F. chasse, 'box, case, frame', fr. L. capsa,
'chest, box'. See case, 'chest', and cp. chassis,
enchase.

## chase
chase, п., a groove. — F. chasse. See prec. word.

## chuser
chuser, п., one who chases or hunts. — OF. cha-
ceor (F. chasseur), fr. OF. chacier. See chase,
'to hunt', and agential suff. -er.

## chaser
chaser, п., a chase gun. — From prec. word.

## chaser
chaser, п., one who embosses or engraves. —
Formed fr. chase, 'to emboss', with agential
suff. -er.

## chasm
chasm, п., a deep crack in the earth; abyss. —
L. chasma, fr. Gk. χάσμα, 'a yawning hollow,
gulf', which is rel. to χαίνειν, 'to yawn, gape'.
See cbaos and cp. polychasium.
Derivatives: chasm-al, chasm-ic, chasm-y, adjs.

## chasse
chasse, n. — Short for chasse-cafe.

## chasse
chasse, п., a quick gliding step in dancing. — F.,
lit. 'chased', pp. of chasser, 'to chase, hunt'. See
chase, 'to hunt'.

## chasse-cafe
chasse-cafe, п., a glass of liqueur taken after
coffee. — F., fr. chasser, 'to chase, hunt, drive,
drive away*, and cafe, 'coffee*. See chase, 'to
hunt', and cafe.

## chassepot
chassepot, п., a rifle used by the French in the war
of 1870. — Named after the French inventor
Antoine-Alphonse Chassepot (1833-1905).

## chasseur
chasseur, п., ι) a hunter; 2) a soldier. — F.,
'hunter, huntsman', fr. OF. chaceor, fr. chacier, 'to
chase'. See chase, 'to hunt', and cp. chaser, 'one
who hunts'.

## Cbassideans
Cbassideans, n. — See Hasideans.

## Chassidim
Chassidim, n. — See Hasidim.

## Cbassidism
Cbassidism, n. — See Hasidism.

## chassignite
chassignite, п., a meteorite. — Named after Chas-
signy in France. For the ending see subst. suff.
-ite.

## chassis
chassis, п., framework. — F. chassis, 'frame,
framework', fr. chasse, 'frame', fr. L. capsa,
'chest, box'. See case, 'chest', and cp. chase,
'iron frame', and sash, 'framework'.

## chaste
chaste, adj. — OF. (= F.), fr. L. castus, 'exempt
(from mistakes), free, pure, chaste', prob. the
pp. of carere, 'to be without, be wanting, be free
from, abstain from', which prob. meant orig.
'to be cut off, be separated', and is rel. to cas-
trare, 'to cut, geld'; see Walde-Hofmann, LEW.,
I, p. 167 s.v. cared. See castrate and cp. caret.
Cp. also caste, castigate, chastise.
Derivatives: chaste-ly, adv., chaste-ness, n.

## chasten
chasten, tr. v. — ME. chastien, fr. OF. chastier
(F. chatter), 'to punish', fr. L. castigare. See
castigate and cp. chastise. For the ending see
verbal suff. -en.
Derivatives: chasten-er, п., chaslen-ed, adj.
chaste tree. — Loan translation of L. castus in
agaus castas (q.v.)

## chastise
chastise, tr. v. — ME. chastisen, a blend of
chastien and suff. -isen (= E. -ise, -ize). See chasten.
Derivatives: chastis-er, п., chastise-ment, n.

## chastity
chastity, n. — OF. chastete (F. chaslete), fr. L.
castitdtem, ace. of castitas, 'purity, chastity', fr.
castus. See chaste and -ity.

## chasnble
chasnble, п., an ecclesiastic vestment without
sleeves. — F., fr. Late L. *casubula (contracted
into casubla, a word used in the 6th cent, by
Gregory of Tours), fr. L. casula, 'a little hut',
dimin. of casa, 'cottage, hut, cabin', which is
of uncertain origin. Chasuble orig. denoted a
hooded garment resembling a little house. Cp.
casino.

## chat
chat, intr. v. — Back formation fr. chatter.
Derivative: chat, n.

## chiteau
chiteau, п., a castle in France. — F., fr. OF.
chaste!, fr. L. castellum, 'citadel, fortress,
stronghold'. See castie.

## chatelatn
chatelatn, п., castellan. — F. See castellan.

## chatelaine
chatelaine, п., the mistress of a castle; key chain
worn at the waist by women. — F., fem. of
chatelain. See prec. word.

## chati
chati, п., a South American tiger cat. — Of South

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:156 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: 129 | CHELONE -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:156 COLUMN:1 -->
American Indian origin.

## chatoyant
chatoyant, adj., of a changeable luster. — F.,
pres. part, of chaloyer, 'to shine with a
changeable luster', lit. 'to shine like the eyes of a cat',
fr. chat, 'cat', fr. Late L. cattus. See cat and -lint.
Derivative: chatoyant, n.

## chathnmite
chathnmite, п., a variety of chloanthite (mineral.)
— Named from Chatham in Connecticut. For
the ending see subst. suff. -ite,

## chatta
chatta, п., an umbrella (Anglo-lnd.) — Hind.
chdtd, chair, fr. OI. catrab.

## chattel
chattel, n. — ME. chatel, fr. OF. chatel, fr. Late L.
capitate, 'property'. See cattie.

## chatter
chatter, intr. v. — ME. chateren, of imitative
origin. Cp. chat.
Derivatives: chatter, п., chatter-er, n.

## chatty
chatty, adj., talkative. — Formed fr. chat with
adj. suff. -y.

## chatty
chatty, п., an eajthen pot (Anglo-lnd.) — Hind.
chati.

## chauffer
chauffer, п., a portable stove. — Prob. a blend
of F. chauffoir, 'a heater' (fr. chauffer, 'to heat'),
and E. chafer, 'a vessel for heating' (q.v.)

## chauffeur
chauffeur, п., driver of a motor car. — F., orig.
'heater, fire man, stoker', fr. chauffer, 'to heat'.
See chafe and cp. chauffer, rechauffe.
Derivative: chauffeur, intr. and tr. v.

## Chaumontel
Chaumontel, п., a variety of pear. — Named from
Chaumontel, a village in the Department of
Seine-et-Oise in France.

## Chauna
Chauna, п., a genus of birds, the chaja (ornilhol.)
— ModL., fr. Gk. χαϋνος, 'gaping, flaccid,
loose, porous', which is rel. to χάος (for ·χΑΡος),
'gulf, schism, abyss', χάσμα, 'a yawning hollow,
gulf. See chaos and cp. words there referred to.

## chaussee
chaussee, п., a causeway. — F., fr. VL. (via)
'calciata, lit. 'a road paved with limestone', fr.
L. calx, gen. calcis, 'lime, limestone'. See causey,
causeway.

## Chantauqua
Chantauqua, п., an assembly for popular
education based on the system introduced in 1874 at
Chautauqua, N.Y. (U.S.A.)
Derivative: chautauqu-an, adj.

## chauvin
chauvin, п., a person affected by blind patriotism.
— F., from the name of Nicolas Chauvin, one
of Napoleon's veterans, ridiculed for his
excessive patriotism and staged by the brothers
Cogniard in their vaudeville La Cocarde Iri-
colore (1831). — The name Chauvin derives fr
L. Calvinus, hence is etymologically identical
with the name of the French reformer John
Calvin (1509-64), orig. called Cauhin, Chauvin.
See Calvinism.
Derivatives: chauvin-ism (F. chauvinisme), chau-
vin-isl, n. and adj., chauvin-ist-ic, adj., chauvin-
ist-ic-al-ly, adv.

## chaw
chaw, tr. v. — A variant of chew.

## chawbuck
chawbuck, n. and tr. v. (obsol.) — Anglicized
form of chabouk (q.v.)

## chawdron
chawdron, п., the entrails (of an animal). — OF.
chaudun, fr. ML. caldina, 'intestina', fr. L. cali-
dus, caldus, 'warm'. See caldron.

## chay
chay, chaya, choya, п., the root of the herb Olden-
landia umbellata — Malayal. ckdyaver, 4it.
'dye root', fr. chaya, 'color', and ver, 'root'.
Malayal. chaya derives fr. OI. chaya, 'shade,
splendor, glitter, color', fr. I.-E. base *ska(i)-,
'to shine, flicker, glimmer'. See skiagraphy.

## chazzan
chazzan, n. — See hazzan.

## cheap
cheap, п., п., ι) market (only in place names as
Cheapside); 2) bargain (obsol.) — OE. clap,
'barter, buying and selling, bargain, price',
whence ceapian, 'to trade, buy, sell'; rel. to
OHG., MHG. kouf, 'trade, buying and selling',
G. Kauf, 'purchase, bargain', Du. koop, of
s.m., OFris. кар, ON. kaup, OS. kop, 'trade,
buying and selling', Swed. kop, Dan. kjeb,
'purchase, bargain'. All these words derive, like
OHG. koufo, 'trader, dealer', fr. L. caupo,
'huckster, innkeeper', which is of uncertain
origin. OSlav. kupiti, 'to buy'. OPruss. kaupis-
kan (ace.), 'trade', are Teut. loan words. Cp.

## cheap
cheap, v., cheapen, chaffer, chapman, cooper,
'a kind of vessel'. Cp. also caper, 'privateer'. L.
caupo is not rel. to L. сира, 'tub, cask', as
suggested by most lexicographers; see Walde-Hof-
mann, LEW., I, p. 189.
Derivative: cheap, adj. (q.v.)

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:156 COLUMN:2 -->

## cheap
cheap, adj., low in price. — Shortened fr. good
cheap, 'a good price or bargain', i.e. 'cheap'. See
cheap, п., and cp. F. bon marche, 'cheap', lit.
'a good bargain'.
Derivatives: cheap-ly, adv., cheap-ness,'n.

## cheap
cheap, intr. v., to barter; tr. v., to buy (obsol.) —
ME. cheapian, fr. OE. ceapian, *lo trade, buy,
sell', fr. clap, 'barter, buying and selling'.
Cp. Goth, каирбп, OHG. koufon, MHG.
koufen, G. kaufen, Du. kopen, ON. kaupa,
Swed. кора, Dan. kjebe, #OS. kopian, kopon,
'to buy'. These verbs orig. meant 'to barter,
bargain', and are traceable to L. caupo,
'huckster, innkeeper'. See cheap, n.
Derivative: cheap-en, tr. v., to buy; intr. v., to
bargain.

## cheat
cheat, n. — Shortened fr. escheat in the sense of
'confiscation'.
Derivatives: cheat, tr. and intr. v., cheat-er, п.,
cheat-ery, п., cheat-ing, adj., cheat-ing-ly, adv.

## chebec
chebec, chebeck, п., a xebec. — F. chebec, fr. It.
sciabecco. See xebec.

## chebule
chebule, п., the dried fruit of Terminalia chebula.
— F. chebule, fr. Arabo-Pers. kabult, lit., 'from
(the city of) Kabul'.

## check
check, п., ι) a sudden stop, restrain, repulse;
2) in chess, an attack upon the king. — ME.
chek, fr. OF. eschec (whence F. echec), 'check
(at chess); defeat, blow, loss', fr. earlier eschac,
borrowed (through the medium of Spanish and
Arabic) fr. Pers. shah, 'king' (in the Arab.-Pers.
phrase shah mat, 'the king is dead'), fr. OPers.
xshaya-, 'king', which is rel. to xshayaftiya-,
'power', fr. I.-E. base *qpe(i)-, *qpe(i)-, 'to rule',
whence also O]. ksayati, 'possesses, rules', ksat-
ram, 'rule, dominion', Gk. κτάομαι, Ί get,
acquire'. See satrap, shah and cp. checkmate, chess,
checker, exchequer, Kshatriya. Cp. also the first
element in Ahasuerus, Xerxes and the second
element in Nakshatra, padishah and pashah.
Derivatives: check, tr. and intr. v., check-less,adj.

## check
check, cheque, п., a written order to a bank. —
Most philologists derive this word from check
in the sense 'a sudden stop'. It is more probable,
however, that check in the sense 'a written order
to a bank', comes fr. Arab, sakk, 'agreement,
contract', fr. Pers. lak, of s.m.

## checker
checker, chequer, п., a pattern resembling a
chessboard. — Shortened fr. OF. eschekier (F. echi-
quiei), 'chessboard', fr. ML. scaccarium, ult.
fr. Pers. shah, 'king'. See check, 'a sudden stop',
and cp. exchequer.
Derivatives: checker, tr. v., checker-ed, adj.,
checkers (q.v.)

## checkers
checkers, chequers, п., a game played on a
checkerboard; draughts. — From prec. word.

## checkmate
checkmate, interj. — ME. chek mat, fr. OF. eschec
el mat (F. echec et mat), fr. Sp.jaque у mate, fr.
Arabo-Pers. shah mat, 'the king is dead' (whence
also It. scaccomatto). See check, 'a sudden stop'
and cp. mate, 'checkmate'.
Derivatives: checkmate, n. and tr. v.

## cheeky
cheeky, adj., divided into squares of alternate
tincture. — Formed fr. check, п., 'a sudden
stop', with adj. suff. -y.

## Cheddar cheese
Cheddar cheese, Cheddar, also Cheddar, n. —
Named fr. Cheddar, Somerset, England, where
it was originally made.
Derivative: cheddar-ing, n.

## cheddite
cheddite, п., an explosive used for blasting. —
Named after Chedde, a town in the Department
Haute-Savoie in France, where it was first
made; cp. lyddite. For the ending see subst.
suff. -ite.

## cheder
cheder, n. — See heder.

## cheek
cheek, n. — ME. cheke, fr. ceace, "jaw, cheek',
rel. to MLG. kake, Du. kaak, 'jaw, cheek'; of
uncertain origin.
Derivatives: cheek, tr. v., cheek-y, adj., cheek-
i-ly, adv., cheek-i-ness, n.

## cheenar
cheenar, n. — A variant spelling of chinar.

## cheep
cheep, intr. and tr. v. — Of imitative origin.
Derivatives: cheep, п., cheep-er, п., cheep-y,
adj., cheep-i-ly, adv., cheep-i-ness, n.

## cheer
cheer, n. — ME. chere, 'face, countenance, cheer',
fr. OF. chiere, chere, 'face' (whence F. chere,
'countenance, cheer, entertainment'), fr. VL.
cara, 'face', fr. Gk. κάρα, 'head'. See cerebrum

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:156 COLUMN:3 -->
and cp. words there referred to. For the sense
development of F. chere, E. cheer, cp. F. bonne
chere, E.goodcheer, prop, 'a happy countenance'.
Derivatives: cheer, tr. and intr. v., cheer-ed, adj.,
cheer-er, п., cheer-ful, adj., cheer-ful-ly, adv.,
cheer-ful-ness,n., cheer-less, adj., cheer-less-Iy,
adv., cheer-less-ness, п., cheer-y, adj., cheer-i-ly,
adv., cheer-i-ness, n.

## cheese
cheese, п., milk curd. — ME. chese, fr. OE. else,
fr. L. caseus, 'cheese', whence also OS. kasi,
MDu. case (Du. kaas), OHG. chasi, kasi
(MHG. kxse, G. Kdse). L. caseus is prob. cogn.
with Prakrit chasi, 'buttermilk', OSlav. kvasu,
'leaven', kyselu, 'sour', kyseti, 'to turn sour',
and with OI. kvdthati, 'boils, seethes', but OE.
hwxg (see whey) is not cognate. Cp. casein,
catechu, chessel.
Derivatives: chees-er, п., chees-y, adj., chees-i-
ness, n.

## cheese
cheese, п., the proper thing (slang). — Urdu.
chiz, 'thing', fr. Pers. chiz, of s.m.

## cheetah
cheetah, n. — Hind, chlta, lit. 'spotted', fr. OI.
citrdh, 'bright, spotted, variegated', rel. to OI.
kltuh, 'brightness', fr. I.-E. base *(s)qait-,
'bright'. See celestial and cp. -hood. Cp. also
chintz, chit, 'a short letter'.

## chef
chef, п., the head cook. — F., short for chef de
cuisine, lit. 'head of the kitchen'. F. chef, 'head',
derives fr. VL. *capum, fr. L. caput, 'head'.
See chief,

## chef-d'oeuvre
chef-d'oeuvre, п., masterpiece. —· F., lit. 'chief
work', fr. chef, 'chief, principal', de, 'from, of
(fr. L.ifc, 'from, away from'), and auvre, 'work'.
See chef, de- and oeuvre. The word chef-
d'oeuvre was introduced into English by Horace
Walpole (1717-97)·

## cheil-
cheil-, form of cheilo-, before a vowel.

## Cheilaathes
Cheilaathes, п., name of a genus of ferns of the
polypody family (hot.) — ModL., lit. 'having
marginal flowers'; coined fr. '(Gk. χείλος, .'lip,
margin', and ανί>ος, 'flower'. For the first
element see cheilo-, for the second see anther,

## cheilitis
cheilitis, chilitis, п., inflammation of the lip
(med.) — Medical L. cheilitis, chilitis, formed
fr. cheil- with suff. -itis.

## cheilo-
cheilo-, before a vowel cheil-, combining form
denoting the lip (anal.) — See chilo-, chil-.

## cheiro-
cheiro-, before a vowel cheir-, combining form
meaning 'hand-, perlaining to the hand'. — See
chiro-, chir-.

## Cheka
Cheka, п., former name of the political branch
of the Soviet secret police. — Formed from the
initial letters of Russ. Chrezvychainaya Komis-
siya, 'Extraordinary Commission'.
■chela, п., a Buddhist disciple. — Hind, chela,
'slave, servant', fr. OI. cetah, cefakah, which is
rel. to Marathi ce4a, 'son', cela, 'pupil', Prakrit
седа-, cilia-, 'boy', Pali cefo, 'servant, youth'.

## chela
chela, п., the pincerlike claw of lobsters, crabs,
etc. (zool.) — ModL., fr. Gk. χηλή, 'fork, claw',
which is rel. to χήμη, 'a yawning, gaping',
χαΐνειν, 'to gape, yawn'. See chaos and cp. the
first element in cheliform. Cp. also chemosis.

## chelate
chelate, adj., having chelae. — See prec. word
and adj. suff. -ate.

## Chelidonium
Chelidonium, п., a genus of plants of the poppy
family (bot.) — ModL., fr. Gk. χελΤ8άνιον,
'celandine'. See celandine,

## cheliform
cheliform, adj., having a movable joint, as the
clawlike pincer of a crab. — A hybrid coined
fr. Gk. χηλή, 'claw', and L. forma, 'form, shape*.

## See chela
See chela, 'claw' and form, n.

## Chellean
Chellean, adj., pertaining to Chelles, France, or
to the early Paleolithic period (archaeol.) — F.
chellien; so called in allusion to the flint

## implements discovered there
implements discovered there, which belong to this
period. For the ending see suff. -an.

## chelone
chelone, п., siege performed with shields united
so as to resemble the shell of a tortoise; the

## same as L
same as L,. tesludo (Greek hist.) — Gk. χελώντ),
'tortoise', fr. χελός, 4ortoise', lit. 'the yellow

## animal'
animal', rel. to χλοος, 'greenish-yellow color',

## and cogn. with OSlav. zely
and cogn. with OSlav. zely, 'tortoise', lit. 'the

## yellow animal'
yellow animal', fr. I.-E. base *ghel-, 'yellow',

## whence also OE. geolo
whence also OE. geolo, 'yellow'. See yellow and
cp. words there referred to.

## Chelone
Chelone, п., a genus of plants of the figwort
family (bot.) — ModL., fr. Gk. χελώνη, 'tor-

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:157 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: CHELONIA | 130 -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:157 COLUMN:1 -->
toise' (see prec. word); so called because the
corolla resembles the head of a tortoise.
Chelonia, п., an order of reptiles, the tortoise or
turtle (zool.) — ModL., fr. Gk. χελώνη,
'tortoise'. See chelone, 'siege performed with
shields', and -ia.
chelonlan, adj., pertaining to the order Chelonia.
— See prec. word and -an.
