## chemic
chemic, adj. — See alchemy and -ic and cp.
chemist. Derivatives: chemic-al, adj. and п.,
chemic-al- ize, tr. v., chemic-al-Iy, adv.

## chemico-
chemico-, combining form meaning 'chemically,
in connection with chemistry'. — Formed fr.
chemic.

## chemin de fer
chemin de fer, 1) railroad; 2) name of a gambling
game resembling baccarat. — F., 'railroad', lit.
'iron road'.

## chemise
chemise, п., woman's undergarment. — F.,'shirt',
fr. Late L. camisa, camisia (whence also It. cami-
cia, Sp. camisa, OProvenc. camiza), borrowed
from Teutonic through the medium of Gaulish.
Cp. OHG. hemidi (MHG. hemede, hemde, G.
Hemd), OFris. hemethe, OS. hemithi, OE.
hemede, 'shirt', fr. Teut. *hamipia, fr. base 'ha-
ma(n)-, 'covering, cover', fr. I.-E. base "kern-,
*kam-, 'to cover'. See name, henven, shame,
and cp. cnmise, camisado, camisole.

## chemisette
chemisette, п., a kind of bodice worn by women.
— K, lit. 'a little shirt', dimin. of chemise. See
chemise and -ette.

## chemist
chemist, n. — F. chimiste, fr. chimie, 'chemistry'.
See alchemy and -ist. Derivative: chemist-ry, n.

## chemo-
chemo-, combining form denoting relation to
chemical actions or chemicals. — See chemic.

## chemosis
chemosis, п., swelling of the conjunctiva (med.) —
Medical L., fr. Gk. χήμωσις, 'affection of the
eye in which the cornea swells like a
cockleshell', fr. χήμη, 'a yawning, gaping; cockleshell',
which is rel. to χαίνειν, 'to yawn, gape'; fr.
I.-E. base *ghei-, *ghi-, 'to gape, yawn'. See
chaos and -osis and cp. chela, 'claw'.

## chemotherapy
chemotherapy, п., — Coined by the Jewish
bacteriologist and chemist Paul Ehrlich (1854-1915)
fr. chemo- and therapy.

## Chen
Chen, п., a genus of geese, the snowgoose (orni-
thol.) — Gk. χήν, 'goose', rel. to Boeotian χάν,
for *χάς, 'goose'. See goose and cp. words there
referred to.

## chen-
chen-, form of cheno- before a vowel.

## chenevixite
chenevixite, п., a copper and iron arsenate
{mineral.) — Named afler the Irish chemist Richard
Chenevix who analyzed it. For the ending see
subst. suff. -ite.

## chenille
chenille, п., tufted cord of silk, wool, etc. — F.,
prop, 'caterpillar*, fr. L. canicula, *a little dog',
dimin. of canis, 'dog'. See canine.

## cheno-
cheno-, before a vowel chen-, combining form
meaning 'goose'. — Gk. χηνο-, χην-, fr. χήν,
gen. χηνός, 'goose'. See Chen,.

## Chenopodiaceae
Chenopodiaceae, n. pi., the goosefoot family
(pot.) — ModL., formed fr. Chenopodium with
suff. -aceae.

## chenopodiaceous
chenopodiaceous, adj. — See prec. word and
-aceous.

## Chenopodium
Chenopodium, п., a genus of plants of the goose-
foot family (hot.) — ModL., lit. 'goosefoot', fr.
Gk. χήν, gen. χηνός, 'goose', and πους, gen.
ποδός, 'foot'. See cheno- and -pod.

## cheque
cheque, n. — The British spelling of check, 'a
written order to a bank' (q.v.)

## cheqner
cheqner, n. — See checker.

## cherish
cherish, tr. v. — ME. cherischen, fr. OF. cheriss-,
pres. part, stem of chair (F. cherir), 'to hold
dear, cherish', fr. cher, 'dear', fr. L. earns
(whence also It., Sp., Port, caro, OProvenc.,
Catal. car). See charity and verbal suff. -ish
and cp. caress. Derivatives: cherish-er, п., cher-
ish-ing, adj., cherish-ing-ly, adv.,cherish-ment,n.

## chema
chema, п., any of the fishes of the family Ser-
ranidae. — Sp., 'a fish resembling a salmon,
ruffle', fr. Late L. acernia, which is rel. to Gk.
αχερνα, a word glossed by Hcsychius; of
unknown origin.

## cheroot
cheroot, п., a kind of cigar. — Tamil iurultu,
'roll, cigar', fr. iurul, 'curl'.

## cherry
cherry, n. — ME. chery, fr. ONF. cherise (F.
cerise), fr. VL. 'ceresia, fr. Imperial L. cerasium,

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:157 COLUMN:2 -->
fr. Gk. κέρασος, which prob. derives fr. Akkad.
karshu, 'stone fruit'. Cp. Κεράσους, name of a
town in Pontus, lit. '(the town) abounding in
cherries'. The s in ONF. cherise was mistaken
for the pi. suff. and consequently dropped m
English. Cp. cerise, kirsch. Cp. also merry, 'the
wild black cherry'.
Derivatives: cherry, tr. v., cherri-ed, adj.

## Chersonese
Chersonese, п., a peninsula. — L. chersonesus, fr.
Gk. χερσόνησος, 'peninsula', which is
compounded of χέρσος, 'dry, hard, barren', and
νήσος, 'island'. The first element is cogn. with
OI. barsaie, hfsyati, 'becomes stiff, bristles',
L. horrgre, 'to stand on end, bristle, shudder,
tremble'. See horror and cp. -choerus. For the
second element see neso-.

## chert
chert, п., a kind of quartz. — Of uncertain origin.

## cherub
cherub, n. — Heb. k'rubh, 'winged angel', prob.
rel. to Akkad. karabu, 'to bless', karibu, 'one
who blesses', epithet of the bull-colossus, and to
Heb. berakh, 'he blessed', b'rakha", 'blessing'.
See berakah and cp. griffin.
Derivatives: cherub-ic, cherub-ic-al, adjs., che-
rub-ic-al-ly, adv.

## chervil
chervil, п., an aromatic plant. — OE. cerfille, fr.
L. chaerephyllum, fr. Gk. χαιρέφυλλον, which is
compounded of χαίρειν, 'to rejoice', and φΰλ-
λον, 'leaf. The first element is rel. to χάρις,
'grace'; see Charts. For the second element see
phyllo-,
Cheshire cat. — Named from the county of
Cheshire in England.
Cheshire cheese. — So called because it is made
chiefly in the county of Cheshire in England.

## Cheshvan
Cheshvan, n. — See Heshvan.

## chesil
chesil, also chisel, п., gravel, shingle. — OE. cio-
sol, cisil, cysel, rel. to OHG. kisil, MHG. kisel,
G. Kiesel, 'pebble, flint', diminutives formed
from Teut. base *kiso (whence also MHG. kis,
G. Kies, 'gravel'), corresponding to I.-E. base
*geis-, 'gravel', whence Lith. ziezdra, 'gravel',
ziezdros, 'coarse sand', OPruss. sixto, 'sand'. Cp.
the first element in kieselguhr.

## chess
chess, n. — ME. ches, fr. OF. esches, 'chess',
oblique case of eschec, 'check'. Modern French
also differentiates between the sing, echec,
'check', and the pi. echecs, 'chess*. See check,
'a sudden stop'.

## chessel
chessel, п., cheese vat. — Compounded of cheese
and well, n.

## chest
chest, n. — ME. chest, chist, fr. OE. cest, cisle,
fr. L. cista (whence also ΟΝ., OHG. kista,
MDu., MHG., G. kiste, Du. kist), fr. Gk. κίστή,
'basket', which prob. means lit. 'wicker basket',
and is cogn. with Olr. cess, ciss, 'basket', ain-
chess, 'bread basket'. Cp. cisium, cist, cistern,
kist.
Derivative: chesl, 'tr. v.

## chesterfield
chesterfield, п., 1) a kind of overcoat; 2) a kind
of sofa. — Named after one of the Earls of
Chesterfield (19th cent.)

## cbeshint
cbeshint, n. — Shortened fr. chesten nut, fr. ME.
chesteine, chasteine, fr. OF. chastaigne (F. chatai-
gne), fr. L. castanea, fr. Gk. (κάρυα) καστάνεια,
fr. κάστανον, 'chestnut*, which is commonly
derived fr. Καστανίς, a town in Pontus, but in
reality a loan word from a language of Asia
Minor; cp. Arm. kask, 'chestnut', kaskeni,
'chestnut tree'. The town Καστανίς is named after the
fruit andlit.means'ChestnutTown'.Cp.Castanet.
Derivative: chestnut, intr. v.

## cheth
cheth, п., name of the 8th letter of the Hebrew
alphabet. — Heb. heth, lit. 'fence, barrier' (cp.
Arab, hata, 'he encompassed, fenced'); so called
in allusion to the ancient Hebrew form of this
letter. Cp. eta.

## cheval-de-frise
cheval-de-frise, n. pi., chevaux-de-frise, a series of
projecting spikes (mil.) — F., lit. 'Friesland
horse'; so called because it was first used in
Friesland. For the etymology of cheval see
cavalry.

## cheval glass
cheval glass, a long mirror swung in a frame. —
F. cheval, 'horse', fr. L. caballus. See cavalry.

## chevalier
chevalier, п., horseman, knight. — F., fr. Late L.
caballurius, fr. L. caballus. See cavalier.

## cheveril
cheveril, п., soft leather made of the skin of a
kid. — ME. chevrelle, fr. OF. chevrele (F. che-
vreau), 'kid', dimin. o(chievre(F. chivre), 'goat'.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:157 COLUMN:3 -->
See chevron.

## chevet
chevet, п., the apsidal east end of the choir of
a church (archit.) — F., 'pillow, apse', fr.OF.
chevetz, fr. L. capitium, 'covering for the head',
fr. caput, gen. capitis, 'head'. See capital, adj.,
and cp. tete-beche.

## chevin
chevin, п., the chub. — Cp. F. chevanne; of
unknown origin.

## cheviot
cheviot, п., cloth made from wool of sheep of
Cheviot Hills. — Named from the Cheviot Hills,
the range forming the borderland between
England and Scotland.

## chevron
chevron, п., ι) a beam, rafter; 2) a ^ shaped
mark (her.) — F., 'rafter, joist, chevron", fr.
VL. *caprwnem, ace. of 'caprio, fr. L. caper,
gen. capri, 'goat'. See cabriolet.

## chevrotain
chevrotain, п., a very small ruminant mammal,
(Tragulus kanchil); the mouse deer. — F.,
dimin. of OF. chevrot, itself a dimin. formed fr.
chievre (F. chivre), 'she-goat', fr. L. capra. See
cabriolet and cp. prec. word.

## chevy
chevy, also chivy, п., a) a hunting cry; b) a hunt,
chase; tr. and intr. v., to hunt, chase. —
Shortened from CAevy chase, from the 16th
cent, ballad of Chew Chase, a name corrupted
from orig. Cheviot chase.

## chew
chew, tr. and intr. v. — ME. chewen, fr. OE. ceo-
wan, rel. to MLG. keuwen, Du. kauwen, OHG.
kiuwan, MHG. kiuwen, MG. kuwen, 'to chew'
(whence G. kauen, 'to chew'; but cp. G. wieder-
кйиеп, 'to chew the cud', fr. MHG. kiuwen) and
to ON. tyggva (dissimilated fr. *kyggva), and
cogn. with OSlav. zivp, iivati, 'to chew', Lith.
zidunos (pi.), Lett, zaiinas (pi.), 'jaw; gill', Pers.
]avtdan, 'to chew', Toch. Swa, 'to eat'. L. gingiva,
'gum', is not cognate with the above words. Cp.
chaw.
Derivatives: chew, п., chew-er, п., chew-y, adv.

## cheyney
cheyney, п., a woolen fabric. — Lit. 'china ware'.
The word represents the former pronunciation
of China.

## Chian
Chian, adj., pertaining to the island Chios. —
Formed with suff. -an fr. L. Chius, fr. Gk. Χίος,
name of an island off the coast of Asia Minor.

## Chian
Chian, also chiaa, n. — Short for Chian wine.

## Chiante
Chiante, п., a kind of dry red wine. — Named
from the Chianti Mountains in Tuscany, Italy.

## chiaroscuro
chiaroscuro, п., use of light and shade in
painting, drawing, etc. — It., lit. 'clear dark', fr.
chiaro, 'clear', and oscuro, 'dark', fr. L. clarus,
'clear', resp. obscurus, 'dark'. See dear and
obscure.

## cbiasma
cbiasma, п., a crossing or decussation (anat.) —
ModL., fr. Gk. χίασμα, 'two things placed
crosswise', which is rel. to χιασμός, 'a placing
crosswise'. See chiasmus and -ma.
Derivatives: chiasm-al, chiasm-ic, adjs.

## chiasmus
chiasmus, inversion of word order. — ModL., fr.
Gk. χιασμός, 'a placing crosswise', fr. χΐάζειν,
'to write the letter χ', fr. χει, χι, name of the
22nd letter in the Greek alphabet. Cp. cbiasma.

## chiastic
chiastic, adj., pertaining to, or characterized by
chiasmus. — Formed with suff. -ic fr. Gk. χϊαβ-
τός, 'marked with a χ, arranged diagonally',
fr. χΐάζειν, 'to write the letter χ'. See prec.
word.

## cbiastolite
cbiastolite, п., a variety of andalusite (mineral.)
— Compounded of Gk. χϊαστός (see prec.
word) and λίθος, 'stone'. See -lite, litho-.

## chiaus
chiaus, п., a Turkish messenger. — Turk, cha-
wush, chaush. See chouse.

## chiare
chiare, п., clef (music). — It., 'key', fr. L. clavem,
ace*, of clavis, 'key', whence also F. clef, 'key'.
See clavicle and cp. cief, conclave.

## chibouk
chibouk, chibouque, п., a Turkish tobacco
pipe. — F. chibouque, fr. Turk, chubuq, chibuq,
'pipe*, prop, meaning 'stick, staff, tube', and
rel. to chub, 'stick, staff'.

## chlbrit
chlbrit, п., elemental mercury supposed to
produce metais (alchemy). — Arab, chtbrtt, 'sulfur',
rel. to Heb. gophrtth, Jewish-Aram, guphritha,
kubhrithd, Christ.-Palest. Aram, guphrt, Syr.
kebhrilha, Akkad. kupritu, 'brimstone, sulfur*.

## chic
chic, п., style, elegance. — F., prob. fr. G. Schick,
'fitness, tact, skill', fr. MHG. schicken, 4o
arrange, set in-order', whence G. schicken, 4o

## send'
send', Geschick, 'fitness, aptness, fate, destiny',
Schicksal, Schickung, 'fate, destiny'.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:158 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: 131 | CHIOGENES -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:158 COLUMN:1 -->
Derivatives: chic, adj. and tr. v.

## chicane
chicane, п., chicanery. — F., 'quibble, evasion',
fr. chicaner. See chicane, v.

## chicane
chicane, intr. v., to trick. — F. chicaner, 'to
quibble, wrangle, quarrel', of uncertain origin;
prob. not related to MHG. schicken, 'to
arrange, set in order' (see chic).
Derivatives: chican-er, п., chicanery (q.v.)

## chicanery
chicanery, п., trickery, quibbling, sophistry. —
F. chicanerie, fr. chicaner. See chicane, v. and
-ery.

## chich
chich, п., the chick-pea (obsol.) — F. chiche. See
chick-pea,

## chick
chick, n. — Shortened form of chicken.

## chickadee
chickadee, п., the black-capped titmouse. —
Imitative of its note.

## chickaree
chickaree, п., the red squirrel of North America.
— Imitative of its cry:

## chicken
chicken, n. and adj. — ME. chiken, fr. OE. ctcen,
cycen, rel. to MDu. kiekijen, кйкеп, Du. kieken,
kuiken, ON. kjuklingr, Swed. kyckling, Dan.
kylling, G. Kiichlein, 'chicken'. All these words
are diminutives formed fr. base *kjuk-, imitative
of the sound characteristic of a chicken. Cp.
cock.

## chickling
chickling, п., a small chicken. — Formed fr.
chick with dimin. suff. -ling.

## chick-pen
chick-pen, n. — F. pois chiche, chiche, fr. earlier
cice, fr. L. cicer, 'chick-pea', whence also It.
cece, OProvenc. ceze. Cp. Arm. sisefn,
'chickpea'. Cp. also OHG. chihkira (whence MHG.
kicher, G. Kichererbse), 'chick-pea', which is a
loan word fr. L. cicera, pi. of cicer, but was
influenced in form by the unrelated Gk. κιχόριον,
'chicory'. Cp. also OPruss. keekers, 'chick-pea',
which'was prob. also borrowed fr. L. cicer.

## chide
chide, п., a gummy substance. — Nahuatl chictti.

## chicory
chicory, n. — F. chicoree, fr. earlier cicoree, fr.
L. cichoreum, fr. Gk. κιχόριον, κιχόρεία, κίχώρη,
fr. OEgypt. kehsher. Cp. succory.

## chide
chide, intr. and tr. v. — ME. chiden, fr. OE. cidan,
of unknown origin.
Derivatives: chid-er, п., chid-ing, adj., chid-ing-
ly, adv., chid-ing-ness, n.

## chief
chief, n. — ME. chief, chef, fr. OF. (= F.) chef,
fr. VL. *capum, fr. L. caput, 'head'. See capital,
adj., and cp. chef, chieftain, achieve, mischief.
Derivatives: chief, adj., chief-ly, adv.

## chieftain
chieftain, n. — ME. chevetein, chefmyn, fr. OF.
chevetain, fr. Late L. capitaneus, 'head, chief,
fr. L. caput, gen. capitis, 'head'. See prec. word
and cp. capitan, eaptain. Cp. also prec. word.
Derivatives: chieflain-cy, п., chieftain-ess, п.,
chieftain-ry, n.

## ohiffchaff
ohiffchaff, п., the bird Phylhscopus collybila. —
Imitative of its note.

## chiffon
chiffon, п., a sheer silk fabric used for women's
dresses. — F., fr. chiffe, 'rag', pi. 'clothes', fr.
Arab, shiff, 'light garment', fr. shaffa, it was fine
and transparent' (said of materials).
Derivative: chiffon, adj.

## chiffonier
chiffonier, п., a high chest of drawers. — F. chif-
fonnier, fr. chiffon, 'rag'. See prec. word and -ier.

## chigger
chigger, п., 1) the larva of certain mites; z)
chigoe. — Fr. chigoe (q.v.)

## chignon
chignon, п., coil of hair worn at the back of the
head. — F., orig. 'nape of the neck', fr. VL.
*catlni6nem, ace. of *catenio, fr. L. catena,
'chain', which first became chaaignon, then
chaignon; the change of this latter to chignon
as well as the sense development of this word,
are due to the influence of F. tignon, 'coil of
hair'. See chnin and cp. concatenation.

## chigoe
chigoe, п., a flea (Sarcopsylla penetrans) — Of
W. Indian origin. Cp. chigger.

## chfl-
chfl-, form of chile- before a vowel.

## chllblaia
chllblaia, n. — Compounded of chill and blain.

## child
child, n. — ME. childe (pi. childre), fr. OE. cild
(pi. cildru), rel. to Goth, kilpei, 'womb', inkilpo,
'woman with child', OSwed. kulder, holder,
Swed. kull, Dan. kuld, 'children of the same
marriage; litter', and cogn. with OI. jafha-
ram (for *jalth-dram), 'belly, womb'. Cp. kilt
Derivatives: Childermas (q.v.), child-hood, п.,
child-ish, adj., child-like, adj., child-ness, n.

## Childermas (day)
Childermas (day), n. — OE. cildramxsse (dzg),
compounded of cildra, cildru, pi. of cild, 'child'
(see prec. word), and Mass (q.v.)

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:158 COLUMN:2 -->

## chili
chili, n. — See chilli.

## chiliad
chiliad, п., l) a thousand; 2) a thousand years. —
Gk. χΐλιάς, gen. χΐλιάδος, 'the number one
thousand', fr. χίλιοι, 'a thousand', which is of
uncertain origin. It is perh. cogn. with OI.
sahasram and with L. mille, 'a thousand'. See
mile and cp. next word and chiliasm. For the
ending see suff. -ad.

## chiliarch
chiliarch, п., the commander .of a thousand men.
— Gk. χΐλιάρχης, χΐλίαρχος, compounded of
χίλιοι, 'a thousand', and άρχος, 'leader, chief,
ruler'. See prec. word and -arch.

## chiliarchy
chiliarchy, п., the office of a chiliarch. — Gk.
χϊλιαρχίϋ, fr. χϊλιάρχης, χϊλίαρχος. See prec.
word and suff. -y (representing Gk. -15).

## chiliasm
chiliasm, п., the doctrine of the millennium. —
Gk. χΐλιαομός, fr. χϊλιάς, 'the number one
thousand'. See chiliad.

## chiliast
chiliast,n., a believer in the doctrine of chiliasm.—
Gk. χΐλιαστής, rel. to χϊλιασμός. See prec. word.
Derivative: chiliast-ic, adj.

## chill
chill, n. — ME. chele, fr. OE. ,cele, ciele, 'cold',
rel. to OE. calan, 'to be cold'. See cool.
Derivatives: chill, adj. and intr. and tr. v.,
chilling, adj., chill-ing-ly, adv., chill-y, adj., chill-i-
ness, n.

## chilli
chilli, п., the dried pod of Capsicum. — Sp. chili,
fr. Nahuatl chilli.

## chillo
chillo, п., a colored cotton material. — Sp. chilla,
fr. chtflon, 'showy, tawdry', lit. 'crying, loud,
shrill', fr. chillar, 'to scream, cry', fr. L. sibilare,
'to hiss, whistle', whence also OProvenc. siflar,
F. siffler, It. zufdare, 'to hiss, whistle'. See
sibilant and cp. siffle, zufolo.

## chillum
chillum, п., ι) part of the hookah containing the
tobacco; 2) the act of smoking the tobacco. —
Hind, chilam.

## chilo-
chilo-, before a vowel, chfl-, combining form
meaning 'lip' or 'lips'. — Gk. χειλο-, fr. χείλος,
'lip', rel. to χελόνη, 'lip, jaw', and prob. cogn..
with ON. gjelnar (pi.), 'gills'. See gill, 'organ
of respiration', and cp. the second element in
Megachile.

## Chiltern Hundreds
Chiltern Hundreds, the hundreds of Burnham,
Desborough and Stoke, in Buckinghamshire,
England. — See hundred (in its historical sense).
To accept the Chiltern Hundreds means 'to resign
from Parliament', prop, 'to accept an office
under the crown' (which disqualifies a Member
of Parliament).

## chllver
chllver, п., a ewe lamb (dial. Eng.) — OE. cilfor-
lamb, ceolforlamb, 'ewe lamb', rel. to OHG. kil-
bur (neut.), kilburra (fern.), of s.m., OE. cealf
'calf'. See calf, 'young of a cow'.

## Chlmaphila
Chlmaphila, п., a genus of plants of the winter-
green family (hot.) — ModL., lit. 'winter-
loving', fr. Gk. χεϊμα, 'winter', and φιλεϊν, 'to
love'. For the first element see chimera, for the
second see -phile.

## chimb
chimb, n. — See chime, 'rim of a cask'.

## chime
chime, п., a set of bells. — ME. chimbe, chymbe,
'cymbal', fr. OF. chimble, cimble, cimbe, fr. L.
cymbalum, 'cymbal'. See cymbal.
Derivatives: chime, tr. and intr. v., chim-er, n.

## chime
chime, chimb, п., rim of a cask. — ME. chimbe,
from the stem of OE. cimbing, 'joint', which is
rel. to Du. kim, 'chime', G. Kimme, dial. Swed.
kimb, kimbe, 'edge'. These words prob. stand
in gradational relationship to comb. Cp. dial.
Swed. kim, 'cockscomb'.

## chimer
chimer, chimere, п., a robe worn by bishops. —
MF. chamarre, samarre, 'a loose gown', fr. Sp.
zamarra, fr. Arab, sammar, 'weasel, marten'.
Cp. It. zimarra, 'robe; cassock', which was
formed with vowel dissimilation fr. Sp. zamarra.
F. simarre, 'robe; cassock', is a loan word fr. It.
zimarra. Ср. сушат, simar, zimarra.

## chimera
chimera, chimaera, п., a monster with lion's head,
goat's body and serpent's tail (Greek mythol.) —
L. chimaera, fr. Gk. χίμαιρα, 'a young she-
goat', which is rel. to χιμαρός, 'a young he-
goat', lit. 'one winter old', fr. χεϊμα, "winter',
which is cogn. with L. hiems, 'winter', hlbernus,
'pertaining to winter, wintry'. See hibernate and
cp. chiono-, the first element in Chimaphila and
the second element in Hedychium and in iso-
cheime.
Derivaiives: chimer-ic, chlmer-ic-al, adjs.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:158 COLUMN:3 -->

## chimere
chimere, n. — See chimer.

## chimney
chimney, n. — ME. chimenee, fr. OF. cheminee
(F. cheminee), fr. Late L,- (camera) caminala,
'(a room) provided with a chimney', fr. L. ca-
minus, 'forge, hearth', fr. Gk. κάμϊνος, which is
rel. to καμάρα, 'vaulted chamber', fr. I.-E. base
*qam-, "qem-, Ho bend, vault'. See camera and
cp. words fhere referred to.

## chimpanzee
chimpanzee, n. — From a S. African native word.

## chin
chin, n. — ME., fr. OE. cm, rel. to OS., OHG.
kinni, ON kim, MHG. kinne, >4. Kinn, 'chin',.
Goth, kinnus, 'cheek', and cogn. with OI. hdnuh,
'chin', Avestic zanu- (in compounds), 'chin*,
Toch. A ianwem, 'both jaws', Arm. cnawt,
'jawbone, cheek', Gk. γένος, 'the lower jaw,
cheek, chin", γένειον, 'chin', L. gena, 'cheek',
Lith. zandas, 'jawbone', Lett, zudds, 'chin', W.,
Bret., MCo. gen, 'jawbone, chin', Olr. gin, giun,
'mouth'. Cp. gena, genial, 'pertaining to the
chin', genio-, genyo-, gnathic.
Derivatives: chin, tr. v., chinn-ed, chinn-y, adjs.

## China
China, n. — Fr. Chin or Hsin, name of the First
Dynasty of China (255-206 B.C.E.). This word
lit. means 'man'. Cp. cheyney, chine, sinology.
Cp. also serge, Seric, silk.

## china
china, n. — Short for orig. chinaware, i.e. 'ware
from China'. See prec. word.

## chinar
chinar, also cheenar, п., the Oriental plane tree
(platanus Orientalis). — Pers. chinar.

## chinch
chinch, п., the bedbug. — Sp. chinche, fr. L. cf-
micem, ace. of cimex, 'bedbug'. See cimex.

## chinchilla
chinchilla, п., a small S. American rodent. —
Sp., a hybrid coined from a S. American native
name and the Spanish dimin. suff. -ilia.

## chin-chin
chin-chin, п., polite salutation; ceremonious talk.
— Chin, ts'ing-ts'ing, lit. 'please-please'.

## chincough
chincough, п., whooping cough. — Contraction
of chink cough. The first element of this word
is rel. to the first element in Fris. kinkhoast,
MLG. kinkhoste, Du. kinkhoesl, 'whooping
cough', fr. Teut. *kink-, a nasalized form of the
imitative base *kik-, 'to pant, gasp', whence
MHG. kichen, 'to pant'. Cp. G. keuchen, 'to
pant, gasp', which is a blend of MHG. kichen,
'to pant', and kuchen, 'to breathe'. Cp. kinkhost.
For the second element see cough,

## chine
chine, п., ι) a fissure (obsol.); 2) a narrow valley.
— ME., fr. OE. cinu, rel. to OE. cinan, 'to gape,
crack', OS., OHG. kinan, 'to germinate', Goth.
uskeinan, G. keimen, of s.m., MDu. klne, OS.
kin, G. Keim, 'germ', fr..I.-E. base *§li-, *gi-,
'to germinate, rise (said of flowers); to cleave,
split'. See key, п., and cp. chink, 'crack', chit,
'sprout'.

## chine
chine, п., backbone of an animal. — ME. chyne,
'back', fr. OF. eschine (F. echine), fr. Frankish
*skina. Cp. OHG. scina, 'needle, prickle; shin-
bone', and see shin.

## chine
chine, adj., figured after the Chinese fashion. —
F., pp. of chiner, 'to color differently, mottle,
figure', lit. 'to color after the Chinese fashion',
fr. Chine, 'China'. See china.

## Chinee
Chinee, п., a Chinese (vulg.) — Back formation
fr. Chinese, which was mistaken for a plural.

## Chinese
Chinese, adj. and n. — Formed fr. China with
suff. -ese.

## chink
chink, п., split, crack. — Formed fr. chine,
'fissure', with dimin. suff. -k.
Derivatives: chink, tr. v., chink-y, adj.

## chink
chink, п., a sharp clinking sound; intr. and tr. v.,
to make, resp. to cause to make, this sound. —
Of imitative origin.

## Chink
Chink, п., a Chinese (slang). — Fr. Chinee.

## Chinook
Chinook, п., а N. American Indian. — Native
name of a N. American Indian tribe living in
the Columbia River region.

## chintz
chintz, п., printed 'cotton cloth. — Orig. written
chints, fr. the sing, chint, fr. Hind, chin;, 'spotted
cloth', fr. OI. citrdh, 'bright, spotted'. See
cheetah.

## Chiococca
Chiococca, п., a genus of plants of the madder
family (bot.) — ModL., compounded of Gk.
χιών, 'snow', and κόκκος, 'kernel, berry'. See
chiono- and coccus.

## Chiogenes
Chiogenes, п., a genus of plants of the
huckleberry family (bot.) — ModL., lit. Offspring of
snow', fr. Gk. χιών, 'show', and γένος, 'race,
'descent, gender, kind' (see chiono- and geaus);

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:159 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: CHIONANTHUS | 132 -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:159 COLUMN:1 -->
so called from the snowwhite color of its berries.
Cp. E. snowberry.

## Chionanthus
Chionanthus, п., a genus of plants of the olive
family (bot.) — ModL., lit. 'snow flower', fr. Gk.
χιών, 'snow', and άνθος, 'flower' (see chiono-
and anther); so called from the snowwhite color
of its flowers.

## chiono-
chiono-, before a vowel chion-, combining form
meaning 'snow'. — Gk. χιονο-, χιον-, η\.χιών
(for *χιώμ), gen. χιόνος, 'snow', which is rel.
to χεΐμα, χειμών, 'winter', χίμαρος, 'a young
he-goat', lit. 'one winter old'. See chimera.

## chip
chip, tr. and intr. v. — ME. chippen, fr OE -cip-
pian, rel. to Du. kippen, G. kippen, 'to cut', and
in gradational relationship to E. chop, 'to cut'.
Derivatives: chipp-er, п., chipp-ing, n. and adj.,
chipp-y, adj. and n.

## chipmunk
chipmunk, chipmuck, п., a small American
squirrel. — Corruption of Algonquian achitamon,
'red squirrel', lit. 'headfirst'.

## Chippendale
Chippendale, adj. — Named after Thomas
Chippendale, a famous English cabinetmaker
(1718-79).

## chir-
chir-, form of chlro- before a vowel.

## chiragra
chiragra, п., pain in the hand (med.) — Medical
L., fr. Gk. χειράγρδ, 'gout in the hand', which
is compounded of χειρ, 'hand', and Жури, 'а
catching, seizure'. For the first element see
chlro-, chir-. The second element is rel. to Gk.
άγρέειν, 'to take, catch', and cogn. with Olr.
Sr (for *agra), 'defeat', W. aer, 'battle, struggle',
OCo. hair, 'disaster'. Cp. dentagra, pellagra,
podagra.

## chiral
chiral, adj., pertaining to the hand. — A hybrid
coined fr. Gk. χειρ, 'hand' (see chlro-), and -al,
a suff. of Latin origin.

## chirapsia
chirapsia, п., friction, massage (med.) — Medical
L., compounded of chir- and Gk. άψις, άψις,
'a touching, fastening'. See apsis.

## chlrata
chlrata, п., the plant Swertia chirata. — Hind.
chiraita, fr. OI. kirata tikta, lit. 'the bitter plant
of the people called Kiratas'.

## chirm
chirm, п., noise. — ME., fr. OE. cirm, cerm,
'shout, cry, noise'. Cp. charm, 'song of birds'.

## chirm
chirm, intr. v., to make a noise, to chirp. — ME.
chirmen, fr. OE. cirman, 'to shout, cry', fr. cirm.
See prec. word.

## chiro-
chiro-, before a vowel chir-, combining form
meaning 'hand'. — Gk. χειρο-, χειρ-, fr. χειρ,
gen. χειρός, 'hand', cogn. with Toch. A tsar,
В sar, Hitt. keshshar, kishshw, Arm. jern, gen.
jefin. Alb. dors (fr. I.-E. 'ghera-), 'hand', fr.
I.-E. base *§her-, 'to seize, take, hold, close,
envelope', whence also OI. harali, 'brings, carries,
takes away, robs', Gk. χόρτος, 'enclosure',
χορός, 'dance in a ring, dance', L. /tortus,
'garden', Goth, gards, 'house', OE. geard, 'piece of
land, garden, yard'. See yard, 'enclosure', and
cp. words there referred to. Cp. also cheiro-,
chirurgeon, enchiridion. Cp. also chorion, chorus,
chronic, and the second element in Dashahara
and in vihara.

## chirograph
chirograph, п.. a formally written legal document.
— F. chirographe, fr. L. chlrographum, fr. Gk.
χειρόγραφον, neut. of χειρόγραφος, 'written
with the hand', which is compounded of χεΙρ,
gen. χειρός, "hand', and -γράφος, fr. γράφειν, 'to.
write'. See chiro- and -graph.
chirograph)·, п., handwriting. — Cp. Gk. χείρο-
γραφίά, 'a written testimony', and see prec.
word and -y (representing Gk. -15).
Derivative: chirograph-ic, adj.

## chiromancer
chiromancer, п., a palmist. — See next word and
agential suff. -er.

## chiromancy
chiromancy, п., palmistry. — Lit. 'divination
from the hand'. See chiro- and -mancy.

## chiromantic
chiromantic, adj., pertaining to chiromancy. —
Compounded of chiro- and -mantic

## Chiron
Chiron, п., a centaur famous for his knowledge
of medicine (Greek mythol.) — L. Chiron, fr.
Gk. Χειρών, which is a word of uncertain origin.
It is possibly the abbreviation of χειρουργός,
'working by hand; surgeon'. See chirurgeon.

## chiropody
chiropody, п., the treatment of diseases of the
feet (med.) — Orig. 'the treatment of the diseases
of the hands and feet', fr. Gk. χειρ, gen. χειρός,
'hand', and πους, gen. ποδός, 'foot'. See chiro-
and podo-.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:159 COLUMN:2 -->
Derivative: chiropod-ist, n.

## chiropractic
chiropractic, п., ι) a system of treating disease
by adjusting the joints of the body, esp. the
spinal column, by hand; 2) a chiropractor. —
Compounded of Gk. χειρ, gen. χειρός, 'hand',
and πρακτικός, 'fit for action, practical'. See
chiro- and practical.

## chiropractor
chiropractor, п., one who practices chiropractic.
— See prec. word and agential suff. -or.

## Chiroptera
Chiroptera, n. pi., the order of the bats (zool.) —
ModL., compounded of Gk. χειρ, gen. χειρός,
'hand', and πτερόν, 'wing'. See chiro-and ptero-.

## Chirotes
Chirotes, п., a genus of burrowing lizards (zool.)
— ModL., fr. Gk. χειρ, gen. χειρός, 'hand'.
See chiro-.

## chirp
chirp, intr. and tr. v. — Of imitative origin. Cp.
the next two words.
Derivatives: chirp, п., chirp-er, п., chirp-ing,
adj., chirp-ing-ly, adv.

## chirr
chirr, intr. v., to make a trilling sound (as that
made by a grasshopper and some birds): tr.v.,
to utter with a chirr. — Of imitative origin. Cp.
churr. Cp. also prec. word. Derivative: chirr, n.

## chirrup
chirrup, intr. v. — Of imitative origin. Cp. chirp.
Derivatives: chirrup, п., chirrup-er, п., chirrup-
y, adj.

## chirurgeon
chirurgeon, п., a surgeon (archaic). — F. chirur-
gien, fr. chirurgie, 'surgery', ult. fr. Gk. χει-
ρουργίά, lit. 'a working by hand', fr. χειρουργός,
'working by hand', which is compounded of
χείρ, 'hand', and ϊργον, "work". See chiro- and
ergon and cp. surgeon, which is a doublet of
chirurgeon. Cp. also Chiron.
Derivative: chirurgeon-ly, adv.

## chirurgery
chirurgery, n. (archaic). — See surgery, which is
a doublet of chirurgery, and cp. prec. word.

## -chirurgia
-chirurgia, combining form meaning '-surgery'.
— Fr. Gk. χειρουργίδ; see chirurgeon.

## chirurgie
chirurgie, chirurgical, adj. (archaic). — L. chirur-
gicus (whence also F. chirurgique), fr. Gk.
χειρουργικός, 'worked by hand', fr. χειρουργία. See
chirargeon, and -ic

## chisel
chisel, п., a cutting instrument. — ME., fr. AF.
chisel, corresponding to OF. cisel (F. ciseau),
fr. VL. *cisellus, which was altered fr. *caesellus,
'cutting instrument', fr. L. caesus,pp. otcaedere,
4o cut'. Cp. L. cisorium, 'cutting instrument',
and see cement Derivatives: chisel, tr. v., chisel(l)
-ed, adj., chisel(t)-er, n.

## chisel
chisel, n. — A var. of chesll.

## chit
chit, п., a shoot, sprout. — OE. cip, 'germ, shoot,
sprout', rel. to cinan, 'to gape, crack'. See chine,
'a narrow valley'. Derivatives: chit, intr. v., to
shoot, sprout, chitt-y, adj.

## chit
chit, п., ι) a young animal (obsol.); 2) a child. —
Prob. a var. of kit, kitten. Cp. dial. E. chit, 'cat,
kitten'.

## chit
chit, chitty, п., a short letter. — Hind, chi/lhl, fr.
OI. citrdh, 'bright, marked, spotted'. See cheetah.

## chit-chat
chit-chat, n. — Reduplication of chat.

## chitin
chitin, п., a substance forming the hard covering
of insects and other invertebrates (biochem.) —
F. chitine, fr. Gk. χιτών, 'undergarment, coat of
mail, any coat or covering'. See chiton.

## chitinous
chitinous, adj., of the nature of chitin. — Formed
fr. chitin with suff. -она.

## chiton
chiton,n., a garment worn by both sexes in ancient
Greece. — Gk. χιτών, Ion. κιθών, borrowed—
through the medium of the Phoenicians—from
the Semites. Cp. Heb. kultoneth, Aram, kittdna,
Arab, kalian, Akkad. kitinnu, 'linen', Akkad.
kitintu, 'linen garment'. Cp. also chitia, tunic
Χιτών occurs in Mycenaean Greek as early as
the 15th century. See Michael Ventris atid John
Chadwick, Documents in Mycenaean Greek
(Cambridge University Press), Index, s. v. Semitic
Loanwords. Cp. the words chrysalis, cumin, se-
sam.

## chltter
chltter, intr. v. — Of imitative origin. Cp. chatter,
twitter.

## chitterlutg
chitterlutg, п., usually pi. chitterlings, the small
intestines of pigs. — Rel. to OE. cwid, 'womb',
ON. kvidr, 'belly', Goth, qiprn, 'womb', MHG.
kutel, G. Kutteln, 'guts, bowels; tripe;
chitterlings', and cogn. with L. botulus, 'sausage'. See
boweL For the ending see suff. -liag.

## chitty
chitty, п., a short letter. — Hind, chiffhi. See
chit, "a short letter'.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:159 COLUMN:3 -->

## chivaleresque
chivaleresque, adj. — Formed fr. chivalry with
suff. -esque, on analogy of F. chevaleresque.

## chivalrous
chivalrous, adj. — OF. chevalereus, fr. chevalier.
See chevalier and -wis.
Derivatives: chivalrous-ly,adv.,chivalrous-ness,n.

## chivalry
chivalry, n. — ME. chivalrie, chivalerye, fr. OF.
(= F.) chevalerie, 'knighthood', fr. chevalier,
'knight'. See chevalier and cp. cavalry.

## chive
chive, п., a plant related to the onion. — ONF.
chive, corresponding to OF. and F. cive, fr. L.
сера, 'onion'. See cibol.

## chiviatite
chiviatite, п., a lead bismuth sulfide (mineral!) —
Named after Chiviato in Peru. For the ending
see subst. suff. -Ite.

## chivy
chivy, n. and tr. v. — See chevy.

## chladnite
chladnite, п., a variety of enstatite. — Named
after E. F. Chladni, a writer on meteorites. For
the ending see subst. suff. -ite.

## chlamyd-
chlamyd-, form of chlamydo- before a vowel.

## chlamydate
chlamydate, adj., having a mantle (zool.) — L.
chlamydatus, 'dressed in a chlamys', fr. chlamys.
See chlamys and adj. suff. -ate.

## chlamydeous
chlamydeous, adj., having a perianth (hot.) —
Formed fr. chlamys with suff. -eons.

## chlamydo-
chlamydo-, before a vowel chlnmyd-, combining
form meaning 'mantie' (zool. and bol.) — Gk.
χλαμυδο-, χλαμυδ-, fr. χλαμύς, gen. χλαμύδος.
See next word.

## chlamys
chlamys, п., a short mantle worn by the ancient
Greeks (Greek antiq.) — L., fr. Gk. χλαμύς,
gen. χλαμΰδος, 'upper garment, mantle', which
is of uncertain origin.

## chloasma
chloasma, п., a deposit of pigment in the skin
(med.) — Medical L., fr. Gk. χλόασμα,
'greenness', fr. χλοάζειν, 'to be green', fr. χλόη. See
next word.
Chloe", Chloe, fern. PN. — L., fr. Gk. Χλόη, fr.
χλόη, 'a young green shoot, young verdure', rel.
to χλόος, 'greenish-yellow color', χλοάζειν, 'to
be green', χλωρός, 'greenish yellow, pale green,
green, fresh', χολή, 'gall*. See yellow and cp.
choler, chlorine. Cp. also the second element in
Buchloc, Hierochloe.

## chlor-
chlor-, form of chioro- before a vowel.

## chloral
chloral, п., a colorless liquid, CCl3CHO (chem.)
— Coined fr. chlor(ine) and al(cohol).

## chlorate
chlorate, п., a salt of chloric acid (chem.) — See
chlorine and chem. suff. -ate.

## Chiorella
Chiorella, п., a genus of green algae (bot.) —
ModL., formed with suff. -ella fr. Gk. χλωρός.
See Chloe.

## chloric
chloric, adj., pertaining to, or obtained from,
chlorine (chem.) — Formed fr. chlorine with suff. -ic.

## chioride
chioride, chlorid, п., a compound of chlorine with
another element (chem.) — See chlorine and
-ide, -id.

## chlorine
chlorine, n„ name of a nonmetallic element
belonging to the halogen family (chem.) — Coined
by the English chemist Sir Humphrey Davy
(1778-1829) fr. Gk. χλωρός, 'greenish yellow,
pale green, green, fresh'. See Chloe. For the
ending see chem. suff. -ine and cp. brom-ine,

## fluor-ine
fluor-ine, iod-ine. Derivative: chlorin~ous, adj.

## Chloris
Chloris, п.,«name of the goddess of flowers in
Greek mythology; later identified with the
Roman goddess Flora (Greek mythol.) — L., fr.
Gk. Χλωρίς, lit. 'greenness, freshness', which is
rel. to χλωρός. See prec. word.

## Chloris
Chloris, п., a genus of grasses (bot.) — Named
after Chloris, the goddess of flowers. See prec. word.

## chioro-
chioro-, before a vowel chlor-, combining form
1) meaning light-green; 2) denoting the presence
of chlorine in a compound. — Fr. Gk. χλωρός.
See chioriae.

## chloroform
chloroform, п., a volatile liquid, CHC13, used as
an anesthetic (chem.) — F. chloroforme, a hybrid
coined by Jean-Baptiste Dumas (1800-84) in
1834 fr. chioro- and F. formique, 'formic' (fr. L.
formica, 'ant', see formic); so called by him in
allusion to its capacity of forming potassium
chloride and formic acid.

## Chloromycetin
Chloromycetin, п., an antibiotic drug of the
penicillin-streptomycin family discovered by Paul
R. Burkholder of Yale University (med.) —
Coined fr. chioro-, Gk. μύκης, gen. μύκητος,
'fungus' (see myceto-), and chem. suff. -in.

## chlorophyll
chlorophyll, chiorophyl, п., the green coloring
matter of plants. — F. chlorophylle, coined by

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:160 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: 133 | CHORAL -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:160 COLUMN:1 -->
the French chemists Pierre-Joseph Pelletier
(1788-1842) and Joseph-Bienaime Caventou
(1795-1877) fr. chloro- and Gk. φύλλον, 'leaf
See phyllo- and cp. the second element in xan-
thophyU.

## chloroprene
chloroprene, п., a colorless liquid used to
manufacture neoprene (chem.) — Coined fr. chioro-
and (isu)prene.

## chlorosis
chlorosis, п., a kind of anemia, 'green sickness'
(med.) — Medical L., formed with sun", -osis
fr. Gk. χλωρός, 'greenish-yellow, pale green,
green, fresh'. See chlorine.

## choana
choana, п., a funnel-shaped opening (mat.) —
Medical L., fr. Gk. χοάνη, 'funnel, funnel-shaped
hollow in the brain', a derivative of χοή, 'a
pouring out', from the stem of χεΐν, 'to pour', which
is cogn. with L. fundere, 'to pour'. See found,
'to cast', and cp. chyle. Cp. also lhe first element
in chonolith,

## chobdar
chobdar, п., an attendant (Anglo-Ind.) — Hind.
chobdar, fr. Pers. chobdar, lit. 'a stick bearer'.
For the element -dar see aumildar and cp. words
there referred to.

## chock
chock, п., a block of wood. — ONF. chouque, rel.
to F. souche, 'stump, stock, block', fr. Gaulish
*lsukka, which is cogn. with OE. stocc, trunk,
log, stock'. See stock and cp. chuck, n.
Derivatives: chock, tr. v., chock-er, n.

## chocolate
chocolate, n. — Sp., fr. Nahuatl chocolatl.

## Choctaw
Choctaw, п., name of a North-American Indian
tribe.

## Choctaw
Choctaw, п., name of a particular step in fancy
ice-skating. — From prec. word.

## -choerus
-choerus, combining form meaning 'pig', as in
Hydrochoerus (zool.) — ModL., fr. Gk. χοίρος,
'pig', which stands for "ghor-yos and lit. means
'the bristle-bearing animal', fr. I.-E. base *gher-,
'to bristle', whence also Gk. χήρ, 'hedgehog',
L. horrere, 'to stand on end, bristle, shudder,
tremble'. See horror and cp. Chersonese.

## choice
choice, n. — ME. chois, choys, fr. OF. chois (F.
choix), fr. choisir, 'to choose', fr. Goth, kausjan,
'to prove, test' (whence also OProvenc. causir,
'to look at'), which is rel. to Goth, kiusan, OE.
ceosan, 'to choose'. See choose.
Derivatives: choice, adj., choice-ly, adv., choice-
ness, n.

## choir
choir, quire, n. — ME. quer, fr. OF. cuer (F.
chceur), fr. L. chorus, fr. Gk. χορός, 'dance in a
ring'. See chorus.
Derivative: choir, tr. and intr. v.

## choke
choke, intr. and tr. ν — ME. cheken, choken,
aphetic for achcken, achoken, fr. OE. aceocian,
'to choke', which is prob. formed fr. intensive
pref. a- and a Teut. base appearing in ON. kok,
'gullet'.
Derivatives: choke, п., chok-er, п., chok-ing,
adj., chok-ing-ly, adv., chok-y, adj.

## chokidar
chokidar, п., a watchman, porter. — Hind.
chauki-dar, 'watchman', fr. chauki, 'watching',
ahd surf, -dar, 'holder, possessor'. For the first
element see choky. For the second element see
anmildar and Cp. words there referred to.

## chokra
chokra, п., a boy (Anglo-Ind.) — Hind, chokra,
'a boy'.

## choky
choky, п., ι) a station, esp. a police station; 2) a
jail. — Hind, chauki. Cp. the first element in
chokidar.

## cholagogue
cholagogue, adj., promoting the secretion of bile
(med.) — F., fr. Gk. χολαγωγός, 'carrying off
bile', which is compounded of χολή, 'bile', and
αγωγός, 'leading'. See choler and -agogne.
Derivatives: cholagogue, п., cholagog-ic, adj.

## cholangitis
cholangitis, п., inflammation of the biliary ducts
(med.) — Medical L., compounded of Gk.
■χολή, 'bile', άγγεΐαν, 'vessel', and suff. -ΐτις.
See choler, angio- and -itis.

## chole-
chole-, combining form meaning 'gall'. — See
cholo-.

## cholecyst
cholecyst, п., the gall bladder (anat.) — Medical
L. cholecystis, incorrect formation fr. Gk. χολή,
'gall, bile', and κύστις, 'bladder, bag, pouch'.
See choler and cyst.

## cholecyst-
cholecyst-, form of cholecysto- before a vowel.

## cholecystitis
cholecystitis, п., inflammation of the gall bladder.
— Medical L., formed fr. cholecystis (see prec.
word) with suff. -itis.

## cholecysto-
cholecysto-, before a vowel cholecyst-, combining

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:160 COLUMN:2 -->
form denoting the gall bladder. — See prec.
word.

## choledoch
choledoch, adj., conveying bile (anat.) — Gk.
χοληδόχος, 'containing bile', compounded of
χολή, 'bile', and δοχός, 'containing, able to
hold', which is rel. to δέχεσθαι, Attic form of
Gk. δέκεσθ-αι, 'to receive, hold'. For the first
element see choler. The second element is a
derivative of I.-E. base *dek-, 'to receive', whence
also OI. ddksati, 'is apt, proper', daksah, 'apt,
proper, clever', L. decet, decere, 'to be fitting
or seemly'. See decent and cp. the second
element in pandect and the third element in
synecdoche.

## choledocho-
choledocho-, combining form meaning
'containing bile'. — See prec. word.

## choler
choler, n. — ME. coler, colere, fr. OF. colere (F.
colere), 'choler, anger', fr. L. cholera, fr. Gk.
χολέρα, 'bilious diarrhea, cholera', fr. χολή, also
χόλος, 'gall, bile', which is rel. to χλόος, 'greenish-
yellow color', χλοάζειν, 'to be green', χλωρός,
'greenish-yellow, pale green, green, fresh', and
cogn. with Avestic zara-, 'gall, bile', L. fel,
OSlav. zluci, Russ. zelc', Lith. lulzis (metathesis
for *zultls), Lett, zults, OE. gealla, galla, 'gall,
bile', fr. I.-E. base *ghel-, *ghel-, 'to shine;
yellow, yellowish green, green'. See yellow and cp.
gall, 'bile'. Cp. also next word, Chloe, ChioreUa,
chlorine, Chloris, and the second element in
melancholy, Chrysochloris, Echinochloa. Cp. also
the second element in bezoar.

## cholera
cholera, n. — L. cholera, fr. Gk. χολέρα, 'bilious
diarrhea', fr. χολή, 'gall, bile'. See prec. word.

## choleraic
choleraic, adj., related to, or resembling, cholera.
— Formed from prec. word with suff. -Ic.

## choleric
choleric, adj. — MF. (= F.) cholerique, fr. L.
cholericus, fr. Gk. χολερικός, fr. χολέρα, (see
choler and -ic): first used by Chaucer.
Derivatives: choleric-ly, adv., choleric-ness, n.

## cholesterine
cholesterine, п., cholesterol. — See next word
and chem. suff. -ine.

## cholesterol
cholesterol, n, a fatty alcohol (biochem.) —
Formed fr. F. cholesterine, a word coined by the
French chemist Michel-Eugene Chevreul (1786-
1889), and -ol, a suff. denoting an alcohol. F.
cholesterine is formed fr. Gk. χολή, 'gall, bile',
and στερεός, 'solid' (see chole- and stereo-), and
is so called because it was originally found in
gallstones.

## chollamb
chollamb, п., an iambic verse having in the last
foot a spondee (instead of an iambus) (pros.) —
L. choliambus, fr. Gk. χωλίαμβος, 'a lame
iambic', which is compounded of χωλός, 'lame', a
word of uncertain origin, and ίαμβος, 'iambus'.
See iambus.

## choliambic
choliambic, adj., pertaining to a choliamb. —
Gk. χωλιαμβικός, fr. χωλίαμβος. See prec. word
and -ic.
Derivative: choliambic, n.

## cholic
cholic, adj., pertaining to the bile. — Gk. χολικός,
fr. χολή, 'bile'. See choler and -ic.

## choliae
choliae, п., a crystalline base, CjHJ5N02
(biochem.) — Formed with chem. suff. -ine fr. Gk.
χολή, 'bile'. See choler.

## cholo-
cholo-, before a vowel chol-, combining form
meaning 'bile'. — Gk. χόλο-, χολ-, fr. χολή,
'bile'. See choler and cp. cbole-, cholic, choline.

## chololith
chololith, п., a gallstone. — Compounded of
cholo- and Gk. λίθος, 'stone'. See -lith.
Derivative: chololith-ic, adj.

## chdmage
chdmage, п., stoppage, cessation from work. —
F., fr. chdmer, 'to cease from work', fr. Late
L. caumare, fr. сайта, 'tranquillity'. See calm
and -age.

## chondr-
chondr-, form of chondri- before a vowel.

## chondri-
chondri-, — See chondro-.

## chondrify
chondrify, tr. v., to convert into cartilage. — A
hybrid coined fr. Gk. χόνδρος, 'cartilage', and
L. -ficare, fr. facere, 'to make, do'. See chondro-
and -fy.

## Chondrilla
Chondrilla, п., a genus of plants of the chicory
family (bot.) — ModL., fr. L. chondrilll,
'Spanish succory', fr. Gk. χονδρίλλη, χονδρίλη, name
of a gum-exuding plant.

## chondritis
chondritis, п., inflammation of a cartilage (med.)
— Medical L., formed with suff. -itis fr. Gk.
χόνδρος, 'cartilage'. See chondro-.

## chondro-
chondro-, before a vowel chondr-, combining form

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:160 COLUMN:3 -->
meaning 'grain' or 'cartilage'. — Gk. χονδρό-;
χονδρ-, fr. χόνδρος, 'corn, grain, groat;
cartilage', dissimilated fr. *χρόνδρος, cogn. with L.
frendere, 'to gnash the teeth', OE grindan, 'to
grind'. See grind and cp. the second element
in enchondroma, hypochondria, perichondrium,
synchondrosis. Cp. also chrism, chrome.

## chondrodite
chondrodite, п., a yellowish red mineral. —
Formed with subst. suff. -ite fr. Gk. χον&ρώ&ης,
'granular', fr. χόνδρος, 'grain', and -ώδης, 'like'.
See chondro- and -ode, 'like'.

## cbondroid
cbondroid, adj., resembling cartilage. — Formed
fr. Gk. χόνδρος, 'cartilage', and -οειδής, 'like',
fr. είδος, 'form, shape'. See chondro- and -oid.

## chondroma
chondroma, п., a cartilaginous tumor (med.) —
Medical L., formed with suff. -oma fr. Gk.
χόνδρος, 'cartilage'. See chondro-.

## chonolith
chonolith, п., a mass of igneous rock (geol.) —
Compounded of χώνη, 'melting pot, crucible'
and λίθος, 'stone'. The first element is a
contraction of χοάνη, which derives from the stem
of χεΐν, 'to pour', whence also χύσις, 'effusion',
χυλός, χυμός, 'juice'. See chyle and cp. words
there referred to. For the second element see
-lith.

## choose
choose, tr. and intr. v. — ME. cheosen, chesen,
chusen, fr. OE ceosan, rel. to OS., OHG. kiosan,
ON. kjosa, OFris. kiasa, Du. kiezen, MHG., G.
kiesen, Goth, kiusan, 'to choose', and to Goth.
kausjan, 'to prove, test', fr. I.-E. base *geus-,
*gus-, 'to taste, enjoy by tasting', whence also
Gk. γεύεσθαι, 'to taste', L. gustare, 'to taste,
enjoy', OI. josatijusdte, 'enjoys', Avestic zaosh-,
'to find delicious', Olr. gu-, go-, 'to choose1. Cp.
OE. costian, OS., OHG. koston, ON. kosta,
MHG., G. kosten, 'to test, try, taste', which are
all related to OE. ceosan, etc. F. choisir, 'to
choose', OProvenc. causir, 'to look at', OSlav.
kusiti, 'to taste, try', are Goth, loan words. Cp.
choice. Cp. also grist, 'relish', disgust, and the
second element in Fergus and In valkyrie.
Derivatives: choos-er, п., choos-ing, adj., choos-
ing-ly, adv.

## chop
chop, tr. and intr. v., to cut. — ME. choppen, 'to
cut up', in gradational relationship to ME. chap-
pen, 'to cut'. See chap, 'to chop', and cp. chip.
Derivatives: chop, п., chopp-er, п., chopp-ing,
adj., chopp-y, adj.

## chop
chop, п., ι) jaw; 2) entrance of a valley or channel.
— See chap, 'jaw'.
Derivative: chop, tr. v., to snap with lhe jaws.

## chop
chop, tr. and intr. v., to barter. — Rel. to ME.
cheapien, 'to buy, bargain'. See cheap, v., and
chapman.
Derivative: chop, п., a barter.

## chop
chop, п., seal, stamp; brand, quality (Anglo-Ind.)
— Hind, chap, 'seal, stamp'.

## chopin
chopin, chopine, п., a liquid measure. — F. cho-
pine, fr. Du. schopen, lit. 'a scoop'. Cp. MLG.
schope, 'scoop, ladle', and see scoop and shovel.
G. Schoppen, 'mug', has been reborrowed fr.
NF. chopenne, the equivalent of F. chopine.

## chopine
chopine, п., a kind of thick-soled shoe, patten. —
OF. chapin, fr. OSp. (= Sp.) chapin, fr. chapa,
'a plate of metal, foil, leather chape', which is
of uncertain origin.

## chopstick
chopstick, п., two small sticks used by the
Chinese in place of a fork. — Compounded of
Pidgin English chop(-chop), 'quick', prop, a loan
translation of the orig. Chinese name which lit.
means 'the quick ones', and E. stick, n.

## ehop suey
ehop suey, a Chinese dish. — Chin., lit. 'various
pieces'; influenced in form by E. chop, 'to cut'.

## chor-
chor-, form of chore- before a vowel.

## choragic
choragic, adj., pertaining to a choragus. — Gk.
χοραγικός, fr. χοραγός, 'leader of the chorus'.
See next word and -ic.

## choragus
choragus, п., the leader of the chorus (Greek an-
tiq.) — L., fr. Gk. χοραγός, χορηγός,
compounded of χορός, 'chorus', and the stem of αγειν,
'to lead', which is cogn. with L. agere, 'to set
in motion, drive, lead'. See chorus and agent.

## choral
choral, adj. — F. choral, fr. ML. choralis,
'pertaining to the chorus', fr. L. chorus. See chorus
and adj. suff. -al.

## choral
choral, chorale, п., hymn. — G. Choral,
shortened fr. Choralgesang, trans], of ML. cantus·
choralis, 'choral song', fr. L. cantus, 'song', and

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:161 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: CHORD | 134 -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:161 COLUMN:1 -->
ML. choralis. See choral, adj.

## chord
chord, п., string of an instrument. — L. chorda,
'gut, string of a musical instrument, rope, cord',
fr. Gk. χορδή, 'intestine, string of gut, string
of a musical instrument', which is cogn. with
OI. hira, 'vein', hirah, 'band', L. hernia, 'rupture',
him, 'empty gut', haruspex, 'diviner
inspecting entrails', Lith. zarna, Lett, zarna, 'gut', OE.
gearn, 'yarn'. See yam and cp. cord, and the
second element in ncrochordon, clavichord, noto-
chord. Cp. also hernin and the first element in
haruspex. Cp. also quirt
Derivatives: chord, tr. v., chord-ed, adj.

## chord
chord, п., combination of notes (music). — Fr.
earlier cord, abbreviation of accord (q.v.) The
spelling with A is due to a confusion with chord,
'string of an instrument'.
Derivative: chord, intr. v.

## Cbordata
Cbordata, n. pi., a phylum of the animal
kingdom including all vertebrates (zool.) — ModL.,
fr. L. chorda, 'cord'. See chord, 'string'.

## chore
chore, п., a job (U.S.A.} — A var. of chare.
Derivative: chore, intr. and tr. v.

## chorea
chorea, п., a nervous disorder; St. Vitus' dance.
— Medical L., fr. Gk. χορεία, 'dance', fr.
χορός, 'dance in a ring; chorus, choir'. See
chorus.

## choreography
choreography, п., the art of denoting dancing by
signs. — Compounded of Gk. χορεία, 'dance',
and -γραφιά, fr. γράφειν, 'to write*. See chorus
and -graphy.
Derivative: choreograph-ic, adj.

## choreus
choreus, п., a trochee (pros.) — L., fr. Gk.
χορείος, lit. 'pertaining to a chorus', adj. used
as a noun. fr. χορός, 'dance; chorus*. Seechorus.

## chori-
chori-, pref. meaning 'separate' (bot.) — Fr. Gk.
χωρίς, χώρι, 'separate, apart', rel. to χώρος,
χώρα, 'empty space, room, place, land, country',
χωρεΐν, 'to give place; to hold, contain',
χωρίζειν, 'to separate', fr. I.-E. base *ghe(i)-, 'to lack,
be empty', which is identical with *ghl(i)-, 'to
gape, yawn', whence Gk. χαίνειν, 'to yawn,
gape'. See chaos and cp. chorisis, chorist, cho-
rlsto-, chorizontes, chore-, and the second
element in anchorite, enchorial, epichorial, para-
chor.

## choriamb
choriamb, п., a foot composed of a choreus (=
trochee) followed by an iambus (pros.) — L.
choriambus, fr. Gk. χορίαμβος, which is
compounded of χορείος, 'choreus', and Ιαμβος,
'iambus'. See choreus and inmbus.

## choriamblc
choriamblc, adj., pertaining to a choriamb. —
L. choriambicus, fr. Gk. χοριαμβικός, fr.
χορίαμβος. See prec. word and -ic
Derivative: choriambic, n.

## chorioid
chorioid, adj!, pertaining to vascular membranes
(anat.) — Lit. 'like a membrane', fr. Gk.
χοριοειδής, fr. χόριον, 'skin, leather', and -οειδής,
'like', fr. είδος, 'form, shape'. See chorion and
-oid.
Derivatives: chorioid, п., vascular tunic of the
eye, chorioid-al, adj.

## chorioido-
chorioido-, before a vowel chorioid-, combining
form denoting the chorioid. — See prec. word.

## chorion
chorion, п., the membrane enclosing the fetus
(embryol.) — ModL., fr. Gk. χόριον,
'membrane that encloses the fetus, afterbirth', which
is of uncertain origin. It derives perh. fr. I.-E.
base *gher-, 'to seize, hold, close, envelop',
whence also χειρ, 'hand'. See chiro-.
Derivative: chorion-ic, adj.

## choripetalous
choripetalous, adj., having separate petals (bot.)
— See chori-, petal and -ous.

## chorisis
chorisis, п., separation of an organ into parts
(bol.) — ModL., fr. Gk. χώρισις, 'separation',
fr. χωρίζειν, 'to separate', fr. χωρίς, 'separate,
apart'. See chori-.

## chorist
chorist, п., member of a chorus. — F. choriste, fr.
Eccles. L. chorisla, fr. L. chorus. See chorus
and -1st.

## chorister
chorister, п., member of a choir. — See prec.
word and -ister.

## choristo-
choristo-, before a vowel chorist-, combining form
meaning 'separated'. — Fr. Gk. χωριστός,
verbal adj. of χωρίζειν, 'to separate', fr. χωρίς,
χώρι, 'separate, apart'. See chori-.

## chorizontes
chorizontes, n. pi., the Alexandrian critics who
maintained that the Iliad and Odyssey were

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:161 COLUMN:2 -->
written by different authors. — Gk. χωρίζοντες,
lit. 'separators', pi. of χωρίζων, pres. part, of
χωρίζειν, 'to separate'. See chori- and cp.
chorisis, choristo-.

## choro-
choro-, before a vowel chor-, combining form
meaning 'place*. — Gk. χωρο-,χωρ-, fr. χώρος,
'place'. See chori-.

## chorography
chorography, п., description or mapping of a
particular country or region. — L. chorographia,
fr. Gk. χωρογραφία, which is compounded of
χώρος, 'place', and -γραφιά, fr. γράφειν, 'to
write*. See choro- and -graphy.
Derivatives: chorograph-ic, chorograph-ic-al,
adjs., chorograph-ic-al-ly, adv.

## choroid
choroid, adj., chorioid (anat.) — Gk. χοροειδής,
inexact form for χοριοειδής. See chorioid.
Derivatives: choroid, п., choroid-al, adj.

## choroldo-
choroldo-, before a vowel choroid-, combining
form denoting the choroid. — See prec. word
and chorioido-.

## chorology
chorology, п., the study of the geographical
distribution of organisms (biol.) — Compounded
of choro- and Gk. -λογία, fr. -λόγος, 'one who
speaks (in a certain manner); one who deals
(with a certain topic)'. See -logy.
Derivatives: chorolog-ical, adj., chorolog-ist, n.

## chortle
chortle, intr. and tr. v. and n. — A blend of
chuckle and snort; coined by Lewis Carroll

## chorus
chorus, n. — L., fr. Gk. χορός, 'dance in a n.,g,
festive dance, dance; band of dancers; chorus,
choir; troop, band; place for dancing'. The first
meaning was prob. 'an enclosed place for
dancing', from I.-E. base *gher-, 'to seize, take, hold,
close, envelop', whence also Gk. χείρ, 'hand',
χόρτος, 'feeding place, courtyard'. See chiro-
and cp. words there referred to. Cp. also choir,
quire, chorea, choreus, the first element in carol
and in choragus and the second element in
Terpsichore.
Derivatives: chorus, v., chorus-er, n.

## chose
chose, past tense of choose. — ME. choos, formed
on analogy of the pp. chosen. See chosen.

## chose
chose, п., thing, property (used in the legal terms
chose in action, chose in possession). — F. chose,
'thing', fr. L. causa, 'cause, reason', in Late L.
also 'thing'. Cp. OProvenc. cauza, It., Sp. cosa,
Port, cousa, 'thing', which all derive fr. L.
causa in its Late Latin sense, and see cause.

## chosen
chosen, pp. of choose. —· ME. chosen, fr. OE.
coren; influenced in form by choose.

## chou
chou, п., an ornamental ribbon or knot in
women's dress. — F., 'cabbage', fr. L. caulis, 'stalk',
esp. 'cabbage stalk'. See cole.

## Chouan
Chouan, п., one of the antirevolutionary
insurgents in Western France in 1791. — F., from
the surname of one of their leaders Jean Cot-
terau, called Jean Chouan, fr. chouan, dialectal
contraction of chat-huant, 'screech owl'. He
and his three brothers were so named because
they used to imitate the cry of the screech owl
to warn one another in time of danger. Chat-
huant lit. 'shouting cat', is a popular alteration
of OF. javan (for ckavan), fr. ML. cavannus,
'owl', a word of Gaulish origin.

## choucronte
choucronte, п., sauerkraut. — F., fr. Alsatian G.
surkrut (corresponding to G. Sauerkraut), lit.
'sour cabbage', fr. sur, 'sour', and krut,
'cabbage', with folk-etymological change of sur, to
F. chou, 'cabbage', and krut to F. croute, 'crust'.
See sanerkraut.

## chough
chough, п., the red-legged crow. — ME. choughe,
rel. to OE. ceo, ciae, MDu. cauwe, Du. kauv/,
OHG. kSha, 'chough', Dan. kaa, Swed. kaja,
'jackdaw'; of imitative origin. Cp. OF. choe,
'screech owl', which derives fr. Frankish *kawa,
'chough', and F. chouette, 'screech owl', which
is a dimin. of OF. chae.

## chouse
chouse, п., a swindler (obsol.); a swindle (colloq.)
— Turk, chawush, chaush, 'sergeant, herald,
messenger'. The meaning of E. chouse is due to
the circumstance that in 1609 a chiaus is said
to have cheated several Turkish merchants
residing in England. Cp. chiaus.
Derivatives: chouse, tr. v., to swindle (colloq.).

## chow
chow, п., Chinese (Australian slang). — See
next word.

## chowchow
chowchow, п., Chinese preserves. — Pidgin
English, lit. 'mixed', of Chinese origin.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:161 COLUMN:3 -->

## chowder
chowder, п., a dish of stewed fish, clams, onion,
etc. — F. chaudiire, 'pot', fr. Late L. caldaria, 'a
vessel containing warm water'. See caldron.

## choya
choya, n. — A var. of chay.

## choza
choza, п., hut, hovel, cabin. — Sp., fr. khoss,
vulgar pronunciation of Arab, khuss, 'hut,
hovel'.

## chrematistic
chrematistic, adj., pertaining to the acquisition
of wealth. — Gk. χρηματιστικός, 'pertaining to
money making', fr. χρηματίζεσ&αι, 'to transact
business', fr. χρήμα, 'a thing that one needs',
in pi. χρήματα, 'goods, money', fr. χρή, 'it is
necessary', whence also χρήσ&αι, 'to make use
of, χρήσις, 'use, employment'. See chrestomathy
and cp. words there referred to.

## chrematistics
chrematistics, п., the science of wealth. — Gk.
χρηματιστική (scil. τέχνη), 'the art of money
making', fem. of χρηματιστικός, 'pertaining to
money making*. See prec. word.

## chrestomathy
chrestomathy, п., a collection of literary passages,
esp. from a foreign language. — F. chrestoma-
thie, fr. Gk. χρηστομάθεια, 'desire of learning;
book containing select passages', lit. 'useful
learning', fr. χρηστός, 'useful' (prop, verbal adj.
of χρήσθαι, 'to make use of), and the base of
μανθάνειν, 'to learn'. See chrematistic and
mathematics and cp. the second element in
catachresis, polychrestic.
Derivatives: chrestomath-ic, adj., chrestomath-
ics, n. pi.

## chrism
chrism, п., holy oil. — ME. crisme, fr. OE. cris-
ma, fr. Eccles. L. chrisma, fr. Gk. χρίσμα, 'an
unguent', fr. χρίειν, 'to anoint', which is of
uncertain origin. It possibly derives fr. I.-E.
*ghrei-, *ghri-, whence also Lith. grieju, grieti,
'to skim the cream off. I.-E. *ghrei-, *ghri- are
enlargements of base "gher-, 'to rub'. See grind
and cp. chondro-. Cp. also rusma, which is a
doublet of chrism. Cp. also Christ. Cp. also
cream.
Derivative: chrism-al, adj.

## chrism
chrism, tr. v., to anoint with chrism. — OF. chres-
mer, fr. Eccles. L. chrismare, fr. chrisma. See
chrism, n.

## chrisom
chrisom, n. — A var. of chrism.

## Christ
Christ, n. — L. Christus, fr. Gk. χριστός,
'anointed', translation of Heb. mashf'h; verbal adj.
of χρίειν, 'to anoint'. See chrism.

## Christabel
Christabel, fem. PN. — Prob. a compound of
Christ and Belle. Cp. elaribel.

## Christadelphian
Christadelphian, п., one of a religious sect
founded in the U.S.A. by John Thomas (1805-71)
about 1850. — Compounded of Christ and Gk.
αδελφός, 'brother'. See adelpho- and -ian.

## Christ-cross
Christ-cross, n. — See criss-cross.

## christen
christen, tr. v. — ME. cristnen, cristen, fr. OE.
cristnian, 'to baptize', lit. 'to make Christian',
fr. cristen, 'Christian', fr. Eccles. L. christianus.
See Christian.
Derivatives: chrislen-er, п., christen-ing, n.

## Christendom
Christendom, n. — OE. cristendom, formed fr.
cristen, 'Christian', with suff. -dom. See
christen and -dom.

## Christian
Christian, n. and adj. — Eccles. L. christianus, fr.
Eccles. Gk. χριστιανός. See Christ and -ian.

## Christian
Christian, masc. PN. — Fr. prec. word.

## Christianity
Christianity, n. — OF. chrestienle (F. chrilientg),
'Christendom', fr. Eccles. L·. christianitdtem, ace.
of christiSnitds, fr. christianus. See Christian
and -ity.

## christianize
christianize, tr. v. — Eccles. L. christianizare,
fr. Eccles. Gk. χρΐστιίνίζειν, fr. χριστιανός.
See Christian and -ize.
Derivatives: christianiz-ation, п.,
christionizer, n.

## Christinas
Christinas, n. — ME. cristesmesse, fr. Late OE.
Cristes msBsse. See Christ and Mass.

## Christology
Christology, n. — Compounded of Christ and
Gk. -λογία, fr. -λόγος, 'one who speaks (in a
certain manner); one who deals (with a certain
topic)'. See -logy.
Derivatives: Christolog-ical, adj., Chrislolog-
ist, n.

## Christopher
Christopher, masc. PN. — Eccles. L. Christo-
phorus, fr. Eccles. Gk. Χριστόφορος, lit. 'bearing
Christ'. See Christ and -phore.

## -chroia
-chroia, combining form meaning 'discoloration'.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:162 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: 135 | CHUB -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:162 COLUMN:1 -->
as in cacochroia. — Fr. Gk. χροιά, 'color', which
is rel. to χρώμα, 'color'. See chrome and cp. the
second element in dischroa, Xanthochroi.

## -chroic
-chroic, combining form meaning 'colored', as in
erythrochroic. — Formed with suff. -ic fr. Gk.
χροιά, 'color'. See -chroia.

## chroma
chroma, п., the quality or intensity of a color. —
Gk. χρώμα, 'color'. See chrome.

## chromaffin
chromaffin, adj., having affinity for chromium
salts. — A hybrid coined fr. Gk. χρώμα, 'color',
and L. affinis, 'related'. See chrome and affinity
and cp. paraffin.

## chromatic
chromatic, adj., 1) pertaining to color; 2)progres-
sing by halftones (mus.) — L. chromaticus, fr.
Gk. χρωματικός, 'relating to color', fr. χρώμα,
gen. χρώματος, 'color'. See chrome and -atic and
cp. achromatic, dichromatic, trichromatic, ortho-
chromatic.
Derivatives: chromatic, п., chromatic-al-ly, adv.,
chromatics (q.v.)

## chromatics
chromatics, п., the science of color. — See prec.
word and -ics.

## chromatin
chromatin, п., protoplasm occurring in the nuclei
of cells {biol.) — Coined by the German
anatomist Walther Flemming (1843-1905) in 1879
fr. Gk. χρώμα, gen. χρώματος, 'color'. See
chrome and chem. suff. -in.

## chromatism
chromatism, п., abnormal coloration. — Gk.
χρωματισμός, 'a coloring', fr. χρωματίζειν, 'to
color', from χρώμα, gen. χρώματος. See chrome
and -ism and cp. chromism.

## chromato-
chromato-, before a vowel chromat-, combining
form denoting color or chromatin. — Gk. χρω-
ματο-, χρωματ-, fr. χρώμα, gen. χρώματος,
'color'. See chrome.

## chromatophore
chromatophore, п., a pigment cell. —
Compounded of chromato- and -phore.

## chromatoscope
chromatoscope, п., an instrument for combining
light rays of different colors into one compound
color. — Compounded of chromato- and Gk.
-σκόπιον, fr. σκοπεΐν, 'to look at, examine'. See
-scope.

## chrome
chrome, п., ι) chromium; 2) chrome steel. — F.,
coined by the French chemist Nicolas-Louis
Vauquelin (1763-1829) in 1797 fr. Gk. χρώμα,
gen. χρώματος, 'surface of the body, skin, color
of the skin, color', which is rel. to χροιά, of
s.m., χρως, gen. χρωτός, of s.m., χρώζειν, 'to
touch the surface of a body, to tinge, to color',
fr. I.-E. base *ghro~u-, *ghrd-, 'to rub, smear,
tinge', which is rel. to base *gher-, 'to rub',
whence Gk. χρίειν, 'to rub, anoint', χρίσμα,
'an unguent'. See chrism and cp. -chroia, chroma,
chromatic, and the second element in helio-
chrome, homochromous, metachromatism,
metachrosis, monochrolc, monochrome, parachroma.
Derivative: chrome, tr. and intr. v.

## chromic
chromic, adj., pertaining to chromium. — Formed
fr. chromium with suff. -ic
Derivative: chromioize, tr. v.

## chromism
chromism, п., abnormal coloration. —
Irregularly formed fr. Gk. χρώμα, 'color', with suff. -ism.
The correct form is chromatism (q.v.)

## chromite
chromite, п., oxide of iron and chromium,
FeCr204 (mineral.) — Formed fr. chromium
with subst. suff. -ite.
Derivative: chromit-ite, n.

## chromium
chromium, п., name of a metallic element (chem.)
— ModL., coined by the French chemist Count
Antoine-Francois de Fourcroy (1755-1809) and
the French mineralogist Reni-Just Haiiy (1743-
1822) fr.Gk. χρώμα, 'color; see chrome and -ium.
The element was so called by them because of
its colored compounds.
Derivatives: chrom-ic, adj., chromite, n. (q.v.)

## chromo-
chromo-, before a vowel chrom-, combining form
denoting color or pigment. — Fr. Gk. χρώμα,
'color'. See chromato-.

## chromogen
chromogen, п., the coloring matter of a plant. —
Compounded of chromo- and -gen.

## chromolithograph
chromolithograph, п., colored picture printed
from stones. — Compounded of chromo- and
lltograph.
chromolithograph}', п., lithographing in colors. —
See prec. word and -y (representing Gk. -ία).
Derivative: chromolitho-graph-ic, adj.

## chromophyll
chromophyll, п., pigment occurring in leaves
(biochem.) — Compounded of chromo- and Gk.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:162 COLUMN:2 -->
φύλλον, 'leaf. See phyllo-.

## chromosome
chromosome, п., a minute body occurring in
definite number in the cells of a given animal
species (biol.) — Coined by the German
anatomist Wilhelm von Waldeyer-Hartz (1836-
1921) in 1888 fr. Gk. χρώμα, 'color', and σώμα,
'body'. See chromo- and -some, combining form
denoting the body.

## chromosphere
chromosphere, п., envelope of gas around the sun
(astron.) — Compounded of chromo- and sphere.
Derivative: chromospher-ic, adj.

## chromotype
chromotype, п., a photograph in colors. —
Compounded of chromo- and type.

## chromotypography
chromotypography, п., printing in colors. —
Compounded of chromo- and typography.

## chromotypy
chromotypy, п., the same as chromotypography.
— See chromotype and -y (representing Gk. -IS).

## chromous
chromous, adj., pertaining to chromium (chem.)
— See chromium and -ous.

## chron-
chron-, form of chrono- before a vowel.

## chronaxy
chronaxy, chronaxie, п., the shortest time
required to cause the excitation of a nerve cell by
an electric current (physiol.) — F. chronaxie,
coined by the French physiologist Louis La-
picque (1866-1952) in 1909 fr. Gk. χρόνος,
'time', and αξία, 'worth, value', which is re!, to
άξιος, 'worthy'. See chrono- and axiom.

## chronic
chronic, adj., 1) lasting a long time; 2) habitual.
— F. chronique, fr. L. chronicus, fr. Gk.
χρονικός, 'pertaining to time', fr. χρόνος, 'time',
which prob. stands for *ghr-on-os and derives
fr. I.-E. base *gher-, 'to seize, take, hold, close,
envelop', whence also Gk. χειρ, 'hand'; see
chiro-. Time is regarded as 'that which embraces
all things'. See Hofmann, EWG., p. 424 s.v.
χρόνος. Ср. chronicle, crony, and the second
element in isochronous, anachronism, metachro-
nism, parachronism.
Derivatives: chronic-al-ly, adv., chronic-i-ty, п.,
chronicle (q.v.), chron-ist, n.

## chronicle
chronicle, n. — ME. cronicle, fr. cronique, cro-
nike, fr. OF. cronique (F. chronique), fr. L.
chronica, neut. pi. mistaken for a fern, sing., fr. Gk.
τά χρονικά, neut. pi. of χρονικός, 'pertaining
to time', fr. χρόνος, 4ime*. See prec. word.
Derivative: chronicl-er, n.

## chrono-
chrono-, before a vowel chron-, combining form
meaning 'time'. — Gk. χρόνο-, χρον-, fr. χρόνος,
'time'. See chronic

## chronogram
chronogram, п., inscription in which certain
letters, usually made conspicuous, record a date
expressed in Roman numerals. — Compounded
of chrono- and Gk. γράμμα, 'that which is
written'. See -gram.
Derivatives: chronogramm-atic, chronogramm-
atic-al, adjs., chronogramm-alic-al-ly, adv.

## chronograph
chronograph, п., an instrument for measuring
and recording minute intervals of time. —
Compounded of chrono- and Gk. -γράφος, fr. γρά-
φειν, 'to write'. See -graph.

## chronology
chronology, п., the science of measuring time by
periods. — F. chronologic See chrono- and
-logy-
Derivatives: chronolog-ic, chronolog-ical, adjs.,
chronolog-ical-ly, adv., chronolog-ist, п., chro-
nolog-ize, tr. v.

## chronometer
chronometer, п., an instrument for measuring
time. — Compounded of chrono- and Gk.
μέτρον, 'measure'. See -meter.
Derivatives: chronometr-ic, chonometr-ic-al,
adjs., chronometr-ic-al-ly, adv., chronometr-y, n.

## chronopher
chronopher, п., an instrument used to broadcast
time signals by electricity. — Compounded of
Gk. χρόνος, 'time', and the stem of φέρειν, 'to
bear, carry'. See chrono- and bear, 'to carry'.

## chronoscope
chronoscope, п., an instrument for measuring
minute intervals of time. — Compounded of
chrono- and Gk. -σκόπιον, fr. σκοπεΐν, 'to look
at, examine'. See -«cope.
Derivatives: chronoscop-y, п., chronoscop-ic,
adj., chronoscop-ic-al-ly, adv.

## -chroous
-chroous, combining form meaning 'having (such
and such) a color'. — Gk. -χροος, fr. χρως,
gen. χρωτός, 'color', rel. to χροιά, 'color'. See
-chroia and -ous.

## chrys-
chrys-, form of chryso- before a vowel.

## chrysalid
chrysalid, п., a chrysalis. — See chrysalis.

## chrysalid
chrysalid, п., pertaining to a chrysalis. — See

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:162 COLUMN:3 -->
next word.

## chrysalis
chrysalis, п., the pupa of butterflies and other
insects. —-L. chrysallis, fr. Gk. χρΰσαλλίς, gen.
-18ος, 'the gold-colored pupa of the butterfly',
fr. χρυσός, 'gold', fr. Hebrew-Phoenician haratz,
'gold', which is rel. to Ugar. hrs, Akkad. hurasu,
'gold', lit. 4he yellow metal'; cp. Aram.-Syr.
hard', 'yellow'. Cp. also Mitanni hiaruka, 'gold',
which is a Sem. loan word. Heb.-Phoen. haratz,
'gold', found its way into Mycenaean Greek in
the 15th century. See Michael Ventris and John
Chadwick, Documents in Mycenaean Greek
(Cambridge University Press), Index, s.v.
Semitic Loanwords. — Cp. the words chiton,
cumin, sesam.

## Chrysanthemum
Chrysanthemum, n. (hot.), a genus of herbs of
the thistle family; (not cap.) any plant of this
genus. — L. chrysanthemum, fr. Gk. χρϋσάνθε-
μον, 'goldflower', the corn marigold', which is
compounded of χρυσός, 'gold', and άνθεμον,
'flower', fr. δν&ος, 'flower'. See chrysalis and
anther.

## chryselephantine
chryselephantine, adj., overlaid wilh gold and
ivory. — Gk. χρυσελεφάντινος, compounded of
χρυσός, 'gold', and έλεφάντινος, 'made of ivory',
fr. έλέφάς, gen. έλέφαντος, .'elephant, ivory'.
See chrysalis, elephant and -ine (representing
Gk. -ΐνος).

## Chrysemys
Chrysemys, п., a genus of American turtles (zool.)
— ModL., compounded of chrys- and Gk. έμύς,
'fresh water turtle'. See Emys.

## chryso-
chryso-, before a vowel chrys-, combining form
meaning 'gold, golden, golden yellow'. — Gk.
χρϋσο-, χρϋσ-, fr. χρυσός, 'gold'. See chrysalis.

## chrysoberyl
chrysoberyl, п., a semi-precious stone (mineral.)
— L. chrysoberyllus, fr. Gk. χρϋσοβήρυλλος,
which is compounded of χρυσός, 'gold', and
βήρυλλος, 'beryl'. See chrysalis and beryL

## Chrysochloris
Chrysochloris, п., a genus of moles (zool.) —
ModL., lit. 'golden yeuow', compounded of Gk.
χρυσός, 'gold', and χλωρός, 'greenish yellow'.
See chrysalis and chlorine.

## chrysolite
chrysolite, п., a magnesium iron silicate. — ME.
crisolite (F. chrysolithe), fr. L. chrysolithus, fr.
Gk. χρϋσόλιθος, which is compounded of
χρυσός, 'gold', and λίθος, 'stone'. See chrysalis
and -lite.
Derivative: chrysolit-ic, adj.

## chrysoprase
chrysoprase, п., an apple-green variety of
chalcedony (mineral.) — Gk. χρΰσόπρασος,
compounded of χρυσός, 'gold', and πράσον, 'leek'.
See chryso- and prase.

## Chrysopsis
Chrysopsis, п., a genus of plants of the thistle
family, the golden aster (bot.) — ModL.,
compounded of Gk. χρυσός, 'gold', and όψις, 'sight,
view' (see chrysalis and -opsis); so called from
its golden blossoms.

## Cnrysothamnus
Cnrysothamnus, п., a genus of plants of the
thistle family (bot.) — ModL., compounded of
Gk. χρυσός, 'gold' and θάμνος, 'bush, shrub'.
For the first element see chrysalis. The second
element is related to θαμέες, 'crowded', θαμά,
'often', orig. 'thickly', and stands in gradational
relationship to θημών, 'heap', from the stem of
τίθημι, Ί put, place', whence also θέμα,
'anything laid down, deposit', θέσις, 'a placing,
setting'. See theme and cp. words there
referred to.

## chthonian
chthonian, adj., pertaining to the gods of the
underworld (Greek mythol.) — Formed with
suff. -an fr. Gk. χθόνιος, 'of the earth', fr. χθων,
gen. χθονός, 'earth', which stands for *χθωμ and
is cogn. with OI. ksah, ace. ksam, 'earth', fr.
I.-E. *ghdem-, *ghiom-, 'earth'. Cp. Tech. A
tkam (В кап), 'earth, place', Hitt. tegan, gen.
taknas, 'earth', which derive from the above
base through metathesis. Cp. also Olr. clft, gen.
don, 'place' (for *d6n, fr. *dom, corresponding
to Gk. χθων), duine, 'man'. From *ghom-,
"ghem-, simplified forms of the above base,
derive Gk. χαμαί, 'on the ground', L. humus,
'earth', Lith. zeme, Lett, zeme, OPruss. same,
semme, OSlav. zemlja, 'earth'. See humus and
cp. words there referred to. Cp. also the second
element in autochthon. Cp. also zemstvo, the
first element in chameleon, camomile,duniwassal,
zemiadar, and the second element in bridegroom.

## chub
chub, п., a fresh water fish, the chevin. — ME.
