Kipling (1865-1936).

## James
James, masc. PN. — Late L. Jacdmus, altered
fr. Jacobus. See Jacob and cp. jimmy,

## jamesonite
jamesonite, п., a lead antimony sulfide {mineral.)
— Named after Professor Robert Jameson of
Edinburgh (1774-1854), who analyzed it. For
the ending see subst. suff. -ite.

## jampan
jampan, also jompon, п., a kind of sedan {India).
— Bengali jhSpan, fr. Hind, japan, jhappan, fr.
jap, 'a cover'.

## Jane
Jane, fem. PN. — F. Jeanne, fr. OF.· Jehane, fr.
ML. Johanna, Joanna. See Joan and cp. Jean,
fem. PN. Cp. also demijohn, jenny.

## Jane
Jane, п., a small Genoese coin. — OF. Jane, fr.
ML. Janua, 'Genoa'. Cp. L. Genua, whence It.
Geneva, F. Genes.

## Janet
Janet, fem. PN. — A dimin. of Jane (q.v.)

## jangada
jangada, п., a kind of catamaran. — Port., fr.
Malayalam сапЩат, fr. OI. samghafah, 'a
joining together of timber, union'.

## jangar
jangar, п., a raft. — Port, jangada. See prec. word.

## jangle
jangle, intr. and tr. v. — ME. janglen, 'to chatter,
quarrel', fr. OF. jangler, 'to chatter', which is
of Teut. origin. Cp. MDu. jangelen, Du. jen-
gelen, 'to whine', dial. G. jangeln, 'to speak in
a whining manner','which are prob. imitative.
Cp. jingle.
Derivatives: jangl-er, п., jangl-ing, n.

## jangle
jangle, n. — ME., fr. OF. jangle, fr. jangler. See
jangle, v.

## Janissary
Janissary, n. — See Janizary..

## janitor
janitor, п., doorkeeper, porter. — L., formed
with suff. -tor fr. jdnus, 'a covered passage,
arcade', which is of uncertain origin. It is perh.
cogn. with OI. ydnah (masc), 'path', (neut.),
'a going', ydti, Avestic yaiti, 'goes, travels',
Avestic yah-, 'crisis, decision', Toch. A yd, 'he
went', Hitt. Pa-, 'to walk, go', Lith. joju, joti,
Lett, jaju, jot, 'to ride', OSlav. jadg, *jati
(whence jachati), 'to travel'. The underlying base
*yd- represents an enlargement of base *ei-,
'to go', for which see itinerate. Cp. January,
Janus. Cp. also jadoo, jaun and the second
element in Rathayatra.
Derivatives: the nouns janitor-ess, janitr~ess,
janitr-ix (which all mean 'female janitor'),and
the adj. janiior-ial.

## Janizary
Janizary, also Janissary, n. — Fr. janissaire, it.
It. giannizzero, fr. Turk, yeni-cheri, lit. 'new
troops', name of the troops formed in 1362 from
slaves and prisoners of war, fr. yehi, 'new', and
cheri, 'troops'.

## jaanock
jaanock, adj., genuine, candid, frank (dial) —
Of uncertain origin.

## Jansenism
Jansenism, п., the doctrine of Cornells Jansen,
bishop of Ypres (1585-1638). For the ending
see suff. -Ism.

## Jansenist
Jansenist, п., an adherent of Jansenism. — See
prec. word and -ist.
Derivative: jansenist-ic, adj.

## Janthlna
Janthlna, h., a genus of pelagic snails (zool.) —
ModL., fr. L. ianthinus, 'violet blue', fr. Gk.
ίάνθινος, which is compounded of iov, 'violet',
and άνθος, 'flower'. See iolite, anther and -ine
(representing Cik. -ίνος).

## January
January, n. — L. Jdnudrius (mensis), 'the month
dedicated to Jdnus. See Janus and -ary.

## Janus
Janus, п., ancient Italian god of doors and gates,
entrances and beginnings; represented with two
faces. — L. Janus, personification of jdnus,
'arched passage, arcade', whence janua, 'door'.
See janitor and cp. January.

## Jap
Jap, adj. and n. — Colloquial abbreviation for
Japanese.

## Japan
Japan, n."— Chinese Jih-pun (corresponding to
Jap. Ni-pon), 'sunrise', formed fr. jih (resp. Jap.
ni), 'sun', and pun (resp. Jap. pon), 'origin'.

## japan
japan, п., a hard kind of varnish. — Fr. prec.
word; so called because this varnish was orig.
used in Japan.
Derivative: japan, tr. v., to lacquer with japan.

## Japanese
Japanese, adj. and n. — Formed fr. Japan with
suff. -ese.

## Japanesque
Japanesque, adj., in the Japanese style. — A
hybrid formed fr. Japan with suff. -esque.

## jape
jape, intr. v., to joke, jest. — Prob. a blend of OF.
gaber, 'to mock',, and OF. japer (F. japper), 'to
yelp'.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:419 COLUMN:2 -->
Derivatives: jape, n.,jap-er, n.,jap-ery, n.

## Japheth
Japheth, П., the youngest of the three sons of
Noah (Bible). — L Japheth, fr. Gk. Ίαφέ», fr.
Heb. Yepheth, lit. 'enlargement' (see Gen.
9:27), fr. Hiph'il (= causative) form of stem
p-t-h (prop, p-t-y), 'to be wide, spacious', and
rel. to Aram.-Syr. p'tha, p*thi, 'was wide,
spacious', Bibl.-Aram. p*thdy, Aram, puthya,
Syr. p'thdyd, 'width'. Cp. Iapetus.
Derivatives: Japhet-ic, adj. and п., Japhet-ide,
adj. and п., Japheth-ite, adj. and n.

## Japonic
Japonic, adj., Japanese. — Formed with suff. -ic
fr. F. Japan, 'Japan'. See Japan.

## japonica
japonica, п., the camelia; the Japanese quince. —
ModL., lit. 'Japanese', fr. Japonia, 'Japan'. See
Japan.

## jar
jar, intr. and tr. v., to make a harsh, creaking
noise. — Prob. of imitative origin. Cp. ajar,
'out of harmony', nightjar.
Derivatives: jar, п., a harsh noise, jarr-ing, adj.,
jarr-ing-ly, adv.

## jar
jar, п., a vessel of earthenware, glass or stone. —
F. jarre, it. OProvenc. jarra, fr. Arab. jdrrah,
'a large earthen vessel' (whence also Sp. jarra.
It. giarra).
Derivative: jar-ful, adj.

## jardiniere
jardiniere, п., an ornamental flower stand. — F.,
prop. fem. of jardinier, 'of the garden', ft.jardin,
'garden' (used as a noun, jardinier means
'gardener'). See garden and cp. Jordan aimond.

## jargon
jargon, п., confused speech. — OF., 'chatter,
warbling', from the same base as E. gargle. This
base means lit. 'to make noise with the throat'.
See gargle, gurgle.
Derivative: jargon-ize, intr. and tr. v.

## jargon
jargon, also jargoon, п., a variety of zircon. —
F., fr. Port, zarcao, fr. Arab, zarqun, 'minium',
ult. fr. Pers. zargun, 'gold-colored', compound of
zar, 'gold' (see arsenic), and gun- 'color', which
is rel. to Avestic gaona-, 'color'. Cp. zircon.

## jargonelle
jargonelle, п., an early variety of pear. — F.,
dimin. of prec. word; so called from its color.

## jarl
jarl, п., a Scandinavian chieftain. — ON. jarl,
'a man of noble birth, chief. See earl.

## jarool
jarool, п., the tree Lagerstroemia reginae. —
Hind, jarul.

## jarosite
jarosite, п., a potassium iron sulfate (mineral.) —
Named after Barranco Jaroso, Almeria, Spain.
For the ending see subst. suff. -ite.

## jarrah
jarrah, п., a eucalypt of Australia (Eucalyptus
marginata). — From Australian native name.

## jarvey
jarvey, п., a cabdriver. — From Jarvey or Jervis,
name of a Dublin driver who lived in the 18th
century.

## jasey
jasey, also jazy, a wig, esp. a wig of worsted. —
Orig. the word meant a wig made of Jersey
yarn, jasey being a corruption of Jersey.

## Jasione
Jasione, п., a genus of plants, the sheep's bit
(bot.) — ModL., fr. Gk. ίόίσιώνη, 'bindweed', fr.
ϊϊσις, 'healing', fr. ϊασθαι, 'to heal'. See iatric
and cp. ist Jason.

## jasmiue
jasmiue, jasmin, n. — F. jasmin, fr. Arab, yasa-
mtn, fr. Pers. yasemin. Cp. jessamine, Gelsemium.

## Jason
Jason, п., son of Aeson and famous leader of the
Argonauts in Greek mythology. — L. Jason, fr.
Gk. Ιάσων, which is prob. rel. to ίάσθαι, 'to
heal'. See iatric and cp. Jasione.

## Jason
Jason, masc. PN. — Gk. Έάσων, Είάσων, Gre-
cized forms of Heb. Y'hdshaa', YeshBa'; see
Joshna. The name Jason was in frequent use
among Hellenistic Jews, and it occurs
occasionally in modern times; it should not be confused
with Jason, the equivalent of the Greek name
'Ιάσων (see Jason, 'leader of the Argonauts'),
with which it is only connected inasmuch as the
latter influenced the Greek transliteration of
Hebrew YeshBa'.

## jasper
jasper, п., an opaque variety of quartz. — ME.
iaspre, fr. OF. jaspe, jaspre, fr. L. iaspis, it. Gk.
ΐαστπς, 'jasper', which is of Sem. origin. Cp.
Heb. yash'phi", Akkad. yashupu, ashpit, 'jasper'.

## Jasper
Jasper, masc. PN. — A name of Persian origin.
Jas-per lit. means 'treasure holder'. The first
element of this compound name is traceable to
Pets.ganj, 'treasure'. See genizah and cp. Caspar.

## Jataka
Jataka, п., a birth story of Gautama Buddha. —
OI. jatakah, 'begotten by; birth', fr. jatdh,
'born; son', which is cogn. with L.gndtus, 'born',

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:419 COLUMN:3 -->
Gk. -γνητος (in compounds), 'born*, fr. I.-E.
base gen-, 'to beget, bear, bring forth, produce',
whence also L. gignere, 'to beget, bear, bring
forth', genus, 'birth, descent, origin'. See genus
and cp. words there referred to.

## Jatropha
Jatropha, п., a genus of plants of the spurge
family (bot.) — ModL., inaccurately formed by
the Swedish botanist Carolus Linnaeus (1717-
83) fr. Gk. ιατρός, 'healer, physician' (see iatric),
and τροφή, 'food, nutrition' (see trophic).

## jaun
jaun, п., a small palankin. — Bengali jan, ydn,
ft. OI. ydnah (masc), 'path', (neut.), 'a goinf'.
See janitor and cp. the second element in
Rathayatra.

## jaundice
jaundice, n. — Formed with intrusive d fr. OF.
jaunice, jaunisse (F. jaunisse), fr. jaune, 'yellow',
fr. L. galbinus, 'greenish yellow', which is rel
to galbanus, 'yellow', prop, 'having the color of
galbanum', fr. galbanum, name of a yellowish
gum resin. See galbanum and suff. -ice
(representing L. -itia). For the so-called inorganic d
in jaundice ср.. gender, sound, 'noise', thunder.
Derivative: jaundice, tr. v.

## jaunt
jaunt, intr. v., to make a short pleasure journey;
п., a short pleasure journey. — Of uncertain
origin.

## jaunty
jaunty, adj., careless, sprightly. — Earlier jantee,
janty, it. F. gentil. See gentle.
Derivatives: jaunti-ly, adv., jaunti-ness, n.

## jaup
jaup, intr. and tr. v., to splash (Scot, and N. of
England). — Of imitative origin.

## javali
javali, п., the collared peccary. — Amer. Sp.
javali,it. Sp.jabali, 'wild boar', fr. Arab, jabalf,
'pertaining to the mountains, inhabitant of
mountains', adj., formed fr. jobat, 'mountain',
which is rel. to Heb. g'bhul, 'frontier,
boundary', orig. 'earth wall or mountain serving as
boundary'. Cp. Bible and the first element in
Gibraltar.

## javelin
javelin, п., a light spear. — F. javeline, of Gaul,
origin. Cp. Olr. gabul, W. gafl, 'fork', W. gaf-
lach, 'feathered spear', and see gable.
Derivative: javelin, it. v.

## jaw
jaw, n. — ME. jawe, jowe, fr. OF. (= F.) joue,
'cheek, jaw', fr. VL. "gauta, which is prob. a
contraction of *gavita, it. "gabita, it. pre-Latin
*gaba, 'gorge, jaw, goiter', whence also F. gaver,
'to cram, gorge', OProvenc. gava, 'crop, maw';
prob. influenced in form by jowl. Cp. jabot.
Derivative: jaw, intr. v., to talk (slang); tr. v.,
to scold (tr. v.)

## jawab
jawab, п., an answer; a building corresponding
to, or imitating, another. — Hind, jawab, it.
Arab, jawab, 'answer', which is rel. to ajdba,
jawaba, 'he answered'.

## jay
jay, n. — ME., fr. OF. iay, gay (F. geai), fr. Late
L. gaius, a word of imitative origin. The word
gaius arose from the attempt of rendering the
natural sound gau, gai made by this bird, but
was assimilated in form to the Latin PN. Gaius.
Cp. L. titus, 'blue rock', lucius, 'pike' (see luce),
which come from Latin PN's. Cp. also the
French bird names martinet, sansonnet, pierrot,
which all derive from PN's. Cp. also E. martin,
a kind of swallow.

## jazerant
jazerant, п., armor made of small overlapping
metal plates. — ME. jesseraunt, it. OF. jaseran,
jaserenc, jazerenc, it. Sp. jacerina, fr. Arab.
Jazd'ir, 'Algerian', fr. al-Jaza'ir, 'Algiers', lit.
'(the) islands', pi. of jaztra", 'island'.

## jazz
jazz, п., ι) a kind of syncopated music; 2) dance
to this music. — An Amer. Negro word of W.
African origin. Derivatives: jazz, tr. and intr.
v., jdzz-er, п., jazz-y, adj.

## jealous
jealous, adj. — ME. jalous, gelus, fr. OF. gelos
(F. jaloux), it. ML. zetosus, fr. Late L. zelus,
'zeal'. See zeal and -ous and cp. zealous, which
is a doublet of jealous.
Derivatives: jealous-ly, adv., jealous-ness, n-

## jealousy
jealousy, n. — OF. gelosie (F. jalousie), it. gelos,
'jealous'. See prec. word and -y (representing
OF. and F. -ιβ).

## Jean
Jean, masc. PN. — The French equivalent of
John. Cp. jenneting.

## Jean
Jean, fem. PN. — Equivalent of Jane.

## jean
jean, п., a strong cotton fabric — OF. (= F.)
Genes, Genoa, city in Italy. Cp. Jane, 'a Genoese
coin'.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:420 COLUMN:1 -->

## jeans
jeans, η. pi., trousers. — Fr. jean.

## jecoral
jecoral, adj., pertaining to the liver (ana!.) —
Formed with adj. suff. -al fr. L. jecur, gen. je-
coris, 'liver', which is cogn. with OI. yakft, Gk.
ήπαρ, 'liver'. See hepatic.

## jeep
jeep, п., a small rugged automobile. — Prob.
contraction of gee pee, i.e. GP, the initials of
General Purpose (Car).

## jeer
jeer, intr. and tr. v., to mock. — Of uncertain
origin. Derivative: jeer, п., derision.

## jeers
jeers, n. pi., a combination of tackles for hoisting
and lowering the lower yards (naut.) — Of
unknown origin.

## JefTersonia
JefTersonia, п., a genus of plants, the twinleaf
(bot.) — ModL., named after Thomas Jefferson
(1743-1826), third· president of the United
States of America. For the ending see suff. -ia.

## jefTersonite
jefTersonite, п., a variety of pyroxene (mineral.)
— Named after Thomas Jefferson. See prec.
word and subst. suff. -ite.

## jehad
jehad, n. — See jihad.

## Jehovah
Jehovah, п., an erroneous transliteration of the
Tetragrammaton, first used in 1518 by Peter
Gallatin, confessor of Pope Leo X; formed
through the addition of the vowel points of
Adondy, 'my Lord', to the consonants forming
the Tetragrammaton.

## jehu
jehu, п., a fast, skillful driver. — Fr. Jehu, king
of Israel, with reference to I] Kings 9:20. "The
driving is like the driving of Jehu, the son of
Nimshi; for he driveth furiously".

## jejune
jejune, adj., 1) barren; 2) dull, dry. — L. jejunus,
'fasting, hungry; barren, unproductive', of
obscure origin. Cp. next word. Cp. also
dejeuner, dine.
Derivative: jejune~ly, adv., jejune-ness, n.

## jejunum
jejunum, п., the second part of the small intestine
(anal.) — Medical L., fr. L. jejunus, 'fasting'
(see prec. word), translation of Gk. νήστις, a
name given to the second part of the small
intestine by the Greek physician Claudius Galen
(cca 130-cca 200), because he thought it was
always found empty after death.

## jelly
jelly, n. — Fr. earlier gelly, fr. F. gelee, 'frost,
jelly', fr. L. gelata, fern. pp. of gelare, 'to freeze,
stiffen', used as a noun, fr. gelu, 'frost'. See gelid
and cp. gelatin, galantine.
Derivatives: jelly, tr, v.,jelli-ed, adj.

## jemadar
jemadar, п., a native officer in the Indian army,
corresponding to the lieutenant in the English
army. — Hind, jama'dar, lit. 'the holder of a
body of men', fr, Pers. jamd'at, 'a body of
men', and -dar, 'holder, possessor'. The first
element is borrowed fr. Arab. jamdtah, 'a body
of men, troop', fr. jama'a, 'he gathered together'
whence also jum'ah, 'union; week', yaum al-
jum'ati, 'Friday', lit. 'the day of gathering'; cp.
jumma. For the second element see aumildar
and cp. words there referred to. v

## Jemima
Jemima, 1) fern. PN.; 2) in the Bible, one of Job's
daughters. — Heb. Ylmimdh, lit. 'dove'; rel. to
Arab. yamdmah, 'dove'.

## jemmy
jemmy, п., burglar's short crowbar. — Formed
fr. Jimmy, Jemmy, popular variants of James.

## jennet
jennet, п., a small Spanish horse. — F. genet, fr.
Sp. jinele, 'a light horseman', fr. Arab. Zandtah
(in vulgar pronunciation Zenata), name of a
Berber tribe famous for its horsemen.

## jenneting
jenneting, п., a kind of early apple. — Formed
with subst. suff. -ing fr. F. Jeannel, dimin. of
Jean (see Jean, masc. PN.); so called because
supposed to be ripe about St. John's Day,
June 24.

## jenny
jenny, п., a locomotive crane. — Dimin. form
of the name Jane.

## jeopard
jeopard, tr. v., to put in jeopardy. — Back
formation fr. jeopardy.
Derivatives: jeopard-er, п., jeopard-ous, adj.,
jeopard-ous-ly, adv., jeopard-ous-ness, n.

## jeopardy
jeopardy, n„ hazard, danger. — ME. jeparti, ju-
parti, fr. OF. jeu parti, 'split game, even game
or chance', fr. jeu, 'game' (fr. L. jocus, 'jest'),
and parti, pp. of partir, 'to divide' (fr. ~L.partire,
of s.m., fr. pars, gen. partis, 'part'). See joke
and part, v. and n.
Derivatives: jeopard (q.v.), jeopard-ize, tr. v.,
jeopardy, tr. v.

## Jephthah
Jephthah, п., a judge of Israel (Bible). — Gk.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:420 COLUMN:2 -->
Ίεφθάε, fr. Heb. Yiphtdh, lit. 'God opens', im-
perf. of pdthdh, 'he opened', whence pethah.
'opening, entrance, doorway', miphtdh,
'opening', maphta'h, 'key' (lit. Opening instrument'),
rel. to Aram.-Syr. p'thah, Arab, fdtaha, Ethiop.
fataha, 'he opened', Akkad. pitu, patu, 'to
open'.

## jequirity
jequirity, п., ι) the Indian licorice plant; 2) its
seeds (Abrus abrus), used in medicine. — F.
jequirity, fr. Port, jequiriti, which is of uncertain,
possibly Indian, origin.

## jerboa
jerboa, п., a mouselike jumping rodent. —
ModL., fr. Arab. yarbQ'.

## jereed
jereed, Jerid, п., javelin used in Mohammedan
countries. — Arab, jartd, which orig. meant 'a
leafless palmbranch'.

## jeremiad
jeremiad, п., lamentation, tale of woe. — F. jere-
miade, fr. Jeremie, fr. Late L. Jeremias (see
Jeremiah and -ad); so called in allusion to the
Lamentations of Jeremiah.

## Jeremiah
Jeremiah, 1) masc. PN.; 2) the great Hebrew
prophet whose activity extended from 626 to
586 B.C.E.; the Book of Jeremiah. — Late L.
Jeremias, fr. Heb. Yirmlyah, shortened fr.
Yirm'ydhu, which is prob. compounded of
rama", 'he cast, threw', and a shortened form
of the Tetragrammaton, and accordingly
means 'the Lord casts' or 'the Lord founds'.
For rami" = 'he founded', see S. Kraus,
Palestine Exploration Quarterly, 1945, p. 23. Several
scholars explain Yirm*yah in the sense of yarxm-
yah, 'the Lord exalts', or of yarum-yah, 'the
Lord is exalted'. For the second element in the
name Jeremiah see Elijah and cp. words there
referred to.

## Jeremy
Jeremy, п., a form of the name Jeremiah. — F.
Jeremie, fr. Late L. Jeremias. See Jeremiah.

## jerk
jerk, tr. and intr. v., to move suddenly; п., а
sudden movement. — Prob. of imitative
origin.
Derivatives: jerk-y, adj., jerk-i-ly, adv., jerk-
i-ness, n.

## jerk
jerk, tr. v., to dry meat. — Anglicized fr. S. Am.
Sp. charquear, 'to dry meat', fr. Peruv. charqui.
See charqui.

## jerkin
jerkin, п., a jacket. — Of uncertain origin.

## Jeroboam
Jeroboam, name of two kings in Israel (Bible) —
Heb. Yarobh'dm, lit. meaning 'let the people
increase', fr. ydrSbh, 3rd person sing, imperf. of
base r-b-b, 'to become many, to increase', and
'am, 'people'. For the first element see rabbi,
for the second see Amhaarez. See Martin Noth,
Die israelitischen Personennamen im Rahmen
der gemeinsemitischen Namengebung, 206, and
G. Buchanan Gray, Studies in Hebrew Proper
Names, 59.

## Jeroboam
Jeroboam, п., a large wine bottle (slang). — From
prec. word, in allusion to I Kings, 11:28 "a
mighty man in Israel", and 14:16 "who made
Israel to sin"..

## Jerome
Jerome, masc. PN. — F. Jerome, fr. L. Hierd-
nymus, fr. Gk. 'Ιερώνυμος, lit. 'holy name',
compounded of ίερός, 'holy', and δ"νυμα,
dialectal form of 6νομα, 'name'. For the first
element see hiero-, for the second see name and
cp. onomato-.

## Jerry
Jerry, masc. PN. — A popular form of Jeremy.

## jerry
jerry, п., ι) a machine for shearing cloth; 2)
chamber pot. — Fr. prec. word.

## jerry-built
jerry-built, adj., built poorly; flimsy. — The first
element of this word is prob. ■; blend of the
adjective jury, 'temporary' (cp. jury-mast, jury-
rigged), and of the name Jerry.
Derivative: jerry-build-er, n.

## jersey
jersey, п., a kind of knitted or woven garment. —
Named from one of the Channel Islands. Cp.
jasey.

## Jerusalem
Jerusalem, n. — Gk. 'Ιερουσαλήμ, fr. Heb. Yeru-
shdldyim, lit. 'foundation of peace', fr. base of
yarah, 'he threw, cast', and shalom, 'peace'.
Heb. ydrdh in the above sense is rel. to Ethiop.
warawa, 'he threw', ModArab. wdrra, of s.m.
For sense development cp. Akkad. nadu ushshe,
Gk. βάλλεσ&αι άστυ, L. fundamenta jacere, 'to
lay the foundations'. Cp. ShaUm, the ancient
Heb. name of Jerusalem. Cp. also Aram. Y'ru-
sh'Um, Akkad. Ursalimmu (in the Tell El-
Amarna Tablets: Urusalim), Arab. Ortshalam,

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:420 COLUMN:3 -->
Gk. 'Ιεροσόλυμα, 'Jerusalem' (see Hierosoiyma).
For the second element in Heb. Y'rushatayim
see Shalom.
Jerusalem artichoke. — Folk etymological
alteration of It. girasole, 'sun flower'. See girasol.

## Jeshurun
Jeshurun, п., poetic name of Israel. — Heb.
Y'shurun, prop, 'the righteous people',
denominated fr. yashar — yashdr, 'straight, right,
upright', which derives fr. yashar, 'was smooth,
straight, right', whence also yasher, 'straight-
ness, uprightness', meshdr, 'evenness,
uprightness, equity', mishSr, 'uprightness, level place,
plains'; rel. to Aram, meshra, 'level place',
Arab, ydsara, 'was gentle, tractable, easy',
yasar, 'tractable, easy', Akkad. eshiru, 'to be
straight or right,' mesharu, 'justice'; cp. Sharon.
The defective writing of the first и in Y'shurun
(with qubbutz inst. of with shureq) does not
affect its quantity, and is due to the tendency
to avoid the scriptio plena in two successive
syllables.

## jess
jess, п., a short strap fastened round the leg of
a hawk (falconry) — ME. ges, fr. OF. ges, gies,
pi. of get, giet (F. jet), 'a throwing', lit. 'that
which is thrown', fr. L. jactus, pp. of jacere, 'to
throw'. See jet, 'to spirt forth'.
Derivative: jess, tr. v.

## jessamine
jessamine, п., jasmine. — MF. jassemin; a var.
of jasmine (q.v.)

## Jesse
Jesse, 1) masc. PN.; 2) in the Bible, father of
David. — L., fr. Gk. Ίεσσαί, fr. Heb. Yishay,
which is of uncertain etymology.

## Jessica
Jessica, fern. PN. — Late L. Jesca (Gen. 11:29),
fr. Gk. Ίεσχά (Septuagint I.e.), fr. Heb. Yiskdh,
name of a daughter of Haran.

## jest
jest, n. — Lit. 'a deed, exploit', fr. ME. geste,
jeste, fr. OF. geste, 'a deed, exploit', fr. L. gesta,
'deeds, acts', neut. pi. of gestus, pp. of gerere,
'to bear, carry, produce, perform, do', used as a
noun. See gerent and cp. gest, gestation,
gesticulate, gesture, register.
Derivatives: jest, intr. v.,jest-ee, n.,jest-er, п.,
jest-ing, n. and adj., jest-ing-ly, adv.

## Jesuit
Jesuit, n. — ModL. Jesuita, formed fr. Jesus
with suff. -ite.
Derivatives: Jesuit-ess, п., Jesuit-ic, adj., Jesuit-
ic-al-ly, adv., Jesuit-ish, adj., Jesuit-ism, п.,
Jesuit-ist, п., Jesuit-ize, v., Jesuit-ry, n.

## Jesus
Jesus, n. — L. Jesus, fr. Gk. Ίησοΰς, fr. Heb.
Yeshaa', later form of Y'hdshua'. See Joshua.

## jet
jet, п., a hard black mineral. — ME. jete, geet,
fr. OF. jayet (F. jatet, jais), fr. L. gagatem, ace.
of gagates, fr. Gk. γαγάτης (scil. λίθος), 'jet',
lit. 'stone of Gagas (a town and river in Lycia)'.
The exact equivalent of L. gagatem should have
been *jaie. The form jatet is due to change of
suffix.
Derivative: jet, adj., of the color of jet.

## jet
jet, intr. and tr. v., to spirt forth. — F. jeter, 'to
throw', fr. VL. jecldre, fr. L. jactare, 'to throw,
toss, fling, hurl', freq. of jacere, 'to throw, cast',
which is rel. to jacere, 'to lie', orig. 'to cast
oneself down', and cogn. with Gk. ϊημι, ίέναι (for
*yi-yi-mi, *yi-ye-nai), 'to send, throw', Hitt.
ijami, Ί make'. Cp. abject, adjective, adjacent,
amice, 'vestment', aphesis, aphetic, catheter,
circumjacent, conjecture, deject, ejaculate, eject,
enema, ephetae, gist, inject, interject, interjection,
jactitatioa, jess, jetsam, jettison, jetty, joist, jut,
object, paresis, parget, project, reject, subjacent,
subject, superjacent, synesis, traghetto, trajectory.
Derivative: jet, п., stream, spirt.

## Jethro
Jethro, 1) masc. PN.; 2) in the Bible, father of Zip-
porah, Moses' wife. — Heb. Yithra, collateral
form of Yether, lit. 'abundance', from basey-r-r,
'to be left over, remain', whence also yothir,
'remainder, excess' (prop, partic. Qal), hothlr
(Hiph'il), 'he left over', yether, 'cord' (lit. 'that
which hangs over'), Aram.-Syr. yathrd, Arab.
wdtar, Ethiop. weter, 'bowstring', Heb. yithron,
'advantage, profit', Aram, yuthrdna, 'gain'. Cp.
Martin Noth, Die israelitischen Personennamen
im Rahmen der gemeinsemitischen
Namengebung, 193.

## jetsam
jetsam, п., goods thrown overboard to lighten a
ship. — AF. getteson, 'jetsam', corresponding
to OF. getaison, 'a throwing', fr. L. jactdtionem,
ace. of jactdtto, of s.m., it.jactdtus, pp. oijac-

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:421 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: JETTISON | 394 -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:421 COLUMN:1 -->
tare, freq. oijacere, 'to throw'. See jet, 'to sput
forth', and cp. next word. The ending of jetsam
was influenced by the Scand. suff. -sam. Cp.
flotsam.

## jettison
jettison, п., the act of throwing goods overboard
to lighten a ship. — AF. getteson. See prec.
word.

## jetton
jetton, п., a counter used in gambling. — F.jeton,
'mark, counter', fr. jeter, 'to throw'. See jet, 'to
spirt forth'.

## jetty
jetty, п., ι) projecting part of a building; 2) a
landing pier. — ME. jettey, fr. OF. getee, jetee,
prop. fem. pp. of geter, jeter (F. jeter), 'to
throw'. See jet, 'to spirt forth', and -y
(representing OF. -e, -ее).
Derivative: jetty, tr. v.

## jeii
jeii, п., play, game. — F., fr. L. jocus, 'jest, joke'.
See joke.

## Jew
Jew, n. — ME. Gui, Jui, Jewe, fr. OF. giu, juiu
(F. juif), fr. L. Judaeus, fr. Gk. 'Ιουδαίος, fr.
Aram. Ylhudhay(S); fr. Heb. Y'hudht, 'Jew'.
See Judaic and cp. words there referred to.
Derivatives: Jew-ess, п., Jew-ish, adj., Jewry
(q.v.)

## jewei
jewei, n. — ME. jowel, juel, fr. OF. joiel, joel,
jouel, juel (F'. joyau), fr. VL. *jocalis, 'that which
causes joy', fr. L. jocus, 'joy'. See joke and
cp. jen.
Derivatives: jewel, tr. v., jeweler (q.v.), jewelry
(q.v.), jewel(Iying, n.

## jeweier
jeweier, jeweller, n. — ME. jueler, joweler, fr.
KF.jueler, corresponding to OF. juelier, ir.juel.
See prec. word and agential suff. -er and cp.
F. joaittier.

## jewelry
jewelry, jewellery, ft. — ME. juelrie, jowelrie, fr.
OF. juelerie, fr. juelier. See prec. word and -ry,
resp. -ery, and cp. F. joaillerie.

## Jewry
Jewry, n. — OF. juierie (F. juiverie), fr. juiu,
'Jew'. See Jew and -ry.
Jew's harp or jews' harp. — Cp. G. Judenharfe,
which is the exact equivalent of the English word.
Jew's harp is prob. a folk-etymological alteration
of the original name, which is unknown to us.

## jezail
jezail, juzail, п., a big Afghan rifle. — Pers. ja-
zail, prob. fr. Arab, jazd'il, broken plural of
jaztl, 'big', used as a noun.

## Jezebel
Jezebel, п., daughter of Ethbaal, king of Tyre,
and wife of Ahab, king of Israel (Bible); used
to denote a vicious woman. — Heb. lzebhel, a
name of uncertain origin and meaning.

## jeziah
jeziah, jezia, п., poll tax imposed by
Mohammedan law on unbelievers. — Arab. jizyah, fr.
Syr. g'zithd, 'poll tax'. See Fraenkel, Die ara-
maischen Fremdworter im Arabischen, p. 283,
and cp. Arthur Jeffery, -Ph. D., The Foreign
Vocabulary of the Qur'an, pp. 101-102.

## jhow
jhow, jow, п., a tamarisk used for rough basket
making (India). — Hind, jhaii, fr. OI. jhavuh,
jhavukah, 'Tamarix Indica', which is of
uncertain origin.

## jib
jib, intr. v., to swing round (said of a sail, boom,
etc.) — Prob. a variant of jibe, 'to swing round'.

## jib
jib, п., a triangular sail. — Prob. fr. prec. word
and orig. meaning 'that which swings from
side to side'.

## jib
jib, intr. v., to move restively sideways or
backward. — Prob. from figurative use of jib, 'to
swing round'.
Derivative: jiba-er, n.

## jib
jib, п., projecting arm of a crane. — Prob.
abbreviation of gibbet.

## jibe
jibe, also gybe, intr. v., to swing round; tr. v., to
cause to swing round (said of a fore-and-aft
sail or its boom). — Obsol. Du. gijben, Du.
gijpen, rel. to Dan. gibbe, Swed. gippa. Cp. also
jib, 'to swing round'.

## jibe
jibe, intr. v., to sneer. — See gibe.

## jiffy
jiffy, also jiff, п., a moment; an instant (colloq.)
— Of unknown origin.

## jig
jig, intr. and tr. v., to dance. — OF. giguer, 'to
move the shanks, hop, dance', fr. gigue, 'shank;
fiddle',fr. ODu.giga,'stringed instrument, a kind
of violin', which is rel. to ON. gigja, late OHG.
giga, MHG. gige, G. Geige, 'violin', and to
ON. geiga, 'to move across'. Cp. gigolo, gigot,
gigue.
Derivatives .jig, п., lively dance, jigg-er,
п.,jigger, tr. v.Jigg-ish, adj., jiggle (q.v.), jigg-y, adj.,

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:421 COLUMN:2 -->
jigg-i-ness, n.

## jigger
jigger, п., a kind of mite. — A var. of chigger.

## jiggered
jiggered, adj., a word used in oaths for the sake
of euphemism. — Of uncertain origin.

## jiggle
jiggle, intr. and tr. v. — Freq. of jig (q.v.) For the
ending see freq. suff. -le.
Derivative: jiggl-y, adj.

## jihad
jihad, also jehad, п., religious war against
unbelievers. — Arab, jihad, 'contest, war', prop,
inf. oijuhada, 'he waged war', 3rd conjugation
of jahada, 'he applied himself to'.

## Jill
Jill, fem. PN. — A variant of Gill.

## jilt
jilt, п., a woman who casts off a lover after
encouraging him. — Prob. fr. obsol. Gillot, dimin.
of Gill (q.v.)
Derivatives: jilt, tr. v., jilt-ee, п., jilt-er, n.

## Jim Crow
Jim Crow, 1) discrimination against Negroes
(colloq.); 2) a contemptuous name for a Negro
(slang). — From a Negro song with the refrain
'Wheel about and turn about and jump,
Jim Crow'.

## jimmy
jimmy, п., burglar's crowbar. — From a popular
form of the name James.
Derivative: jimmy, tr. v.

## jimp
jimp, adj. (Scot, and dial. Engl.), I) slender;
2) scanty. — Of uncertain origin.
Derivatives: jimp-ly, adv., jimp-ness, n.

## Jimson weed
Jimson weed, a poisonous weed (Datura
stramonium). — For earlier jimson weed, Jimson
weed, refashioned from Jamestown weed, named
after Jamestown in Virginia.

## jingal
jingal, also gingal, п., a musket of India, China,
etc. — Hind, janjal.

## jingle
jingle, intr. and tr. v. — ME. ginglen, of imitative
origin. Cp. jangle.
Derivatives: jingle, п., jingl-er, п., jingl-ing, п.,
jingl-ing, adj., jingl-ing-ly, adv., jingl-y, adj.

## jingo
jingo, п., a chauvinist. — Possibly corruption of
Jatnko, name of the supreme god of the
Basques, from whom the word was brought into
England through the medium of the Basque
soldiers used by Edward I in his Welsh wars.
Derivatives: jingo, adj., jingo-ish, adj., jingo-ism,
п., jingo-ist, п., jingo-ist-ic, adj.

## jinn
jinn, n. — PI. of Jinnee (q.v.)

## jinnee
jinnee, jinni, п., demon, spirit (Mohammedan
mythology). — Arab, jinnt (pi. jinn), 'spirit,
genie'; in English often confused with genie
(q.v.)

## jinriklsha
jinriklsha, jinricksha, п., a two-wheeled vehicle
drawn by a man, used in Japan and China. —
Jap., lit. 'manpower-vehicle', fr.jin, 'man', riki,
'power', and sha, 'vehicle'. The word is usually
shortened to ricksha(w).

## jinx
jinx, п., hoodoo (slang). — See Jynx.

## jirgah
jirgah, п., Afghan council of elders. — Pers. jarga,
'a ring of men'.

## jitney
jitney, п., a five-cent piece, a nickel. — Of
uncertain origin.
jin-jitsu. — See ju-jitsu.

## jiva
jiva, п., life, the individual soul, vital energy
(Hinduism). — OI. jivah, 'living, alive'; cogn.
with L. vivus, OE. cwicu, 'alive', Gk. βίος, 'life'.
See quick and cp. words there referred to.

## jnana
jnana, п., knowledge (Hinduism). — OI. jnanah,
'knowledge', from the stem of jandti, 'he knows',
which is rel. to Avestic zanaiti, of s.m. and cogn.
with Gk. γ^γνώσκείν, OL. gnoscere,LJnoscere,
OE. cnawan, 'to know'. See can, aux. v., and cp.
words there referred to.

## Joab
Joab, 1) masc. PN.; 2) in the Bible, the chief
captain of David's army. — Late L. Joab, fr. Gk.
Ίωάβ, fr. Heb. Yd'dbh, lit. 'the Lord is (his)
father'. For the first element cp. the PN's Joel,
John, Jonathan, Joshua, for the second see
Aboth and cp. words there referred to.

## Joanna
Joanna, fem. PN. — ML. Johanna, Joanna, fem.
form of ML. Johannes, Joannes. See John and
cp. Jean, fem. PN., Johanna.

## job
job, п., piece of work. — Of uncertain origin.
Derivatives: job, intr. v., to do odd jobs, etc;
tr. v., to hire or to let out for hire (a horse or
carriage), jobb-er, п., jobb-ery, п., jobb-ing, adj.

## job
job, tr. v., to stab, to prod. — ME. jobben,
apparently of imitative origin. Cp. jab.

## Job
Job, 1) masc. PN.; 2) in the Bible: a) a man who
endured much suffering with faith and patience;
b) the Book of Job. — Late L. Job, Jobus, it. Gk.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:421 COLUMN:3 -->
Ίώβ, fr. Heb. Iyyibh, which—according to
several scholars—lit. means 'treated as an
enemy, hated, persecuted', fr. ayyabh, 'he was
hostile to', rel. to ebhd", 'enmity'. For the
passive sense of the form of the word cp. yillodh,
'born'. Cp. Niobe. Others explain the name
lyyobh as rel. to Arab, aba, 'he returned', iydb,
'return', awwab, 'repentant'; accordingly Iyyibh
would mean 'the penitent one'. See J.Hastings,
A Dictionary of the Bible, II 660-661. Cp. the
first element in jobbernowl,

## jobbernowl
jobbernowl, п., a foolish person. — A compound
of F. jobard, 'fool', and ME. nol, 'head'. F.
jobard is a derivative of OF. jobe, 'patient fool',
fr. Job, the great sufferer of the Bible whose
afflictions were increased by the reproachful
'consolations' of his friends. See Job. For the
second element see noil.

## Jocasta
Jocasta, п., the wife of Laius and mother of
Oedipus (Greek mythol.) — L„ fr. Gk. Ίοκάστη.

## Jocelin
Jocelin, masc. PN. — A name with many variants
(cp. Joslin, Joselin, Gosling, etc.), fr. OHG.
Gautelen, Gauzelen, fr. Gauta, lit. 'Goth'; see
Goth, The name was introduced into England
by the Normans. See The Oxford Dictionary
of English Christian Names, 2nd ed., pp. 169-
170.

## Joceline
Joceline, fem. PN. — From prec. word.

## Jocelyn
Jocelyn, masc. and fem. PN. — See Jocelin.

## jockey
jockey, n. — Dimin. of Scot. Jock, equivalent to
E. Jack (q.v.)
Derivatives: jockey, tr, and intr. v., jockey-dom,
jockey-ship, a.

## jocko
jocko, п., ι) a chimpanzee; 2) any monkey. —
F., coined by the French naturalist, Count
Georges-Louis Leclerc Buffon (1707-88) from
native West African ncheko.

## jocose
jocose, adj., merry; humorous. — bjoedsus,
'jocose, humorous, facetious', fr. jocus, 'jest, joke'.
See joke and adj. suff. -ose.
Derivatives: jocose-ly, adv., jocose-ness, п.,

## jocos-ity
jocos-ity, n.

## jocular
jocular, adj., joking; humorous. — L. jocularis,
'jocular, facetious', fr. joculus, 'a little jest',
dimin. of jocus, 'jest, joke'. See joke, -ule
and -ar.
Derivatives: jocular-ity, п., jocular-ly, adv.,

## jocular-ness
jocular-ness, n.

## jocund
jocund, adj., cheerful. — ME. jocunde, joconde,
fr. OF. jocond, fr. ~L.jocundus, collateral form of

## jucundus
jucundus, 'pleasant, agreeable, delightful', orig.
'useful', contraction of *juvicondos, fr. juvare,
'to help, aid, assist'. See aid and cp. words there
referred to. For the suff. cp. fecund. L. jocundus
(fr. jucundus) shows the influence of L. jocus,
'jest, joke'.
Derivatives: jocundity (q.v.), jocund-ly, adv.,

## jocund-ness
jocund-ness, n.

## jocundity
jocundity, n. — L. jocunditas, a collateral form
of jucunditas, 'pleasantness', fr. jucundus. See
prec. word and -ity.

## jodhpurs
jodhpurs, n. pi., riding breeches. — Shortened fr.
Jodhpur breeches, fr. Jodhpur, name of a state
in Rajputana (India).

## Joe
Joe, masc. PN. — Dimin. of Joseph.

## Joel
Joel, 1) masc. PN.; 2) a) the second in the order
of the Twelve Prophets; b) the Book of Joel
(Bible). — Late L. Joel, fr. Gk. Ίωήλ, fr. Heb.
Υδ'έΙ, lit. 'the Lord is God'. See Elijah, in which
the same two elements are contained, but in an
inverted order.

## Joe Miller
Joe Miller, 1) a jestbook; 2) a stale joke. —
From Joseph Miller, name of a comedian (1684-
1738), whose name was connected with a jest-
book published in [739.

## Joey
Joey, п., masc. PN. — Dimin. of Joe.

## joey
joey, п., a young kangaroo. — Fr. native
Australian joe.

## jog
jog, tr. v., to push or shake slightly; to nudge;
intr. v., to move slowly. — Of imitative origin.
Cp. shock, 'to collide'.
Derivative:^, n.

## joggle
joggle, tr. and intr. v. — Formed fr. jog with freq.
suff. -le.

## jogee
jogee, n. — A var. of yogi.

## Johanna
Johanna, fem. PN. — See Joanna.

## Johannean
Johannean, adj., Johannine. — Formed fr.
Johannes with suff. -an. Cp. Johannine.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:422 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: 395 | JDVIAL -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:422 COLUMN:1 -->

## Johannes
Johannes, masc. PN. — ML., fr. Gk. 'Ιωάννης.
See John and cp. next word.

## Johannes
Johannes, n„ a Portuguese gold coin. — Modi..,
named after King John V of Portugal. See
Johannes and cp. half joe.

## Johannine
Johannine, adj., pertaining to John, esp. the
apostle John. — Formed with adj. sun", -ine fr.
ML. Johannes. See Johannes, John.

## Johannisberger
Johannisberger, п., a delicate white Rhine wine.
— G., prop, '(wine) of Johannisberg' in the
Rheingau in Germany. For the ending see
suff. -er.

## johannite
johannite, п., a hydrous uranium copper sulfate
(mineral.) — G. Johannir, named after
Archduke Johann of Austria (1782-1859). The enr. ng
-it goes back to Gk. (της; see subst. suff. -ite.

## John
John, masc. PN. — ML. Johannes, fr. Late L.
Joannes, fr. Gk.'Ιωάννης, fr. Heb. Yohandn, lit.
'the Lord is gracious'. For the first element see
Joab and cp. words there referred to. The second
element derives fr. hanan, 'he was gracious'. See
Hannah and cp. Ivan, Jane, Jean, masc. and
fem. PN., jenneting, Jcuny, Joan, Joanna,
Johnny.

## John Bull
John Bull, the English nation personified. — Fr.
John Bull, a character representing the English
nation in Arbuthnot's satire The History of
John Bull (1712).

## Johnny
Johnny, masc. PN. — Formed fr. John with
dimin. suff. -y.

## Johnsonese
Johnsonese, п., a pompous, inflated style. —
Prop, the style of Dr. Samuel Johnson (1709-84).
For the ending see suff. -ese.

## Johnsonian
Johnsonian, adj., pertaining to, or resembling,
Dr. Samuel Johnson or his style. — See prec.
word and -iau.
Derivative: Johnsonian-ism, n.

## johnstrupite
johnstrupite, п., a complex silicate of cerium
and other metals (mineral.) — G. Johnstrupit,
named after Professor Frederik Johnstrup of
Copenhagen (died in 1894). The ending -it goes
back to Gk. -ίτης; see subst. suff. -ite.

## join
join, tr. and intr. v. — ME. joinen, fr. OF.
(= F.) join-, joign-, stem of joindre, 'to
join', fr. L. jungere, 'to join, unite', which is
cogn. with OI. yunakti, 'he harnesses', yukrth,
'harnessed', Gk. ζευγνύναι, 'to yoke,
harness', Avestic yaoj-, yuj-, Ί harness', yuxta-,
'harnessed', Lith. jungiu, jangti, "to yoke'. All
these words are dervatives of I.-E. base *yeug-,
'to join, unite', enlargement of base *yeu-, of
s-.m., whence OI. yduti, yuvdti, 'he harnesses'.
See yoke and cp. adjoin, adjunct, conjoin,
conjoint, conjugal, conjugate, conjugation, conjunct,
disjoin, disjoint, disjunct, injunction, Jostle, joust,
Jugatinus, jugular, jugulate, junction, juncture,
junta, junto, juxta-, rejoin, rejoinder, subjoin,
subjugate, subjunctive, and the second element
in quadriga. For a special use of base *yeu- in
the sense 'to mix', see juice and cp. jube.
Derivatives: join-ing, verbal п., and adj.,
joining-ty, adv.

## joinder
joinder, п., the act of joining (law), — F. joindre,
'to join' (fr. L. jungere), used as a noun; see
join. For the subst. use of infinitives in law
terms see attainder. Cp. rejoinder.

## joiner
joiner, n. — ME. joynour, fr. OF. joigneor, fr.
joigner (F. joindre), 'to join'. See join and
agential suff. -er.
Derivative: joiner-y, n.

## joint
joint, n. — OF. (= F.) joint, 'a joint', fr. joint,
pp. of joindre. See joint, adj.
Derivatives: joint, tr. v.,joint-ed, adj., joint-ed-
ly, adv., joint-ed-ness, п., joint-less, adj.

## joint
joint, adj. — OF. (= F.), 'joined', fr. L. junctus,
pp. of jungere, 'to join'. See join and cp. prec.
word.
Derivative: joint-ly, adv.

## jointress
jointress, п., a woman who has a jointure. —
Formed with suff. -ess fr. obsol. jointer, 'one
who holds a jointure'. See Joint and -ess.

## jointure
jointure, п., an estate settled on a wife at her
marriage. — F., fr. L. jimctura, 'a joining,
juncture', fr. junctus, pp. of jungere, 'to join*. See
join and -hire.
Derivative: jointure, tr. v.

## joist
joist, п., any of the small timbers supporting the
boards of a floor. — ME. giste, gyste, fr. OF.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:422 COLUMN:2 -->
giste (F. gite), 'stratum, bed (of mineral)', fr.
VL. jacita, 'lying place', prop. fem. pp. of L.
jacere, 'to lie', orig. 'to cast oneself down', rel.
to jacere, 4b throw, cast'. See jet, 'to spirt
forth', and cp. gist.
Derivative: joist, tr. v., to provide with joists.

## joke
joke, n. — L. jocus, 'jest, joke', fr. I.-E. base
*yek-, 'to speak', whence also Umbr. iuka, iuku,
'request, prayer', MW. ieith, Bret, iez,
'language', OS. gehan, OHG. jehan, 'to say,
declare; to confess', Du. biechten, OHG. bi-jehan,
MHG. be-jehen, 'to confess', and the verbal
nouns OS. Ы-gihto, Du. biecht, OHG., MHG.
bi-jiht, Ы-giht, MHG. biht, G. Beichte,
'confession'. Cp. jeopardy, jeu, jewel, jocular, juggle,
ju-ju.
Derivatives: joke, intr. and tr. v.,jok-er, n.,jok-
ing-ly, adv., jok-y, adj.

## Jokull
Jokull, jokull, п., mountain covered with snow;
snow mountain. — Icel. jokull, 'icicle'. See icicle.

## jollification
jollification, n. — See next word and -ation.

## jollify
jollify, tr. v., to make jolly; intr. v., to become
jolly (colloq.) — Compounded of jolly and -fy.

## Jollity
Jollity, п., the quality or state of being jolly. —
ME. jolivete, jalite, fr. OF. jolivete, joliete, fr.
jolif, joli, 'merry, gay'. See next word and -ty.

## jolly
jolly, adj. — ME. jolif, joli, fr. OF. jolif, joli,
'merry, gay' (whence F. joli, 'pretty, fine, nice'),
lit. 'festive', fr. ON. jol, 'Christmas, yule'. See
yule. For the formation of the OF. adjective
jolif (fr. ON. jdl) cp. OF. aisif, 'easy', fr. aise,
'ease'.
Derivatives: jolly, п., tr. v. and adw.,jolli-ly, adv.

## jolly boat
jolly boat, a kind of boat. — Prob. fr. Dan. jolte
or Du. jol (see yawl); influenced in form by the
adj. jolly. The word boat, which is tautological,
was added to explain the foreign word.

## jolt
jolt, tr. and intr. v., to jerk. — Prob. corruption
of jot, 'to jolt'.
Derivatives: jolt, a.,jolt-er, a.,jolt-y, adj., jolt-
i-ness, n.

## jolterhead
jolterhead, jolthead. — Compounded of Jolt and
head; lit. 'one whose headhsis been jolted'.

## jompon
jompon, n. — A var. of jampan.

## Jonah
Jonah, 1) masc. PN.; 2) in the Bible, the fifth in
the order of the Twelve Prophets; whence 3)
often used in the sense 'bringer of bad luck'. —
Late L. Jonas, fr. Gk. Ίωνας, fr. Heb. Ydndh,
fr. ydndh, 'dove, pigeon' (cp. Aram, yond, Syr.
yaund, of s.m.); lit. 'the moaning one', rel. to
Heb. and", 'he groaned, moaned, mourned'.

## Jonathan
Jonathan, п., ι) masc. PN.; 2) in the Bible, son of
Saul and friend of David. — Heb. Yonathdn,
shortened fr. Y'honathdn, lit. 'the Lord has
given'. For the first element see Joab. For the
etymology of Heb. nathdn, 'he has given' see
Nathan and cp. words there referred to. Cp. also
Brother Jonathan.

## jongleur
jongleur, п., a wandering minstrel. — F. jongleur,
'jongleur; juggler', fr. OF. jogleor, fr. L. jocu-
lator, 'jester, joker'. See juggler.' The
nasalization of F. jongleur (fr. OF. jogleor) is prob. due
to the influence of the OF. verb jangler, 'to
chatter' (see jangle).

## jonquil
jonquil, п., ι) a variety of narcissus; 2) its bulb. —
F. jonquille, fr. Sp. junquilla, dimin. of junco,
'rush', fr. L. juncus, 'rush'. See Jnncus.

## joola
joola, п., a rude suspension bridge in the
Himalaya (India). — Hind, jhuja, 'a swing'.

## Jordan almond
Jordan almond, n. — Transformation of ME.
jardyne almaunde, lit. 'garden almond', fr. OF.
jardin, 'garden', and almande, 'almond'; see
jardiniere and almond. The change of ME. jar-
dyne to Jordan is due to folk etymology.

## jordanite
jordanite, п., a lead arsenic sulfide (mineral.) —
G. Jordanit, named after Dr. Jordan of Saar-
brucken, Germany. The ending -it goes back to
Gk. -ίτης; see subst. suff. -ite.

## jorum
jorum, п., a large drinking vessel or its contents
(colloq.) — Lit. 'the vessel of Joram', fr. Heb.
Ydrdm; so called in allusion to II Sam. 8:10,
where we read: "And Joram brought with him
vessels of silver ands vessels of gold and vessels
of brass".

## joseite
joseite, п., a telluride of bismuth, containing
some sulfur and selenium (mineral.) — Named
after Sio Jose do Paralso in Brazil. For the
ending see subst. suff. -ite.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:422 COLUMN:3 -->

## Joseph
Joseph, 1) masc. PN.; 2). in the Bible, the elder
son of Jacob by Rachel. — Late L. Joseph,
Jdsephus, fr. Gk. 'Ιωσήφ, fr. Heb. Yosiph (also
Y'hdsiph, Ps. 81:6), lit.'adds, increases', Hiph'il
(= causative form) oiyasaph, 'he added', which
is rel. to Aram, ostph, Syr. ausiph, 'he added,
increased'. Cp. next word.

## Joseph
Joseph, п., a woman's riding coat. — Prob. so
called fr. Joseph's 'coat of many colors'. See
Gen. 37:3.

## Josepha
Josepha, fem. PN. — ModL., it. L. Jdsephus. See
Joseph and cp. next word.

## Josephine
Josephine, fem. PN. — F. Josephine, fr. Joseph.
See Joseph and -ine (representing L. -Ina).

## josephinite
josephinite, п., a natural alloy of iron and nickel
(mineral.) — Named after Josephine County in
Oregon.

## Joshua
Joshua, 1) masc. PN.; 2) in the Bible, Moses'
successor and the leader of the Israelites into the
Land of Canaan. — Heb. Y'hdshaa', lit. 'the
Lord is salvation'. For the first element see Joab,
for the second see hosanna.

## joss
joss, п., an idol (Pidgin English). — Port, deos,
'a god', fr. L. deus. See deity.

## josser
josser, п., a fellow (slang). — Of uncertain origin.

## jostle
jostle, tr. and intr. v., to push roughly. — Formed
fr. joust with freq. suff. -le.
Derivatives: jostle, x\.,jostle-ment, n.,jostl-er, n.

## jot
jot, п., the letter iota; a point. — L. ίδια, fr. Gk.
ιώτα, the smallest letter of the Greek alphabet,
fr. Heb. yddh, name of the loth letter of the
Hebrew alphabet. See yodh and cp. iota.
Derivatives: jot, tr. v., jott-er, п., jott-ing, п.,
jott-y, adj.

## jot
jot, tr. and intr. v., to jolt (now dial.) — Of
imitative origin. Cp. jolt.

## Jotham
Jotham, 1) masc. PN.; 2) in the Bible: a) the
youngest son of Gideon; b) a king of Judah. —
Heb. Jotham, lit. 'the Lord is perfect'. For the
first element of this name cp. Joab and words
there referred to. The second element derives
from the base of tarn, 'he was complete', whence
also torn, 'completeness, integrity', tarn, tamim,
'complete, sound', m'thom, 'soundness'. Cp.
Aram. tem\md, Syr. tammimd, 'complete,
perfect', Arab, tamma, 'he was complete'.

## joule
joule, п., unit of electrical energy (physics). —
Named after the English physicist James Prescott
Joule (1818-89).

## jounce
jounce, tr. and intr. v., to jolt; п., a jolt. — Prob.
a blend of Jump and bounce.

## journal
journal, adj., daily (archaic). — ME., fr. OF.
jornal, jurnal, journal (F. journal), 'daily', fr.
L. diurnalis, 'diurnal', fr. diurnus, 'daily'. See
diurnal, which is a doublet of journal and cp.
journey.

## journal
journal, n. — F., lit. 'a daily paper', fr. OF.
jornal, jurnal, journal, 'daily'. See journal, adj.
Derivatives: journal-ese, п., journal-ism, п.,
journal-ist, п., journal-ist-ic, adj., journal-ize,
tr. and intr. v.

## journey
journey, n. — OF. jornee, jurnee, journee (F. jour-
nee), 'day; day's work, day's journey', fr. VL.
*diurnata, 'day, day's work', fr. L. diurnus,
'daily'. Cp. It. giornata, OProvenc. Jornada and
see diurnal, adj. Cp. also journal, adj. and п.,
adjourn, sojourn. The ending -ala in diurnata is
prop. fem. pp. suff. See adj. suff. -ate.
Derivatives: journey, intr. v., journey-er, п.,
journey-ing, n.

## joust
joust, just, intr. v., to tilt. — ME. justen, jousten,
fr. OF.joster,juster,jouster(F.jouter), 'to joust,
tilt', fr. VL. 'juxtare, 'to approach', fr. L./илгго,
'near, close'. See juxta- and cp. juxtaposition.

## jonst
jonst, just, п., combat of two knights on
horseback. — ME. juste, jouste, fr. OF. joste, juste,
jouste (F. joute), 'joust, tilt', fr. joster, juster,
jouster. See jonst, just, v.

## Jove
Jove, п., Jupiter. — L. Jovis, fr. OL. Jovis, also
Diovis, used as the gen. (also nom.) of Jupiter.
See Jupiter and cp. next word. Cp. also the first
element in Juglans.

## jovial
jovial, adj., cheery, merry. - F., fr. It. joviale,
lit. 'pertaining to Jupiter', whence arose the
meaning 'born under the planet Jupiter;
joyful' (this planet having been regarded as the
source of joy), fr. L. Jovialis, 'of Jupiter', fr.
Jovins, of s.m., fr. OL. Jovis, Diovis, 'Jupiter*.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:423 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: JOVIAN | 396 -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:423 COLUMN:1 -->
See prec. word and adj. suff. -a].
Derivatives: jovial-ity, /ovial-ly, adv., jovial-
ness, n.

## Jovian
Jovian, adj., i) pertaining to, or resembling,
Jupiter; 2) pertaining to the planet Jupiter. —
See Jove and -ian.

## jow
jow, n. — A var. of jhow.

## jowar
jowar, jowari, jowarree, п., millet, durra (India).
— Hind, jawar, joar, juar, prob. fr. OI. yava-
akara-, 'of the nature of barley'.

## jowl
jowl, п., jaw. — ME. chawl, chavel, cholle, fr. OE.
ceafi, 'jaw', rel. to MHG. kiver, kivel, G. Kiefer,
ON. kjaptr, 'jaw', and cogn. with Olr. gop, lr.
gob, 'beak, mouth', Avestic zafar1, 'mouth,
gullet'. Cp. chafer, 'beetle'.

## joy
joy, n. — ME. joye, fr. OF. joie, joye (F. joie), fr.
L. gaudia, pi. of gaudium, 'joy' (but mistaken
for a fern, singular noun), which is rel. to gau-
dere, 'to rejoice'. See gaud and cp. enjoy. Cp.
also feu de joie, rejoice.
Derivatives :joy, v. (qy.),joy-ful, adj. ,joy-ful-ly,
adv., joy-ful-ness, п., joy-less, adj., joy-less-ly,
adv., joy-less-ness, n.

## joy
joy, intr. and tr. v., to rejoice. — OF. joir (F.
jouir), fr. VL. *gaudire (whence also OProvenc.
jauzir), corresponding to L.. gaudere, 'to
rejoice' (whence It. godere, of s.m.) See joy, n.

## Joyce
Joyce, fern. PN. — Earlier Josse, Goce, etc., orig.
used both for men and women; of Celtic origin.

## joyous
joyous, adj. — OF. joios, joious, joyous (F. joy-
eux), fr. joie, 'joy'. See joy and -ous.
Derivatives: joyous-Iy, adv., joyous-ness, n.

## jube
jube, п., rood loft in a church. — F. jube, fr. L.
jube, 'bid thou', imper. oijubere, 'to bid,
command', fr. OL. joubere, of s.m., orig. 'to set
in motion, stir', fr.. I.-E. base 'yeudh-, whence
also OI. yodhayati, 'involves in a fight', yudh-,
'fight', yudhmah, 'warlike, warrior', Avestic
yuiSyeinti, 'they fight', yaoshli-, 'activity, agility',
Arm. yuzem, Ί stir up', Gk. ΰσμίνη (for *yudh-
s-mini), 'battle' (prop, 'turmoil'), Lith. judit,
judeti, 'to move trembling, to quarrel', L. jitba,
'mane', lit. 'that which waves, flutters'. All these
words derive fr. I.-E. base *yeu-dh-, 'to be
moved, to be shaken', which seems to be a
dental enlargement of base *yeu-, 'to mix, stir'.
The rood loft is called from the first word of a
Latin prayer, which was said from the gallery
above the rood screen.

## jubilance
jubilance, jubilancy, n. — Formed from next
word with suff. -ce, resp. -cy.

## Jubilant
Jubilant, adj. — L. jubilans, gen. -antis, pres. part.
oi jubilare. See next word and -ant.
Derivative: jubilant-ly, adv.

## jubilate
jubilate, intr. v., to exult. — Fr. L. jubilat-(um),
pp. stem of jubilare, 'to shout for joy' (whence
prob.—through back formation—y'uii/ит, 'wild
cry, shout of joy'), fr. I.-E. *yu-dhe-los, lit. 'one
who makes yu\ compounded of the imitative
base "уй-, 'to shout for joy, shout', and base
*dhe-, 'to place, make, do'. The first element
appears also in Gk. ίΰγή, 'outcry', [υγμός,
'shout of joy; cry of pain', ϊύζειν, 'to shout,
yell', Lith. yvas, 'owl', MHG. ju, juch, 'shout
of joy', juwen, juwezen, 'to jubilate', G. jauch-
zen, 'to shout for joy, exult'. Base *уй is rel. to
base *yo-, whence MHG. jodelnjolen, 'to shout,
yodel'. See yodel, yowl and cp. jynx. For the
second element in jubilate see do and cp. fact,
theme. See also verbal suff. -ate.
Derivatives: jubilation (q.v.), jubilal-ory, adj.

## Jubilate
Jubilate, п., name of the one-hundredth psalm. —
L. jubilate, 'shout with joy', imper. pi. of
jubilare, 'to shout with joy' (see prec. word); so
called from the introductory word of the Latin
rendering of the psalm.

## jubilation
jubilation, n. — L. jiibilatio, gen. -onis, 'a
shouting', fr. jubilatus, pp. of jubilare. See Jubilate,
'to exult', and -ion.

## jubilee
jubilee, n. —F.jubile, fr. Late L. jubilaeus (scil.
annus), '(year of) jubilee', fr. Gk. ίωβηλαϊος,
'pertaining to a jubilee', fr. ίώβηλος, 'jubilee',
fr. Heb. yobhel, 'ram; ram's horn; rejoicing;
jubilee' (so called because the inauguration of
every fiftieth year was proclaimed through the
sound of the ram's horn on the Day of
Atonement; see Lev. 25:9). Heb. ydbhil is prop, the
partic. of stem y-b-l, 'to bear, conduct, lead',

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:423 COLUMN:2 -->
hence lit. means 'leader, leading animal'. Cp.
Heb. hdbhil, 'he lead, conducted', y'bhul,
'produce', yubhal, 'stream', Aram, obhll, Syr. aubhel,
'he lead, conducted'. L. jubilaeus (annus) was
influenced in form by a confusion of this word
with L. jubilare, 'to shout for joy'.

## Judah
Judah, 1) masc. PN.; 2) in the Bible a) son of
Jacob by Leah; b) a tribe of Israel. — Heb.
Y'hUdha", prop, imperfect Hoph'al (= passive
of the causative) of stem y-d-h (prop, y-d-y), lit.
'praised'; cp. the causative hodha", 'he gave
thanks, praised, confessed', todhd",
'thanksgiving, thank-offering', Mishnaic Heb. hodha'a",
'thanksgiving, confession', Aram, ddht, Syr.
audhi, 'he gave thanks, praised, confessed',
Arab, istauda, 'he confessed'. For the
explanation of the name see Gen. 29:35 and cp.
49:8. Cp. next word and words there referred to.
Derivative: Judah-ite, n.

## Judaic
Judaic, adj., pertaining to the Jews; pertaining
to Judaism. — L. JWdaicus, fr. Gk. 'Ιουδαϊκός,
'Jewish', fr. 'Ιουδαίος, fr. Aram. Yihudhay(a),
'Jew', fr. Heb. Y'hudht, 'Jew', orig. meaning 'of
the tribe of Judah', fr. Y'hudhd*, 'Judah'. See
Judah and -ic and cp. Jew, Yiddish. Cp. also
Chueta.

## Judaism
Judaism, n. — Late L. judatsmus, fr. Gk.
ιουδαϊσμός, fr. 'Ιουδαίος, 'Jew*. Cp. F. judaisme and
see prec. word and -ism.

## Judaist
Judaist, n. — See prec. word and -ist.
Derivative: Judaist-ic, adj.

## judaize
judaize, tr. and intr. v. — Late L.- jiidaizare, fr.
Gk. ίουδαίζειν, fr. 'Ιουδαίος, 'Jew'. See Jndaic
and -ize and cp. Judaism.
Derivatives: judaiz-ation, п., judaiz-er, n.

## Judas
Judas, n. — L., fr. Gk. Ίούδϊς, fr. Heb. Y'hudha".
See Judah.

## Jude
Jude, masc. PN. — A variant of Judah.

## judex
judex, п., a judge. — L. See judge.

## judge
judge, n. — ME. juge, fr. OF. (= F.)juge, fr. L.
judicem, ace. of judex, 'judge', which stands for
*jous-dik-s and orig. meant 'one who shows
right', it. jus, 'right', and the stem oidicere, 'to
show, tell, say'. See jus and diction and cp.
prejudice. Cp. also the second element in preach.

## judge
judge, tr. and intr. v. — ME. jugen, fr. OF. jugier,
juger (F. juger), 'to judge', fr. L. judicSre, of s.m.,
fr. judex, gen. judicis. See judge, п., and cp.
adjudicate. Cp. also hoosegow.

## judgmatic
judgmatic, judgmatical, adj., showing good
judgment (colloq.) — A hybrid formed fr. jndge, п.,
with the ending -malic (on analogy of dogmatic).
Derivative: judgmatic-al-ly, adv.

## judgment
judgment, judgement, n. — ME. jugement, fr. OF.
(= F.) jugement, it. juger, 'to judge'. See jndge,
v., and -ment.

## judicatory
judicatory, adj., pertaining to judgment. — Late
L. jiidicatorius, 'pertaining to judgment', fr. L.
judicatus, pp. of judicare, 'to judge'. See judge,
v., and adj. suff. -ory.

## judicatory
judicatory, п., a court of justice. — Late L. judi-
catorium, prop. neut. of jiidicatorius, 'pertaining
to judgment', used as a noun. See prec. word.

## judicature
judicature, n. — F., fr. ML. judicalura,.fr. L.
jddiedtus, pp. of judicare, 'to judge'. See jndge,
v., and -ure.

## judicial
judicial, adj. — L. jiidicialis, 'judicial', fr.
judicium, 'judgment', fr. judex, gen. judicis, 'judge'.
See judge, п., and -ial.
Derivatives: judicial-ly, adv., judicial-ness, n.

## jndiciary
jndiciary, adj., pertaining to a court of justice. —
L. judiciarius, fr. judex, gen. judicis, 'judge'. See
judge, п., and adj. suff. -ary.
Derivative: judiciary, п., judges collectively.

## jndicious
jndicious, adj., having sound judgment; wise. —
F. judicieux (fern, judicieuse), fr. L. judicium,
'judgment'. See jndge, п., and -ous.
Derivatives: judicious-ly, adv., judicious-ness, n.

## Judith
Judith, fem. PN. — L., fr. Gk. -Ιουδί», fr. Heb.
Y'hudtth, prop. fem. of Y'hudht, 'Jewish;
Jewess', fr. Ylhudhah, 'Judah'. See Judah.

## judo
judo, п., a modern form of jujitsu. — Jap. judo,
fr. ju, 'soft', and do, 'road, way'.

## jng
jng, п., a vessel. — Fr. Jug, a pet form of Joan or
Judith; cp. juggins. For sense development cp.
jack, 'sleeveless coat'.
Derivatives: jug, tr. v., jug-ful, adj.

## jug
jug, п., note of a nightingale. — Of imitative

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:423 COLUMN:3 -->
origin.

## jngate
jngate, adj., having the leaflets in pairs (hot.) —
L. jugatus, 'connected', pp. of jugare, 'to join,
connect', fr. jugum, 'yoke'. See yoke and cp.
next word and conjugate, subjugate.

## Jugatmus
Jugatmus, п., the god of marriage in Roman
mythology. — L. Jugatmus, fr. jugatus, pp; of
jugare, 'to join, connect'. See prec. word.

## Juggernaut
Juggernaut, also Jagannath, n., 1) a title of Vishnu
or of Krishna (Hindu mythol.); 2) anything that
demands blind devotion or merciless sacrifice,
— Hind. Jagannath, fr. OI. Jagannmhah, 'lord
of the world', fr. jdgat, 'world', and nalhah,
'lord'. The first element lit. means 'mobile', and
is a participial formation from the base of OI.
jigati, 'goes'; see jagat..The second element is
rel. to natham, 'help', and derives fr. I.-E. base
*na-, 'to help, be useful', whence also Gk.
όυίνημι, Ί help, profit, benefit'. Cp. jaconet.

## juggins
juggins, п., a simple person (slang). —
Diminutive of Jug, which is a pet form of Joan. Cp.
jug, 'vessel', and muggins.

## juggle
juggle, intr. and tr. v. — ME. jogelen, fr. OF.
jogler (F. jongler), fr. L. joculari, 'to joke, jest',
fr. jocus, 'jest'. See joke and cp. jongleur.
Derivatives: juggle, п., juggler (q.v.), juggl-ery,
п., juggl-ing, n. and adj., juggl-ing-ly, adv.

## juggler
juggler, n. — ME. jogelour, joglere, fr. OF. jog-
leor (nom. joglere), fr. L. joculatorem, ace. of
joculator, 'jester', it. joculari. See prec. word and
agential suff. -er.

## Juglandaceae
Juglandaceae, п., the walnut family (hot.) —
Formed from next word with suff. -aceae.

## Juglans
Juglans, п., a genus of trees, the walnut. — L.
juglans, 'walnut', contraction of Jovis glans,
which is a loan translation of Gk. Διός βάλανος,
'chestnut', lit. 'acorn of Jupiter'. See Jove and
gland.

## Jugoslav
Jugoslav, n. — A var. of Yugoslav.

## Jugoslavia
Jugoslavia, n. — A var. of Yugoslavia.

## jugular
jugular, adj., 1) pertaining to the throat and neck
(anal.); 2) having the pelvic fins beneath the
throat under the pectoral (zool.); п., a jugular
vein. — ModL. jugularis, fr. L. jugulum,
'collarbone, throat', which is rel. to L. jugum, 'yoke'
See jugate and -ar.

## jugulate
jugulate, tr. v., to cut the throat of, strangle. —
L. jugulatus, pp. of jugulare, 'to cut the throat
of, kill, destroy', it. jugulum. See prec. word and
verbal suff. -ate.

## juice
juice, n. — ME. juce, juse, fr. MF. (= F.) jus,
fr. L. jus, 'broth, soup', fr. I.-E. base *yus-,
whence also OI. yus-, 'broth', OSlav., Pol., etc.,
jucha, 'broth, soup', OPruss. iuse, 'broth, soup'.
Lith. juSe, 'fish soup', Gk. ζύμη, 'leaven' (G.
Jauche, 'liquid manure', is a loan word fr. Pol.
jucha), ON. oslr, 'cheese'. Cp. verjnice. Cp. also
zyme. Base yus- is an enlargement of base *yeu-,
'to mix', which represents properly a special use
of base *yeu-, 'to join, unite'; see Join and cp.
jube.
Derivatives: juice-less, adj., juic-y, adj., juic-i-ly,
adv., juic-i-ness, n.

## ju-jitsu
ju-jitsu, ju-jutsu, n. — Jap. ju-jutsu, fr. ju, 'ten',
and juts, 'trick'. See Lokotsch, EW., No. 963.·

## ju-ju
ju-ju, п., charm, spell; ban. — Prob. fr. F.joujou,
'toy', infantile reduplication of jouel, of s.m.,
ft.jouer, 'to play', fr. ~L.jocare, 'to jest'. See joke.

## jujube
jujube, п., the fruit of the tree called zizyphus. —
F., fr. Late L. zizyphum, 'jujube', which together
with Late L. zizyphus, 'jujube tree', derives fr.
Gk. ζίζυφον, 'jujube tree; jujube', which is of
unknown origin. Cp. Zizyphus.

## jnlep
jnlep, п., a sweet drink. — F., fr. OProveng. julep
or fr. Sp. julepe, it. VAr. jultb, corresponding
to classical Arab, julab, fr. Pers. gulab, 'rose
water, julep', which is compounded of gut, 'rose',
and ab, 'water'. See rose and abdest.

## Julia
Julia, fem. PN. — L. Julia, fem. of Julius. See
Julius.

## Julian
Julian, masc. PN. — L. Julianas, a derivative of
Julius. See Julius and -an.

## Julian
Julian, adj., pertaining to Julius Caesar. — L.
Julianus, 'of, or belonging to, Julius Caesar'.
See prec. word and cp. the PN. GUI.

## Juliana
Juliana, fem. PN. — L. Juliana, fem. of JQlianus,
lit. 'belonging to Julius'. See Julius and cp.
Julian.

## julienite
julienite, п., a hydrous cobalt chloronitrate
(mineral.) — Named after the Belgian geologist
Henri Julien (died in 1920). For the ending see
subst. suff. -ite.

## julienne
julienne, п., a kind of clear soup. — F., prop,
'soup made in the manner of Julien', an
otherwise unknown cook. For the origin of the PN
see Julian.

## Juliet
Juliet, fem. PN. — It. Giutietta, dimin. of Giulta.
Cp. F. Juliette and see Julia and -et.

## Julius
Julius, masc. PN. — L. Julius, name of a Roman
gens (Caius Julius Caesar was a member of this
gens). The name Julius is prob. a contraction
of *Jovilios, lit. 'pertaining to, or descending
from, Jupiter'. See Jove, Jnpiter.

## July
July, n. — ME. Jule, fr. OF. Jule (F. juillet), fr.
L. Julius (mensis), lit. 'month of Julius Caesar';
see Julius. It was orig. the fifth month of the
year and was therefore called Quinttlis (fr. quin-
tus, 'fifth'). It was renamed in honor of Julius
Caesar, who was born in this month.

## jumble
jumble, tr. and intr. v., to mix up. — Prob. of
imitative origin.
Derivatives Jumble, n.,jumbl-er, n.Jumbl-y, adj.

## jumhle
jumhle, п., a thin sweet cake. — Prob. fr. prec.
word.

## jumbo
jumbo, п., a large and clumsy animal or person.
— Fr. Jumbo, name of a very large elephant
exhibited by the American showman Phineas
Taylor Barnum (1810-91).

## jumma
jumma, п., assessment (India). — Hind. prop.
'total assessment', fr. Arab, jam', 'assembly;
addition', fr. jdma'a, 'he gathered together'. See
jemadar,

## jump
jump, intr. and tr. v. — Of uncertain, possibly
imitative, origin. Cp. jounce,

## jump
jump, п., a kind of jacket. — Corrupted—prob.
under the influence of jump, 'to leap'—fr. F.
juppe, variant of jupe, 'petticoat, skirt'. See jupon
and cp. jumper, 'blouse'.

## jumper
jumper, п., one who, or that which, jumps. —
Formed fr. jump, v., with agential suff. -er.

## jumper
jumper, п., a loose blouse or jacket. — Formed
fr. jump, 'a kind of jacket', with agential suff. -er.

## Juncaceae
Juncaceae, n. pi., the rush family (hot.) — ModL.,

## Junco
Junco, п., a genus of American finches (ornithol.)
— ModL., lit. 'rush bird', fr. Sp. junco, 'rush',
fr. L. juncus. See Juncus.

## Jnncoides
Jnncoides, п., a genus of plants, the wood rushes
(hot.) — A ModL. hybrid coined fr. L. juncus, 'a
rush', and Greek suff. -οειδής, '-like', fr. είδος,
'form, shape'; see Juncus and -aid. The correct
form would be Thryoides (fr. Gk. θρύον, 'rush',
and -οειδής).

## Junction
Junction, п., a joining. — L. junctio, gen. -onis,

## juncture
juncture, п., ι) a joining; z) a critical point of
time. — L. juncture, 'a joining, uniting; a joint',
fr. junctus, pp. of jungere, 'to join'. See join
and -ure.

## Juncus
Juncus, п., a genus of plants, the rush (bot.) —
L. juncus, 'rush, bulrush', which stands for

and prob. also with ON. einir, Swed. en,
'juniper'; see Walde-Hofmann, LEW., I, 7Z7f. Cp.
jonquil, Junco, junk, 'bulrush', junk, 'old cable',
junket, and the first element in juniper.

## June
June, n. — L. Junius (mensis), lit. 'the month
(named in honor of) Juno', fr. Juno. See Juno.

## jungle
jungle, n. — Hind, jangal, 'desert, forest', fr. OI.

## jangalab
jangalab, 'dry ground, waste land, desert', which
is of uncertain origin.
Derivatives: jungl-ed, jungl-y, adjs.

## Junior
Junior, adj., younger. — L. junior (prob.
contracted fr. *juvenios), compar. of juvenis, 'young
man'. See juvenile and cp. Juno.
Derivatives: junior, п., junior-ate, п.,
juniority, n.

## juniper
juniper, п., any shrub or tree of the genus Juni-
perus. — L.juniperus, 'juniper tree', a compound,
the first element of which is prob. rel. to juncus,
'rush'; see Juncus. The second element is of
uncertain origin.

## Junius
Junius, masc. PN. — L. Junius, name of a Roman
gens.

## junk
junk, п., a bulrush (obsol.) — ME., fr. OF. jonc.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:424 COLUMN:2 -->
junc (F. jonc), fr. L. juncus. See Juncus and cp.
words there referred to.

## junk
junk, п., ι) old cable; 2) old cordage. — Port.
junco, 'rush, cordage', fr. L. juncus. See Juncus
and cp. prec. word.
Derivative: junk, tr. v., to make into junk.

## junk
junk, п., a Chinese three-masted vessel. — Port.
junco, fr. Javanese jon, of s.m.

## junker
junker, n. — G. See younker.

## junket
junket, п., curd sweetened and flavored. — It.
giuncata, 'cream cheese', fr. VL. *juncata, prop.
'something served in a rush basket', fr. L. juncus,

Derivatives: junket, intr. v.,junket-ing, verbal n.

## Juno
Juno, п., wife of Jupiter and queen of the gods
in Greek mythology. — L. Juno, of uncertain
origin; possibly rel. to juvenis, 'young' (cp.
junior, 'younger', compar. of juvenis), and lit.
meaning 'the youthful one'. See juvenile and
cp. junior. Cp. also June,

## junta
junta, п., ι) Spanish legislative council; 2) a junto.
— Sp., 'meeting, conference, assembly, council,
convention, union, fraternity', fr. L.juncta, fem.
pp. of jungere, 'to join'. See join and cp. next
word.

## junto
junto, п., a political faction, cabal. — Sp. junto,
corruption of prec. word due to the influence
of Spanish nouns in -o.

## Jupiter
Jupiter, п., the supreme god of heaven in Roman
mythology. — L. Juppiter, Jupiter, for JU-piter,
which is orig. a vocative and stands for *dyeu
p'ter (corresponding to Gk. Ζεΰ πάτερ, voc. of
Ζευς πατήρ, 'Father Zeus'). Cp. the nominative
Diespiter, 'Jupiter', and Ol. Dyauspita,
'heavenly father', and see deity and father. Cp. also
Jove, Zeus.

## jupon
jupon, п., skirt, petticoat. — F., fr. Arab. jubbah,
'a long woolen garment' (whence also It. giubba,
OProveng. jupa, Sp. aljuba). Cp. gyp, jump, 'a
kind of jacket', jumper, 'blouse'.

## Jura
Jura, п., name of a mountain range between
France and Switzerland. — F., fr. L. Jura.

## jural
jural, adj., pertaining to law. — Formed with adj.
suff. -al fr. L. jus, gen. juris, 'right, law'. See Jus.
Derivative: jural-ly, adv.

## juramentado
juramentado, п., a Moro of Mohammedan faith
who has taken an oath to die while killing
Christians. — Sp., 'bound by an oath', pp. of
juramentar, 'to bind by an oath', fr. juramento,
'an oath', fr. L. juramentum, of s.m., fr. jurare.
See jury and cp. jurat (in both senses).

## Jurassic
Jurassic, adj., 1) of granular limestone (as are
the Jura Mountains); whence 2) pertaining to
the middle period of the Mesozoic era (geol.)
— Prop, 'of the character of the Jura
Mountains', formed fr. Jura on analogy of Hassic
(from lias) and triassic (from trias).

## jurat
jurat, п., one who has taken an oath. — F., fr.
ML. juratus, lit. 'a sworn man', and prop. pp.
of L. jurare, 'to take an oath, swear'. See jury
and cp. jurameatado.

## jurat
jurat, п., memorandum on an affidavit (law). —
L. jiiratum, neut. pp. of jurare. See prec. word.

## jurel
jurel, п., any of several carangoid food fishes. —
Sp., fr. Gk. σαϋρος, 'lizard'. Cp. OProvenc.
saurel (whence F. saureT), which is of the same
origin. See sauro- and cp. saurel.

## juridical
juridical, adj. — Formed with adj. suff. -al fr. L.
juridicus, 'judicial', which is compounded of jus,
gen. juris, 'right, law', and dicere, 'to say'. See
jus and diction and cp. jurisdiction.

## jurisconsult
jurisconsult, п., a jurist. — L. jurisconsultus, 'one
skilled in the law, lawyer', compounded of jus,
gen. juris, 'right, law', and consultus, 'skilled',
pp. of consulere, 'to take counsel, consult'. See
consult.

## jurisdiction
jurisdiction, n. — OF. jurediction, juridiclion (F.
juridiction), fr. L. jurisdictidnem, ace. of juris-
dictio, 'administration of justice, jurisdiction',
which is compounded οι jus, gen. juris, 'right,
law', and dictio, gen. -onis, 'a saying', fr. dictus,
pp. of dfcere,_'to say'. See jus and diction. In OF.
and F., the omission of the s is due to the
influence of the adjective juridicus, 'judicial' (see
juridical).
Derivatives: jurtsdiction-al, adj.,

## jurisdiction-ally
jurisdiction-ally, adv.

## jurisprudence
jurisprudence, п., the science of law. — L. juris-

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:424 COLUMN:3 -->
prudentia (also prddentia juris, 'science of law,
jurisprudence', compounded of jus, gen. juris,
'right, law', and prddentia, 'a foreseeing*. See
jus and prudence.

## jurisprudent
jurisprudent, adj. and n. — Obsol. F. jurisprudent,
back formation fr. F. jurisprudence. See prec.
word and prndent.

## jurisprudential
jurisprudential, adj., pertaining to jurisprudence.
— Formed with adj. suff. -al fr. h.jurisprudentia.
See jurisprudence.
Derivative: jurisprudential-ly, adv.

## jurist
jurist, n. — F. juriste, fr. ML. jurista, 'jurist', fr.

Derivatives: jurist-ic, jurist-ic-al, adjs., jurist-
ic-al-ly, adv.

## juror
juror, п., a member of a jury. — ME. juroure, fr.
AF. jurour, corresponding to OF. jureor (F.
jureur), 'one who swears', fr. L. juratorem, ace.

oath, swear'. See jus and agential suff. -or.

## jury
jury, п., a body of persons sworn to give a true
answer or verdict on a matter submitted to
them. — OF. juree, 'oath, legal inquiry', prop,
fem. pp. used as a noun, fr. OF. (= F.) jurer,

(representing OF. -ее, F. -ее) and cp. jurat (in
both senses), juror, abjure, adjure, conjure,
perjure.

## jury
jury, adj., temporary (esp. in jury mast). —
Aphetic for ajury, fr. OF. ajurie, 'aid, help', fr.
L. adjutare, 'to help'. See aid.

## jus
jus, п., right, law. — L. jus (OL. jous), gen. juris,
'right, justice, law', prob. cogn. with OI. yd(i,'szfe-
ty\ Cp. judge, Judgment, judicious, juramentado,
jurat (in both senses), juridical, jurisconsult,
jurisdiction, jurisprudence, juror, jury, п., just,
adjudge, adjudicate, injury.

## Jussiaen
Jussiaen, п., a genus of plants, the primrose

## jussive
jussive, adj., expressing command. — Formed

Derivative: jussive, п., a word or form

## Jnst
Jnst, adj. — ME. just, juste, fr. F. juste, fr. L.

Justin, Justina, Justus, adjust and the first
element in juste-milieu.
Derivatives '.just, adv.,just-ly, adv., just-ness, n.

## just
just, v. — See joust.

## juste-milieu
juste-milieu, п., the golden mean. — F., lit. 'the

## justice
justice, n. — ME., fr. OF. justice, justise (F.

## justiciable
justiciable, adj., subject to jurisdiction. — OF.

Derivatives: justiciable, п., a person subject to

## justiciar
justiciar, п., the highest judicial officer of the

## justiciary

## justifiable

## justification

## justificative
justificative, adj. — Formed with suff. -ive fr.

## justificatory
justificatory, adj. — Formed with adj. suff. -ory

## justify
justify, tr. v. — F. justifier, fr. Late L. justificare,
'to justify', which is compounded of L. Justus,
'just', and -ficare, fr. -ficere, unstressed form of

## Justina
Justina, Justine, fem. PN. — L. Justina, fem. of

## Justus
Justus, masc. PN. — Lit. 'just', fr. L. Justus. See

## jut

Derivatives:,/«f, a.Jutt-ing, aaj.Jutt-ing-ly, adv.

## Jute
Jute, п., one of the ancient inhabitants of

## jute
jute, п., a fiber of two East Indian plants, Cor-

Bengali joto, jup, fr. OI. jutab, 'twisted hair',

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:425 COLUMN:2 -->

## Juturna
Juturna, п., a water nymph (.Roman mylhol.) —
L., Juturna, a name of Etruscan origin.

## juveuescence
juveuescence, n. — Formed from next word with

## juvenescent
juvenescent, adj., becoming young or youthful. —
L. /uvenescens, gen. -entis, pres. part, of juven-
escere, 'to grow up to youth', an inchoative verb

## Juvenile
Juvenile, adj., young, youthful. — F. juvenile,
'youthful', fr. L. juvenilis, 'youthful', fr. juvenis,

tas, rejuvenate. Cp. also junior, Juno, Evan.

## Juventas
Juventas, n. (.Roman mythol.), the goddess of

## juxta-
juxta-, pref. meaning 'near, close to*. — Fr. L.
juxta; 'near, next, close to, by the side of,
contracted fr. "jugista, adv. super!, formed from

the adjective 'jugos, 'closely connected', from

## juxtapose
juxtapose, tr. v., to place side by side. — Formed
fr. juxta- and pose, 'to place'.

## juxtaposition
juxtaposition, n. — F.. formed fr< juxta- and
position.

## juzail
juzail, n. — A var. of jezail.

## jynx
jynx, п., ι) the wryneck; 2) a charm (from the use
of this bird in witchcraft). — ModL. jynx (pi.
jynges), fr. L. lynx, fr. Gk. ϋυγξ (gen. ϊυγγος),

ίύζειν, 'to shout, yell', so that ΙΙυγξ would lit.
mean 'the shouting bird' (see jubilate).
According to others, ίυγξ is a word of foreign origin,
but was assimilated in form to Ιύζειν. See
Frisk, GEW., 1744 s.v. ϊυγξ.

## Jynx
Jynx, п., a genus of birds, the wryneck (ornithol.)
— ModL., fr. L. iynx, 'the wryneck'. See prec.
word.

## Kaaba
Kaaba, п., the cube-shaped building in the Great
Mosque of Mecca containing the Black Stone
of Mecca. — Arab. kd'ba*, 'square house', fr.
ka'b, 'cube*. Cp. cube.

## kaama
kaama, п., a hartebeest. — S. African native name.

## Kabyle
Kabyle, п., ι) a Berber of Algeria or Tunisia;
2) the langauge spoken by the Kabyles. — F.,
fr. Arab, qaba'il, pi. of qabtlah, 'tribe', rel. to
qabila, 'was jn front of*. See cabal and cp.
kiblah.

## kaddish
kaddish, п., doxology of the Jewish ritual. — Fr.

to the second word of the text (v'yithqaddash,
'and sanctified be').

## Kaffir
Kaffir, Kafir, п., i)anon-Mohammedan;2)amem-
ber of the most intelligent group of S. African
Bantu races. — Fr. Arab, kifir, 'infidel', prop,
part, of kdfara, 'he blotted out, covered, hid;·he
denied'. See Yom Kippur and cp. cafard.
Derivative: Kaffir, Kafir, adj.

## kaftan
kaftan, n. — A var. of caftan.

## kaga
kaga, п., a crested bird peculiar to Caledonia. —
Native name.

## kaid
kaid, п., the chief of a tribe in N. Africa. — Arab.
qa'id, 'leader', part, of qada, 'he led (the army)'.
Cp. alcaide.

## kail
kail, n. — See kale.

## kaimakam
kaimakam, п., lieutenant colonel of the Turkish
army. — Turk, qaimaqam, 'deputy', contraction

'standing in the place (of another)', fr. qa'im,

'place' (also from the base oiqama), rel. to Heb.
and Aram, qum, 'to arise, stand up', Heb.
maqim, 'place', Ethiop. qoma, 'he stood', Ak-
kad. kummu, 'place, dwelling', кит, kimu, 'in
place of, and prob. also to Akkad. kaiamanu,
'constant, enduring; the planet Saturn' (whence
Heb. kiyyan, Syr. ke'wdn, Arab, and Pers.
kaiv/άη, the planet Saturn').

## kainite
kainite, n„ a compound of sulfates of potassium
and magnesium (mineral.) — G. Kainit, coined
by С F. Ziricken in 1865 fr. Gk. καινός, 'new',
which is cogn. with L. re-cen-s, gen. recentis,
'fresh, new', and suff. -it, which goes back to
to Gk. -ίτης. See recent and subst. suff. -ite.

## Kainozoic
Kainozoic, adj. — See Cenozoic.

## kairine
kairine, п., an alkaloid made from quinoline
(mineral.) — Prob. fr. Gk. καιρός, 'the right

## kaiser
kaiser, п., an emperor; esp. (cap.) a German

OS. kesur, OFris. keiser (Goth, kaisar is
borrowed fr. Gk. Καίσαρ, which itself is a loan
word fr. L. Caesar). See Caesar and cp. czar.

## kaka
kaka, п., any of certain New Zealand parrots. —
Maori kaka, 'parrot', imitative of its cry.

## kakapo
kakapo, п., the owl parrot. — Maori. Cp. prec.
word.

## kakemono
kakemono, п., a Japanese hanging picture usually
mounted on a roller. — Jap.

## kakistocracy
kakistocracy, п., government hy the worst men.
— Formed on analogy of aristocracy fr. Gk.
κάκιστος, 'worst' superl. of κακός, 'bad', and
-κρατίϊ, 'rule of, fr. κράτος, 'strength, power,
rule'. See caco-, and -cracy. For the Greek
superl. suff. -ιστός in κάκιστος see -est and cp.
Callisto and words there referred to.

## kala
kala, п., a black bulbul. — Hind, kali, 'black',
