## kala azar
kala azar, an infectious tropical disease. — Hind.
kala azar, 'black sickness'. See kala.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:426 COLUMN:2 -->

## kale
kale, also kail, n. — Scot, variants of cole (q.v.)
Cp. sea kale.

## kaleidophone
kaleidophone, п., an instrument invented by the
English physicist Sir Charles Wheatstone (1802-
75) to make sound waves visible (physics). —
Lit. 'beautiful form of sound', coined fr. Gk.
καλός, 'beautiful', είδος, "form, shape', and
φωνή, 'sound, voice'. See calo-, eido- and phone,
'speech sound', and cp. next word.

## kaleidoscope
kaleidoscope, п., an instrument showing various
patterns. — Lit. 'observer of beautiful forms';
coined by its inventor, Sir David Brewster
(1781-1868) in 1817 fr. Gk. καλός, 'beautiful',
είδος, 'form, shape', and -σκόττιον, fr. σκοπεΐν,
'to look at, examine'. See calo-, eido- and -scope.
Derivative: kaleidoscop-ic, kaleidoscop-ic-al,
adjs. kaleidoscop-ic-al-ly, adv.

## kaleyard
kaleyard, kailyard, п., a cabbage garden. —
Compounded of kale, resp. kail, and yard.

## Kali
Kali, п., one of the seven tongues of the goddess
Agni (Vedic mythol.) — OI. Kali, lit. 'the black
one', fern, of kalafy. See kala.

## kali
kali, п., glasswort. — Arab, qilt, 'charred ashes
of the saltwort'. See alkali and cp. kalium.

## kalidiuin
kalidiuin, п., a cystocarp (hot.) — ModL., fr. Gk.
καλίδιον, dimin. formed fr. καλιά, 'hut, nest*.
See caliology and -idiuni.

## kaligenous
kaligenous, adj., producing alkalis. — A hybrid
coined fr. kali and Gk. γενναν, 'to beget, bring
forth, generate, produce'. See -genous.

## kalium
kalium, п., potassium (chem.) — ModL., fr.
Arab. qilt. See kali and 2nd -ium.

## kallilite
kallilite, п., a nickel bismuth sulfide (mineral.) —
Compounded of Gk. κάλλος, 'beauty' (fr. καλός,
'beautiful') and λίθ-ος, 'stone' (see calo- and
-lite); prop, translation of G. Schonstein (lit.
'beautiful stone'), name of the place where it
was first found.

## Kalmia
Kalmia, п., a genus of plants, the laurel of
America (boi.) — ModL., named after Peter Kalm
(П15-79), a pupil of Linnaeus. For the ending
see suff. -ia.

## kalmuck
kalmuck, п., a member of any of a group of
Buddhist Mongol tribes. — Turk, kalmuk, prop,
'that part of a tribe which remains at home', pp.
of kalmak, 'to remain'.

## kalong
kalong, п., a fruit-eating bat. — A Malay word,

## Kama
Kama, п., the god of love in Hindu mythology. —
OI. Kdmah, fr, kdmah, 'desire, love', rel. to
kdyamanah, 'loving', Avestic ka-, 'to desire',
kama, 'desire', fr. I.-E. base *qa-, 'to desire',
whence also L. cams, 'dear, precious'. See
charity.

## kamala
kamala, п., name of an East Indian tree. — OI.
kamalam, 'lotus', which is prob. of Dravidian
origin.

## kame
kame, п., a narrow hill, ridge; an eskar (geol.) —
Scot, variant of comb.

## kamsin
kamsin, n. — See khamsin.

## Kanaka
Kanaka, п., a native of the South Sea Islands. —
Hawaiian kanaka, 'man'.

## Kanarese.n
Kanarese.n , 1) a member of the people inhabiting
the districts of North and South Kanara in
India; 2) the language spoken by this people. —
Formed fr. Kanara with suff. -ese.

## kangaroo
kangaroo, n. — Australian native name.

## kantar
kantar, п., an Egyptian weight corresponding
to the hundredweight. — Arab, qinfdr, fr. Aram.
qinfdr, qinfard, short for qinfinara, 'hundred
pounds', fr. Late Gk. κεντηνάριος, representing
~L.centenarius, 'consisting of a hundred; weighing
a hundred pounds'. (See S. Fraenkel, Die ara-
maischen Fremdworter im Arabischen, Leiden
1886, p. 203). See centenarian and cp. centner.
Cp. also quintal and kilderkin.

## Kantian
Kantian, adj., pertaining to Immanuel Kant
(1724-1804) or his philosophy; п., an adherent
of the teachings of Kant.

## Kantianism
Kantianism, п., the philosophy of Immanuel
Kant. — See prec. word and -ism.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:426 COLUMN:3 -->

## kaolin
kaolin, п., china clay. — F., fr. Chinese kao-ling,
lit. 'high hill'; so called from the name of the
place where it was first found.

## kapellmeister
kapellmeister, п., conductor. — G., lit. 'chapel
master', compounded of Kapelle, 'chapel', and
Meister, 'master'. See chapel and master.

## kaph
kaph, п., name of the nth letter of the Hebrew
alphabet. — Heb. kaph, lit. 'the hollow of the
hand' (rel. to kaphaph, 'he bent'); so called in
allusion to the ancient Hebrew form of this
letter. Cp. kappa.

## kapok
kapok, п., silky fiber gained from the seed of the
cotton tree. — Malay kapoq, 'cotton tree'.

## kappa
kappa, п., the 10th letter of the Greek alphabet.
— Gk. κάππα, fr. Heb. kaph; see kaph. The α
was added because a Greek word cannot end
with а к; ср. alpha and words there referred to.

## Karaism
Karaism, п., doctrine of the Karaites, based
exclusively on the literal interpretation of the Holy
Scriptures.—A hybrid coined fr. Heb. qdrd', 'he
read', and suff. -ism (representing Gk. -ισμός).
Karaism lit. means 'religion based on miqra'
(i.e. the Bible text)'. See mikra and cp. kere,
Koran.

## Karaite
Karaite, п., an adherent of Karaism. — A hybrid
coined fr. Heb. qard, 'he read', and suff. -ite
(representing Gk. -ίτης). See prec. word.

## kareeta
kareeta, п., a silk bag for letters in the
correspondence of native nobles; letter (India). — Hind.
kharifa, fr. Arab. kharhah, 'bag, purse', which
is rel. to Heb. khartt, of s.m.

## karma
karma, п., act; fate (Buddhism). — OI. karma,
'action, work, deed; fate', rel. to krnoti, karoti,
Avestic kerenaoiti, 'makes', fr. I.-E. base
*qwer-, 'to make, form'. See corpus and cp.
Sanskrit and words there referred to. Cp. also
the second element in Vishvakarma.

## kaross
kaross, п., a cloak of skin worn by S. African
natives. — Prob. fr. Hottentot.

## karroo
karroo, karoo, п., barren table land in S. Africa.
— From a Hottentot word meaning 'dry'.

## karyo-
karyo-, before a vowel kary-, combining form
denoting the nucleus of a cell (biol.) — Gk.
κάρυο-, καρυ-, fr. κάρυον, 'nut, kernel', which is
cogn. with L. carina, 'keel of a ship'. See careen.

## karyoplasm
karyoplasm, п., nuclear protoplasm. —
Compounded of karyo- and Gk. πλάσμα, 'something
molded'. See -plasm and cp. cytoplasm.
Derivative: karyoplasm-ic, adj.

## kasher
kasher, also kosher, adj., ritually fit or pure (said
esp. of food). — Heb. kosher, 'fit, suitable,
proper', in Mishnaic Heb. 'ritually fit, kasher',
from the base of kashir, 'was suitable, proper,
succeeded, prospered,' whence also hikhshtr, 'he
made fit', in Mishnaic Heb. also 'he pronounced
ritually fit, he pronounced kasher', Heb. kishrSn,
'skill, success, advantage', in Modern Heb. also
'aptitude, talent', Mishnaic Heb. kosher,
'fitness' (whence sheath hakkosher, 'opportunity'),
kashrath, 'fitness', esp. 'ritual fitness'; rel. to
Aram.-Syr. keshar, 'was fit or suitable', akhshdr,
'made fit or suitable', ithkashshdr, 'was made
fit', Mishnaic Heb. heksher, Mod. Heb. hakh-
shardh, 'a making fit, preparation'.
Derivative: kasher, kosher, tr. v,

## kasolite
kasolite, п., a hydrous uranium lead silicate
(mineral.) — Named after Kasolo in Katanga,
Congo. For the ending see combining form
-lite.

## kata-
kata-, combining form. — A var. of cata-.

## katabolism
katabolism, n. — See catabolism.

## katha
katha,.n., story (Indian liter.) — OI. katha,
'narrative, story' (whence kathdyati, 'tells, narrates'),
lit. 'how (scil. happened this)?', from the I.-E.
pronom. stem ka-, whence also OI. kah, L. quis,
OE. hwa,.'who'. See who.

## Katharine
Katharine, Katherine, fern. PN. — See Catherine.

## katydid
katydid, п., an insect of the locust family. — So
called from the stridulous sound of the insect,
suggestive of the words katy did.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:427 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: KAURI | 400 -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:427 COLUMN:1 -->
Derivative: katydid, intr. v.

## kanri
kanri, п., a tall tree of New Zealand (Agathis
australis). — Maori.

## kava
kava, п., a Polynesian pepper shrub. — Native
name.

## kavass
kavass, п., a Turkish policeman. — Turk, qawas,
fr. Arab, qawwds, 'bowman', fr. Arab, qaus,
'bow', which is rel. to Heb. qesheth, Aram.
qashtd, Syr. qeshta, Akkad. qasthu, Ethiop.
qast, 'bow', Heb. qashshath, Aram, qashshatha,
Syr. qushshatha, 'bowman'.

## Kavi
Kavi, Kawi, п., the ancient language of Java. —
Javanese kavi, 'poetic (scil. language)', fr. OI.
kavih, 'wise, sage; seer, poet', which is rel. to
kavarih, 'stingy', a-kuvate, 'intends', and cogn.
with Gk. κοέω (for *κο5έω), Ί mark, perceive,
hear', fr. I.-E. base *(s)q$u-, 'to look at, observe,
perceive', whence also OE. sciawian, 'to look,
see'. See show and cp. words there referred to.

## kayak
kayak, п., an Eskimo canoe made of sealskin
stretched on a wooden frame. — Eskimo.

## kea
kea, п., a large New Zealand parrot. — Maori.

## keck
keck, intr. v., to retch. — Imitative.

## Kedar
Kedar, п., a tribe of northern Arabia. — Heb.
Qedhar, fr. Qedhar, son of Ishmael (see Gen.
25:3, IChr. 1:29), rel. to qadhar, 'was black,
dark, swarthy', whence also qadhruth,
'darkness, gloom', q'dhorannlth, 'gloomily,' Qidhron,
name of a wady and valley east of Jerusalem,
Mishnaic Heb. q'dhera", 'pot', qadddr, 'potter',
and to Aram, qidhra, q'dhlrd, Syr. qedhra, 'pot',
Arab qadhura, qadhira, 'was dirty'.
Derivative: Kedar-ile, adj. and n.

## keddah
keddah, п., an enclosure for entrapping
elephants (India). — Hind, kheda, rel. to khedna
'to chase, hunt', fr. OI. akhetab, khefab,
'hunting', which is of uncertain origin.

## kedge
kedge, tr. v., to warp (a ship); intr. v., to move
a ship by kedging (naut.) — Of uncertain
origin ; perh. a var. of cadge.

## kedgeree
kedgeree, п., a mixture of rice and lentils cooked
together (India) — Hind, khichri, fr. OI. khicca,
which is of uncertain origin.

## Kedushah
Kedushah, п., proclamation of holiness, inserted
before the third benediction of the Amidah; it
is recited during the repetition of the Amidah
by the Reader (Hebrew liturgy). — Mishnaic
Heb. q'dhushshd1·, 'holiness', from the stem of
Heb. qadhash, 'was holy', whence also Heb.
qadhSsh, 'holy', qodhesh, 'holiness', qodhesh
qodhdshtm, 'the Holy of Holies', miqdash,
'sanctuary, temple' (lit. 'a sacred place'), qiddhh, 'he
hallowed, sanctified', Mishnaic Heb. qiddhh,
'sanctification'; rel. to Aram.-Syr. qaddish, 'he
hallowed, sanctified', qaddish, 'holy', Arab, qa-
dusa, 'was pure, was holy', qaddasa, 'he
purified, hallowed, sanctified; he went to
Jerusalem', quds, 'purity, holiness', al-Quds,
'Jerusalem' (lit. 'the Holy Place'), qiddfs, 'holy', qad-
dus, 'very holy', Akkad. quddusuh, 'to cleanse,
hallow, sanctify'. Cp. kaddish, kiddush, klddu-
shin, Kodashim.

## keek
keek, intr. v., to peep. — ME. kiken, fr. MDu.
kiken (whence Du. kj/ken).
Derivatives: keek, п., keek-er, п., keek-ing, n.

## keel
keel, п., the lowest longitudinal timber of a ship.
— ME. kele, fr. ON. kjblr, (whence Dan.,
Norw. kjel, Swed. kbl). Cp. MDu. kel, kil, G.
Kiel, 'keel'.
Derivatives: keel, tr. v., to turn up the keel of;
intr. v., to turn up the keel; keel-age, п., keel-ed,
adj., keel-less, adj.

## keel
keel, п., ship, barge. — ME. kele, fr. MDu. kiel,
'ship', rel. to OE. ceol, OS., OHG. kiol, ON.
kjoll, MHC, G. Kiel, 'ship*; of uncertain
origin. Gk. γαυλός, 'milkpail, waterbucket',
γαϋλος, 'round-built Phoenician merchant
vessel', with which the above words are usually
connected, are prob. Sem. loan words; cp. Heb.
guild'', 'basin, bowl' (see gelilah).

## keel
keel, tr. v., to keep cool. — ME. kelen, fr. OE.
celan, 'to cool', fr. col, 'cool'. See cool.

## keelhaul
keelhaul, tr. v., to drag under the keel of a ship.
— Du. kielhalen, compounded of keel, 'kiel*,
and halen, 'to haul'. See keel, 'timber of a ship",
and haul,

## keelson
keelson, kelson, п., a set of timbers or plates
above the keel. — Prob. of Scand. origin. Cp.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:427 COLUMN:2 -->
Dan., Norw. kjelsvin, Swed. kolsvin, which are
compounded of kjel, resp. kol, 'keeP, and svin
(fr. ON. svlnri), 'pig'. Cp. also MDu. colzwijn,
Du. kolzwijn, G. Kielschwein, and see keel,
'timber of ship', and swine,

## keen
keen, adj., sharp. — ME. kene, 'sharp, bold', fr.
OE. cine, 'brave, bold, wise', rel. to ON. kann,
'skillful, wise'. MDu. coene, Du. koen, 'bold',
OHG. kuoni, 'pugnacious, strong', MHG.
kiiene, G. kiihn, 'bold, daring'. These words
derive fr. Teut. *kon-i and orig. denoted one
who knows. They are rel. to E. can, aux. v., and
to the first element in Conrad and in Kenelm
(qqv.)
Derivatives: keen-ly, adv., keen-ness, n.

## keen
keen, п., lamentation, dirge. — Ir. caoine, 'wail,
dirge', fr. caoinim, Ί wail'. See keen, v.
Derivative: keen-er, n.

## keen
keen, intr. v., to wail; tr. v., to bewail. — Ir.
caoinim, fr. Olr. cainim, coinim, Ί wail'.

## keep
keep, tr. and intr. v. — ME. kepen, fr. OE. сёрап,
'to observe, notice, attend to, seek, keep', rel.
to OE. capian, OS. kapdn, OHG. kapfen, 'to
look', ON. кора, 'to stare, gaze'; of uncertain
origin.
Derivatives: keep, n. (q.v.), keep-er, п., keep-er-
ship, п., keep-ing, n.

## keep
keep, n. — ME. kep, keep, fr. kepen, 'to keep';
see prec. word. All meanings of the noun keep
are traceable to the original sense 'that which
keeps'.

## keepsake
keepsake, n. — Compounded of keep and sake.
The literal meaning of the word is Object kept
for the sake (of the giver)'.

## keeshond
keeshond, п., a small kind of dog. — Du., fr.
Kees hond. Kees is dimin. of the PN. Cornells,
'Cornelius' (see Cornelius). Hond is rel. to E.
hound (q.v.)

## keeve
keeve, п., a large tub. — ME. kive, keve, fr. OE.
cyf, which is of uncertain origin. It possibly
derives fr. VL. *cupia, fr. L. cupa,'tub cask, tun,
vat'. See cup.

## kef
kef, kief, п., state of dreaminess caused by the
use of hemp or bhang. — Arab, kayf, in VArab.
pronounced kef, 'ease, well-being, pleasure'.

## keg
keg, п., a small cask. — Of Scand. origin; cp.
ON. kaggi, Swed. and Norw. kagge, 'cask'.

## kehillah
kehillah, п., Jewish community or congregation.
— Heb. qlhillah, 'assembly, congregation'; from
the stem of qahdl, of s.m., hiqhtt, 'he assembled',
whence also Qoheleth, 'Ecclesiastes', lit.
'assembler, collector'; rel. to qol, 'sound, voice', and to
Arab, qaul, of s.m. See cowie and cp. Koheleth
and the second element in bathkol.

## kelp
kelp, п., a large seaweed. — From earlier kilp,
fr. ME. culp; of unknown origin.

## kelpie
kelpie, kelpy, п., a water spirit resembling a horse
(Gaelic mythol.) — Prob. rel. to Gael, colpach,
'heifer, steer, colt', colpa, 'cow, horse'.

## kelson
kelson, n. — See keelson.

## Kelt
Kelt, n. — See Celt.

## kelt
kelt, п., salmon after spawning (Scot.) — Of
unknown origin.

## kelyphite
kelyphite, n. (petrogr.) — Formed with subst.
suff. -ite fr. Gk. κέλυφος, 'sheath, case', which
stands in gradational relationship to κκλύπτειν,
'to cover, hide, conceal'. See calyptra.

## kemb
kemb, tr. v., to comb (dial. Engl.) — ME. kemben,
fr. OE. cemban, rel. to OS. kembian, ON. kemba,
OHG. kemben, 'to comb'. These words are
denominated fr. OE. camb, 'comb', resp. its OS.,
ΟΝ., OHG. equivalents. See comb and cp.
kempt.

## kemp
kemp, n. (esp. used in the pi. kemps), coarse hair.
— ME. kempe, fr. Scand. Cp. ON. kampr,
'mustache', which is rel. to OE. cenep, OFris.
kanep, of s.m.

## kempt
kempt, partic, adj., combed (archaic). — Pp. of
kemb.

## ken
ken, tr. v., to know. — ME. kennen, fr. OE. cen-
nan, 'to make known, declare, attest', prop,
causative of cunnan, 'to know', rel. to ON.

## kenna
kenna, 'to know, make known', Swed. к anna,
Dan. kjende, 'to know', OFris. kanna, kenna,
'to recognize, admit', OHG. chennan, OHG.,
MHG., 'to make known', G. kennen, 'to know',
Goth, kannjan, 'to make known'. See can, aux.
v., and cp. know.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:427 COLUMN:3 -->

## ken
ken, п., range of sight; range of knowledge. —
Fr. prec. word.

## ken
ken, п., a resort for thieves (slang). — Prob. short
for kennel, 'shelter for a dog'.

## ken-
ken-, form of keno- before a vowel.

## kendal
kendal, п., a green woolen cloth. — So called
from Kendal in Westmorland, England, where
this cloth was manufactured and dyed green.

## Kenelm
Kenelm, masc. PN. — OE. Cenhelm, compounded
of сёпе, 'brave, bold', and helm, 'helmet'. See
keen, adj. and helmet.

## Kennedya
Kennedya, п., a genus of herbs of the pea family
(hot.) — ModL., named after Lewis Kennedy,
a London gardener (1775-1818).

## kennel
kennel, п., shelter for a dog. — ME. kenel, fr.
OF. (= F.) chenil, fr. chen (F. chien), 'dog', fr.
L. canem, ace. of canis, 'dog'. See hound and
cp. canine. Derivative: kennel, tr. and intr. v.

## kennel
kennel, п., a gutter. — A doublet of cannel.

## Kenneth
Kenneth, masc. PN. — Scot., fr. Gael. Caioneach,
lit. 'handsome, comely'.

## keno
keno, п., a game of chance resembling lotto. —
Prob. fr. F. quine, 'five winning numbers in a
lottery', fr. L. quint, 'five each', which is rel. to
quinque, 'five' (see qumque); so called because
in this game numbered balls are arranged in
rows of five; the player who first has a row of
five covered wins.

## keno-
keno-, before a vowel ken-, combining form
meaning 'empty'. — Gk. κενό-, κεν-, fr. κενός,
'empty', which stands for "κενίός and is cogn.
with Arm. sin, 'empty, vain'. Cp. the first
element in cenotaph.

## kenosis
kenosis, n. (Christian theol.) — Eccles. L., fr.
Gk. κένωσις, 'an emptying', fr. κενοϋν, 'to
empty', fr. κενός, 'empty'. See keno- and -osls.

## kent
kent, п., a long staff or pole. — L. contus, fr. Gk.
κοντός, 'a pole', which stands in gradational
relationship to κεντεϊν, 'to prick, goad', κέν-
τρον, 'point, prickle, ox goad'. See center and
cp. quant, 'pole'.

## Kentish
Kentish, adj., pertaining to the county of Kent. —
ME., fr. OE. Centisc, formed with suff. -isc fr.
Cent, 'Kent'. For the ending see adj. suff. -ish.
Cp. the first element in canterbury,

## kentledge
kentledge, п., pig iron used as ballast. — Of
uncertain origin.

## kephalic
kephalic, adj. — See cephalic.

## kepi
kepi, п., a peaked cap worn by soldiers. — F.
kepi, fr. Swiss G. Kappi, dimin. of G. Kappe,
'cap', fr. Late L. cappa, 'hood, cap'. See cap.'

## kept
kept, past tense and pp. of keep. — ME. kepte,
kept, past tense and pp. of kepen, 'to keep'. See
keep, v.

## keramlc
keramlc, adj. — See ceramic.

## keratin
keratin, п., the basic substance of horns, nails,
hair and feathers (biochem.) — Formed with
chem. suff. -in fr. Gk. κέρας, gen. κέρατος,
'horn'. See cerate-.

## keratitis
keratitis, п., inflammation of the cornea of the
eye (med.) — Medical L., formed with suff. -itis
fr. Gk. κέρας, gen. κέρατος, 'horn'. See cento-.

## kerato-
kerato-, before a vowel kerat-, combining form
meaning 'horn, horny'. — Sec cerato-.

## keratose
keratose, n>, a horny substance forming part of
the skeleton in some sponges (biochem.) —
Formed with subst. -ose fr. Gk. κέρας, gen.
κέρατος, 'horn'. See cerato-.

## keratusis
keratusis, п., an excess of the horny layer of the
skin (med.) — Medical L., formed with suff.
-osis fr. Gk. κέρας, gen. κέρατος, 'horn'. See
cerato-.

## kerauno-
kerauno-, combining form meaning 'thunderbolt'.
— Gk. κεραυνό-, fr. κεραυνός, 'thunderbolt'.
See cerauno-,

## keraunograph
keraunograph, n. — See ceraunograph.

## kerb
kerb, n. — A variant spelling of curb.

## kerchief
kerchief, n. — ME. curchef, coverchef, fr. OF.
covrechief, lit. 'cover head', fr. covrir (F. cou-
vrir), and chief, 'head; chief. See cover and
chief and cp. the first element in curfew.

## kere
kere, less correctly, keri (term of the Masorah),
part, adj., indicating that the reading given
in the margin should be substituted for what is
written in the text; п., the reading to be
substituted. — Lit. '(to be) read', fr. Aram, q're,
passive part, of q'ra", 'he read', which is rel. to
Heb. qard', of s.m. See mikra and cp. Karaism,

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:428 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: 401 | KIDDUSH -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:428 COLUMN:1 -->
Koran,

## kerf
kerf, п., ι) the act of cutting; 2) a cut made by
a saw; 3) a piece cut off. — ME. kirf, kerf, fr.
OE. cyrf, 'a cutting', rel. to OE. ceorfan, 'to
cut'. See carve.
Derivative; kerf, tr. v.

## Kerite
Kerite, п., a trademark for artificial cautchouc.
— Formed with subst. suff. -ite fr. Gk. κηρός,
'wax'. See cere, п., and cp. kerosene.

## kermes
kermes, п., the bodies of the females of an insect
found on the kermes oak. — F. kermes, fr.
Arab, qirmiz, ult. fr. OI. kimi-dza-, 'produced
by a worm'. See crimson and cp. carmine.

## kermess
kermess, kermis, п., ι) an annual outdoor fair
in the Low Countries; 2) in the United States,
an indoor fair. — Du. kermis, 'church-mass',
contraction of kerk mes, fr. kerk, 'church', and
mis, 'mass'. See church and Mass.

## kern
kern, kerne, п., a light-armed foot soldier in
ancient Ireland. — Ir. ceatharn, 'a band of
soldiers, a soldier'. Cp. cateran.

## kernel
kernel, n. — ME., fr. OE. cyrnel, dimin. of corn.
See corn, 'grain', and dimin. suff. -el.
Derivatives: kernel, tr. v., kerneKfyed, adj.

## kerosene
kerosene, п., an illuminating oil. — Formed with
suff. -ene fr. Gk. κηρός, 'wax'. See cere, п., and
cp. Kerite.

## Kerria
Kerria, п., a genus of plants of the rose family
(bot.) — ModL., named after the English
gardener WilliamKerr(died in 1814). For the ending
see suff. -ia.

## kerrite
kerrite, п., a kind of vermiculite (mineral.) —
Named after the American geologist W. C. Kerr
(1827-85). For the ending see subst. suff. -ite.

## Kerry
Kerry, п., an Irish breed of cattle. — Named after
County Kerry in the Irish Free State.

## kersey
kersey, п., a kind of coarse cloth. — Named after
Kersey, a village in Suffolk, England.

## kerseymere
kerseymere, п., cassimere. — A blend of cassi-
mere and kersey.

## kerygma
kerygma, п., preaching. — Gk. κήρυγμα,
'proclamation', from the stem of κηρύσσειν, 'to
proclaim (said of a herald)', which is
denominated fr. κήρυξ, 'herald'. See caduceus and -ma.

## kestrel
kestrel, п., a kind of falcon (Falco tinnuncutus). —
ME. caslrel, fr. MF. cresserelle (F. crecerelle),
'kestrel', enlarged fr. cresselle, 'kestrel', fr. cres-
selle (F. crecelle), '(hand-)rattle', which prob.
derives fr. VL. *crepicella, 'a rattle', a word
related to L. crepitdculum, 'a rattle', crepitd-
cillum, 'a small rattle', fr. crepitare, 'to rattle';
see crepitate. See Bloch-Wartburg, DELF.,
p. 160 s. vv. crecelle and crecerelle.

## ketch
ketch, п., a kind of small sailing vessel. — Fr.
earlier catch, from the verb catch, 'to seize' (q.v.)

## ketchup
ketchup, also catchup, catsup, п., a kind of
tomato sauce. — Chin, ke-lsiap, 'pickled fish
sauce'.

## kethib
kethib, also spelled ketib (term of the Masorah),
part, adj., designating that which is written in
the text as opposed to the reading in the margin
called kere; п., that which is written in the text.
— Aram. kethibh, 'written', passive part, of

## k'thabh
k'thabh, 'he wrote' (whence also k'thabh, 'a
writing'), rel. to Heb. kalabh, 'he wrote'. See
ketubah.

## kethubah
kethubah, n. — See ketubah.

## Kethubim
Kethubim, n. — See Ketubim.

## ketone
ketone, п., a group of compounds containing
CH (chem.) — G. Keton, coined by the German
chemist Leopold Gmelin (1788-1853) in 1848

## fr. G. Aketon
fr. G. Aketon, fr. F. acetone. See acetone.
Derivatives: keton-ic, adj., keton-ize, tr. v.

## kettle
kettle, n. — ME. ketel, fr. ON. ketill, fr. L. catil-

## lus (dimin. of catinus
lus (dimin. of catinus,' deep vessel for cooking,

## or serving up food')
or serving up food'), whence also OE. cetel, OS.

## ketil
ketil, ON. ketill, OFris. zetel, zitel, MDu. (Du.)

## ketel
ketel, OHG. кез5И (MHG. ke33el, G. Kessel),

## Goth
Goth, 'katils or *katilus (occurring only in gen.

## pi. katile)
pi. katile), 'kettle'. L. catinus is possibly cogn.
with Gk. κοτύλη, 'anything hollow, cup, socket
of a joint'. OHG. кезр (MHG. cAejji) is

## borrowed fr. L. catinus
borrowed fr. L. catinus, OSlav. kotilH is a Teut. loan

## word
word, Lith. kStilas, Lett, katb, OPruss. catils

## are borrowed from Slavonic. Cp. cotula
are borrowed from Slavonic. Cp. cotula,

## cotyledon. OI. catvalah (masc)
cotyledon. OI. catvalah (masc), 'hole', is prob. not

## cognate with L. catinus
cognate with L. catinus, but rel. to catvarah,
'four' (see four) and orig. denoted a square

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:428 COLUMN:2 -->
hole.

## ketubah
ketubah, also spelled kethubah, п., Jewish
marriage contract. — Mishnaic Heb. k'thubbd", lit.
'writing, writ', from the stem of Heb. kathabh, 'he
wrote' (whence also mikhtahh, 'a writing, letter');
rel. to Aram.-Syr. k'thabh, 'he wrote' (whence
k'thabh,'a. writing'). Cp. Arab, kataba, 'he wrote',
kitdb, Ethiop. katab, 'book', which are Heb. or
Aram, loan words. The original meaning of the
Semitic base k-t-b seems to have been 'to
engrave'; cp. Heb. k'lhobelh, 'tattooing' (Lev.
19:28), Arab, kataba in its orig. sense 'he sewed
together', and S. Arab, miktab, 'awl'. Cp.
kethib, Ketubim, kitab. For sense development
cp. Gk. γράφειν, 'to scratch, engrave, write'
(see -graph).

## Ketubim
Ketubim, also spelled Kethubim, n.pl., the Hagio-
grapha (Bible). — Heb. k'thubhtm, lit. 'written
things', pi. of kathabh, '(something) written',
passive panic, aikatabh, 'he wrote*. Seeprec. word.

## Keturah
Keturah, fern. PN. (Bible). — Heb. Q'tura1·, lit.
'incense', from the stem of qittir, hiqf/r, 'he
made sacrifices, smoke', whence also q'toreth,
'sweet smoke of sacrifice, incense'. See nectar.

## kevalin
kevalin, п., a soul freed from matter (Jainism). —
OI., fr. kevalah, 'alone, belonging exclusively
to a single person', fr. I.-E. base *qati-, *qoiI-,
'complete, sound, well, happy', whence also
Goth, haifs, 'complete, whole, well, sound', OE.
ha/, 'whole, uninjured, healthy'. See whole and
cp. words there referred to.

## kevel
kevel, п., a peg or bollard to which certain ropes
are fastened (naut.) — ONF. kevilk
(corresponding to F. cheville), 'peg, pin, bolt', fr. VL.
*cdvicula, dissimilated fr. Late L. clavicu/a, 'a
little key'. See clavicle.

## Kewpie
Kewpie, п., trademark for a doll. — Prob. altered
fr. Cupid.

## kex
kex, п., the dry stocks of hemlock or other
plants. — ME. kex, kyx, ult. fr. L. ciciita,
'hemlock'. See Cicuta.

## key
key, п., an instrument for opening or closing a
door, box, etc. — ME. keye, keige, etc., fr. OE,
cxg, lit. 'tool to cleave with', fr. Teut. base mki-,
'to cleave, split; to germinate, rise (said of
flowers)', whence also OHG., MHG. kit, G.
Keil, 'wedge', Goth, us-kijans (passive part.),
'come forth' (said of seeds), OS., OHG. kimo,
MHG. kime, G. Keim, 'germ', G. keimen, 'to
germinate', OS. kin, MLG. kine, MDu. кёпе,
'germ', OS., OHG. kinan, Goth, keinan, 'to
germinate', OE. cinan, 'to gape, crack', OE.
cid, OS. kith, OHG. (frumi) kidi, MHG. kide,
'sprout'. Teut. base *ki- corresponds to I.-E.
*gei-, *gi-, whence Arm. cii, ciui, 'stalk, blade',
Lett, zeiju, ziet, 'to rise' (said of flowers; also
fig.) See chine, 'valley', and chink, 'crack'.

## key
key, tr. and imr. v. — ME. keyen, fr. key, keye,
'key'. See key, n.

## key
key, n. — A var. of quay.

## Keziah
Keziah, ]) fem. PN.; 2) in the Bible, one of Job's
daughters. — Heb. Qftzi'ah, lit. 'cassia'. See
cassia.

## khaki
khaki, adj., dust-colored; п., a dust-colored cloth
used for military uniforms. — Hind, khaki,
'dusty, dust-colored', fr. Pers. khak, 'dust'.

## khalif
khalif, n. — A var. of caliph.

## khalifate
khalifate, n. — A var. of caliphate.

## khalsa
khalsa, п., the community of the Sikhs. — Hind.,
fr. Arab, khalisa", 'pure', prop. fem. pp. of
khulasa, 'he was pure, withdrew, retired', which
is rel. to Akkad. halsu, 'pure', Heb. haldtz, 'he
drew off, withdrew', hilletz, 'he saved, delivered,
freed', Aram.-Syr. haldtz, 'he drew off,
withdrew', Syr. halitza, 'free'.

## khamsin
khamsin, also spelled kamsin, п., a hot wind
flowing from the Sahara for about fifty days
(in March, April and May). — Arab, khamsin,
'fifty', short for rikh-al-khamstn, 'the wind of
fifty (days)'. Khamsin is gen. of khamsuni 'fifty',
which is rel. to Heb. humishshtm, Aram.-Syr.
hdmshin, Akkad. hamshati, 'fifty'.

## khan
khan, п., a title of ruler in Mohammedan
countries. — Pers. and Arab, khan, 'lord, prince', fr.
Turki khan, contraction of khaqdn, 'ruler,
sovereign', which is prob. of Mongolian origin.

## khan
khan, п., a caravanserai. — Pers. and Arab, khan,
'caravanserai, inn'. Cp. astrakhan.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:428 COLUMN:3 -->

## khanate
khanate, п., a district ruled by a khan. — A
hybrid coined fr.khan, 'title of ruler', and -ate,
a suffix of Latin Origin.

## khansamah
khansamah, п., a butler (India). — Hind, khan-
sdman, fr. Pers. khansaman, lit. 'lord of stores',
fr. khan, 'lord' (see khan, 'title of ruler'), and
sdman, 'stores, household'.

## khedive
khedive, п., title of the Turkish viceroy of Egypt
(hist.) — F. khedive, fr. Turk, khidiv, fr. Pers.
khidiw, 'prince', a derivative of khuda, 'master,
prince'.
Derivatives: khediv-al, khedivi-αϊ, adjs., khe-
divi-ate, n.

## khidmatgar
khidmatgar, khidmutgar, п., a male waiter
(India). — Hind, khidmatgar, fr. Pers. khidmatgar,
a hybrid formed fr. Arab. khidmah, 'service' (fi.
khadama, 'he served'), with Pers. suff. -gar,
'holder, owner'.

## Khitan
Khitan, adj. and п., Tatar. — Lit. 'of the
kingdom of the Khitans', fr. Khitai, name of a Tatar
kingdom"- See Cathay.

## khoja
khoja, khojah, п., a title of respect in Persia,
India and Turkestan. — Turk, khojah, fr. Pers.
khwajah.

## kibbutz
kibbutz, п., a collective agricultural settlement in
Israel. — Heb. qibbatz, lit. 'gathering,
assemblage', prop, verbal noun oiqibbitz, 'he
gathered, gathered together', Pi'el of qabhau, 'he
gathered'; rel. to Arab, qdbada, 'he grasped,
seized'.

## kibe
kibe, п., chillblain. — ME. kybe. Cp. W. cibi,
cibiost, 'chillblain'.

## kibitzer
kibitzer, п., ι) looker-on at a card-game; 2) a
meddlesome person. — G. Kiebitzer (slang), 'a
looker-on (at cards)', fr. kiebitzen, 'to look on',
fr. Kiebitz, 'pewit, plover', whence arose the
meaning (used only in slang) 'a meddlesome
looker on'. The birdname Kiebitz derives fr.
MHG. gibis, gtwis, which is of imitative origin.
Cp. MLG. kivit, MDu., Du. kievit, 'plover', and
E. pewit, which all are imitative.

## kiblah
kiblah, п., the point toward which the
Mohammedans turn in prayer (i.e. the Kaaba in
Mecca). — Arab, qib/a", 'direction to which
Mohammedans turn in prayer', fr. qabila, 'he
lay opposite, was in front of. See cabal and
с p. Kabyle.

## kibosh
kibosh, п., in the phrase to put the kibosh on, 'to
put an end to'. — Of unknown origin.

## kick
kick, intr. and tr. v., to strike with the foot. —
ME. kiken, of unknown origin. Cp. kicksies.
Derivatives: kick, п., a blow with the foot,
kick-er, n.

## kickshaw
kickshaw, kickshaws, п., fancy dish; delicacy. —
Corrupted fr. F. quelque chose, 'something', fr.
quelque, 'some', and chose, 'thing'. F. quelque
is compounded of quel (fr. L. qualis), 'of what
kind or nature', and que (fr. L. quod), 'what';
see quality and quod. F. chose derives fr. L.
causa; see cause, n.

## kicksies
kicksies, n. pi., trousers (slang). — Fr. kick, 'to
strike with the foot'.

## kid
kid, п., ι) a young goat; 2) (slang) a chM. — ME.
kid, kidde, fr. ON. Ш (whence also Dan., Swed.
kid), 'a kid', rel. to OHG. kizzi, chizzi, MHG.,
G. kitze, 'kid'; of imitative origin. Cp. next
word and the first element in kidnap.
Derivative: kid, intr. v., to bring forth young
(said of goats).

## kid
kid, tr. v., to hoax, humbug. — Prob. fr. kid,
'a young goat', and lit. meaning, 'to make a
kid of.
Derivative: kid, п., a hoax.

## kid
kid, п., a small tub. — Prob. a var. of kit, 'tub'.

## Kidderminster
Kidderminster, п., a kind of carpet. — Prop, 'a
.carpet made at Kidderminster'; so called after
the town Kidderminster in England.

## kiddle
kiddle, п., a barrier with nets, used for catching
fish. — ME. kydle, fr. OF. quidel, guidel (F.
guideau), of uncertain origin.

## kiddush
kiddush, п., proclamation of the holiness of the
sabbath or a festival, by saying the benediction
over wine (or over two loaves) and over the
sabbath, resp. the festival (Jewish ritual). —
Mishnaic Heb. qiddash, 'sanctification', prop.
verbal noun of Heb. qiddish, 'he hallowed,
sanctified'. See Kednshah and cp. words there
referred to.

<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: KIDDUSKIN | 402 -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:429 COLUMN:1 -->

## kiddushin
kiddushin, η. pi., ι) Jewish betrothal; 2) (cap.)
a Mishnaic and Talmudic treatise dealing with
betrothal and marriage. — Mishnaic Heb. Qid-
dushtn, prop. pi. of qiddush, 'sanctification'. See
prec. word.

## kiddy
kiddy, η., ι) a young goat; 2) a little child (slang).
— Formed with suff. -y fr. kid, 'a young goat'.

## kidnap
kidnap, tr. v. — Compounded of kid, 'a young
goat', used in the sense of 'child', and nap, dial,
form of nab, 'to seize, catch, steal'.
Derivatives: kidnapp-er, п., kidnapp-ing, n.

## kidney
kidney, n. — ME. kidenei, which stands for
kiden-ei. The first element is unknown. The
second element is identical with ME. ei, 'egg'.
See egg.

## kief
kief, n. — See keg.

## kieselguhr
kieselguhr, п., a fine siliceous powder used as an
absorbent. — G. (now spelled Kieselgur),
compounded of Kiesel, 'flint' (see chesil) and Guhr
(Gur), 'earthy deposit', lit. 'fermentation', from
the stem of garen, 'to ferment'. See chesil and
guhr.

## kieserite
kieserite, п., a hydrous magnesium sulfate
(mineral) — G. Kieserii, named after Dietrich G.
Kieser, president of the Academy of Jena (died
in 1862). For the ending -it, which goes back to
Gk. -ίτης, see subst. suff. -ite.

## kiki
kiki, п., the castor-oil plant. — Fr. Egypt.,
whence also Akkad. kukkanita, Heb. qiqayon.

## kikumon
kikumon, п., Japanese imperial emblem,
representing an open chrysanthemum. — Jap.,
compounded of kiku, 'chrysanthemum', and
топ, 'crest'. Cp. the se'cond element in kirimon.

## kii-
kii-, the first element in many Celtic place names,
meaning 'cell, church, burial place'. — Gael,
and Ir. -cil, fr. cill, a gradational variant of
ceall, 'cell, church, burial place', fr. L. cella.
See cell.

## kilerg
kilerg, a physical unit of work, equal to 1000
ergs. — See kilo- and erg.

## kilderkin
kilderkin, п., l) a cask; 2) an old English liquid
measure. — ME., dissimilated fr. MDu. kin-
derkin (also kindeken), a dimin. formed with
suff. -kin, fr. OF. quintal, 'quintal,
hundredweight'. See quintal.

## kill
kill, tr. and intr. v. — ME. killen, fr. earlier
cutten, prob. rel. to ME. quellen, 'to kill, strike',
fr. OE. cwellan, of s.m., causative of cwetan, 'to
die'. See quell and cp. qualm.
Derivatives: kill, п., kill-er, п., kill-ing, adj.
and n.

## killadar
killadar, п., commandant of a fortress (India). —
A hybrid coined fr. Arab. qal'a", 'fortress', and
Pers. suff. -dar, 'holder, possessor'. For the
etymology and force of this suff. see aumildar and
cp. words there referred to.

## kiln
kiln, п., a large oven. — ME. kilne, kulne, fr. OE.
cylene, cylne, fr. L. cutina, 'kitchen'. See
culinary.

## kilo-
kilo-, combining form meaning 'one thousand'.
— F. kilo-, fr. Gk. χίλιοι (Ion. χείλιοι), 'a
"thousand', which is of uncertain origin. It is
perh. cogn. with L. mille, 'a thousand'; see
mille.

## kilo
kilo, п., a kilogram. — F., short for kilogramme.
See next word.

## kilogram
kilogram, kilogramme, n. — F. kilogramme, lit.
'one thousand grams', coined fr. kilo- and gram,
'the metric unit of weight'.

## kiloliter
kiloliter, kilolitre, n. — F. kilolitre, lit. 'one
thousand liters', coined fr. kilo- and liter,

## kilometer
kilometer, kilometre, n. — F. kilometre, lit. 'one
thousand meters', coined fr. kilo- and Gk.
μέτρον, 'measure'. See -meter.
Derivatives: kilometr-ic, kilometr-ic-al, adjs.

## kilowatt
kilowatt, n. (electr.) — Lit. 'one thousand watts',
coined fr. kilo- and watt,

## kilt
kilt, tr. v., to tuck up. — Of Scand. origin; cp.
Dan. kilte, Swed. kilta, 'to tuck up', ON.
kilting, 'shirt'.
Derivatives: kilt, п., kilt-ed, adj., kilt-ing, n.

## kilter
kilter, kelter, п., good condition (colloq.) — Of
uncertain origin.

## kimberlite
kimberlite, n„ a peridotite often containing
diamonds (petrogr.) — Named after Kimbertey in
S. Africa, where it occurs. For the ending see
subst. suff. -ite.

## kimono
kimono, п., a long, loose Japanese garment. —

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:429 COLUMN:2 -->
Jap., lit. a thing (mono) put on (ki).

## kin
kin, п., family, relationship. — ME. kin, кип, fr.
OE. cynn, 'kind, kin, race, species, family', rel.
to UE. cennan, 'to beget', to bear', ON. kyn,
OHG. chunni, MHG. kiinne, Goth, kuni, 'family,
race', ON. kundr, 'son', OS., OHG., MHG., G.
kind, 'child', fr. Teut. base *ken-, corresponding
to I.-E. *gen, 'to beget, bear, bring forth',
whence OI. janati, 'begets', janah, 'race', Gk.
γίγνεσθαι (for γί-γνε-σ&αι), 'to become,
happen', γένεσις, 'origin, source, birth, race
descent', L. genus, 'birth, descent, origin, race,
sort, kind, class'. See genus and words there
referred to and cp. esp. kinchin, kind, п., kind,
adj., kindred, king. Cp. also the first element in
kindergarten.
Derivative: kin-ship, n.

## kin-
kin-, form of kino- before a vowel.

## -kin
-kin, dimin. suff. as in kilderkin, lambkin, manni-
kin. — ME. -kin, fr. MDu. -kin, -kijn, prop, a
double dimin. suff. formed from the dimin.
suffixes -k and dimin. -in; cp. OS. -kin, MHG.
-kin, G. -chen.

## kinah
kinah, п., an elegy, a dirge (Hebrew poetry). —
Heb. qina", 'elegy, dirge' (whence qinin, 'he
chanted a kinah'), rel. to Syr. qintd, 'elegy',
qaynah, 'slave girl who is a singer', Ethiop.
qene, 'song' (with reduplication, Syr. qanqen,
'he sang', Jewish-Aram, qunqannithd, 'musical
instrument'), fr. Sem. stem q-y-n, 'to fit to-,
gether, fabricate', whence also Arab, qana, 'he
fabricated, forged', qayn, 'craftsman, worker in
steel or another metal, smith', Aram, qena'a,
Syriac qenaya, Akkad. qinai, 'metal worker'.
For sense development cp. Gk. ποιητής, 'poet',
lit. 'a maker', fr. ποιεϊν, 'to make, produce'.
Cp. Cain, Elkanah.

## kinchin
kinchin, п., child. — Corrupted fr. G. Kindchen,
'little child', dimin. of Kind, 'child', which is rel.
to ON. kundr, 'son'. See kin and -kin.

## kincob
kincob, п., a kind of East Indian brocade. —
Hind, kimkhab, fr. Pers. kimkhab.

## kind
kind, n. — ME. kinde, kund, kende, fr. OE. cynd,
ge-cynd, 'kind, nature, quality, manner, origin,
generation, offspring', rel. to OE. суп, 'kind,
kin'. See kin and cp. kind, adj.

## kind
kind, adj. — ME. kinde, kynde, kande, fr. OE.
cynde, ge-cynde, 'innate, natural', lit. 'according
to nature', fr. cynd, ge-cynd. See kind, n.
Derivatives: kindly, kindness (qq.v.)

## kindergarten
kindergarten, n. — G. Kindergarten, lit. 'garden
of children', coined by the German educator
Friedrich Frobel (1782-1852)^ 1840 fr. Kinder,
pi. of Kind, 'child', and Garten, 'garden'. For the
first element see kin, for the second see garden.
Derivatives: kindergarten-er, n. (cp. G. Kinder-
gartner), kindergarten-ing, n.

## kindhearted
kindhearted, adj. — Compounded of kind, adj.,
and -hearted (see heart and 3rd -ed); first used
by Miles Coverdale (1488-1569), English
translator of the Bible, in 1535.
Derivatives: kindhearted-ly, adv., kindhearted-
ness, n.

## kindle
kindle, tr. and intr. v. — ME. kindlen, formed fr.
ON. kynda, 'to light a fire*, with freq. suff. -le.
Derivatives: kindl-er, п., kindl-ing, n.

## kindly
kindly, adj. — ME., fr. OE. cyndelic, ge-cyndelic,
'natural', fr. cynd, ge-cynd, 'nature'. See kind,
п., and adj. suff. -ly.
Derivative: kindli-ness, n.

## kindly
kindly, adv. — ME., fr. OE. cyndetice, ge-cynde-
lice, 'naturally', fr. ge-cynde, 'natural'. See kind,
adj., and adv. suff. -ly.

## kindness
kindness, n. — ME. kindenesse, fr. kinde. See
kind, adj., and -ness.

## kindred
kindred, n. — ME. kinrede,kinreden, compounded
of kin, fr. OE. cynn, 'kind, kin, race, species,
family', and -red, fr. OE. rSden, 'rule, condition'
(fr. rxdan, 'to advise, discuss, rule, guess, read'),
used as a noun. See kin and read and cp. the
second element in hatred. The first d in kindred
is epenthetic.
Derivatives: kindred, adj., kindred-ship, n.

## kine
kine, п., archaic and poetic pi. of cow. — OE.
супа (gen. pi.), 'of cows', fr. cp, 'cows', pi. of
cu, 'cow'. See cow.

## kinema
kinema, n. — See cinema,

## kinematic
kinematic, also kinematical, adj., pertaining to

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:429 COLUMN:3 -->
kinematics. — See cinema and -ic, resp. also -al.
Derivative: kinematic-al-ly, adv.

## kinematics
kinematics, п., that branch of science which deafs
with motion. — Formed with suff. -ics fr. Gk.
κίνημα, gen. κινήματος, 'motion*, fr. κΐνεϊν. See
kinetic and cp. words there referred to.

## kinematograph
kinematograph, n. — See cinematograph.

## kinesis
kinesis, п., physical movement. — Gk. κίνησις,
'movement, motion', fr. κΐνεϊν. See next word
and cp. akinesia, diadochokinesis, hyperkinesia,
telekinesis.

## kinesthesia
kinesthesia, kinesthesis, also kinaesthaesia, kin-
aesthesis, п., the muscle sense (psychol.) —
MoiiL., compounded of Gk. κΐνεϊν, 'to move',
and αίσθησις, 'perception'. See kin- and esthetic.

## kinesthetic
kinesthetic, also kinaesthetic, adj., pertaining to
kinesthesia. — See prec. word and esthetic,

## kinetic
kinetic, adj., 1) pertaining to motion; 2) having
moving force. — Gk. κινητικός, 'putting in
motion', fr. κινητός, 'moved', verbal adj. of
κΐνεϊν, 'to move', which is rel. to κίειν, 'to go',
and cogn. with L. ciere, 'to put in motion',
citare, 'to put into quick motion'. See cite and
cp. cinema, cinerama, kinematics, kino-, Acineta.
Derivatives: kinetic-al, adj., kinetic-al-ly, adv.

## kinetics
kinetics, п., that branch of science which deals
with the action of forces in causing or changing
the motion of bodies.— See prec. word and-ics.

## kineto-
kineto-, combining form denoting motion. — Gk.
κινητό-, fr. κινητός, 'moved', verbal adj. of
κΐνεϊν, 'to move'. See kinetic.

## kinetoscope
kinetoscope, п., an instrument for producing
motion pictures. — Compounded of kineto- and
Gk. -σκόπιον, fr. σκοπεΐν, 'to look at, examine'.
See -scope.
Derivative: kinetoscop-ic, adj.

## king
king, n. — ME. kynge, fr. OE. cyning, cyng,
'king', rel. to Du. koning, OS., OHG. kuning,
kunig, ON. konungr, Dan. konge, Swed. konung,
kung, MHG. kiinic, kiinec, G. Konig; fr. Teut.
"kuninga-z, 'king', which is formed fr. *kunya-,
'kind, kin, race, species, family' and suff. -ing,
-ung; see kin and patronymic suff. -ing. OE.
cyning, etc., orig. denoted 'pertaining to a kin',
whence arose the meaning 'the first of his kin'.
Cp. the second element in erlking. Finn, kunin-
gas, 'king', and OSlav. kunegu, kunezi, 'prince',
Lith. kunigas, Lett, kungs, 'clergyman, priest',
are Teut. loan words. Cp. knez.
Derivatives: king, tr. and intr. v., king-less, adj.,
king-less-ness, п., king-like, adj. and adv.,
kingly, adj. and adv., king-li-ness, n.

## kingdom
kingdom, n. — ME., fr. OE. cyningddm, п., fr.
cyning, 'king'. See prec. word and -dom.

## kinglet
kinglet, n. — A hybrid coined fr. king and -let,
dimin. suff. of French origin.

## kink
kink, п., a twist in a rope. — Fr. Swed. or Du.
kink, 'a twist in a rope', which are rel. to ON.
kika, 'to bend at the knee', Norw. kank, 'a
twist'.
Derivatives: kink, intr. and tr. v., kink-y, adj.,
kink-i-ly, adv., kink-i-ness, n.

## kinkajou
kinkajou, п., a racoonlike animal. — F., of AI-
gonquian origin.

## kinkhost
kinkhost, п., whooping cough. — Rel. to Fris.
kinkhoast, MLG. kinkhdste, Du. kinkhoest,
'whooping cough', and to chincough (q.v.)

## kinkle
kinkle, n. — Formed fr. kink with dimin. suff. -le.
Derivatives: kinkle, tr. and intr. v., kinkl-ed, adj.

## kinnikinnic
kinnikinnic, kinnikinic, n„ mixture of dried leaves
and bark, used instead of tobacco. — A
N. American Indian word lit. meaning 'mixture'.

## kino
kino, п., gum of various tropical trees. — A
W. African native word.

## kino-
kino-, before a vowel kin-, combining form
denoting motion. — Gk. κΐνο-, κΐν-, fr. κΐνεϊν,
'to move'. See kinetic

## kinoplasm
kinoplasm, п., the active element of protoplasm.
— Compounded of kino- and Gk. πλάσμα,
'something molded'. See -plasm.

## kiosk
kiosk, also kiosqne, п., an open pavilion or sum-
merhouse; an open building used as a
newsstand. — F. kiosque, fr. Turk, kioshk, 'pavilion*,
fr. Pers. kushk, 'palace*.

## kip
kip, п., the hide of a calf or another young beast.
— Of uncertain origin.

## kip
kip, п., a lodging; a bed (slang). — Rel. to Dan.
kippe, 'a miserable inn'.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:430 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: 403 | KNEE -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:430 COLUMN:1 -->

## kipper
kipper, п., the male salmon. — ME. kypre, fr.
OE. cypera, 'a kind of salmon', prob. rel. to OS.
cupiro, of s.m., and to OE. copor, 'copper' (see
copper), and so called in allusion to the copper-
colored spots of the male salmon.
Derivative: kipper, tr. v., to cure (fish) by salting
and drying.

## kirimon
kirimon, п., the Japanese Imperial emblem
representing three leaves and three buds of the
paulownia tree. — Jap., compounded of kiri,
'the paulownia tree', and топ, 'crest'. Cp. the
second element in kikumon.

## kirk
kirk, п., a church (Northern Engl, and Scot.). —
ON. kirk/a, fr. OE. cirice, circe, 'church'. See
church and cp. kermis.

## klrsch
klrsch, п., kirschwasser. — See next word.

## kirschwasser
kirschwasser, п., an alcoholic liquor distilled from
the fermented juice of cherries. — G., lit. 'cherry
water', fr. Kirsche, 'cherry', and Wasser, 'water'.
The first element derives fr. MHG. kirse, fr.
OHG. kirsa, fr. VL. "ceresia, fr. Imperial L.
cerasium, 'cherry*; see cherry. For the second
element see water.

## kirtle
kirtle, п., I) a man's tunic; 2) a woman's skirt
{archaic or dial.) — ME. kirtel, fr. OE. cyrlel,
rel. to ON. kyrtill, 'tunic'. Both the OE. and
the ON. word are prob. formed fr. L. curtus,
'short', and the dimin. suff. -el, resp. -ill, and
orig. denoted a short garment. See curt and cp.
words there referred to. For the ending see
sufT. -el.

## Kislev
Kislev, also Kislew, п., name of the ninth Jewish
month. — Heb. kislew, fr. Akkad. kislimu, kis-
liwu. For the interchangibility of w and m in
Akkadian cp. Marheshvan.

## kismet
kismet, п., fate. — Turk, qismet, fr. Arab, qtsma!1,
'portion, lot, fate', fr. qasama, 'he divided,
distributed, apportioned', esp. 'he divided by
drawing lots at the sanctuary', whence dqsama, 'he
swore'; rel. to Ethiop. qasama, Heb. qasam,
Aram. qesam, Syr. qetzam, 'he practiced
divination', Heb. qesem, Aram, qisma, 'divination'

## kiss
kiss, tr. and intr. v. — ME. kissen, fr. OE. cyssan,
rel. to OS. kussian, ON. kyssa, OFris. kessa,
Du., OHG. kussen, MLG., MHG., G. kiissen,
'to kiss', which are denominated fr. OE. coss,
ΟΝ., OFris. koss, resp. OS., MLG., Du., OHG.
kus, 'kiss'; prob. cogn. with Gk. κυνεϊν, 'to
kiss', Hitt, kuwash-anzi, 'they kiss', OI. cum-
bati, 'he kisses'. All these words are of imitative
origin.

## kiss
kiss, n. — ME., alteration (due to the influence
of the verb kissen) of cos, fr. OE. coss. See
kiss, v.

## kist
kist, п., a chest (Northern Engl, and Scot.) —
ME. kiste, kist, fr. ON. kista, 'chest', fr. L.
cista. See chest and cp. cist.

## kist
kist, n. — The same as cist, 'a sepulchral stone
chest'.

## kistvaen
kistvaen, п., a stone coffin. — W. cistfaen, lit. 'a
stone chest'. See cistvaen.

## kit
kit, п., a wooden tub, tankard. — MDu'. kitte
(Du. kit), rel. to Norw. kitte, 'bin'. Cp. kid,
!a small tub', and caboodle.

## kit
kit, п., a small fiddle used formerly by dancing
teachers. — Abbreviation of OE. cythere, fr.
L. cithara, 'lute', fr. Gk. κιθάρα. See cither.

## kit
kit, n. — Abbreviation of kitten.

## kitab
kitab, n„ a book; esp. the Koran or the Bible
(Mohammedanism). — Arab, kitab, 'book', lit.
'a writing', fr. Aram, k'thabh, 'a writing', fr.
k'thabh, 'he wrote' (whence Arab, kataba, 'he
wrote'). See ketubah and cp. words there
referred to.

## Kit-cat
Kit-cat, adj., 1) designating a club founded by
Whig politicians in London in 1703; so called
from Christopher (Kit) Caf(ling), keeper of the
tavern in which the club first met; 2) designating
a particular size of portrait which is less than
half-length; said to have been so called because
the room in which the portraits of the members
of the Kit-cat Club were to be hung was too
low for half-length pictures.
Derivatives: Kit-cat, n. 1) the Kit-cat Club; 2) a
Kit-cat portrait.

## kitchen
kitchen, n. — ME. kuchene, kichene, kichen, fr.
OE. cycerte, fr. L. cucina [whence also It. cucina,
OProvenc. cozina, F. cuisine, Sp. cocina, and

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:430 COLUMN:2 -->
MDu. cokene (Du. keukeri), OHG. chuhhina
(MHG. kitchen, kUche, G. Kiiche), Dan. kjek-
ken], dissimilated var. of L. coquina, 'kitchen',
fr. coquere, 'to cook'. See cook and cp. cuisine.
Derivatives: kitchen, tr. v., kitchen-er, п.,
kitchenette (q.v.)

## kitchenette
kitchenette, n. — A hybrid coined fr. kitchen
with -ette, a suff. of French origin.

## kitchen midden
kitchen midden, refuse marking a primitive
human settlement, — Dan. kjekken madding, lit.
'kitchen midden'. See kitchen and midden.

## kichery
kichery, n. — A variant of kedgeree.

## kite
kite, n. — ME. kite, fr. OE. cpta, 'kite, bittern',
rel. to ciegan (for orig. *kau]an), 'to call', MHG.
(stein-)kuze, G. Kauz, 'screech owl', MLG.
kuten, 'to chatter, babble, prate', LG. koter
(whence G. Koter), 'cur, dog', fr. I.-E. base
*gou-, "gow-, 'to shout, cry', whence also OI.
gavate, 'sounds, resounds', Gk. γοαν, 'to wail,
groan, weep', γόος, 'wailing, groaning, weeping',
OE. cyme, 'fine, beautiful, splendid', orig. 'frail,
delicate, tender'. See comely.

## kith
kith, п., now used only in the phrase kith and kin.
— ME. cuththe, kith, fr. OE. судд\и)-,
'knowledge, acquaintance, relationship; native
country', fr. cud, 'known', pp. of cunnan, 'to know'.
See can, aux. v., and cp. uncouth.

## kitting
kitting, п., a small kitten. — ME., fr. ON. ket-
lingr, 'kitten; young of other animals', dimin.
of kottr, 'cat'. See cat and dimin. suff. -ling.
kitte], п., a white cotton robe which pious Jews
wear during the High Holiday services, and in
which they are buried. — Yiddish kite/, fr. G.
Kittel, 'frock, coat', fr. MHG. kittel, kitel, ult.
fr. Arab, qutn, 'cotton', whence also G. Kattun,
'cotton'; see cotton. For the ending -el in kittel
see the suffixes -el and -le.

## kitten
kitten, n. — ME. kitoun, a blend of killing and
ONF. caton (corresponding to OF., F. chaton),
'little cat', dimin. of ONF. cat (corresponding
to OF., F. chat), 'cat'. See cat and cp. kittle, 'to
bring forth kittens', kitty, 'kitten'.
Derivatives: kitten, intr. v., kitten-ish, adj.,
kitten-ish-ly, adv., kitten-ish-ness, n.

## kittiwake
kittiwake, п., seagull of the genus Rissa. —
Imitative of its cry.

## kittle
kittle, tr. v., to tickle. — ME. kytyllen, fr. MDu.
(= Du.) kietelen; rel. to ON. kitla, OHG. kiz-
zildn, kuzzildn, MHG., G. kitzeln, 'to tickle'.
Cp. tickle, which is a metathesis var. of kittle.

## kittle
kittle, intr. v., to bring forth kittens (obsol.) —
Prob. back formation fr. kitting.

## kitty
kitty, п., a pet name for a kitten. — Formed fr.
kit, 'kitten', with dimin. suff. -y.

## kitty
kitty, п., a prison or jail (Northern Engl, or slang).
— Of uncertain origin.

## kiwi
kiwi, п., a flightless bird of New Zealand; ap-
teryx. — Maori, of imitative origin.

## klaprothite
klaprothite, п., a synonym of lazulite (mineral.) —
Named after the German mineralogist Martin
Heinrich Klaproth (1743-1817). For the ending
see subt. suff. -ite.

## klaprotholite
klaprotholite, п., a copper bismuth sulfide
(mineral.) — See prec. word and -lite.

## Klaxon
Klaxon, п., a trade mark for motor horns. —
Coined from the stem of Gk. κλάζω (fut.
κλάγξω), Ί shout aloud, scream', which is cogn.
with L. clangere, 'to resound'. See clang.

## kleeneboc
kleeneboc, п., a small kind of antelope (Antilope
perpusilla). — S. African Du. kleinbok, lit.
'little buck', fr. Du. klein, 'small', and bok, 'buck'.
See clean and buck.

## kleisto-
kleisto-, combining form. — See cleisto-.

## klepht
klepht, п., one of a group of Greeks who after
the conquest of Greece by the Turks formed
communities of partisans; a brigand. — Mod.
Gk. κλέφτης, corresponding to Gk. κλέπτης^
'thief, robber', from the stem of κλέπτειν, 'to
steal', whence—with vowel gradation—κλοπή,
'theft', κλοπές and κλώψ, 'thief; cogn. with L.
clepere, 'to steal', Goth, hlifan, 'to steal', hliftus,
'thief, Mir. cluain, 'deception, flattery', cluai-
nech, 'deceptive'. Cp. klepto-, kleptomania,
clepsydra.
Derivatives: klepht-ic, adj., klepht-ism, n.

## klepto-
klepto-, combining form meaning 'theft' or
'thief. — Gk. κλεπτο-, fr. κλέπτης. See klepht.

## kleptomania
kleptomania, п., an uncontrollable propensity to

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:430 COLUMN:3 -->
steal (med.) — Medical L., coined fr. klepto-
and Gk. μανία, 'madness, frenzy'. See mania.
Derivative: kleptomani-ac, n. and adj.

## klino-
klino-, combining form. — See clino-.

## klippe
klippe, п., a thrust mass of strata, an outlier
(geol.) — G. Klippe, 'cliff, crag, steep rock', fr.
MHG. klippe, fr. MDu. klippe (Du. klip), which
is rel. to OHG. klep, OE. clif. See cliff.

## klipspringer
klipspringer, п., a small African antelope. -—S.
Afr. Du., lit. 'cliff-springer', fr. Du. klip, 'cliff,
rock' and springer, 'leaper, springer'. See cliff
and spring, v.

## kloof
kloof, п., a deep gorge, ravine. — S. Afr. Du.,
fr. MDu. clove, 'cleft', which stands in gradatio-
nal relationship to OE. cleofian, clifian, 'to stick,
adhere'. See cleave, 'to stick, adhere'.

## knack
knack, tr. v. and n. — Of imitative origin. Cp.
Dan. knage, Swed., Norw. knaka, MHG., G.
knacken, 'to crack', and E. knock, which all are
imitative.

## knacker
knacker, п., one who buys or slaughters worn
out horses. — Of uncertain, possibly Scand.,
origin. Cp. Icel. hnakkur, 'saddle', which is rel.
to ON. hnakki, hnakkr, 'nape of the neck', and
to OE. hnecca, 'nape of the neck'. See 1st neck
and agential suff. -er.
Derivative: knacker-y, n.

## knag
knag, п., a knot in wood. — ME. knagge; cp.
Swed. knagg, 'knot in wood', LG. knagge
(whence G. Knagge), of s.m., Dan. knag, 'hook
to hang clothes on'. These words prob. derive
fr. I.-E. *gnegh-, enlargement of base *gen-,
'pressed together'. Cp. knight.
Derivative: knagg-y, adj.

## knap
knap, п., the crest of a hill. — ME., fr. OE. стер,
спверр, 'top, mountain top, knob, button', rel.
to LG. knap, 'summit, top', ON. knappr, 'knob,
button', and to E. kaob, knop.

## knap
knap, tr. v., to snap; to strike with a sharp sound
(obsol.) — Of imitative origin. Cp. MDu. cnap-
pen, Du. and G. knappen, 'to crack'.
Derivative: knapp-er, n.

## knapsack
knapsack, n. — Du. knapzak, compounded of
knappen, 'to crack, snap; to crunch, eat', and
zak, 'bag, sack'. See knap, v. and sack, 'bag'.
Derivatives: knapsack-ed, adj., knapsack-ing, n.

## knapweed
knapweed, n. ~- ME. knopwed, fr. knop, 'knop',
and wed, 'weed'. See knop and weed.

## knar
knar, п., a knot in wood. — ME. knarre; rel. to
MHG. gnarren, knarren, G. knarren, 'to creak,
rattle', and to E. gnarl (q.v.) Cp. knur, knurl.

## knave
knave, п., ι) a boy, a servant (archaic); 2) a rascal;
3) a playing card; the jack. — ME. knaue
(= knave), 'boy, servant, knave', fr. OE. cnafa,
'boy, youth, servant', rel. to OHG. knabo, 'boy,
youth, servant', MHG., G. knabe, 'boy, lad',
and to OE. cnapa, 'boy, youth, servant', ON.
knapi, 'servant boy', MLG. knape, ODu. knapcr,
MDu. knape, Du. knaap, 'a youth, servant',
OHG. knappo, MHG. knappe, 'a young squire',
G. Knappe, 'squire, shieldbearer, attendant'. The
orig. meaning of these words prob. was 'stick,

## peg
peg, piece of wood'; cp. dial. G. Knabe and dial.
Swed. knabb,'knappe, 'peg', ON. knefill,
'crossbar', MLG. knevel, OHG. knebil, MHG., G.

## knebel
knebel, 'peg, short piece of wood, crossbar'. See

## Kluge-Mitzka
Kluge-Mitzka, EWDS., p. 379 s.v. Knabe.
Derivatives: knav-ery, a., knav-ish, adj., knav-

## ish-ly
ish-ly, adv., knav-ish-ness, n.

## knead
knead, tr. v. — ME. kneden, fr. OE. cnedan, rel.

## to OS. knedan
to OS. knedan, MDu. cneden, Du. kneden, OHG.

## knetan
knetan, MHG., G. kneten, ON. knoda, Swed.

## knada
knada, 'to knead', and cogn. with OSlav. gnedg,

## gnesli
gnesli, 'to crush, squeeze', OPruss. gnode, 'a
trough for kneading bread'.
Derivatives: knead-er, п., knead-ing, adj., knead-

## ing-ly
ing-ly, adv.

## knee
knee, n. — ME. kne, knee, fr. OE. cneo, cneow,

## rel. to OS. kneo
rel. to OS. kneo, knio, ON. kne, OFris. kni, kne,

## MDu. cnie
MDu. cnie, Du. knie, OHG. kniu, MHG., G.

## knie
knie, Goth, kniu, and cogn. with OI. jam, Avestic

## znum (ace.)
znum (ace.), Toch. A kanwem (dual), В kenine,

## Hitt. genu
Hitt. genu, 'knee', Arm. cun-r, pi. cunk-k', Gk.
γόνυ, gen. γόνατος (for *γόν5ατος), 'knee', γωνία
(for *γωνίίϊ), 'corner, angle', γνύξ, 'on the

## knees'
knees', γνύ-πετας, 'falling on the knees', L.

## genu
genu, 'knee'. Cp. genual, genuflect, gonio-,
diagonal.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:431 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: KNEEL | 404 -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:431 COLUMN:1 -->
Derivatives: knee, tr. and intr. v., knee-d, adj.,
kneel (q.v.)

## kneel
kneel, intr. v. — ME. knelen, fr. OE. cneowtian,
fr. спёо, 'knee'; rel. to MLG. knelen, MDu.
cnielen, Du. knielen, 'to kneel'. See knee.
Derivatives: kneel-er, п., kneel-ing, adj., kneel-
ing-ly, adv.

## kneelet
kneelet, п., a covering for the knee. — A hybrid
coined fr. knee and -let, a suff. of French origin.

## knelppism
knelppism, п., system of hydrotherapy introduced
by Sebastian Kneipp, a German priest (1821-97).
— G. Kneippismus. For the ending see suff.
-ism.

## knell
knell, intr. and tr. v. — ME. knyllen, knellen, fr.
OE. cnyllan, 'to sound the bell, to ring', of
imitative origin. Cp. MHG. erknellen, 'to resound',
whence, with back formation, G. Knall, 'sharp
report, detonation', knallen, 'to explode,
detonate'.

## knell
knell, n. — ME. knell, fr. OE. cnytt, fr. cnyllan.
See knell, v.

## knelt
knelt, past tense and pp. of kaeel,

## Kneseth
Kneseth, n„ the Israeli Parliament. — Mishnaic
Heb. k'neseth, 'gathering, assembly' (cp. beth
k'neseth, 'synagogue' lit. 'house of assembly'),
from the stem of Heb. kanas, 'he gathered,
assembled, collected', which is rel. to Aram.
k'nash, 'he gathered, assembled, collected'
(whence be k'nishtd, 'synagogue', lit. 'house of
assembly').

## knew
knew, past tense of know. — ME. knew, fr. OE.
cneow, 'he knew', past tense of cnawan. See
know.

## knez
knez, kniaz, п., a Slavonic title. — Russ. knyaz',
'prince', fr. OSlav. kunegu, kunezi, of s.m., of
Teut. origin. Cp. OHG., OS. kuning, kunig,
'king', and see king.

## Knickerbocker
Knickerbocker, п., a descendant of the Dutch
settlers of New York; a New Yorker. — From
Diedrich Knickerbocker, the pretended author
of Washington Irving's History of New York.
The name Knickerbocker is formed fr. Du.
knikker, 'marble' (fr. imitative knikken, 'to
crack, click'), and bocker, 'baker', hence it lit.
means 'baker of marble'.

## knickerbockers
knickerbockers, n. pi., loose, short breeches. —
Fr. prec. word.

## knickers
knickers, n. pi., bloomers (vulgar). —
Abbreviation of prec. word.

## knickknack
knickknack, п., triHe, toy. — Antiphonic
reduplication of knack.
Derivatives: knickknack-ed, adj., knickknack-
ery, п., knickknack-y, adj.

## knife
knife, n. — ME. knif, Гг. OE. cnif prob. fr. ON
knifr, which is rel. to MLG. knif, MDu. cnijf,
Du. kntjf, G. Kneif, Kneip, 'knife', MLG.
knipen, G. kneifen, 'to pinch, to nip', and prob.
cogn. with Lith. gnybiu, Ί pinch, I nip', gnybis,
'a pinching, nipping'. F. canif, 'penknife', is
borrowed fr. OE. or fr. ON.
Derivative: knife, tr. v.

## knight
knight, n. — ME., 'boy, youth, knight', fr. OE.
cniht, 'boy, youth, attendant, servant, retainer',
rel. to OFris. kniucht, MLG., MDu., Du. knecht,
OS., OHG., MHG. knehl, 'boy, youth, lad,
man, hero', G. Knecht, 'servant, bondman,
vassal'; of uncertain origin; perhaps rel. to
Swed. knagg, 'knot in wood', dialectally used
also in the sense of 'a thickset man'. Ср. Е.
knag and see Kluge-Mitzka, EWDS., pp. 380-81
s.v. Knecht. Cp. also the second element in
lansquenet.
Derivatives: knight, tr. v., knight-hood, п.,
knight-ly, adj. and adv., knight-i-ness, n.

## knit
knit, tr. v. — ME. knitten, fr. OE. cnyttan, 'to
tie, knot', rel. to ON. knytja, MLG. kniitten,
'to tie, knot', and to OE. cnotta, 'a knot'. Cp.
knot.
Derivatives: knit, п., knitt-er, п., knitt-ing, n,

## knob
knob, n. — ME., rel. to LG. knobbe, 'knob', and
to E. knap, 'crest of a hill', knop, knub, nub.
Derivatives: knobb-y, adj., knobb-i-ness, n.

## knobkerrie
knobkerrie, п., a short Kaffir club used as a
weapon. — S. Afr. Du. knopkierie, a hybrid coined
fr. Du. кпоЬфе), 'knob' (see knop), and
Hottentot kirrie, 'stick, club'.

## knock
knock, tr. and intr. v. — ME. knokken, fr. OE.
cnucian, cnocian, of imitative origin. Cp. ON.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:431 COLUMN:2 -->
knoka, 'to knock', which is also imitative.
Derivatives: knock, п., knock-er, n.

## knoll
knoll, п., top of a small hill. — ME. knot, fr. OE.
cnoll, 'bill top, hill', rel. to ON. knollr, 'hilltop',
MLG., MHG., G. knolle, 'clod, glebe, lump',
Du. knot, 'turnip', and to OHG. nollo, Du. no],
'a hill'.
Derivative: knoll-y, adj.

## knoll
knoll, tr. and intr. v., to knell, ring. — A blend
of knell and toll.
Derivative: knoll, п., knell.

## knop
knop, п., a knob. — ME. knop, knoppe, fr. OE.
cnoppa, rel. to MLG. knoppe, MDu. cnoppe,
Du. knop, knoppe, 'knob, bud', OHG., MHG.
knopf 'knotty excrescence, bud, knob, knot',
G. Knopf, 'button, knob, top, pommel', Swed.
knopp, Dan. knop, 'knob, bud', and to E. knap,
knob. Cp. the first element in knobkerrie.

## knopite
knopite, п., a mineral intermediate between pe-
rovskite and dysanalyte. — G. Knopit, named
after Professor Adolf Knop of Karslruhe,
Germany (died in 1893). The ending -it goes back
to Gk. -ίτης; see subst. suff. -ite.

## knot
knot, п., bow, tie. — ME. knot, knotte, fr. OE.
cnotta, rel. to OE. cnyttan, 'to knit', and to Du.
knot, OHG. knoto, knodo, MHG. knote, knode,
G. Knoten, ON. knutr, Swed. knut, Dan. knude,
'knot'. Cp. knit, knout. Cp. also queaelle.
Derivatives: knot, tr. v., knott-ed, adj., knott-er,
п., knott-ing, п., knolt-y, adj., knott-i-ness, n.

## knot
knot, п., a variety of the sandpiper. — Of
unknown origin.

## knout
knout, п., a leather whip. — Russ. knut, lit.
'knotted whip', of Scand. origin. Cp. ON.
knutr, Swed. knut, 'knot', and see knot, 'bow,
tie'.

## know
know, tr. and intr. v. — ME. knawen, knowen,
fr. OE. cnawan, rel. to OHG. Ы-chnaan, ir-
chnaan, 'to know', Goth, kannjan, 'to make
known', OE. cunnan, 'to know', cennan, 'to
make known, declare, attest', fr. I.-E. base
*gene-, *geno-, 'to know'. See can, aux. v., and
words there referred to and cp. esp. keen, adj.,
ken, 'to know', ken, 'range of sight'.
Derivatives: know, a., know-er, п., know-ing,
adj., know-ing-ly, adv., know-able, adj., know-
abil-ity, п., know-able-ness, n.

## knowledge
knowledge, n. — ME. knawleche, knoweleche,
knowlege, fr. knawlechen, knowlechen, 'to
acknowledge', fr. knawen, knowen, Ίο know'
(see prec. word), and the suff. -ledge, which
prob. derives fr. Swed. -leek a suff. rel. to E.
-lock in wedlock (q.v.) Cp. acknowledge.
Derivatives: knowledge-able, adj., knowledge-
abil-ily, п., knowledge-able-ness, п., knowledge-
abl-y, adv.

## known
known, pp. of know.

## knnb
knnb, п., a protuberance. — Prob. fr. LG. knub-
be, 'knob, protuberance', fr. MLG. knubbe, of
s.m., which is rel. to E. knob, nub.

## knuckle
knuckle, n. — ME. knokel, knokil, knokyl, rel. to
MLG. knokel, MDu. cnockel, Du. kneukel,
MHG. kndchel, kniichel, G. Knochel, 'knuckle'.
All these words lit. mean 'little bone'; they are
formed fr. MLG. knoke, resp. MDu. cnoke, Du.
knok, MHG. knoche, G. Knochen, 'bone', with
the dimin. suff. -ie.
Derivatives: knuckle, v., knuckl-ed, adj., knuckl-
У, adj.

## knur
knur, п., a knotty excrescence. — ME. knorre,
rel. to MLG., MHG. knorre, G. Knorren, 'a
knotty excrescence'. Cp. knar, knurl, gnarl.

## knurl
knurl, п., a small knotty excrescence. — Related
to prec. word.
Derivatives: knurl, tr. v., knurl-ed, adj.,
knurling, n.

## koa
koa, п., the Hawaiian acacia (.Acacia koa). —
Native name.

## koala
koala, п., a small Australian marsupial (Phasco-
larctus cineteus). — Native name.

## kob
kob, п., any of various African antelopes. —
Native name.

## koban
koban, kobang, п., an obsolete Japanese coin. —
Jap. ko-ban, fr. ко, 'small', and ban, 'division'.

## kobellite
kobellite, п., a lead bismuth antimony sulfide
(mineral.) — Named after the German
mineralogist Franz von Kobell (1803-82). For the
ending see subst. suff. -ite.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:431 COLUMN:3 -->

## kobold
kobold, n. — MHG. kobolt (also kobolt), fr. ML.
cobalus, fr. Gk. χόβϊλος, 'a malicious sprite'.
The ending of Gk. κόβ-δλος, resp. ML.
cobalus was mistaken for a suff. and confused with
MHG. suff. -alt, -olt (cp. MHG. heralt, herolt
and see herald). See cobalt and goblin.

## Kodak
Kodak, n. — Trade name coined by the American
inventor George Eastman (1854-1932) about
1890.
Derivatives: kodak, tr. and intr. v., kodak-er, a.

## Kodashim
Kodashim, n. pi., the fifth order of the Mishnah.
— Heb. qoddshfm, 'holy things', pi. of qodesh,
'holiness'. See Kedushshah and cp. words there
referred to.

## koel
koel, п., a cuckoo of the genus Eudynamys orien-
talis. — Hind, koel, fr. OI. kokilah, 'the Indian
cuckoo', which is of imitative origin. See
cuckoo.

## Kohelcth
Kohelcth, п., the book of Ecclesiastes. — Heb.
qdhileth, 'preacher', rel. to qahul, qlhittdh,
'assembly, congregation'. See kehillah.

## Kohen
Kohen, also Cohen, a priest (Jewish religion). —
Heb. kohen, 'a priest', from the base of kihin,
'he acted as a priest', whence also k'hunnd",
'priesthood'; rel. to Aram, kahtn, kahuna,
'priest', Arab, kahana, 'he divined, prophesied',
kahtn (properly partic. of the prec. verb), 'seer'.
Cp. Cohen.

## Koh-i-noor
Koh-i-noor, п., a famous diamond, one of the
British crown jewels. — Pers. kdh-i-пйг, lit.
'mountain of light', prop, a hybrid coined fr.
Pers. koh, 'mountain', which is rel. to Pers.
kohe, 'hump', OPers. kaufa-, 'mountain', Aves-
lic kaofa-, 'mountain, hump', and fr. Arab,
лиг, 'light' (see Menorah).

## kohl
kohl, п., powder (esp. of antimony), used by
Eastern women to darken the eyelids. — Arab.
kuhl. See alcohol.

## kohlrabi
kohlrabi, п., a kind of cabbage. — G. Kohlrabi,
fr. It. cavoli rape, pi. of cavolo rapa, lit. 'cole
rape'; influenced in form by G. Kohl, 'cabbage'.
Cp. F. chou-rave and see cole and rape, 'a plant
allied to the turnip'.

## kola
kola, п.; ι) the kola nut; 2) extract of the kola
nut. — See Cola, 'a genus of trees'.

## kolach
kolach, п., a variety of cake. — Czech koldc (rel.
to Pol. kolacz, Serbo-Croatian kolac, Church
Slavonic kolaii, etc.), lit. 'a cake resembling a
wheel', fr. kolo, 'wheel'; so called from its
original shape. See kolo.

## kola nut
kola nut, nut of the African tree called Cola
acuminata. See kola.

## kolinsky
kolinsky, п., fur of certain kinds of mink. —
Russ., lit. 'of Kola', fr. Kola, name of a district
in N.W. Russia.

## Kol Nidre
Kol Nidre, declaration made in Aramaic at the
beginning of the evening service on the eve of
Yom Kippur. — Aramaic kol nidhre, 'all vows';
so called from the opening words of the
declaration.
koio> п., a popular round dance of the Slavonic
nations. — OSlav. kolo, 'circle, wheel', cogn.
with OI. cakrdh, Gk. κύκλος, OE. hweogol,
hweol, 'wheel'. See wheel, and cp. kolach.

## konak
konak, п., a large mansion or government house
in Turkey. — Turk, qdnaq, 'inn, mansion, go-
vernmenthouse'.

## kopeck
kopeck, also copeck, kopek, п., one hundredth
part of a ruble. — Russ. kopeika, fr. kop'e,
'lance'; so called because orig. the coin
represented the czar with a lance in his hand. Russ.
kopeika is rel. to Russ. kopat', 'to dig', Lett.
kapans, 'chopper, chopping knife', and cogn.
with Gk. κοπίς, 'chopper, cleaver, billhook'.
See capon.

## kopje
kopje, п., a small hill in S. Africa. — S. African
Du., dimin. of Du. kop, 'head; hill'. See cop,
'mound, hill'.

## koph
koph, qoph, п., name of the 19th letter of the
Hebrew alphabet. — Heb. qoph, lit. 'eye of a
needle'; so called in allusion to the ancient
Hebrew form of this letter. Cp. next word.

## koppa
koppa, п., a letter of the early Greek alphabet,
corresponding to Hebrew qoph. — Gk. κόττττα,
fr. an Aramaized form of Heb. qoph. See
prec. word.

## koppite
koppite, п., a cerium mineral. — G. Koppit,
named after Professor Hermann F. M. Kopp of

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:432 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: 405 | KYRIEELEISON -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:432 COLUMN:1 -->
Heidelberg (1817-92). The ending -it goes back
to Gk. -ίτης; see subst. suff. -ite.

## kor
kor, п., a Hebrew measure, also called homer. —
Heb. kor, lit. 'a round vessel', fr. base k-r-r,
'to be round'.

## Koran
Koran, п., the sacred book of the
Mohammedans. — Arab. Qur'an, lit. 'reading', fr. qaraO,
'herecited, read aloud, read', which is prob.
borrowed fr. Aram. q'ra". 'he called, recited, read'.
See mikra and cp. karaism.
Derivative: Koran-ic, adj.

## kos
kos, п., a measure of distance in India. — Hind.
kos, fr. OI. krasah, lit. 'a call, a shout' (i.e. 'the
distance within which a man's shout can be
heard'), from the I.-E. imitative base "qer-,
*qor-, *q{-, 'to shout'. See raven and cp. words
there referred to.

## kosher
kosher, adj. — See kasher.

## Kosteletzkya
Kosteletzkya, п., a genus of plants of the family
Malvaceae (bot.) — ModL., named after the
Czech botanistVincenzFranzKosteletzky(iSo\-
87).

## koto
koto, п., a Japanese thirteen-stringed musical
instrument. — Jap.
kotow. — See kowtow.

## kotwal
kotwal, п., a police officer (East-India). — Hind,
fr. Pers. kotwal, 'seneschal, commandant of a
castle', fr. Turk, kotaul, kotawal, 'keeper of a
castle, chief of a garrison'.

## koumiss
koumiss, n. — See kumiss.

## kourbash
kourbash, n. — See kurbash.

## kouskons
kouskons, kuskus, n. — See cous-cous.

## kovil
kovil, п., a Hindu temple (Anglo-lnd.) — Tamil
кб-v-il, 'house of God', fr. ко, 'lord, heaven',
and il, 'house'.

## kowtow
kowtow, kotow, п., the act of kneeling and
knocking the forehead on the ground.a Chinese form
of salutation to a superior.—Chin.,
compounded of ко, 'knock', and tou, 'head'.
Derivative: kowtow, kotow, intr. v., to make a
kowtow.

## kraal
kraal, п., a village of S. African natives. — S.
African Du. kraal, 'village, pen, enclosure', fr.
Port, curral, 'pen for cattle', fr. correr, 'to run'.
See current, adj., and cp. corral, crawl,
'enclosure'.

## krait
krait, .п., a venomous Indian snake. — Hind.
karait.

## kraken
kraken, п., a mythical seamonster of northern
seas. — Formed fr. dial. Norw. krake and the
definite article n.

## kran
kran, п., name of a gold and a silver coin in
Persia. — Pers. qran.

## krantz
krantz, kranz, п., precipice. — S. African Du.,
fr. Du. krans, 'garland, Wreath, cornice', which
is related to G. Kranz, of s.m.; of uncertain
origin.

## krantzite
krantzite, п., a fossil resin (mineral.) — G.
Krantzit, named after A. Kraritz, a German
mineralogist of the 19th cent. The ending -it
goes back to Gk. -ίτης; see subst. suff. -ite.

## krater
krater, п., a large bowl used for mixing wine and
water (archeol.) — Gk. κρϊτήρ. See crater.

## kraurosis
kraurosis, п., shriveling of the skin due to atrophy
(med.) — Medical L., lit. 'brittle condition (of
the skin)', fr. Gk. κραϋρος, 'brittle, friable',
which is of unknown origin. For the ending see
suff. -osis.

## kraurotic
kraurotic, adj. — See prec. word and -otic.

## kremersite
kremersite, п., a hydrous chloride of potassium,
ammonium and iron (mineral.) — G. Kremersit,
named after the German chemist Peter Kremers
(born in 1827), who first analyzed it. The ending
-it goes back to Gk. -ίτης; see subst. sufT. -ite.

## Kremlin
Kremlin, kremlin, п., the citadel of a Russian city,
esp. that of Moscow. — F., fr. Russ. kreml',
'citadel', which is of Tatar origin.

## krennerite
krennerite, п., a gold silver telluride (mineral.) —
G. Krennerit, named after the Hungarian
mineralogist Joseph S.Krenner (1839-1920). The
ending -it goes back to Gk. -ίτης; see subst. sufT.
-ite.

## kreutzer
kreutzer, kreuzer, п., a former German and
Austrian coin. — G. Kreuzer, fr. MHG. kriuzer,
fr. kriuze, 'cross'; so called from the figure of a

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:432 COLUMN:2 -->
cross stamped upon it. See cross and -er.
kriegspie], п., a war game. — G. Kriegsspiel, lit.
'war game', fr. Krieg, 'war', and Spiel, 'game'.
The first element is of uncertain origin. For the
second element see spiel and cp. the second
element in bonspiel, glockenspiel.

## Krigia
Krigia, п., a genus of plants, the dwarf dandelion
(bot.) — ModL., named after David Krieg or
Krig, an 18th cent. American plant collector.
For the ending see sufT. -la.

## krimmer
krimmer, п., also crimmer, krimma, a kind of fur
made from the fleeces of lambs. — G., prop,
'fur of lambs of Crimea', fr. Krim, a Russian
name of Tatar origin (whence Crimea, the
Latinized name of the peninsula).

## kris
kris, also creese, creas, п., a short Malay dagger
with a waved blade. — Malay kris.

## Krishna
Krishna, п., the eighth avatar of Vishnu (Hindu
mythot.) — OI. Kfsnah, lit. 'the Black One',
cogn. with Church Slav, frunu, Russ. toron
(iernyj), Serbo-Croatian cm, Czech cerny,
OPruss. kirsnas, 'black', Lith. kerfas, 'black
and white, variegated'.

## Krishna ism
Krishna ism, п., the worship of Krishna.—Formed
fr. prec. word with suff. -ism.

## krona
krona, п., the monetary unit of Sweden. — Swed.
See krone.

## kroehnkite or krohnkite
kroehnkite or krohnkite, п., a hydrous copper
sodium sulfate (mineral.) — Named after
B. Krbhnke, a German mineralogist of the 19th
cent., who analyzed it. For the ending see subst.
suff. -ite.

## krone
krone, п., ι) the monetary unit of Denmark and
Norway. — Dan. and Norw. krone, rel. to Swed.
krona, G. Krone, fr. L. corona, 'crown'. See
crown.

## krone
krone, п., the former monetary unit of Austria-
Hungary. — G. Krone, fr. L. corona. See prec.
word.

## krummhorn
krummhorn, п., a curved wind instrument. — G.,
lit. 'a crooked horn', fr. krumm, 'curved,
crooked', and Horn, 'horn'. See crumple and horn and
cp. cromorne.

## krypto-
krypto-, combining form. — The same as crypto-.

## krypton
krypton, п., name of an inert gaseous element
(chem.) — ModL., lit. 'the hidden (element)', fr.
Gk. κρυπτόν, neut. of κρυπτός, 'hidden' (see
crypto-); coined by the discoverers of this
element, the Scottish chemist Sir William Ramsay
(1852-1916) and the English chemist Morris
William Travers (1872-1961) in 1898. The
element was long undiscovered, hence its name.
Cp. neon, xenon.

## Kshatriya
Kshatriya, п., a member of the Hindu military
caste. — OI. ksatriyah, fr. ksatram, 'rule,
dominion'. See check, 'sudden stop'.

## Kuba
Kuba, also kuba, п., a kind of fine rug. — Short
for Kuba rug; so called after Kuba, a town in
Azerbaijan.

## Kubera
Kubera, п., the god of wealth (Hinduism). — OI.
Kuberah, prob. meaning lit. 'the humpbacked
one*, and rel. to kubjah, kubhrah, 'crooked,
humpbacked'; prob. of Austroasiatic origin.

## kuchen
kuchen, п., a variety of German cake. — G.
Kuchen, fr. MHG. kuoche, fr. OHG. chuohho,
kuocho, rel. to MDu. koke, 'cake', and in gra-
dational relationship to ON. как a. See cake
and cp. Cockayne. Cp. also Catal. coca and
OProvenc. coco, which are Teut. loan words.

## kndos
kndos, п., fame, renown (colloq.) — Gk. κϋδος,
'glory, fame', which stands for *qudos and lit.
means 'that which is heard of. It is cogn. with
OSlav. cudo, gen. -ese (for *qeudos), 'wonder',
lit. 'that which is heard of',, fr. cujo, iuti, 'to
feel, perceive, hear'. Cp. Gk. κοέω, Ί mark,
perceive, hear', and see show.

## kudu
kudu, п., a large S. African antelope (Slrepsiceros
kudu). — Hottentot.

## Kuflc
Kuflc, Cnflc, adj., 1) pertaining to the town Kufa;
2) applied to a form of Arabic letters used at
Kufa by copyists of the Qoran. — Formed with
Kupffer (died in 1865). For the ending see subst.
suff. -ite.

## kurbash
kurbash, kourbash, п., a whip. — Turk, qyrbach
(whence also Hung, korbdcs, Czech karabai,

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:432 COLUMN:3 -->
suff. -ic fr. Kufa (fr. Arab. al-Kafa"), name of a
town on the Euphrates.

## Kuhnia
Kuhnia, п., a genus of plants of the thistle family
(bot.) — ModL., named after the American
physician and botanist Adam Kuhn (died in 1817),
who brought this plant to Linnaeus. For the
ending see suff. -ia.

## Kuklux
Kuklux, Ku-klux, Ku-Klux Klan, п., name of a
secret organization in the U.S.A. — Said to be
a corruption of Gk. κύκλος, 'circle' (see cycle).

## kukri
kukri, п., a knife with a broad curved blade. —
Hind, kukri.

## kultur
kultur, п., culture, civilization. — G. Kultur, fr.
L. cultura. See culture.

## Kulturkampf
Kulturkampf, п., the struggle between the
German government and the Roman Catholic
Church over the control of educational and
ecclesiastical appointments (1872-86). — G.,
lit. 'struggle for culture', compounded bf Kultur
(see prec word) and Kampf, 'combat, fight,
struggle', which is a loan word fr. L. campus,
'field, battlefield'. See camp.

## knmlss
knmlss, konmiss, п., fermented mare's or camel's
milk. — Russ. kumys, fr. Tatar kumiz.

## kiimmel
kiimmel, п., liqueur flavored with carawai seeds.
— G. Kiimmel, 'cumin', fr. OHG. kumil, a dis-
simil. var. of kumin, fr. OF. cumin, comin (F.
cumin), fr. L. cuminum. See cumin.

## kummerbund
kummerbund, n. — See cummerbund.

## kumquat
kumquat, also cumquat, п., a small orange (Citrus
Japonica). — Cantonese pronunciation of Chin.
kin-kii, lit. 'gold orange'.

## kuomintang
kuomintang, п., the Chinese nationalist
revolutionary party. — Chin., compounded of kuo,
'nation, nationalist', min, 'people', and tang,
'party'.

## kunkur
kunkur, п., a coarse kind of limestone (India). —
Hind, kankar, 'gravel', fr. OI. karkarab, lit.
'raw'. See cancer.

## kunzite
kunzite, п., a variety of spodumene (mineral.) —
Named after the American mineralogist and
gem expert Dr. George Frederick Kunz (1856-
1932). For the ending see subst. suff. -ite.

## kupfferite
kupfferite, п., a variety of amphibole (mineral.) —
Named afther the Russian physicist Adolph T.
G. Karbatsche), 'a whip'.

## Kursaal
Kursaal, п., public hall at a health resort, casino.
— G. Kursalon, compounded of Kur, 'cure,
medical treatment', and Salon, 'hall'. See cure,
n. and v., and salon.

## kusa
kusa, п., a grass used in Hindu ceremonies. —
Hind, kusa, fr. OI. kuSdh, 'grass; sacred grass',
which is of uncertain origin. It is possibly rel.
to OI. kusumam, 'flower', kusumbhah, 'saf-
flower'. Cp. next word.

## kusum
kusum, п., the safflower (India). — Hind., fr. OI.
kusumbhah. See prec. word.

## kvass
kvass, п., a Russian fermented drink made from
rye or barley. — Russ. kvas, fr. OSlav. kva.su,
'yeast', which is cogn. with L. caseus, 'cheese'.
See cheese, 'milk curd'.

## kyanize
kyanize, tr. v., to preserve wood from decay by
impregnating it with corrosive sublimate. —
Formed with suff. -ize from the name of John
H. Kyan (1774-1850), who invented this process
in 1832.

## kyle
kyle, п., a strait, a narrow channel. — Gael. caol.

## kymatology
kymatology, п., the science of waves. —
Compounded of Gk. κϋμα, gen. κοματος, 'wave', and
-λογίϊ, fr. -λόγος, 'one who speaks (in a certain
manner); one who deals (with a certain topic)'.
See cyma and -logy.

## kymograph
kymograph, n. — See cymograph.
Derivative: kymograph-ic, adj.

## kyphosis
kyphosis, п., backward curvature of the spine
(med.) — Medical L., formed fr. Gk. κϋφός,
'bent, crooked, Йитр-backed' (see cyphella),
with suff. -osis.

## Kyrie eleison
Kyrie eleison, a brief petition used in various
offices of the Eastern and Roman Churches. —
Gk. K4pi£ έλέησον, 'Lord, have mercy'. Κόριε
is voc. of κύριος, 'lord, master'; see church.
Gk. έλέησον is aorist imper. of ελέω, Ί have
pity on, show mercy to', fr. έλεος, 'pity, mercy';
see alms.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:433 -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:433 COLUMN:1 -->

## la
la, interj. — Imitative. Cp. the interjection law.

## la
la, п., a syllable used in solmization to denote the
sixth tone of the diatonic scale (mus.)

## laager
laager, п., a temporary camp. — S. Afr. Da, rel.
to Du. leger, G. Lager, 'camp'. See lair and cp.
lager, leaguer, 'camp'.
Derivative: laager, intr. v.

## labarum
labarum, п., the military standard of the late
