παιδευτικός, 'pertaining to teaching', fr. παιδευτός,
verbal adj. of παιδεύειν, 'to teach', fr. παΐς,
gen. παιδός, 'child*, See pedo- and cp. words
there referred to. For the ending see suff. -ics.

## paidology
paidology, п., the study of the child. —
Compounded of Gk. παις, gen. παιδός, 'child', and
-λογία, fr. -λόγος, 'one who speaks (in a

topic)'. See pedo-, 'boy, child', and -logy.
Derivatives: paidolog-ic-al, adj., paidolog-ist, n.

## pall

gelia, 'a measure', fr. L. pdgella, 'column', dim.

palavah, 'chaff', OSlav. pleva, Russ. pe/eva,
Lith. pelus (pi.), Lett, pelus, pelavas (pi.),

is a Slavonic loan word), Gk. έπ£-πλο(5)ος,
'omentum', and prob also with L. pellis (for
*pel-nis), 'skin', for which see pellicle. Cp.
pallet, 'mattress',

## paillette
paillette, п., 1) a piece of metal used in enamel

Derivative: paillett-ed, adj.

## pain
pain, n. — ME. peyne, fr. OF. ( = F.)pain, fr. L.

pain, tr. and intr. v. — ME.peynen, fr. OF. pener

Derivatives: pain-ed, adj., pain-ing, adj., pain-
ing-ly, adv.

paint, tr. and intr. v. — ME. peynten, painter, fr.

pieSiu, pieSti, 'to write', Lith. pieSd, 'soot',

paint-ing-ness, п., paint-y, adj., paint-i-ness, n.

painter, п., a rope fastened to the bow of a boat.

## painter
painter, п., the cougar. — A var. of panther.
paint иге, п., a painting (obsol.) — OF. (= F.)

## pair
pair, n, — ME. paire, peir, fr. OF. (= F.) paire,
fr. L. paria, neut. pi. of par, 'equal' (taken as a

## pajamas
pajamas, pyjamas, n. pi., loose trousers or
drawers. — Hind, pdjdma, paijdma, lit. 'leg-garment',
fr. Pers. pa, ράϊ, 'foot, leg', and jama, 'clothing,
garment'. Pers. ράϊ, 'foot, leg', is rel. to Avestic
pad-, 'foot', and cogn. with Gk. πους, gen.
ποδός, L. pes, gen. pedis, 'foot', Goth, fotus, OE.

in charpoy, teapoy, seerpaw.

## pal
pal, п., an intimate friend. — English Gypsy pal,

## palabra
palabra, п., word; palaver. — Sp., fr. L.parabola,

παραβολή, lit. *a throwing beside, juxtaposition". See
parabola, parable, and cp. palaver.

## palace
palace, n. — ME. palais, fr. OF. (= F.) palais, fr.
L. palutium, 'palace', orig. 'palace built by
Augustus on Palatine Hill', fr. Paldtium,

Etruscan origin and rel. to Pales, name of an Italian
goddess of shepherds and cattle. Cp. F. AJt-
heim, A History of Roman Religion, p. 102.
Cp. palatial, Palatine, Pales, paladin and the
first element in palsgrave.

## paladin

Charlemagne. — F., fr. It. paladino, fr. L. palatinus,

## palae-
palae-, combining form. — See pale-.

Palaemon, п., the genus consisting of the typical

## palaestra
palaestra, palestra, п., 1) wrestling school; 2)

'wrestling school, gymnasium', formed with
-τρα, a suff. denoting place, fr. παλαίειν, 'to

■ cp. orchestra.
Derivatives: pal(a)estr-al, adj., pal(a)estr-ian,
ad/, and п., pal(a)estr-ic, adj.

palafitte, п., a prehistoric lake dwelling built on

palo, 'stake', anafitto, 'fixed'. It. palo derives fr.

'stake'; It. fitto is pp. of figgere, 'to fix', fr. L.

## figere
figere, 'to fix'; see fix.

## palagonite
palagonite, п., a basaltic t\ifa(petrogr.) — Named
after Palagonia_ in Sicily. For the ending see

pal ait e, п., a hydrous manganese phosphate

## palama

## palanquin

## palatal
palatal, adj., pertaining to the palate. — F., fr. L.

## palate
palate, n. — ME. palat, fr. OF. palat, fr. L.

fala(n)dum, 'sky'. Cp. L. caeli palatum, 'vault

abil-ity, п., palat-able-ness, п., palat-abl-y, adv.

## palatial
palatial, adj., pertaining to, or resembling, a

## palatinate

## palatine
palatine, adj., pertaining to the palace. — F. pala-

(representing L. -Inus).

## palatine
palatine, п., officer of the palace. — F. palatin, fr.
L. paluunus, 'an officer of the palace', prop, an
adj. meaning 'pertaining to the palace', used as
a noun. See prec. word and cp. paladin.

## palatine
palatine, adj., pertaining to the palate. — F.
palatin, 'pertaining to the palate', fr. L. palatum.
See palate and -ine (representing L. -inus) and
cp. palatal.

## palato-
palato-, combining form meaning 'palate'. — Fr.
L. palatum. See palate.

## palaver
palaver, п., 1) conference, talk; 2) idle talk; 3)
flattery. — Port, palavra, 'word, talk', rel. to Sp.
palabra, of s.m., fr. L. parabola, 'comparison,
parable, speech', fr. Gk. παραβολή,
'comparison, parable'. See parable and cp. paiabra.
Derivatives; palaver, tr. v., palaver-er, п., pala-
ver-ist, n.,palaver-ment, п.,palaver-ous, adj.

## pale
pale, п., 1) a pointed stake; 2) boundary. — ME.,
fr. MF. (= F.)pal, 'stake', fr. L.palus, 'stake',
which stands for *pak-slos, and is rel. to pax,
gen. parts, 'peace', pacisci, 'to make an
agreement', pangere, 'to fasten'. See pact and cp.
impale. Cp. also palafitte, palette, pallet,
'potter's tool', paly, 'divided palewise', peel, 'a small
tower', peel, 'baker's shovel', pole, 'stake',
travail, travel.

## pale
pale, tr. v., to enclose with pales; to enclose with
a fence. — ME. palen, fr. MF. palir, fr. pal,
'stake'. See prec. word.

## pale
pale, adj., whitish, wan. — ME., fr. OF. pale (F.
pale), fr. L. pallidus, 'pale', tr. pallere, 'to grow
pale'. See pallor and cp. words there referred to.
Derivatives: pale, intr. and tr. v., pale-ly, adv.,
pale-ness, n. v

## pale-
pale-, combining form. — See paleo-.

## palen
palen, п., a chaffy bract or scale (hot.) — L.,
'chaff'. See paillasse.
Derivative: pale-aceous, adj.

## paleate
paleate, adj., having paleae (hot.) — L. paleatus,
'mixed with chaff', fr. palea. See prec. word and
adj. suff. -ate.

## paleo-
paleo-, palaeo-, before a vowel usually pale-,
palae-, combining form meaning 'ancient,
primitive'. — Gk. παλαιό-, πάλαι-, fr. παλαιός,
'ancient', fr. πάλαι, 'long ago', which is rel. to
πάλιν, 'again, backward', Aeol. Gk. πήλυι,
Gk. τηλε, 'far off, at a distance', Gk. τέλος,
'end', fr. I.-E. base *qwel-, 'to turn, move about'.
See tele- and words there referred to.

## paleobotany
paleobotany, paleobotany, п., botany dealing
with fossil plants. — Compounded of paleo-
and botany.
Derivatives: pal(a)eobotan-ic, pal(a)eobotan-ic-
al, adjs., pal(a)eobotan-ist, n.

## Paleocene
Paleocene, Palaeocene, adj., pertaining to the

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:555 COLUMN:2 -->
epoch preceding the Eocene (geol.) —
Compounded of paleo- and Gk. καινός, 'new'. See
katuo-.
Derivative: Pal(a)eocene, п., the Pal(a)eocene
period.

## paleethnology
paleethnology, palaeethnology, п., ethnology of
prehistoric man. — Compounded of pale- and
ethnology.
Derivatives: pal(a)eethnolog-ic, pal(a)eethnolog·
ic-al, adjs., pal(a)eethnoIog-ist, a.

## paleographer
paleographer, palaeographer, п., one learned in
paleography. — See paleo- and -grapher.

## paleography
paleography, palaeography, п., study of ancient
writing. — Compounded of paleo- and -graphy.
Derivatives: pal(a)eograph-ic, pal(a)eograph-ic-
al, adjs., pal(a)eograph-ic-al-ly, adv., pal(a)eo-
graph-ist, n.

## paleolith
paleolith, palaeolith, п., a stone implement of the
earlier Stone Age. — Back formation fr.
paleolithic.

## paleolithic
paleolithic, palaeolithic, adj., pertaining to the
Earlier Stone Age (geol.) — Coined by John
Lubbock, the later Baron Avebury (1834-1913),
fr. Gk. παλαιός, 'ancient', λίθος, 'stone', and
suff. -ic. See paleo- and litho- and cp. neolithic.

## paleology
paleology, palaeology, п., the study of antiquity.
— Compounded of paleo- and Gk. -λογία, fr.
-λόγος, 'one who speaks (in a certain manner);
one who deals (with a certain topic)'. See -logy.
Derivatives: pat(a)eolog-ic-al, adj., pal(a)eolog-
ist, n.

## paleontography
paleontography, palaeontograpby, п., the
description of fossils. — F. paUontographie, lit.
'description of ancient existing things';
compounded of Gk. παλαιός, 'ancient', δντα,
'existing things', plural ofuv, neut. pres. part, of
είναι, 'to be', and -γραφίϊ, fr. γράφειν, 'to
write'. See paleo-, onto- and -graphy.
Derivatives: pal(a)eontograph-ic, pat(a)eonto-
graph-ic-at, adjs.

## paleontology
paleontology, palaeontology, п., the study of
ancient life on earth; the study of fossils. F. ραΐέ-
ontologie, compounded of paleo- and ontology.
Derivatives: pal(a)eontolog-ic,pal(a)eontolog-ic-
al, adjs., pal(a)eontolog-ist, n.

## paleopathology
paleopathology, paleopathology, п., the study
of pathology in fossil organisms. —
Compounded of paleo- and pathology.

## paleothere
paleothere, palaeothere, п., a genus of extinct
mammals resembling the tapir. — Compounded
of Gk. παλαιός, 'ancient', and&^p, 'wild beast'.
See paleo- and therio-.

## Paleozoic
Paleozoic, Palaeozoic, adj., pertaining to the era
between the Precambrian and the Mesozoic
(geol.)—Coined by Adam Sedgwick(I785-1873)
fr. Gk. παλαιός, 'ancient' (see paleo-), ζωή,
'life' (see zoic), and suff. -ic.
Derivative: Pal(a)eozoic, n.

## paleozoology
paleozoology, palaeozoology, п., paleontology
of fossil animals. — Compounded of paleo- and
zoology.
Derivatives: pal(a)eozoolog-ic-al, adj., pal(a)e-
ozoolog-ist, n.

## Pales
Pales, the Italian goddess of shepherds and cattle.
— L. Pales, prob. of Etruscan origin and related
to Palatium, 'Palatine Hill', the central of the
seven hills of Rome. — See palace and cp.
palatine, 'pertaining to the palace'.

## Palestine
Palestine, n. — F., fr. L. Palaestina, fr. Gk.
Παλαιστίνη, fr. Heb. Psle'sheth, 'Philistia,
land of the Philistines'. The name Παλαιστίνη
was first used by Herodotus. See Philistine.
Derivatives: Palestin-ian, adj. and n.

## paletot
paletot, п., an overcoat. — F. paletot, fr. MF,
paltoke, paletoc, paletot, fr. ME. paltok, the
first element of which is identical with ME. pal,
fr. L. pallium, 'cloak'. See pall, 'cloak'. The
second element of the compound pal-tok is of
uncertain origin.

## palette
palette, п., painter's color-board. — F., prop, 'a
thin piece of wood', diminutive formed fr. L.

## pala
pala, 'spade, shovel', which is of uncertain
origin. It is perh. rel. to L. pains, 'stake'. See pale,
'stake', and cp. pallet, peel, 'baker's shovel'. For
the ending see suff. -ette.

## palfrey
palfrey, п., saddle horse (archaic). — ME., fr.
OF. palefrei (F. palefroi), fr. ML. palafredus,
dissimilated fr. Late L. paraveredus, generally

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:555 COLUMN:3 -->
supposed to be a hybrid coined fr. Gk. παρά
(see para-, 'beside') and Late L. veredus,
'courier's horse', which is usually derived from
Celtic *voredos; cp. W. gorwydd, 'horse', Olr. ria-
daim, Ί ride', and see ride. It is more probable,
however, that Late L. veredus is borrowed fr.
Heb. peredh, pheredh, 'mule' (through the
medium of Arab.-Pers. barid, 'courier'). OS. perid,
MDu. peert, paert, Du. paard, OHG. pfarifrit,
pferfrit (MHG. pharvrit,phart, G. Pferd), 'horse',
are borrowed fr. ML. paraveredus.

## Pali
Pali, п., the Old Indian dialect used in the sacred
writings of the Buddhists. — OI. putt, for puli
bhasa, 'language of the canonical books', fr.
pall, 'line, role, canon', and bhasa, 'language'.

## palikar
palikar, п., a follower of a Greek or Albanian
military chief. — ModGk. παλικάρι, 'boy',
dimin. of Gk. πάλλαξ, gen. πάλλακος, 'youth',
which is rel. to παλλακή, παλλακίς,
'concubine', and to Παλλάς, gen. -άδος, epithet of
Athene. See Pallas.

## palilogy
palilogy, п., repetition of a word or words for the
sake of emphasis (rhet.) — Late L. palilogia, fr.
Gk. παλιλογίϊ, 'repetition', compounded of
πάλιν, 'again', and -λογία, fr. -λόγος, 'one who
speaks (in a certain manner); one who deals
(with a certain topic)'. The first element is rel.
to Gk. πάλαι, 'long ago'; see pale-. For the
second element see -logy.

## palimpsest
palimpsest, п., a parchment from which the
earlier writing has been removed to make room for
the next.—L. palimpsestus,fr.Gk. παλίμψηστος,
'scraped again'(whence the noun παλίμψηστον,
'a palimpsest'), compounded of πάλιν, 'again',
and verbal adj. of ψήν, 'to touch on the surface,
to rub'. For the first element see prec. word. The
second element is rel. to Gk. ψάμμος (for *ψάς>-
μος), 'sand', ψήφος, Dor. ψαφος, 'small
stone, pebble'; see sand and cp. psammite, pse-
phism.
Derivatives: palimpsest, adj. and tr. v., palim-
psest-ic, adj.

## palindrome
palindrome, п., a word, line or sentence reading
the same backward or forward. — Gk.
παλίνδρομος, 'running again', compounded of
πάλιν, 'again, backwards', and δρόμος, 'course',
whence δρομαϊος κάμηλος, 'dromedary'. See
palilogy and dromedary.
Derivatives:palindrom-iCi palindrom-ic-al, adjs.,
palindrom-ic-al-ly, adv., palindrom-ist, n.

## paling
paling, п., a fence made of pales. — Formed fr.
pale, v. with -ing, suff. forming verbal nouns.

## palingenesis
palingenesis, n. rebirth, regeneration. — ModL.,
compounded of Gk. πάλιν, 'again', and γένε-
σις, 'origin, birth, descent, race'. See palilogy and
genesis.
Derivative: palingenes-ist, n.

## pallagenetic
pallagenetic, adj. — See prec. word and genetic.
Derivative: palingenetic-al-ly, adv.

## palinode
palinode, n:, recantation. — MF. palinode, fr. L.
palinodia, fr. Gk. παλινωδία, 'recantation,
palinode', which is compounded of πάλιν, 'again',
and ώδή, 'song'. See palilogy and ode.
Derivatives: palinode, v., palinod-ist, n.

## palinodic
palinodic, adj. — Gk. παλινωδικός, fr.
παλινωδία. See prec. word and adj. suff. -ic.

## palinody
palinody, п., palinode (archaic) — MF. (= F.)
palinodie, fr. L. palinodia. See palinode and -y
(representing Gk. -ία).

## palisade
palisade, п., a fence of stakes. — F. palissade, fr.
palisser, 'to fence in, enclose', fr. palis, 'paling',
fr. OF. pal, 'stake', fr. L. palus. See pale, 'stake'
and -ade.
Derivatives: palisade, tr. v., palisad-ing, a.

## palisander
palisander, palissander, п., Brazilian rosewood.
— F. palissandre, fr. earlier palixandre, which is
prob. of Caribbean origin.

## Paliurus
Paliurus, п., a genus of shrubs (bot.) — ModL.,
fr. L. paliurus, fr. Gk. παλίουρος, 'Christ's
thorn'.

## pall
pall, п., 1) a cloak (archaic); 2) a shroud. — ME.
pall, fr. OE. pxll, 'costly cloak, robe, purple
garment', fr. L. pallium, 'cloak", which is rel. to
palla, 'long upper garment of Roman women',
and prob. cogn. with OSlav. pelena, 'swaddling
clothes', ON. feldr, 'sheepskin, mantle', and L.
pellis (for *pel-nis), 'skin'. See peilicle and cp.
paletot, palliate and the second element in tar-

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:556 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: 529 | PALTRY -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:556 COLUMN:1 -->
paulin.
Derivatives: ρα//, tr. v.fpalli-al, ad).,pall-ed, adj.

## pall
pall, intr. v., to become insipid. — ME. patten,
prob. aphetic for apallen, 'to appall'. See appall.

## Palladian
Palladian, adj., in the style of the Italian
architect Andrea Palladio (1518-80). — For the
ending see stiff, -an.

## palladium
palladium, п., an image of Pallas Athene on the
custody of which depended the safety of the
city of Troy. — L., fr. Gk. παλλάδιον, 'statue
of Pallas', dimin. formed fr. Παλλάς, gen.
Παλλάδος, a surname of the goddess Athene.
See Pallas.

## palladium
palladium, п., name of a metallic element. —
ModL., coined by its discoverer the English
chemist William Hyde Wollaston (1766-1828)
in 1803 fr. Pallas, name of an asteroid
discovered by the German physician and astronomer
Heinrich Wilhelm Matthaus Olbers (1758-1840)
in 1802, and called after the goddess Pallas
Athene. See next word and 2nd -ium and cp.
prec. word.
Derivatives: pallad-ize, tr. v., pallad-ous, adj.

## Pallas
Pallas, п., a surname of the Greek goddess
Athene {Greek mythol.)—L. Pallas, gen. Palladis, fr.
Gk. Παλλάς, gen. Παλλάδος, lit. 'maiden'
(whence τταλλάδιον, 'statue of Pallas'), which is
re], to τταλλακή, παλλακίς, 'concubine'. Gk.
πάλλαξ, gen. πάλλακος, 'youth, girl', is
prob. a back formation fr. παλλακή or
παλλακίς . (L. paelex, 'concubine of a married man',
is pern, a loan word fr. Gk. *παΐλαξ, a
hypothetic secondary form of πάλλαξ.) Ср. Avestic

## pairikd
pairikd, 'beautiful women seducing pious men'
(whence Middle Pers. parlk, ModPers. pari,
'fairy'). Cp. also Heb. pileghesh, Aram, pilaqta,
'concubine', and Arab. Bilqfs, name of the queen
of Sheba. All these words are certainly related,
but it is difficult to establish the degree of iheir
relationship to one another. The above cited
I.-E. words are possibly Sem. loan words. See
Gesenius-Buhl, HWAT., p. 642, and Ludwig
Koehler, Lexicon in Veteris Testamenti Libros,
p. 761. Cp. palladium, palikar, Paelignian, peri.

## pallasite
pallasite, п., a meteorite (geol.) — Named after
the German naturalist and traveler Peter Simon
Pallas (1741-1811), who brought it to St.
Petersburg. For the ending see subst. suff. -ite.

## pallesthesia
pallesthesia, п., sensitiveness to vibration
(psycho/.) — ModL., compounded of Gk. πάλλειν,
to wield, brandish, swing, quiver', and αίσ-
θάνεσθαι, 'to perceive'. The first element is rel. to
πάλος, 'lot cast from a shaken helmet', παλτός,
'brandished', and in gradational relationship to
πελεμίζειν, 'to shake, cause to tremble', and to
πολεμάς, 'war'; see polemic. For the second
element see esthesia.

## pallet
pallet, п., mattress. — Late ME. paillet, fr. MF.
(= F.) paillet, 'heap of straw', fr. OF. (= F.)
paille, 'straw', fr. L. palea, 'chaff'. See paillasse
and -et.

## pallet
pallet, п., potter's tool. — MF. (= F.) palette,
dimin. of pale, 'shovel', fr. L. pdla, 'spade*,
which is perh. rel. to pdlus, 'stake'. See pale,
'stake', and cp. palette.
Derivative: pallet-ize, tr. v.
pallia], adj., pertaining to a pallium. — See
pallium and adj. suit", -al.

## palliasse
palliasse, n. — See paillasse.

## palliate
palliate, tr. v., to extenuate, excuse. — Lit. 'to
cloak', fr. L. palliatus, 'cloaked', fr. pallium,
'cloak'; cp. Late L. palliare (pp. palliatus), 'to
cloak, palliate'. See pall, п., and verbal suff. -ate.
Derivatives: palliation (q.v.), palliat-ive, adj.
and п., pattiat-ive-ly, adv., palliat-or, п., palliat-
or-y, adj.

## palliation
palliation, n. — MF. (— F.), fr. ML.pallidtionem,
ace. of pallidtio, fr. Late L. palliatus, pp. of
palliare. See prec, word and -ion.

## pallid
pallid, adj.rpale; wan. — L. pallidus, 'pale', fr.
pallere, 'to grow pale', rel to pallor, 'paleness'.
Seelpallor, and cp. words there referred to.
Derivatives: pallid-ly, adv., pallid-ness, n.

## pall-mall
pall-mall, п., an old game. — MF.pallemaille, fr.
It. pallamaglio, lit. 'ball-mallet', fr. palla, 'ball',
and maglio, 'mallet*. The first element is a Teut.
loan word; see ball, 'a round body', and cp.
paltone. The second element derives fr. L.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:556 COLUMN:2 -->
malleus, 'a hammer'; see malleus.

## pallone
pallone, п., an Italian game. — It., 'large ball',
formed with augment. sufT. -one fr. palla, 'ball',
a word of Teut. origin. See pall-mall and cp.
balloon.

## pallor
pallor, п., paleness. — L. pallor, 'paleness', fr.
pallere, 'to be pale', rel. to pullus, 'dark-colored,
blackish gray, dusky', palumbes, 'wood pigeon',
lit. 'the dark-colored bird', fr. I.-E. base *pel-,
'dark-colored, gray', whence also OI. palitdh,
'gray', pdndith (Jot *pdln-du-), 'whitish, pale',
Gk. πελιός, πελιδνός, 'livid', ττελλός, 'dark-
colored, dusky', πελαργός (for *πελα.Ρ-αργός),
'stork', lit. 'the blackish white bird', πέλεια,
'pigeon', lit. *the dark-colored bird', πολιάς,
'gray', OE. fealo, 'dull-colored, yellow,
yellowish red, brown'. See fallow, 'brownish yellow*,
and cp. pale, pall, v., pallid, appall.

## palm
palm, п., the inner part of the hand. — ME.
palme, fr. OF. palme, раите (F. раите), 'palm
of the hand', fr. L. palma, of s.m., which is
cogn. with Gk. παλάμη, 'open hand, palm',
Olr. lam, W. Haw, OCo. lof, 'hand', OE. folm,
OHG. folma, of s.m., and with OI. panih (for-
*pdlnib), 'hand; hoof. All these words derive
fr. I.-E. base *psld-, 'spread out, flat', for which
see plain, adj., flat. Cp. palama.
Derivatives: palm, tr. v., palm-ar, adj., palmate
(q.v.), palm-ed, adj., palm-ic, adj., palmist (q.v.)
palmistry (q.v.).

## palm
palm, п., a tropical tree. — ME. palme, fr. OE.
palm, fr. L. palma, 'palm tree', orig. identical
with palma, 'palm of the hand'; so called from
the flatness of its leaves. See prec. word and cp.
palmetto, palmitic.
Derivative: palm-y, n.

## palmate
palmate, adj., 1) having divisions radiating from
a common center (said of leaves; hot.); 2) having
the toes united by a web, web-footed (zool.) —
L. palmdtus, 'marked with the palm of a hand',
pp. of palmare, 'to make the mark of the palm
of one's hand', fr. palma. See palm, 'the palm of
the hand', and adj. suff. -ate.
Derivative: palmat-ed, adj.

## palmati-
palmati-, combining form meaning 'palmate' (as
inpalmatiform), or 'palmately' (as inpalmatifid).
— Fr. L. palmdtus. See palmate,

## palmatifld
palmatifld, adj., palmately cleft (said of leaves).
— Compounded of palmati- and the stem of
fidere, 'to cleave'. See fissile.

## palmatiform
palmatiform, adj., palmate (said of leaves). —
Formed fr. palmati- and L. forma, 'form, shape'.
See form, n.

## palmation
palmation, п., 1) the state of being palmate; 2) a
palmate structure (hot.) — See prec. word and
-ion.

## palmer
palmer, п., a pilgrim who had returned from the
Holy Land. — ME. palmere, fr. AF. palmer,
corresponding to OF. palmier, paumier, fr. ML.
palmarius, fr. L. palma, 'palm tree' (see palm,
the tree, and agential suff. -er); so called from
the palm branch worn by the pilgrim in
commemoration of his journey.

## palmerite
palmerite, п., a hydrous potassium aluminum
phosphate (mineral.) — Named after the Italian
scientist Paride Palmeri. For the ending see
subst. suff. -ite.

## palmetto
palmetto, п., any of various species of small palm
— Sp. palmito, fr. palma, 'palm', with change of
the Sp. dimin. suff. -ito to its It. equivalent -etto.
See palm, the tree, and -et.

## palmi-
palmi-, combining form fr. L. palma, 'palm'. See
palm, 'the tree'.

## palmiped
palmiped, adj., web-footed (zool.) — L. palmipes,
gen. palmipedis, 'broad-footed', compounded of
palma, 'palm', and pes, gen. pedis, 'foot'. See
palm and pedal.
Derivative: palmiped, n.

## palmist
palmist, п., one who practices palmistry. — Back
formation from palmistry.

## palmistry
palmistry, п., divination from the palm of the
hand; chiromancy — ME. pawmestry, prob.
shortened from *palme~mestry, lit. 'mastery of
the palm of the hand', fr. palme, 'palm of the
hand', and mesiry, 'mastery', fr. OF. maistrie;
see palm, 'the inner part of the hand', and
mastery. For the shortening of ME. *palmemestry
into pawmestry see haplology.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:556 COLUMN:3 -->

## palmitate
palmitate, п., a salt or ester of palmitic acid
(chem.) — See palmitic and chem suff. -ate.

## palmitic
palmitic, adj., pertaining to a crystalline acid
occurring uncombined in palm oil (chem.) — F.
palmitique, fr. palmite, 'palm marrow', fr, Sp.
palmito, 'bud shooting from a palm tree;
palmetto'. See palmetto and -itic.

## palmus
palmus, adj., palpitation; twitching (med.) —
Medical L., fr. Gk. παλμός, 'a quivering', from
the stem of πάλλειν, 'to wield, brandish, swing,
quiver'. See pallesthesia.

## palmyra
palmyra, п., a kind of palm tree. — Fr. earlier
palmeira, fr. Port, palmeira, 'palm tree', fr. L.
palma, of s.m. (see palm, the tree); influenced in
form by a false association with the city of
Palmyra in Syria.

## palp
palp, п., palpus. — F. palpe, fr. L. palpus, 'feeler'.
See palpus.

## palp
palp, tr. v., to touch, fee]. — MF. (= F.) palper,
fr. L. palpdre. See palpable.

## palpable
palpable, adj. — ME., fr. MF. (= F.)palpable, fr.
L. palpdbilis, 'that may be touched softly', fr.
palpdre, 'to touch softly, stroke', whence palpi-
tare, 'to move quickly, tremble, throb, palpitate'.
See feel and -able and cp. palpebra, palpitate,
psalm.
Derivatives: palpabil-ity, п., palpable-ness, п.,
palpabl-y, adv.

## palpal
palpal, adj., pertaining to a palpus or palpi. —
See palp, п., and adj. suff. -al.
palpate, adj., having a palpus or palpi. — See
palp,"n., and adj. suff. -ate.

## palpate
palpate, tr. v., to examine by touch. — L. palpd-
tus, pp. palpdre, 'to touch, stroke'. See palpable
and verbal suff. -ate.

## palpation
palpation, n. — L. palpatio, gen. -onis, fr. palpd-
tus, pp. of palpdre. See prec. word and -ion.

## palpebra
palpebra, п., eyelid (anat.) — L., 'eyelid', lit. 'that
which moves quickly', rel. to palpdre, 'to touch,
stroke*, palpitdre, *to move quickly, tremble,
throb, palpitate'. See palpable and cp. palpitate.
For the suff. -bra cp. terebra, vertebra.
Derivatives: palpebr-al, palpebr-ate, adjs., pal-
pebr-ation, n.

## patpebritis
patpebritis, п., blepharitis (med.) — A hybrid
coined fr. L. palpebra, 'eyelid', and the Gk. suff.
-ΐτις; see palpebra and -itis. The correct form
is blepharitis (q.v.)

## palpitate
palpitate, intr. v., 1) to beat rapidly (said of the
heart); 2) to pulsate, throb. — L. palpitdt(um),
pp. stem of palpitdre, 'to move quickly, tremble,
throb', freq. of palpdre. See palpable and -ate.

## palpitation
palpitation, n. — L. palpitdtio, fr. palpitat(um),
pp. stem of palpitdre. See prec. word and -ion.

## palpulus
palpulus, п., a small palpus (zool.) — ModL.,
dimin. of palpus, 'feeler'. See next word and
-ule.

## palpus
palpus, n., a feeler; a jointed sense organ attached
to an oral part (zool.) — ModL., *a feeler', fr.
L. palpdre. See palpable and cp. palp, n.

## palsgrave
palsgrave, п., a count palatine. — MDu.
palsgrave (Du. paltsgraaf); compounded of pals
(Du. palts), 'palace', fr. L. paldtium, 'palace',
and grave (Du. graaf), 'count'. Cp. MHG.
pfalzgrave (G. Pfalzgraf) and see palace and
grave, *a count'. — See J. F. Bense, A
Dictionary of the Low-Dutch Element in the English
Vocabulary, p. 264.

## palsgravine
palsgravine, п., a countess palatine. — MDu.
palsgravin (Du. paltsgravin). Cp. G. Pfalzgrafin
and see prec. word and subst. suff. -ine.

## palstave
palstave, п., a celt (archeol.) — Dan. paalstav, fr.
ON. pdlstafr, fr. pall, 'hoe, spade', and stafr,
'staff'. The first element derives fr. OE. pal, 'hoe,
spade', fr. L. pdla, 'spade', which is perh. rel. to
L, pdlus, 'stake'; see pale, 'stake'. The second
element is rel. to OE. stsef, 'staff'; see staff.

## palsy
palsy, п., paralysis. — ME. palesie, parlesie, fr.
MF. paralysie, fr. L. paralysis, fr. Gk. παρά-
λυσις. See paralysis.
Derivatives: palsy, tr. \,,palsi-ed, adj.

## palter
palter, intr. v., to trifle. — Prob. a freq. formed
with suff. -er fr. dial. E. palt, 'rubbish', a word
of LG. origin. Cp. next word.

## paltry
paltry, adj., trifling, petty. — LG. paltrig, pultrig
(Du. palterig), 'rubbishy', fr. palt, pult, *rub-
bish'.
Derivatives: paltry, n. (q.v.), paltri-ness, n.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:557 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: PALTRY | 530 -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:557 COLUMN:1 -->

## paltry
paltry, п., rubbish (obsol.) — From the LG.

## adjective paltrig
adjective paltrig, puitrig (see prec. word), mistaken

## for a noun. See J. F. Bense
for a noun. See J. F. Bense, Dictionary of the

## Low-Dutch Element in the English Vocabulary
Low-Dutch Element in the English Vocabulary,
p. 265.

## paludal
paludal, adj., pertaining to marhes, marshy;
malarial. — Formed with adj. suff. -al fr. L.

## palus
palus, gen. paludis, *marsh\ which is cogn. with
OI. palvalam, 'pond', palvalyah, 'marshy', fr.
I.-E. base *pel-, 'to flow', whence also Lith. pilu,

## pi/ti
pi/ti, 'to pour, shed', Lett, pilet, 'to drip, trickle'.
Fr. *pleu-, enlargement of base *pel-, derives
Gk. πλέω (for *πλέ7ω), Ί sail, go by sea,

## swim'
swim', L. pluit, 'it rains', QN.fijota, OE. fleotan,

## etc.
etc., 'to float, swim', ΟΝ. βόα, OE. flowan, 'to

## flow'. See flow
flow'. See flow, v. and cp. pluvial.

## paludi-
paludi-, combining form meaning 'marsh'. — L.

## paludi-
paludi-, fr. palus, gen. paludis, *marsh\ See prec.
word.

## paludic
paludic, adj., paludal. — Formed with adj. sufT.

## -ic fr.L
-ic fr.L, palus, gen. paludis, 'marsh'. See paludal.

## Paludicella
Paludicella, п., a genus of polyzoans (zool.) —
ModL., compounded of L. palus, gen. paludis,
'marsh', and cella, 'cell'. See paludal and ceil.

## Paludicolae
Paludicolae, n. pi., an order of birds; also called
Gruiformes {ornithol.) — ModL., lit.
'inhabitants of marshes', fr. L. palus, gen. paludis,
'marsh', and colere, 'to inhabit'. See paludal and
cult.

## paludine
paludine, palndinous, ailjs., pertaining to a marsh,
marshy. — See paludal, -ine (representing L.
-inus) and -ous.

## paludis m
paludis m, п., malaria (med.) — Formed with
suff. -ism fr. L. palus, gen. -udis, 'marsh'. See
paludal.

## paly
paly, adj.,palish {poet.) — Formed fr. pale,
'whitish', with adj. suff. -y.

## paly
paly, adj., divided palewise {her.) — F. pale, fr.
pal, 'pale, stake'. See pale, 'stake', and cp. coun-
terpaly.

## pam
pam, п., 1) a card game; 2) the knave of clubs. —
Abbreviation of F. pamphile, fr. the L. PN.
Pamphilus, fr. Gk. ΙΙάμφίλος, a name lit.
meaning 'beloved of all', fr. παν- (see pan-) and φίλος,
'lover, friend* (see -phile). Cp. pam phi et.

## pampas
pampas, n. pi., large plains of South America. —
Sp., pi. oipampa, fr. Quechua pampa, 'a plain'.
Cp. pampero.

## pamper
pamper, tr. v., 1) to glut {obsol.); 2) to be over-
indulgent with. — ME. pampren, of MFlem.
origin (cp. Flem. pamperen, 'to pamper); from
the nasalized form of the imitative base *pap,
'to eat pap, to eat', whence L. pappa, child's
word for 'food', and papa, 'father'. See pap,
'food', papa, 'father'.
Derivatives: pamper-ed, adj.,pamper-ed-ly, adv.,
pamper ed-ness, п., pamper-er, n.

## pampero
pampero, п., a cold wind blowing across the
pampas. — Sp., formed fr. pampa, 'a plain', with
suff. -его, fr. L. -arius (see adj. suff. -ary).

## pamphlet
pamphlet, п., a small unbound treatise. — ME.
pamflet, alteration of Pamphilet ax Panflet,
popular name of a Latin comedy of the 12th cent.,
entitled Pamphilus seu de amore. See pam.
Derivatives: pamphlet, intr. and intr. v.,
pamphlet-age, п., pamphlet-ary, adj., pamphlet-eer,
intr. v. and п., pamphlet-er, п., pamphlet-ic,
pamphlet-ic-al, adjs., pamphlet-ize, tr. and intr.
v.

## pampiniform
pampiniform, adj., tendril-shaped (anat.) —
Compounded of L. pampinus, 'tendril of vine',
and forma, 'form, shape'. Pampinus is a
derivative of base *pamp-, nasalized form of base
*pap-, 'to swell', whence L. papula, 'a swelling,
njmple', papilla, 'nipple'. See papula, and cp.
pap, 'nipple'; cp. also pompano. For the second
element see form, n.

## Pan
Pan, п., a god of the woods and fields {Greek
mythol.) — L. Pan, fr. Gk. Πάν, which is prob.
contracted fr. *Παύσων and is cogn. with OI.
Pusdn-, a Vedic god, guardian and multiplier of
cattle and of human possessions in general, lit.
'nourisher'. Cp panic. Cp. also the second
element in tragopan.

## pan
pan, п., a broad vessel. — ME. panne, fr. OE.
panne, which, together with ΟΝ., Swed. panna,
Dan. pande, OFris. panne, OLG. panna (whence
MLG., LG., MDu. panne, Du. pan), OHG.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:557 COLUMN:2 -->
phanna, pfanna (whence MHG., G. pfanne),
'pan', is borrowed fr. ML. panna, fr. VL. *pat-
na, fr. L. patina, 'broad dish, pan', ult. fr. Gk.
πατάνη, 'flat dish', which is rel. to πεταννύναι,
'to spread out', fr. I.-E. base *pet-, 'to spread*.
See fathom, п., and cp. paten.
Derivatives: pan, tr. and intr. v., pan-ful, adj.,
pann-er, п., pann-ery, n.

## pan-
pan-, combining form meaning 'all, every'. —
Gk. παν-, fr. πας, πάσα, παν, 'all, every',
which is of uncertain origin; it is not related to
L. quantus, 'how great'. Cp. the second element
in diapason, pasigraphy.

## panacea
panacea, п., a supposed remedy for all diseases.
— L. panacea, fr. Gk. πανάκεια, 'universal
remedy', fr. πανακής, 'all-healing',
compounded of παν- (see pan-) and άκος, 'remedy'
(whence άκεΐσ&αι, 'to heal'), which is of
uncertain origin. It is pern. cogn. with Olr. hicc,
'healing', icaim, Ί heal', W. lack, 'healthy'. Cp.
panax.
Derivatives: panace-an, adj., panace-ist, n.

## panache
panache, п., a plume of feathers. — F., formerly
(down to the 17th cent.) written pennache, fr. It.
pennaccio, avar. of pennacchio, fr. penna,
'feather', fr. L. penna. See pen, 'feather'.
Derivative: panach-ed, adj.

## panada
panada, п., a dish made of bread boiled to a pulp.
— Sp., fr. pan, 'bread', fr. L. panem, ace. of
pants, 'bread'. See pantry. For the ending see
suff. -ade.

## Panama hat
Panama hat, a hat made from the leaves of the
screw pine. — A misnomer, for 'Panama' hats
were first made in Ecuador, South America.
The association with Panama is due to the
circumstances that orig. the city of Panama was
the distributing center for such hats.

## Panathenaea
Panathenaea, n. pi., an ancient Athenian festival.
— L., fr. Gk. Παναθήναια, shortened fr.
Παναθήναια ίερά, prop, festivities in honor of the
goddess Pallas Athena, fr. παν- (see pan-) and
'Αθήνη, 'Athena'. See Athena.
Derivative: Panathene-an, adj.

## Panathenaic
Panathenaic, adj., pertaining to the Panathanaea.
— L. Panathenaicus, fr. Gk. Παναθηναϊκός, fr.
Παναθήναια. See prec. word and adj. suff. -ic.

## panax
panax, п., 1) a plant supposed to heal all
diseases; 2) (cap.) a genus of plants of the ginseng
family (bot.) — L., name of a plant, fr. Gk.
πανάκεια, 'a universal remedy'. See panacea.

## pancake
pancake, n. — Compounded of pan and cake.
Derivative: pancake, intr. v. (aviation).

## Pancbatantra
Pancbatantra, п., a collection of the animal
fables of Bidpai in five books — OI. Pancatantra-,
lit. 'the book of five', fr. panca, 'five', and tan-
tram, 'the essential, main thing, textbook,
treatise'. The first element is cogn. with Gk. πέντε,
'five'; see pent a-. For the second element see
t antra.

## panchayat
panchayat, п., a village council of five or more
members (Hindu law) — Hind, pancayat, fr. OI.
panca, 'five', which is cogn. with Gk. πέντε,
'five'. See penta- and cp. prec. word.

## panchromatic
panchromatic, adj., sensitive to all the colors of
the spectrum. — Compounded of pan- and
chromatic.
Derivatives: panchromatic, п., panchromat-ism,
п.,panchromat-ize, tr. v.,panchromat-iz-ation,n.

## pancratiast
pancratiast, п., a competitor in the pancratium.
— L. pancratiastes, fr. Gk. παγκρατιαστής, fr.
παγκράτιον, 'pancratium'. See next word.
Derivative: pancratiast-ic, adj.

## pancratium
pancratium, п., athletic contest in wrestling and
boxing. — L., fr. Gk. παγκράτιον,^ complete
contest', fr. παν- (see pan-) and κράτος,
'strength, power, rule'. See -cracy.
Derivatives: pancrat-ic, adj., pancrat-ist, n.

## pancreas
pancreas, п., a gland lying behind the stomach
(anat.) — Medical L., fr. Gk. πάγκρεας, gen.
παγκρέατος, lit. 'entirely flesh', fr. παν- (see
pan-) and κρέας, 'flesh'. See creatine.
Derivatives: pancreat-ic, adj., pancreatin (q.v.),
pancreat-ism, п., pancreatitis (q.v.), pancreat-
ize, tr. v., pancreat-iz-ation, n.

## pancreatin
pancreatin, п., any of the enzymes of the
pancreatic juice (biochem). — Formed from prec. word
with suff. -in.

## pancreatitis
pancreatitis, п., inflammation of the pancreas

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:557 COLUMN:3 -->
(med.) — Medical L., formed fr. pancreas with
suff. -itis.

## panda
panda, 'п., a carnivorous mammal of the
Himalayas. — Native name.

## pandal
pandal, п., a shed (India). — Tamil, fr. OI. ban-
dhanah, 'a building', lit. 'a binding', fr. bandhab,
'a binding'. See bandanna.

## Pandean
Pandean, adj., pertaining to Pan. — Irregularly
formed fr. Gk. Παν, 'Pan'. — See Pan and -ean.

## pandect
pandect, п., a digest of Roman civil law made by
the order of the emperor Justinian in the 6th
cent. — F. pandecte, fr. Late L. pandecta, pan-
dectes, fr. Gk. πανδέκτης, 'a book that
contains everything', lit. 'all-containing', fr. παν-
(see pan-), and δέκτης, 'receiver', fr. δέκε-
σθαι, Att. δέχεσθαι, 'to receive', which is cogn.
with OI. ddksati, 'is apt, proper, pleasing', dak-
sab, 'able, apt, clever; competent, intelligent', L.
decet, decere, 'to be seemly or fitting'. See decent
and cp. the second element in choledoch,
synecdoche.

## pandemic
pandemic, adj., widely epidemic — Formed with
adj. sufT. -ic fr. Late L. pandemus, fr. Gk.
πάνδημος, πανδήμιος, 'pertaining to all the people', fr.
παν- (see pan-) and δήμος, 'people'. See demos.
Derivatives-, pandemic, п., pandemic-ity, n.

## pandemonium
pandemonium, п., the abode of the demons. —
ModL., the capital of Hell in Paradise Lost, an
epic poem by John Milton (1608-74); coined by
him fr. pan- and Late L. daemonium, 'inferior
divine being', in Eccles. L. 'evil spirit', fr. Gk.
δαιμόνιον, 'divine power; inferior divine being',
in Eccles. Gk. 'evil spirit', prop, subst. use of the
neut. of δαιμόνιος, 'belonging to a δαίμων', fr.
δαίμων, 'demon, devil'. See demon.
Derivatives: pandemoni-ac, pandemoni-an, pan-
demon-ic, adjs., pandemon-ism, n.

## pander
pander, п., a procurer, pimp. — ME. Pandare,
shortened fr. Pandarus, a character in
Boccaccio's Filostrato (in the form Pandaro), and in
Chaucer's Troylus and Cryseyde (in the forms
Pandare and Pandarus), fr. L. Pandarus, fr. Gk.
Πάνδαρος, leader of the Lycians in the Trojan
war, said to have procured for Troilus the love
of Chryseis. The spelling pander was prob.
influenced by the agent, suff. -er.
Derivatives: pander, intr. v., pander-age, п.,
pander-er, п., pander-ess, п., pander-ing, п.,
pander-ism, n.,pander-ize, intr. \.,pander-ly, adj.

## pandermite
pandermite, п., a hydrous calcium borate
(mineral.) — Named after Panderma (now Bandirma),
a port on the Black Sea (in Turkey), whence it
is exported. For the ending see subst. suff. -ite.

## pandiculation
pandiculation, п., a stretching of oneself, as on
wakening from sleep. — F., fr. L. pandiculdtus,
pp. of pandiculari, 'to stretch oneself, fr. pan-
dere, 'to spread out, extend, open', which is rel.
to patere, 'to be open', patulus, 'extended', and
cogn. with Gk. πεταννύναι, 'to spread out', fr.
I.-E. base *pet-, 'to spread', whence also OE.
fxdm, 'fathom'. See fathom and cp. pandy,
expand, expanse, patent, repand. For the ending
see the suff. -cule and -ation.

## pandit
pandit, n. — See pundit.

## pandora
pandora, pandore, п., a bandore — Jt. pandora,
pandura, fr. L. pandura, 'a three-stringed
musical instrument', fr. Gk. πανδοΰρα, which is of
unknown origin. Cp. bandore, banje, mandola,
mandolin, mandorla.

## Pandora
Pandora, п., the first mortal woman on whom all
the gods and goddesses bestowed gifts (Greek
mythol.) — L., fr. Gk. Πανδώρα, lit. 'giver of
all', fr. παν- (see pan-), and δώρον, 'gift', fr.
I.-E. base*i/o-, to give'. Seedate,'point of time',
and cp. Dorus, Dorothy and the second element
in Isidore.

## Pandora
Pandora, п., a genus of marine bivalves (zool.) —
Fr. prec. word.

## pandour
pandour, also pandoor, п., one of a force of
Croatian soldiers organized by Austria against the
Turks in 1741. — F., fr. G. Pandur, fr. Croat.
pandur, fr. earlier bandur, fr. ML. banderius,
'one fighting under a banner*. See banner.

## pandy
pandy, п., a stroke on the palm of the hand. — L.
pande {palmam), 'open (the palm of the hand)',
imper. of pandere. See pandiculation.

## Pandy
Pandy, п., a Sepoy mutineer. — From Pande, a
surname commonly used in Bengal and corre-

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:558 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: 531 | PANTISOCRACY -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:558 COLUMN:1 -->
sponding to OI. Panditah, lit. 'a learned man'.
See pundit.

## pane
pane, n. — ME. panne, pane, 'pane of glass,*
piece', fr. Οι. pan, fr. L.pannum, ace. of pannus,
'piece of cloth', which is cogn. with Goth, fana,
'piece of cloth', OHG., OS. fano, of s.m.; Gk.
πηνος, 'web*, πήνη, 'web, bobbin'. See pawn,
'pledge', and cp. words there referred to.
Derivatives: pane, tr. v., pan-ed, adj., pane-less,
adj.

## panegyric
panegyric, п., eulogy, laudation. — F. panegy-
r'tque, fr. L. panegyricus, fr. Gk. πανηγυρικός,
'for a public festival', fr. πανήγυρις, 'public
assembly, public festival', fr. παν- (see pan-) and
ίίγυρις, Aeol. form of αγορά, 'assembly', which
is rel. to άγείρειν, 'to assemble', and cogn. with
L- grex, gen. gregis, 'flock'. See gregarious and
ср.; agora, paregoric.
Derivatives:panegyric,panegyric-al, ad')S.,pane-
gyr-ist, n.

## panegyrize
panegyrize, tr. v., to write or pronounce a
panegyric upon, to eulogize; intr. v., to make
panegyrics. — Gk. πανηγυρίζειν, 'to celebrate a
public festival, to deliver a panegyric', fr. πανή-
γυρις. See panegyric and -ize.

## panel
panel, n. — ME., fr. OF. panel, fr. VL. 'pannel-
lus, corresponding to L. pannulus, dimin. of
pannus, 'piece of cloth'. Cp. It. pannello, OPro-
νεης. panel, 'a piece of cloth', which also derive
fr. VL. 'pannellus. See pane and cp. empanel,
panuelo.
Derivatives: panel, tr. v., panel(l)er, п.,
panelling, п., panel-isl,n.

## panetela
panetela, п., a cigar of a certain shape. — Sp.,
'sponge cake; a cigar', a diminutive formed fr.
L. panis, 'bread'. See pantry.

## pang
pang, п., a sudden pain. — Perh. fr. ME. prang,
prong, 'pang', and orig, identical with prong,
'point'.

## pangamy
pangamy, п., random mating. — Compounded
of pan- and Gk. γάμος, 'marriage'. See -gamy.
Derivatives:, pangam-ic, pangam-ous, adjs.,
pangam-ous-ly, adv.

## pangen
pangen, pangene, п., a hypothetical unit of the
cell (biol.) — G. Pangen, compounded of pan-
and the abbreviation of genesis.

## pangenesis
pangenesis, n. — Compounded of pan- and
genesis.

## pangenetic
pangenetic, adj. — Compounded of pan- and
genetic.
Derivative: pangenetic-al-ly, adv.

## Pangloss
Pangloss, п., an optimist (used in an ironical
sense). — Fr. F. Panglosse, the central character
in Voltaire's Candide (1758). The name is
compounded of pan- and Gk. γλώσσα, 'tongue'.
See gloss, 'interpretation'.
Derivatives: Pangloss-ian, Pangloss-ic, adjs.

## pangolin
pangolin, п., any of scaly, toothless mammals of
Asia and Africa. — Malay peng-guling, lit.
'roller', fr. pe-, peng- (the latter form is used
before g), a denominative prefix, and guling,
'to roll'; so called from its habit to roll itself
into a ball.

## panhandle
panhandle, п., a narrow strip of land. — Prop,
land resembling the handle of a pan.

## panhandle
panhandle, tr. and intr. v., to beg on the streets. —
Back formation from next word.

## panhandler
panhandler, п., a street beggar (slang). — Lit.
handler of a pan for alms.

## Panhellenic
Panhellenic, adj. — Compounded of pan- and
Hellenic. Cp. Gk. Πανέλληνες, 'all the Hellenes'.

## Panhellenism
Panhellenism, п., the idea of the political union
of all Greeks. — Compounded of pan- and
Hellenism.

## Panhellenist
Panhellenist, п., an adherent of Panhellenism. —
Compounded of pan- and Hellenist.

## panic
panic, п., panic grass. — ME. panik, fr. MF.
panic, 'Italian millet', fr. L. panicum, of s.m.,
fr. panus. See panicle.

## panic
panic, adj., inspired by sudden terror. — F. pant-
que, fr. Gk. πανικός, 'panic', lit. 'pertaining to
Pan', fr. Πδν, 'Pan'. See next word.

## panic
panic, п., panic, fear. — F. panique, fr. Gk. iti-
υικόν (shortened fr. πανικού δεϊμα), 'panic
fright', neut. of πανικός, 'panic' (adj.), lit.
'pertaining to Pan', fr. Παν, 'Greek god of the
woods and fields'; 'panic fear' orig. meant 'fear
caused by Pari. See Pan.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:558 COLUMN:2 -->
Derivatives: panick-ed, panick-y, adjs.

## panicle
panicle, п., a flower cluster — L. panicula, 'tuft,
panicle', dimin. formed fr. panus, 'tuft, swelling,
ear of millet', which is of uncertain origin. Cp.
paunch. Cp. also panocha.
Derivative: panicl-ed, adj.

## paniculate
paniculate, adj., arranged in panicles. — ModL.
paniculatus, fr. L. panicula, 'tufi'. See panicle
and adj. suff. -ate.
Derivatives: paniculat-ed, adj., paniculate-ly,
adv.

## Panicum
Panicum, п., a genus of plants, the panic grass
(bot.) — L., 'the Italian panic grass'. See panic,
'panic grass'.

## panification
panification, п., conversion into bread. — F., fr.
panifier, 'to make into bread', fr. Mh.panificare,
fr. L. panis, 'bread', and -ficare, fr. facere, 'to
make, do'. See pantry and -fication.

## panjandrum
panjandrum, п., a mock name for a pompous
personage. — A name invented by Samuel
Foote (1720-77), to test the memory of the
actor Macklin.

## panmixia
panmixia, п., indiscriminate interbreeding. —
ModL., fr. pan- and Gk. μίξις, 'a mingling,
mixing', from the stem of μίγνύναι, 'to mix,
mingle', which is cogn. with L. miscere, of s.m.
See mix and 1st -ia.

## pannage
pannage, п., the pasturage of swine. — ME.
pannage, fr. OF. pasnage, panage, VL. *pa~stionati-
cum, fr. L. pastio, gen. -onis, 'pasturing, feeding',
fr. pastus, pp. of pascere, 'to feed, pasture'. See
pastor and -age.

## panne
panne, п., a soft material resembling velvet. —
F. panne, 'soft material, plush', fr. OF., fr. L.
penna, 'feather'. See pen, 'feather'.

## pannier
pannier, п., basket. — ME. panier, fr. OF.
pannier, panier (F. panier), 'basket', fr. L. panarium,
'breadbasket', fr. panis, 'bread'. See pantry and
-ier.
Derivatives: pannier, tr. v., pannier-ed, adj.

## pannier
pannier, п., waiter in the dining hall of the Inner
Temple in London (colloq.) — Prob. fr. L. pana-
rius, 'pertaining to bread; bread-seller', fr.
panis. See prec. word.

## pannikin
pannikin, п., a small metal cup. — Dimin. of pan
(q.v.). For the ending see suff. -kin.

## panocha
panocha, п., a coarse Mexican sugar; a kind of
candy. — Sp. panocha, panoja, fr. L. panucula,
panicula, 'tuft, panicle'. See panicle.

## panoply
panoply, п., a complete suit of armor. — Gk.
πανοπλία, 'full armour', fr. πάνοπλος, 'in full
armour', fr. παν- (see pan-) and όπλα,
'arms, armor', pi. of δπλον, 'tool, implement,
weapon'. See hoplite. For the ending of panoply
see -y (representing Gk. -ίϊ).
Derivative: panopli-ed, adj.

## panoptic
panoptic, also panoptical, adj., visible in one
view. — Fr. Gk. παυόπτης, 'all-seeing',
compounded of παν- (see pan-) and I.-E. base *okw-,
'to see', whence also όπτός, 'seen; visible',
οπτικός, 'pertaining to sight'. See optic.

## panopticon
panopticon, п., 1) an optical instrument; 2) a
circular prison. — Compounded of pan- and Gk.
όπτικόν, neut. of οπτικός, 'pertaining to sight'.
See prec. word.

## panorama
panorama, n. — Lit. 'a complete view';
compounded of Gk. παν- (see pan-) and δράμα,
'that which is seen, view, sight', fr. όραν, 'to
see'. See cosmorama and cp. words there
referred to.
Derivatives: panoram-ic, panoram-ic-al, adjs.,
panoramic-at-ly, adv^panoram-ist, n.

## panpsychism
panpsychism, n. the doctrine that all nature has
a psychic aspect. — Lit. 'the doctrine that all
is psychic', compounded of pan-, Gk. ψυχή,
'soul' (see psyche), and suff. -ism.

## panpsychist
panpsychist, п., and adj., an adherent of
panpsychism. — See prec. word and -ist.
Derivative: panpsychist-ic, adj.

## Panslav
Panslav, Panslavic, adj., pertaining to all the
Slavic races; pertaining to Panslavism. — See
Panslavism.

## Panslavism
Panslavism, п., movement toward the
unification of all the Slavic races. — G. Panslavismus,
compounded of pan-, Slav and suff. -ism; orig.
a linguistic term coined in 1826 by Herkel in his
Elementa universalis linguae slavonicae.

## pansophism
pansophism, п., claim to universal wisdom. — Fr.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:558 COLUMN:3 -->
Gk. πάνσοφος, 'all-wise, all-clever',
compounded of παν- (see pan-) and σοφός, 'wise, clever'.
See sophism.

## pansophist
pansophist, n. — See prec. word and sophist.

## pansophy
pansophy, п., universal wisdom. — See
pansophism and -y (representing Gk. -[£).
Derivatives: pansoph-ic, pansoph-ic-al, adjs.,
pansoph-ic-al-ly, adv.

## pansy
pansy, n. — MF. (= F.) pensee, 'thought; pansy',
prop. pp. oipenser, 'to think', fr. L.pensare, 'to
weigh carefully, examine, ponder, consider'
(see pensive); so called because it is regarded as
the symbol of thought or remembrance.

## pant
pant, intr. and fr. v. — ME. panten, fr. MF. pan-
toisier, pantesier, 'to be out of breath' (whence
also F. pantois, 'out of breath, amazed'), fr. VL.
*pantasiare, 'to have visions', hence 'to be
amazed', fr. *panlasia, for L. phanlasia, fr. Gk.
φαντασία, 'appearance; imagination'. See
phantasm.
Derivatives: pant, п., pant-ing, adj., pant-ing-ly,
adv.

## pant-
pant-, form of panto- before a vowel.

## Pantagruel
Pantagruel, п., a character in Rabelais' work of
that name.
Derivative: Pantagruel-ian, adj.

## Pantagruelism
Pantagruelism, п., coarse humor resembling
that of Pantagruel. — F. pantagruelisme, fr.
Pantagruel. See prec. word and -ism.

## Pantagruelist
Pantagruelist, п., an imitator of Pantagruel. —
F. pantagrue/iste, fr. Pantagruel. See Pantagruel
and -ist.
Derivative: Pantagruelist-ic, adj.

## pantalets
pantalets, also pantalettes, n. pi. — Dimin.
formed fr. pantaloon.

## pantaloon
pantaloon, п., in old Italian comedies, a foolish
old man wearing tight trousers. — MF. (= F.)
Pantalon, fr. It. Pantalone, Pantaleone, a
character representing the Venetian in Italian comedy,
from the Venetian saint Pantaleone, a name of
Greek origin, which lit. means 'entirely lion'.
See pan- and leonine.
Derivatives: pantaloon, intr. v., pantaloon-ery,
n.

## pantaloons
pantaloons, n. pi., trousers. — Orig. 'tight
trousers , i.e. 'trousers resembling those worn by the
pantaloon'. See prec. word.

## pantechnicon
pantechnicon, п., 1) orig. a bazaar where all
kinds of things of art were sold; 2) a warehouse
where furniture is stored; 3) a furniture van. —
Coined fr. pan- and Gk. τεχνικόν, neut. of
τεχνικός, 'pertaining to art', fr. τέχνη, 'art'. See
techmc.

## pantheism
pantheism, n. — F. pantheisme, lit. 'the doctrine
that 'all is God'; formed on analogy of pan-
theiste (see pantheist) fr. pan- and Gk. θεός,
'God'. See 1st theism.

## pantheist
pantheist, п., an adherent of pantheism. —
Coined by the Irish deist John Toland (1670-
1722) in 1705. Cp. Gk. πάνθειος, 'common to
all gods', fr. παν- (see pan-) and θεός, 'god'. See
prec. word and -ist.
Derivatives: pantheist-ic, pantheist-ic-al, adjs.,
pantheist-ic-al-ly, adv.

## panthelism
panthelism, п., the doctrine that all is based on
will. — Coined by the German philosopher
Arthur Schopenhauer (1788-1860) fr. pan- and
Gk! θέλειν, 'to will', which is prob. cogn. with
OSlav. ieliti, 'to wish', Arm. gei-J, 'wish'. For
the ending see suff. -Ism.

## pantheon
pantheon, п., a temple for all the gods. — L.
Pantheon, fr. Gk. Πάνθειον (scil. ιερόν), 'temple
consecrated to all gods', esp. denoting the
Pantheon at Rome, prop. neut. of πάνθειος, 'of
all gods', which is compounded of παν- (see
pan-) and θείος, 'of, or sacred to, a god', fr.
θεός, 'god'. See theo-.

## panther
panther, п., the leopard. — ME. pantere, panter,
fr. OF. pantere (F. panthere), fr. L. panthera, fr.
Gk. πανθήρ, which is of Indian origin; cp. OI.
pundarikam, 'tiger', which means perh. lit. 'the
yellowish (animal)', and is rel. to pandarah,
'whitish yellow'.
Derivative: panther-ess, n.

## pantile
pantile, n. — Compounded of pan and tile.
Derivatives: pantil-ed, adj., pantil-ing, a.

## pamisocracy
pamisocracy, п., ideal (Utopian) community in
which all were to have the same rights. — Lit.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:559 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: PANTLER | 532 -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:559 COLUMN:1 -->
'equal rule of all'; coined fr. Gk. παντ- (see
pant-) and ίσοκρατία, 'equality-of power'. See
isocracy.

## pantler
pantler, п., the officer in charge of the pantry
(archaic). — ME- pantere, pantelere, pantlere,
fr. OF. panetier, 'pantler', fr. ML. panetarius,
'baker', fr. L. panis, 'bread'. See pantry. The
change of ME. pantere to pantelere, pantlere, is
prob. due to the influence oibotelere, 'butler*.

## panto-
panto-, before a vowel pant-, combining form
meaning *all\ — Gk. παντο-, παντ-, fr.
παντός, gen. of πας (masc), παν (neut.), 'all'. See
pan-.

## pantofle
pantofle, pantoffle, п., slipper. — ME.pantufle, fr.
MF. (= F.)pantoufie, fr. It. pantofola, fr. MGk.
παντόφελλος, 'whole cork', which is
compounded of Gk. παντο- (see panto-) and φελλός,
'cork'. See phello-.

## pantograph
pantograph, п., an instrument for copying
drawings, plans etc. — Lit. 'all-writer*, compounded
of panto- and Gk. -γράφος, fr. γράφειν, 'to
write'. See -graph.
Derivatives: pantograph, tr. v., pantograph-er,
п., pantograph-ic, pantograph-ic-al, adjs., pan-
tograph-ic-al-ly, adv., pantograph-y, n.

## pantology
pantology, п., a system comprehending all
knowledge. — Compounded of panto- and Gk.
-λογία, fr. -λόγος, 'one who speaks (in a
certain manner); one who deals (with a certain
topic)'. See-logy.
Derivatives: pantolog-ic, pantolog-ic-al, adjs.,
pantolog-ist, n.

## pantomime
pantomime, п., an actor in a dumb show; a dumb
show. — F., fr. L. pantomimus, fr. Gk. παντό-
μϊμος, 'pantomimic actor', lit. 'all-imitating',
compounded of παντο- (see panto-) and μίμος,
'imitator'. See mime.
Derivatives: pantomime, tr. and intr. v., pan-
tomim-ic, adj. anan.,pantomim-ic-al, ad].,pan-
iomim-ic-al-ly, adv., pantomim-ic-ry, п., pan-
tomim-ist, n.

## pantoscope
pantoscope, п., a wide-angled lens. —
Compounded of panto- and Gk. -σκόποον, fr. σκο-
πεΐν, 'to look at, examine'. See -scope.
Derivative: pantoscop-ic, adj.

## pantothenate
pantothenate, п., a salt of pantothenic acid
(chem.) — See next word and chem. suflf. -ate.

## pantothenic
pantothenic, adj., designating a B-complex
vitamin acid, C9Hj705N (chem.) — Formed with
suff. -ic fr. Gk. πάντοθεν, 'from all quarters, on
every side* (see panto-); so called in allusion to
the various sources in which this acid was found.

## pantoum
pantoum, п., a series of rhyming quatrains. —
Malay; cp. pantun.

## pantry
pantry, n. — ME. pane trie, pantrie', fr. OF. pane-
terie, '-a place where bread is kept1, fr. ML.
panetaria, panitaria, 'a place where bread is
made', fr. L. panis, 'bread', fr. I.-E. base *ρά-,
'to tend, keep, pasture, feed, guard, protect',
whence also ρά-bulum, 'food, fother\ See food
and cp. pabulum. Cp. also panada, panetela,
panification, pannage, pannier, pantier,
companion, company, impanate.

## pants
pants, n. pi. — Abbreviation of pantaloons.

## pantun
pantun, п., a Malay verse form consisting of four
lines rhyming abab. — Malay. Cp. pantoum.

## panuelo
panuelo, п., a kerchief. — Sp., 'kerchief,
handkerchief, dimin. of paho, fr. L. pannum, ace. of
pannus, 'piece of cloth'. See pawn, 'pledge*, and
cp. pane, panel.

## Panurge
Panurge, п., companion of Pantagruel in
Rabelais' work of this name. — F., fr. Gk.
πανούργος, 'ready to do anything', compounded of
παν- (see pan-) and ε*ργαν, 'work', which is cogn.
with OE. weorc, etc., 'work*. See work and cp.
ergon and words there referred to.

## pap
pap, п., nipple. — ME. pappe, prob. of Scand.
origin; from the I.-E. imitative base *pap-, 'to
swell', whence also L. papula, 'a swelling,
pimple', papilla, 'nipple', Lith. papas, 'nipple',
Lett, papa, papis, 'swelling, pustule'. See papula.

## pap
pap, п., soft food for infants. — A child's lip
word; cp. MHG., Du. pap, G. Pappe, 'pap', L.
pappa, 'pap', pappare, 'to eat pap, to eat', and
Gk. πάππα (voc), Ό father'. See papa, 'father',
and cp. pamper. Pap in this sense is not rel. to
pap, 'nipple'.
Derivative:pap, tr. v., to feed with pap.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:559 COLUMN:2 -->

## papa
papa, п., father. — F. papa, fr. L. papa, 'father',
orig. a child's lip word for father. Cp.Gk. πάππα
(voc), *o father', πάπας,'father',
πάππος,'grandfather, ancestor'» which are also orig. child's lip
words. L.pappa,*pap', is of the same origin; see
pap, 'food'. Cp. pappus.

## papa
papa, п., pope; parish priest. — Eccles L. pupa,
'bishop; pope', fr. L. papa, 'father'. See prec.
word and cp. pope.

## papable
papable, adj., qualified for the papacy. — F., fr.
It. papabile. See prec. word and -able.

## papacy
papacy, n. — ME. papacie, fr. ML. papatia, fr.
Eccles. L. papa, 'pope'. See papa and -асу.

## papain
papain, п., a vegetable enzyme (biochem.) —
Formed fr. papaya with subst. suff. -in.

## papal
papal, adj. — ME., fr. MF. (= F.) papal, fr.
Eccles. L.papaliS) fr. papa, 'pope'. See papa and
adj. suff. -al.
Derivatives: papal-ism, п., papal-ist, п., papal-
ist-ic, adj., papal-ize, tr. and intr. v., papal-iz-
ation, п., papal-iz-er, n.
Ρ a paver, п., a genus of plants, the poppy (bot.)
— L. papaver, 'poppy', which prob. stands for
*papd-wes, and derives from the imitative base
*pap-, 'to swell, blow', whence also papula, 'a
swelling, pimple'. See papula and cp. poppy. For
the formation of the word cp. L. cadaver, 'dead
body, carcass', fr*. cadere, 'to fall'.

## Papaveraceae
Papaveraceae, n. pi., the poppy family (bot.) —
Formed with suff, -aceae fr. L. papaver, 'poppy'.
See prec. word.

## papaveraceous
papaveraceous, adj. — See prec. word and -ace-
ous.

## papaverine
papaverine, п., an alkaloid (C20H21NO4) obtained
from opium (chem.) — See Papaver and chem.
suff. -ine.

## papaverous
papaverous, adj., pertaining to, or resembling,
poppy. — See Papaver and -ous.

## papaw
papaw, п., the papaya. — Sp. papayo, 'papaw
tree', papaya, 'fruit of the papaw tree'; of
Caribbean origin. Cp.^papaya.

## papaya
papaya, п., 1) a tropica] tree; 2) its fruit. — Sp.,
'fruit of the papaw tree', fr. papayo, 'papaw
tree'. See papaw.

## paper
paper, n. — ME. papire, papir, fr. OF. (= F.)
papier, fr. L. papfrus, 'papyrus, paper made of
papyrus stalk', fr. Gk. πάπυρος, 'papyrus'. See
papyrus.
Derivatives: paper, tr. v., paper-mg, п., paper-y,
adj.

## papeterie
papeterie, п., a box for paper and other writing
materials. — F., fr. papetier, 'papermaker', fr.
papier, 'paper'. See prec. word and -ery.

## papier-mache
papier-mache, п., paper pulp molded into various
objects. — F., lit. 'chewed paper', fr. L. papyrus,
'papyrus, paper', and masticatus, pp. of masti-
care, 'to chew'. See paper and masticate.

## PapiHo
PapiHo, п., a genus of butterflies (zool.) — L.
papilio, 'butterfly'; cogn. with OE. fifealde,
'butterfly', OS.fifoIdara, ON.fzfrildi, OHG. vivaltra,
MHG. vivalter, G. Falter, of s.m. These words
derive from the reduplicated form of the I.-E.
base *pel-, 'to shake, swing'. Cp. Lith. piepala,
Lett, paipala, 'quail', which are from the same
reduplicated base. Cp. papillon, pavilion. For
derivatives of the simple base *pel- see polemic.
Derivative: papilion-aceous, adj.

## Papilionidae
Papilionidae, n. pi., name of a family of
butterflies (zool.) — See prec. word and -idae.

## papilla
papilla, п., any nipplelike protuberance. — L.,
'nipple', rel. to papula, 'a swelling, pimple'. See
papula.
Derivatives: papill-ar, papill-ary, papill-ate, pa-
pill-ose, adjs., papill-os-ity, n.

## papilloma
papilloma, п., tumor on the skin (med.) — A
ModL. hybrid formed fr. L. papilla, 'nipple',
with suff. -oma (fr. Gk. -ωμα).
Derivative: papillomat-ous, adj.

## papillon
papillon, п., name of a breed of dog. — F., lit.
'butterfly', fr. L.papiliortem, zcc.of papilio,
'butterfly' (see Papilio); so called from the shape of
its ears. Cp. papiliote.

## papillote
papillote, п., curl paper. — F., back formation fr.
papil/oter, 'to blink,.twinkle; to put (hair) into
curl paper', fr. papillot, 'a small butterfly', fr,
papillon, 'butterfly'. See papillon.

## papist
papist, п., an adherent of the Pope— MF. (= F.)
papiste, fr. pape, 'Pope', fr. Eccles. L. papa,

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:559 COLUMN:3 -->
'pope'. See papacy and -ist.
Derivatives: papist-icy papist-ic-al, adjs., papist-
ic-al-ly, aav.,papist-ry, n.

## papoose
papoose, п., a North American Indian baby. —
Algonquizn papoos, 'child'.

## pappus
pappus, п., a downy appendage of certain fruits
(bot.) — L., 'an old man, grandfather; the
woolly, hairy seed of certain plants', fr. Gk.
πάππος, 'an old man, grandfather', orig. a
child's lip word. See papa, 'father', and cp. the
second element in Aplopappus.
Derivatives: papp-ose, papp-ous, papp-y, adjs.

## pappy
pappy, n.} father. — Dimin. of papa.

## paprika
paprika, п., the fruit of Capsicum xetragonum. —
G. Paprika, fr. Hung, paprika, fr. Serbian
paprika, a dimin. formed fr. ModGk. πίπερι,
'pepper', fr. Gk. πέπερι. See pepper.

## Papuan
Papuan, n. and adj. — Fr. Malay papuwah,
'curled, frizzle-haired'. For the ending see suff.
-an.

## papula
papula, papule, п., a pimple. — L. papula, 'a
swelling, pimple', from the imitative base *pap-, 'to
swell', whence also OI. pippali, 'berry,
peppercorn', Lith. papas, 'nipple', Lett, papa, papis,
'swelling, pustule'; cp. pap, 'nipple'. The
nasalized form of the same base appears in L. pam-
pirtus, 'tendril of vine'; see pampiniform and cp.
pimple. Cp. also pepper.
Derivatives: papul-ar, papul-ate, papul-at-ed,
adjs., papul-ation, п., papul-ose, papul-ous, adjs.

## papuliferous
papuliferous, adj., having pimples. — Lit.
'bearingpimples'; compounded of L.papula, 'a
swelling, pimple'» and ferre, 'to bear, carry'. See
prec. word and -ferous.

## papulo-
papulo-, combining form meaning 'pertaining to
papulae'. — See papula.

## papyro-
papyro-, combining form meaning 'papyrus', —
Fr. Gk. πάπυρος. See papyrus.

## papyrograph
papyrograph, п., an instrument for
multiplying copies of writings. — Compounded of
papyro- and Gk. -γράφος, fr. γράφειν, 'to write'.
See -graph.
Derivatives .papyrograph, tr. \.,papyrograph-er,
R-, papyrograph-ic, adj., papyrograph-y, n.

## papyrology
papyrology, п., the study of papyri. —τ
Compounded of papyro- and Gk. -λογία, fr. -λόγος,
'one who speaks (in a certain manner); one who
deals (with a certain topic)'. See -logy.
Derivatives: papyrolog-ic-al, adj., papyrolog-ist,
n.

## papyrus
papyrus, n. — ME. papirus, fr. L. papyrus, fr.
Gk. πάπυρος, 'papyrus', which is of unknown
etymology; said to be of Egyptian origin. Cp.
paper, taper.
Derivatives: papyr-aceous, papyr-a/, papyr-ian,
papyr-ine, papyr-itious, adjs.

## par
par, п., equality, equal value. — L. par, 'equal'.
See pair, and cp. words there referred to.
Derivative: par, tr. v.

## par
par, n. (co/loq.) — Short for paragraph.

## par-
par-, form of para-, 'beside', before a vowel.

## par-
par-, pref. in words of French origin meaning
'by'. — F. par-, fr. par, 'through, by', fr. L. per.
See per-.

## para
para, п., name of a Turkish and a Yugoslavian
coin. — Turk, parah, fr. Pers. parah, 'piece'.

## para-
para-, before a vowel par-, pref. used in the
senses 'by the side of, beside, past, beyond;
contrary, wrong, irregular, abnormal'. — Gk. πάρα-,
παρ-, fr. παρά, from beside, beyond, against,
contrary to', cogn. with OI. para, 'beyond',pro-,
'before, forward, forth', Avestic para, paro,
'before', Hitt.para, 'on, forth', Gk. πρό, 'before',
L. pro, 'before, for, in favor of', prae, 'before',
per, 'through', Goth, faiir, 'along', OE. for-, OfT,
away'. See fore, adv., and cp. per, peri-, pre-,
preter-, pro-,

## para-
para-, combining form meaning 'that which
protects from', as in parachute, parapet, parasol. —
Fr. It. para, imper. of par-are, 'to ward off', fr.
L. parare, 'to prepare'. See pare and cp. parry,
spar, 'to fight with the fists'.

## parabasfs
parabasfs, п., choral part in Greek comedy. —
Gk. παράβασης, 'a going aside', fr. παραβαίνει,
'to go aside', fr. παρά (see para-, 'beside') and
βαίυειν, 'to go'. See basis.

## parablast
parablast, п., the yolk of an ovum (embryol.) —
Compounded of para-, 'beside', and Gk. βλα-

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:560 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: 533 | PARALLACTIC -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:560 COLUMN:1 -->
στός, 'bud, sprout, shoot'. See -blast.
Derivative: parablast-ic, adj.

## parable
parable, n. — ME-, fr. MF. parabole, parable (F.
parable), fr. L. parabola, 'comparison, parable,
speech', fr. Gk. παραβολή, 'comparison,
parable1, lit. 'a throwing beside, juxtaposition', fr.
παραβάλλειν, 'to throw beside', fr. παρά (see
para-, 'beside') and βάλλειν, 'to throw'. See
ballistic and cp. parabola, pa I a bra, parol, parole,
which are doublets of parable.
Derivative: parable, tr. and intr. v.

## parabola
parabola, п., one of the three conic sections (ge-
om.) — ModL., fr. Gk. παραβολή, 'a throwing
beside, laying side by side; application,
comparison, analogy'; see prec. word. The
Pythagoreans used the word παραβολή if the base of a
figure, that was to be constructed so that it
should be equal in area to a given figure of
different shape, proved to be equal to the base of
the original figure. Apollonius of Perga, 'the
Great Geometer', who lived in the 3rd cent.
B.C.E., applied this term for the first time to
denote the parabola (in his Conica Ι, Π), in
reference to the circumstance that the square on
the ordinate is equal to a rectangle whose height
is equal to the abscissa, applied to the
parameter; see T. L..Heath, Apollonius of Perga,
Treatise on Conic Sections, Cambridge
University Press, 1896, Introduction, p. LXXX. Cp.
ellipse and hyperbola.

## parabolic
parabolic, adj., I) pertaining to a parable; 2)
resembling a parabola. — L. parabolicus, fr. Gk.
παραβολικός, 'expressive of comparison,
figurative', fr. παραβολή. See parabola and adj. suff.
-ic, resp. also -al.
Derivatives: parabolic-al, adj., parabolic-al-ism,
п., parabolic-al-ly, adv.

## parabolist
parabolist, п., one who lells parables. — Formed
with suff. -ist fr. Gk. παραβολή, 'comparison,
analogy'. See parable,

## parabolize
parabolize, tr. v., t) to tell in a parable or
parables; 2) to make parabolic in shape. — Formed
with suff. -ize fr. Gk. παραβολή, 'comparison,
analogy'. See parable, resp. parabola.
Derivatives: paraboliz-ation, п., paraboliz-er, n.

## paraboloid
paraboloid, п., a solid generated by the rotation
of a parabola around its axis {geom.) —
Compounded of parabola and Gk. -οε^δής, 'like',
fr. είδος, 'form, shape'. See -oid.

## paracentesis
paracentesis, п., perforation (surgery) —
Medical L., fr. Gk. παρακέντησις, fr. παρακεντεΐν,
'to pierce at the side', fr. παρά (see para-,
'beside') and κεντεΐν, 'to prick, goad, pierce'.
See center.

## paracentric
paracentric, also paracentrical, adj., moving from
the center. — Compounded of para-, 'beside',
and centric, resp. centrical.
Derivative: paracentric, n.

## parachor
parachor, п., name of a constant in chemistry. —
Coined fr. para-, 'beside', and Gk. χώρος,
'definite space*, which is rel. to χώρα, 'space,
country', χωρίς, 'separately, apart'. See chori-.

## parachordal
parachordal, adj., situated beside the notochord
(embryol.) — Coined fr. para-, 'beside', chord,
and adj. suff. -al.

## parachroma
parachroma, п., discoloration {med.) — Coined
fr. para-, 'beside', and Gk. χρώμα, 'color of the
skin, color'. See chrome.
Derivatives: parachromat-ism, п., parachromat-
ic, adj.

## parachronism
parachronism, п., chronological error in which a
date is set too late. — Irregularly formed fr.
para-, 'beside, beyond', and Gk. χρόνος, 'time'.
See chronic and -ism and cp. anachronism, me-
tachronlsm.

## parachute
parachute, n. — F., lit. 'that which protects', a
hybrid coined by the French aeronaut Francois
Blanchard (Π53-1809), fr. para-, 'that which
protects', and chute, 'fair. See chute.
Derivatives '.parachute, tr. and intr. \.,parachut-
i'c, adj., parachut-ism, п., parachut-ist, n.

## paraclete
paraclete, п., advocate. — OF. paraclet, fr. Late
L. paracletus, fr. Gk. παράκλητος, 'advocate',
verbal adj. of παρακαλεΐν, 'to call to aid, to
summon, invite, console, exhort, encourage',
fr. παρά (see para-, 'beside') and καλεΐν, 'to

## call'
call', which is cogn. with L. calare, 'to proclaim,

## call
call, shout', clamare, 'to shout, cry aloud,

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:560 COLUMN:2 -->
call, declare', clamor, 'a loud cry', clarus, 'clear,
bright'. See claim, v., and cp. words there
referred to.

## paracme
paracme, п., the stage of degeneration after
maturity (biol.) — Gk. παρακμή, 'point at which
the prime is past, decay', fr. παρά (see para-,
'beside, beyond') and ακμή, 'point, edge, prime
of life'. See acme.

## paracusia
paracusia, paracusis, п., abnormal sense of
hearing (med.) — Gk. παράκουσις, 'defect of
hearing\fr. 7tapa(seepara-,'beside'')andootouot^,
'hearing', fr. άκούει,ν, 'to hear'. See acoustic
and cp. words there referred to.

## paracymene
paracymene, п., a colorless liquid (C10HJ4)
obtained from oils of cumin, thyme, etc. (chem.) —
Compounded of para-, 'beside', and cymene.

## parade
parade, n. — F., fr. Sp. parada, 'halt, stop,
suspension, parade', fr. parar, 'to stop, halt,
prepare', re], to It. parare, 'to prepare, ward off', fr.
L. parare, 'to prepare'. See pare and -ade and
cp. para-, 'that which protects'.
Derivatives: parade, tr. and intr. v.,parad-er, п.,
parad-ing, adj., parad-ing-ly, adv.

## paradigm
paradigm, п., example (esp. in grammar) — F.
paradigme, fr. Late L. paradigma, fr. Gk.
παράδειγμα, 'pattern, model', fr. παραδεικνύναι., 'to
exhibit, represent', fr. παρά (see para-, 'beside')
and δεικνύυαι, 'to show', which is cogn. with L.
dicere, 'to show, te]J\ See diction.

## paradigmatic
paradigmatic, paradigmatical, adj. — Gk.
παραδειγματικός, 'serving as a pattern or model', fr.
παράδειγμα, gen. παραδείγματος. See prec.
word and adj. suff. -ic, resp. also -al.
Derivative: paradigmatical-ly, adv.

## paradisaic
paradisaic, paradisaical, adj. — Formed fr.
paradise on analogy of Hebraic.
Derivative: paradisaical-ly, adv.

## paradise
paradise, n. — ME. paradis, fr. OF. (= F.) para-
dis, fr. Late L. paradisus, fr. Gk. παράδεισος,
'park, the garden of Eden, paradise', a word of
Old Persian origin; cp. Avestic pairidaeza, 'an
enclosure', whence Heb. pardes, 'park, garden'
(whence Aram, pardes, pardesa, of s.m.).
Avestic pairidaeza is compounded of pairi, 'around',
and daeza, 'wall'. The first element is cogn. with
Gk. περί, 'around, about'; see peri-. The second
element is cogn. with Olr. digen, 'firm, solid'
(orig. 'kneaded into a compact mass'), Gk.
τείχος, 'walT, L.fingere, 'to form, fashion', Goth.
deigan, 'to smear', OE. dag, etc., 'dough'. See
dough and cp. deha, fiction and the first element
in dizdar. Cp. also parvis, which is a doublet of
paradise.
Derivatives: paradisaic (q.v.), paradisiac(al)
(q.v.), paradis-ial, paradis-ian, paradis-ic, para-
dis-ic-al, adjs.

## Paradisea
Paradisea, п., the typical genus of birds of
paradise. — ModL., fern, of ML. paradiseus,
'pertaining to paradise', fr. Late L. paradisus. See
prec. word.
Derivative: paradise-an, adj., pertaining to
bird's of paradise.

## paradisiacal
paradisiacal, also paradisiac adj., pertaining to,
or resembling, paradise. — Late L. paradisiacusy
fr. L.paradisus. See paradise and suff. -ac and -al.

## parados
parados, п., parapet behind a trench. — F., prop,
'defense from the rear', coined fr. para-, 'that
which protects*, and F. dos, 'back', fr. L.
dorsum. See dorso-,

## paradox
paradox, п., a statement seemingly absurd, yet
really true. — F. paradoxe, fr. L. paradoxum,
fr. Gk. παράδοξον, 'paradox', prop. neut. of the
adjective παράδοξος, 'contrary to
expectation-, incredible, marvelous', which is formed fr.
παρά (see para-, 'beside, contrary to') and δόξα,
Opinion, expectation'. See doxastic and cp.
words there referred to.
Derivatives: paradox, tr. and intr. v.,
paradoxal, paradox-ial, paradox-ic-al, adjs., paradox-ic-
al-ly, adv., paradox-ic-al-ity, п., paradox-ic-al-
ness, п., paradox-ist, n.

## paradoxy
paradoxy, п., a paradox; paradoxical quality. —
ϋ^παραδοξία, 'marvelousness', fr. παράδοξος.
See prec word and -y (representing Gk. -ία).

## paraffin
paraffin, n. — Lit., 'of small affinity', coined by
the German chemist Karl von Reichenbach
(1788-1869) in 1830 fr. L. par(um), 'little', and
affinis, 'connected with, related to'; so called

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:560 COLUMN:3 -->
by him because of its comparative lack of
chemical affinity. L. parum is cogn. with parvus,
'small',paucus, 'little', Gk. παϋρος, 'small'; see
paucity. For the etymology of L. affinis seeaffine.

## paraform
paraform, п., a white powder (chem. )—
Abbreviation of paraformaldehyde. See para-, 'beside',
and formaldehyde.

## paragenesis
paragenesis, п., the formation 'of minerals in
close contact (geol.) — Lit.'mutual formation'.
Coined fr. para-, 'beside', and Gk. γένεσις,
Origin, source, birth, descent, race'. See genesis.

## para genetic
para genetic, adj. — See prec. word and genetic.

## paragoge
paragoge, п., addition of a sound at the end of a
word (grammar). — Late L. paragoge, fr. Gk,
παραγωγή, 'a leading by or past, variation,
addition', fr. παράγει, 'to lead by or past', fr.
παρά (see para-, 'beside') and άγει,ν, 'to lead',
which is cogn. with L. agere, 'to set in motion,
drive, lead'. See agent, adj., and cp. -agogne and
words there referred to.
Derivatives: paragog-ic, paragog-ic-al, adjs.,
paragog-ic-al-ly, adv.

## paragon
paragon, п., a pattern of excellence. — F. paragon
(now parangon), fr. It. paragone, 'touchstone,
test, comparison, model', fr. Gk. παρακοναν,
'to sharpen, whet', fr. παρά (see para-, 'beside')
and άκόνη, 'whetstone', which is re], to άκή,
'point', ακίς, 'pointed object, needle', #κρας,
'sharp', fr. I.-E. base *ak-, 'sharp, pointed;
stone*. See acrid.
Derivative: paragon, tr. v., to compare.

## paragonite
paragonite, п., a kind of mica resembling
common mica, but containing sodium instead of
potassium (mineral.) — Formed fr. Gk.
παράγων, 'misleading', pres. part, of παράγείν, 'to
lead by or past; to lead aside, mislead'. See
paragoge and subst. suff. -ite.

## paragraph
paragraph, n. — OF. (= F.) paragraphe, fr. ML.
paragraphias, fr. Gk. παράγραφος, 'a line drawn
in the margin', lit. 'anything written beside', fr.
παρά (see para-, 'beside') and -γράφος, fr.
γράφείν, 'to write'. See -graph. Cp. paraph,
which is a doublet οι paragraph.
Derivatives: paragraph, tr. and intr. v., para·
graph-er, п.,paragraph-ic, paragraph-ic-al, adjs.,
paragraph-ic-al-ly, adv., paragraph-ist, n.,para-
graph-ist-ic-al, adj., paragraph-y, n.

## Paraguay tea
Paraguay tea, mate. — Named after the S.
American republic Paraguay.

## paraheliotropic
paraheliotropic, adj. — See next word and adj.
suff. -ic.

## paraheliotropism
paraheliotropism, п., tendency of leaves to place
themselves in a plane parallel to the sun's rays.
— Coined fr. para-, 'beside', and heliotropism.

## parahypnosis
parahypnosis, п., sleep suggestive of, but not
necessarily caused by, hypnosis. — Coined fr.
para-, 'beside', and hypnosis.

## parahypnotic
parahypnotic, adj. — See prec. word and hypnotic.

## parakeet
parakeet, also spelled parrakeet, n. — MF.
paroquet (F. perroquet), fr. It. parrocchetto, prop.
'little priest', a diminutive facetiously formed
fr. parroco, 'parish priest', fr. Eccles L. paro-
chus, for paroecus, fr. Gk. πάροικος, 'living
beside'. See parish and cp. parrot. Cp. also Pro-
νεης. perucat, 'resembling a parrot; fine hair
dress' (see peruke).

## parakinesis
parakinesis, parakinesia, п., irregular movement
of motor. — ModL., coined fr. para-, 'beside',
and Gk. κΐνησις, 'movement', fr. κίνεΐν, 'to
move'. See kinesis.

## parakinetic
parakinetic, adj. — See prec. word and kinetic.

## parakite
parakite, п., a tailless kite used in meteorology.
— Coined fr. para-, 'beside', and kite,

## paralalia
paralalia, п., a speech defect. — Medical L.,
coined fr. para-, 'beside', and Gk. λαλιά, 'talk,
chat, speech', fr. λαλός, 'talkative, loquacious'.
SeeLalageandcp. Eulalia, mogilalia.Cp. also lull.

## paraldehyde
paraldehyde, п., a hypnotic drug. — Coined fr.
para-, 'beside', and aldehyde.

## paraleipsis
paraleipsis, paralipsis, п., a rhetorical device to
stress a point by stating that it is too obvious to
be mentioned. — Gk. παράλειψες, 'neglect,
disregard, omission', fr. παραλείπειν, 'to leave
out, omit', fr. παρά (see para-, 'beside') and λε£-
πειν, 'to leave'. See relinquish and cp. eclipse,

## ellipse
ellipse, ellipsis, elliptoid.

## parallactic
parallactic, adj., pertaining to a parallax. — Gk.
παραλλακτικός, 'pertaining to change', fr. πα-
