<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:561 COLUMN:1 -->
ραλλακτός, 'liable to change7, verbal adj. of
παραλλάσσει, 'to ci.ange'. See next word and adj.
suff. -ic.
Derivative: parallactic-al-ly, adv.

## parallax
parallax, п., apparent change in the position of
an object. — F. parallaxe, fr. Gk. παράλλαξις,
'change*, fr. παραλλάσσειν, 'to change', fr.
παρά (see para-, 'beside') and άλλάσσειν, 'to
change', fr. άλλος, 'other'. See alio- and cp. al-
lactite and words there referred to.

## parallel
parallel, adj. — F. parallele, fr. L. parallelus, fr.
Gk. παράλληλος, 'parallel', fr. παρά (see para-,
'beside') and αλλήλων, 'of one another',
reduplication of όίλλος, 'other*. See allele-.
Derivatives: parallel, n. and tr. v.,parallel-ism,
п., parallel-ist, п., parallel-ist-ic, adj.

## parallelize
parallelize, tr. v., to render parallel. — Gk.
παραλληλίζει, 'to place side by side*, fr.
παράλληλος. See prec. word and -ize.

## parallelepiped
parallelepiped, paralieiopipedon, п., a prism with
six faces, each of which is a parallelogram
(geom.) — Gk. παραλληλεπίπεδον, 'body with
parallel surfaces', fr. παράλληλος, 'parallel', and
έπίπεδον, 'plane surface', prop. neut. of the adj.
επίπεδο;, 'on the ground, plane, superficial', fr.
έπί, 'on', and πέδον, 'ground, earth*, which is
cogn. with OI. padam, 'step, track', Arm. het,
gen. hetoy, 'track', Lith. ρέάά, 'track', and L.
peda, 'footstep', pes, gen. pedis, 'foot*, ON./ei,
'step*, Goth, fotus, OE.fot, 'foot'. See parallel,
epi- and foot.

## parallelogram
parallelogram, n.—F. parallelogramme, fr. LateL.
parallelogrammum, fr. Gk. παραλληλόγραμμον,
prop. neut. of the adj. παραλληλόγραμμος,
'bounded by parallel lines', fr. παράλληλος,
'parallel', and the "stem of γράφειν, 'to write'. See
parallel and -gram.
TbQrivalives-.parallelogrammat-ic, parallelogram·
mat-ic-al, parallelogramm-ic, parallelogramm-
ic-al, adjs.

## paralogism
paralogism, n., false reasoning. — F. paralogisme,
fr. L. paralogismus, fr. Gk. παραλογισμός,
'false reasoning', fr. παραλογίζεσθαι. See
paralogize and -ism.

## puralogist
puralogist, п., one who reasons falsely. — F.para-
logiste, fr. Gk. παραλογιστής, 'one who
reasons falsely', fr. παραλογίζεσθαί. See next
word.
Derivative: paralogist-ic, adj.

## paralogize
paralogize,intr. v., to reason falsely— Gk. παρα-
λογίζεσθαι, 'to reason falsely', fr. παράλογος,
'beyond reason, beyond calculation', fr. παρά
(see para-, 'beside, beyond") and λόγος, 'word,
speech, reason'. See logos and -ize.

## paralysant
paralysant, adj. — See paralyzant.

## paralysis
paralysis, п., partial or complete incapacity of
motion or sensation (med.) — L., fr. Gk. παρά-
λυσις, 'disabling of the nerves, paralysis', fr.
παραλύει, 'to loosen, detach, disable, enfeeble',
fr. παρά (see para-, 'beside*) and λύειν, 'to
unfasten, loosen, slacken', which is cogn. with L.
luere, 'to loose, release; to atone for, expiate',
OE. for-leosan, 'to lose; to destroy', losian, 'to
perish, be lost'. See lose and cp. -lysis. Cp. also
palsy, which is a doublet of paralysis.

## paralytic
paralytic, adj. and n. — ME. peralitik, fr. MF.
paralitique (F. paralytique), fr. L. paralyticus, fr.
Gk. παραλυτικός, fr. πάραλυσι,ς. See prec.
word and adj. suff. -Ic.
Derivative: paralytic-al-ly, adv.

## paralyzant
paralyzant, also spelled paralysant, adj., causing
paralysis. — Formed fr. paralyze with suff. -ant.

## paralyze
paralyze, tr. v. — F. paralyser, Tr. paralysie. See
paralysis.
DenVatives: paralyz-ation, n.,paralyz-er, n.

## paramatta
paramatta, п., name of a'light dress fabric. —
From Paramatta, name of a town in New South
Wales, Australia.

## Paramecium
Paramecium, п., name of a ciliate infusorian
(zool.) — ModL., fr. Gk. παραμήκης, Oblong,
oval', fr. παρά (see para-, 'beside, beyond*) and
μήκος, 'length', which is rel. to μακρός, 'long',
and cogn. with L. macer, 'thin', and ON. magr,
OE. mseger, 'thin'. See macro-, meager. For the
ending see 1st -ium.

## parameter
parameter, п., a variable constant (math.) —
Coined fr. para-,*beside', and Gk. μέτρον,
'measure'. See meter, 'poetical rhythm'.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:561 COLUMN:2 -->
Derivatives: parametr-al, parametr-ic (qq. v.),
parametric-al, adjs.

## parametral
parametral, parametric, adj., pertaining to a
parameter. — See parameter and adj. suff. -al, resp.
-ic.

## parametric
parametric, adj., near the uterus. — See
parametrium.

## parametritis
parametritis,n., inflammation of the parametrium
(med.) — Medical L. See next word and -itis.
Derivative: parametrit-ic, adj.

## parametrium
parametrium, п., the connective tissue around the
uterus (anat.) — ModL., fr. Gk. παρά (see
para-,'beside') and μήτρα,'womb', which is rel.
to μήτηρ, 'mother'. See mother and cp. metro-,
'uterine'.

## paramnesia
paramnesia, п., distortion of memory (med.) —
Coined fr. para-, 'beside', and Gk. μνήσιος,
'pertaining to memory', which is rel. to μνά-
σθαι, 'to remember'. See mnesic and 1st -ia.

## paramo
paramo, п., a high treeless plain in South America.
— Sp. paramo, 'desert, paramo', fr. L. paramus,
a word of ancient Spanish origin.

## paramorphic
paramorphic, adj. — See paramorphism and -ic.

## paramorphine
paramorphine, п., thebaine. — Coined fr. para-,
'beside', and morphine.

## paramorphism
paramorphism, п., the alteration of one mineral to
another of the same chemical composition
(mineral.) — Compounded of para-, 'beside*, and
morphism.

## paramount
paramount, adj. — OF. paramont, 'that which is
at the top*, compounded of par, 'by' (fr. L.per-),
and amont (fr. a mont), 'uphill, above'. See per-
and amount.
Derivatives: paramount, п., paramount-cy, п.,
paramount-ly, adv., paramount-ness, n.

## paramour
paramour, п., lover of a married person. — ME.,
fr. OF. par amour, 'by love*, fr. par, 'by,
through' (fr. L. per), and amour, 'love*, fr. L.
атогет, асе. of amor, 'love*. See per- and
amorous.

## paranephric
paranephric, adj., near the kidney (anat.) —
Coined fr. para-, 'beside', and Gk. νεφρός, 'kidney'.
See nephritic.

## paranephritis
paranephritis, п., inflammation of the
paranephric (med.) —■ Medical L., formed fr. parane-
phros with suff, -itis.

## paranephros
paranephros, п., the suprarenal gland. —
Medical L. See paranephric.

## parang
parang, п., a short, heavy knife used by the
Dyaks. — Malay.

## paranoia
paranoia, also paranoea, п., mental disorder
characterized by systematized delusions (psychiatry).
— Medical L. paranoia, fr. Gk. παράνοια,
'derangement, madness', fr. παράνοος,
'demented, distracted', fr. παρά (see para-, 'beside,
beyond') and νόος, νους, 'mind'. See nous and 1st
-ia.
Derivatives: paranoi-acy adj. and n.,paranoi-ic,
adj. and n.

## paranoid
paranoid, adj., resembling paranoia. —
Compounded of Medical L. paranoia (see prec.
word) and Gk. -οειδής, 'like', fr. είδος,·'form,
shape'; see -oid. For the contraction of paranoia
and -oid into paranoid see haplology and cp.
words there referred to.
Derivatives: paranoid, п., paranoid-al, adj.

## paranymph
paranymph, п., groomsman or bridesmaid in
ancient Greece. — L. paranymphus, fr. Gk. παρά-
νυμφος, 'groomsman, bridesmaid', lit. 'being
beside the groom or bride*, fr. παρά (see para-,
'beside') and νύμφη, 'bride'. See nymph.

## parapegm
parapegm, parapegma, п., a tablet set up
containing some public information. ■— L.
parapegma, fr. Gk. παράπηγμα, 'something fixed
beside*, from the stem of παραπηγνύνα^, 'to fix
beside', fr. παρά (see para-, 'beside') and πη-
γνύναι, 'to make firm, fix', fr. l.-E. base *pdg-,
*palc-, 'to fix, join together-» unite'. See pact and
cp. words there referred to.

## parapet
parapet, п., a protective wall. — F., fr. It. para-
petto, which is compounded of par are, 'to ward
off* (see para-, 'that which protects'), and petto,
'breast', fr. L. pectus, 'breast'. See pectoral.
Derivative: parapet-ed, adj.

## paraph
paraph, п., a flourish made after a signature. —
MF. paraffe (F. paraphe), orig. meaning
'paragraph*, fr. ML. paraphus, contraction of
paragraphs. See paragraph.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:561 COLUMN:3 -->

## paraph
paraph, tr. v. — F. parapher, 'to put one's initials
to, to sign', fr. paraphe. See paraph, n.

## paraphernalia
paraphernalia, п., personal belongings. — ML.
paraphernalia (short for paraphernalia bons,
'paraphernal goods'), neut. pi. of Late L. pard-
phernalis, 'pertaining to the parapherna\ fr. L.
parapherna (pi.), 'the property of a married
woman besides her dowry*, fr. Gk. παράφερνα
(pi.) 'goods which a bride brings over and above
her dowry', fr. παρά (see para-, 'beside, beyond')
and φερνή, 'dowry', which is rel. to φέρειν, 'to
bring'. See bear, 'to carry*.

## paraphia
paraphia, п., abnormal sense of touch (med.) —
Medical L., coined fr. para-, 'beside, contrary
to', and Gk. άφή, 'touch', which is rel. to όίπτειν,
'to touch, fasten; to kindle', άψις, 'a fastening'.
See apsis and cp. words there referred to. For
the ending see 1st. suff. -ia.

## paraphrase
paraphrase, n., a free rendering. — F., fr. L.
paraphrases, fr. Gk. παράφρασες, 'paraphrase', fr.
παραφράζει, 'to say the same thing in other
words, to paraphrase', fr. παρά (see para-,
'beside') and φράζει, 'to point out, show, tell'. See
phrase and cp. periphrase, metaphrase.
Derivatives: paraphrase, tr. and intr. v., para-
phras-er, n.

## paraphrasis
paraphrasis, п., paraphrase. — L. See prec. word.

## paraphrastic
paraphrastic, adj., pertaining to, or of the nature
of, a paraphrase*. — ML. paraphrasticus, fr. Gk.
παραφραστικός, fr. παραφραστής, 'one who
paraphrases', fr. παραφράζειν, 'to paraphrase'.
See paraphrase.
Derivative: paraphrastic-al-ly, adv.

## paraphrenia
paraphrenia, п., dementia precox (psychiatry). —
Medical L., coined fr. para-, 'beside', Gk. φρήν,
'mind', and 1st suff. -in. See phrenetic.
Derivative: paraphren-ic, adj.

## paraphrenias
paraphrenias, п., inflammation of tissues near the
diaphragm (med.) — Medical L., coined fr.
para-, 'beside', Gk. φρήν, 'diaphragm, mind*,
and suff. -itis. See phrenetic and cp. prec. word
and phrenitis.

## paraphysis
paraphysis, п., a sterile filament in the sporogen-
ous organs of many cryptograms. — ModL.,
coined fr. para-, 'beside', and Gk. φύσις,
'growth, nature', fr. φύειν, 'to produce, make
to grow'. See physio-,

## paraplegia
paraplegia, п., paralysis of the lower half of the
body on both sides (med.) — Medical L., fr. Gk.
παραπληγία, 'hemiplegia', fr. παραπλήσσειν,
'to strike at the side', fr. παρά (see para-) and
πλήσσειν, 'to strike', which is rel. to πληγή,
'stroke', πλήγμα, 'blow*. See plague and 1st -ia.
Derivatives: parapleg-ic, adj. and n.

## parapraxis
parapraxis, п., faulty action, blunder
(psychoanalysis).— ModL., coined fr. para-, 'beside',
and Gk. πραξις, 'a doing, transaction, business',
from the stem of πράττει/ν,'to do'. See practical,

## parapsychology
parapsychology, п., that branch of psychology
which deals with psychic phenomena, as
extrasensory perception; psychical research. —
Coined fr. para-, 'beside', and psychology,

## parapsychosis
parapsychosis, п., abnormal psychosis. — ModL.,
coined fr. para-, 'beside', and psychosis,

## parasang
parasang, п., a Persian measure of length, equal
to about 3 2/5 miles. — L. parasanga, fr. Gk.
παρασάγγης, 'parasang', which is of Iranian
origin. Cp. Pehlevi frasang, farsang, ModPers.
ferseng.

## parasceve
parasceve, п., the day before the Jewish Sabbath.
— F. parasceve, fr. Late L. parasceve, fr. Gk.
παρασκευή, short for ήμερα παρασκευής, 'day
of preparation' (scil. for the Sabbath), fr. παρά
(see para-, 'beside') and σκευή, 'equipment',
which is rel. to σκεύος, 'implement, tool, vessel'.
See diaskeuasis.

## paraselene
paraselene, п., mock moon. — Coined fr. para-,
'beside*, and Gk. σελήνη, 'moon'. See seleno-.

## para shah
para shah, п., a section of the Pentateuch. —
Mishnaic Heb. parashdh, 'section', specif, 'a
section of the Torah', fr. Bibl. Heb. pdrash, 'he
separated, divided* (whence Bibl. Yleb.parashah,
'an exact statement*), Aram. perash, 'he kept

## off
off, abstained' (whence perisha, 'Pharisee'),

## aphresh
aphresh, 'he separated, divided', Akkad. parashu,

## pardsu
pardsu, 'to separate, decide'. Cp. Pharisee,

## parasite
parasite, п., an animal or plant that lives on or in
another organism. — F., fr. L. parasitus, fr. Gk.

παράσιτος, 'parasite', lit. 'eating beside
somebody', fr. παρά (see para-, 'beside') and σίτος,
'food', which is of uncertain origin. Cp. endo-
parasite.
Derivatives: parasite, intr. v., parasit-af, parasit-
ary, adjs., parasitic
(q.v.),parasit-ism,п.,parasitize, tr. v.

## parasitic
parasitic, parasitical, adj. — L. parasiticus, fr. Gk.
παρασιτικός, 'of, or pertaining to, a parasite', fr.
παράσιτος. See prec. word and -ic, resp. -ical.
Derivatives: parasinc-al-ly, adv., parasitic-al-
ness, n.

## parasiticide
parasiticide, adj., that which destroys parasites;
п., an agent that destroys parasites. — Lit.
'killer of parasites', compounded of L. parasttus,
'parasite', and -cida, 'killer', fr. caedere, 'to kill'.
See -cide, 'killer*.

## parasitology
parasitology, п., the study of parasites (biol.) —
Compounded of Gk. παράσιτος, 'parasite', and
-λογία, fr. -λόγος, 'one who speaks (in a certain
manner); one who deals (with a certain topic)'.
See parasite and -logy.
Derivatives: parasitolog-ic-ai, adj.,
parasitologist, n.

## parasol
parasol, п., a light umbrella. — F., fr. MF., fr. It.
parasole, lit. 'protection against the sun', fr.
parare, 'to ward off1 (see para-, 'that which
protects'), and sole, fr. L. solem, ace. of sol, 'sun'.
See Sol.
Derivatives-.parasol, tr. v., parasol-ed, adj.

## parasolette
parasolette, п., a small parasol. — Dimin. of
parasol. For the ending see suff. -ette.

## parasympathetic
parasympathetic, adj., pertaining to, or
designating, that part of the autonomic nervous
system which originates in the cranial and sacral
regions of the spinal cord. — Coined fr. para-,
'beside' and sympathetic.
Derivative: parasympathetic, п., a
parasympathetic nerve.

## parasynapsis
parasynapsis, п., the side-by-side union of
chromosomes (biol.) — ModL., coined fr. para-,
'beside', and synapsis.
Derivatives: parasynapt-ic, adj., parasynapt-ist,
n.

## parasyndesis
parasyndesis, n., parasynapsis. — Coined fr. para-,
'beside1, and Gk. σύνδεσης, 'a binding together'.
See syndesmo-.

## parasynthesis
parasynthesis, п., formation of words by both
derivation and combination. — ModL., fr. Gk.
παρασύνθεσις, 'formation from a compound'.
See para-, 'beside', and synthesis.

## parasynthetic
parasynthetic, adj., pertaining to, or formed by,
parasynthesis. — Fr. Gk. παρασύνθετος,
'formed from a compound*. See para- and synthetic.

## paratactic
paratactic, adj., pertaining to parataxis. —
Formed from the stem of παρατάσσειν, 'to lay side
by side', whence also παράταξις, 'arrangement'.
See parataxis and adj. suff. -ic.
Derivatives: paratactic-al, adj., paratactic-al-ly,
adv.

## parataxis
parataxis, п., the arrangement of successive
clauses without connectives (gramm.)— ModL.,
fr. Gk. παράταξις, 'arrangement', lit. 'a placing
side by side', from the stem of παρατάσσειν,
'to place side by side', fr. παρά (see para-,
'beside') and τάσσειν, 'to arrange, array, post,
place, appoint'. See taxis and cp. words there
referred to.

## parathymia
parathymia, п., irregular emotional response. —
ModL., coined fr. para-, 'beside, contrary to',
and Gk. θυμός, 'spirit, mind, soul, desire'. See
thyme and 1st -ia and cp. thio-.

## parathyroid
parathyroid, adj., pertaining to, or lying near, the
thyroid gland (med.) — Coined by Ivar Sand-
strom of Upsala in 1879, fr. para- and thyroid.
Derivative: parathyroid-al, adj.

## para troop
para troop, n. — Abbreviation of parachute troop.
Derivative: paratroop-er, n.

## paratyphoid
paratyphoid, adj., pertaining to a fever resembling
typhus, but usually milder; п., a paratyphoid
fever {med.) — Coined fr. para-, 'beside', and
typhoid.

## paraunit
paraunit, п., a unit of paratroops. —
Abbreviation of parachute unit.

## paravane
paravane, n. — Coined fr. para-, 'beside*, and
vane.

## parboil
parboil, tr. v., to boil partially. — ME. parboilen,
'to boil thoroughly', ir. OF. parboillir, fr. VL.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:562 COLUMN:2 -->
perbullire, of s.m., fr. L. per, 'through*, and
buUire, 'to boil'; see per- and boil, 'to cook'. E.
parboil was influenced in meaning by part.

## parbnckle
parbnckle, п., a device for raising or lowering a
heavy object. — Alter, of earlier parbunke/, due
to the influence of buckle; of unknown origin.
Derivative: parbuckle, tr. v., to raise or lower by
means of a parbuckle.

## Parca
Parca, n. (Greek mythol.) — L., 'goddess of birth*,
fr. pario, рагёге, 'to bring forth'; see parent.
' Later, owing to a false derivation fr. pars, 'part',
Parca was identified with the Greek Moira,
goddess of fate (fr. μοίρα, 'part, fate'), whence
arose three Parcae, corresponding in number to
the Moirai.

## parcel
parcel, n. — ME., fr. MF. (= F.)parce/le, fr. VL.
*particella, corresponding to L. particula,
dimin. of pars, gen. partis, 'part'. See part and cp.
particle.
Derivatives: parcel, tr. v., parcel(l)-ing, n.

## parcenary
parcenary, п., co-heirship. — W.parcenarie,
corresponding to OF. pargonerie, fr. parfonier.See
next word and subst. suff. -ary and cp.
coparcenary.

## parcener
parcener, п., co-heir (law). — AF. parcenier,
corresponding to OF. pargonier, fr. ML. partiona-
rius, short forpartitionarius (see haplo/ogy), One
who has a share*, fr. L. partitid, gen. -onis,
'division'. See partition and agential suff. -er and
cp. coparcener.

## parch
parch, tr. and intr. v. — Late ME. parchen. Some
authorities derive this verb fr. OF. perchier, par-
chier, now percher, Picard form of F. percer, 4o
pierce* (see pierce); others see in it a derivative
of L. persiccare, 'to dry thoroughly'. Both these
etymologies are justly rejected by OED. for
phonetic and historical reasons. — I tentatively
suggest that Late ME- parchen derived through
back formation fr. parchment (q.v.) The noun
parchment was divided into parch-ment and
through this division the verb parch in the sense
'to dry' was 'reconstructed'. (The orig. meaning
of parchment was supposed to have been
'anything dried*, and the meaning 'dried skin of
animals used for writing' to be secondary). This
etymology is supported by the rather striking
fact that while the orig. form parchemin appears
for the first time in English about 1300, the form
parchment and the verb parch appear for the first
time only about a hundred years later (see
OED.)
Derivatives: parch-ed, parch-ing, adjs., parch-
ing-ly, adv.

## parchment
parchment, n. — ME. parchemin, fr. OF. (= F.)
parchemin, fr. L. Pergamena, Pergamina,
'parchment', shortened for Pergamina charta (so in
Pliny), fr. Gk. Περγαμηνή, '(skin) of Perga-
raon', fr. Πέργαμον, 'Pergamon*, the famous
town in Mysia in Asia Minor, now called
Bergama. F. parchemin was influenced in form
by an association with L. Parthica (pellis\ 'skin
from the land of the Parthians'. The alteration
of ME. parchemin into E. parchment is due to a
confusion of the ending -min with the suff. -тем
(fr. L. -mentum) and was prob. suggested by
ML. pergamentum, 'parchment', which occurs
in England already in the X cent., and which
itself owes its form to a confusion of the ending
-тёпит (in L. Pergamenum) with the suff.
-mentum. Cp. parch.
Derivatives: parchment-ize, tr. v., parchment-y,
adj.

## parebnonious
parebnonious, parcimony. — Variants of
parsimonious, parsimony.

## parclose
parclose, п., a screen or railing (archit.) — ME.
parclos(e), fr. OF. parclose, 'enclosure, end',
prop. fem. pp. of parclore, 'to enclose, shut in',
fr. par- (for L. per) and clore, 'to close', fr. L.
claudere. See per- and close, adj.

## pard
pard, п., leopard (archaic) — ME.parde, fr. OF-,
fr. L. pardus, fr. Gk. πάρδος, πάρδαλις,
'panther', generally connected with OI. prdakuh,
'panther, tiger'. It is more probable, however,
that Greek πάρδος has been borrowed fr. Heb.
barodh, 'spotted' (said of an animal), and lit.
denotes 'the spotted animal'; see Heinrich
Lewy, Die semitischen Fremdworter im Grie-
chischen, Berlin, 1895, p. 7. For the change of

fr. Heb. 'erebh, 'evening, west'. Cp. leopard
camelopard, guepard.
Derivative: pard-inet adt.

## pard
pard, п., partner (slang). — Abbreviated fr.
pardner, a slang variant of partner.

## pardao
pardao, п., a former Portuguese gold coin of
Western India. — Port, pardao, ult. fr. OI.
pratapah, 'splendor', which is formed fr. pref.
pro-, 'before, forward, forth', and tapati, 'makes
warm, heats'. OI. pra- is cogn. with Gk. πρό,
'before'; see pro- and cp. Purana and the first
element in Prajapati, Prakrit, prakriti, Pralaya.
OI. tapati is cogn. with L. tepere, 'to be warm or
lukewarm'; see tepid and cp. topaz,

## pardon
pardon, n. — ME.pardoun, fr. OF. (= F.) pardon,
fr. pardoner (F. pardonner), 'to forgive*. See
pardon, v.

## pardon
pardon, tr. v. — ME. pardonen, fr. OF. pardoner
(F. pardonner), fr. Late L. perdonare, 'to remit',
fr. L. per, 'through', and donare, 'to give*. See
per- and donation.
Derivatives: pardon-able, adj., pardon-able-ness,
п., pardon-abl-y, adv., pardon-ee, n.

## pardoner
pardoner, п., one authorized to sell papal
indulgences (hist.) — ME. pardonere, fr. OF. par-
donier, fr. pardoner, 'to forgive'. See prec. word
and agential suff. -er.

## pare
pare, tr. v. — ME. paren, fr. MF. (= F.) parer,
'to adorn, prepare', fr. L. parare, 'to get, prepare,
make ready', fr. I.-E. base *per-, 'to bring
forward, bring forth', whence also pario, рагёге, 'to
bring forth*,Lith. pariu,pereti, 'to brood',Gk. πό-
ρίς,πόρτις,πόρταξ,^ΙΓ,ΟΗΟ./ΰί-,/α/το,ΜΗΟ.
far,farre, G. Farre, 'bullock*, Du. vaars, 'heifer',
ON./am, OE. fearr, 'bull', OI. prthukah, 'child,
calf, young of an animal*, Czech s-pratek, 'calf
born prematurely; brat, urchin'. Cp. amparo,
apparatus, apparel, disparate, emperor, empire,
imperative, imperator, imperious, para-,
parachute, parade, parapet, parasol, parry,
parturition, parure, pauper, poor, poverty, prepare,
rampart, repair, 'to restore', reparation,
repertory, separate, sever, spar, 'to fight with the fists',
vituperate. Cp. I.-E. base *per-, *to sell', which
is prob. ult. identical with base *per-, 'to bring
forward, bring forth'; see pair and cp. words
there referred to.

## paregoric
paregoric, adj., soothing pain; п., a medicine that'
soothes pain. — Late L. paregoricus, fr. Gk.
παρηγορικός, 'encouraging, consoling,
soothing', fr. παρά (see para-, 'beside') and αγορά,
'public assembly', which is rel. to άγείρείν, 'to
assemble*, and cogn. with L. grex, gen. gregis,
'flock'. See gregarious and cp. agora, panegyric.
For the ending see adj. suff. -ic.

## pareira or pareira brava
pareira or pareira brava, п., the root of a Brazilian
vine. — Port, parreira, 'vine trained against the
wall', whence parreira brava, lit. 'wild vine*.

## parenchyma
parenchyma, п., soft, cellular tissue (anat. and
bot.) — Medical L., fr. Gk. παρέγχυμα; lit. 'that
which is poured in beside', a name coined by
Erasistratus fr. παρεγχεΐν, 'to pour in beside',
fr. παρά (see para-, 'beside'), and έγχεΐν, 'to
pour in'. See enchymatous.
Derivatives: parenchym-al, parenchymat-ic, pa-

## renchymat-ous
renchymat-ous, adjs., parenchymax-ous-ly, adv.

## parenchymals
parenchymals, п., inflammation of the
parenchyma of an organ (med.) — Medical L.,
formed fr. parenchyma with suff. -itis.

## parent
parent, n. — ME., fr. OF. (= F.), fr. L. parentem>

## ace. of parens
ace. of parens, 'parent', fr. pario, рагёге, 'to

## bring forth
bring forth, produce', fr. I.-E. base *per-, 'to

## bring forward
bring forward, bring forth', whence also parare,
'to prepare'. See pare and -ent and cp. Parca,

## parturient and the second element in oviparous
parturient and the second element in oviparous,

## primipara
primipara, puerperal, quadripara, repertory, tri-

## para
para, viviparous.
Derivatives: parent, adj. and tr. v., parent-age,
п., parental (q.v.), parent-hood, n.

## parental
parental, adj. — L. parentalis, 'of parents', fr.

## parens
parens, gen. -entis, 'parent'. See parent and adj.
suff. -al.
Derivatives: parental-ism, п., parental-ity, п.,

## parental-ly
parental-ly, adv.

## Parentalin
Parentalin, n. pi., an annual feast in Rome, in
commemoration of the dead (Roman Religion).
— L., prop. neut. pi. of parentalis. See prec.

## parenteral
parenteral, adj., outside the intestine (med.) —
Coined fr. Gk. παρά (see para-, 'beside, beyond')
and άντερα (pi.), 'intestines'. See enteric and adj.
suff. -al.
Derivative: parenteral-ly, adv.

## parenthesis
parenthesis, п., word, clause etc. inserted into a
sentence. — ML., fr. Gk. ·παρέν*εσις,
'insertion', lit. 'a putting in beside', fr. παρεντιθένκι,
'to put in beside', fr. παρά, 'beside', έν, 'in', and
τιθέναι, 'to put, place'. See para-, 'beside', 2nd
en- and thesis.
Derivatives: parenthes-ize, tr. v., parenthetic
(q-v.)

## parenthetic
parenthetic, parenthetical, adj. — ML. parenthe-
ticus, as if fr. Gk. 'παρενθετικός,' fr. παρέν-
&ετος, 'inserted, interpolated', verbal adj. of
παρεντιθέναι, 'to put in beside'. See parenthesis
and the suff. -etic, resp. also -al.
Derivatives: parenthetical-ly, adv.,parenthetical-
ness, n.

## paresis
paresis, п., partial paralysis (med.) — ModL., fr.
Gk. πάρεσις, 'a letting go, slackening,
remission', from the stem of παριέναι, 'to let go',
fr. παρά (see para-, 'beside') and ίέναι, 'to set
in motion, throw, send', which is cogn. with L.
jacire, 'to throw'. See jet, 'to spirt forth', and
cp. words there referred to.

## paresthesia
paresthesia, paraesthesia, п., abnormal sense of
touch (med.) — Coined fr. para- and esthesia.

## paresthetic
paresthetic, paresthetic, adj. — See prec. word
and adj. suff. -Ic.

## paretic
paretic, adj., pertaining to, or affected with
paresis ; п., a person having paresis. — See paresis
and adj. surf. -ic.
Derivative: paretic-al-ly, adv.

## par excellence
par excellence, preeminently. — F. See par- (fr.
L. per) and excellence.

## par exemple
par exemple, for example, for instance. — F. See
par- (fr. L. per) and example.

## parfait
parfait, п., a kind of frozen dessert. — F.,
'perfect', fr. L. perfectus, pp. of perficere, 'to bring
to an end'. See perfect.

## parfleche
parfleche, п., rawhide. ·'— Can. F. parfliche, lit.
'that which protects against arrows', fr. para-,
'that which protects', and fleche, 'arrow'. See
Heche.

## pargana
pargana, also pergana, pergunnah, п., district (in
India). —Hind, parganah, 'division, district', fr.
Pers. parganah.

## pargasite
pargasite, п., a green variety of hornblende
(mineral.) — Named after Pargas in Finland. For
the ending see subst. suff. -ite.

## parget
parget, tr. v., to plaster. — ME. pargeten, fr. MF.
pargeter, formed, with change of pref., fr. L.
prdjecturer freq. of projicere (pp. projectus), 'to
throw out'. See project.
Derivatives: parget, п., parget(t)-ing, n.

## pargo
pargo, п., the porgy. — Sp. pargo, a collateral
form of pagro, fr. L. pagrus, phagrus, pagarus,
fr. Gk. φάγρος, 'sea bream, braise', prob.
identical with φάγρος, 'whetstone', which is possibly
cogn. with Arm. bark, 'sharp, sour, bitter'. Cp.
porgy.

## parhelion
parhelion, п., a mock sun. — L. parelion, fr. Gk.
πκρήλιον, fr. πάρα (see para-, 'beside') and
ήλιος, 'sun'. See helio-.
Derivatives: parheli-ac-al, parhel-ic, adjs.

## pari-
pari-, combining form meaning 'equal'. — L.
pari-, fr. par, gen. paris, 'equal'. See par,
'equality'.

## pariah
pariah, n. — Tamil paraiyar, pi. of paraiyan,
'(hereditary) drummer', fr. patai, 'a large drum',
so called because it was pariahs who used to beat
the drums at certain festivals.

## Parian
Parian, adj., of Paros — Formed with suff. -an fr.
L. Partus, fr. Gk. Πάριος, fr. Πάρος,'Paros', one
of the Cyclades in the Aegean Sea.
Derivative: Parian, n.

## paries
paries, п., a wall; specif, the wall of a cavity in the
body (biol.) — L. paries, 'wall', which is of
uncertain origin. It possibly stands for orig.
*tweriet- and derives fr. I.-E. base "twer-, 'to
seize, hold', whence also Lith. tveriit, tverti, 'to
seize, fence in, hedge', tvartas, 'hedge, hurdle',
Lett, tveru, tveft, 'to seize, take hold of, OSlav.
tvoriti, 'to make, fashion', tvoru, 'creature'. Cp.
parietary, pellitory, the plant. Cp. also siren.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:563 COLUMN:2 -->

## parietal
parietal, adj., pertaining to the walls of a cavity
in the body. — MF. (= F.) parietal, fr. L.
parietalis, 'of, or pertaining to, walls', fr. paries,
gen. parietis. See prec. word and adj. suff. -al.

## Parietaria
Parietaria, п., a genus of plants, the pellitory. —
L. parietaria, 'parietary, pellitory' (short for
herba parietaria, lit. 'wall plant'), fern, of the adj.
parietarius, 'of the wall', used as a noun (see
paries); so called because it grows on old walls.
Cp. next word.

## parietary
parietary, п., the pellitory. — AF. paritarie, fr.
OF. paritaire (F. parietaire), fr. L. parietaria. See
Parietaria and cp. pellitory, the plant. For the
ending see adj. suff. -ary.

## parillm
parillm, п., a white crystalline glucoside (chem.)
— Formed with suff. -in from the abbreviation
of (sarsa) parilla.

## pari mutuel
pari mutuel, a .system of registering bets. — F.,
'mutual wager'. The first word derives fr. VL.
pariare, 'to make equal', fr. L. par, gen. paris,
'equal'; see pair. For the second word see
mutual.

## pari passu
pari passu, with equal pace. — L. pari passu,
'with equal pace', fr. abl. of par, 'equal', and
passus, 'pace'. See pair and pace,

## paripinnate
paripinnate, adj., equally pinnate (bot.) — Coined
fr. L. par, 'equal' (see pair), and pinnate.

## Paris
Paris, п., the capital of France. — F., fr. L.
Lutetia Parisiorum (in Late L. also Parisii),
'Paris', fr. L. Parisii, name of a Gallic tribe.

## Paris
Paris, п., name of a genus of plants (bot.) —
ModL., fr. ML. herba paris. See herb Paris,

## parish
parish, n. — ME. parish, paroche, fr. MF. par-
roche, fr. Late L. parochia, dissimilated fr. Gk.
παροικία (whence also the rare Late L. form
paroecia), lit., 'dwelling beside', fr. παρά (see
para-, 'beside') and οίκεϊν, 'to inhabit, possess;
to manage, govern', fr. οίκος, 'house'. See
economy and cp. paroecious. The ch in L.
parochia (instead of c) is due to the influence of
parochus, 'purveyor* (fr. Gk. πάροχος). For a
similar dissimilation see diocese.
Derivatives: parish-ed, adj., parish-ion-eer, n.

## parishioner
parishioner, n. — ME.parisshoner, fr. MF. (= F.)
paroissien, fr. paroisse, a collateral form of par-
roche. See prec. word and agential suff. -er.

## Parisian
Parisian, adj. — F. parisien, fr. ML. Parisidnus,
fr. Late L. Parisii, 'Paris'. See Paris, the capital
of France, and -ian.
Derivative: Parisian, n.

## parisyllabic
parisyllabic, adj., having the same number of
syllables. — Compounded of L. par, gen. paris,
'equal' (see pair), and syllabic,

## parity
parity, п., equality. — L. panto's, gen. -talis,
'equality', fr. par, 'equal'. See pair and -ity.

## park
park, n. — yiE.parc, fr. OF. (= F.)parc, fr. ML.
parricus, 'enclosure; park', fr. Iberian *parra,
'espalier, trellis', whence also Sp. parra, of s.m.
Cp. paddock, parrock, parquet.
Derivatives: park, tr. and intr. v., park-er, п.,
park-ing, п., park-ish, adj., park-y, adj.

## parkin
parkin, п., a kind of cake. — Prob. from the
surname Parkin.

## Parkmsonia
Parkmsonia, n., a genus of shrubs (bot.)— ModL.,
named after John /Or/Union (1567-1650),
apothecary of London. For the ending see 1st suff.
-ia.

## parlance
parlance, п., manner of speaking. — MF., fr. OF.,
fr. parler, 'to speak'. See parley and cp. words
there referred to. For the ending see suff. -ance.

## parlando
parlando, adj. and adv., speaking (musical
direction) — It. parlando, fr. par/are, 'to speak', fr.
VL. *paraulare. See parley, v., and cp. words
there referred to.

## Parlatoria
Parlatoria, п., a genus of insects (entomol.) —
ModL., named after the Italian botanist Felipe
Parlatore (1816-77). For the ending see 1st
suff. -ia.

## parlay
parlay, п., a term of betting. — F. paroli, fr.
Neapolitan It. paroli, pi. of parolo, dimin. of
paro (= It. pari), 'equal', fr. L. par, of s.m. See
pair,

## parley
parley, tr. v., to hold a conference with (archaic);
intr. v., to hold a conference. — MF. (= F.)

## parler
parler, 'to speak*, fr. VL. *paraulare, 'to speak',
fr. Late L. parabolare, 'to speak in parables, to
speak', fr. parabola, 'parable, speech', whence
also F. parole, 'word'. See parable and cp.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:563 COLUMN:3 -->
parlando, parleyvoo, parlor, parole, pourparler.
Derivative: parley-er, n.

## parley
parley, п., gonference, esp. with an enemy. —
Prob. fr. parley, v.

## parleyvoo
parleyvoo, п., the French language. — Fr. F.
partez-vous(francais) ?, 'do you speak (French) ?*
See parley, v.
Derivative: parleyvoo, intr. v.

## Parliament
Parliament, n. — ME. parlement, parliament, fr.
OF. (= F.) parlement, orig. meaning 'speaking,
talk', fr. parler, 'to speak'. See parlance and
-ment.
Derivatives: parliament-arian, adj. and п.,
parliament-arian-ism, п.,parliament-ari-ly, adv.,
parliament-ar-ism, п., parliamem-ar-ize, tr. v.,
parliament-ar-iz-ation, п., parliament-ary, adj.
and п., parliament-ari-ness, n.

## parlor
parlor, parlour, n. — ME. parlour, fr. OF. parleor,
parlere (F. parloir), fr. parler, 'to speak'. See
parley, v., and -or.

## parlous
parlous, adj., perilous, dangerous (partly archaic,
partly dial.) — Late ME. perlous, contraction of
perilous (q.v.)

## Parmentiera
Parmentiera, п., a genus of American trees of the
family Bignoniaceae (bot.) — ModL., named
after the French agricultural economist Antoine-
Augustin Parmentier (1737-1813).

## Parmesan
Parmesan, adj. — F., fr. It. Parmegiano, 'of
Parma', fr. Parma, a city in Italy, fr. L. Parma.
Cp. pearmain.

## Parmesan cheese
Parmesan cheese, dry hard cheese of delicate
flavor. — So called because orig. made at
Parma, in Italy. See prSc. word.

## Parnassin
Parnassin, п., a genus of plants, the grass of
Parnassus (bot.) — ModL., named from Mount
Parnassus. See Parnassus and 1st -ia.

## Pamassiaceae
Pamassiaceae, n. pi., a family of plants. —
ModL., formed fr. prec. word with suff. -aceae.

## parnassiaceous
parnassiaceous, adj. — See prec. word and
-aceous.

## Parnassian
Parnassian, adj. and n. — Formed with suff. -ian
fr. L. Parnassius, 'Parnassian', fr. Parnassus,
name of a mountain in Greece. See Parnassus
and -Ian.

## Parnassian
Parnassian, п., member of a school of French
poets in the second half of the 19th century. —
F. parnassien, fr. L. Parnassus; so called from
Parnasse contemporain, title of the first volume
published by this school (in 1866). See prec.
word.
Derivative: Parnassian-ism, n.

## Parnassus
Parnassus, п., mountain in Greece; poetry. — L.,
fr. Gk. Παρνασός, later spelled Παρνασσός.

## Parnellism
Parnellism, п., policy of Irish Home Rule. —
Named after C. S. Parnell (1846-91). For the
ending see suff. -ism.

## Parnellite
Parnellite, п., an adherent of Parnellism. — See
prec. word and subst. suff. -ite.

## parochial
parochial, adj., pf a parish. — ME. perochiel, pa-
rochiel, fr, MF. parochial, fr. ML. parochialis,
'pertaining to a parish', fr. parochia. See parish
and adj. suff. -al.
Derivatives: parochial-ism, п., parochial-ist, п.,
parochial-ity, п., parochial-ize, tr. v.,
parochially, adv., parochial-ness, n.

## parados
parados, п., first entrance of the chorus in Greek
tragedy. — Gk. πάροδος, prop, 'a way by',
hence 'side entrance, passage, gallery', fr. παρά
(see para-, 'beside') and οδός, 'way'. See odo-
graph.

## parodist
parodist, n. — F. parodiste, fr. parodie. See next
word and -ist.
Derivatives: parodist-ic, adj., parodist-ic-al-ly,
adv.

## parody
parody, n. — F. parodie, fr. L. parodia, fr. Gk.
παρωδία, 'parody, burlesque', fr. παρά (see
дага·, 'beside') and ώδη, 'song'. See ode and -y
(representing Gk. -ία).
Derivatives: parody, tr. v., parodist (q.v.)

## paroecious
paroecious, adj., having the male and female
organs of plants developed near each other (bot.)
— Fr. Gk. πάροικος, 'dwelling beside', fr. παρά
(see para-, 'beside') and οίκεϊν, 'to dwell', fr.
οίκος, 'house'. See economy and cp. parish. For
the ending see suff. -ous.
Derivatives :paiwc/oMj-/y, Sidv., paroecious-ness,
n.

## paroeclsm
paroeclsm, n. — See prec. word and -ism.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:564 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: 537 | PARTHIAN -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:564 COLUMN:1 -->

## paroemia
paroemia, п., a proverb (rhet.) — Gk. παροιμία,
'proverb', fr. παρά (see para-, 'beside') and
οΐμος also (οΐμος), 'way, road, path', which is
perh. rel. to οϊμη, 'song, lamentation' (lit. 'the
way of song' ?, cp. the term οΐμος άοι8ής, 'the
course of song'), and perh. also to ΐεμχι (for
•Γίεμαι), Ί tend to, aspire to, make haste, long
for'. See venery, 'hunting', and cp. proem,

## paroemiac
paroemiac, adj., 1) proverbial; 2) pertaining to
the verse form called the paroemiac. — Gk.
παροιμιακός, 'proverbial', fr. παροιμία,
'proverb'. See prec. word and -ac.

## paroemiac
paroemiac, п., an anapaestic dimeter catalectic
(Gk.-L. Pros.) — Gk. παροιμιακοί* (scil.
μέτρον), 'the paroemiac meter', neut. of
παροιμιακός, lit. 'proverbial'. See prec. word.

## paroemiographer
paroemiographer, п., a writer of proverbs. —
Compounded of Gk. παροιμία, 'proverb' (see
paroemia), and -grapher.

## paroemiography
paroemiography, п., writing of proverbs. — See
prec. word and -graphy.

## paroemiology
paroemiology, п., the study of proverbs. —
Compounded of Gk. παροιμία, 'proverb', and
-λογία, fr. -λόγος, 'one who speaks (in a certain
manner); one who deals (with a certain topic)'.
See paroemia and -logy..
Derivative: paroemiolog-ist, n.

## parol
parol, п., word (law). — OF. (= F.) parole,
'word'. See next word.
Derivative: parol, adj.

## parole
parole, п., word of honor. — OF. (= F.), 'word',
fr. VL. *paraula, fr. L. parabola, 'comparison,
parable, speech', fr. Gk. παραβολή. See parable
and cp. parol.
Derivatives:parol-able, adj.,parole, tr. v.,parol-
ee, п., parol-ist, n.

## paroli
paroli, п., the leaving of staked money as a
further stake. — F., fr. It. paroli, dimin. of par,
'equal', fr. L. par, 'equal'. See par, 'equality'.
Derivative: paroli, tr. and intr. v.

## paronomasia
paronomasia, п., pun. — L., fr. Gk-παρονομασία,
'play upon words which sound similarly', fr.
παρονομάζειν, 'to call with a slight change of
name', lit. 'to name beside', fr. παρά (see para-,
'beside') and όνομάζειν, 'to call, name', fr.
δνομα, 'name'. See onomato- and cp. parony-
mous.
Derivatives: paronomasi-al, paronomasi-an, pa-
ronomasi-astic, adjs., paronomasi-astic-al-ly,
adv.

## paronychia
paronychia, п., a whitlow (med.) — L. paronychia,
fr. Gk. παρωνυχία 'whitlow', fr. παρά (see
para-, 'beside') and δνυξ, gen. ονυχος, 'nail'.
See nail and 1st -ia and cp. onyx.

## Paronychia
Paronychia, п., a genus of plants, the whiilow-
wort (bot.) — ModL. (see prec/word); so called
because the plant was supposed to cure whitlow.
— Cp. Anychia.

## paronym
paronym, п., a cognate word. — See next word.

## paronymous
paronymous, adj., of the same derivation. — Gk.
παρώνυμος, 'formed by a slight change, a
derivative', fr. παρά (see para-, 'beside') and ονυμα
dialectal form of βνομα, 'name'.· See ononiato-
and cp. paronomasia.

## paronymy
paronymy, п., the quality of being paronymous.
— See prec. word and -y (representing Gk. -ία).

## paroquet
paroquet, п., a parakeet. — A var. of parakeet,

## parosmia
parosmia, п., abnormal sense of smell (med.) —
Medical L., fr. para-, 'beside, contrary to', and
Gk. οσμή, 'smell, odor'. See osmium. For the
ending see 1st s IT. -ia.
Derivative: parosm-ic, adj.

## parotic
parotic, adj., situated near the ear (zool.) —
Formed fr. Gk. παρά (see para-, 'beside'), ους, gen.
ώτός, 'ear' (see oto-), and adj. suff. -ic.

## parotid
parotid, adj., situated near the ear; hence
designating a salivary gland situated near the ear; п.,
the parotid gland (anal.) — F. parotide, fr. L.
parotis, gen. -idis, fr. Gk. παρωτίς, 'tumor near
the ear', fr. παρά (see para-, 'beside') and ους,
gen. ώτός, 'ear'. See oto-.
Derivative; parotid-ean, adj.

## parotitis
parotitis, п., inflammation of the parotid gland
(anal.) — Medical ~L. parotitis, formed with suff.
-itis fr. Gk. παρωτίς. See prec. word.

## parotoid
parotoid, adj., resembling a parotid gland. —
Compounded of Gk. παρωτίς (see parotid) and
-οειδής, 'like', fr. είδος, 'form, shape'. See -oid.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:564 COLUMN:2 -->

## parous
parous, adj., 'givingbirth to*. — Fr. ~L.parere. See
-parous.

## -parous
-parous, combining form meaning 'bearing,
producing', as in multiparous. — L. -parus (in vivi-
parus, 'bringing forth its young alive'), fr. parere,
'to bring forth, beget, bear, produce'. See
parent and cp. viviparous. For E. -ous, as
equivalent to L. -us, see -ous.

## parovarium
parovarium, п., the epoophoron (anat.) — A
Medical L. hybrid lit. 'that which is beside the
ovary'; coined by Kobelt in 1847 fr. Gk. παρά
(see para-, 'beside') and L. ovarium, 'ovary'. See
ovary. The correct form is epoophoron (q.v.)

## paroxysm
paroxysm, п., a sudden attack or convulsion. —
F. paroxysme, fr. Gk. παροξυσμός, 'irritation,
exasperation', fr. παροξΰνειν, 'to provoke,
irritate, fr. παρά (see para-, 'beside') and όξυνειν,
'to sharpen', fr. οξύς, 'sharp'. See Oxalis.
Derivatives; paroxysm-al, adj., paroxysm-al-ly,
adv., paroxysm-ic, adj.

## paroxytone
paroxytone, adj., having the accent on the
penultimate syllable (gram.) — Gk. παροξύτονος,
'with acute accent on thepenultimate syllable', fr.
παρά (see para-, 'beside') and όξύτονος, 'having
an acute accent'. See oxytone.
Dcnvativesiparoxytone, n. and tT.v.,paroxyton-
ic, adj., paroxyton-ize, tr. v.

## parquet
parquet, n. — F., dimin. of pare, 'enclosure'. See
park and -et.

## parr
parr, п., a young salmon. — Of uncertain origin.

## parrakeet
parrakeet, n. — See parakeet,

## parrel
parrel, also parra], n. (naut.) — ME.perell, a var.
of parail, aphetic form of aparail, 'equipment'.
See apparel,

## parricide
parricide, п., murderer of a parent. — F., fr. L.
paricida, later spelled parricida, 'murderer of a
near relative', later also 'murderer of one's
father'. The first element of this compound is of
uncertain origin; it is perh. cogn. with Dor. Gk.
παός, Att. πηός, 'relation'. The second element
derives fr. L. caedere, 'to kill'; see -tide, 'killer'.

## parricide
parricide, п., murder of a parent. — F., fr. L.
paricldium, later spelledparricidium, fr. paricida,
resp. parricida. See prec. word and -cide, 'killing'.

## parrock
parrock, п., a small field, a paddock. — ME.
parrok, fc.OYi.pearroc, pearruc, 'enclosure',
borrowed—together with MLG- perk, park
(whence Du. park), OHG. pfarrih, pferrih
(whence MHG. pferrich, G. Pferch)—fr. ML.
parricus, which itself was borrowed fr. Iberian
"parra, 'espalier, trellis'. See park and cp.
paddock, 'enclosure'.

## parrot
parrot, n. — F. perrot, a dial, form of perroquet.
See parakeet.
Derivatives: parrot, tr. v., parrot-let, п.,
parrotry, п., parrot-y, adj.

## parry
parry, tr. v., to ward off. — F. parez, imper. of
parer, fr. It. parare, 'to ward off', fr. L. parare,
'to prepare'. See pare and cp. para-, 'that which
protects'. Cp. also spar, 'to fight with the fists'.
Derivative: parry, n.

## parse
parse, tr. v., to state the parts of speech in a
sentence. — Fr. L. pars, 'part', in the stereotypic
question Quae pars orationisl ('What part of
speech?'). See part, n.
Derivative: pars-er, n.

## parsec
parsec, п., a unit of length used to measure the
distance of stars (astron.) — Abbreviation of
the words parallax-second.

## Parsee
Parsee, also Parsi, п., a descendant of the Zoro-
astrians who fled from Persia to India at the
time of the Mohammedan persecutions in the
7th and 8thcenturies. — Persian Parsi, 'Persian',
fr. Pars, 'Persia'. Cp. Persia and words there
referred to.
Derivatives: Parsee-ism, Pars(i)-ism, п., Pars-
ic, adj.

## parsettensite
parsettensite, п., a hydrous manganese silicate
(mineral.) — G. Parsettensit, named after Mt.
Parsettens in Grisons, France. The ending -it
goes back to Gk. -ΐτης; see subst. suff. -ite.

## Parsifal
Parsifal, n. — See Parzival.

## parsimony
parsimony, parcimony, п., extreme economy. —
ME. parcimony, fr. L. parsimonia, parcimonia,
sparingness, thrift', formed with suff. -monia, fr.

## pars-(um)
pars-(um), pp. stem oiparcere, 'to spare', which
is rel. to compescere (for *com-parc-scere), 'to

## confine
confine, curb, restrain'. L. parvus, 'small', pa-

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:564 COLUMN:3 -->
rum, 'too little*, are not related to parcere. For
the ending see -mony and cp. words there
referred to.
Derivatives: parsimoni-ous, adj.,
parsimoniously, adv., parsimoni-ous-ness, n.

## parsley
parsley, n. — ME. persely, fr. earlier peresil, fr.
OF. perresil (F. persil), fr. VL. *petrosilium
(whence also OE. petersilie), alteration of L.
petroselinum, fr. Gk. πετροσέλΐνον, 'rock
parsley', which is compounded of πέτρα, 'rock,
stone', and σέλίνον, 'celery'. See petro- and
celery and cp. Petroselinum. Cp. also the second
element in Conioselinum, Hipposelinum.

## parsnip
parsnip, n. — ME. passenep, pasnep, fr. MF.
pasnaie (F. panais), fr. L.pastinaca, 'parsnip', fr.
pastinare, 'to dig up the ground', fr. pastinum,
'a two-pronged dibble'. Cp. Pastinaca. The
ending of the word parsnip was formed on analogy
of turnip.

## parson
parson, n. — ME. persone, 'person; parson', fr.
OF. persone, of s.m.; see person. The meaning
'parson' prob. arose from the abbreviation of L.
persona ecclesiae, 'person of the church'.
Derivatives: parsonage (q.v.), parson-ic, parson-
ic-al, adjs., parson-ic-al-ly, adv., parson-ed, adj.,
parson-ers, п., parson-ity, п., parson-ry, n.

## parsonage
parsonage, n. — ME.personage, fr. MF., fr. OF.,
fr. OF. persone. See prec. word and personage.

## part
part, n. — ME., fr. OE. and OF. part, fr. L.,
partem, ace. of pars, 'part', which is re], to L.
portion 'share, portion', and cogn. with Gk. πέ-
πρω-ται, 'it has been granted', έπορον, Ί gave,
granted', OI. piirtam, 'reward', Hitl. parshiya-,
'fraction, part'. All these words derive fr. I.-E.
base *per-, 'to assign, allot', which is prob. ult.
identical with base 'per-, 'equal; to sell, to buy',
whence L. par, 'equal'. See pair and cp. apart,
apartment, champerty, compartment, depart,
department, departure, dispart, ex parte, impart,
jeopardy, parcel, parcener, parse, partake,
participate, participle, particle, partite, partition,
partner, portion. Cp. also pare and words there
referred to.
Derivatives: part, v. (q.v.), part-ing, adj. and п.,
part-ly, adv.

## part
part, tr. and intr. v. — ME. parten, fr. OF. ( =
F.) partir, 'to divide, separate, leave', fr. L.
partire, partiri, 'to divide', fr. pars, gen. partis,
See part, п., and cp. depart, dispart,
repartee.

## partake
partake, tr. and intr. v. — Back formation fr.
partaker, partaking, fr. original part-taker, part-
taking. See part, п., and take.

## partaker
partaker, n. — For part-taker. See prec. word
and agential suff. -er.

## parterre
parterre, n. — F., fr. MF., compounded of par
terre, 'on the ground', fr. par, 'through, on' (fr.
L. per), and terre, 'earth' (fr. L. terra). See per-
and terra.
Derivative: parterr-ed, adj.

## parthenic
parthenic, adj., of, or of the nature of, a virgin. —
Formed with adj. suff. -ic fr. Gk. παρθένιος, fr.
παρθένος, 'virgin', which is of uncertain origin.
Cp. Parthenium, Parthenon.

## Parthenium
Parthenium, п., a genus of plants of the thistle
family (bot.) — L. parthenium, the name of
several plants, fr. Gk. παρθένιον, prop. neut. of
the adj. παρθένιος, 'maidenly', fr. παρθένος,
'maiden, virgin' (see parthenic and 1st -ium); so
called from the whitish flowers.

## parthenogenesis
parthenogenesis, п., reproduction without
fertilization — ModL., lit. 'birth from a virgin',
coined fr. Gk. παρθένος, 'virgin', and γένεσις,
'origin, source, birth, descent, race'. See parthenic
and genesis.
parthenogenetic. adj. — See prec. word and
-genetic.
Derivative: parthenogenetic-al-ly, adv.

## Parthenon
Parthenon, п., name of the temple of the goddess
Athena on the Acropolis at Athens. — L., fr.
Gk. Παρθενών, prop, 'temple of Athena, the
virgin', fr. παρθένος, 'virgin'. See parthenic.

## Parthian
Parthian, adj., of Parthia. — Formed with suff.
-an fr. Parthia, name of an ancient kingdom,
northeast of Persia. Parthian shot is a 'parting
shot'; so called from the habit of Parthian
horsemen to shoot backward while retiring.
Derivative: Parthian, n.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:565 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: PARTIAL | 538 -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:565 COLUMN:1 -->

## partial
partial, adj. — ME. partial, fr. MF. ( = F.)
partial, fr. Late L. partialis, fr. L. pars, gen.
partis, 'part'. See part, п., and -ial.
Derivatives: partial-ist, п., partial-ly, adv.

## partiality
partiality, n. — ME. partialitey fr. MF. (= F.)
partialite, fr. Late L. partialitatem, ace. of par-
tialitas, fr. partialis. See prec. word and -ity.

## partible
partible, adj., divisible. — Late L. panibilis, fr. L.

## partiri
partiri, 'to divide', fr. pars, gea.pariis, 'part*. See
part, n. and v., and -ible.
Derivative: partibil-ity, n.

## participant
participant, adj., participating. — L. participans,
gen. -antis, pres. part, of participare. See next
word and -ant.
Derivative: participant, adj.

## participate
participate, intr. and tr. v. — L. participat{um),
pp. stem of participare, 'to share, partake of,
participate in', fr. particeps, gen. participis,
'sharing, partaking, participant*, which is
compounded of pars, gen. partis, 'part', and capere,
'to catch, seize, take, hold'. See part and captive.
For the change of ά(\η capere) to i {inparti-cipis
and in parti-cipare) see abigeat and cp. words
there referred to.
Derivatives: participation (q.v.), participat-ive,
adj., participat-ive-ly, adv., participator (q.v.)

## participation
participation, n. — ME. participacioun, fr. Late
L. participationem, ace. of participation
'partaking', fr. L. participat(um), pp. stem of
participare. See participate and -ion.

## participator
participator, n. — Late L. participator, fr. L.
participat{um), pp. stem of participare. See
participate and agential suit", -or.
Derivative: participator-y, adj.

## participial
participial, adj. — L. participialis, fr. participium.
See participle and -ial.

## participle
participle, n. — ME., fr. OF. participle, collateral
form of OF. (= F.) participe, fr. L. participium,
'a sharing, partaking; participle', fr. particeps,
gen. participis, 'sharing, partaking', viz. '(a
verbal form) partaking of the functions of a noun';
see participate. For sense development cp. Gk.
μετοχή, 'participle', fr. μετέχειν, 'to share in,
partake of.

## particle
particle, n. — ME.,fr. L./mriicM/α, dimin. ofpars,
gen. partis, 'part'. See part, п., and -cule.
Derivative: particl-ed, adj.

## parti-colored
parti-colored, party-colored, adj., variegated. —
The first element comes fr. F. parti, 'divided', pp.
of partir, 'to divide'; see party, adj., and cp.
part, v. For the second element see color.

## particular
particular, adj. — ME. particuler, fr. MF. parii-
culer (F. particulier), fr. L. particulars,
'concerning a small part', fr. particula. See particle
and adj. suff. -ar.
Derivatives: particular, п., particular-ism, п.,
particular-ist, n.,particular-ist-ic, au'y,particular-
ist-ic-al-ly, adv., particularity (q.v.),
particularize, tr. and intr. v.-, particular-iz-ation, п.,
particular-ly, adv., particul-ate, adj.

## particularity
particularity, n. — MF. (= F.) particulate, fr.
Late L. particularitdtem, ace. of particularitds,
fr. L. particular'^. See prec. word and -ity.

## partisan
partisan, partizan, п., an adherent to a party,
cause or person. — MF. (— F.)partisan, fr. dial.
It. partigiano, fr. It. partey 'part, party', fr. L.
partem, ace. of pars. See part, n. For the ending
cp. artisan.
Derivatives: partisan, partizan, adj.,
partisanship, partizan-ship, n.

## partisan
partisan, partizan, п., a kind of pike (hist.)— MF.
partisane, fr. dial. It. partigiana, fem. of
partigiano (see prec. word), hence orig. meaning
'weapon carried by a partisan'. The change of
earlier French partisane to pertuisane in modern
French is due to the influence of F. pertuis, 'hole,
opening', fr. VL. *pertusiare, 'to pierce' (see
pierce).

## partite
partite, adj. — L. partitus, pp. of parttre, partiri,
'to divide'. See part, v., and cp. unipartite,
bipartite, tripartite, multipartite.

## partition
partition, n. — ME. particioun, fr. OF. (= F.)
partition, fr. L. partitionem, ace. of partitio,
'division', fr. partitus, pp. of parttre, partiri, 'to
divide'. See prec. word and -ion and cp. tri-
partition. Cp. also parcener.
Derivatives: partition, tr. v., panixion-ary,
partition-eel, adjs., partition-er, п., partition-ing, п.,

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:565 COLUMN:2 -->
partition-ist, п., partition-ment, n.

## partitive
partitive, adj. and n. — Late L. partitivus, fr. L.
partitus, pp. αϊ par tire, partiri, 'to divide'. See
partite and -ive.
Derivative: partitive-ly, adv.

## partlet
partlet, п., woman's ruff. — Fr. earlier patlet, fr.
MF. patelete, 'a band of stuff', dimin. of pate,
patte (F. pane), 'paw'. The r in partlet is due to
the influence of the next word.

## Partlet
Partlet, п., name of the hen in medieval romance.
— ME. Pertelote, fr. OF. Pertelote, a fem. PN.

## partner
partner, n. — ME. partener, a var. of parcener,
(q.v.); influenced in form by part, n. Cp.
copartner.
Derivatives: partner, tr. v., partner-less, adj.,
partner-ship, n.

## partridge
partridge, n. — ME. partrich, pertrich, fr. OF.
perdriz, fr. perdiz (F. perdrix), fr. L. perdicem,
ace. of perdix, fr. Gk. πέρδΐξ, gen. πέρδίκος,
of s.m., which is related to πέρδεσθ-αι. 'to break
wind'; so called from the whirring sound made
by the bird when it rises from the ground. Gk.
πέρδεσθοα is cogn. with OI. pardate, 'breaks
■wind', Alb. pjerfi, Ί break wind', Lith. perdiu,
persti, Lett, pirdu, pirst, Russ. perdet\ OHG.
ferzan, ON- freta, ME. fer ten, far ten, 'to break
wind'. All these words derive from the I.-E.
imitative base *perd-, 'to break wind'. Cp. also
pedicular.

## parturiency
parturiency, n. — Formed from next word with
suff. -cy.

## parturient
parturient, adj., about to give birth. — L. par-
turiens, gen. -entis, pres. part, ofparturire, 'to be
in labor', lit. 'to wish to bring forth', a desider-
ative verb formed fr. partus, pp. of pario, parere,
'to bring forth', whence also parens, gen.
parentis, 'parent'. See parent and cp. postpartum. For
the Latin desiderative suff. -turire, -surire, cp.
abiturieni, esurient, vomiturition.

## parturifacient
parturifacient, adj., promoting parturition (med.)
— Coined fr. L. parturire, 'to desire to bring
forth', and faciens, gen. facientis, pres. part, of
facere, 'to make'. See prec. word and -facient.

## parturition
parturition, п., childbirth. — L. parturitio, gen.
itionis, 'desire to bring forth', fr. parturit(um),
pp. stem of parturire. See parturient and -ition.

## party
party, n. — OF. (= F.) partie, 'part', lit. 'that
which is divided', prop. fem. pp. of partir, 'to
divide', used as a noun; in some senses fr. F.
parti, 'party', prop. masc. pp. of partir, 'to
divide', used as a noun. See partite.

## party
party, adj., divided into parts of different
tinctures {her.) — F. parti, 'divided', pp. of partir.
See partite.

## party-colored
party-colored, adj. — See parti-colored.

## parulis
parulis, п., infection in the gum {med.) —
Medical L., fr. Gk. παρουλίς, 'gumboil', fr. παρά
(see para-, 'beside') and οδλον, 'gnm'. See ulitis.

## parure
parure, п., a set of ornaments. — F., fr. OF., fr.
parer, 'to prepare, dress, trim, adorn, pare', fr.
L. parare, 'to prepare'. See pare and -ure.

## parvenu
parvenu, п., an upstart. — F., prop. pp. of par-
venir, 'to arrive at, reach, attain, succeed', fr. L.
pervenire, 'to arrive at', fr. per, 'through', and
venire, 'to come'. See per- and come and cp.
venue, 'arrival'.
Derivatives", parvenu, adj., parvenu-ism, n.

## parvi-
parvi-, combining form meaning 'small, little'. —
L. parvi-, fr. parvus, 'small, little', which is re],
to parum, 'a little, too little', and cogn. with Gk.
παΰρος, 'small' (L. parvus stands to Gk. παϋρος
as L. nervus, 'nerve', stands to Gk. νεΰρον, of
s.m.); fr. I.-E. base *pou-, *рёи-, *ри-, 'small,
little, few'. See few and words there referred to
and cp. esp. the second element in semper-,

## parvis
parvis, п., open space in front of a church. —
ME. parvys, fr. OF. parevis, parvis (F. parvis),
fr. ML. Paradisus, lit. 'paradise', name of the
court in front of St. Peter's in Rome. See paradise.

## parvoline
parvoline, also par vol in, п., an oily liquid CSH13N.
— Coined by the English chemist Charles
Hanson Greville Williams (1829-1910) fr. L.
parvus, 'small', prob. on the analogy of picoline;
so called by him in allusion to its relatively small
volatility. See parvi-.

## Parzival
Parzival, п., hero of medieval Jegends. — OF.
Perceval, lit. 'he that breaks through the valley',
fr. percer, 'to pierce, break through' and vaf,

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:565 COLUMN:3 -->
'valley'. See pierce and vale, valley and cp.
Parsifal.

## pas
pas, п., step, dance, precedence. — F., 'step,
pace', fr. L. passus. See pace and cp. the second
word in faux pas.

## Pasch
Pasch, n., Passover; Easter. — ME. paske, pasche,
fr. OF. pasche, pasque (F. pdque), fr. Late L.
pascha, fr. Late Gk. πάσχα, fr. Aram, pasha,
emphatic state corresponding to Heb. ha-p-
pesah, 'Passover', fr. pusab, 'he passed over'; see
Ex. 12: 13, 23 and 27. Cp. next word.

## paschal
paschal, adj., pertaining to Passover; pertaining
to Easter. — ME., fr. MF. (- F.) pascal, fr.
Late L. pascha/is, fr. pascha. See prec. word and
adj. suff. -al.

## pascoite
pascoite, п., a hydrous vanadate of calcium
{mineral.) — Named after Cerro de Pasco in Peru.
For the ending see subst. suff. -ite.

## pascual
pascual, adj., pertaining to plants growing in
pastures. — OF., fr. ML. pascualis, Of, or
pertaining to, pasture1, fr. L. pascuus, of s.m., fr.
pasco, pascere, 'to feed, pasture'. See pastor and
adj. suff. -al.

## pash
pash, tr. and intr. v., to hurl, dash {dial) — Of
imitative origin.
Derivative: pash, п., a smashing blow.

## pash
pash, п., the head {no wdial.)—Of uncertain origin.

## pasha
pasha, pacha, п., a Turkish honorary title given
formerly to officers of high rank. — Turkish
pasha, basha, prob. contracted fr. Pers. padshah
(see padishah); influenced in form by Turkish
baskak, 'governor'. See Houtsma, The
Encyclopaedia of Islam, III, 1114, and cp. bashaw.

## pashalik
pashalik, also pashalic, п., the jurisdiction of a
pasha; the province governed by a pasha. —
Turk., fr. pasha, 'pasha', and -life, suff. of-qual-
ity. See pasha and cp. the suff. in beylik.

## pashm
pashm, п., wool obtained from the Tibetan goat.
— Pecs, pashm, 'wool', cogn. with Ol.paksman-,
'eyebrows, hair', Gk. πέκειυ, 'to comb', ττέκος,
'fleece, wool', πόκος, 'wool uncombed, fleece',
πέκειν, 'to comb', L.pectere, of s.m.; fr. I.-E.
base *pek-, 'to pluck (wool or hair)'. Seepecten
and cp. words there referred to.

## pasigraphy
pasigraphy, п., system of writing proposed for
universal use. — Lit., 'a writing for all';
irregularly formed fr. Gk. ttkol, 'for all', dative pi. of
πας, πάσα, πάν, 'all', and -γραφία, fr. γρά-
φειν, 'to write'. See pan- and -graphy and cp. next
word.
Derivatives: pasigraph-ic, pasigraph-ic-al, adjs.

## Pasiphae
Pasiphae, п., wife of Minos and mother of An-
drogeus, Phaedra and Ariadne (Greek mythol.)
— L,, fr. Gk. Πασ(.φάη, fr. πασιφαής, 'shining
for all', fr. πασι, 'for all', and φάος, 'light'. For
the first element see prec. word, for the second
see phosphorus.

## Paspalum
Paspalum, п., a genus of plants. — ModL., fr.
Gk. πάσπαλος, 'millet*, which is rel. to πασπά-
λη, παιπάλη, 'the finest flour'. These words are
prob. formed from the reduplication of I.-E.
base *pel-, 'dust, porridge made of meal'. Cp.
Gk. πάλη, 'sifted meal', which prob. derives
from the simple base *pel-, whence also L.
pollen, 'fine flour, milldust'. See pollen and cp.
words there referred to,

## pasqueflower
pasqueflower, n. — Earlier pass-flower, loan
translation of F. passe-fleur, 'a variety of anemone',
fr. passer, 'to pass, surpass'; see pass, v. Pass-
flower was changed into pasque-flower by John
Gerard (1546-1612) from a confusion of the first
element of the name with Pasque (now Pdques),
'Easter', fr. L. pascha; see Pasch.

## pasquil
pasquil, п., a pasquinade. — ModL. pasquillus,
fr. It. pasquillo, dimin. of pasquino, fr. Pasquino.
See next word.
Deriv-iiives: pasquil, tr. and intr. v., pasquil{l)-
ant, п., pasquil(l)-er, п., pasquil{l)-ic, adj.

## Pasquln
Pasquln, п., the statue named after Pasquino. —
F., fr. h. Pasquino, name of a mutilated statue
set up by Cardinal Caraffa in Rome in 1501. The
statue was named after a schoolmaster called
Pasquino, who lived near-by. (Now we know
that the statue in question is a representation of
Menelaus dragging the body of the dead Pa-
troclus.) It became customary to post satirical
verses and lampoons on this statue, whence It.

## pasquino
pasquino, 'pasquinade'. See next word and pas-

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:566 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: 539 | PATCH -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:566 COLUMN:1 -->
quinade.

## pasquin
pasquin, п., a pasquinade. — F. pasquin, fr. It.
pasquino, 'pasquinade', fr. Pasquino, name of a
statue in Rome. See ртес. word.

## pasquinade
pasquinade, п., a lampoon. — MF. (= F.), fr. It.
pasquinata, fr. Pasquino. See Pasquin and -ade
and cp. pasquij.
Derivatives: pasquinade, tr. v., pasquinad-er, n.

## pass
pass, intr. and tr. v. — ME. passen, fr. OF. (= F.)
passer, fr, VL. *passare, fr. L. passus, 'step,
pace'. See pace and cp. past. Cp. also impass,
trespass.
Derivatives: pass-ed, adj., pass-ing, adj. and п.,
pass-ing-ly, adv.

## pass
pass, n. — Partly fr. ME. passe, fr. MF. (= F.)
passe, fr. passer, 'to pass', panly directly fr.
pass, v.

## passable
passable, adj. — ME., fr. MF. ( = F.), fr. passer,
'to pass'. See pass, v., and -able.
Derivatives: passabl-y, adv.

## passade
passade, п., the course of a horse forward and
backward. — F., fr. It. passata, fr. passare, 'to
pass', fr. VL. *passare. See pass, v., and -ade.

## passage
passage, intr. v., to move sideways in riding. —
F. passager, altered fr. passeger (under the
influence of the noun passage), fr. It. passeggiare,
'to walk', fr. passeggio, 'a walk', fr. passo, 'pace,
step', fr. L. passus. See pace and -age and cp.
pass, n.

## passage
passage, п., the act of passing — ME., fr. OF.
(— F.), ft. passer, 'to pass'. See pass, v., and-age.
Derivative: passage, intr. v., to make a passage;
to pass.

## passant
passant, adj., represented as walking (her.) ~ ¥.,
pres. part, of passer, 'to pass'. See pass, v., and
-ant.

## passe
passe, fern, passee, past; faded — F., pp. of
passer, 'to pass'. See pass, v.

## passementerie
passementerie, п., dress trimming- — F., fr. passe-
menter, 'to trim', fr. passement, 'trimmings', fr.
passer, 'to pass'. See pass, v., and the suffixes
-ment and -ery.

## passenger
passenger, n. — ME. passager, fr. MF. (= F.)
passager, fr. passage, 'passage'; see passage, п.,
and -er. The η in passenger is inirusive. Cp.
harbinger, messenger, porringer, scavenger,
wharfinger.

## passe-partout
passe-partout, п., 1) master-key; 2) a kind of
picture frame— F., lit. 'pass everywhere', fr.passer,
'to pass', and partout, 'everywhere'. F. passer
derives fr. VL. "passare; see pass, v. F. partout
is compounded of par, 'through' (fr. L. per), and
tout, 'all' (fr. L. totus); see per- and total and cp.
tout, n.

## Passer
Passer, п., the genus of the sparrow and its
relatives (omithoi.) — L.passer; possibly of imitative
origin. Cp. Passeres, passerine.

## Passeres
Passeres, n. pi., an order of birds equivalent to
the Passeriformes (prnithol.) — ModL. passeres,
prop. pi. of L. passer, 'sparrow'.
See Passer.

## Passeriformes
Passeriformes, n. pi., an order of birds (omithol.)
— ModL. Passeriformes, lit. 'having the form of
sparrows', fr, L. passer, 'sparrow', and -formis,
'of the form of, fr. forma, 'form, shape'. See
Passer and form, n.

## passerine
passerine, adj., pertaining ю the Passeriformes or
Passeres; п., a passerine bird. — L. passerfnus,
'pertaining to the sparrow', fr. passer. See passer
and -ine (representing L. -inus).

## passibility
passibility, n. — Late L. passibilitas, 'capability
of suffering, passibility', fr. passibilis. See next
word and -ity.

## passible
passible, adj., that which can feel or suffer;
sensible. — ME., fr. MF. (= F.) passible, fr.^Late
L. passibilis, 'capable of suffering, passible', fr,
L. passus, pp. of pati, 'to suffer'. See patient and
-ible and cp. passion.
Derivative: passible-ness, n.

## Passffiora
Passffiora, п., a genus of vines (bot.) — ModL.
Passiflora, coined fr. L. passio, 'passion', and

## flos
flos, gen. fioris, 'flower'; see passion and flower.
Hence Passiflora lit. means 'passionflower'; see
passionflower,

## passim
passim, adv., here and there. — L., 'hither and
thither', lit. 'scattered about', ϊτ. passus (ΐοτ *pat-
sus), pp. of pandere, 'to spread out, scatter
about', rel. to patere, 'to be open', patulus,

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:566 COLUMN:2 -->
'extended*, Gk. πεταννύναι, 'to spread out', ON.
fadmr, 'embrace, bosom', OE. fsedm, 'embrace,
bosom, fathom'. See fathom and cp. words there
referred to.

## passion
passion, n. — ME., fr. OF. (= F.), fr. L. pas-
s'wnem, ace. of passio, 'suffering, passion,
affection', fr. passus, pp. of pari, 'to suffer'. See
patient and -ion and cp. compassion.
Derivatives: passion-less, adj., passion-less-ly,
adv., passion-less-ness, n.

## passion
passion, tr. v., to affect with passion; intr. v., to
show, or be affected with, passion — ME. pas-
sionen, fr. MF. (= F.) passionner, fr. passion.
See passion, n.

## passional
passional, adj., pertaining to, or characterized by,
passion — Late L. passionalis, 'pertaining to
suffering', fr. L. passio, gen. -ionis. See passion,
п., and adj. suff. -al.

## passional
passional, п., a book describing the sufferings of
martyrs. — ML. passionate, neut. of the Late
L. adj. passionalis, used as a noun. See passional,
adj.

## passionate
passionate, adj. — ML. passionatus, fr. L. passio,
gen. -ionis, 'passion'. See passion, п., and adj.
suff. -ate.
Derivatives: passionate-ly, adv., passionate-ness,
n.

## passionflower
passionflower, n. — So called from the fancied
resemblance of parts of the flower to the
instruments of the crucifixion. Cp. Passiflora.

## passive
passive, adj. — ME., fr. L. passivus, 'capable of
suffering', fr. passus, pp. ofpatt, 'to suffer'. See
passion, v., and -ive.
Derivatives .passive, n.,passiv-ate, tr. v.,
passivation, п., passive-ly, adv., passive-ness, п.,
passiv-ism, п., passiv-ist, п., passiv-ity, n.

## Passover
Passover, n. — Compounded of pass over;
rendering of Heb. pasab, in Ex. 12 : 13, 23 and 27.
See pass, v., and over and cp. Pesah.

## passport
passport, n. — MF. (= F.)passeport, orig.
meaning 'permission to pass through a port', fr. passe,
imper. of passer, 'to pass', and port, 'port,
harbor'. See pass, v., and port, 'harbor'.
Derivative: passport, tr. v.

## passus
passus, п., part of a poem or story. — L, 'a step,
pace'. See pace.

## past
past, adj. — Pp. of pass.
Derivatives: past, п., prep., adv.

## paste
paste, п., an adhesive compound —ME., fr. OF.
paste (F. pate), fr. Late L. pasta (whence also
It., OProveng. and Sp. pasta), fr. Gk. πάστη,
'barleymash', which is rel. to παστός, παστή,
παστόν, 'sprinkled with salt', verbal adj. of
ττάσσειν, 'to sprinkle'. Cp. pastel, pasticcio,
pastiche, pastry, pasty, pate, patisserie, patty,
impaste.
Derivatives '.paste, tr. v.,past-ed, ad'}.,past-er, n.

## paste
paste, tr. and intr. v., to strike, beat — Fr. baste,
'to strike, beat'.
Derivatives '.paste, a.,past-y, %A\.,past-i-ness, n.

## pastel
pastel, п., woad. — MF. ( — F.), fr. Proven?.
pastel, fr. Late L. pastellus, 'woad', dimin.
formed fr. Late L. pasta, 'paste'; so called from the
paste made of the twigs of the plant in producing
the dye.

## pastel
pastel, п., a kind of dry paste used for making
crayons. — F.} fr. It. pastello, fr. Late L.
pastellus (see prec. word); introduced into English by
the diarist John Evelyn (1620-1706).
Derivatives: pastel, tr, and intr. v.,pastel(/)-ist,
n.

## pastern
pastern, п., part of a horse's foot between the
fetlock and the hoof. — ME. pastron, fr. MF.

## pasturon (F. paturon)
pasturon (F. paturon), 'tether for a grazing
horse', later used in the sense 'joint (of a grazing
horse)', fr. pasture, 'tether for a grazing horse',
formed, with change of suff., fr. VL. *pastoria,
of s.m. (whence also It.pastoia, 'tether, shackle;
pastern'), fr. L. pastura, 'pasture'. See pasture
and cp. pester.

## Pasteureila
Pasteureila, п., name of a genus of
Gram-negative bacteria— ModL., named after the French
chemist Louis Pasteur (J822-95). For the ending
see suff. -ella.

## pasteurism
pasteurism, п., Pasteur's method in treating
disease, esp. hydrophobia. — See prec. word and
•ism.

## pasteurize
pasteurize, tr. v., to sterilize (milk, beer, etc.) by

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:566 COLUMN:3 -->
Pasteur's methods — See Pasteureila and -ize.
Derivative: pasteuriz-ation, n.

## pasticcio
pasticcio, п., a medley made up of fragments from
different works — It., 'medley', fr. VL. *pasti-
cium, fr. L. pasta, 'paste'. See paste, n.

## pastiche
pastiche, п., a pasticcio, esp. a literary work made
in the professed imitation of the work of
another author. — F., fr. It. pasticcio. See prec.
word.

## pastille
pastille, pastil, n. — F. pastille, 'lozenge, jujube',
fr. Sp. pastilla, 'aromatic smelling cake', fr. L.
pastillus, d!min. formed fr. panis, 'bread'. See
pantry.

## pastime
pastime, n. — Coined fr. pass and time, on the
analogy of F. passe-temps.

## Pastinaca
Pastinaca, п., a genus of plants, the parsnip (bot.)
— L. pastinaca, 'parsnip', fr. pastinum, 'a two-
