Rathayatra, п., car festival of a divinity
{Hinduism). — Lit. 'chariot procession', fr. OI. rd-
thah,''car, chariot', and ydtrd, 'procession,
festival'. The first element is rel. to Avestic ratio-,
'car, chariot*, and cogn. with L. rota, 'wheel';
see rota. The second element is a derivative of
OI. ydti, yate, 'goes, travels'; see janitor and cp.
jann.

## rathe
rathe, rath, adj., early. — ME., 'quick, swift*, fr.
OE. пгэгд, var. hrsed, 'quick, swift, agile, hasty',
which is rel. to ON. hradr, OHG. hrad, of s.m.,
and to OE. hradian, ON. hrada, 'to hasten'.
These words derive perh. from a dental
enlargement of I.-E. base *(s)qer-, 'to leap'. See
cardinal, adj., and cp. rather.
Derivatives: rathe-ly, adv., rathe-ness, n.

## rathe
rathe, adv., early. — ME., 'quickly', fr. OE.
hrade, rel. to the adjective hrsed. See prec. word.

## rather
rather, adv. — ME., 'more quickly', fr. OE. hra-
dor, compar. of hrade. See prec. word and
compar. suff. -er.

## rathite
rathite, п., a lead sulfarsenite {mineral.) —
Named after the German mineralogist Gerhard
vom Rath (1830-88). For the ending see subst.
suff. -ite.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:645 COLUMN:2 -->

## ratification
ratification, п., confirmation. — ME., fr. MF.
(= F.(, fr. ML. ratificdtionem, ace. of ratifiedtio,
fr. ratificatus, pp. of ratificare. See next word
and -ation.

## ratify
ratify, tr. v., to confirm. — ME. ratifien, fr. MF.
(== F.) ratifier, fr. ML. ratificare, 'to fix by
reckoning', formed fr. L. ratus, pp. of reor, rert, 'to
reckon, believe, think', and -ficdre, fx.facere, 'to
make, do*. See rate, 'amount', and -fy.
Derivative: ratifi-er, n.

## ratio
ratio, п., proportion. — L. ratio, 'reckoning,
calculation, matter, affair, relation; reason*, fr.
ratus, pp. of reor, reri, 'to think, judge, reckon'.
See reason and cp. ration, which are both
doublets of ratio. Cp. also rate, 'amount'.

## ratiocinate
ratiocinate, intr. v., to reason. — L. ratidcindtus,
pp. of ratiocindri, 'to reckon, calculate,
consider, deliberate', compounded of ratio (see prec.
word) and -cindri, which is prob. rel. to L.
condri, 'to try, endeavor', and cogn. with Gk.
έγκονεΐν, 'to be quick and active', διάκονος,
'servant'. See deacon and cp. the'second element
in vaticinate.

## ratiocination
ratiocination, п., reasoning. — MF. (= F.), fr. L.
ratiocinationem,accofratidcindtid,'areasoning\
fr. ratidcindtus, pp. of ratiocindri. See prec. word
and -ion.

## ratiocinative
ratiocinative, adj., pertaining to reasoning. — L.
ratidcindtivus, fr. ratiocindtus, pp. of ratiocindri.
See ratiocinate and -ive.

## ration
ration, п., 1) a fixed portion; 2) a fixed allowance.
— F., fr. L. rationem, ace. of ratio. See ratio.
Derivatives: ration, tr. v., to supply with rations,
rational (q.v.)

## rational
rational, adj. — ME. racional, fr. L. rationdlis,
'pertaining to reason*, fr. ratio. See ratio and adj.
suff. -al.
Derivatives: rational, п., rational-ism, п., ration-
af-ist, п., and adj., rational-ist-ic, adj., rational-
ist-ic-al-ly, adv., rational-ize, tr. and intr. v.,
rational-iz-ation, п., rational-ly, adv.

## rationale
rationale, п., exposition of principles. — L.
rationale, 'a rational thing', neut. of the adjective
rationdlis. See prec. word.

## rationality
rationality, n. — Late L. rationdlitds, fr. L.
rationdlis. See rational and -ity.

## Ratitae
Ratitae, n. pi., a division of birds (zool.) —
ModL., prop. fem. pi. of ratitus, 'marked with
the figure of a raft', fr. L. ratis, 'raft'. See rood
and cp. radeau.

## ratite
ratite, adj., 1) having a flat breastbone; 2)
pertaining to the division of Ratitae; п., one of the
Ratitae. — See prec. word and adj. suff. -ite.

## ratlin
ratlin, ratline, rattling, n. {naut.) — Of uncertain
origin.

## ratoon
ratoon, п., a sprout from the sugar cane after it
has been cut down. — Sp. retono, 'sprout', fr.
retonar, 'to sprout again', lit. 'to sprout after
autumn', fr. pref. re-, 'again* (see re-), and
otonar, 'to grow in autumn', fr. otono, 'autumn',
fr. L. autumnus. See autumn.
Derivative: ratoon, intr. and tr. v., to send up.

## rattan
rattan, also ratan, п., the long stem of the palms
of the genera Calamus and Daemonorops. —
Malay rotan, for rautan, fr. raut, 'to peel, pare,
trim'. Cp. rotang.
Derivative: rattan, ratan, tr. v., to supply with
rattan; to punish by striking with a rattan.

## rat-tat
rat-tat, rat-a-tat, п., the sound of a loud knocking
at the door. — Imitative.

## ratteen
ratteen, п., a thick woolen fabric (archaic). — F.
ratine, 'frieze, ratteen', of unknown origin.

## ratten
ratten, п., to destroy machinery in defiance of a
trade union. — Lit. 'to be harmful like a rat*,
denominated fr. ratten, an English dial. var. of
rat.

## rattle
rattle, intr. and tr. v. — ME. ratelen, rel. to OE.
hratele, name of a plant, MDu., Du. ratelen, 'to
rattle', ratel, 'rattle*, MHG: газзеп, 'to rage',
ratelen, of s.m., G. rasseln, 'to rattle* (the
meaning of the latter was influenced by Du.
ratelen), OE. hratian, hradian, 'to hasten', ON.
hrata, 'to reel, stagger', and prob. cogn. with
Gk. κραδάω, κραδαίνω, Ί brandish, shake*.
See cardinal, adj.
Derivatives: rattle, п., rattl-er, п., rattl-ing, adj.,
rattl-ing-ly, adv., rattl-ing-ness, п., rattl-y, adj.

## raucity
raucity, п., hoarseness. — L. raucitds, fr. raucus.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:645 COLUMN:3 -->
See next word and -ity.

## raucous
raucous, adj., hoarse. — L. raucus, 'hoarse', which
is contracted fr. *rawicos, and, accordingly, a
derivative of ravus, 'hoarse', from the imitative
base *re-, *rd, whence also OI. rayati, 'barks',
rduti, ruvati, ravati, 'roars'. Arm. ornal, 'to
howl* (said of wolves), Gk. ώ-ρυεσθαι, 'to
howl, roar', OSlav. revo, rjevot Ί roar', raru, 'a
sound', ON. rdmr, 'hoarse', OE. ryn, 'a roaring',
rynan, 'to roar', rdrian, 'to wail; to bellow'. Cp.
roar, Rudra, rumble, rumor, rut, 'sexual
excitement of animals'.
Derivatives: raucous-ly, adv., raucous-ness, П.

## Rauwolfia
Rauwolfia, п., a genus of tropical plants of the
dogbane family {bot.) — ModL., named after
the German botanist and traveler Leonhard
Rauwolf (died in 1596). For the ending see 1st
suff. -ia.

## ravage
ravage, п., devastation, ruin. — F., fr. ravir, 'to
carry off, ravish'. See ravish and -age.

## ravage
ravage, tr. and intr. v. — F. ravager, 'to
devastate, ravage', fr. ravage. See ravage, n.
Derivatives: ravage-ment, п., ravag-er, n.

## rave
rave, intr. v., to speak as in delirium; tr. v., to
utter as if in delirium. — ME. raven, fr. OF.
raver, resver, 'to rave* (whence F. river, 'to
dream', rive, 'dream'). OF. resver is formed fr.
pref. re- (see re-) and *esver, 'to wander, roam
about' (whence also desver, 'to be mad'), fr.
Gaulish-Latin base *esvo, 'vagabond', fr. VL.
*exvagus, fr. 1st ex- and L. vagus, 'wandering';
see vagary and cp. reverie. See also
Bloch-Wartburg, DELF., p. 525.
Derivatives: rave, п., rav-ing, adj., rav-ing-lyy
adv.

## rave
rave, п., framework placed in a cart. — Of
uncertain origin.

## ravel
ravel, tr. v., 1) to entangle; 2) to untwist; 3) to
disentangle; intr. v., ]) to become entangled;
2) to become untwisted; 3) to be disentangled.
— Early ModDu. ravelen, 'to entangle' (Du.
rafelen, 'to unravel'), rel. to EFris. rafelen, LG.
rabbeln, rebeln, rebbeln, reffeln. See raffle,
'lottery' .
Derivatives: ravel, п., ravel(l)-edy adj.,
ravelling, п., ravel{l)-er, п., ravel-ment, n.

## ravelin
ravelin, п., a triangular work placed between two
bastions. — F., fr. It. ravellino, a later var. of
rivellino, which is of unknown origin.

## raven
raven, п., a large bird of the crow family (Corvus
corax). — ME., fr. OE. hrxfn, rel. to ON. hrafn,
Dan. ravn, MLG. rave, Du. raaf, OHG. hraban,
rabo, MHG. raben, rabe, G. Rabe, 'raven', and
cogn. with L. crepdre, 'to creak, clatter',
possibly also with OI. kfpate, 'laments'. These
words are labial enlargements of I.-E. base
*qer-y *qor-, *qr-, imitative of harsh sounds.
From the same base are Gk. κόραξ, 'crow,
raven', κορώνη, 'crow', L. cornix, 'crow', corvus,
'raven', OI. krofati, Avestic xraosaiti, 'cries,
shouts', OI. krosah, 'a call, a shout', OSlav.
kriku, 'shout', kricati, 'to shout', Gk. κράζειν,
κρώζειν, 'to croak', κραυγή, 'a crying, a
shouting', L. crocire, 'to croak', OSlav. kraiu, kra-
kati, Lith. kraukiu, kraukti, 'to croak', OSlav.
kruku, 'raven', Lith. krauklps, 'crow', Lett.
krauklis, 'raven7, Lith. krdke, OPruss. krakkoy
'the black woodpecker', MIr. corr, 'crane',
cercc, 'hen', OE. hrdc, ON. hrdkr, 'rook'. Cp.
corbel, Coronis, Corvus, rook, the bird, and the
first element in С ire actus, coracoid, cormorant,
Coronopus, Cp. also kos. Cp. also crepitate.
Derivative: raven-ry, n.

## raven
raven, intr. v., to prey; tr. v., to devour greedily
(rare). — MF. raviner, 'to ravager*, fr. ravine,
'rapine'. See ravin.
Derivatives: raven-ing, adj., raven-ing-ly, adv.,

## raven-ous
raven-ous, adj., raven-ous-ly, adv., raven-ous-
ness, n.

## ravigote
ravigote, п., shallot sauce. — F., back formation
fr. ravigoter, 'to revive, refresh', which is
formed—with change of suff.—fr. OF. ravigorer,
of s.m., fr. pref. ra-, contraction of L. re- and ad
(see re- and ad-) and vigor, gen. vigor is,
'liveliness'. See vigor,

## ravin
ravin, ravine, п., plunder. — ME. ravin, ravine, fr.
MF. ravine, 'rapine, robbery', fr. OF., fr. L. ra-

## pina. See rapine and cp. raven
pina. See rapine and cp. raven, 'to prey'. In ModF.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:646 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: 619 | REARM -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:646 COLUMN:1 -->
ravine means 'torrent, gully'. Cp. next word.

## ravine
ravine, п., a deep cleft or gorge. — F., 'mountain
torrent, ravine', fr. OF. ravine, 'rapine, robbery;
rapidity, impetuosity; rush of water, torrent'.
See prec. word.

## ravish
ravish, tr. v. — ME. ravisshen, fr. F. raviss-, pres.
part, stem of ravir, 'to carry off, ravish', fr. VL.
*rapire, fr. L. rapere, 'to seize'. See rapid and
verbal sufT. -ish and cp. rape, 'to seize'.
Derivatives: ravish-er, п., ravish-ing, adj., rav-
ish-ing-ly, adv., ravish-ment, n.

## raw
raw, adj. — ME., fr. OE. hreaw, rel. to OS. hra,
ON. hrar, Dan. raa, Swed. ra, MDu. rau, Du.
rauw, OHG. (k)rao, krawer, MHG. rdt roer, G.
roh, fr. l.-E. base *qrew -, *qreu-, 'congealed,
bloody', whence also 01. kravih, 'raw flesh', Gk.
κρέας (for *κρέΡας), 'flesh', L. cruor, 'blood',
crudus, 'raw, not cooked'. See crude and cp.
words there referred to.
Derivatives: raw, п., and tr. v., raw-ish, adj.,
raw-ish-ness, n.

## ray
ray, п., beam, radiance. — ME., fr. OF. rax
(whence F. rai, rais, 'spoke of wheel', rayon,
'ray', see rayon), fr. L. radius. See radius.
Derivatives: ray, intr. and tr. v., ray-ed, adj.,
ray-less, adj.
гпу, п., a fish of the order Selachii. — ME. raye,
fr. OF. (= F.) raie, fr. L. raia, a word of
uncertain origin.

## rayah
rayah, п., a non-Moslem subject in a Moslem
state, esp. in Turkey. — Arab. raltyah, 'flock,
herd; subjects', fr. ra'a, 'he fed, pastured',
which is rel. to Heb. гй'аН, Aram. reia, 'he
pastured, tended', Akkad. гё'й, *to pasture'. Cp.
ryot.

## raylet
raylet, п., a small ray. — Formed fr. ray, 'beam',
with the dimin. suff. -let.

## Raymond
Raymond, also Raymund, masc. PN. — OF. Rai-
mund (F. Raymond), fr. Frankish Raginmund,
lit. 'counsel-protection'; compounded of ragin,
'counsel, might', and mund, 'hand, protection',
which is rel. to OHG. munt, OE. mund, 'hand,
protection*, and cogn. with L. manus, 'hand'.
See manual and cp. mound, 'a heap of earth'. Cp.
also the second element in Edmond, Osmond,
Siglsmund.

## rayon
rayon, п., artificial silk. — F. rayon, 'ray', fr.
OF. rai, 'ray' (see ray, 'beam'); so called
because of its glossy appearance.

## raze
raze, tr. v., to level to the ground, destroy. —
Alter, of rase.
Derivatives: raze, п., razee (q.v.), razor (q.v.)

## razee
razee, п., a ship whose upper deck has been cut
away. — Fr. F. (vaisseau) rase, lit. '(a ship) cut
down', pp. of raser. See prec. word.
Derivative: razee, tr. v.

## razor
razor, n. — ME. rasour, fr. OF. rasor, rasour, fr.
raser. See rase and agential surf. -or.
Derivative: razor, tr. v.

## razzia
razzia, п., a raid. — F., fr. Algerian
pronunciation of Arab, ghdziycr, 'raid', a derivative of the
verb ghaza (base gh-z-w), 'he made war'. Cp.
ghazi.

## razzle-dazzle
razzle-dazzle, п., confusion, spree (slang). — The
first element is a blend of rattle and dazzle.

## re
re, п., a syllable used in solmization to denote
the second tone of the diatonic scale (mus.)

## re
re, in the matter of. — L. re, abl. οι res, 'thing,
matter'. See res, real, adj.

## re-
re-, red-, pref. meaning 1) back; 2) again. —
ME., fr. OF., fr. L. re-, before a vowel red-,
'back; again', either directly or through the
medium of F. re-, re-, resp. red-, red-. Cp. retro-.

## reach
reach, tr. and intr. v., to obtain. — ME. rechen, fr.
OE. гёёсап, 'to stretch out', rel. to OFris. reka,
reza, MDu. reiken, reken, Du. reiken. OHG.,
MHG., G. reichen, 'to attain, reach', ON. and
Norw. reik, 'parting of the hair', and cogn. with
Lith. raiiius, raiitis, 'to stretch oneself, and its
iterative rdizaus, raizytis, Olr. riag (fr. riga),
'torture (caused by racking)'. All these words
derive fr. I.-E. base *reig-, 'to stretch out'. Cp.
the related I.-E. base *reg-, 'to stretch,
straighten', whence Gk. όρέγειν, 'to reach, stretch
out', L. regere, 'to stretch, extend, make
straight; to rule*, and see regent, adj.
Derivatives: reach, п., reach-able, adj., reach-er,
п., reach-ing, reach-less, reach-y, adjs.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:646 COLUMN:2 -->

## react
react, tr. and intr. v. — ModL. reactus, pp. of
reagere, fr. re- and L. agere, 'to set in motion,
drive, lead; to do, act'. See act.
Derivatives: react-ance, n. (electr.), react-ive,
adj., react-ive-ly, adv., react-ive-ness, п., react-
iv-ity, п., react-or, n.

## re-act
re-act, tr. v., to act again. — Formed fr. re- and
act.

## reaction
reaction, n. — Formed fr. re- and action.
Derivatives: reaction-ary, adj. and п., reaction-
ari-ness, п., reaction-ar-ism, п., reaction-ar-ist,
п., reaction-ism, п., reactionist, n.

## read
read, tr. and intr. v. — ME. reden, fr. OE. rxdan,
'to advise, counsel, discuss, deliberate, rule,
guess, interpret, read' (whence OE. rxd, 'advise,
counsel'), rel. to OS. radan, ON. гада, Swed.
rada, OFris. reda, Du. raden, OHG. rdtan,
MHG. rateti, 'to advise, counsel*, G. raten, 'to
advise, counsel, guess', erraten, 'to guess',
Goth, -redan (e.g. in ga-redan, 'to provide for
oneself) and cogn. with OI. radhndti, radhyati,
'makes fit, succeeds, satisfies', OSlav. raditi, 'to
care for', Olr. radim, *1 speak', rad, 'speech*,
immradim, Ί deliberate', OW. amraud, 'mind',
ModW. amrawdd, 'conversation'. All these
words derive fr. I.-E. *re-dh-, *re-dh~,
enlargements of base *ar-, *are-, *re-, *r -, 'to join,
fix', whence L. reor, reri (pp. ratus), 'to think,
judge, reckon'. See arm, 'the upper limb', and
cp. raad, rede, 'counsel', riddle, 'engima', and
the second element in hatred, kindred and in the
PNs. Conrad, Eldred. Cp. also reason and
words there referred to.
Derivatives: read, п., the act of reading,
readable, adj., read-abil-ity, п., read-able-ness, п.,
read-abl-y, adv., reader (q.v.), read-ing, n. and
adj.

## read
read, pret. and pp. of read. — ME. redde, resp.
(ge)red, fr. OE. rxdde, resp. {ge)red.

## reader
reader, n. — ME. redere, fr. OE. rxdere, fr. rx-
dan, 'to read*. See prec. word and agential suff.
-er.

## readjust
readjust, tr. v., to adjust again. — Formed fr. re-
and adjust.
Derivative: readjust-ment, n. (cp. adjustment.)

## ready
ready, adj. — ME. redi, readi, formed—with
change of suff.—fr. OE. rxde, gerxde, 'ready',
which is related to OFris. rede, MDu. gereit,
gereet, Du. gereed, bereid, OHG. reiti, bireiti,
MHG. bereite, gereite, G. bereit, 'ready', ON.
greidr, 'ready, plain', Goth, garaips, 'ordered,
arranged'. These words prob. meant orig.
'prepared for riding', and are rel. to ride (q.v.) For
sense development cp. G.fertig, 'ready', which
derives fr. Fahrt, 'journey, voyage, trip* (fr.
fahren, 'to go, travel'), and lit. means 'ready to
travel'. Cp. already. Cp. also redd, array, curry,
'to dress leather*, graith, and the second element
in hatred, kindred. Cp. also redowa.
Derivatives: ready, adj. and tr. v., readi-ly, adv.,
readi-ness, n.

## reaffirm
reaffirm, tr. v., to affirm again with emphasis. —
Formed fr. re- and affirm.
Derivatives: reaffirm-ance, п., reaffirm-ation, n.

## reagency
reagency, п., action of a reagent. — Formed from
next word with suff. -cy.

## reagent
reagent, п., that which reacts (chem.) — Formed
fr. re- and agent. Cp. react.

## real
real, adj., genuine. — ME., fr. OF. real (F. reel),
'real, actual', fr. Late L. realis, 'pertaining to a
thing*, fr. L. res, 'thing, object, matter, affair,
circumstance', which is rel. to Umbr. ri
(corresponding to L. re, abl. of res) and cogn. with
OI. rah, 'possession, property*, rayih, 'gift',
raiah, Avestic rato, 'offered' (pp.), OI. revdnt-,
Avestic raevant-, 'rich'. Cp. res, Cp. also re, 'in
the matter of, reatus, rebus, reify, reus, the first
element in republic and the first word in res
gesta. For the ending in real see adj. suff. -a).
Derivatives: real, п., realism (q.v.), realist (q.v.),
realize (q.v.), real-ly, adv., real-ness, n.

## reai
reai, п., an old Spanish silver coin. — Sp., prop.
an adjective meaning 'royal*, fr. L. regdlis
(whence also F. royal). See regal, adj., and cp.
royal. Cp. also reis.

## realgar
realgar, п., arsenic sulfide. — ME., fr. ML., fr.
Sp. rejalgar, fr. Arab, rahj al-ghar, lit. 'powder
of the mine', fr. rahj, 'powder', al-, 'the', and

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:646 COLUMN:3 -->
ghar, 'cave, mine'.

## realism
realism, n. — G. Realismus, formed fr. Late L.
realis (see real, adj.) with suff. -ismus, fr. L. -is-
mus (see -ism).

## realist
realist, n. and adj. — F. realiste, formed fr. OF.
real (see real, adj.) with suff. -iste (see -ist).
Derivatives: realist-ic, adj., realist-ic-al-ly, adv.

## reality
reality, n. — F. realite, fr. ML. realitatem, ace. of
realitas, fr. Late L. realis. See real, adj., and
suff. -ity.

## realize
realize, tr. and intr. v. — F. realiser, fr. MF., fr.
OF. real, 'real, actual'. See real, adj., and -ize.
Derivatives: realiz-able, adj. realiz-ation, η.,
realiz-er, п., realiz-ing, adj., realiz-ing-ly, adv.

## realm
realm, n. — ME. realme, reaume, fr. OF. realme,
reaume (F. royaume), 'kingdom, realm', which
is a blend of OF. reial (F. royal), 'regal, royal*
(see royal), and OF. reiame, reemme, which
derives fr. L. regimen, 'direction, government';
see regimen. Cp. OProvenc. reyalme, realme,
which also derives fr. L. regimen, and It. reame,
OSp. reame, realme, which are borrowed fr.
OProvenc. or OF.

## realmless
realmless, adj. — Coined by the English poet
John Keats (1795-1821) fr. realm and suff. -less,

## realpolitik
realpolitik, п., real, i.e. practical, politics. — G.
Realpolitik. See real, adj., and politic,

## realschule
realschule, п., secondary school in which no
classics are taught; the opposite of a gymnasium. —
G. Realschule, lit. 'real (= practical) school';
first used by the German parson Chr. Semler in
1706. See real, adj., and school,'a place of
learning', and cp. the first element in prec. word.

## realtor
realtor, п., a real estate broker. — Coined by С
Chadbournof Minneapolis about 1915 fr.realty,
'real estate', and agential suff. -or.

## realty
realty, п., real estate. — Formed fr. real, adj.,
with suff. -ty.

## realty
realty, п., royalty (obsol.) — OF. realte (F.
royaute), fr. VL. *regalitatem, ace. of *regalitas,
fr. L. regdlis, 'belonging to a king'. See regal,
adj., and cp. words there referred to.

## ream
ream, п., 20 quires of paper. — ME. reme, fr. OF.
rayme (F. rame), fr. Sp. resma, fr. Arab. rlzmaht
'bundle, bundle of paper'.

## ream
ream, п., cream; froth. — ME. rem, fr. OE.
ream, 'cream*, rel. to MLG. rom, rdme, Du.
room, MHG. roum,G.Rahm,lce\.rjdmi,'cream*,
fr. Teut. base *rauma-, which corresponds perh.
to I.-E. *raugma-, whence Avestic raoyna-,
'butter*. Cp. ramekin.

refuse'. See recusant.
Derivative: recus-able, adj.

## red
red, adj. — ME. red, read, reed, fr. OE. read, rel.
to OE. reod, ON. raudr and rjodr, Dan. red,
Swed. rod, OFris. rdd, MDu. root, rood, Du.
rood, OHG., MHG. rot, G. rot, Goth, roups,
'red', fr. I.-E. base *reudho-, *roudho-, *rudhro-,
'red', whence also OI. rohitah (for *rodhita-)t
rudhirah, Avestic raodita-, 'red, bloody', Gk.
έρυ&ρός 'red', L. ruber, 'red, ruddy', rufus,
'redd, reddish', Umbr. rufru (masc. pi.), 'red',
OSlav. rudu, rudru, Lith. raudas, Olr. ruad,
OCo. rud, Bret, ruz, 'red'. The initial ε in Gk.
έ-ρυθρός is prosthetic and due to the
circumstance that originally the Greek never began a
word with r. (Initial ρ in Greek words is the
equivalent of I.-E. *sr- or *wr-; cp. Gk. ρ4ΐν, 'to
flow*, with OI. sravati, 'it flows', and Gk. ρήτρα,
'word, saying', with Elean fpaxpa, Cypr.
5ρητα). Cp. rud, rudd, 'the fish', ruddle, rust.
Cp. also Erythema, erythro-, rissole, robust,
rochet, 'gurnard', roussette, rubefacient, rubella,
rubeola, rubeosis, rubicund, rubidium, rubify,
rubiginous, rubric, ruby, rufous, russet, Russula,
rust, rutile, and the second element in Erysibe,
erysipelas, Erysiphe, Erythronium. Cp. also the
first element in rorqual.
Derivatives: red, п., redd-en, tr. and intr. v.,
redd-ish, adj., redd-isk-ness, п., red-ly, adv.,
redness, n.

## red-
red-, pref. — See re-.

redact, tr. v. — Back formation fr. L. reddctus,

## pp. of redigere
pp. of redigere, 'to bring back, collect, gather
together', fr. red- and agere, 'to set in motion,
drive, lead; to do, act'. See act.
Derivatives: redaction (q.v.), redact-or, n.

## redaction
redaction, n. — F. redaction, fr. Late L. reddc-

Derivative: redaction-al, adj.

## redan
redan, п., a fortification work consisting of two
parapets at a salient angle. — F. redan, formerly

## redd

— ME. redden, fr. MLG. redden, which is rel.

## reddendum
reddendum, п., a clause in a deed containing a

give back, return, restore', which is formed fr.

See date, 'point of time', and cp. reddition. Cp.
also addendum. For other Latin gerundives or
their derivatives used in English cp. agenda and
words there referred to.

## reddition
reddition, п., 1) restoration; 2) rendering. — ME.
reddicion, fr. MF. (= F.) reddition, fr. L. reddi-
tionem, ace. of redditio, 'a giving back,
returning', fr. redditus, pp. of reddere. See reddendum

of reddition.

## reddle
reddle, tr. v. and n. — A var. of ruddle.

## rede
rede, tr. v., to advise. — ME. reden, 'to advise,
guess, read'. See read.

## rede
rede, п., counsel, advice (archaic or dial) — ME.

'to advise, consent'; rel. to OS. rdd, 'advice,

raad, Swed. rod, 'advice, counsel, remedy',
OFris. red, MDu. raet, Du. raad, 'advice,
counsel', OHG., MHG. rat, 'advice, counsel, aid,
stores', G. Rat, 'advice, counsel'. See read and
cp. the first element in Ralph and the second
element in Conrad,

## redeem
redeem, tr. v. — ME. redemen, fr. MF. (= F.)

Derivatives: redeem-able, adj., redeem-abil-ity,
п., redeem-able-ness, п., redeem-abl-y, adv.

## redeemer
redeemer, n. — ME. redemer, fr. redemen. See

## redeless
redeless, adj., without counsel (obsol.) — OE.

## redemption

## redemptive
redemptive, adj., redeeming. — Formed with suff.

redemptor, n.( redeemer. — ME. redemptour, fr.
Eccles. L. redemptor, 'redeemer', fr. L.

Redemptorist, п., a member of the order founded

## redif
redif, п., soldier in the reserve of the army of the

rel. to Heb. rdddph, Aram.-Syr. redaph, 'he

## followed

## redingote
redingote, п., a long double-breasted outer coat.
— F., corruption of E. riding coat.

## redintegrate
redintegrate, tr. v. — L. redintegrdtus, pp. of

red- and integrare, 'to make whole', fr. integer,

## redintegration
redintegration, n. — L. redintegrdtio, gen. -onis,

## redirect
redirect, tr. v., to direct again, readdress. —

redolence, n. — Formed from next word with suff.

## redondilla
redondilla, п., a kind of rhymed stanza. — Sp.,

re-double, tr. and intr. v., to double again. —

## redoubt
redoubt, п., 1) an enclosed outwork; 2) a

## redoubt
redoubt, tr. v., to dread. — ME. redouten, fr. OF.
(— F.) redouter, 'to fear', fr. re- (see re-), and

The spelling with t (occurring also in MF.) is
due to the influence of L. dubitdre.

(= F.) redonder, 'to overflow, abound', fr. L.

Derivative: redound, n.

## redowa
redowa, п., name of a dance. — G. Redowa, fr. F.

ON. reidi, 'equipment of a ship'. These words
orig. denoted 'a place where ships were made

See ready and cp. road. Czech rejdovati was
influenced in meaning by a confusion with Czech
re}, fr. G. Reihen, Reigen, 'dance*.

## redress
redress, tr. v., to compensate; to adjust. — ME.

(see re-) and drecier, 'to make straight'. See

Derivatives: redress-al, n.,redress-er, п., redress-
ive, adj., redress-or, n.

## redress
redress, п., compensation, adjustment. — ME.

## re-dress

## red-short
red-short, adj., brittle when red-hot. —
Englishing of Swed. rodskort, neut. of rodskor, lit. 'red

shear. Swed. rodskort became in English red-
short, owing to a confusion of Swed. skort with

coldshort.
Derivative: red-short-ness, n.

## redsturt

tail', compounded of red and ME. stert, 'tail'.
See start, 'tail', and cp. stark-naked.

reductio ad absurdum. — L., 'reduction to the

гее, п., the female of the ruff. — A var. of 1st

## reed
reed, n. — ME. reod, rede, fr. OE. hreod, rel. to
OS. kriod, OFris. /triad, MLG. ret. MDu. ried,
Du. riet, OHG. knot, riot, MHG., G. riet, fr.
Teut. *hreuda- and *hreupa-, corresponding to
Ϊ.-Ε. *qreuto-, fr. base *qreut-, 'to move quickly,
shake, swing'. Accordingly reed orig. meant
'the quickly moving plant'. MHG. rutten
(whence MHG., G. ruttein), 'to shake', and the
first element in OE. hreade-mus, *bat\ are rel.
to the above words. Cognates outside Teut. are
Toch. Ахи, 'reed, cane', and Lith. kruteti, 'to
move, stir' (intr.)
Derivatives: reed, tr. v., reed-y, adj., reed-i-ness,
п., reed-less, adj.

reedbuck, n. — Loan translation of Du. rietbok.

reeve, п., the female of the ruff. — Also called

referendary, п., ]) a referee {rare); 2) a.higher

refine, tr. and intr. v. — Formed fr. re- and fine,

flex-ibil-ity,n.,reflex-ive, adj. and п., reflex-ive-

## refiex
refiex, n. — Fr. L. refiexus, gen. -us, 'a bending

## refraindre

L. regulus, 'a little king', dimin. of rex, gen.

in ML. for its readiness to combine with gold,
the royal metal.

## Regnlus
Regnlus, п., a first magnitude starin the
constellation Leo (astron.) — Not fr. L. regulus, 'a little
king' (see prec. word), but a corruption of the
Arabic name of this star, rijl (al-asad), 'paw (of
the lion)'. Arab, rijl, 'foot, paw', is rei. to Heb.
reghel, Aram, raghla, Syr. reghld, Μ and. lighrd
(metath.), 'foot'. Cp. Rigel.

## regurgitant
regurgitant, adj., flowing back. — ML. regurgi-
tdns, gen. -antis, pres. part, of regurgitdre. See
next word and -ant.

## regurgitate
regurgitate, tr. v., to surge back; intr. v.. to cause
to surge back. — ML. regurgitatus, pp. of
regurgitdre, 'to engulf, fr. re- and L. gurgitdre, 'to
engulf. See gurgitation.

## regurgitation
regurgitation, п., a pouring back; the backward
flow of blood to the heart (med.) — ML. regur-
gitdtio, fr. regurgitatus, pp. of regurgitdre. See
prec. word and -ion.

## rehabilitate
rehabilitate, tr. v., to restore to good condition.
— ML. rehabilitatus, pp. of rehabilitdre, fr. re-
and habilitare, 'to make fit'. See habilitate.
Derivative: rehabilitat-ion, n.

## rehash
rehash, tr. v., to hash again; to work over (old

## rehearse
rehearse, n. — ME. rehercen, rehersen, fr. OF.

fr. hercer (F. herser), to harrow', fr. herce (F.

Derivatives: rehears-al, п., rehears-er, n.

## rei
rei, п., real (coin). — Erroneous E. form of Port.
real (see real, name of a. coin), fr. back
formation of the Port. pi..reis (as if standing for rei-s).
Cp. reis, milreis.

## Reich
Reich, п., formerly, name of the German
Empire; since 1919, the German Republic. — G.,
lit. 'empire, kingdom', fr. MHG. riche, fr.
OHG. rihhi, which is rel. to OE. rice, ON. rtki,
Swed. rike, Dan. rige, OFris., MLG., MDu.
rike, Du. rijk, Goth, reiki. These words derive
fr. Teut. *rikja-, 'rule', which is borrowed fr.
Celtic *rigiom, 'kingdom, rule', fr. *ri£-, 'king'.

See rich and cp. next word and rix-dollar.

## Reichstag
Reichstag, п., the legislative assembly of the
former German empire. — G., lit. 'diet of the
empire', fr. Reich and Tag, 'day'. See prec.

'parliamentary assembly'. Cp. Rigsdag, Riksdag,
landtag,

## rein

## reina

first element is prob. cogn. with Gk. κριός,

deer. Cp. Dan. rensdyr, Swed. rendjur, Du.
rendier, G. Renntier, which all are borrowed fr.

reins, n. p]. — ME., fr. OF. (= F.) reins, fr. L.

remark, tr. and intr. v. — F. remarquer, fr. MF.
remarquer, a hybrid coined fr. re- (see re-) and
marquer, 'to mark', a word of Teut. origin. See
mark, 'sign'.

## remark
remark, n. — F. remarque, back formation fr.
remarquer, fr. MF. See remark, v.

## remarkable
remarkable, adj. — F. remarquable, fr. remarquer.
See remark, v., and -able.
Derivatives: remarkabil-ity, п., remarkabie-ness,
п., remarkabl-y, adv.

## remarque
remarque, п., a miniature sketch on the margin.
— F. See remark, n.

## remblai
remblai, п., filling material, excavation,
embankment. — F., back formation fr. remblayer, 'to
fill up, embank', fr. re- and -em (see re- and
em-) and bli, 'corn', fr. Frankish *blad. €p. ОЕ.
blxd, 'shoot, flower; harvest, crops', blsed,
'leaf, and see blade.

## Rembrandtesque
Rembrandtesque, adj., resembling the style of the
Dutch painter Rembrandt van Rijn (1606-69).
— Formed fr. the name of Rembrandt with suff.
-esque.

## remediable
remediable, adj., capable of being remedied. —
ME., fr. MF. (= F.) remediable, fr. L. remedia-
bilis, 'that which may be healed, curable*, fr. re-
mediare, remediari, 'to heal, cure', fr. remedium.
See remedy, п., and -able.
Derivatives: remediable-nesst п., remediabl-y,
adv.

## remedial
remedial, adj., serving as a remedy. — L. reme-
didlis, 'healing, remedial', fr. remedium. See
remedy, п., and adj. suff. -al.

## remedy
remedy, n. — ME. remedie, fr. AF. remedie (F-
remede), fr. L. remedium, 'relief, remedy', lit. 'a
healing again', fr. re- (see re-) and mederi, 'to
heal'. See medical and cp. next word.
Derivatives: remedi-less, adj., remedi-less-ly,
adv., remedi-less-ness, n.

## remedy
remedy, tr. v. — ME. remedien, fr. MF. (= F.)
remedier, fr. L. remedidre, remedidri, 'to remedy',
fr. remedium. See remedy, n.

## remember
remember, tr. and intr. v. — ME. remembren, fr.
OF. remembrer, fr. Late L. rememorari, 'to call
to mind again, remember again', fr. re- and L.
memordri, Чо remember, be mindful', fr. memor,
'mindful*. See memory.
Derivatives: remember-able, adj., remember-
abil-ity, п., remember-able-ness, n.,remember-er,
п., remembrance (q.v.)

## remembrance
remembrance, n. — ME., fr. MF., fr. remembrer.
See prec. word and -ance.
Derivative: remembranc-er, n.

## remex
remex, n. pi., remiges, any of the quill feathers of
the wing of a bird (ornithol.) — ML. remex (resp.
remiges), fr. L., 'rower, oarsman', compounded

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:655 COLUMN:2 -->
of remus, 'oar', and -ex, gen. -igis, fr. -igere, used
in compounds for agere, 'to lead'. L. remus
stands for *re-smos and is cogn. with OI. aritrafy,
'oar', Gk. έρέσσείν, Чо row', έρέτης, 'rower',
OE. гбдог, 'rudder', fr. I.-E. base *ere, 'to row;
oar', whence also ON. roa, OE. rowan, 'to row*.
See row, 'to propel a boat', and cp. rudder. Cp.
also bireme and words there referred to. For the
second element see agent, adj.

## remind
remind, tr. v. — Formed fr. re- and mind.
Derivatives: remind-al, п., remind-er, п.,
remindful, adj.

## reminisce
reminisce, intr. v. — Back formation fr. remi-,
niscent. Cp. luminesce.

## reminiscence
reminiscence, n. — F. reminiscence, fr. Late L. re·
miniscentia, 'recollection', fr. reminiscens, gen.
-entis; see next word and -ce. Late L. remini-
scentia is prop, a loan translation of Gk. άνά-
μνησις, 'a calling to mind, reminiscence*, fr.
άναμιμνήσκειν, 'to remind of, recall to memory*.

## reminiscent
reminiscent, adj. — L- reminiscens, gen. -entis, pp.
of reminisci, 'to recall to mind, remember', fr.
re- and miniscf, 'to remember', which is rel. to
mens, 'mind', memini, meminisse, 'to remember',
and cogn. with Gk. μιμνήσκειν, 'to remember',
fr. I.-E. base *men-, 'to think'. See mind and cp.
words there referred to. For the ending see suff.
-ent.
Derivatives: reminiscent, п., reminiscent-ialt
adj., reminiscent-ial-ly, adv.

## remise
remise, п., a surrender. — ME., fr. MF. ( = F.),
prop. fem. pp. of remettre, 'to put back', used
as a noun, fr. L. remittere. See remit.
Derivative: remise, tr. v.

## remise
remise, п., a second thrust {fencing). — F., of the
same origin as prec. word.

## remiss
remiss, adj., lax, negligent. — L. remissus, pp. of
remittere. See remit.
Derivatives: remiss-ly, adv., remiss-ness, n.

## remissible
remissible, adj., forgivable. — MF. (= F.)
remissible, fr. Late L. remissibilis, fr. L. remissus, pp.
of remittere. See remit and -ible.
Derivatives: remissibil-ity, п., remissible-ness, n.

## remission
remission, n. — ME., fr. OF. remission (F.
remission), fr. L. remissidnem, ace. of remissid, *a
sending back, remission', fr. remissus, pp. of
remittere. See remit and -ion.

## remissive
remissive, adj., causing remission. — ML. re-
missivus, fr. L. remissus, pp. of remittere. See
next word and -ive.

## remit
remit, tr. and intr. v. — ME. remytten, fr. L.
remittere, 'to send back; ίο relax, slacken; to
remit, forgive*, fr. re- and mittere, 'to send'. See
mission.
Derivatives: remitt-al, п., remitt-ance, п., remitt-
anc-er, п., remitt-ee, п., remittent (q.v.),
remitter, п., remitt-or, n.

## remittent
remittent, adj. and n. — L. remittens, gen. -entis,
pres. part, of remittere. See prec. word and -ent.
Derivative: remittent-ly, adv.

## remnant
remnant, n. and adj. — ME., contraction of ME.
remenant, fr. OF. remanant, remenant, prop,
pres. part, of remanoir, remaindre^ 'to remain .
See remain and -ant.

## remodel
remodel, tr. v., to model afresh. — Formed fr. re-
and model, v.

## remonetize
remonetize, tr. v., to restore as lawful currency.
— Formed fr. re- and monetize.
Derivative: remonetiz-ation, n.

## remonstrance
remonstrance, n. — MF. remonstrance (F. remon-
irance)^ fr. ML. remonstrantia, fr. remdnstrans,
gen. -amis. See next word and -ce.

## remonstrant
remonstrant, adj. and n. — ML. remdnstrans,
gen. -amis, fr. remonstrare. See next word and
-ant.

## remonstrate
remonstrate, intr. v. — ML. remdnstratus, pp. of
remonstrare, fr. re- and L. mdnstrare, 'to show'.
See monster and verbal suff. -ate.
Derivatives: remonstrat-ing, adj., remonstrat-
ing-ly, adv., remonstrat-ion, п., remonstrat-ive,
adj., remonstrat-or, n.

## remontant
remontant, adj., blooming a second time in a
season. — F., pres. part, of remonter, 'to go up
again'. See remount and -ant.
Derivative: remontant, n.

## remora
remora, п., any fish pertaining to the genera
Echeneis, Remora (ichthyol.) — L. remora,
'delay, hindrance', fr. re- and mora, 'delay'; see

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:655 COLUMN:3 -->
moratory. The fish was believed to stop boats,
whence its name.

## remorse
remorse, n. — ME. remors, remorse, fr. MF. re-
mors (F. remords), fr. VL. remorsus, pp. of re-
mordere, 'to bite again, vex, torment', fr. re- and
mordire, 'to bite'. See mordant and cp. morsel.
Derivatives: remorse-ful, adj., remorse-ful-ly,
adv., remorse-less, adj., remorse-less-ly, adv.,
remorse-less-ness, n.

## remote
remote, adj. — L. remotus, 'afar off, remote', pp.
of removere. See remove.
Derivatives: remote-ly, adv., remote-ness, n.

## remotion
remotion, п., removal. — ME. remocion, fr. L.
remotio, gen. -onis, fr. remotus, pp. of removere.
See prec. word and cp. motion,

## remount
remount, tr. and intr. v., to mount again. — ME.
remounten, fr. OF. (= F.) remonter, fr. re- (see
re-) and monter, 'to go up'. See mount, 'to go
up', and cp. remontant.
Derivative: remount, n.

## remove
remove, tr. and intr. v. — ME. removen, fr. OF.
removoir, remouvoir, fr. L. removere, 'to move
back, draw back, remove', fr. re- and movere.
See move' and cp, remote, remotion.
Derivatives: remove, п., remov-able, adj.,
removability, п., remov-ai, п., remov-ed, adj., remov-
ed-ly, adv., remov-ed-ness, п., remov-er, n.

## remuda
remuda, п., relay of horses. — Sp., shortened
from remuda de caballos, lit. 'exchange of horses',
fr. remudar, 'to exchange', fr. re-, 'again', fr. L.
re- (see re-) and mudar, 'to change*, fr. L.
mature, 'to change'. See mutnble.

## remimerable
remimerable, adj. — See next word and -able,

## remunerate
remunerate, tr. v., to pay for work or service; to
recompense. — L. remuneratus, pp. of remune-
rdri (later remunerdre), 'to repay, reward,
recompense', fr. re- and тйпегйге (also munerdri),
'to give, present', fr. munus, gen. muneris, 'gift,
present, reward'. See municipal and cp. words
there referred to. For the ending see verbal suff.
-ate.
Derivatives: remuneration (q.v.), remunerat-ive,
adj., remunerat-ive-ly, adv., remunerat-ive-ness,
п., remunerat-or, n.

## remuneration
remuneration, n. — L. remunerdtio, gen. -o/iis, 'a
repaying, recompense', fr. remuneratus, pp. of
remunerari. See prec. word and -ion.

## renaissance
renaissance, п., revival of learning, literature and
art. — F., 'rebirth*, fr. MF., fr. renaissant, pres.
part, of renaitre, 'to be born again', fr. OF. re-
nestre, fr. VL. *renascere, corresponding to L.
renasci, 'to be born again'. See renascence,

## renal
renal, adj., pertaining to the kidneys. — F. renal,
fr. Late L. rendlis, fr. L. ren, 'kidney', pi. renes.
See reins and adj. suff. -al and cp. adrenal,

## renascence
renascence, п., rebirth. — Formed from next
word with suff. -ce. Cp. renaissance, which is a
doublet of renascence.

## renascent
renascent, adj., being born again. — L. renascens,
gen. -entis, pres. part, of renasci, 'to be born
again', fr. re- and nasci, 'to be born'. See nascent,

## rencontre
rencontre, п., a rencounter. — MF. (= F.), fr.
rencontrer, 'to meet', fr. re- (see re-) and encon-
trer, 'to meet', fr. OF. See encounter and cp.
next word.

## rencounter
rencounter, n. — Anglicized fr. rencontre (q.v.)

## rencounter
rencounter, tr. and intr. v. — MF. (= F.)
rencontrer, 'to meet'. See rencontre,

## rend
rend, tr. and intr. v. — ME. renden, fr. OE. ren-
dan, 'to tear, cut', rel. to OFris. renda, randa, 'to
cut, break', MLG. rende, 'anything broken',
prob. also to OE. rind(e), 'bark, rind, crust'; see
rind. Outside Teut. cp. OI. randhram, 'an
opening, slit, fissure'. Cp. also rent, 'a hole'.
Derivative: rend-er, п., one who rends.

## render
render, tr. and intr. v. — ME. rendren, fr. MF.
(= F.) rendre, fr. VL. *rendere, which was
formed fr. L. reddere, 'to give back, restore; to give
up; to translate', on analogy of the antonym
prendere, Чо take'. L. reddere is formed fr. red-
and -dere, weakened form of dare, 'to give'. See
date, 'point of time', and cp. reddition,
rendezvous, rendition, rent, 'payment', surrender.
Derivatives: render, п., render-ing, n.

## rendezvous
rendezvous, п., meeting. — F. rendez-vous, prop.
'render, betake yourselves', imper. pi. of se
rendre, 'to render oneself. See render.
Derivative: rendezvous, intr. v.

## rendition
rendition, п., a rendering. — Obsol. F., fr. VL.
*renditionem, for L. redditioпет, ace. of redditio,
'a giving back'. See reddition and cp. render.

## renegade
renegade, п., an apostate. — Sp. renegado (with
substitution of suff. -ade for Sp· -ado), fr. ML.
renegdtus, prop. pp. of renegdre, 'to deny', fr.
re- and L. negare, *to deny*. See negation and
cp. next word.
Derivative: renegade, adj. and intr. v.

## renege
renege, intr. and tr. v., to deny, renounce. — ML.
renegdre. See prec. word.
Derivatives: renege, п., reneg-er, n.

## renew
renew, tr. and intr. v. — ME. renewen, formed
fr. re- and newe, 'new' (see new), on analogy of
L. renovdre. See renovate.
Derivatives: renew-able, adj., renew-abil-ity, п.,
renew-al, n.

## reni-
reni-, combining form denoting the kidney. — L.
reni-, fr. rin, pi. rinis, 'kidney*. See reins.

## reniform
reniform, adj., kidney-shaped. — Formed fr.
reni- and L. forma, 'form, shape'. See form, n.

## renitence
renitence, reultency, n. — F. renitence, fr. renitent,
fr. L. remtentem, ace. of renttins. See next word
and -ce, resp. -cy.

## renitent
renitent, adj., resistant, recalcitrant. — L. reni-
tens, gen. -entis, pres. part, of renitor, reniti, 'to
strive against, withstand', fr. re- and tutor, niti,
'to strive, make an effort, exert oneself. See
nisus and -ent.

## rennet
rennet, п., inner membrane of a calf's stomach
used for curdling milk. — Late ME., lit. 'that
which causes (milk) to run', related to ME.
rennen, 'to cause to run', fr. OE. rinnan, 'to run*.
Cp. OE. gerinnan, 'to run together, coagulate',
G. rinnen, 'to run', gerinnen, *to curdle', geron-
nene Milch, Du. geronnen melk, 'curdled milk*.
See run.

## rennet
rennet, п., a variety of apple. — F. reinette, lit.
'little queen', dimin. of reine, 'queen', fr. L. re-
gina; see regina and -ette. For sense
development cp. Sp. manzana de reina, lit. 'queen's
apple'. The F. var. rainette is due to a confusion
of this word with rainette, 'tree frog' (dimin. of
L. rdna, 'frog'), whose spotted skin resembles
that of the rennet (cp. rainette green).

## rennin
rennin, п., name of a ferment that causes
coagulation ibiochem.) — Coined from the
abbreviation of rennet, 'inner membrane of a calf's
stomach', and suff. -in.

## reno-
reno-, combining form meaning ]) the kidney;
2) renal and (med.) — Fr. L. renes, 'kidney'. See
renal.

## renounce
renounce, tr. and intr. v. — ME. renouncen, fr.
MF. (= F.) renoncer, fr. L. renuntiare, 'to carry
back word, report; to retract, renounce',
formed fr. re- and nuntidre, 'to relate, report', fr.
nuntius, 'messenger1. See nuncio and cp. renun-
cintion.
Derivatives: renounce, п., renounce-able, adj.,
renounc-er, n.

## renouncement
renouncement, n. — MF. (= F.) renoncement, fr.
renoncer. See prec. word and -ment.

## renovate
renovate, tr. v., to renew; intr. v., to become
renewed. — L. renovdtus, pp. -of renovdre, 'to
renew', fr. re- and novdre, 'to make new', fr. novus,
'new'. See new and verbal suff. -ate and cp.
novel, adj. and n. Cp. also renew.

## renovation
renovation, n. — ME. renovation, fr. L. renovdtid,
'act of renewing, renewal' [possibly through
the medium of MF. (= F.) renovation], fr. re-
novdtus, pp. of renovdre. See prec. word and -ion,

## renovator
renovator, n. — L. renovator, fr. renovdtus, pp. of
renovdre. See renovate and agential suff. -or.

## renown
renown, n. — ME. renoun;ix. AF. renoun, fr. OF.
renon, later renom, fr. renomer, 'to make
famous', fr. re- (see re-) and nomer, fr. L. nomindre,
'to name'. See noun.
Derivative: renown-ed, adj.

## rent
rent, adj., torn. — Pp. of rend.

## rent
rent, п., an opening, a hole, a cleft. — Fr. prec.
word.

## rent
rent, п., payment made by a tenant to the owner
or landlord. — ME. rente, fr. OF. rente, prop.
fem. pp. used as a noun, fr. VL. *rendita,
corresponding to L. reddita, 'that which is
rendered', fem. pp. of *rendere, resp. reddere, 'to give
back'. See reddition and cp. render, rendition.
Derivatives: rent-al, rent-less, adjs.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:656 COLUMN:2 -->

## rent
rent, tr. v., to pay rent for; intr. v., to be for rent.
— ME. renten, rente. See rent, 'payment'.
Derivatives: rent-able, rent-ed, adjs., rent-ee, n.

## rental
rental, п., sum paid as rent; rent roll. — ME., fr.
ML. rentdle, formed with L. suff. -die, neut. of
-dlis (see -al), fr. ME. rente. See rent, 'payment'.

## rente
rente, п., rent, income. — F., fr. VL. *rendita.
See rent, 'payment'.

## rentier
rentier, п., a holder of rentes. — F., fr. rente. See
rente.

## renunciation
renunciation, n. — ME., fr. L. renuntidtid, gen.
-onis, fr. renuntidtus, pp. of renuntiare. See
renounce and -ation.

## renunciative
renunciative, adj. — Formed with. suff. -ive fr. L.
renuntiatus, pp. οι renuntiare. See renounce.

## renunciatory
renunciatory, adj. — Formed with adj. suff. -ory
fr. renuntiatus, pp. of renuntiare. See renounce.

## Reo
Reo, п., a trade name in the automobile industry.

## reopen
reopen, tr. and intr. v., to open again. — Formed
fr. re- and open, v.

## reorganize
reorganize, tr. v., to organize again. — Formed
fr. re- and organize. Cp. F. reorganises
Derivative: reorganiz-ation, n. Cp. F.
reorganisation.

## rep
rep, also repp, reps, п., a thick ribbed fabric of
silk. — F. reps, prob. fr. E. ribs, pi. of rib. Cp.
Du. rips, G. Rips, which are English loan words.

## rep
rep, п., dissolute. — Abbreviation of reprobate.

## rep
rep, п., repetition [schoolboy's slang). —
Abbreviation of repetition.

## repair
repair, tr. v., to mend. — ME. repairen, reparen,
fr. OF. (= F.) reparer, fr. L. repardre, 'to get
again, recover, repair, repair renew', fr. re- and
pardre, 'to get, prepare, make ready'; see pare
and cp. reparation.
Derivatives: repair, п., repair-able, adj.,
repairer, n.

## repair
repair, intr. v., to resort. — ME. repairen, fr.
MF. repairier, repairer, 'to return to one's
country', fr. OF. repairier, of s.m., fr. Late L.
repatridre, of s.m., fr.re- and h.patria, 'country,
homeland'. See patriot and cp. repatriate.

## repair
repair, п., resort. — ME. repaire, repair, fr. MF.
repaire, 'return to one's country', fr. OF. repaire,
of s.m., fr. OF. repairier. See prec. word.

## repand
repand, adj., wavy (bot., said of leaves); the
opposite of serrate. — L. repandus, 'bent
backward, turned up', fr. panddre, 'to bend, curve',
which is rel. to pandere, 'to spread out'. See
fathom and cp. pandiculation.

## reparable
reparable, adj. — F. reparable, fr. L. repardbilis,
'capable of being repaired'. See repair, 'to mend',
and -able.
Derivative: reparabl-y, adv.

## reparation
reparation, n. — ME. reparacioun, fr. MF. (= F.)
reparation, fr. L. repardtidnem, ace. of repa-
rdtid, 'repair, restoration', fr. repardtus, pp. of
repardre. See repair, *to mend*, and -ntion.

## reparative
reparative, adj. — Late L. repardtlvus, fr. L.
repardtus, pp. of repardre. See prec. word and -ive.

## repartee
repartee, п., a witty reply. — F. repartie,
'repartee', prop. fem. pp. of repartir, 'to start again;
to reply', fr. OF., fr. re- (see re-) and partir, 'to
part; to depart, start'. See part, 'to divide', and
cp. depart.

## repartition
repartition, n. — Formed fr. re- and partition.

## repast
repast, n. — ME., fr. MF. repast (F. repas), prop.
pp. of repaistre (F. repattre), 'to feed*, fr Late L.
repdstus, pp. of repdscere, 'to feed again', fr. re-
and L. pascere, 'to feed*. See pastor.

## repatriate
repatriate, tr. and intr. v. — Late L. repatridtus,
pp. of repatridre, 'to return to one's country*.
See repair, 'to resort'.

## repatriation
repatriation, n. — ML. repatridtio, gen. -onis, 'the
act of returning to one's own country', fr. Late
L. repatridtus, pp. of repatridre. See prec. word
and -ion.

## repay
repay, tr. and intr. v. — OF. repaier (F. repayer),
fr. re- and payer, 'to pay*. See pay.
Derivatives: repay-able, adj., repay-al, п.,
repaying, adj., repay-ment, n.

## repeal
repeal, tr. v., to revoke. — ME. repelen, fr. MF.
rapeler, repeler (F. rappeler), 'to call back,
recall', fr. OF., fr. re- (see re-) and apeler. See
appeal.
Derivatives: repeal, n. (q.v.), repeal-able, adj.,
repeal-abtl-ity, П., repeal-able-ness, п., repeaJ-er,
n.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:656 COLUMN:3 -->

## repeal
repeal, п., revocation. — ME. rapel (F. rappel),
fr. OF., back formation fr. rapeler. See repeal,
v.

## repeat
repeat, tr. and intr. v. — ME. repeten, fr. MF.
(= F.) repeler, fr. L. repetere, 'to go back, seek
again, revisit; to recommence, repeat', fr. re-
andpetere, 'to seek; to ask'. See petition.
Derivatives: repeat, п., repeat-able, adj.,
repeatability, п., repeat-ed, adj., repeat-ed-ly, adv.,
repeat-er, n.

## repel
repel, tr. v., to drive back. — ME. repellen, fr. L.
repellere, 'to drive back, repulse', fr. re- (see re-)
and pellere, 'to drive'. See pulse,'throb', and cp.
appeal, repeal. Cp. also repulse, v.

## repelleut
repelleut, adj. — L. repellins, -entis, pres. part, of
repellere. See prec. word and -ent.
Derivatives: repellent, п., repellent-ly, adv.

## repent
repent, intr. v., to feel penitence; tr. v., to be sorry
for. — ME. repenten, fr. OF. (= F.) (se) repentir,
fr. (se) pentir, fr. VL. *penitire, corresponding to
L. paenitere, 'to cause to repent'. See penitent.

## repent
repent, adj., creeping, trailing (said of plants). —
L. ripens, gen. -entis, pres. part, of ripere, 'to
creep, crawl'. See reptile and -ent and cp. rep-
tant.

## repentance
repentance, n. — ME. repentaunce, fr. MF.
repentance, fr. OF., fr. repentant, pres. part, of

## repercussion

## repertory

pertus, pp. of reperire, 'to procure, find again,

Derivatives: repetitious-ly, adv., repetitious-ness,
n.

## repetitive
repetitive, adj. — Formed with suff. -ive fr. L.
repetltus, pp. of repetere. See repeat.
Derivatives: repetitive-ly, adv., repetitive-ness,
n.

## repine

Derivatives: repin-er, п., repin-ing-ly, adv.

See full, adj., and verbal suff. -ish and cp.
plenum, deplenish.

Cp. F. ripliquer, 'to reply', which has been

## report

report, n. — ME., fr. MF. (= F.) report, fr. OF.

reprehend, tr. v., 1) to reprove; 2) to blame. —

reprove.
Derivatives: reprieve, п., repriev-er, n.

## reprimand

mendus, gerundive of reprimere, 'to press back'.
See repress. The spelling reprimande is due to
the influence of the verb mander, 'to summon*.
For other Latin gerundives or their derivatives
used in English cp. agenda and words there
referred to.

## reprimand

mander, fr. reprimande. See reprimand, n.
Derivatives: reprimand-er, п., reprimand-ing,
adj., reprimand-ing-ly, adv.

and print, v.
Derivatives: reprint, п., reprint-er, n.

## reprisal

take back', fr. ri~ (fr. L. re-) and prendere, 'to
take' (fr. L. prehendere, prendere). See re-,
prehensile and subst. suff. -al and cp. reprehend,
reprise.

## reprise

ME., fr. MF. (= F.), 'a taking back', fr. OF.,
prop. fern, of repris, pp. fr. reprendre, *to take
back', fr. L. reprehendere, reprendere. See
reprehend and cp. prec. word.

y, adv.

Derivatives: reprov-er, п., reprov-ing-ly, adv.

reps, n. — A var. of 1st rep.

## reptile

Hplioti, 'to creep', Lett. rapt, of s.m. L. repere

## reptilivorous
reptilivorous, adj. — Lit. 'eating reptiles'. See

## republic

publico, respublica, 'state, commonwealth', lit.
'a public thing', fr. res, 'thing*, and fem. of pu-
blicus, 'public'. See real, adj., and public.
Derivatives·, republic-an, adj. and п.,

republication, n. — Formed fr. re- and

which is formed fr. re- and the stem of pudere^
'to feel shame'. See pudency ^and verbal suff.
-ate.

Opposition, resistance', fr. repugnans, gen. -amis.

## require
require, tr. and intr. v. — ME. requeren, requiren,

*re-quaerere, remodeled after L. quaerere, 'to

## requisite

quisite-ness, n.

requisitory, adj., containing, or conveying, a
requisition. — ME. requisitorie, fr. ML. requisi-

torius, fr. L- requisitus, pp. of requirere. See

Derivatives: requit-able, adj., requit-al, п., re-

## reredos
reredos, п., screen at the back of an altar. —
Aphetic for AF. areredos, which is compounded
of OF. arere (F. arriere), 'at the back', and dos,
'back'. The first element derives fr. VL. *ad
retro, for L. retro, 'backward'; see arrear. The
second element comes fr. VL. dossum, fr. L.
dorsum. See dorsal,

## reremouse

OE. hriremus, appar. fr. hreran, 'to move, stir,
shake', and mus, 'mouse' (see rare, 'undone',
and mouse); so called from the flapping of the
wings.

## res
res, п., thing, matter, cause, esp. used in legal
phrases. — L. res, whence Late L. redlis,
'pertaining to a thing'. See real, adj., and cp. words
there referred to.

## rescind
rescind, tr. v., to annul. — L. rescindere, 'to cut
off, tear oif, abolish', fr. re- and scindere, 'to
cut, split'. See shed, v., and cp. scissile, abscind,
absciss.
Derivatives: rescind-er, п., rescind-ible, adj.

## rescission
rescission, п., annulment. — Late L. rescissio,
gen. -onis, fr. L. rescissus, pp. of rescindere. See
prec. word and -ion. Cp. recision.

## rescissory
rescissory, adj., rescinding. — Late L. rescisso-
rius, fr. L. rescissus, pp. of rescindere. See
rescind and adj. suff. -ory,

## rescript
rescript, n. — L. rescriptum, 'written reply of the
Emperor', prop. neut. pp. of rescribere, 'to
write back in reply', used as a noun, fr. re- and
scribere, 'to write'. See scribe and cp. script.
Derivatives: rescript-ive, adj., rescript-ive-ly,adv.

## rescription
rescription, n. —LateL. resetiptio(peih. through '
the medium of MF. (= F.) rescription), fr. L.
rescriptus, pp. of rescribere. See prec. word and
-ion.

## rescue
rescue, tr. v. — ME. rescouen, rescowen, fr. MF.
rescourre, fr. OF., fr. ML. rescutere,
contraction of L. re- (see re-) and excutere, 'to shake
off, drive away', fr. ex and quatere, 'to shake'.
Cp. It. riscuotere, which is of the same origin
and meaning as OF. rescourre. See quash, 'to
annul', and cp. words there referred to.
Derivatives: rescue, n. (q.v.), rescu-able, adj.,
rescu-er, n.

## rescue
rescue, n. — ME. rescoue, rescowe, fr. rescouen,
rescowen. See rescue, v.

## research
research, n. — MF. recerche (whence, with
assimilation, F. recherche), back formation fr.

## research
research, intr. v. — MF. recercher (F. recker-
cher), fr. re- (see re-) and cercker. See search and
cp. prec. word. Cp. also recherche.
Derivatives: research-er, п., research-ful, adj.

## reseau
reseau, п., a network. — F. riseau, var. of archaic
reseuil, fr. L. ritiolus, 'a little net', dimin. of
reus, a collateral form of rite, 'net'. (F. rets, 'net',
prob. derives fr. L. rites, pi. of ritis, 'net'. The
t in rets is due to 'etymological spelling'.) Cp.
Sp. redecilla, dimin. of red, 'a net', which
derives fr. L. retis. See retiary.

## resect
resect, tr. v. — L. resectus, pp. of resecare, 'to cut
off', fr. re- and secure, 'to cut'. See section.

## resection
resection, n. — L. resectio, gen. -onis, 'a cutting
oif', fr. resectus, pp. of resecare. See prec. word
and -ion.
Derivative: resection-al, adj.

## Reseda
Reseda, п., 1) a genus of plants (bot.); 2) (not
cap.) the color of the mignonette flower. — L.,
name of a plant, fr. Reseda, first word in the
magic formula Reseda morbus, reseda ('Assuage
diseases, assuage'). The flower was applied to
reduce tumors (see Pliny, Hist. Nat. 27, 131).
On such occasions the above formula was used.
L. reseda is the imper. of reseddre, 'to allay,
assuage, heal', fr. re- and siddret 'to make calm,
to allay', lit. 'to cause to settle down', causative
of sedire, 'to sit'. See sedentary.

## Resedaceae
Resedaceae, n. pi., the mignonette family (bot.)
— ModL., formed fr. Reseda with suff. -aceae.

## resedaceous
resedaceous, adj. — See prec. word and -aceous.

## resemblance
resemblance, n. — Late ME., fr. AF., fr. OF. re-

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:658 COLUMN:3 -->
semblant, pres. part, of resembler. See next word
and -ce.

## resemblant
resemblant, adj. — ME., fr. MF., pres. part of
resembler. See next word and -ant.

## resemble
resemble, tr. v. — ME. resemblen, fr. OF.
resembler (F. ressembler), fr. OF., fr. re- (see re-)
and sembler, 'to seem, be like', fr. L. simuldre,
'to make like, imitate', fr. similis, 'like; similar'.
See similar andep. simulate, assemble, dissemble.
Derivative: resembl-er, n.

## resent
resent, tr. v. — F. ressentir (esp. in the phrase se

resentment, n. — F. ressentiment, fr. ressentir.

## reservation
reservation, n. — ME. reservacioun, fr. MF. ( —

Derivative: reservat ion-is t, n.

## reserve
reserve, tr. v. — ME. reserven, fr. MF. (= F.)
reserver, fr. L. reservdre, 'to keep back, save up,

Derivatives: reserve, n. (q.v.), reserv-ed, adj.,
reserv-ed-ly> adv., reserv-er, n.

## reserve
reserve, n. — F. reserve, fr. MF., back formation

## reservist
reservist, n. — F. riserviste, formed fr. reserve

## reservoir
reservoir, n. — F. reservoir, fr. MF., fr. reserver.

reset, tr. v., to receive stolen goods (Scot. law).

reship, tr. v., to ship again. — Formed fr. re- and

## residence
residence, n. — ME., fr. OF. ( — F.) residence, fr.
Late L. reside/itia, fr. L. residens, gen. -entis.
See resident and -cy.

## residency
residency, n. — Formed from next word with
suff. -cy.

resident, adj. and n. — Late ME., fr. L. residens,

resident-skip, n.
residentiary» adj., residing; resident. — ML. resi-
dentiarius, fr. Late L. residentia. See residence

residue, п., a remainder. — ME., fr. MF. (= F.)

## residuum
residuum, п., a remainder. — L., neut. oiresiduus.

resign, tr. and intr. v. — ME. resignen, fr. MF.
(= F.) resigner, fr. L. resigndre, 'to break the
seal off, annul, cancel, resign', fr. re- and signdre,

resignation, fr. ML. resignationem, ace. of resignation

## resist
resist, tr. and intr. v. — ME. resisten, fr. MF. (=

Derivatives: resist, п., resistance (q.v.), resistant
(q.v.), resist-er, п., resist-ful, adj., resistible
(q.v.), resist-ive, adj., resistless (q.v.)

resolute, adj. — L. resolutus, pp. of resolvere, 'to

able-ness, п., resolv-abil-ity, п., resolv-ed, adj.,

## resorb

## resorbence
resorbence, n. — Formed from next word with

resorbent, adj. — L. resorbens, gen. -entis, pres.

## resorcin
resorcin, п., resorcinol. — See next word.

## resorcinol
resorcinol, also resorcin, п., a colorless crystalline
compound CaH4(OH)2 (chem.) — The word
resorcin was coined by its discoverers, Hein.
Hlasiwetz, Bohemian-Austr. chemist (1825-75),
and Barth in 1864 fr. resin and orcin. The suff.
-ol (see 1st -ol) was added later to the word in
allusion to the phenolic nature.

## resorption

resorptus, pp. of resorbere. See resorb.

pect-er, п., respect-ingt prep., respective (q.v.)

respirator, n. — Formed with agential suff. -or fr.

resplend, intr. v., to shine brightly. — ME. re-

resplendence, resplendency, n. — Late L. resplen-

## res publica
res publica, commonwealth. — L. See republic.

## ressala
ressala, risala, п., a troop of native cavalry in

next word.

word.

## rest
rest, п., support for a lance on medieval armor.
— Aphetic for arrest.

## restate
restate, tr. v., to state again. — Formed fr. re-
and state, v. See state.
Derivative: restate-merit', n.

## restaurant
restaurant, n. — F. — Boulanger opened the
first restaurant in Paris (Rue des Poulies) in
1765 and wrote over the entrance the Latin
words Venite ad me omnes qui stomacho labora-
tis et ego vos restaurabo ('Come to me ye all that
suffer from the stomach and I will restore you')·
The name restaurant was coined in reference to
the word restaurabo in the above Latin sentence.
Formally, F. restaurant is pres. part· of restau-
rer, 'to restore'. See restore and -ant.
restaurateur» п., the keeper of a restaurant. — F.,
formed fr. Late L. restaurdtorem, ace. of restau-
rator, 'restorer', fr. L. restaurdtus, pp. of
restaurare, 'to restore'. See restore and agential suff. -or.

## restiform
restiform, adj., ropelike, cordlike (anat.) — Lit.
'горе-shaped', fr. Medical L. restiformis, a word
coined by H. Ridley fr. L. restis, 'rope, cord',
and forma, 'form, shape*. L. restis stands for
*rezgtis and is cogn. with Lith. rezgis, 'basket,
wickerwork', OI. rajjuh, 'rope, cord', and
possibly also with OE. rise, rysc, 'rush'. See rush,
'aquatic herb'. For the second element see form,
n.

## restitute
restitute, tr. v. — L. restitutus, pp. of restituere,
'to restore', fr. re- and statuere, 'to set up'. See
statute. For the change of Latin a (in statuere)
to / (in re-stituere) see abigeat and cp. words
there referred to.

## restitution
restitution, n. — ME., fr. OF, (= F.), fr. L. resti-
tutionem, ace. of restitutio, 'restoration', fr.
restitutus, pp. of restituere. See prec. word and
-ion.

## restitutory
restitutory, adj., pertaining to restitution. —
Late L. restitutorius, fr. L. restitutus, pp. of
restituere. See restitute and adj. suff. -ory.

## restive
restive, adj., 1) refusing to go forward; hence 2)
stubborn, obstinate. — ME. restif, restife, fr.
OF. restif (fern, restive) (whence F. retij, resp.
retive), fr. VL. *restivus, fr. L. restore, 'to stand
still; to withstand, resist'. See rest, 'to remain',
and -ive.
Derivatives: restive-ly, adv., restive-ness, n.

## restoration
restoration, n. — ME. restauracion, fr. OF. ( =
F.) restauration, fr. Late L. restaur ationem, ace.
of restauratie, fr. L. restaurdtus, pp. of restaura-
re. See restore and -ation.
Derivatives: restoration-er, п., restoration-ism,
п., restoration-ist, n.

## restorative
restorative, adj. — ME. restoratif, fr. earlier
restaurs/, fr. MF. (= F.) restauratij (fern, restaura-
tive), fr. restaurer. See restore and -ive.
Derivatives: restorative-ly, adv., restorative·
ness, n.

## restore
restore, tr. v. — ME. restoren, fr. OF. restorer,

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:660 COLUMN:2 -->
fr. L. restaurare, 'to restore, repair, rebuild*,
formed fr. re- and -staurdre (found only in
compounds), which is prob. cogn. with Gk.
σταυρός, 'pale, stake, pole', ON. staurr, of s.m.,
ON. styri, OE. steor, 'rudder, helm', steoran, *to
steer, guide'. Accordingly the orig. meaning of
restaurare prob. was 'to attach again to a stake,
to fasten again'. See steer, 'to direct', and cp.
store, v. and п., instauration.
Derivatives: restor-able, adj., restor-er, n.

## restrain
restrain, tr. v., 1) to hold back; 2) to limit,
confine. — ME. restreynen, fr. OF. restraindre, res-
treindre (F. r'estreindre), fr. L. restringere, 'to
bind back, tighten', fr. re- and stringere, 'to
draw tight; to draw, bind or press together'. See
stringent and cp. restrict.
Derivatives: restrain-ed, adj., restrain-ed-ly,
adv., restrain-ed-ness, п., restrain-er, п., res-
train-ing-ly, adv.

## re-strain
re-strain, tr. v., to strain again. — Formed fr. re-
and strain.

## restraint
restraint, n. — ME., fr. MF. restrainte, prop,
fern. pp. of restraindre, used as a noun. See
restrain.

## restrict
restrict, v., to limit, confine. — L. restrict us, pp.
of restringere. See restrain.
Derivatives: restrict-ed, adj., restrict-ed-ly, adv.,
restrict-ed-ness, п., restriction (q.v.), restrictive
(Q-v.)

## restriction
restriction, n. — ME. restriccioun, fr. Late L.
restrictionem, ace. of restrictio, fr. L. restrictus,
pp. of restringere. See prec word and -ion.
Derivative: restriction-ist, n.

## restrictive
restrictive, adj. — ME., fr. MF. (= F.) restrictif
(fern, restrictive), fr. L. restrictus, pp. of
restringere. See restrict and -ive.
Derivatives: restrictive-ly, adv., restrictive-
ness, n.

## result
result, intr. v. — ME. resulten, fr. ML. resuliare,
'to result', fr. L. resultdre, 'to leap back, spring
back, rebound', which stands for *re-saltdre
and is freq. of resilire, 'to leap back, spring
back, rebound*. See resile and cp. saltant. For
the change of Latin d (in salire and in its freq.
saltare) to н (in re-sultare) see desultory and cp.
words there referred to.
Derivatives: result, п., resultance (q.v.),
resultant (q.v.), result-ful, adj., result-ing-ly, adv.,
result-less, adj.

## resultance
resultance, resultancy, n. — Formed from next
word with suff. -ce, resp. -cy.
resultant·, adj., effective. — ML. resuftdns, gen.
-amis, pres. part, of resultare. See result and
-ant.
Derivative: resultant, n.

## resume
resume, tr. v., to take up again, begin again; intr.
v., to begin again. — ME. resumen, fr. MF. ( —
F.) resumer, fr. L. resumere, 'to take up again*,
fr. re- and sumere, 'to take up'. See assume and
cp. words there referred to.
Derivative: resum-er, n.

## resume
resume, п., summary. — F., prop. pp. of resumer,
'to resume'. See resume.

## resumption
resumption, п., act of resuming. — ME. resump-
cioun, possibly through the medium of MF. ( =
F.) resumption, fr. L. resumptio, gen. -onis, 'a
taking up again', fr. resumptusy pp. of resumere.
See resume and -ion and cp. sumption and words
there referred to.

## resumptive
resumptive, adj., resuming. — Formed with suff.
-ivefr. L. resumptus, pp. of resumere. See resume.
Derivative: resumpiive-ly, adv.

## resupinate
resupinate, adj., inverted (bot.) — L. resupinatns,
'turned back, bent back', pp. of resuplnare, 'to
turn back, bend back', fr. supinus, 'backward'.
See supine and adj. suff. -ate.

## resupination
resupination, п., inverted position (bot.) —
Formed with suff. -ion fr. L. resupinatus, pp. of
resuplnare. See prec. word.

## resurge
resurge, intr. v., to rise again, revive. — L.
resurgere, 'to rise again', fr. re- and surgere, 'to rise'.
See surge, 'to rise', and cp. resource.

## resurgence
resurgence, п., revival. — Formed from next
word with suff. -ce.

## resurgent
resurgent, adj., revived, renewed. — L. resurgens,
gen. -ends, pres. part, of resurgere. See resurge
and -ent and cp. surgent.

## resurrect
resurrect, ]) tr. v., to raise from the dead; 2) intr.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:660 COLUMN:3 -->
v., to rise from the dead. — Back formation fr.
resurrection. The corsect form is resurge, which,
however, is intransitive only, whereas the verb
resurrect can be used both as transitive and
intransitive verb.
Derivatives: resurrect-or, п., resurrect-ive, adj.

## resurrection
resurrection, n. — ME. resur(r)ectiounf fr. Late
L. resurrectionem, ace. of resurrectio, 'a rising
again from the dead', fr. resurrect(um), pp. stem
of resurgere. See resurge and -ion.
Derivatives: resurrection-al, adj., resurrection-
ary, adj., resurrection-ize, tr. v.

## resurrectionism
resurrectionism, п., body snatching. — Formed
from prec. word with suff. -ism.

## resurrectionist
resurrectionist, п., body snatcher. — Formed fr.
resurrection with suff. -ist.

## resuscitate
resuscitate, ]) tr. v., to restore to life; 2) intr. v.,
to return to life. — L. resuscitatus, pp. of resus-
citdre, 'to rouse again, revive', fr. re- and susci-
tare, 'to raise up', which is a compound of sub-
and citdre, 'to put into quick motion.'. See cite.
Derivatives: resuscitation (q.v.), resuscitat-ive,
adj., resuscitat-or, n.

## resuscitation
resuscitation, п., the act of resuscitating. — Late
L. resuscitdtio, gen. -onis, fr. L. resuscitdtus, pp.
of resuscitdre. See prec. word and -ion.

## ret
ret, also rate, tr. v., to soak; intr. v., to rot. —
ME. reten, 'to soak', fr. MDu (= Du.) roten,
'to ret*, which are rel. to OE. rotian, 'to rot'.
See rot.

## rotable
rotable, п., a shelf behind an altar. — F. retable,
fr. Sp. retablo, fr. ML. retrotabulum, which is
compounded of L. retro, backward, back,
behind', and tabula, 'table'. See retro- and tuble.

## retail
retail, n. — ME., fr. MF. retaille, retail (F. re-
taille), 'a piece cut off', fr. OF. retaille, retail, of
s.m., back formation fr. OF. retaillier (F.
retainer), 'to cut off', fr. re- and taillier (F. tailler),
'to cut'. See tailor and cp. detail.
Derivatives: retail, tr. and intr. v., retail-er, п.,
retail-ment, n.

## retain
retain, tr. v. — ME. reteinen, retainen, fr. MF. ( =
F.) retenir, fr. OF., fr. VL. *re-tenire, for L.
retinere, 'to hold back, retain*, which is formed
fr. re- and tenere, 'to hold, keep'. See tenable,
and cp. retention, retinaculum, retinue, rein. Cp.
also abstuin and words there referred to.
Derivatives: retain-able, adj., retain-er, п., re-
tain-ment, n.

## retainer
retainer, п., the act of a client by which he retains
the services of a lawyer (law). — ME. reteiner,
fr. MF. retenir, fr. OF., 'to retain', infin. used as
a noun; see retain. For the subst. use of
infinitives in law terms cp. attainder and words there
referred to.

## retaliate
retaliate, tr. and intr. v., to return like for like,
repay. — L. retdliatus, pp. of retdliare, 'to
retaliate', fr. re- and talis, 'such'. See talion and
verbal suff. -ate.
Derivatives: retaliat-ion, п., retaliat-ion-ist, п.,
retaliat-ive, adj., retaliat-or, п., retaliat-ory, adj.

## retama
retama, п., genista. — ModL., fr. Sp. retama, fr.
Arab, rdtama , in vulgar pronunciation retama,
'a shrub of the genus Genista', nomen unitatis
(= noun of individuality), fr. ratam, 'the genus
Genista, the broom.plant', which is rel. to Heb.
rdthem, Aram. (Targum) rathma, rithmd,
'broom plant'.

## retard
retard, v. — Either fr. F. retarder or directly fr.
L. retarddre, 'to keep back, hinder, delay', fr.
re- and tardare, 'to make slow, hinder', fr.
tardus, 'slow'. See tardy and cp. ritardando.
Derivatives: retard, n. (q.v.), retard-ation, п.,
retard-ative, adj., retard-at-ory, adj., retard-er,
п., retard-ment, n.

## retard
retard, n. — F., back formation fr. retarder. See
retard, v.

## retch
retch, intr. v., to make an effort to vomit. — ME.
*rechen, fr. OE. hrxcan, 'to clear the throat,
spit', rel. to OE. hrdca, 'expectoration, spittle',
ON. hrdki, 'spittle', OHG. rdhhison, 'to clear
one's throat', and cogn. with Lith. kregeti, 'to
grunt*, krogiu, Ί rattle'.
Derivative: retch, n.

## rete
rete, п., network (anat.) — L. rete, 'net'. See re-
tiary.

## retene
retene,п., a hydrocarbon, C18H18
(chem.)—Formed fr. Gk. ρητ(ΐνη), 'resin' (see resin), with

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:661 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: RETENTION | 634 -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:661 COLUMN:1 -->
suff. -ene.

## retention
retention, n. — ME. retenciount fr. L. retention
gen. -onis, 'a holding back, retention', fr. reien-
tus, pp. of retinere. See retain and -ion.

## retentive
retentive, adj. — ME. retentif, retentive, fr. MF.
retentif(fem. retentive), fr. ML. retentivus, fr. L.
retentus, pp. of retinere, 4to hold back'. See
retain and -ive.
Derivatives: retentive-ly, adv., retentive-ness,
n.

## retiarius
retiarius, п., a gladiator who tried to throw a net
over his adversary (Roman antiq.) — L. retiarius,
lit. 'a net-fighter', fr. rete, 'net'. See next word.

## retiary
retiary, adj., constructing a net (said of spiders).
— L. retiarius, *a net-fighter' (see prec. word),
fr. rete, 'net, bag', which is cogn. with Lith.
retis, 'bast sieve'; possibly rel. to L. rams, 'thin,
loose'· See rare, 'thin', and cp. reticulum Cp.
also reseau. For the ending see adj. suff. -ary.
Derivative: retiary, п., a retiary spider.

## reticence
reticence, n. — F. reticene, fr. L. reticentia,
'silence', fr. reticins, gen. -entis. See next word
and -ce.

## reticent
reticent, adj., inclined to keep silent. — L. reti-
cens, gen. -entis, pres. part, of reticere, 'to be
silent', fr. re- and tacere, 'to be silent'; see tace.
For the change of Latin ά (in tucere) to Ϊ (in
reticere) see abigeat and cp. words there referred
to. For the ending see suff. -ent.
Derivative: reticent-ly, adv.

## reticle
reticle, п., network of fine threads on the object
glass of an optical instrument. — L. reticulum,
'a small net'. See reticulum.

## reticular
reticular, adj., netlike. — ModL. reticularis, fr.
L. reticulum. See reticulum and adj. suff. -ar.

## reticulate
reticulate, adj., having the form of a network. —
L. reticulatus, 'netlike', fr. reticulum, 'a small
net'. See reticulum and adj. suff. -ate.
Derivative: reticulate-ly, adv.

## reticulate
reticulate, tr. v., to divide in a network. — L.
reticulums. See reticulate, adj.
Derivatives: reticulat-ed, adj., reticulat-ion, n.

## reticule
reticule, п., a small bag carried by women. — F.
reticule, fr. L. reticulum, 'a small bag', dimin.
tfrete, 'bag'. See retiary, adj., and -cule.

## reticulose
reticulose, adj., forming a network. — Formed
fr. L. reticulum (see next word) with adj. suff.
-ose.

## reticulum
reticulum, п., ]) network; 2) the second stomach
of a ruminant (so called in allusion to the folds
of the mucous membrane). — L- reticulum, *a
small net'. See reticule.

## retiform
retiform, adj., having the form of a network. —
ModL. retiformis, compounded of L. retis, 'net',
and forma, 'form, shape'. See retiary and form,
n.

## retina
retina, п., the sensitive membrane at the back of
the eyeball {anat.) — Medical L. retina, coined
by the translator Gerard of Cremona (1114?-
1187) fr. L. rite, 'net' (see retiary), as a loan
translation of Hebrew resheth, 'net', used in
Medieval Hebrew to denote the retina. See
Joseph Hyrtl, Das Arabische und Hebraische in
der Anatomie, p. 58, and his Onomatologia
Дпа1от1са, pp. 452-55.
Derivative: retin-al, adj.

## retinaculum
retinaculum, п., a retaining band {anat., bot. and
entomol.) — L. retinaculum, 'a holdfast, band,
tether', prop, 'that which holds back or binds',
fr. retinere. See retain.
Derivatives: retinacul-ar, retinacul-ate, adjs.

## retinitis
retinitis, п., inflammation of the retina (med.) —
A Medical L. hybrid coined fr. Medical L.
retina (fr. L. rete) and Gk. suff. -ΐτις. See retina
and -itis.

## retinue
retinue, n. — ME. retenue,-fr. MF. retenue, prop.
fern. pp. of retenir, 'to retain, hold back', used
as a noun; see retain. For the mode of formation
cp. continue, detinue,

## retire
retire, intr. and tr. v. — MF. ( = F.) retirer, 'to
withdraw (something)', se retirer, 'to withdraw,
retire', fr. re- (see re-) and tirer, 'to pull, draw'.
See tire, 'to pull'.
Derivatives: retire, п., retir-ed, adj., retir-ed-
ness, п., retir-ed-ly, adv., retire-ment, п., retir-er,
п., retir-ing, adj., retir-ing-ly, adv., retir-ing-
ness, n.

## retort
retort, tr. v., to reply sharply to; intr. v., to make

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:661 COLUMN:2 -->
a sharp reply. — L. retortus, pp. of retorquere,
'to twist back, turn back', fr. re- and torquere,
'to twist'. See torque and cp. retort, a vessel of
glass. Cp. also contort, distort, extort.
Derivatives: retort, п., a sharp reply, retort-able,
adj., retort-ed, adj., retort-er, п., retortion (q.y.),
retort-ive, adj.

## retort
retort, п., a vessel of glass used in chemistry. —
MF. (= F.) retorte, fr. ML. retorta, 'a vessel
with a bent neck', prop, 'anything bent*, fr. L.
retorta, fern pp. of L. retorquere. See retort, v.

## retortion
retortion, n. — ML. retortio, gen. -onis, fr. L.
retortus, pp. of retorquere. See retort, v., and -ion.

## retouch
retouch, tr. v., to touch up, modify. — F.
retoucher, fr. MF., fr. re- (see re-) and toucher,
'to touch*. See touch.
Derivatives: retouch-er, п., retouch-ing, n.

## retrace
retrace, tr. v., to go over again. — F. retracer, 'to
trace again, retrace*, fr. MF. retracier, fr. re-
(see re-) and trader, *to trace'. See trace, v.

## retract
retract, tr. and intr. v., to draw back, draw in. —
L. retractus, pp. of retrahere 'to draw back', fr.
re- and trahere, 'to pull, draw'. See re- and
tract, 'region' and cp. retreat. Cp. also attract
and words there referred to.
Derivatives: retract-able, adj., retract-Ue, adj.,
retract-il-ity, п., retraction (q.v.), retract-ive,
adj., retract-or, n.

## retrnct
retrnct, tr. v., to withdraw, recant, revoke. — L.
retractare, 'to handle again, reconsider; to
refuse', freq. of retrahere, 'to draw back, draw
again*. See prec. word.

## retractation
retractation, п., retraction. — L. retractatio, gen.
-onis, fr. retractatus, pp. of retractare. See
retract, 'to withdraw', and -ation.

## retraction
retraction, n. — ME. retraccioun, fr. MF. (= F.)
retraction, fr. L. retractionem, ace. οϊ re tr actio,
'a drawing back, hesitation, refusal', fr.
retractus, pp. of retrahere. See retract, 'to draw back',
and -ion.

## retral
retral, adj., backward. — Formed with adj. suff.
-al fr. L. retro, 'at the back, backward'. See
retro-.

## retread
retread, tr. v., to put a new tread (on the tire of
an automobile, etc.) — Formed fr. re- and
tread, n. See tread.

## re-tread
re-tread, tr. v., to tread again. — Formed fr. re-
and tread. Cp. prec. word.

## retreat
retreat, n. — Late ME., fr. MF. retret, a var. of
retrait, retraite (F. retraite), prop. pp. of retraire,
'to withdraw', fr. L. retrahere. See retract, 'to
draw back'.
Derivatives: retreat, intr. and tr. v., retreat-er,
п., retreat-ing, adj., retreat-ing-ness, n.

## retrench
retrench, tr. and intr. v. — Obsol. F. retrencher
(F. retrancher), 'to cut off', fr. MF. retrenchier,
fr. re- (see re-) and trenchier, 'to cut'. See
trench, v.
Derivative: retrenck-ment, n.

## retribution
retribution, п., recompense; reward or
punishment. — ME. retribucioun, fr. OF. retribution
(F. retribution), fr. L. retributionem, ace. of re-
tributio, fr. retributus, pp. of retribuere, 'to
repay, restore', fr. re- and tribuere, 'to assign, allot,
bestow, give, grant*. See tribute and -ion. The
word retribution was introduced into English by
the English religious reformer John fcVycliffe
(1320 7-84).

## retributive
retributive, adj. — Formed with suff. -ive fr. L.
retributus, pp. of retribuere. See prec. word.
Derivative: retributive-ly, adv.

## retributory
retributory, adj., retributive. — Formed with suff.
-ory fr. L. retributus, pp. of retribuere. See
retribute.
Derivative: retributive-ly, adv.

## retrieve
retrieve, tr. and intr. v. — ME. retreven, retriven,
fr. OF. retrover, retrouver (F. retrouver), 'to
find again', fr. re- (see re-) and trover, trouver,
'to compose verses; to invent; to find* (whence
F. trouver, 'to find'). See trover and cp. contrive.
Derivatives: retrieve, п., retriev-able, adj., re-
triev-al, п., retreiv-er, n.

## retro-
retro-, pref. meaning I) 'backward', as in retro-
act; 2) 'behind', as in retrocardiac. — L. retro,
formed fr. re-, 'back' (see re-). L. retro stands to
re- as intro, 'in, within', to in, 'in', and as citro,
'hither', stands to cis, 'on this side*. Cp. reredos.
Cp. also arrear, darrein and the first word in

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:661 COLUMN:3 -->
dernier ressort.

## retroact
retroact, intr. v. — L. retrodctus, pp. of
retroagere, 'to drive back, turn back', fr. retro- and
agere, 'to set in motion, drive", lead; to do, act'.
See act.

## retroaction
retroaction, n. — Formed with suff. -ion fr. L.
retrodctus-, pp. of retroagere. See prec. word.

## retroactive
retroactive, adj. —F. retroactif(fem. retroactive),
fr. L. retrodctus, pp. of retroagere. See retroact
and -ive.
Derivatives: retroactive-ly, adv., retroactiv-ity,
n.

## retrocede
retrocede, intr. v., to go back, recede. — L. re-
trocedere, 'to go back or backward, to retire,
recede', fr. retro- and cedere, 'to go'. See cede.
Derivatives: retroced-ent, adj., retroced-ence, n.

## retrocede
retrocede, tr. v., to give back (territory). — F.
retroceder, fr. retro-, 'back' (fr. L. retro), and
cider, *to cede'. See retro- and cede and cp. prec.
word.

## retrocession
retrocession, п., a going back. — Late L. retro·
cessio, gen. -onis, *a going back or backward*,
fr. L. retrocess-(um), pp. stem of retrocedere.
See retrocede, 'to go back*, and -ion.

## retrocession
retrocession, п., the act of giving bacjc or
restoring. — See retrocede, * to give back', and -ion.

## retrocessive
retrocessive, adj., tending to move backward. —
Formed with suff. -ive fr. L. retrocess-(um), pp.
stem of retrocedere. See retrocede, 'to go back*.

## retrochoir
retrochoir, п., space in a church behind the choir.
— Formed fr. retro- and choir on analogy of
ML. retrochorus.

## retroflected
retroflected, adj., bent or turned backward. —
Formed with suff. -ed fr. L. retroflectere, *to
bend back', fr. retro- anaflectere, 'to bend'. See
flex and cp. reflect,

## retroflex
retroflex, adj., retroflected. — L. retroflexus, pp.
οι retroflectere. See prec. word.
Derivatives: retroftex-ed, adj., retroflex-ion, n.

## retrograde
retrograde, adj., ]) moving backward; 2)

## revere

## Reynard
Reynard, п., proper name of the fox in the epic

(G. Reinhart), lit. 'skilful in counsel'. The first
element in OHG. Reginhart is rel. to Goth, ra-
gin, 'counsel', rahnjan, 'to count, reckon', OE.
(ge)recenian, *to explain', recen, ricen, 'ready,
quick'; see reckon and cp. words there referred
to. For the second element in OHG. Reginhart
see hard. Cp. G. Reineke, 'Reynard'.

## Reynold

naut (F. Renaut), fr. OHG. Reginald, Raginald
(G. Reinwald). The first element is rel. to Goth.
ragin, 'counsel'; see prec. word. The second
element is rel. to OE. (ge)weald, 'power, strength',
wealdan, 'to rule', and cogn. with L. valere, 'to
be strong, be well'. See valiant and cp. Reginald.

rhabdo-, before a vowel rhabd-, combining form

rhabdomancy, п., divination by means of a rod.

rhachis, n. — See rachis.

rhachitis, n. — See rachitis.

Rhadamanthus, п., son of Zeus and Europe, one

— L. Rhadamanthus, fr. Gk. 'Ραδάμαν&ος,

## Rhaetia
