## rhagades
rhagades, п., cracks or fissures in the skin {med.)
— L., fr. Gk. φαγάδες, pi. of ($αγάς, *crack,
Assure', from the stem of ρηγνύναι, 'to break'. See
regma.

## Rhamnaceae
Rhamnaceae, n. pi., the buckthorn family {bot.)
— ModL., formed fr. Rhamnus with sutf.-aceae.

## rhamnaceous
rhamnaceous, adj. — See prec. word and -aceous.

## Rhamnus
Rhamnus, п., a genus of plants, the buckthorn
(bot.) — L. rkamnos, fr. Gk. ράμνος, 'a pricky
shrub; the buckthorn', which stands for *(5dc-
βνος and is rel. to ράβδος, 'rod, twig, stick'. See
rhnbdo-.

## Rhapis
Rhapis, п., a genus of fan palms (bot.) — ModL.,
fr. Gk. ρ'απίς, 'rod, stick', which is rel. to
(5άμνος, 'a pricky shrub; the buckthorn'. See
prec. word.

## rhapontic
rhapontic, п., a species of rhubarb. — ModL. rha-
ponticum, fr. MedL. rha Ponticum, lit. 'Pontic
rhubarb*. The first element stands for orig.
rkeum, 'rhubarb', fr. Gk. ρήον, fr. Pers. rewend,
of s.m.; the alteration of rheum into rha is due
to a confusion with Rha, the ancient name of
the river Volga. See Rheum, rhubarb. For the
second element see Pontic.

## rhapsode
rhapsode, п., a reciter of rhapsodies. — Gk.
£αψωδός. See rhapsody.

## rhapsodic
rhapsodic, adj., pertaining to a rhapsody. — Gk.
ραψωδι,κός, fr. ραψωδία. See next word and -«ic.
Derivatives: rhapsodic-al, adj., rhapsodic-al-ly,
adv.

## rhapsody
rhapsody, n. — F. rhapsodie, rapsodie, fr. L. rkap-
sodia, fr. Gk. Ραψωδία, 'epic poem, recitation of
epic poetry', fr. ραψωδός, 'rhapsodiSt', which is
compounded of ράπτειν, 'to sew, weave; to
compose songs', and φδή, 'song'. For the first
element see vervain, for the second see ode and
cp. comedy, tragedy.
Derivatives: rhapsod-ist, п., rhapsod-ize, tr. and
intr. v.

## r hat any
r hat any, п., name of a Peruvian shrub. — Sp. ra-
tana, fr. Quechua ratana.

## Rhea
Rhea, п., the mother of the gods in Greek
mythology. — L. Rhea, fr. Gk. 'Ρέα, a Titaness,
mother of Zeus, which is of uncertain origin.

## Rhea
Rhea, п., a genus of birds, the South-American
ostrich. — ModL., named after Rkea, the
mother of the gods in Greek mythology. See prec.
word.

## Rhenish
Rhenish, adj. — MHG. rinisch (G. Rheinisch), fr.
Rin (G. Rhein), 'Rhine', fr. Gaul. Renos (whence
L. Rhenus), lit. 'that which flows', fr. l.-E. base
, *rei-, 'to move, flow, run*. See rise and cp.
rhenium, cisrhenane, transrhenane. For the ending
see adj. suff. -ish.

## Rhenish
Rhenish, п., Rhine wine. — Short for Rhenish

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:663 COLUMN:3 -->
wine.

## rhenium
rhenium, п., name of a very rare element (chem.)
— ModL., coined by its discoverers, the
German chemist Walter Karl Friedrich Noddack
(1893- ) and his wife Ida Tacke, fr. Rhenus,
the name of the Rhine (see Rhenish, adj.), and
chem. suff. -ium.

## rheo-
rheo-, combining form meaning 'current of a
stream, current'.— Gk. pea-, fr. £έος, 'anything,
flowing, stream', from the stem of ρέειν, £etv,
(for *σρέ5ειν), 'to flow, run' (whence also
ρόος, ρους, 'current', £εϋμα, 'that which flows,
current, stream)', fr. I.-E. base *sreu-, 'to flow',
whence also—with inserted -t—OE. stream,
'flowing, river*. See stream and cp. words there
referred to.

## rheostat
rheostat, п., lesistor (electr.) — Coined by the
English physicist Sir Charles Wheatstone (1802-
75) from Gk. ρέος, 'anything flowing, stream',
and στατός, 'placed, standing*. See rheo- and
static and cp. nerostat and words there referred
to.
Derivative: rheostat-ic, adj.

## rhesus
rhesus, п., an East Indian monkey. — ModL.,
coined by the French naturalist Jean-Baptiste
Audebert (1759-1800).

## rhetor
rhetor, п., teacher of rhetoric; orator. — L., fr.
Gk. £ήτωρ (Aeol. *5ρήτωρ], 'public speaker,
orator; rhetor', rel. Τ,ο'ρ'ημα, 'word*, lit. 'that
which is spoken', ρήσις, 'speech', and to είρω
(for *Γέριω), Ί say, speak', είρων (for *fi-
ρΐων), 'dissembler', lit. 'sayer' (i.e. one who
speaks in order to hide his thoughts), εΕρωνεία,
'irony', and cogn. with OL vratamy
'commandment, order', L. verbum, 'word', Goth, waurd,
OE. word, 'word*. See word and cp. irony. Cp.
also verb.

## rhetoric
rhetoric, n. — ME. rethorik, fr. OF. rhetorique
(F. rhetorique), fr. L. rhetorica, rhetoricey fr. Gk.
Ρητορική (scil. τέχνη), *art of rhetoric', fem. of
Ρητορικός, 'fit for a public speaker or public
speaking, oratorical; rhetorical', fr.£ήτωρ, gen.
£ήτορος. See prec. word and -ic.
Derivatives: rhetoric-al, adj., rhetoric-al-ly, adv.

## rhetorician
rhetorician, n. — ME. rethoricien, fr. MF. (= F.)
rhetoricien, fr. rhetorique. See prec. word and
-ian.

## rheum
rheum, п., discharge from the mucous membranes
(archaic). — ME. reume, fr. OF. reume (F.
rhume), 'a cold', fr. L. rheuma, fr. Gk. ρεΰμα,
4hat which flows; discharge, flux, rheum', from
the stem of £έειν, (5εΐν, Чо flow'. See rheo-.
Derivatives: rheum-ic, adj., rheum-yy adj.,
rheum-i-ly, adv., rheum-i-nessy n.

## Rheum
Rheum, п., a genus of herbs (bot.) — L., 'rhubarb',
fr. Gk. £ήον, fr. Pers. rewend, of s.m. See
rhubarb and cp. rhapontic.

## rheumatic
rheumatic, adj. — ME. rewmatik, fr. MF. reuma-
tique (F. rhumatique), fr. L. rheumaticus,
'troubled with rheum*, fr. Gk. Ρευματικός, fr. ρ'εΰμα,
gen. ρεύματος. See rheum and 1st -atic.
Derivatives: rheumatic, п., rheumatic-al, adj.

## rheumatism
rheumatism, n. — L. rheumatismus, 'rheum,
catarrh', fr. Gk. ρευματισμός, fr. ρευματίζεσ&αΐ,
Чо suffer from a flux', fr. ρεΰμα, gen. γεύματος.
See rheum and -ism.

## rheumatoid
rheumatoid, adj., resembling rheumatism. —
Compounded of Gk. ρ'εΰμα, gen. γεύματος (see
rheum), and -οειδής, 'like', fr. είδος, 'form,
shape'. See -oid.
Derivatives: rheumatoid-al, adj.,
rheumatoid-ally, adv.

## Rhcxia
Rhcxia, п., a genus of plants, the deergrass, the
meadow beauty (bot.) — L., a name used by
Pliny.

## rhigolene
rhigolene, п., a volatile petroleum product used
as a local anesthetic. — A hybrid coined fr. Gk.
^Τγος, 'frost, cold', and L. oleum, 'oil'. The first
element stands for *σρϊγος and is cogn. with L.
frigus, 'cold'; see frigid. For»the second element
see olive, for the ending see suff. -ene.

## rhin-
rhin-, form of rhino- before a vowel.

## rhinal
rhinal, adj., pertaining to the nose. — Formed
with adj. suff. -al fr. Gk. £ΐς, gen. ρΊνός, 'nose'.
See rhino-.

## Rhinanthus
Rhinanthus, п., a genus ofplanis, the yellow rattle
(bot.) — ModL., compounded of Gk. (5ϊς, gen.
ρ4νός, 'nose, snout', and άνθ-ος, 'flower'. See

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:664 -->

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:664 COLUMN:1 -->
rhino- and anther.

## rhine
rhine, п., a large ditch in marshy land. — OE.
rene, ryne, 'bed of a river', lit. 'a running'. See
run, n.

## rhlnencephalon
rhlnencephalon, п., the olfactory part of the brain
(anat.) — Medical L., coined by the Swiss
anatomist Rudolf Albert von KOIliker (1817-1905)
fr. Gk. ρις, gen. ρινός, 'nose', and εγκέφαλος,
'brain'. See rhino- and encepbalon.

## rhinestone
rhinestone, п., a colorless imitation stone. — Loan
translation of F. caillou de Rhin, lit. 'pebble of
the Rhine'.

## rhinitis
rhinitis, п., inflammation of the nose (med.) —
Medical L., formed with suff. -itis, fr. Gk. ρις,
gen. ρινός, 'nose'. See rhino-.
rhino (slang). — Short for rhinoceros.

## rhino
rhino, п., money (slang). — Of uncertain origin.

## rhino-
rhino-, before a vowel rhin-, combining form
denoting the nose. — Gk. ρΐνο-, fr. ρις, gen.
ρινός, 'nose', a word of uncertain origin. Cp. the
second element in Antirrhinum, Catarrhina,
Gymnorhina, platyrrhine.

## rhinoceros
rhinoceros, n. — L., fr. Gk. ρΐνόκερως,
'rhinoceros', lit. 'nose-horn', fr. ρις, gen. ρινός,
'nose', and κέρας, 'horn'. See rhino- and cerato-.

## rhinocerotic
rhinocerotic, adj., pertaining to a rhinoceros. —
Formed with adj. suff. -ic fr. Gk. ρΐνόκερως,
gen. ρΤνοκέρωτος. See prec. word.

## rhinology
rhinology, п., that branch of medicine which
treats of the nose and its
diseases.—Compounded of rhino- and Gk. -λογία, fr. -λόγος, 'one who
speaks (in a certain manner); one who deals
(with a certain topic)'. See -logy.
Derivatives: rhinolog-ic-al, adj., rhinolog-ist, n.

## rhinoplasty
rhinoplasty, п., plastic surgery of the nose. —
Compounded of rhino- and Gk. -πλαστία, fr.
πλαστός, 'molded, formed'. See -plasty.

## rhinoscope
rhinoscope, п., an instrument for viewing the
nose. — Compounded of rhino- and Gk. -σκά-
πιον, fr. σκοπεΐν, 'to look at, examine'. See
-scope.
Derivative: rhinoscop-ic, adj.

## rhinoscopy
rhinoscopy, п., examination of the nose (med.) —
Compounded of rhino- and Gk. -σκοπία, fr.
'σκοπεΐν, 'to look at, examine'. See -scopy.

## rhizo-
rhizo-, before a vowel rhiz-, combining form
meaning 'root', as in rhizogenic. — Gk. ριζο-,
ριζ-, fr. ρίζα, 'root', which stands for 'Fp^Sia
and is re], to ράδαμνος (for *Γράδαμνος),
'branch', and cogn. with L. radix (for *wrddix),
'root'. See radix and cp. words there referred to.
Cp. also risk.

## Rhizobium
Rhizobium, η., a genus of rod-shaped bacteria
(bacteriol.) — ModL., formed fr. rhizo- and Gk.
βίος, 'life'. See bio-.

## Rhizocephala
Rhizocephala, п., an order of parasitic cirripeds.
— ModL., compounded of rirlzo- and Gk.
κεφαλή, 'head'. See cephalic.

## rhizocephalous
rhizocephalous, adj., pertaining to the order
Rhizocephala. — See prec. word and -ous.

## rhizogenic
rhizogenic, adj., root-producing. — Compounded
of rhizo- and -genie.

## rhizoid
rhizoid, adj., resembling a root. — Formed fr.
rhizo- and Gk. -οειδής, 'like', fr. είδος, 'form,
shape'. See -oid.
Derivative: rhizoid, п., filament.

## rhizome
rhizome, п., an underground rootlike stem (hot.)
ModL. rkizoma, fr. Gk. ρίζωμα, 'the mass of
roots of a tree', fr. ρ4ζοϋν, 'to take root', fr. ρ'ίζα,
'root'. See rhizo- and -oina.

## rhizophagous
rhizophagous, adj., feeding on roots. —
Compounded of rhizo- and Gk. φαγεΐν, 'to eat'.
See -phagous.

## Rhizopodn
Rhizopodn, n. pi., a division of Protozoa (zool.)
— ModL., lit. 'having rootlike feet',
compounded of rhizo- and Gk. πους, gen. ποδός, 'foot'.
See -pod.

## rho
rho, п., name of the 17th letter of the Greek
alphabet. — Gk. ρώ, shortened fr. ρως, fr. Heb.
rash, resh. See resh.

## rhod-
rhod-, form of rhodo- before a vowel.

## Rhodian
Rhodian, adj., 1) pertaining to the island of
Rhodes; 2) pertaining to the Knights of Rhodes.
— Formed with suff. -an fr. L. Rhodius, 'of
Rhodes', fr. Rhodus, fr. Gk. 'Ρόδος, 'Rhodes',
one of the Dodecanese Islands, southwest of
Turkey.
Derivative: Rkodian, n.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:664 COLUMN:2 -->

## rhodium
rhodium, п., name of a rare metallic element
(chem.) — ModL., coined by its discoverer, the
English chemist and physicist William Hyde
Wollaston (1766-1828) from Gk. ρόδον, 'rose'
(see rhodo-); so called by him from the rose-red
color of its salts. For the ending see chem. suff.
-ium.
Derivatives: rhod-ic, adj., rhod-ite,n. (mineral.),
rhod-ous, adj.

## rhodium
rhodium, п., also rhodium wood, a scented wood.
— ModL. rhodium, short for rhodium lignum, lit.
'rose-wood'. See prec. word and 1st suff. -ium.

## rhodo-
rhodo-, before a vowel rhod-, combining form
meaning rose, as in rhododendron. — Gk. ρόδο-,
fr. (5 όδου, 'rose', for * fpoSov, fr.OIran. *w£da. See
rose and cp. the second element in cynorrhodon.

## Rhododendron
Rhododendron, п., a genus of plants; (not cap.)
any plant of this genus (bot.) — L., fr. Gk.
ροδόδενδρον, lit. 'the rose-tree', fr. ρόδον, 'rose',
and δένδρον, 'tree'. See rhodo- and dendro-.

## rhodolite
rhodolite, п., a rose-colored variety of garnet. —
Lit. 'rosy stone', compounded of rhodo- and
-lite.

## rhodonite
rhodonite, п., a red manganese metasilicate
MnSiO, (mineral.) — G. Rhodonit, formed fr.
Gk. ρόδον, 'rose' (see rhodo-), with suff. -it,
which goes back to Gk. -ΐτης; see subst. suff. -ite.

## Rhodora
Rhodora, п., a genus of plants (bot.) — ModL.,
fr. L. rhodora, name of a plant; of Gallic origin.

## rhomb
rhomb, п., rhombus. — MF. (= F.) rhombe, fr.
L. rhombus, fr. Gk. ρόμβος, 'a spinning top,
wheel, rhomb', which is rel. to ρέμβειν, 'to turn
round, roll about', fr. I.-E. base *wremb-, a
nasalized form of base *wer-b-, 'to turn, twist,
bend' (see vervain and cp. rhombus, rhumb); so
called from its resemblance to a spinning top.
Derivatives: rhomb-ic, rhomb-ic-al, adjs.

## rhombencephalon
rhombencephalon, п., part of the brain consisting
of the cerebellum, pons and medulla (anat.) —
Medical L., compounded of rhomb- and ence-
phalon.

## rhombo-
rhombo-, before a vowel rhomb-, combining form
meaning *a rhomb', as in rhombohedron. — Gk.
ρόμβο-, ρομβ-, fr. ρόμβος. See rhomb.

## rhombohedral
rhombohedral, adj., forming a rhombohedron. —
See next word and adj. suff. -al.

## rhombohedron
rhombohedron, п., a prism bounded by six equal
rhombs. — Compounded of rhombo- and
-hedron.

## rhomboid
rhomboid, п., an oblique-angled parallelogram in
which the adjacent sides are unequal; adj., 1)
shaped like a rhomboid; 2) shaped somewhat
like a rhombus. — MF. (= F.) rhomboide, fr. L.
rhomboides, fr. Gk. ρομβοειδής, 'rhomboid', lit.
'resembling a rhomb', fr. ρόμβος, 'rhomb',
and -οειδής, 'like', fr. είδος, 'form, shape'. See
rhomb and -oid.

## rhomboidal
rhomboidal, adj., shaped somewhat like a
rhomboid. — Formed fr. rhomboid, п., with adj. suff.
-al.

## rhombus
rhombus, п., an oblique-angled equilateral
parallelogram. — L. See rhomb.

## rhoncial
rhoncial, also rhonchal, adj., pertaining to a rhon-
chus. See next word and adj. suff. -al.

## rhonchus
rhonchus, п., a whistling sound heard on the
auscultation of the chest. — L-, 'a snoring', fr.
Gk. ρόγχος, which is rel. to ρόγκος, ρέγχος,
ρέγκος, of s.m. ρέγχείϊ, ρέγκειν, 'to snore';
prob. of imitative origin.

## rhotacism
rhotacism, п., mispronunciation of the letter r. —
ModL. rhotacismus, fr. Gk. ρωτακισμός, fr.
ρωτακίζειν. See next word and -ism.

## rhotacize
rhotacize, intr. v., to mispronounce the letter r,
— Gk. ρωτακίζειν, 'to use the letter r
excessively', fr. ρω, name of the letter r. See rho and -ize.

## rhubarb
rhubarb, п., a garden plant with large leaves and
edible leaf stalks. — ME. rubarbe, fr. MF. reu-
barbe, rubarbe (F. rhubarbe), fr. ML. rheubar-
barum. The first element in ML. rheubarbarum
derives fr. L. rheum, fr. Gk. ρήον, ultimately fr.
Pers. rewend, 'rhubarb' (whence also Russ.
reven). Cp. the ML. form rhabarbarum, which
comes fr. Gk. pa βάρβαρον, lit. 'foreign rhubarb';
ρά, 'rhubarb', is a blend of ρήον, 'rhubarb', with
'Pa, the Scythian name of the Volga; see roric.
The second word in pec βάρβαρον refers to the
foreign origin of the plant. It. rabarbaro (whence
G. Rhabarber) derives fr. Gk. pi βάρβαρον. Ср.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:664 COLUMN:3 -->
rhapontic, rheum.

## rhumb
rhumb, п., any of the 32 points of the mariner's
compass. — Sp. rumbo, fr. L. rhombus. See
rhomb and cp. F. rumb.

## rhumba
rhumba, n. — A var. spelling of rumba.

## Rhus
Rhus, п., a genus of plants, the sumac (bot.) —
L., fr. Gk. ρους, 'sumac'.

## rhyme
rhyme, n. — ME. rime. rvme. fr. OF. rime,
'rhyme', a word of Teut. origin. Cp. OHG. and
OE. rim, 'number'; for the cognates of these
Teut. words see arithmetic and rite. The spelling
of E. rhyme (for rime) is due to a confusion with
Gk. ρυθμός, 'rhythm', with which it has nothing
in common. Cp. rime, 'rhyme'. Cp. also the
second element in bouts-rimes, monorhyme, and the
second word in ottava rima.

## rhyme
rhyme, tr. and intr. v. — ME. rimen, rymen, fr.
OF. rimer, 'to rhyme', fr. rime, 'rhyme'. See
rhyme, n.
Derivatives: rhym-ed, adj., rhyme-less, adj.,
rhym-er, п., rhym-ery, п., rhymester, п.,
Thymic, adj., rkym-ing, adj., rhym-ist, n.

## rhyncho-
rhyncho-, before a vowel rhynch-, combining
form meaning 'snout'. — Gk. ρυγχο-, ρυγχ-,
fr. ρύγχος, 'snout, beak', which, together with
ρύζειν (prob. for ·ρύγ&ειν), 'to growl, snarl', is
of imitative origin. Cp. Arm. rngun-к', r ngun-k\
'nostrils, nose', which is also of imitative
origin. Cp. also Rhynchosia and the second
element in ornithorhynchus.

## Rhynchosia
Rhynchosia, п., a genus of plants of the pea
family (bot.) — ModL., fr. Gk. ρύγχος, 'snout,
beak' (see rhyncho- and 1 st -ia). The genus was
so called in allusion to the beaklike shape of the
keel.

## rhyolite
rhyolite, п., a volcanic rock containing quartz
(petrogr.) — G. Rhyolith, compounded of Gk.
puo- (for ρύαξ, 'stream of lava', from the stem
of ρεΐν, 'to flow') and λίθος, 'stone'. See rheo-
and -lite.

## rhyparographer
rhyparographer, п., a painter of sordid subjects.
— Formed fr. Gk. ραπαρογράφος (see next
word) with agential suff. -er.

## rbyparography
rbyparography, п., the painting of mean or sordid
subjects. — Formed with suff. -y (fr. Gk. -is)
fr. Gk. ρυπαρογράφος, 'painting sordid
subjects', ft. ρυπαρός, 'dirty, filthy', and -γράφος,
'writing, painting', fr. γράφειν, 'to write'. The
first element derives fr. ρύπος, 'dirt, filth', which
is of uncertain origin; cp. rupia. For the second
element see -graph.
Derivative: rhyparograph-ic, adj.

## rhythm
rhythm, n. — MF. rhythme (F. rhytme), fr. L. rhyth-
mus, fr. Gk. ρυθμός, 'measured motion, time,
proportion, symmetry, rhythm', formed from
the stem of ρεΐν 'to flow', with suff. -θμός, a
var. of -σμός (ср. -ism). See rheo- and cp. next
word.
Derivatives: rhythm-ize, tr. and intr. v., rhythm-
iz-able, adj., rhythm-iz-ation, п.,rhythm-less1, adj.

## rhythmic
rhythmic, adj. — Late L. rhythmicus, fr. Gk.
ρυθμικός, fr. ρυθμός. See prec. word and adj.
suff. -ic.
Derivatives: rhythmic-al, adj., rhythmic-al-ly,
adv., rhythmic-ize, tr. v.

## ria
ria, п., creek; inlet. — Sp. rla, 'mouth of a river',
rel. to rlo, 'river'. See rio.

## rial
rial, n. — A var. of riyal.

## rial
rial, п., the monetary unit of Iran. — Pers., fr.
Arab, riyal. See riyal.

## rialto
rialto, п., exchange, market. — It. Rialto, name
of a quarter of Venice where the exchange was
situated. The name is a contraction of Rivoalto,
former name of the island on which Venice was
built, fr. L. rivus alius, 'deep river'. For the first
word see rio, for the second see alt.

## riant
riant, adj., smiling. — MF. (= F.), pres. part, of
rire, 'to laugh', fr. L. ridire. See risible and -ant.
Derivative: riant-ly, adv.

## riata
riata, n. — See reata.

## rib
rib, n. — ME. ribbe, fr. OE. ribb, rel. to OS. ribb,
ribbi, ON. rif, Dan. ribbe, Swed. rev, OFris. ribb,
rebb, MDu. ribbe, Du. ribbe, rib, OHG. ribba,
rippi, MHG. ribbe, riebe, rippe, G. Rippe, and
to the second element in OHG. hirni-reba, 'skull',
lit. 'brain cover', fr. I.-E. base *rebh-, 'to root,
cover'. The ribs are so called because they "roof"
the cavity of the chest. From the same base de-

surface, orbit, orb'. Cp. orb, reef, 'ridge of sand',
