-dar, 'holder, possessor'. For the first element
see thana; for the second see aumildar and cp.
words there referred to.

## thanage
thanage, п., rank of a thane. — ME., ft. ML.
thanagium, a hybrid formed fr. ME. theyn,
thayn, and ML. suff. -agium (fr. OF. -age). See
thane and -age.

## thanato-
thanato-, before a vowel thanat-, combining form
meaning 'death'. — Gk. θάνατο-, θανατ-, ft.
θάνατος, 'death', prob. for *θ5άνατος, fr. I.-E.
base *dhw-en·, 'to be extinguished', whence also
OI. ddhvanit, 'vanished', dhvantah, 'dark'. Cp.
athanasy, euthanasia. Base *dhw-en- is an
enlargement of base "dhewe-, *dheu-, 'to fly about
like dust; to smoke, be scattered, vanish',
whence fumus, 'smoke, steam, vapor'. See thio-
and cp. words there referred to.

## thanatoid
thanatoid, adj., deathlike. — Compounded of
thanat- and Gk. -οειδής, 'like', fr. είδος, 'form,
shape'. See oid.

## thane
thane, n. — ME. thein, fr. OE. pegn, pen, 'thane,
man, servant, attendant, soldier', rel. to OS.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:785 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: THANK | 758 -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:785 COLUMN:1 -->
tkegan, 'follower, warrior, boy*, ON. pegn,
'thane, freeman', OHG. tkegan, MHG. degen,
G. Degen, 'thane, warrior, hero*, fr. I.-E. base
*tekno-t whence also OI. takman-, 'descendant,
child', Gk. τέκνον, 'child'. This base is a
participial enlargement of base *tek-, *tok-, 'to
beget, bear', whence Gk. τέκος, 'child, the
young of animals', τόκος, 'childbirth, offspring,
produce of money, interest', τοκεύς, 'father', in
pi. 'parents', τίκτειν, 'to bring forth, bear',
which stands for *τί,-τκειν, reduplication of
*tk-, zero degree of base *tek-. Cp. thegn,
dirndl. Cp. also tecno-, teknonymy, -tocia, toco-.

## thank
thank, n. — ME. thank, tkonk, fr. OE. pane,
pone, 'thought, favor, satisfaction, thanks', prop,
verbal n. fr. pencian, 'to think'; rel. to OS.
thank, ON. pokk, Dan. tak, Swed. tack, OFris.
thank, tkonk, MDu. danc, Du. dank, OHG.,
MHG. danc, G. Dank, Goth, pagks, 'thanks';
see think. Hence thank orig. meant 'thought-
fulness'.
Derivatives: thank, v. (q.v.), thank-ful, adj.,
thank-ful-ly, adv., thank-ful-ness, п., thank-less,
adj., thank-less-ly, adv., thank-less-ness, n.

## thank
thank, tr. v. — ME. thanken, thonken, fr. OE.
pancian, Poncian, fr. pane, Pone (see thank, п.);
ср. OS. thancon, ON. pakka, Dan. takke, Swed.
tacka, OFris. thankia, thonkia, MLG., MDu.,
Du. danken, OHG. danchon, MHG., G. danken,
'to thank*, which all derive from the respective
noun.

## Thargelia
Thargelia, п., a festival of Apollo celebrated on
the 7th of the month of Thargelion {Greek an-
tiq.) — Gk- Θαργήλια (scil. ιερά), prop, 'the
festival on which was brought the θάργηλος
άρτος,'bread baked from the new crop'. The
origin of the word θάργηλος is unknown. Cp.
next word.

## Thargelion
Thargelion, п., name of the eleventh month of
the Attic Greek year (corresponding to the
second half of May and first half of June).—
Gk. Θαργηλίων, prop, 'the month on which the
Thargelia festival was celebrated', fr. Θαργήλια.
See prec. word.

## tharm
tharm, п., intestine (dial.) — OE. parm, pearm,
rel. to OS. tharm, parmr, Dan., Swed. tarm,
OFris. therm, MDu., Du. darm, OHG. daram,
darm, MHG., G. darm, 'gut*, fr. Teut. ч par-ma-,
which corresponds to I.-E. *tor-mo-, 'lit. 'that
which goes through', from I.-E. base *ter-, 'to
pierce, go through', whence also Gk. τόρμος,
'hole (into which a pin or peg is stuck)', τράμις,
'the perineum', τρήμα, 'perforation', τιτράν,
'to pierce, perforate'; for the suff. -ma in Teut.
*Par-ma (= E. -m) cp. beam, seam, team. See
throw and cp. terebra.

## Thaspiuin
Thaspiuin, п., a genus of plants, the meadow
parsnip (bot.) — ModL., coined by the English-
American naturalist Thomas Nuttall (1786-
1859) from a play upon Thapsia, prop. 'flower
of Thapsus*, fr. Gk. Θάψος, name of an island.
For the ending see 1st suff. -ium.

## that
that, demonstr. pron. — ME. that, thety fr. OE.
pset, neut, nom. and ace. sing, of the def. art.
se, seo, Pxt, used already in OE. also in
demonstr. sense. See the, art., and words there
referred to.
Derivatives: that, adj., adv., rel. pron., adv.,
that, conj. (q.v.)

## that
that, conj. — Identical with that, demonstr. pron.
Cp. Gk. δτι L. quod, F. que, It. eke, Sp. que,
which show the same sense development. In
German, the demonstr. pronoun das, 'that', is
only graphically distinguished from the
conjunction dafi, 'that'.

## thatch
thatch, tr. v. — ME. tkeccken, tkaccken, fr. OE.
peccan, 'to cover', rel. to OS. tkekkian, ON.
pekja, Swed. tacka, Dan. dcekke, OFris. thekka,
MDu. decken, Du. dekken, OHG. decchen,
decken, MHG., G. decken, 'to cover', and to
OE. рзес, 'roof, thatch', ON. рак, Swed. tak,
Dan. tag, OFris. thek, MLG., MDu., Du. dak,
'roof, OHG. dak, MHG., G. dock, 'roof, fr.
I.-E. base *(s)teg-, 'to cover', whence also L.
tegere, 'to cover*, tegumentum, ' a covering',
tectum, 'roof (prop. neut. pp. of tegere used as
a noun), tegula, 'tile', toga, 'toga', Olr. tech, teg,
OW. tig, 'house*, Olr. -tuigim, Ί cover', OCo.,

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:785 COLUMN:2 -->
W. to, 'roof, Gk. τέγος, τέγη, 'roof, and—
with initial s—OI. sthagati, sthagayati, 'covers
hides, conceals', Gk. στέγειν, 'to cover', στέγος,
στέγη, 'roof, στεγανός, 'covering; covered',
OSlav. o-stegu, 'garment', o-stegnqti, 'to cover*,
OPruss. steege, 'barn', stogis, 'roof, Lith.
stogas, 'roof. Cp. deck, deckle. Cp. also detect,
detective, integument, obtected, protect, stegano-,
tecto- (fr. L. tectum, 'roof), tectorial, tectrices,
tegument, thug, tile, tog, toga.
Derivatives: thatch-er, п., thatch-ing, n.

## thatch
thatch, n. — ME. thacche, fr. thecchen, thacchen,
'to thatch'. See thatch, v.
Derivative: thatch-y, adj.

## thaumasite
thaumasite, п., a calcium silicate, carbonate and
sulfate (mineral.) — Coined fr. Gk. θαυμάζει,
'to wonder' (see thaumato-), and subst. suff. -ite;
so called in allusion to its remarkable
composition.

## thaumato-. before a vowel thaumat-
thaumato-. before a vowel thaumat-, combining
form meaning 'wonder*. — Gk. θαυματο-, θαυ-
ματ-, fr. θαύμα, gen. θαύματος, 'wonder, a
wondrous thing', prop, 'a thing to look at', fr.
*θα.Ρ-, 4to look at', and rel. to θέα (for *θα-
Fct), 'sight, spectacle'. See theater.

## thaumatrope
thaumatrope, п., an optical instrument showing
the persistence of visual impressions. —
Compounded of Gk. θαϋμα, 'wonder' and-τρόπος,
'that which turns', fr, τρόπος, τροπή, 'turn,
turning*. See thaumat- and -trope.

## thaumaturge
thaumaturge, п., 1) a worker of miracles; 2) a
magician. — ML. tkaumaturgus, fr. Gk.
θαυματουργός, 'wonder working*, which is
compounded of θαϋμα, gen. θαύματος, 'wonder',
and έργον, 'work'. See thaumat- and work and
cp. ergon.

## thaumaturgy
thaumaturgy, п., magic. — Gk. θαυματουργίδϊ,
'magic', lit. 'wonder working' (п.), fr.
θαυματουργός. See prec. word and -y (representing
Gk.-ict).
Derivatives: thaumaturg-ic, thaumaturg-ic-al,
adjs., thaumaturg-ist, n.

## thaw
thaw, intr. and tr. v., to melt. — ME. thawen, fr.
OE. pdwian, rel. to ON. peyja, MLG. douwen,
doien, MDu. douwen, doyen, Du. dooien, OHG.
douwen, dewen, MHG. touwen, touwen, G. tauen,
'to thaw', OS. farthewian, OHG. firdouwen,
MHG. verdouwen, verdouwen, G. verdauen, 'to
digest', prop, 'to liquefy', fr. I.-E. base *td-,
*tu·, 'to melt*, whence also OI. tSyam, 'water',
Ossetic tkayun, 'to thaw', Arm. t'anam, Ί
moisten', Olr. tarn, 'pestilence', W. tawdd, 'molten',
Dor τακειν, Ion. τήκειν, 'to melt, waste, be
consumed*, τακερός, 'melting; tender, soft', L.
tdbere, of s.m., OSlav. tajati, 'to melt*. Cp. eu-
tectic, eutexia, tabes, tigilc. Cp. also the second
element in laurustine. For the sense
development of OS. farthewian, etc., 'to digest', cp.
Swed. smalta, 'to smelt; to digest'.
Derivatives: thaw, п., tkaw-er, n.

## the
the, def. article. — ME., fr. OE. pi, a blend of
earlier fe, 'that, the', and pset, of s.m. (see that).
OE. se, fern, seo, is rel. to ON. sa (masc.), su
(fem.), 'that', Goth, sa (masc), so (fern.),
'that', and cogn. with OI. sa, sab (masc), sa
(fem.), Avestic ha, ho (masc), ha (fem.), Toch.
A sds, В se (masc), sd-u (fem.), 'this', Gk. δ
(masc), ή (fem.), 'the'; from the I.-E. demonstr.
base *so-, *sd, 'that; the'. — OE. pxt is rel. to
ON. pat (neut.), 'that', Swed. den (masc. and
fem.), det (neut.), 'the', Dan. den, det, 'that',
OFris. tht (masc), thiu (fem.), thet (neut.), Du.
de, 'the', dat, 'that', OHG., MHG. der (masc),
diu (fem.), da^ (neut.), G. der (masc), die (fem.),
das (neut.), 'the', Goth, pata (neut.), 'the', and
cogn. with OI. tad (neut.), Avestic tat (neut.),
*it, that', Toch. B. te (neut.), 'this', Gk. τό
(neuL), 4he', OSlav. tu (masc), ta (fem.), to
(neut.), Russ. tot (masc), ta (fem.), to (neut.),
'that', Lith. tas (masc), ta (fem.), 'that*. Cp. the
second element in L. is-te (masc), is-ta (fem.),
is-tud (neut.), 'that of yours or near you', Arm.
-d, as e.g. in ter-d, 'the master (who is) here',
Alb. re, 'in order that', Olr. to, W. do, 'yes'. Cp.
also Hitt. ta (neut. pi.,; masc. sing, is tas, sas),
'that'. All these words derive from the I.-E.
demonstr. base *to-, *ta-, 'that, the*. Cp. they,
them, their, than, then, thence, there, this, these,

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:785 COLUMN:3 -->
thither, those, thus and the second element in
both, since, sith. Cp. also rules, tauto-, the first
element in tantamount and the second element
in idem, tandem, Cp. also ye, def. article.

## the
the, adv., by so much — used before the
comparative. — ME. thi, the, fr. OE. py, рё,
instrumental case of the def. article. See prec word.

## the-
the-, form of theo- before a vowel.

## Thea
Thea, п., a genus of plants of the Tea family
{bot.)— ModL., explained by the Swedish
botanist Carolus Linnaeus (1707-78) as 'the divine
plant', fr. Gk. θεά, 'goddess', but in reality of
the same origin as E. tea. Cp. theine.

## Theaceae
Theaceae, n. pi., the tea family {bot.) — Formed
fr. Thea with suff. -aceae.

## theaceous
theaceous, adj., pertaining to the tea family. —
See prec word and -aceous.

## theandric
theandric, adj., pertaining to the combination of
divine and human. — Eccles. Gk. θεανδρικός,
compounded of Gk. θεός, 'god', άνήρ, gen.
ανδρός, 'man', and suff. -ικός. See theo-, andro-
and adj. suff. -ic.

## theanthropic
theanthropic, theanthropical, adj., both divine
and human. — Formed with suff. -ic, resp. -ical,
fr. Eccles. Gk. θεάνθρωπος, which is
compounded of Gk. θεός, 'god', and άνθρωπος,
'man'. See theo- and anthropo- and cp. prec.
word.

## theanthropism
theanthropism, п., anthropomorphism.· — See
prec word and -ism.

## theanthropist
theanthropist, п., a believer in theanthropism. —
See prec word and -ist.

## thearchy
thearchy, п., 1) divine rule; 2) theocracy. —
Eccles. Gk. θεαρχία, compounded of Gk. θεός,
'god', and -αρχία, fr. άρχειν, 'to lead, rule*.
See theo- and -archy.
Derivative: thearch-ic, adj.

## theater
theater, theatre, n. — ME. theatre, fr. MF.
theatre (F. theatre), fr. L. thedtrum, fr. Gk. θέατρον,
'theater*, lit. 'a place for seeing', formed with
-τρον, a suff. denoting place, fr. θέα, 'sight,
spectacle', which stands for *θ«Ρα, *θήΓη,
whence Dor. θαέομαι (for *θαΡέομαι), Ion.
θηέομαι (for *θηΓέομαι), Att. θεάομαι, Ί
behold', θεητής, Att. θεατής, 'spectator',
θαΰμα, 'wonder'. Ср. thaumato-, theory,

## theatrical
theatrical, also {rarely) theatric, adj. — Late L.
theatricus, fr. L. thedtrum. See prec word and
the suffixes -ic and -nl.
Derivatives: theatrical-ity, п., theatrical-ize, tr.
v., theatrical-iz-ation, п., theatrical-ly, adv.,
theatric-als, n. pi.

## thebaine
thebaine, thebain, п., a white crystalline
poisonous alkaloid (ckem.) — Formed with chem. suff.
-ine, -in, fr. Gk. Θήβαι, L. Tkebae, 'Thebes'.
Thebaine lit. means 'alkaloid of Thebes*.

## thee-
thee-, form of theco- before a vowel,

## theca
theca, п., case, capsule (bot. and zool.) — L.
theca, fr- Gk. θήκη, 'a case in which to put
anything', from the base of τίθέναι, 'to put,
place', whence also θέμα, 'a placing, setting'.
See theme and words there referred to and cp.
esp. tick, 'cover', which is a doublet of theca.
Cp. also the second element in bibliotheca,
endothecium, exothecium, ootheca, perithecium.
Derivatives: thec-al, thec-ate, adjs.

## Thecla
Thecla, Thekla, fem. PN. — L. Thecla, fr. Gk.
Θέκλα, contraction of θεοκλεϊα, fem. of
θεοκλης, lit. 'god-famed'. See theo- and loud,

## theco-
theco-, before a vowel thee-, combining form
meaning 'case, capsule'. — Gk. θηκο-, θηκ-,
fr. θήκη. See theca.

## thee
thee, objective case of thou. — ME., fr. OE. рё,
dat. and ace. df рй, 'thou'. See thou.
Derivative: thee, tr. v., to address as thee', intr.
v., to use thee in addressing a person.

## thee
thee, intr. v., to grow, thrive. — OE. theon, rel.
to OS. thihan, OFris. thigia, MDu. (gke)dien,
Du. gedijen, OHG. (gi)dihan, MHG. gedihen,
G. gedeiken, Goth. {ga)peihan, fr. I.-E. base
tenq-, 'to be thick or strong*. See tight,

## theelin
theelin, п., a crystalline hormone (biochem.) —
Formed with suff. -in fr. Gk. θήλυς, 'female'.
See thely-.

## theft
theft, n. — ME. thefte, thiefthe, fr. OE. peofd,
piefd, pyfd, fr. peof, 'thief. Cp. ON. pyf, pyft,
and OFris. thiufthe, thiufte. and see thief and
subst. suff. -t.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:786 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: 759 | -THER -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:786 COLUMN:1 -->

## thegn
thegn, η. — A var. of thane.

## theine
theine, thein, п., another name for caffeine (ckem.)
— F. theine, formed with chem. sutf. -ine, -in, fr.
Thea; so called because it occurs in tea.

## their
their, possessive pron. — ME. their, thair, fr. ON.
peir(r)a, 'of them', gen. pi. of the demonstr.
pron. sa, su, pat, and rel. to OE. para, psera,
gen. pi. of the def. article. See they and cp.
them, that.

## theirs
theirs, possessive pron. — Formed from prec.
word with suff. -s, on analogy of his.

## theism
theism, п., belief in a personal God. — Formed
with suff. -ism fr. Gk. θεός, 'god', which prob.
stands for *dkes-os, and is cogn. with Arm. dik',
'gods' (which prob. stands for *dhes-es), OI.
dhisnyah, 'pious, devoted', L. fdnum (for */as-
nom), 'consecrated place, temple', feriae (fr. OL.
fesiae), 'holy days, festivals', festus, 'festive'; fr.
I.-E. base 'dhes- ( = L. ·/«-> *fas-), 'holy'. Cp.
apotheosis, atheism, ditheism, enthusiasm, heno-
theism, hylotheism, monotheism, pantheism,
polytheism, Thecla, theo-, Theodore, Tbespesia,
Thespian, theurgy, Timothy, tritheism, zootheism
Cp. also fair, fane, feast, Fedora.

## theism
theism, п., a morbid condition due to the
excessive use of tea. — Formed fr. Thea, 'tea', with
suff. -ism. Cp. theine.

## theist
theist, п., an adherent of theism. — See theism (fr.
Gk. θεός) and -ist and cp. atheist, henotheisr,
monotheist, pantheist, polytheist.
Derivatives: theist-ic, theist-ic-al, adjs., theist-
ic-al-ly, adv.

## Theleme
Theleme, п., name of an abbey in Rabelais' Gar-
gantua, given as reward to Friar John. The only
rule in the abbey was to be "Fay ce que voul-
dras" ("Do what you like"). — Gk. θέλημα,
'will', fr. θέλειν, έθέλειν, 'to will, wish', which
is prob. cogn. with Arm. gei-j, 'wish', OSlav.
ielejd, ieleti, 'to wish'.

## thelitis
thelitis, п., inflammation of the nipple (med.) —
Medical L., formed with suff. -itis fr. Gk. θηλή,
'teat, nipple'. See thely-.

## thelium
thelium, п., nipple, papilla. — ModL., fr. Gk.
θηλή, 'teat, nipple'. See thely-,

## thely-
thely-, combining form meaning 'female', — Gk.
θήλυ-, fr. θήλυς, 'feminine', which is rel. to
θηλή, 'teat, nipple', fr. I.-E. base "dhi-, "dhei-,
*dhl-, 'to suck, suckle', whence also OI. dhdyati,
'sucks', L.felare, 'to suck', filius (assimilated fr.
'fflios), 'son'. See filial and cp. theelin and the
second element in endothelium, epithelium,
mesothelinm.

## thelytokous
thelytokous, adj., producing only females. — Gk.
θηλυτόκος, 'bearing females', compounded of
θήλυ- (see thely-) and -τόκος, 'bearing', from
the stem of τίκτειν, 'to bring forth, bear'. See
thane and cp. toco-. For E. -ous, as equivalent
to Gk. -ος, see -ous.

## them
them, pron. — ME., a blend of ME. tham, fr.
OE. pxm, dat, pi. of рё, 'the, that', and of ME.
tkeim, fr. ON. peim, dat. pi. of the demonstr.
and personal pron.; see the, art. Them is the
objective case of they (q.v.)

## thema
thema, п., thema, subject. — L., fr. Gk. θέμα,
'that which is placed'. See*theme.

## thematic
thematic, adj., I) pertaining to the theme (stem)
of a word; 2) pertaining to a theme (music). —
Gk. θεματικός, fr. θέμα. See next word and
adj. suff. -lc.

## theme
theme, n. — ME. teme, fr. OF. tesme (F. theme),
fr. L. thema, fr. Gk. θέμα, gen. θέματος, 'that
which is placed', from the stem of τιθέναι, 'to
put, place', whence also θέσις, 'a placing,
setting' θήκη, 'case in which to put something',
θέμις, 'right, law, decree' θεσμός, 'law, rule,
precept', lit. 'that which is laid down', fr. I.-E.
base *dhe-, 'to put, place'. See do, v., and cp.
next word. Cp. also agnnothete, anathema,
antithesis, apothecary, apothecium, apothem, athe-
tize, athetosis, bibliotheca, Chrysothamnus,
diathesis, enthetic, epenthesis, epithet, Euthamia,
hypothec, hypothesis, hypothetic, logothete, mo-
nothetic, parathesis, parenthesis, peritheciuin,
prosthesis, prosthetic, prothesis, synthesis,
synthetic, Tbamnidium, thamno-, thamnuria, theca,
Themis, thesurus, thesis, thesmothete, thetic,
Thomomys, tick, 'cover', treasure, typothetae.
Cp. also the second element in ethical. For the

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:786 COLUMN:2 -->
ending see suff. -ma.

## Themis
Themis, п., personification of law and justice. —
L., fr. Gk. Θέμις, 'the goddess of law and
justice', fr. θέμις, 'right, law, decree'. See theme
and cp. the first element in Thomomys. Cp. also
doom.

## then
then, adv. — ME. tkanne, than, thenne, then, fr.
OE. ponne, pon, psnne, rel to OS., OFris.
tkanna, than, ON. pa, MDu. danne, dan, Du.
dan, OHG. thanne, denne, MHG. danne, denne,
dan, den, G. dann, Goth, pan, 'then'; from the
I.-E. demonstr. base "to-, *ta-. See the, art., and
cp. than,
Derivatives: then, adj. and n.

## thenar
thenar, п., the palm of the hand (anal.) —
Medical L., fr. Gk. θέναρ, 'palm of the hand', which
is cogn. with OHG. tenar, MHG. tener, 'palm
of the hand'. Cp. the second element in opisthe-
nar.
Derivative: thenar, adj.

## thence
thence, adv. — ME. thannes, thennes (formed,
with adverbial gen. suff. -s, from earlier tkanne,
thenne), contracted later into thens (written
thence, in order to show that the s has the
voiceless sound), fr. OE. panon, which is rel. to OS.
thanana, ON. pana, OFris. thana, OHG. dan-
nana, dannan (^= G. von dannen), 'thence'. See.
that. For the spelling with -ce cp. hence, whence.

## theo-
theo-, before a vowel the-, combining form
meaning 'god'. Gk. θεο-, θε-, fr. θεός, 'god'. See
1st theism.

## Theobald
Theobald, masc. PN. — ML. Theobaldus, fr. OG.
Theudobald Theodbald (rel. to OE. peodbeald),
fr. tkeuda, 'folk, people', and bald, 'bold'. (The
change of OG. Theudobald, Theodbald to ML.
Theobaldus is due to the influence of names
beginning with Theo-, fr. Gk. θεός, 'god'.) For
the first element see Dntch and cp. words there
referred to. For the second element see bold
and cp. the first element in Baldwin. Cp. also
Aldine.

## Theobroma
Theobroma, п., a genus of plants of the chocolate
family (bot.) — ModL., coined by the Swedish
botanist Carolus Linnaeus (1707-78) fr. theo-
and Gk. βρώμα, 'food', which is rel. to βορά,
'food', and cogn. with L. vorare, 'to devour'.
See voracious and cp. devour. Cp. also Abroma.
The name prop, refers to the cocoa as 'the food
of the gods'.

## theobromine
theobromine, п., a bitter crystalline compound,
С,Не^Ог, which occurs in cacao beans (chem.)
— Coined fr. ModL. Theobroma (see prec.
word) with chem. suff. -ine.

## theocentric
theocentric, adj., considering God as the center
of all things. — Compounded of theo- and
centric.

## theocracy
theocracy, n. — Gk. θεοκρατία, 'the rule of
GodS coined by the Jewish historian Josephus
(cca 38-cca 100), fr. θεός (see theo-) and
-κρατίϊ, 'rule of, fr. κράτος, 'strength, power,
rule'. See -cracy.

## theocrat
theocrat, п., one who rules under theocracy. —
Compounded of theo- and -crat. Cp. prec.
word.

## theocratic
theocratic, adj., pertaining to theocracy. — See
theocracy and 1st -atic.

## theodicean
theodicean, adj., pertaining to theodicy. —
Formed from next word with suff. -ean.

## theodicy
theodicy, п., vindication of divine justice. — F.
thiodicee, lit. 'justice of God', formed by the
German philosopher, Baron Gottfried Wilhelm
von Leibniz (1646-1716) in 1710 fr. theo- and
Gk. 8ίκη, 'justice', whence δικάζειν, 'to judge',
δικαστής, 'judge'. See dicast.

## theodolite
theodolite, п., an instrument for measuring
angles. — Of uncertain origin.

## Theodora
Theodora, п., fem. PN. — Gk. Θεοδώρα, fern, of
Θεόδωρος. See next word.

## Theodore
Theodore, masc. PN. — L. Theodorus, fr. Gk.
Θεόδωρος, lit. 'gift of God', compounded of
θεός (see theo-) and δώρον, 'gift'. See donation
and cp. prec. word and Dorothea. Cp. also
Fedora.

## Theodoric
Theodoric, masc. PN. — Late L. Tkeodoricus, a
name of Gothic origin lit. meaning 'ruler of the
people'. Cp. Goth, piuda, 'people', and 'reiks,
'ruler', which is rel. to reiki, 'rule, empire,
kingdom'. For the first element see Dntch and

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:786 COLUMN:3 -->
cp. words there referred to. For the second
element see Felch.

## Theodosia
Theodosia, fem. PN. — Gk. Θεοδοσία, lit. 'gift
of God', compounded of θεο- (see theo-) and
δόσις, 'gift'. See dose.

## theogony
theogony, п., the origin of the gods in heathen
theology. — Gk. θεογονία, 'origin of the gods',
compounded of θεός, 'god', and -γονία, fr.
γόνος, 'race, birth, descent', which stands in
gradational relationship to γένος, 'race,
descent'. See theo- and genus.
Derivatives: theogon-ic, theogon-ic-al, adjs.

## theolatry
theolatry, п., worship of a god. — Gk. θεολατρε-
ία, compounded of θεός (see theo-) and
-λατρεία, -λατρία, fr. λατρεία, 'service worship'.
See -Iatry.

## theologian
theologian, n. — MF. (= F.) rheologien, fr. theo-
logie, 'theology', fr. Eccles. L. theologia. See
theology and -an.

## theological
theological, adj. — Eccles. L. theologicdlis, fr.
theologicus, fr. theologia. See theology and -ical.
Derivatives: theological, п., theological-ly, adv.

## theologico-
theologico-, combining form meaning
'theological and'. — See theological.

## theologue
theologue, п., theologian (obsol. and colloq.) —
Eccles. L. theologus. See theologian.

## theology
theology, n. — ME. iheologie, fr. Eccles. L.
theologia, fr. Gk. θεολογία, 'science of divine
things', fr. θεολόγος, 'student of divine things',
which is compounded of θεός (see theo-) and
-λογία, fr. -λόγος, 'one who speaks (in a certain
manner); one who deals (with a certain topic'.
See theo- and -logy.

## theomachy
theomachy, п., battle of, or with, the gods. —
Gk. θεομαχία, compounded of θεός (see theo-)
and -μαχία, fr. μάχη, 'battle'. See -machy.

## theomorphic
theomorphic, adj., having the form of a god. —
Formed with adj. suff. -ic fr. Gk. θεόμορφος,
which is compounded of θεός (see theo-) and
μορφή, 'form, shape'. See theo- and morpho-.

## theophany
theophany, п., appearance of God to man. —
Eccles. L. theophania, fr. Gk. θεοφάνεια, θεοφα-
νία, 'manifestation of God', compounded of
θεός (see theo-) and the stem of φαίνεσθαι, 'to
appear'. See phantasm and cp. tiffany. For the
ending see suff.-y (representinK Gk.-εια. -ία).

## Tbeophilus
Tbeophilus, masc. PN. — L., fr. Gk. Θεόφιλος,
lit. 'loved by the gods', fr. θεός, 'god', and
φίλος, 'loved, beloved'. See theo- and philo-.

## theopneustic
theopneustic, adj., divinely inspired..— Formed
with suff. -ic fr. Gk. θεόπνευστος, fr. θεός (see
theo-) and -πνευστός, '-inspired', prop, verbal
adj. of πνέειν, 'to breathe, inspire'. See pneuma.

## theorbo
theorbo, п., an obsolete kind of lute (mus.) — F.
theorbe, reorbe, fr. earlier tuorbe, tiorbe, fr. It.
tiorba, which is of unknown origin.

## theorem
theorem, п., a general statement. — Late L.
theorema, fr. Gk. θεώρημα, 'sight, spectacle',
fr. θεωρεΐν, 'to look at, behold', fr. θεωρός,
'spectator'. See theory and -ma.

## theorematic
theorematic, theorematical, adj. — Formed with
suff. -ic, resp. -ical, fr. Gk. θεώρημα, gen.
θεωρήματος, See prec. word.
Derivative: theorematical-ly, adv..

## theory
theory, n. — Late L. theoria, fr. Gk. θεωρία,
'spectacle, contemplation, consideration', fr.
θεωρός, 'spectator', from the stem of θεασθαι,
'to see, behold', whence also θέατρον, 'theater',
lit. 'a place for seeing'. See theater and -y
presenting Gk. -ία).
Derivatives: theor-ist, п., theor-ize, intr. and tr.
v., theor-iz-ation, п., theoriz-er, n.

## theosophy
theosophy, n. — ML. theosophia, fr. -Late Gk.
θεοσοφία, 'knowledge of divine things', which
is compounded of Gk. θεός (see theo-) and
σοφία, 'skill, wisdom', fr. σοφός, 'skilled, wise'.
See sophist.
Derivatives: iheosoph-ic, theosoph-ic-al, adjs.,
theosoph-isi, n.

## ther-
ther-, form of thero- before a vowel.

## -ther
-ther, suff. expressing comparison, alternative,
etc., as in further, hither, thither, either. —
Compar. suff-, from I.-E. base *ter-, *tr-,
whence OI. -tara, Gk. -τερος, L. -terus, lit.
'beyond'. Co. OI. tatra, 'there, thither', L.
trans, 'beyond', and see trans-. Cp. also allotrio-,
alter, contra-, deteriorate, deutero-, dexter,
either, esoteric, exoteric, exterior, hetero-, hinder,

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:787 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: THERALITE | 760 -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:787 COLUMN:1 -->
hither, hysteron proteron, inter-, iterate, magis-
ter, minister, neither, nostrum, other, presbyter,
preter-, sinister, subter-, thither, ulterior, ultra-,
whether.

## theralite
theralite, п., name of a group of plutonic rocks
(petrology). — Lit. 'the stone hunted after', fr.
Gk. θηραν, 'to hunt, chase, to hunt after', and
λίθος, 'stone*; it was so called because its
discovery was expected. Gk. θηραν derives fr.
θήρα, 'hunting of wild beasts, chase*, fr. θήρ,
'beast of prey'; see theriac and cp. words there
referred to. For Gk. λίθος, see iltho-.

## therapeutic
therapeutic, therapentical, adj. — Gk.
θεραπευτικός, lit. 'inclined to serve', hence 'attentive, on
obedient, able to cure', fr. θεραπεύει^, 'to wait
serve, attend, fr. θεράπων, 'servant, attendant',
fr. θέραψ, gen. θέραπος, of s.m. The suff. -εύειν
in θεραπεύειν is due to the analogy of verbs in
which the diphthong ευ belonged to the stem as
e.g. in βασιλεύειν, 'to be king, to rule4, fr.
βασιλεύς, 'king', ίερεύειν, 'to be a priest, to offer,
sacrifice*, fr. ιερεύς, 'priest'. Gk. θέραψ is of
uncertain origin. It possibly derives fr. I.-E.
base *dker(e)-, 'to hold, support', which
appears in Gk. θρόνος, 'seat, chair, throne', L.
firmus, 'strong'. See firm, adj., and cp. words
there referred to. For the ending see suff. -ic,
resp. also -al.
Derivative: therapeutical-ly, adv.

## therapeutics
therapeutics, п., that branch of medicine which
deals with the treatment and cure of disease. —
See prec. word and -ics.

## -therapy
-therapy, combining form meaning 'treatment,
cure'. Fr. Gk. θεραπεία, 'a waiting on, service,
attendance', fr. θεράπων. See therapeutic and
-y (representing Gk. -eicc).

## there
there, adv. — ME. thar, tker, fr. OE. par, pxr,
per, rel. to OFris. tker, OS. thar, ON. par, Dan.,
Swed. der, Du. daar, OHG. ddr, MHG. dar, da,
Goth, par, 'there', and cogn. with OI. tar-hi,
'then', fr. I.-E. *tar·, 'there', enlargement of
pron. base *to-, *ta-. See the, art., and cp. words
there referred to.

## thereabouts
thereabouts, thereabout, adv. — ME. ther aboute,
fr. OE. P&r abutaiib 'about that*. See there and
about.

## thereafter
thereafter, adv. — ME. tkerafter, fr. OE. pxr
sefter, 'after that'. See there and after.

## thereat
thereat, adv. — ME., fr. OE. pier &t, *there'. See
there and at.

## thereby
thereby, adv. — ME. therby, fr. OE. pierbig, 'by
that'. See there and by.

## therefor
therefor, adv. — ME. tkerfor, therfore, therefor,
therefore, 'for that'; ME. fore is a secondary
form οι for. See there and for and cp. next word.

## therefore
therefore, adv.— ME. therfor, etc. See prec. word.

## therefrom
therefrom, adv. — ME. tkerfrom. See there and
from. The orig. spelling was there from.

## therein
therein, adv. — ME. therin, fr. OE, pterin, fr.
pier, 'there', and in, 'in'. See there and in, prep.

## thereof
thereof, adv. — ME. therof fr. OE. pxr of, 'of
that'. See there and of.

## thereon
thereon, adv. — ME. theron, fr. OE. ргёг on, 'on
that'. See there and on.

## thereout
thereout, adv. — ME. theoute, fr. OE. pxrut,
pxrute, 'outside'. See there and out.

## thereover
thereover, adv. — ME. ther over, fr. OE. frairofer,
'over that'. See there and over.

## Theresa
Theresa, also Teresa, fem. PN. — F. Therese, fr.
L. Therasia, Theresia, which is prob. rel. to
Therasia, fr. Gk. Θηρασία, name of two islands
one near Sicily (now called Vulcanello) the
other near Crete (still called Θηρασία).

## thereto
thereto, adv. — ME. therto, fr. OE. pxrtd, 'to
that'. See there and to.

## thereunder
thereunder, adv. — ME. therunder, fr. OE. pxr·
under, 'under that'. See there and under.

## thereupon
thereupon, adv. — ME. ther upon, fr. OE. Peer
uppan. See there and upon.

## Thereva
Thereva, п., the type genus of the stiletto flies (en-
tomol.) — ModL., lit. 'hunter', fr. Gk. θηρεύειν,
'to hunt', fr. θήρ, 'beast'. See therio-.

## Therevidue
Therevidue, n. pi., a family of flies, the stiletto
flies (entomol.) — ModL., formed with suff.
-idae from prec. word.

## therewith
therewith, adv. — ME. therwith, fr. OE. ргёг wid,
p&rwid, 'with that'. See there and with.

## therewithal
therewithal, adv. — Compounded of there and

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:787 COLUMN:2 -->
withal.

## theri-
theri-, form of therio- before a vowel.

## theriac
theriac, п., an ancient antidote for poison. — L.
theriaca, fr. Gk. θηριακή, 'antidote' (for θηρια-
κή άντίδοσις), fem. of θηριακός, 'pertaining
to wild or poisonous animals', fr. θηρίον, 'beast',
dimin. of θήρ (see therio- and cp. treacle). The
name for antidote was coined by Andromachus,
a native of Crete and contemporary of Nero;
the antidote for snake poison, invented by him,
was composed of 61 various ingredients, the
most important of which was the dried flesh of
vipers, whence the name of the antidote θηρια-
κή (scil. άντίδοτος), lit. 'animal (antidote)'.

## therianthropic
therianthropic, adj., combining human and
animal form (as the centaur). — Formed with adj.
suff. -ic fr. Gk. θηριάνθρωπος, 'beast man', fr.
θηρίον, 'beast, animal', and άνθρωπος, 'man'.
See therio- and anthropo-.

## Theridiidae
Theridiidae, n. pi., a family of spiders (entomol.)
— ModL., formed with suff. -idae fr. Gk. θηρί-
δ:ον, dimin. of θηρίον, itself dimin. of θήρ,
'beast, animal'. See therio-.

## therio-
therio-, before a vowel theri-, combining form
meaning 'wild beast'. — Gk. θηρ^ο-, θηρι-, fr.
θηρίον, 'wild animal, beast, animal', formally a
dimin. of θήρ, of s.m., which is rel. to Lesbian
Gk. φήρ, of s.m., from I.-E. base ghwer-, 'wild,
wild animal', whence also L. ferus, 'wild'. See
fierce and cp. words there referred to. Cp. also
prec. word and the second element in Acera-
therium,Dinotherium, Megatherium, Nyctereutes,
Oenothera, paleothere.

## theriomorphic
theriomorphic, adj., having the form of an
animal. — Formed with adj. suff. -ic fr. Gk. θηριό-
μορφος, which is compounded of θηρίον,
'animal', and μορφή, 'form, shape'. See therio- and
morpho-.

## theriomorphous
theriomorphous, adj., theriomorphic. — See prec.
word and -morphous.

## therium
therium, combining form denoting a genus of
animals (conventionally mammals). — ModL., fr.
Gk. θηρίον, 'animal'. See therio-,

## therm
therm, п., British thermal unit {physics). — Gk.
θέρμη, 'heat', rel. to θερμός, 'warm', which
stands for *gwkermos, fr. I.-E. base *gwker-,
'warm'. See warm and cp. thermae, Thermidor,
thermion, thermo-, athermancy, diathermancy,
diathermic, hydrothermal, isothere, isotherm.

## therm-
therm-, form of thermo- before a vowel.

## thermae
thermae, n. pi., hot springs or baths. — L., fr.
Gk. θέρμαι, pi. of θέρμη, 'heat'. See prec.
word.

## thermal
thermal, adj., pertaining to thermae; pertaining
to heat. — Formed with adj. suff. -al fr. L.
thermae. See therm.

## thermantidote
thermantidote, п., an apparatus for cooling the
air. — Compounded of therm and antidote.

## thermesthesia
thermesthesia, thermaesthesia, п., sensitiveness to
heat (pkysiol.) — Compounded of therm and
esthesia.

## -thermia
-thermia, also -thermy, combining form
denoting; 1) the state of heat; 2) generation or
application of heat. — ModL. -thermia, formed
fr. Gk. θέρμη, 'heat', with L. suff. -ia. See
therm and -y (representing L. -ia).

## thermic
thermic, adj., pertaining to heat. — Formed with
adj. suff. -ic fr. Gk. θέρμη, 'heat'. See therm.

## Thermidor
Thermidor, п., the eleventh month (lasting fr.
July 19th to Aug. 17th) of the French
revolutionary calendar. — A word coined by Fabre
d'Eglantine in 1793 fr. Gk. θέρμη, 'heat', and
δώρον, 'gift'; see therm and donation.

## Tbermidorian
Tbermidorian, n. (French hist.) — F. Thermido-
rien, lit. 'pertaining to Thermidor*. See prec.
word and -ian.

## thermion
thermion, п., an electrically charged particle
emitted from an incandescent body (physics). —
Coined by the English physicist Sir Owen
Willans Richardson (1879-1959) fr. Gk. θέρμη,
'heat'. See therm and -ion.
Derivatives: thermion-ic, adj., thermionics (q.v.)

## thermionics
thermionics, n. pi., that branch of physics which
deals with the emission of electrons from heated
bodies. — See prec. word and -ics.

## thermit
thermit, п., a mixture of aluminum with an iron
oxide (trade mark) — G., formed fr. Gk. θέρμη,
'heat' (see therm) with suff. -it, fr. Gk. -ίτης

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:787 COLUMN:3 -->
(see subst. suff. -ite);so called because of the
great heat it produces when it is ignited.

## thermo-
thermo-, before a vowel therm·, combining form
meaning 'heat'. — Gk. θερμό-, θερμ-, fr.
θέρμη, 'heat'. See therm.

## thermobarometer
thermobarometer, п., a thermometer used for
measuring the altitude by determining the
boiling point of water. — Compounded of thermo-
and barometer.

## thermochemistry
thermochemistry, п., that branch of chemistry
which deals with the relation between heat and
chemical action. — Compounded of thermo-
and chemistry.

## thermocouple
thermocouple, п., a thermoelectric couple. —
Compounded of thermo- and couple.

## thermodynamics
thermodynamics, п., that branch of physics which
deals with the reaction between heat and
mechanical energy. — Compounded of thermo-
and dynamics.

## thermoelectric
thermoelectric, adj., pertaining to
thermoelectricity. — Compounded of thermo- and electric.
Derivatives: thermoelectric-al, adj., thermoelec-
tric-al-ly, adv.

## thermoelectricity
thermoelectricity, п., electricity produced by heat.
— Compounded of thermo- and electricity,

## thermoelectrumeter
thermoelectrumeter, п., an instrument for
measuring the power of an electric current by the
heat which it produces. — Compounded of
thermo- and electrometer.

## thermogenesis
thermogenesis, п., the production of heat, esp. in
the body. — Compounded of thermo- and
genesis.

## thermogenetic
thermogenetic, adj., pertaining to thermogenesis.
— Compounded of thermo- and genetic,

## thermogenic
thermogenic, adj., relating to the production of
heat. — Compounded of thermo- and -genie.

## thermogenous
thermogenous, adj., thermogenic. —
Compounded of thermo- and -genous.

## thermogram
thermogram, п., the record produced by a
thermograph. — Compounded of thermo- and Gk.
γράμμα, 'that which is written'. See -gram.

## thermograph
thermograph, п., a self-registering thermometer.
— Compounded of thermo- and Gk. -γράφος,
fr. γράφειν, 'to write". See -graph.

## thermolabile
thermolabile, adj., unstable when subjected to
moderate heat. — A hybrid coined fr. Gk.
θέρμη, 'heat', and L. labilis, 'unstable,
wavering'. See therm and labile and cp. thermostable.

## thermology
thermology, п., the study of heat. —
Compounded of thermo- and Gk. -λογία, fr.
-λόγος, One who speaks (in a certain manner);
one, who deals (with a certain topic)'. See -logy.

## thermolysis
thermolysis, п., 1) dissociation by heat (chem.)',
2) dispersion of heat from the body (pkysiol.) —
G. Thermolyse, coined by the German
pharmacist Karl Friedrich Mohr (1806-79) fr. thermo-
and Gk. λύσίς, 'a loosing, a setting free;
dissolution', fr. λύειν, 'to loose, set free; to
dissolve'. See lysis,

## thermometer
thermometer, n. — F. thermometre, coined by the
Jesuit Father Leurechon in 1624 fr. Gk. θέρμη,
'heat', and μέτρου, 'measure'. See therm and
meter, 'poetical rhythm*.

## thermometry
thermometry, п., the measurement of heat. —
Compounded of thermo- and Gk. -μετρία, 'a
measuring of. See -metry.
Derivatives: thermometr-ic, thermometr-ic-alt
adjs., tkermometr-ic-al-fy, adv.

## thermophile
thermophile, thermophilic, adj., 'heat loving' (said
of certain bacteria). — Compounded of thermo-
and Gk. φίλος, 'friend'. See philo-.

## thermophore
thermophore, п., an apparatus for conveying heat.
— Gk. θερμοφόρος, 'boiler', compounded of
θέρμη, 'heat', and -φόρος, 'carrying'. See
therm and -phore.

## thermopile
thermopile, п., a thermoelectric battery. — A
hybrid coined fr. Gk. θέρμη, 'heat', and L. pila,
'pillar'. See therm and pile, 'heap'.

## thermoplegia
thermoplegia, п., a heatstroke. — Compounded
of thermo- and Gk. πληγή, 'blow, stroke',
which is cogn. with L. plaga, 'stroke, wound'.
See plagae and 1st -ia.

## thermos bottle
thermos bottle, thermos flask. — Fr. Gk. θερμός,
'warm, hot', which is rel. to θέρμη, 'heat'. See
therm.

## thermoscope
thermoscope, п., an instrument for indicating
differences in temperature without measuring
them in degrees. — ModL. thermoscopium,

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:788 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: 761 | THING -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:788 COLUMN:1 -->
compounded of thermo- and Gk. -σκόπιον, fr.
σκοπεΐν, 'to look at, examine*. See -scope.
Derivatives: thermoscop-ic, thermoscop-ic-al,
adjs.

## thermostable
thermostable, adj., stable when subjected to a
moderate degree of heat. — A hybrid coined fr.
Gk. θέρμη, 'heat', and L. stabilis, 'stable'. See
therm and stable, adj., and cp. thermolabile.

## thermostat
thermostat, п., a device for the automatic
regulation of temperature. — Compounded of thermo-
and Gk. στατός, 'placed, standing'. See static
and cp. aerostat and words there referred to.
Derivative: thermostat-ic, adj.

## thermostatics
thermostatics, п., the science that treats of the
equilibrium of heat. — See prec. word and -ics.

## thermotuxic
thermotuxic, adj., pertaining to thermotaxis. —
See next word and adj. suff. -fc.

## thermotaxis
thermotaxis, п., the regulation of bodily heat
(pkysiol.) — ModL., compounded of thermo-
and Gk. τάξις, 'arrangement'. See taxis.

## thermotensile
thermotensile, adj., pertaining to tensile force as
affected by changes in temperature. — A hybrid
coined fr. Gk. θέρμη, 'heat' (see therm), and
tenslie (q.v.), a word of Latin origin.

## thermotherapy
thermotherapy, п., the treatment of disease by
heat. — Compounded of thermo- and -therapy.

## thermotic
thermotic, adj., pertaining to heat. — Gk. θερμω-
τικός, fr. θερμοϋν, 'to make hot', fr. θερμός,
'hot'. See therm and -otic.

## thermotks
thermotks, п., the science of heat. — See prec.
word and -ics.

## thermotropic
thermotropic, adj., having theproperty of
thermotropism. — See next word and adj. suff. -ic.

## thermotropism
thermotropism, п., property of an organism of
turning toward, or away from, heat (biol.) —
Compounded of thermo- and tropism.

## -thermy
-thermy, combining form. — See -thermia.

## thero-
thero-, before a vowel ther-, combining form
meaning 'wild animal, beast'. — Gk. θηρο-,
θηρ-, fr. θήρ, gen. θηρός, 'wild animal, beast,
animal'. See therio-.

## theroid
theroid, adj., resembling a beast. — Compounded
of ther- and Gk. -οειδής, 'like', fr. εϊδος, 'form,
shape'. See -oid.

## therology
therology, п., the study of mammals, mammalogy
— Compounded of there- and Gk. -λογία, fr.
-λόγος, 'one who speaks (in a certain manner);
one who deals (with a certain topic)'. See -logy.

## Theropoda
Theropoda, n. pi., a suborder of carnivorous
dinosaurs (paleontol.) — ModL., compounded of
thero- and -poda.

## theropodous
theropodous, adj., pertaining to the Theropoda.
— See prec. word and -ous.

## thersitical
thersitical, adj., pertaining to, or resembling,
Thersites; scurrilous. — Formed with the suffix
-ical fr. L. Tkersites, fr. Gk. Θερσΐτης, name
of the ugliest of the Greeks before Troy, a man
notorious for his scurrility. The name lit. means
'bold', esp. 'bold of speech' (cp. θερσιεπής,
'bold of speech*), fr. θέρσος, Aeol. equivalent
of Ion., Old Att. θάρσος, Att. θάρρος,
'courage, audacity', and rel. to θαρσύς, θρασύς,
'bold, audacious*, θαρσεΐν, Att. θαρρεΐν, 'to be
bold', fr. I.-E. base *dhars-, 'to dare, be
courageous'. See dare and cp. thrasonical. For the
ending of the name Θερσΐτης see subst. suff. -ite.

## thesaurus
thesaurus, п., a treasury; a treasury of words,
lexicon. — L., fr. Gk. θησαυρός, 'treasure, treasure-
house', a compound whose first element prob.
derives fr. θη-, 'the stem of τιθέναι, to place,
put' (see theme); the second element is of
uncertain origin. *Cp. treasure.

## these
these, demonstr. pron. — ME. thise, these, fr.
OE. pies, 'these', a collateral form of pas, pi. of
pes, 'this'. See this. OE. pas survives in E. those
(q.v.)

## Theseus
Theseus, п., the most famous hero of Attica, son
of Aegeus {Greek mythol.) — L., fr. Gk.
Θησεύς, which is of unknown etymology.

## thesis
thesis, n. — L., fr. Gk. θέσις, 'a placing, setting*,
fr. I.-E. *dhe-ti-, whence also OI. -{d)kitih (only
in compounds), 'a placing', Late L. con-diti-o,
'a founding' (fr. L. conditus, pp. of condere, 'to
found'). Gk. θέσις is verbal n. of τιθέναι, 'to
put, place, set'. See theme and cp. deed. Cp. also
next word.

## thesmothete
thesmothete, п., a legislator, orig. any of the six
inferior archons in Athens (Greek antiq.) — Gk.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:788 COLUMN:2 -->
θεσμοθέτης, compounded of θεσμός, 'that
which is laid down, law', and θέτης, 'one who
places'. Both θεσμός (Dor. τεθμός, Laconic,
Argive and Locrian θεθμός) and θέτης derive
from the stem of τιθέναι, 'to put, place, set'.
See theme and cp. prec. word.

## Thespesia
Thespesia, п., a genus of plants of the mallow
family (bot.)— ModL., fr. Gk. θεσπέσιος,
'divinely sounding, divine'. See next word. For the
ending see 1st-suff. -ia.

## Thespian
Thespian, adj., pertaining to Thespis; pertaining
to the drama. — Formed fr. L. Thespis, fr. Gk.
Θέσπις, the founder of the Greek drama. The
name derives fr. θέσπις, 'inspired by the gods',
which is prob. a short form for θεσπέσιος,
'divinely sounding, divine', fr. *θέσ-σπετος,
compounded of θεσ-, lit. 'divinely uttered', fr.
*θεσ-, 'divine' and *σπέτος, 'uttered' (cp.
ά-σπετος, 'unspeakable, unutterable'). For the
first element see theo-. The second element
derives fr. I.-E. base *seqw-, 'to say'; see say, v.
Cp. prec. word. For the ending see suff. -ian.

## theta
theta, п., name of the 8th letter of the Greek
alphabet. — Gk. θητα, fr. Heb. teth; see teth. The
α was added because a Greek word cannot end
with a τ; cp. alpha and words there referred to.

## the tic
the tic, adj. positive. — Gk. θετικός, 'fit for
placing', fr. θετός, 'placed, affirmative, positive',
verbal adj. of τιθέναι, 'to place, put, set'. See
theme and adj. suff. -ic.

## thcurgic
thcurgic, theurgical, adj., magical. — Late L.
theurgicus, fr. Gk. θεουργικός, fr. θεουργία.
See theurgy and adj. suff. -ic, resp. also -al.

## theurgist
theurgist, n., a magician. — See next word and -ist.

## theurgy
theurgy, п., magic. — Late L. theurgia, fr. Gk.
θεουργία, 'divine work', fr. θεουργός, 'divine
worker', which is compounded of θεός, gen.
θεοΰ, 'god', and the base of έργον, 'work'. See
1st theism and work and cp. ergon. For the
ending see suff. -y (representing Gk. -ία).

## thews
thews, n. pi., bodily strength; vigor. — ME.
thewes, 'habits, manners', fr. OE. peaw,
'custom, usage, habit', pi. peawas, 'manners', rel. to
OS. thau, 'custom', OHG. thau, dau, 'discipline';
of uncertain origin. It is perh. cogn. with L. tue-
ri, 'to look at, regard, consider'; see tuition.
Derivatives: thew-ed, thew-less, thew-y, adjs.

## they
they, pron. of the 3rd person, nom. pi. — ME.
thei, thai, fr. ON. peir, 'they', orig. nom. pi.
masc. of ία, su, pat, 'that'. See the, art., and cp.
them, their.

## thi-
thi-, form of thio- before a vowel.

## thlaminase
thlaminase, п., an enzyme that destroys thiamine
(biochem.) — Formed from next word with suff.
-ase.

## thiamine
thiamine, thiamin, п., a crystalline compound
C12H17ON4SCl (ckem.) — Compounded of
thio- and amin(e).

## thiazine
thiazine, thiazin, п., any of a class of ring
compounds containing one sulfur atom and one
nitrogen atom and four atoms of carbon
(biochem.) — Compounded of thio-, -az and -in(e).

## thiasus
thiasus, п., a religious brotherhood (Greek antiq.)
— L., fr. Gk. θίασος, 'religious guild,
confraternity', which is of uncertain origin.

## thiazole
thiazole, thiazol, п., a colorless liquid C3H3NS
(ckem.) — Compounded of thio- and azole.

## thick
thick, adj. — ME. thicke, thikke, fr. OE. piece,
rel. to OS. thikki, ON. pykkr, pjukkr, piokkr,
Dan. tykt Swed. tjock, Norw. tjukk, OFris.
thikke, MDu. dicke, Du. dik, OHG. dicki, dichi,
'thick', dicco, 'often', MHG. dicke, G. dick,
'thick*, fr. I.-E. base *tegu-, whence also Olr.
tiug, 'thick', W., Co. tew, Bret, teo, of s.m.
Derivatives: thick, п., adv. and v., thick-en, tr.
and intr. v., thick-en-er, п., thick-en-ing, п.,
thick-et, п., thick-et-ed, adj., thick-et-y, adj.,
thick-ness, п., thick-ish, thick-ly, adjs.,
thickness, n. and tr. v., thick-ness-ing, n.

## thief
thief, n. — ME. theef, fr. OE. peof, rel. to OS.
thiof, ON. pjofr, Dan. tyv, Swed. tjuj, Norw.
tjuv, OFris. thiaf, MDu., Du. die/, OHG. thiob,
diob, diub, MHG. diep, diup, G. Dieb, Goth.

## piufs
piufs, and possibly cogn. with Lith. tupiii, tupti,
'to squat oneself down', tupiii, tupeti, 'to crouch,
squat'. Cp. theft and the last element in infang-
thief, outfangthief.
Derivatives: thieve (q.v.), thievery (q.v.),

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:788 COLUMN:3 -->
thieving, n. and adj., thiev-isb, adj., thiev-ish-ly, adv.,
thiev-ish-ness, n.

## thieve
thieve, intr. v., to steal. — OE. peofian, fr. peof,
'thief. See thief.

## thievery
thievery, n. — Formed fr. E. thief with suff. -ery.

## thigh
thigh, n. — ME. theh, thih, thigh, fr. OE. peoh,
pioh, rel. to ON. pfo, 'thigh, rump', OFris.
thiach, ODu. thio, Du. dij, OHG. dioh, 'thigh',
fr. I.-E. base *tu-, *teu-, 'to swell', whence also
Olr. ton, 'rump', W. tin, of s.m., OSlav. tyjo,
tyti, 'to become fat', tuku, 'fat', Lith. tauka,
'fat', taukas, 'pieces of fat', tunku, tiikti, 'to
become fat', Lett, tukt, 'to swell', L. tumere, 'to
swell'. See tumid and cp. words there referred to.
Derivative: thigh-ed, adj.

## thigino-
thigino-, combining form meaning 'touch'. — Gk.
θιγμο-, fr. θίγμα, 'touch', which is rel. to
θιγγάνειν (aor. θιγεϊν), 'to touch', fr. I.-E. base
*dheigh-, 'to form out of clay, to knead, form'.
See dough and words there referred to and cp.
esp. the first element in thixotropy.

## thigmotropism
thigmotropism, п., the property in an organism of
turning under the influence of contact {biol.) —
Compounded of thigmo- and tropism.

## thill
thill, п., the shaft of a vehicle. — ME. thille, fr.
OE. pille, plank', which is rel. to OE. pel,
'plank', ΟΝ. ρ Hi, pil, 'plank, thwart', MDu.
dele, Du. deel, OHG. dil, dilo, dilla, MHG. dil,
dille, G. Diele, 'deal, board, plank', fr. I.-E. base
*tela-, *tla-, 'something flat', whence also L. tel-
lus, 'earth'. See tellurian and cp. deal, 'plank'.

## thimble
thimble, n. — ME. thimbel, fr. OE. ppmel, formed
fr. puma, 'thumb', with suff. -el. See thumb and
instrumental suff. -ie.
Derivative: thimbl-ed, adj.

## thimblerig
thimblerig, п., a swindling game. —
Compounded of thimble and rig, 'trick'.
Derivatives: thimblerig, intr. v., thimblerigg-er,^
п., thimblerigg-ing, n.

## thin
thin, adj. — ME. thinne, fr. OE. pynne, rel. to OS.
thunni, ON. punnr, Swed. lunn, Norw. tunn,
tynn, Dan. tynd, MDu. dunne, Du. dun, OFris.
thenne, OHG. thunni, dunni, MHG. dunne, G.
dunn, 'thin', orig. 'stretched out*, and to OE.
penian, ON. penja, OHG., MHG. dennen, de-
nen, G. dehnen, Goth, uf-panjan, 'to stretch,
extend', fr. I.-E. base *ten-, 'to stretch, extend',
whence also OI. taniih (fern, tanvi), tanukah,
'thin, tender', lit. 'stretched out', Homeric Gk.
ταναός, 'stretched out, long', Gk. τανυ-,
'stretched out, long' (as in τανύγλωσσος, 'long-
tongued'), L. tenuis, 'thin, slender*, tenus, 'cord,
snare', OSlav. tinuku, tiniku, 'thin', dial. Lith.
tenvas, Lett, tiews, 'slender', Olr. tan{a)e, Co.
tanow, W. teneu, MBret. tanau, 'thin*. See tend,
'to move in a certain direction', and cp. tennis.
Derivatives: thin, tr. and intr. v., thin-ly, adv.,
thin-ness, n.

## thine
thine, possessive pron. — ME. thin, fr. OE. pin,
orig. gen. of рй, 'thou', rel. to OS., OFris. thin,
'thy, thine', ON. pinn, 'thy, thine', pin, 'of thee',
Dan., Swed. din, MDu., Du. dijn, OHG. thin,
din, MHG. din, G. dein, Goth, peins, 'thy, thine',
peina, Of thee'. All these words stand for I.-E.
*t(w)ei-no-s, and are cogn. with L, tuus (for
*twei-os), 'thy, thine', fr. I.-E. base *tu-, 'thou,
thee'; see thou and cp. thee. In ME., the final η
was dropped before a word beginning with a
consonant and so arose the form thy (q.v.)

## thing
thing, п., an inanimate object. — ME., fr. OE.
ping, 'condition, state, meeting, court of justice',
rel. to pingian, 'to intercede, plead, arrange',
OS., OFris. thing, ON. ping, 'assembly', MDu.
dine, Du. ding, OHG. thing, ding, MHG. dine,
'assembly', G. Ding, 'thing'. All these words
stand for l.-E. *tenkos, fr. base *ten-, 'to extend
(in space or in time)', and orig. denoted
'meeting at a fixed time', whence developed the
meanings 'affairs, things, thing'. Cp. Goth, peihs,
'time', orig. 'assembly taking place at a fixed
time', fr. I.-E. *tengko-, fr. base *ten-. See tend,
'to move in a certain direction', and cp. thing,
'assembly', and words there referred to. Cp. also
temporal, 'pertaining to time'.
Derivative: tking-y, adj.

## thing
thing, ting, п., a legislative assembly in the
Scandinavian countries. — ON. ping (whence also
Norw. thing, ting, Swed. ting, 'assembly'); de-

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:789 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: THINGAMY | 762 -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:789 COLUMN:1 -->
rivatively identical with thing, 'an object' (q.v.)
Cp. the first element in Tynwald and the second
element in husting, storting.

## thingamy
thingamy, Uiinguinbub, thingummy, п., a thing. —
Jocose formations of thing, 'an object*.

## think
think, intr. v., to seem (obsol.) — ME. thinken, fr.
OE. pyncan, rel. to OS. thunkian, ON. pykkja,
Swed. tycka, OFris. thinka, OHG. dunchen,
MHG. dunken, dunken, G. dunken, Goth.
pugkjan, 'to seem', and prob. cogn. with L. ton-
gere, 'to know', Praenestine tongirio,
'knowledge'. See next word and cp. methinks.

## think
think, intr. and tr. v., to reflect. — A blend of
ME. thinken, 'to seem', and thenken, 'to think'.
This latter comes fr. OE. pencan, causative to
pyncan, 'to seem', hence prop, means 'to cause
to seem' (see prec. word), and is rel. to ON.
pekkja, 'to perceive, know', Dan. tsnke, Swed.
tdnka, OS. thenkian, OFris. rkenza, Du. denken,
OHG. denchen, MHG., G. denken, Goth, pagk-
jan, 'to think*. Cp. thank.
Derivatives: thinkable, adj., ihink-er, п.,
thinking, n. and adj., thinkable-ness, п., thinkabl-y,
adv., think-ing-ly, adv.

## thio-
thio-, before a vowel thi-, combining form used
in the sense of'containing sulfur' (ckem.) — Gk.
&ειο-, &ει-, fr. &εΐον, Homeric Gk. biciov,
'brimstone', for **ίέσ-(ε)ιον, lit. 'that which
smokes', from I.-E. base *dhewes-, *dkwes-, 'to
breathe, smoke*. Base *dhewes-, *dkwes-, is an
enlargement of base *dheu-, 'to fly about like
dust, to smoke, whirl, shake, be scattered,
vanish', whence OI. dhunoti, dkuvdti, 'shakes,
moves', Gk. &υειν, 'to sacrifice', prop, 'to cause
to smoke', &ϋμα, 'sacrifice', &ύμον, also θύμος,
'thyme', θύμιαν, 'to burn so as to produce
smoke', θυμίαμα, 'incense', θύος, 'burned
sacrifice' (whence L. thus, gen. tkuris,
'frankincense'), *ϋμός, 'spirit, breath, life, mind, soul,
desire, courage, anger', &υειν, &υιάζειν, 'to
rage'. Cp. thanato-, Thuja, thurible, Thyiad,
thyine, thyme, thysano-, tumble, typhlo-, typhus,
the first element in Thymelaeceae and the second
element in athymia, barythymia. Cp. also deaf
and words there referred to, and dull, and words
there referred to. Cp. also deer, dizzy, down,
'soft plumage', down, 'hill', dust, feral, 'funereal',
fume, fury, hag, 'a witch', and the first element
in Dukhobors.

## thioacid
thioacid, п., an acid in which oxygen is replaced
by sulfur (ckem.) — A hybrid coined fr. Gk.
&εΐον, 'brimstone' (see thio-), and acid, a word
of Latin origin.

## Thiobacillus
Thiobacillus, п., a genus of bacteria {bacterial.) —
A ModL. hybrid coined fr. Gk. *εΐον,
'brimstone', and Late L. bacillus, *a little staff'. See
thio- and bacillus.

## Thiobacteria
Thiobacteria, n. pi., an order of bacteria (bacter-
iol.) — Compounded of thio- and bacteria.

## thiocyanic
thiocyanic, adj., pertaining to the acid HSCN
(chem.) — Compounded of thio- and cyanic.

## thionic
thionic, adj., pertaining to sulfur (chem.) —
Formed with adj. suff. -ic fr. Gk. *εΐον, 'brimstone'.
See thio-.

## thiophene
thiophene, thiophen, п., a colorless liquid, C4H4S
(chem.) — Compounded of thio- the initial of
phenyl and suff. -ene, resp. -en.
Derivative: thiophen-ic, adj.

## thiophenoi
thiophenoi, п., a colorless liquid CeH5SH (chem.)
— Compounded of thio- and phenol,

## thiosinamine
thiosinamine, thiosinamin, п., a colorless
crystalline compound, CjHjNjS (chem.) —
Compounded of thio-, the first three letters of Gk.
σίναπι, 'mustard' (see sinapism), and amine.

## thiosalfate
thiosalfate, п., a salt of thiosulfuric acid (chem.)
— See prec. word and chem. suff. -ate.

## thiosulfuric
thiosulfuric, adj., pertaining to the acid HjS203
(chem.) — A hybrid coined fr. Gk. *εΐον,
'brimstone', and sulfuric, a word of Latin origin. See
thio-, sulfur and -ic. H2S20, is called thiosulfuric
acid because it may be regarded as a sulfuric
acid in which one oxygen atom is replaced by
sulfur (=■ thio-).

## third
third, adj. — ME. tkirde, metathesis of ME.
ihridda, fr. OE. bridda, rel. to OS. thriddio, ON.
pride, pridi, Dan. tredie, Swed. tredje, OFris.
tkredda, Du. derde, OHG. drittio, dritto, MHG.,
G. driite, Goth, pridja, and cogn. with OI.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:789 COLUMN:2 -->
trttyah, Avestic &ritya-, Toch. A trit, В trite,
trice, Gk. τρίτος, Aeol. τέρτος, Alb. tretc, L.
tertius (for *tritios), OSlav. tretijt, Lith. treoias,
Lett, tresais, OPruss. tints, tirts, Oir. triss, W.
■trydyddand rel. to OE. pri, etc., 'three'. See three
and cp. tercet, tertiary, tierce, trito-. Cp. also
riding, 'administrative district'.
Derivatives: third, п., third-ling, п., tkird-ly,
adv.

## thirl
thirl, п., a hole, aperture. — ME., fr. OE. pyrel.
See thrill.

## thirl
thirl, tr. and intr. v., to pierce, thrill (Engl, dial.)
— ME. thirlen, fr. OE. pyrlian, fr. pyrel. See
prec. word.

## thirl
thirl, tr. v., to restrict. — Related to thrall. The
orig. meaning of thirl was 'to reduce to slavery'.

## thirst
thirst, n. — ME. thirst, fr. earlier thurst, fr. OE.
purst, rel. OS. thurst, ON. porsti, Dan. terst,
Swed. torst, MDu., Du. dorst, OHG., MHG.,
G. durst, Goth, paurstei, fr. L-E. base *trs-, 'to
be dry', whence also OL. torrus (for *torsus),
'dry', L. torrlre, 'to parch, roast', terra (for
*tersa-), 'earth'. See terra and cp. words there
referred to.

## thirst
thirst, intr. v. — ME. thirsten, fr. OE. pyrstan, fr.
purst, 'thirst*. Cp. ON. pyrsta (fr. pursti) and
OHG. dursten, MHG. dursten, dursten, G. dur-
sten (fr. OHG., MHG., G. durst), 'to thirst', and
see thirst, n.
Derivatives: thirst-er, п., thrist-ing, adj. and п.,
tkirst-ing-ly, adv., thirsty (q.v.)

## thirsty
thirsty, adj. — ME., fr. OE. pyrstig, fr. pyrst. Cp.
G. durstig, 'thirsty', fr. Durst, 'thirst', and see
thirst, п., and -y (representing OE. -ig).

## thirteen
thirteen, adj. and n. — Metathesis of ME. thret-
tene, fr. OE. preotyne, preotene, which was
formed fr. preo, 'three', with suff. -tyne, -tene, '-teen'
(see three and -teen); rel. to OS. thriutein, tkru-
tein, ON. prettdn, Dan. tretten, Swed. tretton,
OFris. thretten, Du. dertien, OHG. drizehan,
MHG. drizehen, G. dreizehn, 'thirteen'.

## thirteenth
thirteenth, adj. and n. — Formed fr. thirteen with
numeral suff. -th, on the analogy of tenth. Cp.
ME. threttethe, fr. OE. preoteoda, 'thirteenth',
which was formed fr. preotyne, 'thirteen', on the
analogy of teoda, 'tenth'; see tithe. Cp. also ON.
prettande, Dan. trettende, Swed. trettonde,
OFris. threttinde, Du. dertiende, OHG. dritto-
zehanto, G. dreizehnte, 'thirteenth'.

## thirtieth
thirtieth, adj. and n. — Formed fr. thirty with
numeral suff. -th on the analogy of tenth. Cp.
OE. pritigoda, 'thirtieth', which was formed fr.
pritig, 'thirty'. Cp. also ON. pritugande, later
pritugti, 'thirtieth'.

## thirty
thirty, adj. and n. — Metathesis fr. ME. thritty,
therty, fr. OE. pritig, prittig, which was formed
fr. pri, 'three', with -tig, 'ten' (see three and -ty,
suff. denoting multiples of ten); rel. to OS.
thritig, ON. prjatigi, prjatiu, Swed. trettio, Dan.
tredive, OFris. thritich, Du. dertig, OHG. driz-
zug, MHG. drizec, G. dreifiig, 'thirty', Goth.
preis pig'tus, 'three tens'.

## this
this, demonstr. pron. and adj. — ME. thes, this,
fr. OE. pes, pes, (masc), peos, pios, (fern.), pis
(neut.), rel. to OS. these, ON. pessi, MDu. dese,
Du. deze, OFris. this (fern, thius, neut. thit),
OHG. deser (fem. desiu, neut. diz), MHG. diser
(fern, disiu, neut. ditz), G. dieser; formed fr. the
l.-E. demonstr. bases *to-, *ta- and *so-, *sa-.
See the, art., and cp. that, these, those.

## thisness
thisness, п., quality of being this. — Formed fr.
this with suff. -ness.

## thistie
thistie, n. — ME. thistil, fr. OE. pistel, rel. to OS.
thistil, ON. pistil/, Swed., Norw. tistel, Dan.
tidsel, MDu. destel, distel, diestel, Du. distel,'
OHG. distil, MHG., G. distel, fr. Teut. *pihsti-
la-, a dimin. formation fr. I.-E. base *steig-, 'to
prick, stick, pierce', whence 01. tiktah, 'sharp',
Gk. στίζειν, 'to prick'. See stick, 'to pierce', and
cp. words there referred to.
Derivatives: thistle, tr. and intr. v., thistl-ed, adj.,
thistl-y, adj.

## thither
thither, adv. — ME. thider, thither, fr. OE. pider,
pyder, pseder, rel. to ON. padra, 'there', Goth.
papro, 'thence', formed fr. Teut. demonstrative
base *pa- (corresponding to I.-E. *to-, *ta-),
with the comparative sufT. -ther (q.v.) Set the,
art., and cp. hither.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:789 COLUMN:3 -->
Derivative: thither, adj.

## thixle
thixle, п., ax, hatchet (dial.) — ME. tkixel, rel. to
ON. pexla, Dan. txngsel, Norw. teksel, MLG.
dessele, MDu. dissel, OHG. dehsala, MHG.
dehsel, G. Deichsel, 'ax, hatchet'; formed with
instrumental suff. -le fr. I.-E. base *tekp-, 'to
prepare, build', whence also L. texere, 'to weave,
plait, fit together'. See text and cp. words there
referred to.

## thixotropy
thixotropy, п., the property of becoming fluid
when shaken, as shown by some gels. — Lit.
'turning through touch', fr. Gk. ίΗξις, 'a touch',
and -τροπή, -τροπία, fr. τροπή, 'a turn,
turning'. Gk. θίξις derives fr. *ιγ-, the stem of
ίΗγγάνειν (aor. ίΗγεϊν), 'to touch', whence also
&ίγμα, 'touch'. See thigmo- and -tropy and cp.
thigmotropism.

## Thlaspi
Thlaspi, п., a genus of cresses, the pennycress
(bot.) — L., "a kind of cress', fr. Gk. &λάσπις,
fr. *λαν, 'to crush'; so called in allusion to the
flattened pod. Gk. *λ5ν is prob. cogn. with
Czech dlasmati, 'to press', OI. dhfsad-, 'rock,
millstone'. Cp. next word.

## thlipsis
thlipsis, п., compression of blood vessels (med.)
— Medical L., fr. Gk. *λΐψις, 'pressure',
formed from the stem of &λΐβείν, *to press, crush',
which is a blend of φλίβειν, 'to press, crush',
and θλαν, of s.m. Gk. φλΐβειν is cogn. with L.
fligere, 'to strike'. See afflict and cp. words there
referred to. For the etymology of*XSv see prec.
word.

## thole
thole, tr. v., to endure (archaic or dial.) — ME.
tholien, tholen, fr. OE. polian, 'to endure, suffer',
rel. to OS. tholon, ON. pola, Dan. taale, Swed.
tula, OFris. tholia, OHG. dolen, Goth, pulan, 'to
suffer' and to OHG. gidult, MHG. gedult, G.
Geduld, 'patience' (whence—with back
formation—OHG., MHG. dulten, G. dulden, 'to
suffer, endure'), fr. I.-E. base *tel-, *tol-, *tl-,
'to bear, carry, endure, suffer', whence also Gk.
τλήναι, 'to suffer, endure', L. tollere, 'to lift up,
raise', tolerdre, 'to bear, support'. See tolerate
and cp. words there referred to.

## thole
thole, tholepin, n.„peg in the gunwale of a boat.
— ME. tholle, fr. OE. pol, poll, 'oarpeg,
rowlock', rel. to ON. pollr, OFris. tholl, MLG.
dolle, Du. dot, G. Dolle, 'thole', G. Dollfufi,
'clubfoot', and cogn. with Gk. τύλος, 'nail, bolt
(used in shipbuilding)', L. tumidus, 'swollen,
protuberant', fr. l.-E. base *tu-, 'to swell'. See
tumid and cp. words there referred to.

## Thomas
Thomas, masc. PN. — Eccles. L., fr. Gk. Θωμάς,
lit. 'twin', fr. Syr. toma, 'twin', which is rel. to
Aram, foma, Heb. t от, Akkad. Ыати, ta'·
umu, Arab. tauOm, 'twin'. All these words are
prob. derivatives of the Semitic base w-a-m, 'to
tally'. Cp. Arab, wa'ama, 'it tallied'. In keeping
with the original meaning of the name, Thomas
is three times referred to in John's Gospel as
6 λεγόμενος Δίδυμος (Thomas, called 'theTwin').

## Thomism
Thomism, n. — Lit. 'doctrine of Thomas', formed
from the name of Thomas Aquinas (1225-74)
and suff. -ism.

## Thomist
Thomist, п., an adherent of Thomism. — See
Thomism and -ist.
Derivatives: Thomist, Thomist-ic, adjs.

## Thomomys
Thomomys, п., a genus of rodents (zool.) —
ModL., compounded of Gk. *ωμός, 'heap',
and μυς, 'mouse'. Gk. *ωμός stands in grada-
tional relationship to *έμις, 'right, law, decree'.
See Them's. For the etymology of μΰς see myo-,
mouse.

## thomsenolite
thomsenolite, п., a synonym of pachnolite
(mineral.) — Named after the Danish chemist Hans
Peter JSrgen Julius Thomsen (1826-1909). For
the ending see combining form -ilte.

## thomsonite
thomsonite, п., a hydrous silicate of aluminum,
calcium and sodium (mineral.) — Named after
the Scottish chemist Thomas Thomson (1773-
1852). For the ending see subst. suff. -Ite.

## thong
thong, п., a strip of leather. — ME. thwong, thong,
fr. OE. pwang, pwong, rel. to ON. pvengr, 'thong,
Iatchet', and to OE. twengan, 'to pinch, squeeze'.
See twinge.

## Thor
Thor, п., the Scandinavian god of thunder. —
ON. porr, fr. earlier *punroz, rel. to OE. punor,
'thunder'. See thunder, n. and cp. Thursday.

## thorac-
thorac-, form of thoraco- before a vowel.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:790 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: 763 | THRICE -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:790 COLUMN:1 -->

## thoracic
thoracic, adj., pertaining to, or connected with,
the thorax. — Formed with adj. stiff", -ic fr. L.
thorax, gen. thoracis. See thorax.

## thoraco-
thoraco-, before a vowel thorac-, combining form
denoting the thorax. — Gk. θωρακο-, θωρακ-,
fr. θώρδϊξ, gen. θώρακος. See next word.

## thorax
thorax, п., part of the body between the neck and
the abdomen (anat.) — Gk. θώραξ, gen.
θώρακος, 'breastplate, breast, chest', of uncertain
origin. It is perh. cogn. with OI. dhdrdyati,
'holds', from I.-E. base *dher-, *dkere-, 'to
hold", whence also Gk. θρόνος, 'seat, chair,
throne', L.firmus, 'fast, firm'. See firm, adj., and
cp. therapeutic, throne. Cp. also mesothorax.

## thoria
thoria, п., thorium dioxide TH02 {ckem.) —
ModL., coined by the Swedish chemist J6ns
Jakob Berzelius (1779-1848) in 1828 fr. Thor,
name of the Scand. god of thunder, and 1st suff*.
-ia. See Thor.

## thorianite
thorianite, n. {mineral) — Formed fr. thorium
with surf, -an and subst. suff. -ite.

## thorite
thorite, n. {mineral.) — Swed. thorit, coined fr.
Thor and suff. -it, representing the Greek suff.
-ϊτης; see subst. suff. -ite.

## thorium
thorium, n. — ModL. See thoria and 2nd -ium.

## thorn
thorn, n. — ME., fr. OE. porn, 'thorn,
prickle', rel. to OS., OFris. thorn, ON. porn, Du.
doom, OHG. thorn, later dorn, MHG., G. dorn,
Goth, paurnus, fr. I.-E. base *ter-, 'to pierce*,
whence also OI. tfnam, 'blade of grass', Gk.
τέρναξ, gen. τέρνακος, 'stalk of the cactus',
OSlav. trunu, 'thorn*, Ir. trainln, 'a little blade
of grass*. See throw and cp. the first element in
turbot.
Derivatives: thorn, tr. v., thorn-ed, adj., thorn-
less, adj., thorn-y, adj.

## thorough
thorough, adj. — ME. thorugh, fr. OE. puruh, a
var. of park. See through.
Derivatives: thorough-ly, adv., thorough-ness,
n.

## thorp
thorp, also thorpe, п., village; hamlet (now chiefly
in place names). — ME. thorp, throp, fr. OE.
porp, prop, rel. to OS. thorp, tharp, ON. porp,
'village', OFris. thorp, tkerp, MDu., Du. dorp,
OHG. thorf, later dorf, MHG., G. dorf 'village',
Goth, paiirp, 'field*, prob. fr. I.-E. base *treb-,
'to build', whence also Oscan triibum (ace),
'house', Umbr. trebeit, 'he stays, dwells, lives',
Lith. troba, 'a building*, Lett, traba, of s.m.,
OW. treb, 'house, dwelling', Olr. a-treba, 'he
possesses, dwells', Ir. treb, 'residence*, OBret.
treb, W. tref, 'a dwelling', Gk. τέραμνα (for
*ter bno-), assimil. form τέρεμνα, 'house,
dwelling place', L. trabs (gen. trabis), 'beam, timber*,
taberna, 'hut, booth'. Cp. tabernacle, tavern,
trabea, trabecula, trave, troop, troppo.

## thorrveitite
thorrveitite, п., a scandium yttrium silicate
{mineral.) — Named after Olaus Thortveit of
Iceland. For the ending see subst. suff. -ite.

## Thos
Thos, п., a genus of digitigrade Carnivora, the
jackal {zool.) — L. thos, fr. Gk. θώς (for
""θω/ός), 'Jackal', which is of uncertain origin.
It possibly stands in gradational relationship to
Gk. θαΰνος, 'wild beast*. See fauna.

## those
those, pron. — ME. thos, those,, fr. OE. pas, plural
of pes, 'this'; see this. Accordingly those is
derivatively a collateral form of these (q.v.), but is
now used as the plural of that (q.v.)

## Thoth
Thoth, п., the ancient Egyptian god of wisdom
and magic. — L., fr. Gk. Θώθ, Θωύθ, Θεύθ,
fr. Egypt. Tehuti.

## thou
thou, pron. of 2nd person sing. —ME., fr. OE.
дй, rel. to ON. pu, OS., OFris. thu, Dan., Swed.
du, MDu. du, OHG., MHG. du, G. du, Goth.
pu, fr. I.-E. *tu-, 'thou', whence also OI. tv-am,
Avestic tu, Arm. du, Dor. Gk. τύ, Att. σύ, L. tu,
Alb. ti, OSlav. ty, Lith. tu, Olr. tu, W. ti. Cp.
thee, thine, thy. Cp. also tutoyer, tuum.
Derivative: thou, tr. v.

## though
though, conj. — ME. though, thogh, fr. ON. *pok;
rel. to OE. Peak, ON. po, OS. thoh, OFris. thdeh,
OHG. doh, MHG., G. dock, Goth, pauh,
'though, yet'. Cp. although,

## thought
thought, n. — ME. tkoght, thouht, fr. OE. gepoht,
poht, from the stem of penkan (past tense pokte),
'to think'. Cp. OS. gitkdht, Du. gedachte,
s-thought, idea', MDu. gedachtenisse, 'memory',
Du. gedachtenis, 'remembrance*, OHG. kitheht-

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:790 COLUMN:2 -->
nissi, MHG. gedxhtnisse, 'devotion', G. Ge-
ddchtnis, 'memory' (for Du. and G. suff. -nis see
-ness), Du. aandacht, 'attention', OHG. anaddht,
MHG. anddht, G. Andacht, 'attention, devotion'
G. Bedacht, 'consideration deliberation4, and
see think.
Derivatives: thought-ful, adj., thought-ful-ly,
adv., thought-ful-ness, п., thought-less, adj.,
thought-less-ly, adv., thoughl-fess-ness, п.,
thought-y, adj.

## thought
thought, past tense and pp. of think. — ME.
thought{e), fr. OE. poht{e), resp. gepoht. See
think and cp. thought, n.

## thousand
thousand, n. and adj. — ME., fr. OE. pusend, rel.
to OS. thusind, thusundig, ON. pusiind, Dan.
tusende, Swed. tusen, OFris. thusend, Du. dui-
zend, OHG. thusunt, dusunt, tusund, MHG.
tusent, G. tausend, Goth. Pusundi. These words
are traceable to the Teut. *pus-hundi which prop,
means 'many hundreds', and is cogn. with
OSlav. tysesta, tysqsta, Lith. tukstat\tis, OPruss.
tuslmtons, 'a thousand'. The first element of
Teut. *pus-hundi is prob. cogn. with OI. tavas-,
'strength', L. tumere, 'to swell'; see tnmid. For
the second element see hundred.

## thousandth
thousandth, adj. and n. — Formed with numeral
suff. -th fr. thousand on analogy of fourth, etc.

## thrail
thrail, п., a slave; bondman. — ME. rhral, fr. OE.
prxl, fr. ON. priell, 'slave, servant', which prob.
meant orig. 'runner', and is rel. to OE. prsegan,
Goth. Pragjan, 'to run', OE. prdg, 'course of
time', OHG. dregif, drigil, 'servant'. Cp. thirl,
'to restrict', which stands in gradational
relationship to thrall.

## thralldom
thralldom, thraldom, n. — ME. thraldom, fr.
thral. See thrall with suff. -dom.

## thrash
thrash, tr. and intr. v. —■ ME. threschen, fr. OE.
prescan, perscan, rel. to ON. Pryskva, priskja,
preskja, Dan. txrske, Swed. troska, Norw.
treskja, tryskja, MDu. derscen, dorscen, Du.
dorsen, OHG. threskan, dreskan, G. drescheti,
Goth, priscan. The orig. meaning of these words
was 'to stamp (tread) with noise' (cp. the Teut.
loan words It. trescare, "to prance about',
Provenc. trescar, OF. treschier, 'to dance', Sp.
triscar, 'to stamp the feet', Port, triscar, 'to
quarrel'); they are cogn. with Lith. tresketi, 'to
clatter, rattle1", OSlav. iresku, 'crack, crash'. All
these words derive fr. I.-E. base *ter-, 'to rub'.
See throw and cp. thresh and the first element in
threshold.
Derivatives: thrash, п., thrasher (q.v.)

## thrasher
thrasher, п., one who thrashes. — Formed fr.
thrash with agential suff. -er.

## thrasher
thrasher, п., a long-tailed thrushlike bird. — Dial.
E. thrusher, fr. thrush, 'the bird'.

## thrasonical
thrasonical, adj., boastful. — Formed with suff.
-ical fr. L. Thraso, fr. Gk. Θρασών, name of a
braggart in Terence's Eunuchus. The name
Θρασών lit. means 'boastful*. It derives fr.
θράσος, θάρσας, 'courage, audacity'. See ther-
sitical.

## thraw
thraw, tr. v., to twist. — A collateral form of
throw.

## thread
thread, n. — ME. thred, threed, fr. OE. pried, rel.
to OS. thrdd, ON. pradr, OFris. thred, Dan.
traad, Swed. trad, MDu. draet, Du. draad,
OHG., MHG. drat, G. Draht. All these words
lit. mean 'twisted' and derive fr. I.-E. base *tri-,
a gradational variant of *ter-, 'to rub, to rub by
turning', whence also Gk. τρητός, 'bored
through', τρήμα, 'that which is bored through',
τείρειν (for *τέριειν), 'to rub', L. terere, of
s.m-, OE. prdwan, 'to twist, revolve'. See throw
and cp. terebra, teredo, toreutic, turn.

## threat
threat, n. — ME. thret, threat, fr. OE. preat,
'crowd, troop, violence, threat', rel. to OE.
preotan, 'to weary, vex, annoy', preatian, 'to
press, afflict, threaten', ON. prjota, 'to fail,
lack', Du. verdrieten, 'to vex', OHG. irdrio^an,
MHG. erdrie^en, verdrieten, G. verdriefien,
Goth, us-priutan, of s.m., fr. I.-E. base *treud·,
'to press, push', whence also L. trudere, 'to
thrust, push, shove', OSlav. trudu, 'oppression*,
truditi, 'to oppress, afflict', Olr. tromm (for
*trud-smo), Oppressive, heavy', Alb. tre&, Ί
geld, castrate', lit. Ί crush (the testicles)*. Base
*treud-,is a -rf-enlargement of base *ter-t*to rub.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:790 COLUMN:3 -->
pierce', whence Gk. τρϋειν, 'to wear out,
distress', OSlav. tryjo, tryti, 'to rub', trovo, truti, 'to
wear out, consume'. See throw and cp. throe,
thrust. Cp. also abstruse, detrude, detrusion,
extrude, extrusion, intrude, intrusion, obtrude,
obtrusion, protrude, protrusion, ret rude,
refusion.

## threaten
threaten, tr. and intr. v. — ME. thretnen, fr. OE.
preatnian, fr. preat. See threat.
Derivatives: threaten-er, п., threaten-ing, adj.,
threaten-ing-ly, adv.

## three
three, adj. and n. — ME. thre, threo, thri, fr. OE.
pri, prie (masc), preo (fern, and neut.), rel. to
OS. thria (masc. and fern.), thriu (neut.), ON.
prir (masc), prjar (fern.), prju (neut.), Dan.,
Swed., Norw. tre, OFris. thre (masc), thriu
(fern.), thriu (neut.), MDu., Du. drie, OHG. dri
(masc), drio (fern.), driu (neut.), MHG. dri, drie
(masc. and fem.), driu (neut.), G. drei, Goth.
*preis (masc. and fem.), prija (neut.), 'three', fr.
I.-E. base *treyes, whence also OI. trdyah,
(masc), tisrah (fem.), tri (neut.), Avestic ftrayo
(masc), tiskaro (fem.), Toch. A tri (masc.) tre
(fem.), Hitt. tri-, Arm. erek', Alb. tre (masc), tri
(fem.), Gk. τρεις (masc. and fem.), τρία (neut.),
L. tres (masc. and fem.), trio (neut.), UmbT. trif
(ace), triia, Oscan iris, OSlav. trije, trije
(masc. and fem.), tri (neut.), Lith. try's, Olr. tri
(masc), teoir, teora (fem.), W. tri (masc), teir
(fem.), 'three'. Cp. third, thirteen, thirty, thrice.
Cp. also drill, 'woven material', ter-, tercel,
tercet, tern, 'group of three', ternal, tertian,
tertiary, terzetto, Thrinax, tiercer trammel, trefoil,
tresillo, trey, tri-, triad, triangle, triarii, Trias,
tribe, Tribolium, triceps, tricerium, trident, tri ens,
triental, Trillium, trine, trinity, trio, Trithrinax,
triune, trivet, trivial, trivium, troika. Cp. also the
first element in testament, testicle, testify and in
sebundy, teapoy.

## thremmatology
thremmatology, п., the science of breeding
domestic animals. — Compounded of Gk. θρέμμα,
'nursling', and -λογία, fr. -λόγος, One who
speaks (in a certain manner); one who deals
(with a certain topic)'. The first element derives
from the stem of τρέφειν, 'to feed, nourish'; see
threptic. For the second element see -logy,

## threnetic
threnetic, threnetical, adj., mournful. — Gk.
θρηνητ^κός, 'inclined to lament', fr. θρήνος,
'dirge', which is rel. to θρώναξ, 'drone', τεν-
θρήνη, 'a kind of wasp*, from the I.-E. imitative
base *dhren-, 'to hum, buzz, murmur', whence
also Goth, drunjus, 'sound', OE. drdn, 'drone'.
See drone and cp. Anthrenus, Tenthredinidae.

## threnode
threnode, п., threnody. — See next word.

## threnody
threnody, п., a dirge, song of lamentation. — Gk.
θρηνωδία, compounded of θρήνος, 'dirge', and
φδή, 'song'. See threnetic and ode.
Derivatives: threnodi-al, threnod-ic, adjs., thren-
od-ist, n.

## threpsology
threpsology, п., the science of diet. —
Compounded of Gk. θρέψις, 'nourishment', and -λογία,
fr. -λόγος, One who speaks (in a certain
manner); one who deals (with a certain topic)'. The
first element is a derivative of τρέφειν, 'to feed,
nourish'; see next word. For the second element
see -logy,

## threptic
threptic, adj., pertaining to feeding {zool.) — Gk.
θρεπτικός, 'feeding', fr. θρετττός, 'fed', verbal
adj. of τρέφει, 'to feed, nourish', which stands
in gradational relationship to τροφή, 'food,
nourishment'. See trophic and words there
referred to and cp. esp. thremmatology,
threpsology. For the ending see adj. suff. -ic.

## thresh
thresh, tr. and intr. v. — Earlier form of thrash
(q.v.)
Derivatives: thresh, п., thresh-er, n.

## threshold
threshold, n. — ME. threshwold, fr. OE. persc-
wold, perscold, lit. 'something to tread upon*, fr.
OE. perscan, 'to tread; to thrash'. Cp. ON.
preskjoldr, Swed., Norw. troskel, Dan. txrskel,
'threshold', and see thrash,

## threw
threw, past tense of throw. — ME. threw, fr. OE.
preow, past tense of prdwan. See throw.

## thrice
thrice, adv. — ME. thries, formed with the
adverbial genit. suff. -s fr. OE. priga, priwa, 'three
times'. Accordingly the spelling should be thris.
The ending -ce merely serves to show that the s
has the voiceless sound s. (and not the voiced

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:791 COLUMN:1 -->
