## thrift
thrift, n. — ME., fr. ON. prift, 'prosperity',
formed with suff. -t, fr. ON. prt/, of s.m., lit. 'a
grasping', fr. prifa, 'to grasp'. See thrive.
Derivatives: thrift, tr. v., thrift-y, adj., thrift-i-ly,
adv., thrift-i-ness, n.

## thrill
thrill, tr. and intr. v. — The original meaning
of this verb was 'to pierce', fr. ME. thrillen,
metathesized fr. thirlen, 'to pierce', fr. OE.
pyrlian, 'to iperce', fr. pyrel, 'hole', fr. purh,
'through'. See through and cp. thirl, drill, 'to
bore', drill, 'to train (soldiers)', and the second
element in nostril.
Derivatives: thrill, п., thrill-er, п., thrill-ing, adj.,
thrill-ing-ty, adv., thrill-ing-ness, n.

## Tbrinax
Tbrinax, п., a genus of fan palms (hot.) — ModL.,
fr. Gk. &ρΐναξ, 'trident, three-pronged fork'; so
called in reference to the shape of the leaves.
Θρΐναξ is prob. compounded of the base of
τρεις, 'three', and of δκις, 'point, barb'. See
three and acrid and cp. the second element in
triakis-, tetrakis-. Cp. also Trithrinax.

## thrips
thrips,n., name of various small insects (entomol.)
— Gk. θριψ, 'wood worm', of uncertain
origin.

## thrive
thrive, intr. v. — ME. thriven, fr. ON. prifasfc, 'to
grasp for oneself, to thrive', reflexive of prifa, 'to
grasp, grip*. (For the reflexive suff. -sk see -sk
and cp. bask.) Cp. Norw. triva, 'to seize', trivast
(refl.), 'to thrive', Swed. trifvas and Dan. trives
(refl.), 'to thrive'. Cp. also thrift.
Derivatives: thriv-er, п., thriv-ing, adj., thriv-
ing-ly, adv., tkriv-ing-ness, n.

## thriven
thriven, pp. of thrive. — ME. See prec. word.

## -thrix
-thrix, combining form meaning 'hair, hairlike'.
— Fr. Gk. *ρίξ, gen. τρίχας, 'hair'. See tricho-
and cp. the second element in Clonothrix.

## throat
throat, n. — ME. throte, fr. OE. prote, protu, rel.
to OHG. dro33a, MHG. drosse, G. Drossel,
'throat', and to OS. strata, MDu. strote, Du.
strot, of s.m.; cp. throttle and the first element
in thropple. It. strozza, 'throat', and strozzare,
'to strangle', are Teut. loan words.
Derivatives: throat, tr. v., throat-ed, adj., throat-
y, adj., tkroar-i-ly, adv., throat-i-ness, n.

## throb
throb, intr. v. — ME. throbben; of imitative
origin.
Derivatives: throb, п., throbb-er, n.

## throe
throe, п., great pain, anguish. — ME. throwe,
'pain, pang, throe', fr. earlier thrawe, fr. OE.
prawu, 'threat, oppression, punishment', which
is rel. to OE. prea, of s.m., prean, 'to oppress,
punish, threaten', MHG. dro, 'threat' (whence,
with back formation, MHG. drdn, G. drohen,
'to threaten'), OHG. drewen, drouwan, MHG.
drouwen, G. drauen (now only poetic), 'to
threaten', and possibly cogn. with Gk. τρυειν, 'to
wear out, distress'. See threat.
Derivative: throe, intr. v., to agonize.

## thromb-
thromb-, form of thrombo- before a vowel.

## thrombin
thrombin, п., the substance that causes the
clotting of blood (biochem.) — Formed with suff.
-in fr. Gk. *ρόμβος, 'lump, clot'. See next word.

## thrombo-
thrombo-, before a vowel thromb-, combining
form meaning 'lump, clot'. — Gk. *ρομβο-,
θρομβ-, fr. θρόμβος, 'lump, clot', formed from
a nasalized enlargement of I.-E. base *dhrebh-,
'to make firm, curdle', whence Gk. τρέφειν, 'to
make solid, thicken, congeal, curdle; to
nourish'. See draff and words there referred to.

## thrombosis
thrombosis, п., obstruction of a blood vessel by a
clot (med.) — Medical L., fr. Gk. *ρόμβωσις,
'clot, coagulation', fr. *ρόμβος. See prec. word
and -osis.

## throne
throne, n. — ME., fr. earlier trone, fr. OF. trone
(F. trone), fr. L. thronus, fr. Gk. *ρ6νος, 'seat,
chair, throne', fr. I.-E. base *dher(e)-, 'to hold,
support', whence also Gk. έρανος, 'bench',
*ρήνυς, 'footstool', OI. dharayati, 'he holds,
supports', dharmah, 'custom, law', L. firmus,
'firm, steadfast, stable, strong'. See firm, adj.,
and cp. therapeutic, thorax.
Derivatives: throne, tr. and intr. v., throne-less,
adj.

## throng
throng, п., crowd. — ME. throng, fr. OE. prang,
geprang, 'crowd, tumult', rel. to ON. prong, Du.
drang, G. Drang, Gedrange, 'crowd, throng',

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:791 COLUMN:2 -->
OE.pringan,OS. thringan, ON.pryngva, 'to press
on, crowd', Du. dringen,'topush', OHG. dringan,
MHG., G. dringen, 'to press on, crowd', MHG.
dringen, 'to press round a prince at court', Goth.
preihan (for *prinhan), 'to oppress', and cogn.
with Avestic ftraxtanam (gen. pi.), 'of those
pressed together', Lith. trenkiu, treHkti, 'to push,
jolt'.
Derivatives: throng, intr. and tr. v., throng-er, n.

## thropple
thropple, п., throat, windpipe (chiefly dial.) —
ME. throppill, prob. fr. OE. protbolla,
'windpipe', compounded οι prote, protu, 'throat', and
bolla, 'bowl'. See throat and boll.

## throstle
throstle, n. — ME. throstel, fr. OE. prostle, rel. to
OS. throsla, OHG. drdscala (MHG. droschel, G.
Drossel), 'thrush'. These words are diminutives
of OE. prysce, resp. OHG. drosca, 'thrush'. See
thrush, 'the bird', and dimin. suff. -Ie.

## throttle
throttle, п., a valve controlling the flow of fuel. —
Dimin. of throat (q.v.); see also dimin. suff. -Ie.
Derivatives: throttle, tr. and intr. v., throttl-er,
п., throttl-ing, adj., throttl-ing-ly, adv.

## throngh
throngh, prep. — ME. thurgh, thurugh, thurh, fr.
OE. puruh, purh, which is rel. to OS. thuru(h),
OFris. thruch, MDu. dore, Du. door, OHG.
thuruh, later duruh, durah, MHG. dur, durch, G.
durch, Goth, pairh, 'through' (cp. Goth, pairko,
'hole'), fr. I.-E. base *ter-qwe- *tr-q"e,
enlargement of base *ter-, *tr-, 'through', whence also
OI. tirab, Avestic tarS, 'through, beyond', L.
trans, 'beyond', Olr. tre, tri, W. tra, 'through'.
See trans- and cp. thorough. Cp. also thirl, thrill,
thrum, 'thread', drill, 'to bore', drill, 'to train
soldiers'. Cp. also term and words there referred
to.
Derivatives: through, adv., adj. and п.,
throughly, adv.

## throughout
throughout, prep, and adv. — ME. thurhout,
throughout. See through and out.

## throve
throve, past tense of thrive. — ME. thro/, formed
fr. thriven, 'to thrive', on analogy of dro/ (E.
drove), fr. driven. See thrive.

## throw
throw, tr. and intr. v. — ME. thrawen, throwen,
'to twist, throw', fr. OE. prdwan, 'to cause to
turn, twist', rel. to OS. thraian, MDu. drseyen,
Du. draaien, OHG. drden, MHG. draehen, G.
drehen, 'to turn, twist', fr. I.-E. base *ter-, 'to

τείρει,ν (for *τέριειν), τρΐβειν, 'to rub, rub

grind, pierce', τι-τρο>σκειν, 'to wound, hurt',
τρητός, 'bored through', τρήμα, 'that which
is bored through, hole', τρΰμα, 'hole', L.
terere, 'to rub, thresh, grind, wear away',
terebra, 'borer, drill, auger', OSlav. tirg, treti,
'to rub', Lith. trinu, trlnti, 'to rub', tiriu, tirti,
'to examine", Olr. tarathar, 'borer', W. taraw,
'to strike', Arm. t'rem, Ί knead'. Cp. atresis,
attrition, attritus, contrite, contrition, Cntitere-
bra, detriment, diatribe, ectro-, helicotrema,
intertrigo, lithotrity, Septentrio, teredo' terete,
Termes, termite, tharm, thrash, thread, threat,
throe, toreutic, trauma, Trema, Trematoda,
trepan, -tresia, tribo-, Tribonema, tribulation,
trigo, Tripsacum, tripsis, trite, Triticum, triturate,

Derivatives: throw, п., throw-er, п., throwster, n.

## thrown
thrown, pp. — ME. throwen, fr. OE. geprawen,
pp. of prawan. See prec. word.

## thrum
thrum, п., the end of warp threads. — ME., fr.
OE. -prum, 'band, ligament' (in tungeprum,
'ligament of the tongue'), rel. to OS. thrumi, 'end-
piece (on the spear)', ON. promr, 'edge', MLG.
drom, drum, Du. dreum, 'thrum', OHG. trum,
MHG. drum, 'end, chip, splinter', G. Trumm,
'thrum; fragment, piece' (more frequently used

τέρμα, 'end, boundary*, L. terminus, of s.m. See

Derivatives: thrum, tr. v., to furnish with thrums,
thrumm-y, adj.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:791 COLUMN:3 -->
thrum, intr. and tr. v., to play monotonously. —
Of imitative origin.
Derivative: thrumm-er, n.
thrush, п., any of the birds of the genus Turdus.
— ME. thrusche, thrusch, fr. OE. prysce, var.
prUsce, rel. to ON. prostr, Norw. trost, Swed.
trust, OHG. drosca, fr. I.-E. 'trzdos, 'thrush'.
These Teut. words are prob. cogn. with L.
turdus (for *turzdos), Lith. strazdas, Lett, strazds,
OPruss. tresde, 'thrush', Mir. truid, W. drudwy
(for *trozdi), 'starling'. Cp. throstle. Cp. also
Turdus, Struthio.

## thrush
thrush, п., an affection of mouth and throat. —
Cp. Dan. and Norw. treske, Swed. torsk; of
uncertain origin.

## thrust
thrust, tr. and intr. v. — ME. thrusten, fr. ON.
prysta, 'to thrust, force, compel', which is perh.
rel. to OE. preatian, 'to press, afflict, threaten',
preotan, 'to weary, vex, annoy'. See threat.
Derivatives: thrust, п., thrust-er, n.

## thud
thud, intr. v., to make a dull sound. — Of
imitative origin. Cp. OE. pyddan, 'to strike, thrust,
push'.
Derivatives: thud, п., thudd-ing, п., thudd-ing-ly,
adv.

## thug
thug, п., gangster. — Hind, thag, 'deceiver', fr.
OI. sthagah, of s.m., fr. sthagati, 'conceals',
which is cogn. with Gk. στέγειν, L. tegere, 'to
cover'. See thatch.
Derivatives: thuggee (q.v.), thugg-ess, n.

## thuggee
thuggee, п., murder as carried out by thugs. —
Hind, thagi, fr. thag, 'a deceiver'. Seeprec. word.

## Thuja
Thuja, п., a genus of plants, the arbor vitae (hotЛ
— ModL., fr. Gk. θυίά, name of an African
tree, prop, 'a tree the wood of which was burnt
for sacrificial purposes', fr. &ύειν, 'to sacrifice',
prop, 'to cause to smoke'. See thyme and cp.
thyine.

## Thule
Thule, п., classical name of the northernmost part
of the world. — L. Thule, Thyle, fr. Gk.
Θούλη, Θύλη. Ср. thulium.

## thulia
thulia, п., thulium oxide (chem.) — ModL.,
coined by the Swedish chemist Per Teodor Cleve
(1840-1905) in 1879 ft. Thule, name of the
northernmost land in the world.

## thuilte
thuilte, п., a variety of zoisite (mineral.) —
Formed fr. Thule with subst. suff. -ite.

## thulium
thulium, п., a metallic element belonging to the
rare earths (chem.) — ModL., coined by the
French chemist Paul Emile Lecoq de Boisbau-
dran (1838-1912) in 1886 from prec. word. See
J. Newton Friend, Man and the Chemical
Elements, London, 1951, p. 182.

## thumb
thumb, n. — ME. thoume, thoumbe, thombe, fr.
OE. puma, rel. to OS., OHG. thumo, MHG.,
MLG. dume, G. Daumen, Du. duim, ON. pu-
mall, 'thumb', fr. I.-E. base *tS-, *teu-, 'to swell',
whence also L. tumere, 'to swell', tumidus,
'swollen'. See tumid and cp. thimble.
Derivatives: thumb, tr. and intr. v., thumb-er, п.,
thumb-y, adj.

## Thummim
Thummim, n. pi., one of the two objects attached
to the breastplate of the high priest; cp. Urim
(Bible). — Heb. tummtm (after a mobile sheva
spelled thummfm), prop. pi. of torn,
'completeness, perfection', from the stem of tarn, 'was
complete' (whence also tarn, tamim, 'complete,
sound', methom, 'soundness'), which is rel. to
Aram. tem!ma, Syr. tSmmfma, 'complete,
perfect*, Arab, tamma, 'was complete', tamam,
'perfection; perfect'. Cp. the second element in
Jotham.

## Thunbergia
Thunbergia, п., a genus of plants (bot.) — ModL.,
named after the Swedish botanist Carl Peter
Thunberg (1743-1828). For the ending see 1st
suff. -ia.

## thump
thump, п., a blow with something heavy; tr. and
intr. v., to beat with something heavy; — Of
imitative origin.
Derivatives: thump, п., thump-er, п., thump-ing,
adj.

## thunder
thunder, n. — ME. thuner, later thunder, fr. OE.
punor, rel. to ON. pdrr, OFris. thuner, MDu.
donre, dander, Du. dander, OHG. donar, MHG.
doner, donre, toner, G. Donner, from the I.-E.
imitative base *ten-, whence also OI. tanayitnuh,
'thundering', tdnyati, 'it thunders', Pers. tundar,
'thunder', Aeol. Gk. τέννει (Hesychius), 'moans,

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:792 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: 765 | TIDE -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:792 COLUMN:1 -->

## sighs
sighs, groans', L. tonare, 'to thunder', tonitrus,
'thunder'. The same base, enlarged with initial

## s
s, appears in OI. stanati, staniti. stanayati. 'it

## thunders'
thunders', Gk. στένειν, στενάζειν, *to groan,
moan', στόνος, 'a groaning, moaning', OSlav.

## stenjq
stenjq, stenati, Lith. stenu, steneti, 'to groan,
moan', OE. stenant 'to groan'. Cp. astonish,
astonnd, detonate, Stcntor, stun, Thor, Thursday,
tinnitus, tintinnabulum, tonite, tonitrous, tornado.
Cp. also blunderbuss. For the so-called inorganic
d in thunder cp. gender, jaundice, sound, 'noise'.
Derivatives: thunderous (q.v.), thunder-y, adj.

## thunder
thunder, intr. and intr. v. — ME. thuneren, thun-
deren, fr. OE. punrian, fr. punor, 'thunder'. Cp.
Du. donderen, OHG. donaron, MHG. dunen,
MLG. donen and see thunder, n.
Derivatives: thunder-er, п., thunder-ing, adj.,
thunder-ing-ly, adv.

## thunderous
thunderous, adj. — A hybrid coined fr. thunder,
п.; and -ous, a suff. of Latin origin.
Derivatives: thunderous-ly, adv., thunderous-
ness, n.

## thurible
thurible, п., a censer. — L. turibulum, thuribulum,
fr. tus {thus), gen. turis (thuris), 'frankincense',
fr. *tuwos, fr. Gk. θύος, 'a burnt sacrifice', fr.
θύειν, 'to sacrifice', prop, 'to cause to smoke',
whence also θύμον, 'thyme*. See thyme.

## thurifer
thurifer, п., one who carries a censer. — L. turifer
(thurifer), compounded of tus {thus), gen. turis
{thuris), 'frankincense', and the stem offerre, 'to
bear, carry'. See prec. word and bear, 'to carry4.
Derivative: thurifer-ous, adj.

## thurify
thurify, intr. and tr. v., to burn incense. — F. tku-
rifier, fr. Late L. thurificare, formed fr. L. tus
(thus), 'frankincense', and -ficare, fr. facere, 'to
make, do'. See thurible and -fy.

## Thursday
Thursday, П. — ME. Thoresday, Thuresdai, Thurs-
daye, fr. OE. puresdseg, fr. ON- porsdagr, 'the
day of per (the god of thunder)', (whence also
Dan., Swed. Torsdag), which is rel. to OE.
punresdseg, OFris. thunresdei, MLG. doner{s)-
dach, MDu. donresdack, Du. donderdag, OHG.
Donares ,tag, MHG. donerstac, G. Donnerstag.
These words are prop, loan translations of L.
Jovis dies, 'the day of Jupiter, Thursday', ON.
par, having been identified with the Roman god
Jupiter; whence It. giovedi, OF. juesdi, F. jeudit
Sp. jtieves, 'Thursday'), itself a loan translation
of Gk. Διός ήμερα, 'the day of Zeus'. For the
first element see Thor and thunder, п., for the
second see day.

## thus
thus, adv. — ME., fr. OE. pus, rel. to OS., OFris.
thus, MDu., Du. dus, and to E. the, this, that.

## thwack
thwack, tr. v., to strike with something flat. — Of
imitative origin.
Derivatives: thwack, п., thwack-er, п.,
thwacking, n. and adj., thwack-ing-ly, adv.

## thwaite
thwaite, п., cleared land. — Of Scand. origin. Cp.
ON. pveit, 'a piece of land', lit. meaning 'land
cut off', and rel. to ON. pveita, 'to hew', and
OE. pwitan, 'to cut'. See whittle and cp. doit,

## thwart
thwart, adv., across. — ME. thwert, thwart, fr.
ON. pvert, 'across', orig. neut. of the adjective
Pverr, 'transverse', rel. to OE. pweorh, 'adverse,
perverse, angry', MDu. dwers, dwaers, dwars,
Du. dwars, 'transverse, cross-grained, contrary',
OHG. twerh, dwerah, MHG. twerch, dwerch,
querch, G. quer, zwerch-, Goth, pwairhs, 'angry',
fr. I.-E. base *twereq-, which is rel; to base
*tereq-, 'to turn, twist, wind*, whence L. tor-
quere, 'to twist'. See torque and cp. queer. Cp.
also athwart.

## thy
thy, possessive pron. of the 2nd person sing, of
thee, thine. — Early ME. thi, short for thin, fr.
OE. Pin. The final η was dropped in ME. before
words beginning with consonants. See thine. For
the loss of the η before consonants cp. my and
a, form of the indef. art. an before consonants.

## Thyiad
Thyiad, п., a Bacchante {Greek mythol) — L.
Thyias, gen. -adis, fr. Gk. Θΰιάς, gen. -άδος,
prop, 'a raging woman', rel. to θύειν, 'to rush
along, storm, rage', which is originally identical
with θύειν, 'to sacrifice', prop, 'to cause to
smoke'. The phases of sense development prob.
were: 'to fiy about like dust; to whirl; to rush;
to rage; to smoke; to cause to smoke, to
sacrifice'. See thyme and -ad.

## thyine
thyine, adj., pertaining to the sandarac tree. —

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:792 COLUMN:2 -->
Late L. thyinus, fr. Gk. θύϊνος, fr. θυία, an
African tree. See thyme and adj. suff. -ine.

## thylacine
thylacine, п., a doglike marsupial. — Formed
with suff. -ine fr. Gk. θύλακος, 'pouch', which
is of uncertain origin.

## thyme
thyme, п., a plant of the mint family. — ME. tyme,
fr. OF. tym (F. thym), fr. L. thymum, fr. Gk.
θύμον, also θύμος, 'thyme', fr. θύειν, 'to
sacrifice', prop, 'to cause to smoke', whence also
θυία, an 'African tree, prop, 'a tree the wood of
which was burnt for sacrificial purposes',
θυμίαμα, Ion. θυμίημα, 'incense'. See thio- and
cp. words there referred to.

## Thymelaeaceae
Thymelaeaceae, n. pi., a family of plants (bot.)
— ModL., formed with suff. -aceae fr. L. thy-
melaea, name of a plant, fr. Gk. θυμελαία,
which is compounded of θύμον or θύμος,
'thyme', and έλαία, 'olive tree'. See thyme and
elaeo-.

## thymelaeaceous
thymelaeaceous, adj. — See prec. word and
-aceous.

## thymic
thymic, adj., pertaining to the thyme. — Formed
with adj. suff. -ic fr. L. thymum. See thyme.

## thymic
thymic, adj., pertaining to the thymus. — Formed
with adj. suff. -ic fr. Medical L. thymus. See
thymus. t

## thymol
thymol, п., an aromatic substance, C10H13OH
(chem.) — Formed with suff. -ol fr. L. thymum.
See thyme.
(hymns, п., name of a gland in the chest {anat.) —
Medical L., fr. Gk. θύμος, 'thyme'; so called
from its resemblance to the bud of a thyme. See
thyme.

## Thymus
Thymus, п., a genus of plants, the thyme (bot.) —
Medical L., fr. Gk. θύμος. See thyme.

## thymy
thymy, adj., scented with thyme. — Formed with
adj. suff. -y fr. L. thymus. See thyme.

## thyr-
thyr-, form of thyro- before a vowel.

## thyreo-
thyreo-, before a vowel thyre-, combining form
meaning 'thyroid'. — Shortened fr. Gk. θυρο-
ειδής. See thyroid and cp. thyro-.

## Thyridldae
Thyridldae, n. pi., a family of moths (zool.) —
ModL., formed with suff. -idae fr. Gk. θυρίς,
gen. θυρίδος, Opening in a door, window',
dimin. of θύρα, 'door'. See door and cp.
thyroid.

## thyro-
thyro-, before a vowel thyr-, combining form
meaning 'thyroid'. — Shortened fr. Gk.
θυρεοειδής. See thyroid and cp. thyreo-,

## thyroid
thyroid, adj., pertaining to, or designating the
ductless gland in the neck, which has an
important effect on the growth of the body; lit.
'shield-shaped' {anat.) — Medical L. thyreoi-
deus, fr. Gk. θυρεοειδής, 'shield-shaped*,
compounded of θυρεός, 'stone put against a door;
oblong shield', which is rel. to θύρα, 'door',
and of -οειδής, 'like', fr. είδος, 'form, shape'.
See door and -oid.
Derivatives: thyroid, п., the thyroid gland,
thyroid-ism, п., thyroid-iz-ation, п., thyroid-less,
adj.

## thyroid cartilage
thyroid cartilage, the Adam's apple (anat.) —
Medical L. cartilage thyroidea, lit. 'shieldlike
cartilage*, fr. L. cartilage, 'cartilage', and
Medical L. thyroidea, fern, of thyroideus, fr. Gk.
θυρεοειδής, 'shield-shaped', a name given by
Galen to the Adam's apple; see Joseph Hyrtl,
Onomatologia anatomica, pp. 547-48. See
thyroid.

## thyroiditis
thyroiditis, п., inflammation of the thyroid gland
(med.) — Medical L. See thyroid and -itis.

## thyrotoxicosis
thyrotoxicosis, п., intoxication due to
disturbances caused by the thyroid gland (med.) —
Medical L., coined by Т. В. Dunhill in 1930 fr.
thyro- and toxicosis.

## thyroxine
thyroxine, thyroxin, п., the hormone of the
thyroid gland (biochem.) — Coined by its discoverer
Dr. Edward Calvin Kendall of the Mayo Clinic
in 1915 fr. thyr-, ox- and chem. suff. -ine, resp.

## -in
-in,

## thyrsus
thyrsus, п., a staff tipped with a pine cone,
carried by Dionysus, the satyrs, etc. (Greek mythol.)
— L., fr. Gk. θύρσος, 'a straight, light shaft; a
light wand', a foreign word of unknown origin.
Cp. torso, tursio.

## thysano-
thysano-, before a vowel thysan-, combining form
meaning 'tassel'. — Gk. θύσανο-, θυσαν-, fr.
θύσανος, θύσαννος, 'tassel', which is of

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:792 COLUMN:3 -->
uncertain origin. It is possibly formed with suff.
-ανος fr. *θύσσα, which would stand for
*θύθ-ια, hence—together with Lett, dusa,
'bundle'—would derive fr. I.-E. *deu-dh-,
enlargement of base *dheu-, 'to fly about like dust,
to smoke, be scattered, vanish'. See thio- and
cp. words there referred to.

## Tbysanoptera
Tbysanoptera, n. pi., an order of insects, the thrips
(entomol.) — ModL., compounded of Gk.
θύσανος, 'tassel', and πτερόν, 'wing'. See prec.
word and ptero-.

## Thysanura
Thysanura, n. pi., an order of insects, the bristle-
tail (entomol.) — ModL., compounded of Gk.
θύσανος, 'tassel', and ούρα, 'tail'. See thysano-
and uro-, 'tail-*.

## thyself
thyself, pron. — ME. thi self, fr. earlier the self,
fr. OE. pi selfum, dat. of рй self, 'thou thyself;
ME. thi self was influenced by ME. hire self
'herself.

## tiara
tiara, п., head dress. — L. tiara, fr. Gk. τιάρα,
which is of Oriental origin.

## Tiarella
Tiarella, п., a genus of plants, the false miterwort
(bot.) — A ModL. hybrid coined fr. Gk. τιάρα
(see prec. word) and L. dimin. suff. -ella; so
called in allusion to the form of the pistil. The
correct form would be Tiaryllium, fr. Gk. τιάρα
and the Gk. dimin. suff. -ύλλιον.

## tibia
tibia, n. — L. tibia, 'shin bone, pipe', which is of
uncertain origin. Cp. tige, tigella.

## tibial
tibial, adj., pertaining to the tibia. — L. tibialis,
fr. tibia. See prec. word and adj. suff. -al.

## tibio-
tibio-, combining form meaning 'pertaining to
the tibia and' — Fr. L. tibia, 'shin bone'. See
tibia.

## tic
tic, п., a spasmodic motion of certain muscles
(med.) — F., prob. of imitative origin.

## ticca
ticca, adj., hired (Anglo-Ind.) — Hind, thika, 'hire
fare, fixed price".

## Tichodroma
Tichodroma, п., a genus of small birds, the wall
creeper (ornithol.) — ModL., lit. 'wall runner',
fr. Gk. τεΤχος, 'wall', and the stem of δραμεϊν,
perf. δέδρομα, 'to run'. See dough and
dromedary.

## tick
tick, п., a parasitic insect of the order Acari
(entomol.) — ME. tyke, teke, ticke, rel. to
MLG., MDu. teke, Du. teek, OHG. zechot
MHG. zeche, zecke, G. Zecke, 'tick*, of
imitative origin. Cp. Arm. tizt 'bug', Mir. dega, 'stag
beetle', which are also imitative. F. tique, It.
zecca, 'tick', are Teut. loan words.

## tick
tick, п., the cover of mattresses, pillows, etc. —
L. theca, fr. Gk. θήκη, 'case, cover'. See theme,
theca, which is a doublet of tick.

## tick
tick, intr. and tr. v., to touch gently, tap; п., а
light touch, tap. — Of imitative origin. Cp. Du.
tikken, 'to touch, pat, tick', tik, 'a touch, pat'.

## tick
tick, п., credit (slang). — Shortened fr. ticket.

## ticker
ticker, п., a watch (slang); a tape machine. — Lit.
'that which ticks', formed fr. tick, 'to tap', with
agential suff. -er.

## ticket
ticket, n. — MF. estiquet, estiquete (F. etiquette)*
'a little note', lit. 'something stuck up\ fr. esti-
quier, estiquer, 'to attach'. See etiquette.
Derivatives: ticket, tr. v., ticket-er, п.,
ticketing, verbal n.

## tickie
tickie, tr. and intr. v. — A metathesized var. of
kittle.
Derivatives: tickle, п., tickl-er, п., tickl-ing, adj.,
tickl-ing-ly, adv., tickl-ish, adj., tickl-ish-ly, adv.,.
tickl-ish-ness, n.

## ticktack
ticktack, n. — Of imitative origin. Cp. tick, 'to
pat'.

## tidal
tidal, adj. — A hybrid coined fr. tide, п., a Teut.
word, and -al, a suff. of Latin origin.
Derivative: tidal-ly, adv.

## tide
tide, n. — ME. tid, tide, fr. OE. tid, 'time, season*,
which is rel. to OS. tid, ON. tid, Dan., Swed.,
Norw. tid, Du. tijd, OHG., MHG. zit, G. Zeit,
'time', fr. Teut. *ti-di-, prop, 'division of time',
fr. base *ti-, 'to divide; division; division of
time', whence also ON. ti-mi, OE. ti-ma, 'time';
see time and cp. ted, tiding, tidy. Teut. base
*rf- corresponds to I.-E. base *da-, *ddi-,
, 'to cut off, separate,divide, distribute',
whence OI. dati, dyati, 'cuts, divides', dayate,
'divides', ditih, 'division', Gk. δαίεσθαι, 'to
divide, distribute; to feed on'; δα£ς, δαίτη,
'meal, feast, banquet', δαίζειν, 'to cleave asun-

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:793 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: TIDE | 766 -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:793 COLUMN:1 -->
der, rend, divide', δαίμων, 'god, goddess', lit.
'divider, distributor (of men's destinies)', δήμος,
'district, people', Arm. ti, gen. tioy, 'age, time',
Olr. dam, 'troop, company'. Cp. I.-E. *dap-, a
-p-enlargement of base "da-, whence Gk.
δαπάνη, 'expenditure (esp. expenditure arising
from the entertaining of guests)', L. daps,
'expenditure, sacrificial feast banquet', damnum
(for *dap-nom), 'harm, loss', orig. 'expenditure',
Toch. A lap-, 'to eat'. For the sense
development of OE. tide, 'time; flood tide', cp. Du. ti},
'flood tide', distinguished from tijd, 'time', and
MLG. getide, tide, G. Gezeiten, 'flood tide'. Cp.
the first element in Zeitgeist and the second
element in yahrzeit. Cp. also dah, damage, damn,
dan, dapifer, deme, democracy* demon, demos,
demotic, endemic, epidemic.
Derivatives: tide, intr. v., tidal (q.v.), tid-ed, adj.,
tide-less, adj., tiding (q.v.), tidy (q.v.)

## tide
tide, intr. v., 1) to happen; 2) to be carried with
the tide; tr. v., to carry with the tide. — In the
sense 'to happen', fr. OE. tidan, fr. tid, 'time'
(see tide, n.); in the other senses directly fr. tide,
n.

## tidings
tidings, n. pi., but usually construed as a sing. —
ME. tidinge, tithinge, tidinde, fr. OE. tidung,
which prob. derives fr. ON. tidendi (pi.),
'happenings, news', fr. Mr, 'that which happens in
time', fr. tid 'time'. Cp. Dan., Norw. tidende,
'tidings, news', Du. tijding, G. Zeitung,
'newspaper', and see tide, n.

## tidology
tidology, п., the study of tides. — A hybrid coined
fr. E. tide, п., and Gk. -λογία, fr. -λόγος, 'one
who speaks (in a certain manner); one who deals
(with a certain topic)'. See -logy.

## tidy
tidy, adj., neat; orderly. — ME. tidy, tidi, fr. tid,
fr. OE. tid. 'time', hence prop, 'timely'. Cp.
Dan., Swed. tidig, Du. tijdig, OHG., MHG.
zitig, G. zeitig, 'timely', and see tide, п., and -y
(representing OE. -ig) Cp. also titivate.
Derivatives: tidy, n. and tr. and intr. v., ttdi-ly,
adv., tidi-ness, n.

## tie
tie, п., knot. — ME. teg, ley, tye, fr. OE. tiag,
teah, 'bond, rope', which is rel. to ON. taug,
'tie', tygill, 'string', and to OE. tion, 'to draw,
pull, drag'. See tow, 'to draw'.

## tie
tie, tr. and intr. v., to fasten, bind. — ME. tegen,
teyen, tien, fr. OE. tiegan, tigan, 'to tie, fasten',
fr. teag, teah, 'bond, rope'. See tie, n.
Derivatives: tier (q.v.), ty-ing, n.

## tiemannite
tiemannite, п., a mercuric selenide (mineral.) —
G. Tiemannit, named after the ]9th-cent.
scientist W. Tiemann, its discoverer. For the
ending see subst. sun", -ite.

## rienda
rienda, п., shop. — Sp., prop, 'tent', ft. VL. tenia,
fem. pp. of tendere, 'to stretch, extend', used as
a noun. See tend, 'to move in a certain direction',
and cp. tent, 'shelter'.

## tier
tier, п., one who ties. — Formed fr. tie, 'to bind',
with agential suff. -er.

## tier
tier, п., row, series. — MF. tiere, fr. OF. tiere,
'row, rank, series', fr. Frankish "tiri, which is
rel. to OHG. ziari, MHG. ziere, G. Zier,
'adornment', ON. tirr, OS. tir, OE. Or, 'glory, honor'
(whence ME. tir, E. tire, 'attire', q.v.) See also
attire.

## tierce
tierce, п., 1) Orig. a third; 2) the third canonical
hour, nine o'clock A.M.; 3) a sequence of three
cards of the same suit; 4) a liquid measure
containing one third of a pipe, i.e. 42 gallons; 5) a
position in fencing. — ME. terce, tierce, fr. MF.
tierce, fem. of the adjective tiers, 'third', used as
a noun, fr. OF., fr. L. tertius, 'third'. See tertian
and cp. terce, terce], tercet, tertiary.
Derivative: tierce, tr. v.

## tiff
tiff, п., liquor. — Of uncertain origin. Cp. tiffin.
Derivatives: tiff, tr. v., to sip, drink.

## tiff
tiff, п., a petty quarrel. — Prob. of imitative
origin. Cp. sniff, puff.
Derivative: tiff, intr. v., to be angry.

## tiffany
tiffany, п., a thin silk gauze. — Obsol. F. tiphanie,
fr. Late L. theophania, 'manifestation of
God'; see theophany. The word tiffany was orig.
used as a synonym of epiphany. Its sense
development into 'a silk gauze fabric' has not yet
been explained in a satisfactory manner.

## tiffin
tiffin, п., luncheon (Anglo-Ind.) — Prob. formed
— with change of suff. — fr. tiffing, verbal n. of

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:793 COLUMN:2 -->
tiff, 'to drink'. See tiff, 'liquor'.

## tige
tige, п., the shaft of a column (archil.); stem of a
plant (bot.) — F., ft. L. tibia, 'shin bone; pipe'.
See tibia and cp. next word.

## tigella
tigella, tigelle, п., a primitive stem [hot.) — Mod-
L., fr. F. tigelle, dimin. of tige, 'stalk, stem'. See
prec. word and -ella.
Derivative: tigell-ate, adj.

## tiger
tiger, n. — ME. tigre, fr. OF. (= F.) tigre, ft. L.
tigris, ft. Gk. τίγρις, prop, 'the swift animal',
a word of Iranian origin. Cp. Avestic tiyrisk,
'arrow', tiyra-, 'pointed'. These words are
derivatives of I.-E. base *(s)teig-, 'to prick, stick,
pierce'. Cp. Gk. Τίγρις (whence L. Tigris), 'the
Tigris river', lit. 'the swift river', and see stick,
v., and words there referred to.
Derivatives: tiger-ish, adj., tiger-ish-ly, adv.,
tiger-isk-ness, п., tiger-ly, adj., tigress (q.v.),
tigrine (q.v.)

## tight
tight, adj. — ME. thight, tight, of Scand. origin,
cp. ON. pettr, Dan. tut, Swed. tat, which are
rel. to MHG. dihte, G. and Du. dicht, 'dense,
tight', and to OE. gedihan, gedeon, OS. thihan,
OFris. thigia, MDu. ghedien, Du. gedijen, OHG.
gidthan, MHG. gedihen, G. gedeihen, Goth.
(ga)peihan, 'to thrive, grow, prosper, flourish',
OHG. gidigan, MHG. gedigen, 'grown up, firm,
genuine', G. gediegen, 'genuine, solid, worthy'
(prop. pp. of OHG. gidihan, MHG. gedihen,
resp. former pp. of G. gedeihen), and cogn. with
Ir. ticht, 'curdled, coagulated', Lith. tankus,
'close, tight', Pers. tang, 'tight', OI. tanakti,
'draws together, contracts', fr. I.-E. base *tenq-,
'to be thick or strong'. The initial t (for th) in
ME. and E. tight is due to the influence of Swed.
tat, Dan. tset.
Derivatives: tight, adv. and tr. v., tight-en, tr. v.,
tighten-er, п., tight-er, п., tight-ish, adj., tight-ly,
adv., tight-ness, п., adv., tight-s, n. pi.

## riglic
riglic, also tiglinic, adj., pertaining to a crystalline
acid (C(H,C02H, obtained fr. croton oil (chem.)
— ModL. tiglium, in Croton tiglium, 'the croton
oil plant', fr. Gk. τΐλος, 'a thin stool', so called
in allusion to its purgative properties. Gk. τΐλος
is prob. cogn. with OSlav. tilja, 'decomposition,
putrefaction", ttliti, 'to rot, putrefy', Arm.
t'rem, Ί knead' (prop. Ί moisten the dough'),
t'rik', 'dung', OSlav. tina, 'mud, mire', Lith.
tyras, tpre, 'pap', W. tail, 'dung', OE. pinan, 'to
become moist'; fr. I.-E. base *ti-, *tei-, 'to melt;
to moisten'. Cp. tilley, tinea. For *ta, 'to melt',
a base collateral with base *ti-, see thaw.

## tigress
tigress, n. — Formed fr. F. tigresse, fr. tigre. See
tiger and 1st -ess.

## tigrine
tigrine, adj., tigerlike. — L. tigrinus, fr. tigris. See
tiger and adj. suff. -ine (representing L. -inus).

## tigroid
tigroid, adj., resembling a tiger. — Compounded
of Gk. τίγρις, 'tiger', and -οειδής, 'like', fr.
εϊδος, 'form, shape'. See tiger and -oid.

## tike
tike, n. — See tyke.

## til
til, n., a mark (~ ) placed over a vowel or the first
vowel of a diphthong in Portuguese to indicate
nasalization as in la, grdo. — Port., fr. L. titulus.
See tilde.

## tilasite
tilasite, п., a magnesium calcium arsenate
{mineral.) — Swed. tilasit, named after the Swedish
mining engineer Daniel Ttlas. The ending -it
goes back to Gk. -ΐτης; see subst. suff. -ite.

## tilbury
tilbury, п., a kind of two -wheeled carriage. —
Named after a London coach builder, who first
designed it.

## tilde
tilde, п., a mark (~) placed over the letter я in
Spanish to indicate the palatal sound of n, as in
seHor. — Sp., formed with metathesis fr. L.
titulus, 'inscription, superscription, label, title'.
See title.

## tile
tile, n. — ME., fr. OE. tigele, tigule, which,
together with OS. tiegla, ON. tigl, Dan. tegl, Swed.
tegel, MDu. tiegel (Du. tegel), OHG. ziagala,
ziagal (MHG., G. ziegel), derives fr. L. tigula
(whence also It. tegola,F. tuile), which is rel. to
tegere, 'to cover'. See thatch and cp. tegument.
Cp. also tuille.
Derivatives: tile, tr. v., til-ed, adj., til-er, п.,
tilery, п., til-ing, n.

## tilefish
tilefish, n. — A name formed from the ending of
the generic name of this fish, called Lopholatilus
chamaeleonticeps.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:793 COLUMN:3 -->

## Tula
Tula, п., a genus of trees, the linden (hot.) — L.
tilia, 'the linden tree', of uncertain origin;
possibly cogn. with Gk. πτελέϊ, 'the elm' (see
Ptelea and cp. teil).

## Tiliaceae
Tiliaceae, n. pi., the linden family (bot.) — Formed
with suff. -aceae fr. L. tilia. See prec. word.

## tUiaceous
tUiaceous, adj. — See Tilia and -aceous.

## till
till, prep, and conj. — ME. till, til, ft. OE. til, fr.
ON. til, 'to', which is rel. to ΟΝ., Dan., Swed.,
OFris. til, 'to till', OE., OFris. til, 'good,
convenient', Goth, tils, gatils, 'convenient', OHG.,
MHG. zil, G. Ziel, 'limit, end, goal', and to OE.
tilian, 'to strive after'. See till, 'to cultivate (the
land)', and cp. until.

## till
till, п., a drawer, esp. a money drawer. — Earlier
title, tylle, back formation fr. ME. tillen, tyllen,
'to draw'j fr. OE. -tyllan (e.g. in j'ortyllan, 'to
draw aside, lead astray, seduce'). For the sense
development of till, 'drawer', fr. ME. tillen, 'to
draw', cp. drawer, from the verb to draw, and F.
tiroir, 'drawer', fr. tirer, 'to draw'. ME. tillen
stands in gradational relationship to ME. tullen,
tollen, 'to draw, pull'. Cp. toll, 'to attract'.

## till
till, tr. v., to cultivate (the land). — ME. tilien, fr.
OE. tilian, 'to strive after, endeavor, treat,
cultivate (the land)', rel. to OS. tilian, OFris. tilia, 'to
reach, obtain', MDu., Du. telen, 'to breed, raise;
to grow, cultivate', OHG. zilen, zildn, 'to hurry,
make haste', G. zielen, 'to aim, strive', Goth.
til, til, Opportunity', tilon, gatilon, 'to reach,
obtain', and prob. cogn. with Olr. dil,
'agreeable*. See til], prep.

## Tillandsia
Tillandsia, п., a genus of plants, the long moss
(bot.) — ModL., named after the 18th cent.
Swedish botanist Elias Tillands. For the ending
see 1st suff. -ia.

## tiller
tiller, п., one who tills (the land). — Formed from
the verb tffi with agential suff. -er.

## tiller
tiller, п., bar, lever, fixed to the head of a rudder.
— ME. tiler, 'the wooden beam of a crossbow',
fr. MF. telier, 'weaver's beam', fr. OF., fr. ML.
telurium, fr. L. tela, 'web', which stands for
*texla- and is rel. to texere, 'to weave'. See text
and cp. tela, telary, toil, 'net'.

## tiller
tiller, п., shoot of a plant (now dial.)— OE. telgor,
telgra, 'twig, shoot', ft. telga, 'branch, shoot,'
which is rel. to ON. tjalga, OHG. zelga, of s.m.,
ON. telgja, 'to cut', taiga, 'the act of cutting', and
cogn. with Olr. dluigim, Ί cleave, split', Ir. delg,
'thorn', Lith. dalgis, 'scythe'.
Derivative: tiller, intr. v., to put forth new
shoots.

## tilley
tilley, also tffly, п., the seed of the croton oil plant.
— F. tilly, fr. ModL. tiglium in Croton tiglium,
'croton oil plant'. See tiglic.

## tilt
tilt, intr. v., to slope; tr. v., to cause to slope. —
ME. tilten, 'to fall; to cause to fall', fr. OE.
*tyltan, for *tieltan, fr. tealt, 'unsteady', whence
tealtian, 'to be unsteady'; rel. to ON. tyllast, 'to
trip', Swed. tulta, 'to waddle', Norw. tylta, 'to
walk on tiptoe', MDu. touteren (for *taltereri),
'to swing'.
Derivatives: tilt, п., a sloping position, tilt-ing,
n.

## tilt
tilt, intr. v., to joust. — Fr. tilt, 'to slope, to
assume a sloping position'.
Derivative: tilt, п., a joust.

## tilt
tilt, п., cover of a cart, awning. — ME. telt, tilt,
'tent', a collateral form of teld, fr. OE. teld, ge-
teld, rel. to ON. tjald, MDu. telt, OHG., MHG.,
G. zelt, 'tent', and to OE. beteldan, 'to cover'.
Cp. F. taudis, 'a miserable hovel', fr. OF. (se)
tauder, (se) taudir, 'to project (oneself), shelter
(oneself)', ft. Fr-ankish *teldan, which is rel. to
■OE. teld, etc. Cp. also toldo.
Derivative: tilt, tr. v., to cover with an awning.

## tilth
tilth, п., the act of tilling. — ME. tilth, fr. OE.
tild, fr. tilian, 'to cultivate (the land)'. See til],
'to cultivate', and cp. Du. teelt, 'a crop'. For the
ending see subst. suff. -th.

## Timalidae
Timalidae, n. pi., a family of singing birds (orni-
thol.) — ModL., of uncertain origin. For the
ending see suff. -Idae.

## timbal
timbal, п., 1) a kettledrum; 2) in entomol., a
vibrating membrane resembling a drumhead. —
F. timbale, changed (under the influence of cym-
bale, 'cymbal'), fr. MF. tamballe, which is a
blend of OF. (= F.) tambour, 'drum', and Sp.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:794 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: 767 | TIP -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:794 COLUMN:1 -->
atabaf, 'kettledrum'. See atabal and tambour and
cp. next word.

## timbale
timbale, п., a preparation of chicken, fish or other
food cooked in a drum-shaped mold. — F., 'dish
of fowl, fish, etc.', lit. 'kettledrum' (see prec.
word); so called from the rounded shape of the
mold in which it is cooked.

## timber
timber, n. — ME., fr. OE., 'timber, a building,
act of building', whence timbran, timbrian, 'to
build', rel. to OS. timbar, 'a building, room',
ON. timbr, Swed. timmer, Dan. temmer,
'timber', OFris. timber, MDu. timber, timmer,
'wood, building*, Du. timmer, 'room', OHG.
zimbar, MHG. zimber, 'timber, wooden
dwelling, dwelling, room', G. Zimmer, 'room*, Goth.
iimrjan, timbrjan, 'to build', timrja, 'builder'; fr.
I.-E. base *dem-, *demd-, 'to build', whence also
Gk. δέμειν, "to build'. See dome, *a building',
and cp. tame.

## timber
timber, tr. v. — ME. timbren, fr. OE. timbran,
timbrian, 'to build', fr. timber, 'timber, a
building, act of building'; rel. to OS. timbrian, ON.
timbra, Swed. iimra, Dan. tomre, OFris. timbria,
MDu., Du. timmeren, OHG. zimbaron, zim-
beren, MHG. zimberen, G. zimmern, 'to build',
which derive from the respective nouns. See
timber, n.

## timbre
timbre, п., the characteristic quality of a sound,
quality in the tone of an instrument or voice. —
F., 'a bell with striking hammer, quality of a
tone', fr. OF. tymbre, 'a kind of drum', which
was borrowed fr. MGk. τύμπαυον (pron. tym-
banon). 'kettledrum' (through the intermediary
forms *timbene, *timbne), fr. Gk. τύμπανον.
See tympannm and cp. next word.

## timbrel
timbrel, п., a kind of small drum. — Formed with
the dimin. sufT. -el fr. OF. tymbre, 'a kind of
drum'. See prec. word.
Derivatives: timbrel, tr. and intr. v., timbrel(l)-
ed, adj., timbrel(l)-er, n.

## time
time, n. — ME. time, fr. OE. tima, 'time, date,
period of time, lifetime', rel. to ON. ti-mi, 'time',
fr. Teut. *ti-, 'time', whence also OE. tid (fr.
Teut. *ti-di), 'time', prop, 'division of time', fr.
I.-E. base *dd-, *ddi-, *di-, *de-, 'to divide'. See
tide, п., and cp. words there referred to.
Derivatives: time, tr. v., tim-ed, adj., time-less,
adj., time-less-ly, adv., time-less-ness, п., tim-er,
п., time-ly, adj., time-li-ly, adv., time-li-ness, п.,
timeous (q.v.)

## timeous
timeous, tiinous, adj., early; timely (Scot.) — A
hybrid coined fr. time and -ons^a suff. of Latin
origin.

## timid
timid, adj., fearful. —L. timidus, 'faint-hearted,
cowardly, timid', fr. timere, 'to fear', which prob.
meant orig. 'to be in the dark, to grope about in
the dark', and is rel. to tenebrae (for *temebrae,
fr. *temesrae), 'darkness', temere, 'rashly, at
random', prop, 'in the dark', and cogn. with OI.
tamas-, 'darkness*, tamsrab, 'dark'. See temerity
and 1 st -id.
Derivatives: timid-ly, adv., timid-ness, n.

## timidity
timidity, n. — L. timiditds, 'faint-heartedness,
cowardice', fr. timidus. See timid and -ity.

## timist
timist, п., a musical performer considered
according to his ability to keep time. — A hybrid
coined fr. time and -ist, a suff. of Greek origin.

## timocracy
timocracy, п., I) according to Plato, a state in
which the love of honor is the ruling principle;
2) according to Aristotle, a state in which
political power is bestowed in proportion to the
property possessed. — ME., fr. OF. tymocracie
(F. timocratie), fr. ML. timocratia, fr. Gk.
τΐμοκρατία, compounded of τιμή, 'price,
worth, honor, esteem, respect', and -κρατία, fr.
κράτος, 'strength, power, rule'. The first
element is rel. to τΐειν, 'to place a value on, to
honor', fr. I.-E. base *qwei-, *qwi-, 'to respect,
consider, honor, pay, fine, expiate, punish,
avenge', whence also Gk. ποινή, 'bloodmoney,
fine, penalty, punishment'. See penal and words
there referred to and cp. the first element in
Timothy, Ti si phone and the second element in
xenotime. For the second element see -cracy.

## timocratie
timocratie, tlmocratical, adj. — Formed fr. Gk.
τΐμοκρατία (see prec. word) with suff. -ic, resp.
also -al.

## Timon
Timon, п., a misanthrope. — Fr. Timon, a

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:794 COLUMN:2 -->
misanthrope who lived in Athens at the time of the
Peloponnesian War (431-404). He is the hero of
Shakespeare's Timon of Athens.

## timoneer
timoneer, п., helmsman {rare). — F. timonier, fr.
OF., fr. timon, 'helm', fr. VL. *timonem, ace. of
*timo, altered fr. L. temo, 'beam, pole', which
stands for *tecmo and derives fr. I.-E. *tei]gh-,
'to draw, pull', whence also OHG. diksala,
MHG. dihsef, G. Deichsel, MDu. diesel, Du.
dissel, ON. frist, OS. thisla, OE. pixl, frisl(e),
'carriage pole, shaft*, OPruss. teansis, 'pole',
Avestic $ang-, OSlav. tegngti, 'to draw, pull'. It.
timone, and Sp. timon, 'helm*, also derive fr. VL.
*timonem. For the ending of timoneer see suff.
-eer.

## timorous
timorous, adj., timid. — ME., fr. MF. timoureus,
fr. OF., fr. Timor, 'fear*, fr. L. timorem, ace. oi
timor, 'fear*, fr. timere, 'to fear'. See timid and
-ous.
Derivatives: timorous-ly, adv., timorous-ness, n

## timous
timous, adj. — See timeous.

## timpano
timpano, п., a kettledrum. — It., fr. L. tympanum.
See tympanum.

## Timothy
Timothy, masc. PN. — F. Timothee, fr. L. Timo-
theus, fr. Gk. Τΐμό&εος, lit. 'honoring God', fr.
τϊμή, 'honor, respect', and θ-εός, 'God'. See
timocracy and theo-.

## timothy
timothy, п., also timothy grass, — Named after
Timothy Hanson, who lived in the 18th cent.
and introduced this grass in North America.

## tin
tin, n. — ME., fr. OE., rel. to ΟΝ., Dan., MLG.,
MDu., Du. tin, OHG., MHG. zin, G. Zinn, 'tin';
of unknown origin.
Derivatives: tin, tr. v., tinn-ed, adj., tinn-er, п.,
tinn-ery, п., tinn~ing, п., tinn-y, adj.

## Tinamidae
Tinamidae, n. pi., a family of birds, the tinamou
(ornitkol.) — ModL., formed with suff. -idae fr.
Tinamus, name of the type genus, fr. F. tinamou.

## tinamou
tinamou, п., any bird of the family Tinamidae
(ornitkol.) — F., fr. Galibi tinamu.

## tincal
tincal, п., also tincar, п., crude borax. — Arab.-
Pers. tinkdl, tinker, fr. Malay, tinkal, fr. OI.
tahkanah, 'borax', which is perh. related to the
"Tahkanah, a people mentioned in the Ramayana
and elsewhere.

## tinct
tinct, adj., tinged, colored. — L. tinctus, pp. of
tingere. See tinge.
Derivatives: tinct, n. (q.v.), tinct-ion, n.

## tinct
tinct, п., tint. — L. tinctum, neut. of tinctus, pp.
of tingere. See tinge and cp. taint, tent, 'a sweet
wine'.

## tinctorial
tinctorial, adj., pertaining to dyeing. — Formed
with adj. suff. -al fr. L. tinctdnus, fr. tinctor,
'dyer', fr. tinctus, pp. of tingere. See tinct, adj.

## tincture
tincture, п., tinge, tint. — L. tinctura, 'dyeing', fr.
tinctus, pp. of tingere. See tinge and -ure and cp.
tinct.
Derivative: tincture, tr. v.

## tindal
tindal, п., a petty officer of lascar soldiers (India).
— Malayalam tandal, fr. Telugu tandelu.

## tinder
tinder, п., inflammable material. — ME. tinder,
fr. OE. tynder, tyndre; rel. to ON. tundr, Dan.
tender, Swed. tunder, Du. tondel, tonder, OHG.
zuntara, zuntra, MHG., G. zunder, 'tinder',
which prob. derive from the respective verbs:
OE. -tendan (found only in compounds), 'to
kindle', ON. tenda, tendra, Dan. txnde, Swed.
tanda, 'to kindle', OHG. zunten, 'to inflame,
kindle', MHG. zunden, 'to burn, shine', MHG.,
G. zunden, 'to kindle', which are rel. to Goth.
tundnan, 'to be kindled, burn', tandjan, 'to
kindle*. Cp. also ON. tandri, 'spark, fire', and
the first element in tandstickor. OF. tondre,
'tinder', is a Teut. loan word.
Derivatives: tinder-ed, tinder-ish, tinder-y, adjs.

## tine
tine, п., prong of a fork. — ME. tind, fr. OE. tind,
rel. to ON. tindr, 'point, top, summit', OHG.
zint, 'point, spike', OHG. zinna, MHG., G.
zinne, 'pinnacle'. See zinc.
Derivative: tin-ed, adj.

## tinea
tinea, п., ringworm (a skin disease). — ME., fr.
L., 'a gnawing worm, moth'; of uncertain origin.
It possibly derives fr. I.-E. base *ti·, 'to melt,
moisten', and orig. denoted an insect that grows
in mud. See tiglic and cp. tinosa.

## ting
ting, intr. and tr. v. — Of imitative origin. Cp.tink.

## tinge
tinge, tr. v., to color slightly. — ME. tingen, fr
L. tingere, 'to wet, moisten; to soak in color.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:794 COLUMN:3 -->
dye', fr. I.-E. base *teng-, 'to moisten, soak',
whence also Gk. τέγγειν, 'to moisten', OHG.
thunkon, dunkon, MHG. tunken, dunken, G. tun-
ken, 'to steep, immerse'. Cp. tinct, tinctorial,
tincture, distain, extinguish, extinct, in ι i net ion,
stain, taint, tint. Cp. also dunk, Dlinker,
Derivative: tinge, п., a slight coloring.

## tingle
tingle, intr. v. — Freq. of ting. Cp. tink, tinkle.
Derivative: tingle, n.

## tink
tink, intr. and tr. v., tinkle (rare) — ME. tinken,
of imitative origin. Cp. tinker.

## tinker
tinker, п., a mender of kettles, pans, pots, etc. —
Formed from the verb tink with agential suff.
-er; cp. tinkle. The orig. meaning of tinker was
'one who makes a tinkling sound'.
Derivatives: tinker, intr. and tr. v., tinker-er, п.,
tinker-ly, adj.

## tinkle
tinkle, intr. v., to make ringing sounds; tr. v., to
cause to tinkle. — Formed fr. ME. tinklen, freq.
of tinken. See tink and freq. suff. -le.
Derivatives: tinkle, п., a tinkling sound,
tinkler, п., tinkl-ing, verbal п., tinkl-y, adj.

## tinnitus
tinnitus, п., ringing in the ears (med.) — L.
tinnitus, fr. tinnitus, pp. of tinnire, 'to ring, jingle',
from the imitative base *ten-, whence also
tondre, 'to thunder*. See thunder and cp. tintin-
nabulum and the first element in tintamarre.
tifiosa. п., a poisonous fish, Xurel lugubris. — Sp.,
prop. fern, of tinoso, 'scabby, scurvy', fr. L. ti-
neosus, 'wormy, full of moths', fr. tinea, 'worm,
moth'. See tinea.

## tinsel
tinsel, п., 1) a fabric of silk or wool interwoven
with glittering thin strips of met&\.(nistory); 2)
anything gaudy. — MF. estencelle, estincelle
(F. etincelle), 'spark', fr. OF., fr. VL. *stincilla,
formed with metathesis fr. L. scintilla, 'spark'.
See scintilla and cp. stencil.
Derivatives: tinsel, adj. and tr. v., tinsel-ly, adj.
and adv.

## tint
tint, п., color. — Fr. earlier tinct, п., fr. L.
tinctum, neut. of tinctus, pp. of tingere. See tinge and
cp. words there referred to. Cp. also the second
element in aquatint, monotiat.
Derivatives: tint, tr. v., tint-er, п., tint-ing, п.,
tint-y, adj.

## tintamarre
tintamarre, п., a confused noise, clamor. — F., a
compound whose first element derives fr. tinter,
'to ring*, fr. Late L. tinnitare, freq. of L. tinnire,
'to ring'; see tinnitus. The second element in
tinta-marre is of unknown origin.

## tintinnabular
tintinnabular, tintinnabulary, adj., related to, or
connected with, bells. — Formed fr. tintinna-
bulum with suff. -ar, resp. -ary.

## tintinnabulation
tintinnabulation, п., the ringing of bells. — Form-
fid from next word with suff. -ation.

## tintinnabulum
tintinnabulum, п., bell. — L. tintinnabulum, fr. tin-
tinndre, 'to ring, jingle, tinkle', formed through
reduplication (for the sake of emphasis) from
the base οι tinnire, of s.m., which is of imitative
origin. See tinnitus. For the suff. -ubulum cp.
acetabulum.

## tintometer
tintometer, п., an instrument for the
determination of tints. — A hybrid coined fr. tint, a word
of Latin origin, and Gk. μέτρον, 'measure*. See
meter, 'poetical rhythm*.

## tiny
tiny, adj. — ME. tine, tyne, of unknown origin.
Cp. teeny.
Derivative: tini-ness, n.

## -tion
-tion, suff. denoting action or state. — Fr. L. -tid,
gen. -tionis (either directly or through the
medium of OF. -cion or F. -tion), formed fr. the t-
formative element of the past participle and the
suff. -io, gen. -idnis. See -Ion and cp. -ation, -ition,
-sion.

## tip
tip, п., end, extremity of anything. — ME. tip,
tippe, rel. to Dan., Norw., MLG., MDu., Du.
tip, Swed. tipp, MHG. zip/, zipfel, G. Zipfel and
in gradational relationship to OE. txppa, 'tap'.
See tap, 'pipe', and cp. tippet.
Derivatives: tip, tr. v., to furnish with a tip,
tipper, n.

## tip
tip, tr. v., to touch lightly, tap. — Cp. LG. tippen,
G. tappen, 'to touch lightly', and E. tap, 'to
strike lightly'.
Derivative: tip, п., a slight touch.

## tip
tip, п., 1) gratuity; 2) a hint. — Of uncertain
origin.
Derivative: tip, tr. v., to give a tip to; intr. v., to

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:795 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: TIP | 768 -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:795 COLUMN:1 -->
give a tip or tips.

## tip
tip, tr. v., to cause to tilt, to upset, overthrow;
intr. v., to tilt. — ME. tipen, typen, 'to
overthrow*, of uncertain origin. Cp. tipsy.

## Tiphia
Tiphia, n.,, a genus of insects, the wasp
(entomology)· — ModL., fr. Gk. τίφη, 'a kind of insect,
the water spider', which is of uncertain origin.
For the ending see 1st suff. -fa. Cp. Tipula.

## tippet
tippet, п., a scarf. — ME. tipet, dimin. of tip, 'a
point'. See tip, п., 'end'.
Derivative: tippet, tr. and intr. v.

## tipple
tipple, tr. v., to cause to fall; intr. v., to tip over,
tilt. — Formed with the freq. surT. -le fr. tip, *to
cause to tilt; to tilt'.
Derivatives: tipple, п., a structure for emptying
cars by tipping, tippl-er, n.

## tipple
tipple, tr. and intr. v., to drink frequently. — Cp.
Norw. tipla, *to drink in small quantities, to
drip'; of uncertain origin.

## tipstaff
tipstaff, п., a staff tipped with metal. — For tipped
staff.

## tipster
tipster, п., a seller of tips. — Formed fr. tip, *gra-
tuity; hint', with surT. -ster.

## tipsy
tipsy, adj., mildly drunk. — Fr. tip, 'to cause to
tilt, to upset'. For the suff. cp. tricksy.

## tiptoe
tiptoe, n. — ME. tiptoo, 'the tip of one's toe', fr.
tip, tippe, *tip\ and too, 'toe'. See tip, 'end', and
toe.
Derivatives: tiptoe, adj. and intr. v.

## Tipula
Tipula, п., a genus of insects, typical of the
family Tipulidae, the crane flies (zool.) — L. tippula,
tipula, 'water spider', a loan word fr. Gk. τίφη,
'water spider'. See Tiphia.

## Tipularia
Tipularia, п., a genus of plants, the crane-fly
orchid (bot.) — ModL., formed fr. L. tipula, 'the
water spider* (see Tipula); so called from the
alleged resemblance of the flower to the water
spider. For the ending see 1st suff. -aria.

## tirade
tirade, п., a long, violent speech, esp. one of
denunciation. — F., fr. It. tirata, 'volley', lit. 'a
pulling, drawing, lengthening; a long speech', fr.
tirare, 'to pull, draw', which, together with MF.
(= F.) tirer, Provenc., Sp., Port, tirar, of s.m., is
of uncertain origin. Cp. tirailleur, franc-tireur,
retire. Cp. also terry.

## tirailleur
tirailleur, п., sharpshooter. — F., fr. tirailler, 'to
skirmish', fr. tirer, 'to pull, draw, shoot*. See
tire, 'to pull*, and cp. retire.

## tire
tire, tr. v., to fatigue, weary; intr. v., to become
weary. — ME. tyren, fr. OE. tiorian, teorian, of
unknown origin.
Derivatives: tir-ed, adj., tir-ed-ly, adv., tir-ed-
ness, п., tire-less, adj., tire-less-ly, adv., tire-less-
ness, п., tire-some, adj., tire-some-ly, adv., tire-
some-ness, п., tir-ing, adj., tir-ing-ly, adv.

## tire
tire, tr. v., to attire. — ME. tiren, aphetic for
atiren. See attire.
Derivative: tire, п., apparel.

## tire
tire, also tyre, п., a band placed around a wheel.
— The same a presc. word, the tire being
regarded as the 'attire' or 'apparel' of the wheel.
Derivative: tire, tr. v., to put a tire on.

## tiro
tiro, n. — The better spelling of tyro.

## tirocinium
tirocinium, п., the first service of a young soldier;
lack of experience. — L. tirocinium, formed fr.
tiro, 'young soldier; recruit; beginner' (see
tyro), on analogy of latrocinium, 'service of
mercenaries'. Suff. -cinium is prob. cogn. with
Gk. -κονος in διάκονος, 'servant'. See deacon
and words there referred to and cp. esp. the
second element in larceny.

## tirralirra
tirralirra, n. — Imitative of a bird's note.

## Tirshatha
Tirshatha, п., title of the Persian governor of
Judaea, applied to Nehemiah (Bible), always
preceded by the article: hat-Tirshdthd. — Lit.
'the revered one', fr. Avestic tarshta, 'feared,
revered', which is rel. to 01. trasati, 'trembles',
trastdh, 'trembling', and cogn. with Gk. τρέειν,
'to tremble', L. terrere, 'to frighten'. See terrible.

## tisane
tisane, п., decoction, medicinal tea. — F., fr. L.
lisana, fr. Gk. πτισάνη, 'barley gruel', lit.'crush-
ed barley'. See ptisan.

## Tishri
Tishri, п., name of the seventh Jewish month. —
Mishnaic Heb. Tishri, Akkad. Tashritu, name of
the seventh, orig. the first, month of the year,
lit. 'beginning*, fr. shurru, 'to begin, open,
initiate', which is rel. to Aram., Syr., Mand. sh rd,
'he began; he loosened; he dwelled, lodged,

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:795 COLUMN:2 -->
stayed, abode', Heb. shard, 'he let loose (the
thunder)', Ethiop. sardya, 'he condoned (a sin)'.

## Tisiphone
Tisiphone, п., one of the Erinyes (Furies) (Greek
mythol) — L., fr. Gk. Τΐσιφόνη, lit. 'avenger of
murder', fr. -iatc, 'payment, punishment,
vengeance', and φόνος, 'murder'. Gk. τίσις derives
fr. τίνειν, 'to pay a price, punish, avenge', which
is related to τίειν, 'to place a value on, to honor',
τιμή, 'price, worth, honor, esteem, respect', fr.
I.-E. base *qwei-, *qwt-, 4o respect, consider,
honor, pay, expiate, punish'; see penal and cp.
the first element in timocracy, Timothy. Gk.
φόνος stands for *gwhonos, fr. I.-E. base *gwhen-,
'to strike', whence also L. de-fendere, 'to ward
off, defend'. See defend and cp. words there
referred to.

## tissue
tissue, n. — ME. tissu, fr. OF. (— F.) tissu,
'woven fabric', pp. of tistre (F. titre, tisser), fr.
L. texere, 'to weave'; introduced into medical
terminology by the French anatomist and
physiologist Marie-Francois-Xavier Bichal (1771-
1802) about the year 1800. See text and cp.
words there referred to.
Derivatives: tissue, tr. v., tissu-ed, adj., tissue-y,
adj.

## tit
tit, п., teat. — ME. title, fr. OE. tin, tit. See teat.

## tit
tit, п., a small or poor horse; a girl. — Orig. a
child's word denoting anything small. Cp. Icel.
tittr, Norw. tita, 'a little bird', and next word.
Cp. also the first element in titbit, titlark, and
the second element in tomtit.

## tit
tit, п., any of various small birds. — Back
formation fr. titmouse.

## tit
tit, п., tap; blow; now inly in the phrase 'tit for
tat'. — Of imitative origin.

## Titan
Titan, п., ]) (Greek mythol.) one of the primitive
gigantic deities, the children of Uranus and
Gaea; 2) the sun god, Helios, son of the Titan
Hyperion; 3) any person or thing of enormous
size or power. — L., fr. Gk. Τΐταν, 'a Titan*,
orig. 'god of the sun', and derived fr. τΐτώ, *sun,
day', which is prob. a loan word from Asia
Minor. Cp. titanium.

## titan-
titan-, form of titano- before a vowel.

## titunate
titunate, п., any salt of titanic acid (chem.) —
Formed fr. titan- with chem. suff. -ate.

## Titanesque
Titanesque, adj., resembling a Titan. — A hybrid
coined fr. Gk. Τΐταν (see Titan) and -esque, a
suff. of Italian, ult. Teut., origin.

## Titaness
Titaness, п., a female Titan. — A hybrid coined
fr. Gk. Τΐταν (see Titan) and 1st suff. -ess, fr.
F. suff. -esse. The correct form would be Titanis
or Titanisssa.

## titania
titania, п., titanium dioxide (chem.) — ModL.
See titanium.

## Titanic
Titanic, adj., 1) pertaining to, or like, the Titans;
2) (not cap.) huge, gigantic. — Lit. 'resembling
a Titan'. Formed fr. Titan with adj. suff. -ic.

## titanic
titanic, adj., pertaining to titanium (chem.) —
Formed fr. titanium with adj. suff. -ic.

## titanite
titanite, п., a mineral containing titanic acid. —
G. Titanit, coined by Klaproth in 1795. See next
word. The ending -it goes back to Gk. -ίτης;
see subst. suff. -ite.
Derivative: titanit-ic, adj.

## titanium
titanium, п., name of a metallic element (chem.)
— ModL., coined by the German chemist
Martin Heinrich Klaproth (1743-1817) in 1796
fr. L. Titdni or Titdnes, fr. Gk. Τιτάνες (pi. of
Τΐταν), the sons of Uranus and Gaea, in
reference to another element discovered by him six
years before and called by him uranium. See
Titan and cp. uranium. For the ending of titanium
see 2nd -ium.
Derivative: titan-ic, adj.

## titano-
titano-, before a vowel titan-, combining form for
titanium.

## Titanomachy
Titanomachy, п., the war between the Titans and
the Olympian gods (Greek mythol.) — Gk.
Τιτανομαχία, compounded of Τιτάνες, pi. of
Τΐταν, 'Titan', and -μαχία, fr. μάχη, 'battle'.
See Titan and -machy.

## titbit
titbit, п., a choice morsel. — Lit. 'a little bit', fr.
tit, 'anything small', and the noun bit.

## titer
titer, titre, п., the strength of a solution used in
titration (chem.) — F. titre, 'title; strength', fr.
L. titulus. See title.

## tithe
tithe, n. — ME. tethe, tithe, fr. OE. teogoda, teoda,

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:795 COLUMN:3 -->
'tenth', fr. tien, tyn, ten, 'ten*. Cp. ON. tlunde,
OHG. zehanto, zehendo, 'tenth; tithe', MHG.
zehende, zende, tenth, tithe*, G. zehnte, 'tenth',
Zehnte, 'tithe*, Goth, taikunda, 'tenth', and see
ten, tenth. Cp. also teind. Co. also decimal and
words there referred to.

## tithe
tithe, tr. v. — ME. tithen, fr. OE. teodian, fr.
teoda, 'tenth'. See tithe, n.
Derivatives: tith-able, adj., tith-er, п., tithing
(q.v.)

## tithing
tithing, п., 1) the act of tithing; 2) ten households
forming an administrative unit. — ME. tething,
tithing, fr. OE. teodung, 4a group often men', fr.
teodian, *to tithe'. See tithe, v., and -ing, suff.
forming verbal nouns.

## titian
titian, adj., reddish yellow. — Named after the
Venetian painter Titian (anglicized form of
Tiziano Vecellio), 1477-1576, in allusion to the
circumstance that he often used this color for
painting the hair.

## titillate
titillate, tr. v., to tickle. — L. titillatus, pp. of
titilldre, 'to tickle', of imitative origin. For the
ending see verbal suff. -ate.
Derivatives: titillat-er, п., titillat-ing, adj.,
titillating-ly, adv., titillation (q.v.), titillat-ive,
adj., titillat-or, п., titillat-ory, adj.

## titillation
titillation, n. — ME. titillacione, fr. L. titilldtid,
gen. -onis, fr. titillatus, pp. of titilldre. See prec.
word and -ion.

## titivate
titivate, tittivate, tr. and intr. v., to dress up
(colloq) — Fr. earlier tidivate, tiddivate, prob.
formed from the adjective tidy in imitation of
cultivate and other verbs of Latin origin ending
in -ivate.
Derivatives: tit(t)ivat-ion, п., tit(t)ivat-or, n.

## titlark
titlark, п., pipit. — Lit. *a small lark', fr. tit,
'anything little', and lark.

## title
title, n. — ME. titel, title, fr. OF. title (in French
dissimilated into titre), fr. L. titulus, 'inscription,
superscription, title', which is of uncertain
origin. Cp. til, tilde, titer, titration, tittle, titular,
entitle, intitule.

## title
title, tr. v. — ME. titelen, fr. titel, title, 'title*. See
title, n.
Derivatives: titl-ed, adj., titl-er, п., titl-ing, n.

## titmouse
titmouse, п., any of a number of small birds
including the chickadee. — ME. titemose, tytmase,
compounded of tit, 'anything small' (see tit, 'a
small horse'), and OE. mdse, 'titmouse', which
is rel. to MDu. mese, Du. mees, OHG. meisa,
MHG., G. meise, Swed. mes, Norw. meis, ON.
meisingr, Frankish *meisinga (whence F. тё-
sange), 'titmouse*, and cogn. with W. mwyalch,
OCo. moelh, Bret, mouialc'h, 'blackbird'. E.
titmouse was influenced in form by mouse. Cp
coahnouse.

## titrate
titrate, tr.. v., to determine the strength of a
chemical solution by observing the amount of a
liquid of known strength (called the standard
solution), which it is necessary to add to the
solution in order to produce a definite chemical
reaction. — Formed with verbal suff. -ate fr. F.
titrer, 'to give a title to; to determine the
strength of, fr. titre, 'title; right; fineness (of
coinage), strength, titer (of solution)', fr. OF.
title. See titer.
Derivative: titrat-'ющ n.

## titre
titre, n. — A var. of titer.

## titter
titter, intr. v., to giggle; п., the act of tittering. —
Of imitative origin.

## tittle
tittle, п., mark placed over a letter. — ME. titel,
title, fr. L. titulus. See title. For sense
development cp. tilde.

## tittle-tattle
tittle-tattle, n. — Antiphonic reduplication of
tattle.

## tittup
tittup, intr. v., to behave in a lively manner; to
caper. — Of imitative origin.
Derivatives: tittup, п., tittupp-y, adj.

## titubant
titubant, adj., staggering, tottering. — L. titubdns,
gen. -antis. See next word.

## titubate
titubate, intr. v., to stagger, totter. — L. titubdtus,
pp. of titubdre, 'to stagger, totter, reel', which is
of imitative origin.

## titubation
titubation, n. — L. litubatid, gen. -onis, fr.
titubdtus, pp. of titubdre. See prec. word and -ion.

## titular
titular, adj., 1) pertaining to a title; 2) held in
virtue of a title; 3) existing only in title. — L.
*tituldris, fr. titulus, 'title'. See title and -ar.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:796 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: 769 | TOILET -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:796 COLUMN:1 -->

## titulary
titulary, adj., titular; п., a person who holds a
title. — See prec. word and -y (representing L.
-ни). Formed fr. L. titulus, 'title' (see title), with
adj. suff. -ary.

## Titus
Titus, masc. PN. — L. For the literal meaning of
this name see Kerenyi in Glotta 22, 40 (quoted
by Walde-Hofmann, LEW., 11, 686, s.v. titulus).

## tityre-tu
tityre-tu, п., name of a gang of ruffians in London
in the time of the Restoration. — Fr. L. Tityre,
tu ("O Tityrus, thou"), the opening word of
Virgil's first eclogue.

## tizzy
tizzy, п., a sixpence (slang).— Corruption of
tester, name of coins.

## tmesis
tmesis, п., separation of a compound word by the
intervention of a word or words (gram.) — Gk.
τμήσις, 'a cutting', fr. *tm-, zero degree of I.-E.
base *tem-, 'to cut"1, whence τέμνειν, 'to cut',
τομή, 'a cutting'. See tome and cp. words there
referred to.

## T.N.T.
T.N.T., trinitrotoluene. — Abbreviation of the
initials of the elements of /ri/iitro/oluene.

## to
to, prep. — ME., fr. OE. to, rel. to OS., OFris. to,
Du. toe, OHG. zuo, zua, zo, MHG. zuo, G. zu,
'to', from the I.-E. pronominal base *do-, 'to,
toward, upwards', whence also L. do- in donee,
'as long as, while', and -do in quando, 'when*.
Cp. I.-E. *dd in OSlav. do, 'as far as, to', and in
OL. -do, -du (in endo, endu, 'in')- Cp. also I.-E.
*de in Avestic -da (as in vaesm η-da, 4o the
house'), Gk. -8ε [as in οΐκαδε, οϊκόνδε, 'to
one's home, homeward', and in Άθήναζε (for
*Ά&ανανζδε), 'to or toward Athens*], and in
L. -de (as in inde, 'thence, from there', unde,
'whence, from where4). Cp. too, which is a
doublet of to, and tattoo, 'drumbeat'. Cp. also
de-, endo-, indigene.
Derivative: to, adv.

## toad
toad, п., a tailless froglike amphibian. — ME.
tade, tode, fr. OE. tade, shortened form of
tadige, tadie; of unknown origin. Cp. tadpole,
toady.
Derivatives: toad-ish, adj., toady, adj. (q.v.)

## toadeater
toadeater, п., a flattering parasite, — Orig. a
quack doctor's assistant who pretended to eat
toads to show his master's skill at curing him of
their alleged poison.

## toady
toady, adj., full of toads; resembling a toad. —
Formed fr. toad with suff. -y (fr. OE. -ig).

## toady
toady, п., a toadeater. — Shortened fr. toadeater
(q.v.)
Derivative: toady, tr. v.

## toast
toast, tr. and intr. v. — ME. tosten, fr. MF.
foster, 'to roast', fr. OF., fr. VL. *tostdre (whence
also It. tostare, Sp., Port, tostar, 'to roast'), freq.
of L. torrere (pp. tostus), 'to parch, roast', fr.
I.-E. base *trs-, 'to be dry', whence also OL.
torrus (for *torsus), 'dry', L. terra (for *tersa),
'earth', lit. 'dry land*. See terra and cp. words
there referred to.
Derivatives: toast, n. (q.v.), toast-ee, п., toast-er,
n.

## toast
toast, n. — ME. toste, fr. tosten. See toast, v.
Derivatives: toast-y, adj., toasti-ness, n.

## tobacco
tobacco, n. — Sp., Port, tabaco, fr. Taino
(Caribbean) tabaco, 'pipe for smoking; roll of tobacco
leaves'; the English form of the word was prob.

## influenced by Tobago
influenced by Tobago, name of a West Indian
island; cp. F. tabac, It. tobacco, G. Tabak, Du.

## tabak
tabak, Hind, tambaka, which all derive ult. fr.
Taino tabaco. Cp. also tabatiere.

## tobacconist
tobacconist, n. — A hybrid coined from prec.

## word
word, a euphonic n, and -ist, a suff. of Greek
origin.

## Tobiah
Tobiah, Tobias, masc. PN. — Late L. Tobias, fr.
Gk. Τωβίας, Τωβείας. fr. Heb. Tobhiyyah, lit.
'The Lord is my good*. Heb. tobh, 'good', is rel.

## to Arab
to Arab, tdba, 'was pleasant to the senses',

## Aram
Aram, t ebh, tabh, Syr. te'bk, tobh, 'was good',

## Ugar. tb
Ugar. tb, 'good', tb'n, 'goodness', Akkad. tabu,
'to be good, kind, joyful'. Cp. the second word
in yom tob. For the second element in Tobkiyyah
cp. Elijah and words there referred to. Cp. also

## Toby
Toby,

## toboggan
toboggan, п., a kind of long, flat-bottomed sled.
— Micmac tobagun, 'a sled made of skin'.
Derivatives: toboggan, intr. v., toboggan-er, п.,
tobogganist (q.v.)

## tobogganist
tobogganist, n. — A hybrid coined from prec.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:796 COLUMN:2 -->
word and -ist, a suff. of Creek origin.

## Toby
Toby, masc. PN. — ME., fr. Late L. Tobias. See
Tobiah.

## toby
toby, п., also toby jug. — From the PN. Toby. For
the use of PN.s to form names of vessels cp.
jack, jeroboam.

## tuccata
tuccata, п., an improvised composition for
pianoforte or organ (music). —It., prop. fem. pp. of
toccare, 'to touch', used as a noun. Toccata lit.
means 'a keyboard that is touched'; see touch,

## toccatella
toccatella, п., a kind of short toccata (music). —
It., dimin. of toccata. For the ending see suff.
-ella.

## toccatina
toccatina, toccatino, п., a short toccata (music).
— Dimin. of toccata. Cp. prec. word.

## Tocharian
Tocharian, Tokharian, п., 1) one of a people
living in Central Asia about 500-1000 of the
C.E.; 2) the language spoken by this people;
adj., pertaining to the Tocharians or their an-
guage. — Formed with suff. -ian on analogy of
G. tocharisch, which was adopted by E. Sieg
and W. Siegling fr. L. Tochari, Gk. Τόχαροι, a
people who lived in the basin of the upper Oxus
in the 2nd cent, of the C.E., and suff. -isck (see
adj. suff. -ish). This identification of the I.-E.
language discovered during the last decade of
the ]9th cent., with the language of the Tochari,
that was orig. suggested by F.W.K. Muller (in
Beitrag zur genaueren Bestimmung der unbekann-
ten Sprachen Mittelasiens in Sitzungsberichte
der Preueischen Akademie der Wissenschaften,
Berlin, 1907, p. 958 foil.) is obviously erroneous.

## Tocharish
Tocharish, n. and adj., Tocharian. — G.
tocharisch. See prec. word.

## tocher
tocher, п., dot. dowry (Scot.) — OGael. tochar
(whence Gael, tochradh), rel. to Olr. tochur, lit.
'that which is assigned', fr. cuir, 'to put, assign'.
Derivative: tocher, tr. v., to provide with a dot.

## -tocia
-tocia, -tokia, combining form meaning
'childbirth', as in dystocia, dystokia (obstetrics). —
Medical L. -tocia, fr. Gk. -τοκία, fr. τόκος,
'childbirth, parturition'. See toco- and cp.
dystocia, oxytocia,

## toco
toco, also toko, n,, a thrashing or flogging
(English Slang). — Prop, imper. of Hind, tokna, 'to
censure, blame',
toco-j combining form meaning 'childbirth'
(obstetrics). — Gk. τόκο-, fr. τόκος, 'childbirth,
parturition', whence τοκεύς, 'father', in the pi.
'parents'; in gradational relationship to τέκος,
'child', and to τίκτειν (for *τ£-τκειν), 'to
bring forth, bear'. See thane and cp. tecno-,
anatocism, atocia, thelytokous.

## tocology
tocology, tokology, п., obstetrics, midwifery. —
Compounded of toco- and Gk. -λογία, fr.
-λόγος, 'one who speaks (in a certain manner);
one who deals (with a certain topic)*. See -logy.

## tocsin
tocsin, п., 1) an alarm bell; 2) its sound. — F.,
'alarm bell', fr. OF touquesain, fr. OProven?.
tocasenh, lit. 'touch the bell*, fr. tocar, 'to touch'
(fr. VL. *toccare), and senh, 'bell' (fr. Late L.
signum, 'sign; bell', fr. L. signum, 'sign'). See
touch and sign,

## tod
tod, п., a fox (Scot.) — Lit. 'the bushy-tailed
animal', fr. tod, 'bush',

## tod
tod, п., bush, bundle, weight of wool (archaic or
dial.) — ME. todd, prob. fr. LG. tot, tod,
'bundle', which is rel. to Du. Xodde, 'rag, tatter',
and to ON. toddf, 'bush, bundle, weight of
wool', OHG. zata, zota, zotta (fem.), zotto
(masc), MHG. zote, zotte, (masc. and fem.), G.
Zotte, (fem.), 'bundle, tuft of hair', and to LG.
tater, ON. totturr, 'rag'; see tatter. Olt. tattera,
'secohd hand articles; trifle', and It. zazza,
zazzera, 'long hair of the head', are Teut. loan
words.

## today
today, adv. and n. — ME., fr. OE. tdd&ge (fr. to,
'to', and dxge, dat. oidxg, 'day'), also (unflect-
ed) todzg. See to and day and cp. tonight,
tomorrow.
Derivatives: today, п., today-ish, adj.

## toddle
toddle, intr. v., to go with short unsteady steps,
as a child. — Prob. a var. of Scot, tottle, 'to
walk with short steps', which is a freq. of
totter.
Derivatives: toddle, п., toddl-er, n.

## toddy
toddy, п., 1) the sweet juice of the palmyra tree;
2) a drink made of spirit, sugar, lemon and hot

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:796 COLUMN:3 -->
water. — Hind, tori, 'juice of the palmyra tree',
fr. tdf, 'palmyra tree', fir. OI. talah, 'palmyra
tree', which is perh. of -Dravidian origin. Cp.
Kannada tar, Telegu td^u.

## to-do
to-do, n. — Compounded of to and do. For sense
development cp. F.'affaire, 'business, affair', fr.
a, 'to', and/aire, 'to do' (see affair).

## tody
tody, п., a small brightcolored West Indian bird.
— F. todier, fr. L. todus, a kind of small bird.

## toe
toe, n. — ME. Га, to, too, fr. OE. tahe, tu, rel. to
ON. to, Dan. taa, Swed. ta, OFris. tane, MDu.
te, ten, Du. teen, OHG. zecha, zeha, MHG. zehe,
G. Zehe, 'toe', lit. 'that which shows', fr. I.-E.
base *deifc-, 'to show', whence also Gk. δεικνύ-
vat, 'to show*, L. dicere, 'to show, to say*,
digitus, 'finger', OE. tsecan, 'to show', Goth ga-
teihan, 'to announce'. See teach and cp. digit.
Derivatives: toe, tr. v., to-ed, adj.

## toff
toff, п., a swell, a dandy (slang). — Fr. earlier
toft, a var. of tuft,

## toffee
toffee, п., taffy. — See taffy.

## Tofieldia
Tofieldia,n., a genus of plants, the false asphodel
(bot.) — ModL., named after- the English
botanist Thomas Tofield (1730-79). For the ending
see 1st suff. -ia.

## toft
toft, n. (now dial.), 1) a homestead; 2) a knoll,
hill. — ME., fr. OE. toft, fr. ON. topt (whence
Dan. and Swed. toft, 'croft'), which is prob.
cogn. with the first element of Gk. δά-πεδον,
'ground about a house' (for *dm-pedom), and
with Qk. δόμος, L. domus, 'house'. See dome,
'a building'.

## tog (usually in the pi. togs)
tog (usually in the pi. togs), clothes. — Prob.
from next word.
Derivatives: tog, tr. v., tog-less, adj.

## toga
toga, n. — L. toga, 'a garment', lit. *a covering',
in gradational relationship to tegere, 'to cover'.
See thatch, п., and cp. tegument and words there
referred to.
Derivative: toga-ed, adj. ,

## togated
togated, adj., togaed; dignified. — Formed with
1st suff. -ed fr. L. togdtus, 'wearing the toga', fr.
toga. See toga.

## together
together, adv. — ME. togedere, togidere, fr.
tagadere, togzedere, togzdre, compounded of to,
'to', and gadere, gxdere, gxdre, 'together'. See
to and gather and cp. altogether.
Derivative: together-ness, n.

## toggery
toggery, п., clothes (colloq.) — Formed fr. tog
with suff. -ery.

## toggle
toggle, п., a metal pin inserted between the
strands of a rope. — Prob. a collateral form of
dial, tuggle, which is a freq. of tug.
Derivative: toggle, tr. v., to provide with a
toggle or toggles.

## togs
togs, n. pi. — See tog.

## tohubohu
tohubohu, п., chaos, utter confusion. — F. tohu-
bohu, Heb. tohH wabkSku (Gen. 1:2),
'emptiness and wasteness'. Heb. tShu, 'emptiness', is
rel. to Ugar. thw, ofs.m., and prob. also to Arab.
tih, 'desert, waste', tdha, 'he went astray', and
to Aram, (also Bibl. Aram.), and Syr. tewah,
'was astonished, was amazed'. Heb. bohu,
emptiness, wasteness', developed fr. *buhw. It is
prob. rel. to Arab. bdhiyat 'was empty'.

## toil
toil, п., net, snare. — MF. (= F.) toiles, 'nets,
toils', pi. of toile, 'linen, cloth' (whence toile
d'Oraignee, 'cobweb'), fr. L. tela, 'woven stuff',
which stands for *texlat fr. L. texere, *to weave'.
See text and cp. words there referred to. Cp.
also toilet,

## toil
toil, intr. v., to work hard. — ME. toilen, 'to
argue, struggle', fr. AF. toiller, fr. OF. toeillier,
toillier, 'to pull or drag about; to. stir, mix,
trouble, fr. L. tudiculare, 'to stir', fr. tudlcula, 'a
small machine for bruising olives', fr. tudes, gen.
tuditis, 'hammer', which is rel. to tundere, -'to
strike'. See tund.
Derivatives: toil-er, п., toil-ing, adj., toil-ing-ly,
adv.

## toil
toil, п., hard work, labor. — ME. toile, 'argument,
struggle', fr. AF. toyl, fr. OF. toeil, tooil,
'battle, trouble', fr. toeillier, toillier. See toil, v.
Derivatives: toil-ful, adj., toil-ful-ly, adv., toil-

## ful-ness
ful-ness, п., toil-some, adj., toil-some-ly, adv.,

## toil-some-ness
toil-some-ness, n.

## toilet
toilet, n. — MF. (— F.) toilette, dimin. of toile,
'cloth'. See toil, 'a net*, and -et, -ette.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:797 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: TOISON | 770 -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:797 COLUMN:1 -->
Derivatives: toilet, intr. v., to make one's toilet,
toilet-ed, adj., toilet-ry, n.

## toison
toison, п., fleece. — F., fr. Late L. tonsidnem, ace.
of tdnsio, 'a sheep-shearing', fr. L. tdnsus, pp.
of tondere, 'to shear'. See tonsure. Hence toison
d'or, *the Golden Fleece'.

## Tokay
Tokay, п., a rich kind of Hungarian wine. —
From Тока) (earlier spoiled Tokay), a town in
Hungary.

## token
token, n. — ME. taken, token, fr. OE. tden, 'sign,
token', rel. to OS. tekan, ON. teikn, 'sign (in
the zodiac), omen, token', Swed. tecken, Dan.
tegn, OFris., MLG., MDu. teken, Du. teken,
OHG. zeihhan, MHG.( G. zeichen, Goth, taikn,
'sign, token', fr. I.-E. base *deik-, *to show'.
See teach and cp. words there referred to. Cp.
also tache, 'spot on the skin'.

## Tokharian
Tokharian, n. and adj. — A var. of Tocharian.

## toko
toko, п., a thrashing of flogging. — See toco,

## tokology
tokology, n. — See tocology.

## tol-
tol-, combining form. — See tolu-.

## tola
tola, п., an Indian weight. — Hind, told, fr. OI.
tula, 'a balance', whence tulayati, 'lifts up,
raises, weights'; cogn. with L. tollere, 'to lift up,
raise', toferdre, 'to bear, support'. See tolerate
and cp. tuel, talent.

## tol booth
tol booth, tol I booth, п., — a booth or other place
for paying tolls. Compounded of toll, Чах', and
booth.

## told
told, past tense and pp. of tell. — ME. tolde, resp.
told, fr. OE. talde, resp. getald, past tense, resp.
pp. of tellan. See tell, v.

## tol do
tol do, п., an Indian tent in S. America. — Sp., fr.
Teut. *teld-, 'tent'. Cp. OE. teld, 'tent', and see
tilt, 'cover'.

## Toledo
Toledo, п., also Toledo blade, sword blade of fine
temper. — Prop., 'sword blade made at Toledo'
in Spain. For sense development cp.bayonet,bilbo.

## tolerable
tolerable, adj. — ME. tollerabill, fr. L. tolerdbilis,
'bearable, endurable' [whence also MF. (= F.)
tolerable], fr. tolerdre. See tolerate and -able.
Derivatives: tolerabil-ity, п., tolerable-ness, п.,
tolerabl-y, adv.

## tolerance
tolerance, n. — MF. tolleraunce, fr. MF. (= F.)
tolerance, fr. L. tolerantia, fr. tolerdns, gen.
-antis. See next word.

## tolerant
tolerant, adj. — F. tolerant, fr. L. tolerantem, ace.
of tolerdns, pres. part.of tolerdre. See next word
and -ant.
Derivative: tolerant-ly, adv.

## tolerate
tolerate, tr. v. — L. toleratus, pp. of tolerate, 'to
bear, support, endure, tolerate', from the stem
of tollere, 'to lift up, raise', which is cogn. with
Gk. τολμαν, 'to carry, bear', τελαμών, 'a broad
strap for bearing something', ταλάσσαι (aor.),
'to bear*, τλήμων, 'patient, reckless, miserable',
τληναί. (aor.), 'to suffer, endure', τάλαντον,
'balance (in the pi., a pair of scales); a weight',
τάλας, gen. τάλανος, and τάλαντος, 'bearing,
suffering', "Α-τλας, 'the Bearer (scil. of
Heaven)', πολύ-τλας, 'much enduring', L. latus (for
*tlatos) 'borne' (used as pp. of ferre, 'to bear,
carry'), OI. tula, 'balance', tulayati, 'lifts up,
weighs', Toch. В tal-, A tal-, 'to lift', tlassi, 'to
lift, carry', cakal, 'he lifted', Arm. toium, Ί
allow, suffer, bear', Lith. tiltas, 'bridge', Goth.
pulan, ON. pola, OE. polian, 'to endure, suffer'.
All these words derive fr. I.-E. base *tel-, *tol-,
*tal~, *//-, 'to bear, carry, endure, suffer'. Cp.
ablation, ablative, allative, At al ant a, atlantes,
Atlantic, Atlas, collate, collation, delate,
dilatory, elate, extol, illation, oblate, prelate, prolate,
relate, relation, sublate, sublation, superlative,
tael, talent, Tantalus, telamon, Telamon, thole,
'to endure', tola, toll, 'tax', toll, 'to take away',
tralatitious, translate, translation and the second
element in acceptation, fiddle, legislate.
Derivatives: toleration (q.v.), tolerat-ive, adj.,
tolerat-or, n.

## toleration
toleration, n. — F. toleration, fr. L. tolerdtionem,
ace. of tolerdtio, 'a bearing, supporting,
enduring', fr. toleratus, pp. of tolerdre. Seeprec word
and -ion.

## tolerationist
tolerationist, п., a person who advocates
toleration, esp. in religion. — A hybrid coined from
prec. word and -ist, a suif. of Greek origin.

## tolidine
tolidine,tolidin, п., any of several isomeric bases of
toluene {chem.) — Coined fr. tol- and suff. -idin(e).

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:797 COLUMN:2 -->

## toll
toll, п., tax. — ME. tol, fr. OE. toll, rel. to OS.
tolna, ON. tollr, Dan. told, Swed. full, OFris.
tolen, tolne, OHG., MHG. zol, G. Zoll;
borrowed fr. Late L. toloneum, 'custom house', which
was formed with vowel assimilation fr. earlier
telonium, teloneum, fr. Gk. τελωνεΐον, 'toll
house', fr. τελώνης, 'tax collector', fr. τέλος,
'tax' (whence also εΰ-τελής, 'easily paid for,
cheap', πολυ-τελής, 'very expensive, costly',
ά-τελής, 'free from tax or tribute'), which is
cogn. with ταλάσσαι (aor.), 'to bear, support';
see tolerate. For sense development cp. Gk.
φόρος, 'tax, tribute', which is rel. to φέρειν, 'to
bear, carry'. Cp. the first element in tolbooth
and in zollverein.
Derivatives: toll, tr. v., to collect as toll,
tollable, adj., toll-age, п., toll-er, n.

## toll
toll, tr. v., to attract, allure. — ME. tollen, tullen,
'to draw, pull, attract', in gradational
relationship to ME. tillen, tyllen, 'to draw, pull'. See
till, 'drawer', and cp. next word-

## toll
toll, tr. v., to cause to sound; intr. v., to sound.
— ME. tollen, tullen, 'to draw, pull*; see prec.
word. Toll orig. meant 'to draw a bell so that
it sounds'.
Derivatives: toll, п., the sound of a bell, toll-er,
n.

## toll
toll, tr. v., to take away. — ME. tollen, fr. AF.
toller, fr. L. tollere, 'to lift up, raise; to take
away'. See tolerate.

## toll booth
toll booth, n. — See tolbooth.

## tolpatch
tolpatch, п., a foot soldier. — G. Tolpatsch, fr.
Hung, talpas, lit. 'having big feet', fr. talp, 'sole
of the foot, foot'.

## tolu
tolu, п., also tolu balsam. — Sp. tola, named after
the town Santiago de Tolu, in Columbia.

## tolu-
tolu-, also tol-, combining form used for tolu or
toluene. — See prec. word.

## toluate
toluate, п., a salt of toluic acid. — Formed fr.
tolu with chem. suff. -ate.

## toluene
toluene, п., a colorless liquid hydrocarbon
CeH5CH3 {chem.) — Coined fr. tolu with suff.
-ene (on analogy of benz-ene).

## toluic
toluic, adj., pertaining to any of several isomeric
acids {chem,) — Formed fr. tolu with adj. suif. -ic.

## toluide
toluide, toluid, п., any of a series of compounds
derived from toluidine (chem.) — Formed fr.
tolu with chem. suff. -ide. resp. -id.

## toluidine
toluidine, toluidin, п., any of three isomeric
amines derived fr. toluene (chem.) — Formed fr.
prec. word with chem. suff. -ine.

## toluol
toluol, toluole, п., toluene. — Formed fr. tolu
with suff. -ol (on analogy of benz-ol).

## toluyl
toluyl, п., the univalent hydrocarbon radical
C7H7CO (chem.) — Formed fr. tolu with suff.
-y].

## tolyl
tolyl, п., the univalent radical C?H, (chem.) —
Formed fr. tolu(ic) with suff. -yl.

## Tom
