L., 'kettledrum; a door panel; a triangular area
of a pediment*, fr. Gk. τύμπανον. See prec.
Word.

## Tyndareus
Tyndareus, п., the husband of Leda (Greek my-
thoL) — L., fr. Gk. Τυνδάρεος, Att. Τυνδάρεως,
lit. 'pounder', fr. I.-E. base *(s)tud·, 'to beat,
strike, pound', whence also Gk. Τϋδεύς, the
hero Tydeus, lit. 'pounder', L. tundere, 'to beat,
strike, stump', tudes, gen. -ditis, 'hammer'. See
Stint and cp. tund.

## Tynwald
Tynwald, п., parliament of the Isle of Man. —
ON. pingvollr, lit. 'assembly field', compounded
of ping, 'assembly', and v&llr, 'ground, floor,
field'. See thing, 'assembly', and wold.

## typ-
typ-, form of typo- before a vowel.

## typal
typal, adj., pertaining to a type or types. —
Formed fr. type with adj. suff. -al.

## type
type, n. — Late L. typus, 'figure, image', fr. Gk.
τύπος, 'blow, mark of a blow impression, stamp
on a coin, pattern, model', from the stem of
τύπτειν, 'to beat, strike", fr. I.-E. base *(e)tup-, 'to
strike, cut, hew', whence also Gk. στύπος,
'stem, stump*, OI. tupati, ttimpati,pra-stumpati,
'beats, strikes', L. stupire, 'to be stunned',
stupidus, 'amazed, dull, stupid', stuprum,
'dishonor, disgrace', OSlav. tupati> 'to palpitate,
throb", tuputu, 'clattering, rushing*. Cp. stub,
stupefy, stupid, stupor, stuprum, styptic.
Derivative: typey tr. and intr. v.

## -type
-type, combining form meaning; 1) type; 2)
representative. — Fr. prec. word.

## typh-
typh-, form of typho- before a vowel.

## Typha
Typha, п., a genus of plants, the cat-tail flag (bot.)
— ModL., fr. Gk. τύφη, 'a plant used for
stuffing bolsters, etc.', which together with L. tuber,
*a swelling, protuberance', ON. pufa, 'hillock',
OE. puf, 'tuft, banner', pyfel, 'a leafy plant,
thicket", derives fr. I.-E. base *tu-bh-,
enlargement of base *tu-, 'to swell', whence L. tumcre,
'to swell'. See tumid.

## Typhaceae
Typhaceae, n. pi., the cat-tail family (bot.) —
ModL., formed from prec. word with suff.
-aceae.

## typhlitis
typhlitis, п., inflammation of the caecum (med.)
— Medical L., formed with subst. suff. -itis fr.
Gk, τυφλός, 'blind'. See typhlo-,

## typhlo-
typhlo-, before a vowel typhi-, combining form
meaning 'blind*. — Gk. τυφλό-, τυφλ-, fr.
τυφλός (dissimilated fr. *θυφλός), 'blind,
closed, blunt', which is rel. to τΰφος, 'smoke',
τυφει.ν, 'to smoke'. See typhus.

## typho-
typho-, before a vowel typh-, combining form
meaning 'smoke, vapor', used in the sense of
typhus (med.) — Gk. τΰφο-, τϋφ-, fr. τΰφος.
See typhus.

## typhoid
typhoid, adj., pertaining to, or resembling,
typhus, — Compounded of typh- and Gk.
-οειδής, 'like', fr. είδος, 'form, shape'. See
-oid.
Derivative: typhoid-al, adj.

## typhomania
typhomania, п., delirium characteristic of typhus
(med.) — Medical L., compounded of typho-
and Gk. μανία, 'madness, frenzy'. See mania.

## typhonic
typhonic, adj., pertaining to, or resembling, a
typhoon. — Gk. τΰφωνι,κός, fr. τΰφών, which is
rel. to τΰφος, 'smoke, mist'. See typhus and -ic.

## typhoon
typhoon, п., a cyclone in the western Pacific. —
Chin, tai fung, lit. 'great wind'; influenced in
form by Arab, tufan (whence also Port, lufao),
fr. Gk. τΰφών, 'whirlwind' (see typhus).

## typhous
typhous, adj., pertaining to typhus. — Formed
with suff. -ous fr. Gk. τΰφος. See typhus.

## Typhula
Typhula, п., a genus of fungi (bot.) — A ModL.
hybrid coined fr. Gk. τΰφος, 'vapor' (see next
word), and L. dimin. suff. -ula. The correct form
would be Typhidium (fr. Gk. τΰφος and suff.
-idium, fr. Gk. dimin. suff. -ίδιον).

## typhus
typhus, n. — Medical L., fr. Gk. τΰφος, 'smoke,
mist, cloud, fever accompanied by stupor',
which is rel. to τυφειν, 'to smoke', τυφλός,
'blind', τΰφών, 'whirlwind*. These words are of
uncertain origin. They are perh. cogn. with
Goth, daufs, OE. deaf, 'deaf, Goth, dumbs, OE.
dumb, 'dumb', OE. dufe- (in compounds), 'dove',
lit. 'the dark-colored (bird)', Olr. dub (for *dku-
bu-)t 'black'. All these words possibly derive fr.
I.-E. base *dkeu-bh-, *dku-bk-, 'to fill with
smoke, to cloud, darken; to be dull, dumb or

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:818 COLUMN:3 -->
deaf. See deaf and cp. typhlo-.

## typic
typic, adj. — F. typique, fr. Late L. typicus. See
next word.

## typical
typical, adj. — ML. typicdlis, fr. Late L. typicus,
fr. Gk. τυπικός, fr. τύπος, 'blow, impression,
pattern, model'. See type and -ica].
Derivatives: typical-ity, п., typical-ly, adv.,
typical-ness, n.

## typify
typify, tr. v. — Formed fr. Late L. typus (see
type) and -fy.
Derivative: typifi-er, n.

## typist
typist, п., a person who operates a typewriter. —
See type and -ist.

## typo-
typo-, before a vowel typ-, combining form
meaning 'type, model'. — Fr. Gk. τύπος. See type.

## typographer
typographer, n. — See next word and agential
suff. -er.

## typography
typography, n. — ML. typographia. See typo- and
-graphy.
Derivatives: typograph-ic, typograph-ic-al, adjs.,
typograph-ic-al-ly, adv.

## typothetae
typothetae, n. pi., printers; esp. association of
master printers. — ModL., compounded of Gk.
τύπος, 'blow, impression, pattern, model', and
the stem of τι&έναί,, 'to put, place, set'. See type
and thesis and cp. thesmothete.
Туг, п., a war god in Norse mythology. — ON.
Tpr, rel. to OE. Ttw. See deity and cp. the first
element in Tuesday,
tyr^, form of tyro- before a vowel.

## tyramine
tyramine, tyramin, п., a crystalline base, C8HnNO
(biochem.) — Coined from the first three letters
of tyrosine and amine,

## tyrannical
tyrannical, adj. — Formed with adj. suff. -al fr.
L. tyrannicus, "pertaining to a tyrant' (whence
also F. tyrannique), fr. Gk. τυραννικός, fr.
τύραννος. See tyrant.
Derivatives: ryrannicaf-fy, adv., tyrannical-ness,
II.

## tyrannicide
tyrannicide, п., one who kills a tyrant. — F., fr.
L. tyrannicida, which is compounded of tyran-
nus, 'tyrant', and -cida, 'killer', fr. caedere, 'to
kill". See tyrant and -cide, 'killer'.

## tyrannicide
tyrannicide, п., the killing of a tyrant. — F., fr. L.
tyrannicidtum, fr. tyrannus, 'tyrant', and -cidi-
um, 'killing', fr. caedere, 'to kill*. See tyrant and
-cide, 'killing".

## Tyrannidae
Tyrannidae, n. pi., an American family of birds
(ornithol.) — ModL., formed with suff. -idae fr.
Tyrannus, name of the type genus, fr. L.
tyrannus. See tyrant.

## tyrannize
tyrannize, intr. and tr. v. — MF. (— F.) tyran-
niser, fr. tyran, 'tyrant' Cp. Late L. tyrannizare,
'to act the tyrant', Gk. τυραννίζειν, 'to take the
part of tyrants', and see tyrant and -ize.
Derivatives: tyranniz-er, п., tyranniz-ing-ly,
adv.

## tyrannous
tyrannous, adj. — Formed with suff. -ous fr. L.
tyrannus. See tyrant.
Derivatives: tyrannous-ly, adv., tyrannous-ness,
n.

## tyranny
tyranny, n. — ME. tyrannie, fr. MF. (— F.)
tyrannic, fr. OF., fr. ML. tyrannia, fr. Gk.
τυραννία, 'rule of a tyrant', fr. τύραννος, 'tyrant*. See
next word and -y (representing Gk. -la).

## tyrant
tyrant, n. — ME. tirant, fr. OF. tiran (F. tyran),
fr. L. tyrannus, fr. Gk. τύραννος, 'an absolute
ruler', which is a loan word from one of the
languages of Asia Minor (prob. the Lydian).
Cp. Etruscan Turan, 'mistress, lady' (surname
of Venus). Cp. also the second element in
Amphitryon. The final t in tyrant is due to a
confusion of the ending -an with the pres. part,
suff. -ant. Cp. the words ancient, pageant,
peasant, pheasant.
Derivative: tyrant, intr. v.

## Tyrian
Tyrian, adj. and n. — Formed with suff. -an fr.
L. Tyrius, fr. Tyrus, 'Tyre', name of the famous
insular city in Phoenicia, fr. Gk. Τύρος, fr.
Heb.-Phoen. Tzor, Tzur, lit. 'rock, rocky place'.

## tyro
tyro, tiro, п., a novice. — L. tiro, 'young soldier;
recruit; beginner', of uncertain origin. Cp. the
first element in tirocinium.

## tyro-
tyro-, before a vowel tyr-, combining form
meaning 'cheese". — Gk. τΰρο-, τΰρ-, fr. τυρός,
'cheese*, which is cogn. with OI. turah, Avestic
tuiri-, 'curds, whey', and perh. also with OSlav.
tvarogu, 'curds'. These words possibly derive fr.

<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: TYROCIDINE | 792 -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:819 COLUMN:1 -->
I.-E. base *rw-, 'to swell', whence also L. tumere,
'to swell'. See tumid and cp. the second element
in butter, satyr.

## tyrocidine
tyrocidine, tyrocldin, п., an antibiotic obtained
from a soil bacillus. — Coined by the
bacteriologist Rene Jules Dubos (1901- ), of the
Rockefeller Institute, in 1940 fr. tyrosine, 1st
-clde and chem. sufT. -ine, -in.

## tyrosine
tyrosine, tyrosin, п., an amino acid CeHnN03
(biochem.) — Coined by the German chemist
Baron von Justus Liebig (1802-73) in 1846, fr.
Gk. τυρός, 'cheese' (see tyro-), and chem. suff.
-ine, -in; so called because it is easily obtained
from cheese.

## Tyrrhenian
Tyrrhenian, adj., pertaining to the Tyrrheni,
Etruscan. — Formed with suff. -ian fr. L.
Tyrrheni, fr. Gk. Τυρσηνοί, Τυρρηνοί,
'Tyrrhenians', fr. τύρσις, 'tower; walled city', whence
also L. turris, 'tower'. See tower.

## tysonite
tysonite, п., a fluoride of cerium metals (mineral.)

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:819 COLUMN:2 -->
— Named after the American naturalist S. T.
Tyson, from whom it was received. For the
ending see subst. suff. -ite.

## Tyto
Tyto, п., a genus of owls (ornithol.) — ModL., fr.
Gk. τυτώ (Hesychius), 'owl', which is of
imitative origin. Cp. Gk. τοϋτις (Hesychius),
'blackbird', Lith. tutuati, to trumpet', tutlps, 'hoopoe',
ON. piota, 'to howl, resound', OE. peotan, of
s.m-, which all are imitative.

## Tytonidae
Tytonidae, n. pi., a family of birds (ornitkol.) —
Formed from prec. word with suff. -idae.

## tzaddik
tzaddik, also spelled saddik, zaddik, п., 1) in the
Bible, a righteous man; 2) in the modern sense
of the word, a Hasidic spiritual leader. — Heb.
tzaddiq, 'just, righteous', fr. tzadhaq, 'he was
just, was righteous' [whence also tzedkek,
'righteousness, justice', tzidhuqah, 'righteousness,
justice' (in Mishnaic Heb. also 'alms, charity')],
which is rel. to Aram, tz dheq, 'he was
righteous', Syr. zadheq, '(it is) right'), Arab, sadaqa,

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:819 COLUMN:3 -->
'he spoke the truth', Ethiop. sadaqa, 'he was
just, was righteous', Aram. tzidhqethd, tz6dhaqtd,
'a good deed, charity'; Arab, sadaqa1, 'alms,
charity', is a loan word fr. Heb. tzsdhaqah, in its
Mishnaic Heb. sense (i.e. 'alms, charity'). Cp.
the second element in Melcbizedek.

## tzadhe
tzadhe, tzade, п., name of the 19th letter of the
Hebrew alphabet. — Heb. tzade, lit. 'fishing
hook', fr. tzudh, 'to hunt, catch, capture'; so
called in allusion to the ancient Hebrew form of
this letter. Heb. tzudh (whence tzdyidh,
'hunting, game', tzayyadh, 'hunter', m tzUdhah, 'prey,
net; fastness, stronghold', metzodhah,'net, trap,
snare') is rel. to Aram.-Syr. tzudh, 'he hunted',
Ugar. sd, Akkad. s^du, 'to hunt', Arab, s^da,
'he hunted'. Cp. sadhe. Cp. also Sidonian.

## tzar
tzar, tzarinn. — See czar, czarina.

## tzigane
tzigane, п., gipsy. — F., fr. Hung, ctgany, whence
also G. Zigeuner. Cp. czigany.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:820 -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:820 COLUMN:1 -->

## uberous
uberous, adj., plentiful {rare). — Late L. uberosus,
from the L. adjective uber, 'fruitful', from the
noun uber (for *uder), 'teat, pap, dug, udder'.
See udder and -ous and cp. exuberant.
Derivatives: uberous-iy, adv., uberous-ness, n.

## ubiety
ubiety, п., whereness (philos.) — ModL. ubietas,
formed with suff. -tas (gen. -tatis), fr. L. ubi,
'where' (whence ubi-que, 'everywhere'), which
stands for orig. *cubi (cp. ali-cubi, 'elsewhere'),
rel. to Oscan puf, pufe, Umbr. pufe, 'where', fr.
I.-E. •qwu-dhei-; cp. 01. kuha (for *kudha),
OSlav. kude, 'where'; fr. I.-E. base *qwu-,
'where, whither', whence also Vedic ka, Avestic
кй, 'where', OI. kva, 'where, whither', kutra,
'where', kutak, 'wherefrom', Avestic kiSra,
'where, whither', MW. cw, cwt, 'where,
whither', Alb. kur, 'as, when', Arm. ur, 'somewhere',
Hitt. ku-wapi, 'somewhere'. Cp. who, how,
where, the first element in ibidem and the second
element in aliunde. For the ending see suff. -ity.

## ubiquitous
ubiquitous, adj., being everywhere, omnipresent.
— Formed fr. next word with suff. -ous.
Derivatives: ubiquitous-ly, adv., ubiquitous-ness,
n.

## ubiquity
ubiquity, п., omnipresence. — F. ubiquite, formed
with suff. -He fr. L. ubique, 'everywhere', which
is compounded of ubi, 'where', and enclitic
particle -que, meaning 'also, ever', identical with
-que, 'and', fr. I.-E. *qve-, whence also OI. ca,
Phrygian κε, Gk. τέ, Olr. -ch (in na-ch, 'not').
I.-E. *qwe- is rel. to pron. base *qwo-, See
ubiety, who and -ity.

## U-boat
U-boat, п., submarine. — G. U-Boot,
abbreviation of Unterseeboot, lit. 'undersea boat'. See
under, sea and boat.

## udder
udder, n. — ME., fr. OE. uder, rel. to OS. OFris.,
MLG., MDu. Uder, Du. uier, OHG. utar, utir,
MHG. iuter, G. Euter, QN.}ugr,jHr, Norw.jur,
Dan. yver, Swed. juver, fr. I.-E. base *iudh-,
*oudh-, *udh-, whence also OI. adhar, Gk.
οδ*αρ, L. uber, OSlav. vyme (for *udkmen),
'udder', (whence also Hung, vemkes, 'pregnant').
Cp. uberous, exuberant.
Derivatives: udder-ed, adj., udder-ful, udder-
less, adj.

## udograph
udograph, п., an automatic rain gauge. — A
hybrid coined fr. L. adus, 'wet', and Gk.
-γράφος, fr. γράφειν, 'to write'. See next word and
-graph.

## ndometer
ndometer, п., a rain gauge. — A hybrid coined fr.
L. udus, 'wet', and Gk. μέτρον, 'measure'. L.
udus is a contracted form of uvidus, 'which is rel.
to uvire, 'to be wet', (h)umere, 'to be moist,
wet', (h)umor, 'fluid, moisture'. See humor and
cp. uliginous. For the second element see meter, '
'poetical rhythm'.
Derivatives: udomeir-ic, adj., udometr-y, n.

## Lgaritic
Lgaritic, adj., pertaining to the ancient city Ug-
arit, its inhabitants or their language; п., the
language of Ugarit, closely rel. to Phoen. and
Hebrew. — Formed with suff. -ic from the city
Ugarit. This name prob. derives, through the
medium of Akkadian, from Sumerian ugaru,
'field' (whence also Hung, ugar, 'fallow field').

## ugh
ugh, interj. expressing repugnance. — Imitative.

## uglify
uglify, tr. v., to make ugly. — Compounded of
ugly and -fy.
Derivative: uglifi-er, n.

## ugly
ugly, adj. — ME. uglike, ugly, 'frightful,
repulsive', fr. ON. uggligr, 'fearful', which is formed
fr. uggr, 'fear', with suff. -ligr, 'like'. ON. uggr
and the rel. ugga, 'to fear', are of uncertain
origin. Suff. -ligr is rel. to OE. -lie; see adj. suff. -ly.
Derivatives: ugli-ly, adv., ugli-ness, n.

## Ugrian
Ugrian, adj. — Formed with suff. -ian fr. Ugra
name of the country on either side of the UTal
Mountains.

## Ugric
Ugric, adj., Ugrian. — See prec. word and -ic.

## uhian
uhian, п., a cavalryman. — G. Uhlan, Ulan, fr.
Pol. u-lan, fr. Turk.- Tatar oghlan, 'boy, youth',

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:820 COLUMN:2 -->
и
from stem *ogh, 'child'. For sense development
cp. infantry, which derives fr. L. infans, 'a
young child, a babeT.

## nitlander
nitlander, п., outlander, not of Boer birth. — S.
Afr. Du., compounded of Du. ait, Out', (and,
'land', and suff. -er. See out, land and agential
suff. -er.

## ukase
ukase, п., a decree having the force of law in
Czarist Russia. — F., fr. Russ. ukaz, Order',
back formation fr. ukazat\ 'to show, direct,
order', fr. intensive pref, u- and kazat\ 'to
show'. Pref. и-, which occurs in all Slavic
languages, is cogn. with OI. avah, 'down(ward)',
άνα, 'from', pref. άνα-, 'away from' (as in άνα-
bharati, 'carries away'), L. au-t "away" (in au-
fero, Ί carry away'), OPruss., Lith.. Lett. au-,
'from; un-' (asin Lett, ай-moniom, 'nonsensical,
foolish'), Olr. oy йа, 'down, from". Russ. kazaf
is rel. to OSlav. kazati, Czech karnti, Pol. kazat,
etc., and cogn. with OI. kdsate, 'appears, shines'.
See akasa and cp. the first element in Casimir.

## Ukrainian
Ukrainian, adj. and n. — Formed with suff. -ian
fr. Ukraine, a Slavic word prop, meaning
'frontier' ; so called because orig. it formed the
southern frontier of Poland.

## ukulele
ukulele, п., a Hawaiian gnitarlike musical
instrument. — Hawaiian, lit. 'fiea', prop, 'jumping
insect*, fr. ukUy 'insect', and lelet 'to jump'. The
instrument was so called in allusion to the rapid
motions of the fingers over it.

## -ular
-ular, suff. — Compounded of the suffixes -ule
and -ar.

## ulatrophia
ulatrophia, u la trophy, п., atrophy of the gingiva
(med.) — Medical- L., compounded of Gk.

## ullmannite
ullmannite, п., a nickel sulfantimonide {mineral.)
— G. Ullmannit, named after the German
chemist Johann С UUmann (1771-1821). The ending
-it goes back to Gk. -ΐτης; see subst. suff. -ite,,

## Ulmaceae
Ulmaceae, n. pi., a family of plants, the elm
family (bot.) — ModL., formed with suff. -aceae
fr. L. ulmus, 'elm*. See Ulmus.

## ulmaceous
ulmaceous, adj., pertaining to the elm family. —
See prec. word and -aceous.

## ulmic
ulmic, adj., pertaining to, or found in, ulmin. —
Formed fr. next word with adj. suff -ic.

## ulmin
ulmin, п., a brown substance found in elms
(chem.) — Formed fr. Ulmus with suff. -in.

## Uimus
Uimus, п., a genus of trees, the elm {bot.) — L.
ulmus, 'elm'. See elm.

## uina
uina, п., the inner of the two bones of the forearm
(anat.) — L. ulna (for *olend), *the elbow', cogn.
with Gk. ούλο-, 'elbow', Goth, aleina, OE. eln,
'ell'. See ell.

## ulnar
ulnar, adj., pertaining to the ulna. — Formed fr.
L. ulna (see prec. word) with suff. -ar.

## nlno-
nlno-, combining form meaning 'pertaining to
the ulna. — Fr. L. ulna. See ulna.

## ulo-
ulo-, combining form meaning 'in relation to the
gums'. — Gk. οΰλον, fr. οδλος, 'gum*. See ulitis.

## -ulose
-ulose, adj. suff. meaning 'characterized by*. —
L. -ulosus, compounded of the suffixes -ulus and
-osus. See -ule and subst. suff. -ose and cp.
-ulous, 'characterized by'.

## Ulotrichi
Ulotrichi, n. pi., the race having woolly hair, a
term in Huxley's classification (anthropoid —
ModL., compounded of Gk. ούλος, 'woolly,
crisp', and &ρ£ξ, gen. τριχός, 'hair'. The first
element stands for *?όλνος and is rel. to οδλον,
'gum', είλέω, Ί roll, roll up'; see ulitis. For the
second element see tricho-.

## ulotrichous
ulotrichous, adj., having woolly hair. — See prec.
word and -ous.

## -ulous
-ulous, adj., suff. meaning 'tending to', as in
credulous. — L. -ulus.

## -ulous
-ulous, adj. suff. meaning 'characterized by', as in
populous. — L. -ulosus. See -ulose.

## Ulrica
Ulrica, fern. PN, — Latinized fem. form of G.
Ulricht fr. OHG. Uodalricn,Uolrich, lit. 'of a
rich home', fr. uodaU 'home, nobility', and rihhi,
'rich'. The first element is rel. to OE. xdele,

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:820 COLUMN:3 -->
'noble', odel, 'home, land', ON. odal, 'home,
property'; see atheling. For the second element
see rich and cp. the PN.'s there referred to.

## ulster
ulster, п., a long, loose overcoat. — Fr. Ulster,
the Northern province of Ireland; so called
because first made in Belfast, in the province
Ulster.

## ulterior
ulterior, adj., 1) later; further; 2) undisclosed. —
L., 'farther, beyond', compar. of *ulter, 'that
which is on the other side", rel. to ultra, ultroy
'on the other side, beyond, besides', uls,
'beyond', OL. ollus, 'that one', olim, 'formerly',
and prob. also to alius, 'another'. See else and
cp. alias. Cp. also ultima, ultimate, ultimatum,
ultra, ultra-, ultroneous. Cp. also outrage, outre.
For the ending of ulterior see 1st suff. -ior.
ουλον, 'gum', and ατροφία, 'atrophy'. See ulitis
and atrophy.

## ulcer
ulcer, n. — F. ulcere, fr. VL. ulcerem (for L.
ulcus), ace. of ulcus, 'a sore, ulcer', which is cogn.
with 01. arsalj, 'hemorrhoids', Gk. έλκος,
'wound, abscess'. The rough spirit in έλκος
(inst. of *ελκος), is no doubt due to a
confusion of this noun with the verb ελκειν, 'to draw'.
Derivatives: ulcer, intr. and tr. v., ulcerate (q.v.),
ulceration (q.\.), ulcer-alive, adj., ulcer-ed, adj.,
ulcerous (q.v.)

## ulcerate
ulcerate, tr. v., to make ulcerous; intr. v., to
become ulcerous. — ME. ulceraten, fr. L. ulceru-
tits, pp. of ulcerare, 'to make sore', fr. ulcus, gen.
ulceris. See prec. word and verbal suff. -ate.

## ulceration
ulceration, n. — L. ulceratio, gen. -onis, fr. ulce-
rdtus, pp. οϊ ulcer are. See prec. word and -ion.

## ulcerons
ulcerons, adj. — L. ulcerosust 'full of sores', from
ulcus, gen. ulceris. See ulcer and -ous.
Derivatives: ulcerous-ly, adv., ulcerous-ness, n.

## -ule
-ule, dimin. suff.— This suffix, is used only after
consonants. After vowels its form is -olus. See
-ole, dimin. surf.

## ulema
ulema, n. pi., learned men, scholars. — Turk., fr.
Arab. lulama\ 'learned men', pi. of *a//'m,
'learned, wise*, which is prop, the active partic. of
'alima, *he knew'.
•ulent, adj. suff. meaning 'abounding in, full of.
— L. -ulentus (either directly or through the
medium of F. -ulent).

## uletic
uletic, adj., pertaining to the gums. — Formed
with sufi". -eric fr. Gk. οδλον, 'gum'. See ulitis.

## Ulex
Ulex, п., a genus of plants, the furze (bot.) — L.
ulex, 'a shrub resembling rosemary', contracted
fr. *uvilex, and rel. to uligo, 'moisture*. See
uliginose.

## ulexite
ulexite, п., a hydrous sodium calcium borate
(mineral.) — Named after the German chemist
Georg L. Ulex. For the ending see subst. suff.
-ite.

## uliginose
uliginose, uliginous, adj., oozy, muddy. — L. uli-
ginosus, 'wet, damp, marshy', fr. QUgo, gen.
-ginis, 'moisture, dampness', contraction of
*uviligd, fr. uvere, 'to be wet', whence also uvi-
dus, udus, vset*. See udometer and adj. suff. -ose,
resp. -ous, and cp. Ulex.

## ulitis
ulitis, п., inflammation of the gums (med.) —
Medical L., formed with suff. -itis fr. Gk.
ούλον, 'gum', which is prob. related to είλέω,
Ί roll, roll up', and lit. means 'that which is
rounded or padded'. Είλέω stands for *Ρελνέω
and derives fr. I.-E. base *welu·, *welw-, 'to
bend, turn, twist, roll', whence also L. volvere,
'to roll*. See volute and cp. epulis, parulis,
ulatrophia, Ulotrichi.

## ullage
ullage, п., the amount by which a bottle or cask
of liquor falls short of being full. — ME. oylage,
ulage, fr. MF. eullage, oillage (F. ouillage), 'the
filling up of a cask', fr. eullier, oilier (F. outlier),
'to fill up (a cask) to the bung', lit. 'to fill it to
"the eye"', fr. ueil (F. ceil), 'eye', fr. L. oculus,
'eye'. See ocular and -age.
Derivative: ulterior-ly, adv.

## ultima
ultima, adj., farthest, last, final; п., the last sylla-

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:821 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: ULTIMACY | 794 -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:821 COLUMN:1 -->
bleof a word. — L. ultima fem. oTultimus, 'last'.
See ultimate.

## ultimacy
ultimacy, n. — Formed from next word with suff.
-cy.

## ultimate
ultimate, adj., final, fundamental; п., something
ultimate. — Late L. ultimatus, pp. of ultimare,
'to come to, or be at, an end*, fr. L. ultimus,
'last', superl. of L. uls, 'Beyond*. See ulterior and
adj. suff. -ate. For the superl. suff. -timus in
ultimas see intimate, adj. and cp. posthumous,
maritime.
Derivatives: ultimate-ly, adv., ultimate-ness, n.

## ultimatum
ultimatum, п., final demand. — Late L. ultima·
turn, neut. of ultimatus, pp. οι ultimare. See prec.
word.

## ultimo
ultimo, adv., in the month preceding the present.
— L. ultimo (scil. mense), 'in the last month',
abl. of ultimus, 'last'. See ultima.

## ultimogeniture
ultimogeniture, п., a system of inheritance by
which the estate descends to the youngest son
(as in Borough English). — Compounded of L.
ultimus, 'last', and genitura, 'a begetting,
bearing, birth', fr. genitus, pp. of gignere, *to beget,
bear, bring forth'. See ultimate, adj., genus and
-ure and cp. primogeniture.

## ultra
ultra, adj., extreme; п., an extremist. — L. ultra,
'on the other side, beyond', prop. fem. abl. of
*ulter, *that which is on the other side'. See
ulterior.

## ultra-
ultra-, pref. meaning 'beyond'. — Fr. L. ultra.
See prec. word.

## ultra ism
ultra ism, п., the holding of extreme views,
radicalism. — See ultra and -ism.

## ultraist
ultraist, п., one who holds extreme views. — See
ultra and -ist.

## ultramarine
ultramarine, adj., situated beyond the sea. — ML.
ultrdmarinus, fr. L. ultra, 'beyond*, and. marinus,
'pertaining to the sea'. See ultra- and marine and
cp. transmarine.

## ultramarine
ultramarine, п., a pure blue pigment, orig.
obtained from powdered lapis lazuli. —
Refashioned fr. It. oltramarino, 'from beyond the sea',
fr. ML. ultrdmarinus (see ultramarine, adj.); so
called because the lapis lazuli had to be
imported from 'beyond the sea', i.e. Asia.
Derivative: ultramarine, adj.

## ultramontane
ultramontane, adj., beyond the mountains; esp.
beyond the Alps (in the latter meaning it was
orig. used by the Italians in the sense 'north of
the Alps'; later it was applied by the northern
nations in the sense 'south of the Alps', whence
arose the meanings 'Itaiian' and'of, or
supporting the policy of, the Italian party in the Roman
Catholic Church'; п., 1) a person living beyond
the mountains (esp. beyond, i.e. north, resp.
south, of the Alps); 2) an adherent of the Italian
party in the Roman Catholic Church. — ML.
ultramontanus (corresponding to L.
tramontane), 'situated beyond the mountains', fr. L.
ultra, 'beyond', and montdnus, 'pertaining to a
mountain', fr. mens, gen. montis, 'mountain'.
Cp. It. oltramontano and F. ultramontain and
see ultra· and mount, 'hill'. Cp. also tramontane.

## ultramontanism
ultramontanism, п., the principles of the
ultramontane party. — F. ultramontanisme formed
fr. ultramontain (fr. ML. ultramontanus) with
suff. -isme. See prec. word and -ism.

## ultramontanist
ultramontanist, п., an adherent of the
ultramontane party. — See ultramontane and»-ist.

## ultramundane
ultramundane, п., beyond the world. — L. ultrd-
munddnus, formed fr. ultra, 'beyond', and
munddnus, 'wordly'. See ultra- and mundane.

## ultrasonic
ultrasonic, adj., supersonic. — See ultra- and
sonic.

## ultraviolet
ultraviolet, adj., outside the violet end of the
visible spectrum (physics). — Lit. 'beyond the
violet', compounded of ultra- and violet.

## ultra vires
ultra vires, transcending one's power or
authority (law). — L., 'beyond powers', fr. ultra,
'beyond', and vires, ace. (and nom.) pi. of vis,
'force, strength', which is rel. to vir, 'man'. See
ultra and virile.

## ultroneous
ultroneous, adj., voluntary. — L. ultroneus, 'of
one's own accord, voluntary, spontaneous', fr.
ultra, 'beyond; of one's own accord'. See ultra
and -eous.
Derivatives: ultroneous-ly, adv., ultroneous-ness,
n.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:821 COLUMN:2 -->

## ululant
ululant, adj., howling. — L ululdns, gen. -amis,
pres. part, of ululare. See next word and -ant.

## ululate
ululate, intr. v., to howl. —· L, ululaH-um), pp.
stem of ululare, 'to howl, screech, cry out'
(whenceи/и/ΰ,'owl', prop, 'the screeching bird');
from reduplication of the imitative base *(//-,
*ol-. Cp. Gk. δλολύζειν, 'to cry aloud*, Ol.
ululih, 'a howling'. Cp. also owl. For the ending
see verbal suff. -ate.
Derivatives: ululation (q.v.), ululat-ive, adj.

## ululation
ululation, п., howling, lamentation. — L. ululdtw,
gen. -onis, fr. ululdt(-um), pp. stem of ululare.
See prec. word and -ion.

## Ulva
Ulva, п., a genus of seaweeds, the sea lettuce
(bot.) — L. ulva, 'sedge*, rel. to alga. See alga.

## Ulvaceae
Ulvaceae, n. pi., a family of seaweeds (bot.) —
ModL., formed with suff. -aceae fr. Ulva (q.v.)

## alvaceous
alvaceous, adj. — See prec. word and -aceous.

## Ulysses
Ulysses, п., Latin name for Odysseus. — L.,
more exactly Ulixis, fr. Gk. 'Οδυσσεύς (see
Odysseus). The Latin spellings Ulissis, Ulysses
are an attempt at bringing Ulixis nearer to Gk.
'Οδυσσεύς, more exactly, to its dialectal forms
Όλυσσεύς, Όλυσεύς, Όλισεύς.

## uraangite
uraangite, п., a copper selenide (mineral.) — G.
Umangit, named after the Sierra de Umanga in
Argentina. The ending -it goes back to Gk.
-ΐτης; see subst. suff. -ite.

## umbel
umbel, п., a type of inflorescence (bot.) — L. um-
bella (for *umber-ld), 'sunshade, parasol', lit. 'a
little shade*, dimin, of umbra, 'shade, shadow'.
See umbra and cp. umbrella. For the change of
*umber-ld to umbella cp. L. libetius, 'a little
book', for *liber-lus, fr. liber, 'book' (see libel).
Derivative: umbel(l)-ed, adj.

## umbell-
umbell-, form of umbelli- before a vowel.

## umbella
umbella, п., the same as umbel. — L. See prec.
word.
Derivatives: umbell-ar, adj., umbellate (q.v.)

## umbellate
umbellate, adj., having umbels. — ModL. um-
belldtus, fr. L. umbella. See umbel and adj. suff.
-ate.

## umbeilet
umbeilet, п., an umbellule (bot.) — Formed fr.
umbel with dimin. suff. -et.

## umbelli-
umbelli-, before a vowel umbeli-, a combining
form meaning * umbel' or 'umbellate'. — Fr. L.
umbella. See umbel,

## umbelliferous
umbelliferous, adj., producing umbels (bot.) —
Compounded of umbelli- and -ferous.

## umbelliform
umbelliform, adj., having the form of an umbel
(bot.) — Compounded of umbelli- and forma,
'form, shape'. See form, n.

## umbellule
umbellule, п., a secondary umbel (bot.) — ModL.
umbellula, a double dimin., formed fr. L.
umbella, itself a dimin. of umbra, 'shade, shadow'.
See umbel and -ule.

## umber
umber, п., a brown earthy pigment. — ME. um-
bre, umber, 'shade, shadow*, fr. MF. umbre (F.
ombre), for terre d? Umbre (F. terre d"Ombre),
lit. 'earth of Umbria' (in Italy). For sense
development cp. It. terra di Siena, 'umber', lit.
'earth of Siena', fr. Siena, a town in Northern
Italy (cp. sienna).
Derivatives: umber, adj., dark brown, umber,
tr. v., to paint with umber.

## umber
umber, п., the grayling. — ME. umbre, fr. MF.
umbre (F. ombre), 'the grayling*, fr. OF., fr. L.
umbra, 'shade'. See umbra. For sense
development cp. umbrette and Sciaenidae.

## umbilical
umbilical, adj., pertaining ίο the navel. — ML.
umbilicdlis, fr. L. umbilicus. See umbilicus and
adj. suff. -al.
Derivative: umbilical-ly, adv.

## umbilicate
umbilicate, adj., having an umbilicus. — L. um-
bilicdtus, formed with suff. -atus fr. umbilicus.
See next word and adj. suff. -ate.
Derivatives: umbilicat-ed, adj., umbilicat-ion, n.

## umbilicus
umbilicus, п., navel (anat.) — L. umbilicus, 'navel,
umbilical cord', prob. formed with suff. -chs, fr.
*ombeli which is rel: to umbo, 'boss of a shield',
and cogn. with Gk. ομφαλός, 'navel; boss of
a shield, knob*, ON. nafli, OE. nafela, 'navel'.
See navel and cp. nmbo, nombril, omphalic,

## umbiliform
umbiliform, adj., having the form of an umbilicus
or navel. — See prec. word and -form,

## umble pie
umble pie, pie made of the umbles of a deer. —
See next word and cp. humble pie.

## umbles
umbles, n. pi. — Obsol. var. of nnmbles.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:821 COLUMN:3 -->

## umbo
umbo, п., the boss of a shield. — L. umbo, 4a
convex elevation, knob, boss*, rel. to umbilicus.
'navel'. See umbilicus.

## umbonal
umbonal, adj., pertaining to the umbo. — Formed
with adj. suff. -al fr. L. umbo, gen. umbonis. See
prec. word.

## umbonate
umbonate, adj., shaped like an umbo. — Formed
with suff. -atefr. L. umbo, gen. umbonis. See umbo.

## nmbra
nmbra, п., shade, shadow (of a planet). — L.
umbra, 'shade, shadow*, of uncertain origin. It
is possibly cogn. with OI. andhas-, 'darkness',
andhah, Avestic ando, 'blind'. For the suff. -bra
in umbra cp. the stiff, in L. tenebrae (pi.),
'darkness*. See Ernout-Meillet, DELL., p. 745 s.v.
umbra. Cp. Rum. umbra, It. ombra, F. ombre,
OProvenc., Catal. ombra, 'shade', which all
derive fr. L. umbra, and Catal., Sp., Port, sombra,
'shade', which come fr. VL. subumbrdre, 'to
cast shade upon'. Cp. umbel, umber, 'the
grayling', umbrage, umbrella, umbrette, adumbrate,
adumbration, pennmbra. Cp. also somber,
sombrero.

## umbraculiferous
umbraculiferous, adj., bearing umbracula (bot.)
— Compounded of umbraculum and -ferous.

## umbraculiform
umbraculiform, adj., shaped like an umbraculum
(bot.) — Compounded of umbraculum and L.
forma, 'form, shape'. See form, n.

## umbraculum
umbraculum, п., an appendage of the form of an
umbTe\\a.\bot.) — L., 'umbrella', dimin.'of
umbra. See umbra and -culum.

## umbrage
umbrage, п., 1) shadow; 2) resentment. — ME.,
fr. OF. umbrage, ombrage (F. ombrage), 'shade,
suspicion, distrust', fr. L. umbrdticus,
'pertaining* to shade', fr. umbra. See umbra and -age.

## umbrageous
umbrageous, adj., shady. — F. ombrageux,
'suspicious, distrustful; skittish (said of horses)', fr.
OF. umbrageus, ombrageus, 'shady, suspicious',
fr. umbre, ombre (F. ombre), 'shade'. See umbra
and -ous.
Derivatives: umbrage, tr. v., umbra geo us-ly, adv
umbrageous-ness, n.

## umbral
umbral, adj., pertaining to an umbra. — Formed
fr. umbra with adj. suff. -al.
Derivative: umbral-ly, adv.

## umbrella
umbrella, n. — It. ombrella, fr. Late L. umbrella,
alteration of L. umbella, 'a little shadow,
sunshade, umbrella', dimin. of umbra. See umbra
and -ella and cp. umbel.
Derivatives: umbrella, adj. and tr. v.

## umbrette
umbrette, п., the bird called Scopus umbretta. —
ModL. umbretta, fr. F. ombrette, dimin' of
ombre, 'the grayling'. See umber, 'the grayling',
and -ette.

## Umbrian
Umbrian, adj., pertaining to Umbria. — Formed
with suff. -an fr. L. Umbria, name of a district in
Central Italy.
Derivative: Umbrian, n.

## umbriferous
umbriferous, adj., giving shade. — Formed with
suff. -ous fr. L. umbrifer, 'giving shade, casting a
shade, shady*, which is compounded of umbra,
'shade', and the stem oiferre, 'to bear, carry'.
See umbra and -ferous.

## umiak
umiak, п., an Eskimo boat. — Eskimo.

## umlant
umlant, п., vowel mutation. — G. Umlaut,
'modification of a vowel', coined by the German
poet Friedrich Gottlieb Klopstock (1724-1803)
fr. um, 'around, about', and Laut, 'sound*. The
first element derives fr. MHG. umbe, umbe, fr.
OHG. umbi, which is rel. to OE. ymbe, 'around,
about'; see ambi- and cp. amphi-. The second
element is rel. to G. laut, 'loud'; see loud and cp.
ablaut, aniaut, auslaut. As a technical term of
grammar, the word umlaut was introduced by
the German philologist Jakob Ludwig Karl
Grimm (1785-1863).

## umpire
umpire, п., judge, arbiter. — ME. nompere, nourt-
pere, fr. OF. nomper, earlier nonper, 'not equal',
fr. поп, not\ and per, 'equal, peer', fr. L. поп,
'not', resp. par, 'equal'. See поп and peer, n. The
modern E. form is due to a misdivision of a
numpire into an umpire. For similar misdivi-
sions cp. adder and words there referred to.
Derivatives: umpire, tr. v., umpir-age', п., umpir-
ess, n.

## umpteen
umpteen, adj., any great number (army slang). —
Coined on analogy of thirteen, etc., fr. ump·, an
interjection suggestive of an indefinite number.
Derivative: umpteen-th, adj.
