<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: 82S | WHELM -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:852 COLUMN:1 -->

## wench
wench, п., 1) a girl; 2) a prostitute. — ME. wen·
che, fr. earlier wenchel, fr. OE. wencel, 'child;
weak person4, rel. to ON. vdkr, 'child; weak
person', vakka, 'to stagger, totter', OHG. wan-
kdn, of s.m., OE. wancol, OHG. wanchal,
'fickle', and in gradational relationship to wince,
wink (qq.v.) Cp. wankle.

## wend
wend, intr. v., to go {archaic); tr. v., to proceed
on (now chiefly poetic). — ME. wenden, fr. OE.
wendan, 'to turn, go', rel to OS. wendian, ON.
venda, Dan. vende, Swed. vanda, OFris. wenda,
Du. wenden, OHG. wenten, MHG., G. wenden,
Goth, wandjan, 'to turn'. These verbs are causa-
tives of OE. windan, resp. OS. windan, ΟΝ. vin-
da, Dan. vinde, Swed. vinda, OFris. winda, Du.
windent OHG. wintan, MHG., G. winden, Goth.
windan, 'to turn, wind'. See wind, 'to turn', and
cp. went.

## Wend
Wend, п., a member of a Slavic people in Eastern
Germany. — G. Wende, fr. OHG. Winida,
which is rel. to OE. Winedas (pi.), 'Wends'; fr.
Celtic *vindo-, 'white'. See winter and cp. Yen-
dace.
Derivatives: Wend-ic,&d'j., Wend-ish, adj. andn.

## Wenlock
Wenlock, adj., pertaining to the middle division
of the Upper Silurian age igeol.) — Named after
a town in Shropshire, England.

## WensleydaJe
WensleydaJe, п., a kind of cheese. — Named after
a district in Yorkshire.

## went
went, v. — Prop, past tense of wend, but now
used as the past tense of go.

## wentletrap
wentletrap, п., any of a family of sea mollusks4—
Du. wenteltrap, 'winding staircase' (cp. G.
Wendeltreppe), fr. wentel, 'turning', and trap,
'staircase'. The first element is rel. to Du.
winden, 'to turn, wind; see wind, 'to turn'. The
second element is rel. to MHG. treppe, trappe, G.
Treppe, 'staircase', and to OE. treppe, 'trap'; see
trap, 'a mechanical device for catching animals'.

## were
were, v. — ME. weren, fr. OE. wxron (pi. of wass),
*(we, you or they) were*. Cp. OHG. wdrun, G.
waren '(we or they) were', and see was.

## werewolf
werewolf, also werwolf, п., a person changed into
a wolf (folklore). — ME., fr. OE. werewulf rel.
to MDu., Du. weerwoff, OHG., MHG., G.
werwolf. These words lit, mean 'manwolf, fr.
OE. wer, resp. MDu. weer, OHG. wer, 'man',
and OE. wulf, resp. MDu., Du., OHG. wolf
'wolf. For the 1st element see virile, world,
for the second see wolf.

## Wertherism
Wertherism, п., morbid sentimentality. —
Formed with surf -ism from the name of Werther,
hero of the novel Die Leiden desjungen Werthers
by the German poet Johann Wolfgang von
Goethe (1749-1832).

## Wesleyan
Wesleyan, adj., pertaining to John Wesley,
founder of Methodism (1703-91). — For the ending
see suff. -an.

## Wesleyamsm
Wesleyamsm, п., doctrine of the Wesleyans. —
Formed from prec. word with suff. -ism.

## west
west, adv., adj. and n. — ME., fr. OE. west(adv.),
'to the west' (whence also F. ouest, 'west'), rel.
to ON. vestr, Dan,, Swed. vest, OFris., MLG.,
MDu., Du. west, OHG. -west (only in
compounds, whence MHG., G. west), the enlarged
forms OHG. westan, MHG., G. westen, 'west',
fr. Teut. *west-, which is prob. an enlargement
of I.-E. *we-, 'to go down', whence also Ol.
avah, 'down, downward*. Cp. I.-E. *we-spero,
whence L. vesper, 'evening', Gk. έσπερος (for
*5έ-σπερος), εσπέρα (for *5ε-σπέρα),
'evening'. OE. west, etc., orig. meant 'the region
where the sun sets' (lit. 'goes down'). See vesper
and cp. words there referred to. Cp. also the
first element in Visigoth.
Derivatives: wester (q.v.), western (q.v.)

## wester
wester, intr. v. to go or turn westward. — ME.
westreny formed fr. west with surf. -ren. See west.
Derivatives: wester-ing, adj. and n.

## westerly
westerly, adj., pertaining to the west; western. —
Formed with adj. suff. -ly fr. obsol. E. wester, fr.
ME. wester, fr. OE. westra, 'more toward the
west', which was formed fr. west with compar.
suff. -ra. See west and compar. suff. -er.

## western
western, adj. and n. — ME. westeren, westerne,
fr. OE. westerne. See west and -ern.
Derivatives: western-er, п., western-ize, tr. and
intr. v., western-iz-ation, n.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:852 COLUMN:2 -->

## westward
westward, adj. — ME., fr. OE. westeweard. See
west and -ward.

## westward
westward, westwards, adv. — See prec. word and
-wards.

## wet
wet, adj. — ME. wete, wette, partly fr. pp. of
weten, 'to wet', partly fr. OE. wet, 'wet', which
is rel. to OFris. wet, ON. vdtr, Swed. vat, Dan.
vaad, 'wet', and to OE. wxter, 'water*. See water.
Derivatives: wet, п., wet, v. (q.v.), wet-ly, adv.,
wet-ness, п., wett-ish, adj.

## wet
wet, tr. v. — ME. weten, fr. OE. wxtan, 'to wet',
fr. wxt. 'wet*. See wet, adj.
Derivatives- wett-ed, adj., wett-ег, п., wett-ing,
n.

## wether
wether, n. — ME., fr. OE. weder, 'sheep,
wether', rel. to OS. wethar, ON. vedr, Dan.
v&der, Swed. xadur, OHG. widar, MHG. wider,
G. Widder, Goth, wiprus, 'lamb', fr. Teut.
*wepru-, lit. 'yearling', fr. I.-E. base *wet~,
'year', whence also Ol. vatsah, *calf, Gk. ётос-
λον, Dor. £τελον, 'yearling4, L. vitulus, 'calf,
lit. 'yearling'. See veal and cp. words there
referred to.

## wey
wey, п., a unit of weight. — ME. weye, fr. OE.
wxge, wxg, 'scales, balance weight, wey', rel.
to OS, ODu., OHG. wdga, ON. rag, Swed vag,
Du. waag, OHG. waga, MHG. wage, G. Waage,
'scales balance', and to OE. wegan, 'to move,
carry, weigh'. See weigh and cp. wee.

## whack
whack, tr. and intr. v., to strike sharply. — Prob.
of imitative origin. Cp. thwack.
Derivatives: whack, п., whack-er, п., whack-wg,
n. and adj.

## whale
whale, n. — ME. whale, whal, fr. OE. hwael, rel.
to OS. hwal, ON. hvalr, hvalfiskr, Swed. vat,
MDu. wal, wahisc, Du. walvis, OHG. wal,
walfisc, MHG. wal, watvisch, G. Wal, Walfisch,
'whale', G. Wels, 'shad', and prob. cogn. with
OPruss. kalis, 'shad', and prob. also with Finn.
kala, 'fish', L. squalus, 'a kind of sea fish'. Cp.
walrus and narwhal. Cp. also rorqual, Squalus.
Derivatives: whale, intr. v., whal-er, п., whal-
ery, п., whal-ing, n.

## whang
whang, tr. and intr. v., to strike, blow; п., а
strike, blow. — Of imitative origin. Cp. bang.

## whangee
whangee, п., a bamboo cane. — Prob. fr. Chin.
hwang li, lit. 'yellow bamboo cane'.

## wharf
wharf, п., a structure for mooring ships. — ME.
wherf wharf, fr. OE. hwerf hwearf, 'turn,
exchange, dam, bank, wharf', rel. to MLG. werf
warf 'mole, dam, wharf* (whence Du. werf,
'shipyard, dockyard*, whence G. Werft, of s.m.).
These words orig. denoted a place where one
can move about. They are rel. to OE. hweorfan,
'to turn about, be active*, ON. hverfa, 'to turn
round', OS. hwerban, OFris. hwerva, OHG.
hwerfan, hwerban, werban, MHG. werben, 'to
turn about, be active', G. werben, *to enlist,
solicit, court, woo', Du. werven, 'to enlist',
Goth, hairban, 'to wander*. All these words
derive fr. I.-E. base *kwerp-, 'to turn,
revolve*, whence also Gk. καρπός, 'wrist', and
prob. also Toch. A karp-, 'to turn to, to go', 01.
surpam, 'winnowing fan'. Cp. wharve. Cp. also
varve, whirl, whorl. Cp. also carpus.
Derivatives: wharf, tr. v., wharf-age, п.,
wharfinger (q.v.)

## wharfinger
wharfinger, п., the operator or manager of a
wharf. — Formed fr. wharfage (see prec. word)
with agential suff. -er and with intrusive η as in
messenger and in words there referred to.

## wharve
wharve, п., the whorl of a spindle. — ME. wherve,
fr. OE. hweorfa, rel to OE. hweorfan, 'to turn
about'. See wharf.

## what
what, pron., adj., п., and adv. — ME. what, Тт.
OE. hwxt, 'what*, neut. of hwd, '.who*, rel. to
OS. hwat, ON. hvat, Dan. kvad, Swed. vad,
OFris. hwet, Du. wat. OHG. hwas, was, MHG.
wflj, G. was, Goth, ha, 'what'. See who and
words there referred to and cp. the second
element in forwhy.

## whaup
whaup, п., the European curlew {Scot.) — Of
imitative origin.

## wheal
wheal, п., a pustule. — ME. whele, rel. to OE.
kwe[ian, 'to suppurate', which is perhaps cogn.
with Lett, kvete, 'inflammation*. Cp. whelk,
'pimple'.

## wheal
wheal, п., a mark made on the skin by a whip. —

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:852 COLUMN:3 -->
Alteration of weal, 'wale', caused by an
association with ME. whele, 'pustule'. See prec. word.

## wheal
wheal, п., a mine (Cornwall). — Co. hwel.

## wheat
wheat, n. — ME. whete, fr. OE. hwsete, rel. to OS.
hweti, ON. hveiti, Dan. hvede, Swed. hvete, vete,
Norw. kveite, OFris. hwete, MDu., Du weit,
OHG. weizzi, MHG. weize, G. Weizen, Goth.
fvaiteis, 'wheat', and to OE. hwit, 'white'; see
white. The plant was so called from its white
seed and white flour. For sense development cp.
W. gwenith, 'wheat*, which is rel. to W. gwenn,
'white'.

## wheatear
wheatear, п., the bird Saxicola oenanthe. —
Back formation fr. white-ears, lit. 'the white-
rumped (bird)', compounded of white and ME.
ers, 'arse'. See white and arse. Cp. F. cul-blanc,
'wheatear', lit. 'white-rumped'.

## whenten
whenten, adj. — ME. wheten, fr. OE. hwxten, fr.
hwxte, 'wheat'. See wheat and adj. surf -en.

## wheatstone bridge
wheatstone bridge, a device for measuring
electrical resistance. — Named after its inventor Sir
Charles Wheatstone (1802-75).

## wheedle
wheedle, tr. v., to influence by flattery. — Prob.
fr. G. wedeln, lit. 'to wag the tail', fr. MHG.
wadelen, fr. OHG. wadal, wedil, 'tail, fan',
which is prob. formed from l.-E. base *we-, 'to
blow' (see wind, 'air in motion'), with Teut.
instrumental surf -plo (= I.-E. *tro-).
Accordingly OHG. wedil orig, meant 'an instrument to
fan with'. For the sense development of E.
wheedle, fr. G. wedeln (see above), cp. Gk. σαί-
νειν, προσσαίνειν, 'to wag the tail, to flatter',
and L. aduldri, 'to flatter', which is cogn. with
Ol. vdlah, 'tail'.
Derivatives: wheedl-er, wheedl-ing, adj., wheedl-
mg-ly, adv.

## wheel
wheel, n. — ME. whel, whele, wheel, fr. OE.
hweogol, hweowol, hweol, rel. to ON. hvel, hjol,
Dan. А/и/, OSwed. hiughl, Swed. А/и/, OFris.
hwel, MLG. wel, MDu. weel, wiel, Du. wiel,
and cogn. with Ol. cakrah. Avestic caxra-,
Toch. A kukal, B. kokale, Gk. κύκλος, 'wheel*,
Lith. kaklas, 'neck', fr. I.-E. base *qwe-qwlos,
reduplication of base *(s)qwel-, *(s)qel-, 'to
bend, turn, turn round, move about', whence
OPruss. kelan, OSlav. kolo, 'wheel', Ol. carati,
'moves about, wanders, drives', carah, 'walk,
motion', diva-karah, 'sun', Gk. πέλειν, more
usually as deponent πέλεσ&αι, 'to be in motion,
to be', πόλος, 'pivot', πάλιν, 'back, again',
πάλαι, 'long ago', τέλος, 'end', τέλειος, τέλεος,
'complete', τηλε, 'far off', Alb. sjei/1 turn', kei,
Ί bring, carry', L. colere, 'to till (the ground),
cultivate, dwell, inhabit', colouus, 'tiller of the
ground, husbandman, farmer', incola,
'inhabitant*, inquilinus, 'residing in a city", collum,
'neck', lit. 'that which turns (the head)'. Cp.
cycle and words there referred to. Cp. also
Anatolian, ancillary* bucolic, calash, clown,
collar, cologne, cult, culture, paleolithic, pole,
'the end of an axis', pratincole, pulley, telegnosis,
telegraph, teleology, telephone, telescope, teles-
terion, terricolous, Triteleia. Cp. also felly, ko-
lach, kolo.
Derivatives: wheel, tr. and intr. v., wheeled, adj.,
wheel-er, п., wheel-ery, п., wheel-ing, n. and
adj.

## wheeze
wheeze, intr. v., to breathe with a whistling
sound; tr. v., to utter with a sound resembling
that of wheezing. — ME. whesen, prob. fr. ON.
hvxsa, 'to wheeze', which is rel. to OE. hwxst,
'the act of blowing', from the I.-E. imitative
base *kwes-, 'to sigh', whence also L. queri, 'to
complain'. See quarrel, 'dispute'.
Derivatives: wheeze, п., wheez-er, п., wheez-y,
adj., wheez-i-ly, adv., wheez-i-ness, n.

## whelk
whelk, п., a large marine snail. — ME. witke,
welke, fr. OE. wiluc, wioloc, rel. to MDu. willoc,
wile, Du. wulk, fr. I.-E. base *wel-, 'to roll',
whence also L. volvere, 'to roll' (see volute); so
called from its spiral shell.
Derivative: whelk-ed, adj., whelk-y, adj.

## whelk
whelk, п., a pimple. — ME. whelke, fr. OE. hwyl-
ca, fr. hwelian, 'to suppurate'. See wheal,
'pustule'.
Derivatives: whelk-ed, whelk-y, adjs.

## whelm
whelm, tr. v., to turn upside down. — ME.
whelmen, 'to turn over', a blend of ME. helmen

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:853 COLUMN:1 -->
(fr. OE. helmian), 'to cover' (see helm), and ME.
whelven (fr. OE. d-hwielfan), 'to cover with a
vault; to overwhelm*. See gulf and cp.
overwhelm.
Derivative: whelm, n.

## whelp
whelp, п., young of the dog, wolf, etc.; cub. —
ME. whelp, fr. OE. hwelp, 'whelp, cub', rel. to
OS. hwelp, ON. kvelpr, Du. wetp, OHG. hwelf,
welf, MHG. welf. Cp. Gdelph.
Derivative: whelp, intr. and tr. v.

## when
when, adv. — ME. whan, when, fr. OE. hwaenne,
hwanne, rel. to OS. hwan, OFris. hwenne, MDu.
wan, OHG. hwanne, wanne, MHG. wanne, G.
wann, 'when', G. wenn, 'if, ON. hve(for *hven),
Goth, faan, 'when', from the I.-E. pron. base
*qwo-. See who and cp. next word.
Derivatives: when, pron. and n.

## whence
whence, adv. — ME. whennes, formed fr. whenne
fr. whenne (fr. OE. hwanon, hwanone), 'whence',
with adv. suff. -s. Cp. hence, thence.

## where
where, adv. — ME. where, wher, fr. OE. hwxr, rel.
to OS. hwar, ΟΝ., Swed. hvar, Dan. hvor, OFris.
hwcr, MDu. waer, Du. waar, OHG. hwar, war,
wd, MHG. wd, G. wo, Goth, har, 'where',
from I.-E. pron. base *qwo-, whence also 01.
kar-ki, 'when', Alb. kur, 'when', Lith. kuf,
'where, whither*, L. cur, 'why'. See who and cp.
words there referred to.
Derivatives: where, pron., n. and conj.

## wherry
wherry, п., a kind of boat. — ME. whery, of
unknown origin.
Derivative: wherry, tr. and intr. v.

## whet
whet, tr. v. — ME. whetten, fr. OE. hwettan, 'to
sharpen', rel. to ON. kvetja, 'to sharpen,
encourage', Swed. vattja, MLG., Du. wetten,
OHG. wezzan, MHG., G. wetzen, 'to sharpen',
Goth, ga-fvatjan, 'to sharpen, incite'. These
verbs derive from the Teut. adj. *A wata-,
appearing in OE. hwaet, 'brave, bold', OS. hwat, 'sharp',
ON. hvatr, 'bold, brisk, vigorous', OHG. was,
'sharp'. Teut. *kwata- corresponds to I.-E.
*qwedo~, fr. base *qwed-, *qwod-, *qwed-, 'sharp',
whence OI. codati, 'incit.es', lit. 'sharpens', and
the second element in L. triquetrus, 'three-
cornered'. See triquetra.
Derivatives: whet, n.

## whether
whether, pron. — ME. whether, fr. OE. kwseder,
hweder, rel. to OS. hweabr, ON. hvarr, Goth.
Ivapar, 'which of the two', OHG. hwedar, 'which
of the two*, MHG., G. weder, 'neither' (conj.),
and cogn. with OI. katarah, Avestic katara-.
Ion. Gk. κότερος, Gk. πότερος, L. uter (prob.
for *qwutro-), 'which of the two, either of two*,
Lith. katrdst 'which of the two ?', OSIav. koteru,
kotoru, 'which'. All these words are formed fr.
I.-E. pron. base *qwo~ (see who) with the com-
par. suff. -ther. Cp. either, neither, neuter.
Derivative: whether, conj.

## whetstone
whetstone, n. — ME. whetston, fr. OE. hwetstan,
compounded of the stem of hwettan, *to whet',
and stdn, 'stone*. See whet and stone.

## whew
whew, n.( a whistling sound. — Of imitative
origin.

## whewellite
whewellite, п., calcium oxalate {mineral.) —
— Named after the English philosopher
William Whewell (1794-1866). For the ending see
subst. suff. -ite.

## whey
whey, n. — ME. whet, fr. OE. hwxg, re], to MDu.
wey, Du. wei, of uncertain origin; not cogn.
with L. caseus, 'cheese', OSIav. kvasu, *lea-
ven'.

## which
which, adj. — ME. whiche, fr. OE. hwilc, 'which',
which is short for hwi-llc, Of what form', and
rel. to OS. hwilik, wilik, ON. hvelikr, Dan. hvil-
ken, Swed. vilken, OFris. hwelik, hwelk, MDu.
wifk, Du. welk, OHG. hwelich, welich, MHG..
welich, G. welch, Goth, hileiks, 'which'. These
words lit. mean Of what form, what like', and
derive fr. Teut. *hwa-, 'what', and *lika, 'body,
form, likeness' (whence also OE. lie, 'body,
form', ge-lic, 'like'). See who and like, adj., and
cp. the second element in such.
Derivative: which, adj.
whidah bird. — Alteration of earlier widow bird
after Whidah (now Ouidak), name of a place in
Dahomey, West Africa; the name widow bird
was regarded erroneously as a popular
corruption of whidah bird.

## whiff
whiff, п., a puff; a slight odor. — Of imitative
origin. Cp. whiffle.
Derivatives: whiff, tr. and intr. v,, whiff-er, п.,
whiff-y, adj.

## whiff
whiff, п., a flat fish. — Of uncertain origin.

## whiffle
whiffle, intr. and tr. v. — Formed fr. whiff, v.
(see whiff, 'a puff'), with freq. suff. -le.
Derivatives: wkiffl-er, п., whijfl-ing, adj.,
whijfl-ing-ly, adv.

## Whig
Whig, п., one of a group of Presbyterians who
marched on Edinburgh in 1648 opposing King
Charles. — Shortened fr. Whiggamore, which
is of uncertain origin.
Derivatives: Whigg-ery, п., Whigg-ish, adj.,
Whigg-ish-ly, adv., Whigg-ish-ness, n.

## while
while, n. — ME. whil, while, fr. OE. hwil, 'space
of time, while', rel. to OS. hwil, OFris. hwile,
OHG. hwila, MHG. wile, G. Weile, Goth.
fveila, 'space of time, while', orig. 'rest', ON.
hvlla, 'bed' (lit. 'resting place'), hvild, 'rest', fr.
I.-E. base *qweye-, *qwi{y)e-, 'to rest, repose, be
comfortable*, whence also Avestic shditisk,
'joy', OPers. shiydtish, 'joy', L. quies, 'rest,
repose, quiet', tranquillus (for *trdns-quilnos),
'quiet, still', Arm. hart-gist, 'rest' (fr. pref. han-
and gi, fr. base *qwi-), OSIav. po-koji, 'rest', po-
citi, 'to rest'. Cp. whilom, whilst, awhile. Cp.
also qniet, п., and words there referred to.
Derivatives: while, conj. and tr. and intr. v.

## whiles
whiles, conj. {archaic), while. — ME. -whiles (in
compounds), fr. OE. hwiles, adv. gen. of hwil.
See prec. word and adv. suff. -s.

## whilom
whilom, adv., formerly {archaic). — ME. hwilum,
whilum, fr. OE. hwilum, *at times', tiat. pi. of
hwil, 'time, while'; rel. to OS. hwflun, OHG.
kwilom, wilon, G. weiland, 'formerly, of old'.
See while.
Derivative: whilom, adj.

## whilst
whilst, conj. — ME. whilest, extension of whiles.
See whiles. For the additional -t cp. amidst,
amongst.

## whim
whim, п., a sudden fancy; caprice. — Prob. of
Scand. origin; cp. ON. kvima, *to let the eyes
wander', Norw. kvima, 'to flutter'. Cp. whimsy,
whimwham. Cp. also wimble.
Derivatives: whim, intr. and tr. v., whimm-y,
adj.

## whimbrel
whimbrel, п., the curlew called Phaeopus phaeo-
pus. — Of imitative origin. Cp. whimper. For
the ending see suff. -rel.

## whimper
whimper, intr. v., to whine. — Of imitative origin.
Cp. G. wimmern, 'to whimper'.
Derivatives: whimper, п., whimper-er, п., whim·
per-ing, adj., whimp-er-ing-ly, adv.

## whimsy
whimsy, whimsey, п., a whim. — Rel. to Norw.
kvimsa, 'to skip', fr. kvima, 'to flutter'. See whim.
Derivatives: whims-ic-al, adj., whims-ic-al-ityt
п., whims-ical-ly, adv., whims-ical-ness, n.

## whimwham
whimwham, п., a whimsical device; a trifle. —
Reduplication of whim.

## whin
whin, gorse. — Of Scand. origin. Cp. Norw.
kvine, kvin, *a kind of grass'.

## whin
whin, п., a basaltic rock. — Of uncertain origin.

whinchat, п., a small bird. — Lit. 'chat of the

whin'. See whin, 'gorse', and chat,

whine, intr. and tr. v. — ME. whinen, fr. OE.

shout, cry\ G. wiehern, 'to neigh'; of imitative *

origin. Cp. whinny. Cp. also whisper, whistie.

## ly
ly, adv.

## whinny
whinny, intr. v., to neigh. — Related to prec.
word.
Derivative: whinny, n.

## whip
whip, tr. and intr. v. — ME. whippen, rel. to Dan.

## vippe
vippe, MLG., MDu., Du. wippen, 'to swing',

OHG. wipf, 'swing, impetus'. See vibrate and cp.

and adj., whipp-ing-ly, adv., whipp-y, adj.,

## whippet
whippet, п., a small swift dog. — Formed fr.

Derivatives: whippet, intr. v., whippet-er, n.

## whip-poor-will
whip-poor-will, п., a nocturnal goatsucker. — Of
imitative origin.

## whipster
whipster, п., an insignificant person. — Formed
fr. whip with suff. -ster.

## whir
whir, intr. v., to move with a buzzing sound; п.,
a buzzing sound. — Related to Dan. hvirre, 'to
whirl', and to E. whirl.

## whirl
whirl, intr. and tr. v. — ME. whirlen, prob. fr.
ON. hvirfla (Swed. hvirfia, Dan. hvirvle), 'to
whirl', rel. to Du. wervelen, G. wirbeln, 'to
whirl'. ON. hvirfia is freq. of the verb hverfa, 'to
turn'. See wharf and cp. warble, whorl.
Derivatives: whirl, n. (q.v.), whirl-ed, adj.,
whirf-er, п., whirl-ing, n. and adj., wkirl-ing-ly,
adv.

## whirl
whirl, n. — ME. whirle, partly fr. ON. hvirfill,
'circle, ring; top, summit*, which is rel. to MLG.,
MDu. wirvel, wervel, 'whirlwind', Du. wervel,
'vertebra;, OHG. wirbil, 'whirlwind', MHG.
wirbel, 'crown of the head, top, summit', G.
Wirbel, 'whirl, whirlpool, whirlwind; tuning
peg; vertebra; crown of th# head', and to ON.
Hverfa, 'to turn round', partly directly from
ME. whirlen, 'to whirl'. See whirl, v.

## whirligig
whirligig, п., a spinning toy. — Compounded of
whirl and gig (in its original sense 'whipping
top').

## whisht
whisht, interj. suggesting silence. — Of imitative
origin. Cp. whist, interj.

## whisk
whisk, n. — ME, wisk, of Scand. origin. Cp. ΟΝ.,
Dan., Norw. visk, 'wisp', which are rel. to
MLG., Mt>u. wisch, Du. wis, OHG.' wise.
MHG. G. wisch, 'wisp, brush', fr. I.-E. base
*weis-, 'to turn, twist', whence also .01. veskah,
'noose', Czech vechet, 'a wisp of straw', Pol.
wiecha, 'panicle', and possibly also L. virga (for
*wiz-gd), 'twig, switch, rod'. The noun whisk
derives partlv fr. whisk, v. Cp. whisker, whisky,
'a vehicle', whisp, whist. Cp. also virgate and
words there referred to.

## whisk
whisk, tr. and intr. v. — Of Scand. origin. Cp.
Dan. viske, Norw., Swed. viska, which are rel.
to OE. wiscian, '.to plait', weoxian, 'to wipe,
keep clean', MDu. wisschen, Du. wissen, OHG.
wisken, MHG., G. wischen, 'to whisk, wipe' and
to whisk, n. (q.v.)

## whisker
whisker, п., usually pi.· — Formed fr. whisk, v.,
with suff. -er.
Derivative: whisker-ed, adj.

## whiskey
whiskey, whisky, п., an alcoholic liquor distilled
from grain. — Fr. Ir. and Gael, uisce, 'water',
shortened fr. uiscebeathadh, 'whisky', lit. 'water
of life'. See usquebaugh, which is a doublet of
whiskey.

## whisky
whisky, п., a light vehicle. — Formed fr. whisk,
п., with suff. -y,

## whisper
whisper, intr. and tr. v. — ME. whisperen, fr. OE.
hwisprian, rel. to MDu. wispelen, wisperen,
OHG. hwispalon, wispalon, MHG., G. wispeln,
G. wispern, ON. hviskra, Dan. hviske, 'to
whisper'; of imitative origin. Cp. whine, whistle.
Derivatives: whisper-er, п., whisper-ing, adj. and
п., whisper-ing-ly, whisper-ous, adj., whisper-
ous-ly, adv.

## whist
whist, interj. suggesting silence. — Of imitative
origin. Cp. whist, hist, hnsh. Cp. also next word
and wistful,

## whist
whist, п., a game of cards. — Earlier whisk; so
called from the whisking up of the cards from
the table. This word was changed into whist
(see prec. word) to enjoin silence upon the
players.
Derivatives: whist, intr. v., to play whist, whist-
er, n.

## whistle
whistle, n. — ME-, fr. OE. hwistle, rel. to hwist-
lian. See whistle, v.

## whistie
whistie, intr. and tr. v. — ME. whistlen, fr. OE.
hwistlian, 'to whistle', of imitative origin. Cp.
ON. hvisla, Dan. hvisle, 'to whisper', and E.
whisper.
Derivatives: whistler, whistling, n. (qq.v.),
whistl-ing, adj., whistl-ing-ly, adv.

## whistler
whistler, n. — ME., fr. OE. hwistlere, fr.
hwistlian. See whistle, v., and agential suff. -er.

## whistling
whistling, n. — ME. whistlinge, fr. OE. hwistlung,
fr. hwistlian, 'to whistle*. See whistie and -ing,
suff. forming verbal nouns.

## whit
whit, п., the smallest particle; a bit. — ME.
wiht, wight, fr. OE. wiht, 'thing, creature*. See
wight.
