Derivatives: wrist, tr. v., wrist-ed, adj., wrist-let,
n.

## writ
writ, n. — ME. writ, fr. OE. writ, lit. 'that which
is written', pp. of writan, 'to engrave, write'.
See next word.

## write
write, tr. and intr. v. — ME. writen, 'to write', fr.
OE. writan, 'to engrave, scratch, draw, write',
rel. to OS. writan, 'to tear, scratch, write',
OFris. writa, 'to write', ON. rita, 'to scratch,
write', Swed. rita, 'to draw', OHG. rijan,
MHG. rfyen, G. reiflen, 'to tear, pull, tug,
sketch, draw, design', OE. writ, ON. rlt,
'writing', OHG. rls, 'stroke, letter", MHG. riz, 'tear',
G. Rifi, 'tear, gap; plan, design', Grund-rifl,
'first sketch, design, plan', Reifi-zevg, 'drawing
instruments', Goth, writs, 'stroke, line, letter',
and possibly cogn. with Gk. ρίνη (for "fpivj)),
'file, rasp'; cp. writ. The orig. meaning of OE.
writan, etc., was 'to cut letters in bark or wood'.
For sense development cp. Heb. kdthdb, 'he
wrote', orig. 'he engraved' (cp. its derivative
krthobheth, 'tattooing', and see kethib), Gk.
γράφειν, 'to scratch, engrave, carve; to write'
(see -graph), and L. scribere, 'to write', fr. I.-E.
base 'sqeribh-, 'to scratch' (see scribe).
Derivatives: writ-able, adj., writer (q.v.),
writing, n.

## writer
writer, n. — ME. writere, fr. OE. writere, fr.
writan. See prec. word and" agent, surf. -er.
Derivative: writer-skip, n.

## writhe
writhe, intr. and tr. v. — ME. writhen, fr. OE.
wridan, 'to turn, twist, writhe', rel. to ON. rida,
Dan. vride, Swed. vrida, OHG. ridan, 'to turn,
twist' (whence F. rider, 'to wrinkle, shrivel'),
reid, 'twisted, wrinkled', OE. wrxstan, 'to twist',
wrsep, 'band, wreath', wrap, 'angry*, ON. reidr,
'angry'. All these words derive fr. I.-E. base
*wrei-, 'to turn, twist'. See wry and cp. wrath,
wreath, wrest, wrestle, wriggle, wrist, wroth.
Derivatives: writhe, п., writh-ed, adj., writh-ed-

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:860 COLUMN:2 -->
ly, adv., writh-ed-ness, п., writh-ing-ly, adv.

## writhen
writhen, adj., intertwined. — ME., fr. OE., fr.
gewritken, pp. of writhan. See prec. word.

## written
written, pp. — ME. writen, fr. OE. gewriten, pp.
of writan. See write.

## wrong
wrong, n. — ME. wrong, wrang, fr. OE. *wrang,
'injustice'. See next word.

## wrong
wrong, adj. — ME. wrang, wrong, fr. OE. 'wrang,
'injustice', fr. ON. rangr (Dan., Swed. vrang),
'crooked, wrong', which stands for *wrangr,
and is rel. to MLG. wrank, MDu. wranc, Du.
wrang, 'sour; bitter', lit. 'that which distorts the
mouth', and to OE. wringan, 'to wring'. See
wrench and cp. wring. For the sense
development of wrong cp. F. tort, 'wrong, injustice', fr.
L. tortus, 'twisted', pp. of torquere, 'to twist'
(see torty
Derivatives: wrong, adv. and tr. v., wrong-ed,
adj., wrong-er, п., wrong-ful, adj., wrong-ful-ly,
adv., wrong-fui-ness, п., wrong-ly, adv.,
wrongous (q.v.)

## wrongous
wrongous, adj., wrong; wrongful. — ME. wrang-
wis, wrongwis, formed fr. wrang, wrong, 'wrong',
on analogy of ME. rihtwis, 'righteous'. See
wrong and cp. rlghtwise.
Derivatives: wrongous-ly, adv., wrongous-ness ,n.

## wrote
wrote, past tense of write. — ME. wroot, fr. OE.
wrdt, past tense of writan. See write.

## wroth
wroth, adj., angry. — ME. wrath, wroth, fr. OE.
wrap, 'angry', rel. to OS., OFris. wreth, ON.
reidr, Dan., Swed. vred, 'angry', Du. wreed,
'rough, harsh, cruel', OHG. ridan, 'to turn,
twist', reid, 'twisted, wrinkled'. See writhe and
cp. wrath.
Derivatives: wroth-ful, adj., wroth-ly, adv.,
wroth-у, adj.

## wrought
wrought, past tense of work {archaic and poetic).
— ME. wrohte, fr. OE. worhte, past tense of
wyrcan, 'to work'. See work, v.

## wrought
wrought, pp. and adj. — ME. wroht, wrouht,
wrought, fr. OE. geworht, pp. of wyrcan, 'to
work'. See work, v.

## wrung
wrung, past tense and pp. of wring. — ME.
wrungen, wrung, fr. OE. gewrungen, pp. of
wringan. See wring.

## wry
wry, intr. and tr. v., to twist. — ME. wrien, 'to

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:860 COLUMN:3 -->
turn, twist', fr. OE. wrigian, 'to strive, go
forward', rel. to OFris. wrigia, 'to bend', MLG.
wrich, 'turned, twisted', and prob. rel. also to
MHG. rigel, 'kerchief wound around the head',
OE. wrigels, 'covering, veil', and cogn. with
Avestic urvisyeiti, 'turns, revolves', Gk. ροικός
(for *wroikos), 'crooked', L. rica, (for *wrelka),
'veil to be thrown over the head', Lith. ralSas,
'paralysed', riSu, rlsti, 'to bind, tie', rykste, 'rod,
wand, stick'. All these words are derivatives
of I.-E. *wreik-, 'write-, 'to turn, twist, bind',
which is an enlargement of base *wrei-, 'to
turn, twist'. See writhe and cp. words there
referred to.
Derivatives; wry, adj., wry-ly, adv., wry-ness, n.

## wudn
wudn, п., ablution before prayer (Islam). — Arab.
wuda', rel. to wadu'a, 'he was beautiful, neat or
clean', wada'a, 'he surpassed (another man) in
cleanness' (with reference to the ablution before
prayer), tawadda'a, 'he performed the ablution',
wadu, 'water serving for ablution'. See Asia.

## wulfenite
wulfenite, п., native lead molybdate (mineral.) —
Named after the Austrian mineralogist Frei-
herr von Franz Xaver von Wulfen (1728-1805).
For the ending see subst. surf. -ite.

## wortzilite
wortzilite, п., a hydrocarbon deposit (mineral.) —
Named after the American mineralogist Dr.
Henry Wurtz (1828-1910). For the ending see
combining form -lite.

## wurtzite
wurtzite, п., zinc sulfide (mineral.) — Named
after the French chemist Charles Adolphe
Wurtz (1817-84). For the ending see subst. surf.
-ite.

## Wyandotte
Wyandotte, п., name of a breed of fowls. — So
.called from the name of an Indian tribe in N.
America>

## wych eim
wych eim, — ME. wyche, fr. OE. wice, *wych elm'.
See witch, 'tree with pliant branches', and eim.
wych hazel. — See prec. word and hazel.

## Wykehnmist
Wykehnmist, п., a member of Winchester
College. — Named after William of Wykeham
(1324-1404), founder of the College. For the
ending see surf. -ist.

## wynd
wynd, п., an alley (Scot.) — A spelling var. of
wind, 'a turning'. See wind, 'to turn'.

## wyvem
wyvem, n. — See wivern.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:861 -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:861 COLUMN:1 -->
Χ, χ, principal unknown quantity (alg.) — Sp. X,
χ, shortened fr. Arab, shay, 'a thing, something',
used also in the sense of'unknown quantity' (in
Medieval Spanish χ was pronounced sh);
introduced by Descartes. Cp. X rays.

## xanth-
xanth-, form of xantho- before a vowel.

## xanthein
xanthein, п., soluble yellow coloring matter in
flowers (chem.) — Formed with suff. -in fr. Gk.
ξανθός, 'yellow'. See xantho-.
xanthelasma п., a synonym of xanthoma (med.)
— Medical L., compounded of xanth- and Gk.
ίλασμο;, 'a metal plate', which derives fr. έλάν,
'to drive, strike'. See elastic and cp. elasmn-. For
the ending see surf. -ma.

## Xanthian
Xanthian, adj., pertaining to Xanthus. — Formed
with suff. -ian fr. Xanthus, name of a city in
Lycia in Asia Minor.

## xanthic
xanthic, adj., yellowish. — Formed with adj.
suff. -ic fr. Gk. ξανθός, 'yellow'. See xantho-.

## xantbin
xantbin, п., insoluble yellow coloring matter in
flowers {chem.) — F., coined by the French
chemist Charles-Frederic Kuhlmann (1803-81)
in 1838 fr. Gk. ξανθός, 'yeilow' (see xantho-),
and suff. -In.

## Xanthippe
Xanthippe, also Xantippe, name of the wife of
Socrates, used figuratively to denote a shrewish,
ill-tempered wife. — Gk. Ξανθίππη, rel. to the
Greek masculine PN. Ξάνθιππος, which is
compounded of ξανθός, 'yellow', and Ιππος,
'horse'. See xantho- and hippo- and cp. the PN.
Philip.

## xanthite
xanthite, п., name of a kind of yellowish rock
(mineral.) — Formed with subst. suff. -Ite fr.
Gk. ξανθός, 'yellow'. See xantho-.

## Xanthium
Xanthium, п., a genus of plants, the cocklebur
(bot.) — ModL., fr. Gk. ξάνθιον, 'a plant used
for dying the hair yellow', fr. ξανθός, 'yellow'.
See xantho- and 1st -ium.

## xantho-
xantho-, before a vowel xanth-, combining form
meaning 'yellow'. — Gk. ξανθό-, ξανθ-, fr.
ξανθός, 'yellow', which is of uncertain origin.
There is little probability in the supposition of
Persson, Fick, Hirt, Boisacq and many other
lexicographers, who connect Gk. ξανθός with
L. cascus, 'hoary, old*, and canus, 'gray'; see
Frisk, GEW., II, p. 333 s.v. ξανθός. Ср. the first
element in Zanthorrhiza.

## Xanthochroi
Xanthochroi, n. pi, the blond races of Europe
(ethnol.) — ModL., prop, 'those who have light
hair and pale complexion', fr. Gk. ξανθός (see
xantho-) and ωχρός, 'pale, pale yellow, yellow'.
See ocher.
Derivatives: xantkochro-ic, adj., xanthochroid
(q.v.), xanthochro-ism, n.

## xanthochroid
xanthochroid, adj., xanthochroic. —
Compounded of prec. word and Gk. -οειδής, 'like', fr.
είδος, 'form, shape'. See -oid.

## xanthoma
xanthoma, п., a skin disease characterized by
yellow nodules (med.) — Medical L., coined by
the English physician Erasmus Wilson (1809-
1884) fr. Gk. ξανθός, 'fair, yellow'. See xantho-
and -oma and cp. xanthelasma.

## xanthomatosis
xanthomatosis, п., widespread xanthoma (med.)
— Medical L., coined by R. S. Rowland fr. prec.
word and suff. -osls.

## xantnomelanous
xantnomelanous, adj., yellow skinned and black
haired (ethnol.) — Formed with suff. -ous fr.
Gk. ξανθός, 'yellow', and μέλας, gen. μέλανος,
'black'. See xantho- and melanism.
xanthophyl], xanthophyl, п., the yellow matter
coloring autumn leaves (biochem.) — F. xantko-
phylle, coined by the Swedish chemist Jons
Jacob Berzelius (1779-1848) in 1838 fr. Gk.
ξανθός, 'yellow', and φύλλον, 'leaf. See
xnntho- and phyllo- and cp. chlorophyll.

## xanthous
xanthous, adj., pertaining to the yellow
Mongolian type. — Gk. ξανθός, 'yellow'; see xantho-.
For E. -ous, as equivalent to Gk. -ος, see -ous.

## xebec
xebec, п., a small three-masted vessel. — From
earlier chebec, fr. F. chebec, fr. It. sciabecco, fr.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:861 COLUMN:2 -->
χ
Arab, shabbik (whence also Sp. xabeque, now
spelled jabeque). E. xebec was influenced in
form by Sp. xabeque.

## xen-
xen-, form of xeno- before a vowel.

## xenelasia
xenelasia, п., prevention of aliens from settling in
Sparta (Greek antiq.) — Gk. ξενηλασίά,
'expulsion of foreigners', fr. ξενηλατεΐν, 'to expel
foreigners', which is compounded of ξένος,
'stranger, foreigner', and ελατός, verbal adj. of
έλαύνειν, 'to drive, drive away'. See xeno-,
elastic and 1st -ia.

## xenia
xenia, п., the direct influence of the pollen of one
species on the seed of another species (bot.) —
ModL., fr. Gk. ξενία, 'hospitality', fr. ξένος.
See xeno-.

## xenial
xenial, adj., relating to hospitality. — Formed
with adj. suff. -al fr. Gk. ξένιος, 'pertaining to
hospitality', fr. ξένος. See xeno-,

## xeno-
xeno-, before a vowel xen-, combinin g form
meaning 'stranger, foreigner; strange, foreign'. —
Gk. ξένο-, ξέν-, fr. ξένος (Ion. ξεϊνος, Dor.
ξένιος), 'stranger; guest', which is of
uncertain origin; it is perh. cogn. with L. hostis,
'stranger; enemy'. See host, 'landlord', and cp.
the second element in Polyxena.

## xenogamy
xenogamy, п., cross-fertilization (bot.) —
Compounded of Gk. ξένος, 'strange, foreign', and
-γαμίά, fr. γάμος, 'marriage'. See xeno- and
-gamy.

## xenogenous
xenogenous, adj., due to external causes. —
Compounded of Gk. ξένος, 'strange, foreign*,
and -γενής, 'born of, produced by'. See xeno-
and -genous.

## xenon
xenon, п., name of an inert gaseous element
(chem.) — ModL-, lit. 'the strange, i.e. rare
(element'), fr. Gk. ξένον, neut. of ξένος, 'stranger'
(see xeno-); coined by the discoverers of this
element, the Scottish chemist Sir William
Ramsay (1852-1916) and the English chemist Morris
WilliamTravers (1872-1961)in 1898. Cp. krypton.

## xenotime
xenotime, п., a mineral consisting essentially of
yttrium phosphate. — F. xenotime, coined by
the French mineralogist and physicist Francois-
Sulpice Beudant (1787-1852), apparently fr. Gk.
ξένος, 'strange', and τιμή, 'honor' (see xeno-
and timocracy). In reality, however, xenotime is
a mis-spelling for cenotime, because Beudant
himself, after giving the name xenotime, says
that it derives fr. Gk. κενός, 'empty, vain' (see
keno-), and τιμή, 'honor', and adds that the
name is intended to recall the fact that the
mineral was erroneously (i.e. 'vainly') supposed by
Berzelius to contain a new metal.

## xer-
xer-, form of xero- before a vowel.

## xeraflm
xeraflm, xerafin, п., a former silver coin of
Portuguese India. — Sp., Port., fr. Arab, sharlfl,
adj., formed fr. sharif, 'shereef, with -f a suff.
meaning 'pertaining to'. See shereef and cp.
words there referred to.

## xeransis
xeransis, п., a drying up (med.) — Medical L., fr.
Gk. ξήρανσις, 'drying up', fr. ξηραίνειν, 'to
dry', fr. ξηρός. See xero-.

## Xeranthemum
Xeranthemum, п., a genus of plants of the thistle
family (bot.) — ModL., compounded of Gk.
ξηρός, 'dry', and £νθος, 'flower'. See xero- and
anther.

## xerasia
xerasia, п., excessive dryness of the hair (med.) —
Medical L., fr. Gk. ξηρασία, 'dryness', from
the stem of ξηραίνειν, 'to dry', fr. ξηρός. See
xero-.

## xero-
xero-, before a vowel xer-, combining form
meaning 'dry'. — Gk. ξηρό-, ξηρ-, fr. ξηρός, 'dry',
which is rel. to ξερόν, 'the dry land', and prob.
cogn. with L. serenus (for *kseres-nos), 'clear,
fair, cloudless, serene'. See serene and cp. elixir.
Cp. also the second element in Phylloxera.

## xeroderma
xeroderma, п., roughening of the skin (med.) —
Medical L., coined by Erasmus Wilson (see
xanthoma) fr. xero- and Gk. δέρμα, 'skin'. See
derma.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:861 COLUMN:3 -->

## xerophilous
xerophilous, adj., drought loving (bot.) —
Compounded of xero- and -philous.

## xerophthalmia
xerophthalmia, п., a form of conjunctivitis (med.)
— Medical L-, lit. 'dryness of the eye', fr. Gk.
ξηρός, 'dry', and οφθαλμός, 'eye'. See xero-
and ophthalmia.

## Xerophylium
Xerophylium, п., a genus of plants, the turkey
beard (bot.) — ModL., compounded of xero-
and Gk. φύλλον, "leaf. See phyllo- and cp.
Phylloxera.

## xerophyte
xerophyte, п., a xerophilous plant (bot.) —
Compounded of Gk. ξηρός, 'dry', and φυτάν,
'plant'. See xero- and -phyte.

## Xerxes
Xerxes, п., king of Persia, who reigned 486-465
B.C.E.; called the Great. — Gk. Ξέρξης, Гг.
OPers. Xshayarshan-. See Ahasuerus.

## xlph-
xlph-, form of xlpho- before a vowel.

## Xiphias
Xiphias, п., a genus of fishes, the swordfish (ich-
thyol.) — L., 'swordfish', fr. Gk. ξιφίδς,
'swordfish', fr. ξίφος, 'sword'. See xlpho- and
cp. Ziphus.

## xlpho-
xlpho-, before a vowel xiph-, combining form
meaning 'sword'. — Gk. ξιφο-, ξιφ-, fr. ξίφος,
'sword', of uncertain origin. It is perh. a loan
word fr. Aram, sayphd (whence also Heb. saylf,
Arab, sayf), fr. Egypt, sefet, 'sword', which is a
derivative of the verb sft, 'to slaughter'. See H.
Lewy, Die semitischen Fremdworter im Grie-
chischen, pp. 176 ff., Muss-Arnolt, On Semitic
Words in Greek and Latin, in the Transactions
and Proceedings of the American Philological
Association, p. 141, Spiegelberg in Zeitschrift
fur vergleichende Sprachforschung, 4], 132,
Schrader, Sprachvergleichung und Urgeschich-
te, 3rd ed., II, pp. 110 ff., Cp. prec. word and
Ziphius.

## xiphoid
xiphoid, adj., sword-shaped. — Gk. ξιφοειδής,
'sword-shaped', fr. ξίφος, 'sword', and -οειδής,
'like', fr. είδος, 'form, shape'. See xlpho- and
-oid.

## Xmas
Xmas, п., Christmas. — Prop. = X, the Greek
letter chi, as the initial letter of Χριστός (see
Christ) and -mas (in Christmas).

## xoanon
xoanon, п., a primitive wooden image (Greek
antiq.) — Gk. ξόανον, 'an image carved of wood',
from the stem of ξεΐν 'to scrape, scratch,
polish', which is rel. to ξοειν, of s.m. See xyster.

## X rays
X rays, n. pi., Roentgen rays. — They were called
by their discoverer Wilhelm Konrad von
Roentgen (1845-1923) (in 1896) X Strahlen (=
X-rays), to suggest that the exact nature of
radiation was unknown. For such use of the
letter χ see X, x.

## xyl-
xyl-, form of xylo- before a vowel.

## xylem
xylem, п., woody tissue in higher plants, the
opposite of phloem (bot.) — G. Xylem, coined by
the botanist Karl Wilhelm von Nageli (1817-91),
fr. Gk. ξύλον, 'wood'. See xylo-.

## xylene
xylene, п., any of three isomeric hydrocarbons
distinguished as ortho-, meta- and para-xylene
(chem.) — Formed with suff. -ene fr. Gk. ξύλον,
'wood'. See xylo-.

## xylo-
xylo-, before a vowel xyl-,combining form
denoting 'wood'. — Gk. ξύλο-, ξολ-, fr. ξύλον,
'wood', which is of uncertain origin. It is perh.
cogn. with Lith. itilas, 'pillar', Goth, sauls,
OHG., MHG. sul, G. Suule, OE. syl, 'pillar'.

## xylobalsamum
xylobalsamum, п., the dried twigs of the balm of
Gilead tree. — L-, 'balsam wood', fr. Gk.
ξυλοβάλσαμον, which is compounded of ξύλον,
'tree', and βάλσαμον, 'the balsam tree, resin of
the balsam tree, balsam'. See xylo- and balsam.

## xylocarp
xylocarp, п., hard woody fruit. — Compounded
of Gk. ξύλον, 'wood', and καρπός, 'fruit'. See
xylo- and carpel.

## xylograph
xylograph, п., wood engraving. — Compounded
of Gk. ξύλον, 'wood', and -γράφος, fr. γράφειν,
'to write'. See xylo- and -graph.
Derivatives: xylograph-er, п., xylograph-ic,
xylograph-ic-al, adjs., xylograph-ic-al-ly, adv..

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:862 -->

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:862 COLUMN:1 -->
xylograph-y, η.

## Xylonite
Xylonite, п., trademark for celluloid. — Formed
with subst. suff. -ite fr. Gk. ξύλον, 'wood'. See
xylo-.

## xylophagous
xylophagous, adj., eating wood (said of insects).
— Compounded of xylo- and -φαγος, 'eating*,
fr. φαγεΐν, 'to eat*. See -phagous.

## xylophone
xylophone, п., a musical instrument consisting of
a graduated series of wooden bars. —
Compounded of xylo- and φωνή, 'voice'. See xylo-
and phone, 'speech sound7.

## Xylotrya
Xylotrya, n. pi., a genus of marine bivalves. —
ModL., compounded of xylo- and the stem of
τρϋειν, 'to wear out', which derives fr. I.-E.
*fr-,zero degreeof base *ter-, 'to rub'. See throw.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:862 COLUMN:2 -->

## Xyridaceae
Xyridaceae, n. pi., the yellow-eyed grass family
(bot.) — ModL., formed fr. Xyris with suff.
-aceae.

## xyridnceous
xyridnceous, adj. — See prec. word and -aceous.

## Xyris
Xyris, п., a genus of plants, the yellow-eyed
grass (bot.) — ModL., fr. Gk. ξυρίς, gen.
ξυρΕδος, 'a kind of iris', which is rel. to ξυρόν,
'razor', fr. ξυει,ν, 'to scrape, scratch, polish" (see
next word); so called in allusion to the 2-edged
leaves.

## xyster
xyster, п., an instrument for scraping bones
(surg.) — Gk. ξυστήρ, 'graving tool', fr. ξΰειν,
'to scrape, scratch, polish', wheiKe also ξυρόν,
'razor', ξυστίς, 'robe with a sweeping train*,

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:862 COLUMN:3 -->
ξυστόν, 'polished shaft of a spear' (short for
δόρυ ξυστόν), 'polished shaft of a spear*, neut.
of ξυστός, 'polished' (see next word), and cogn.
with ksurahy 'razor'; fr. I.-E. base *qseu-, Cp.
Xyris, xoanon. For derivatives of *qsneu-, art
enlargement of base *qseu-, see novaculite.

## xystus
xystus, п., a long and open portico for athletic
exercises (Greek and Roman antiq.) — L.,
fr. Gk. ξυστός, 'a covered portico or gallery
where the athletes exercised in winter', short for
ξυστός δρόμος, 'polished course or race';
ξυστός is verbal adj. of ξυειν, 'to scrape,
scratch, polish' (see prec. word); so called in
allusion to the polished floor of the portico.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:863 -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:863 COLUMN:1 -->
у-, perfective pref., orig. meaning 'together with,
with'. — ME. y-, i-, fr. OE. ge-, rel. to OS. gi-,
ge-, i-, OFris. gi-, ge-, e-, MDu., Du. ge-, OHG.
ga-, gi-, MHG., G. ge-, Goth, ga-, ON. g-, and
corresponding to OI. ja- in ja-bhdra, 'she gave
birth to', and cogn. with the L. pref. com-; see
com-. The same E. pref. appears—in the form
of у—in y-clept—in the form of /—in hand-
i-craft, i-wis, and—in the form of e—in
enough.

## -y
-y, suff. forming abstract nouns and
corresponding to OF. or F. -ie, fr. L. -ia. See ] st -ia and cp.
e.g. victor-y, fr. OF. victor-ie, fr. L. victor-ia.

## -y
-y, suff. forming abstract nouns and representing
L. -ia, fr. Gk. -ία, -εία, -εια. See -ia and cp.
e.g. histor-y, fr. L. histor-ia, fr. Gk. Ιστορ-ία.
Ср. also words ending in -асу, -algy, -ancy,
-andry, -archy- -cracy-, ency, -ergy, -ery, -gamy,
-geny, -graphy, -Ihtry, -logy, -mancy, -metry,
-поту, -pathy, -phily, -ry, -sophy, -tomy, -trophy,
■urgy.

## -y
-y, suff. forming abstract nouns and derived fr. L.
-ium (originally through the medium of OF. and
AF. -ie). See -ium and cp. e.g. perjur-y, fr. AF.
perjur-ie, fr. L. perjur-ium. Cp. also augur-y,
myster-y, subsid-y.

## -y
-y, subst. suff. representing OF. -e, -ее (F. -e, -её),
fr. L. -dtus, -Stum, resp. -ata, pp. suff. of verbs
of the first conjugation. See next suff. and cp.
arm-y, cit-y, count-y.

## -y
-y, adj. suff. representing OF. -e (F. -e), fr. L.
-dtus, pp. suff. of verbs of the first conjugation.
See adj. suff. -ate and cp. prec. suff.

## -y
-y, adj. sun", meaning: 1) full of, characterized by,
as in stony, healthy; 2) made of, as in waxy; 3)
somewhat like, as in wavy. — ME. -/, -y, -ie, fr.
OE. -ig, earlier -eg, -Hg, rel. to OS. -ag, ON.
-igr, -agr, -ogr, Dan., Swed., Du., G. -ig, MDu.
-ick, OHG. -ig, -ag, MHG. -ic, -ec, Goth, -eigs,
-igs, and cogn. with OI. -ika, Gk. -ικός, L. -icus.
Cp. e.g. holy, fr. ME. hali, holi, fr. OE. halig. Cp.
adj. suff. -ic.

## -y
-y, sometimes -ie, suff. forming diminutive nouns
and adjectives, e.g. Dick-y, bab-y, puss-y, dark-
y. For spelling with -ie cp. bird-ie, dear-ie,
laddie- lass-ie.

## yabu
yabu, yaboo, п., a hardy pony from Afghanistan.
— Pers. yabu.

## yacht
yacht, п., a small pleasure ship. — Early ModDu.
jaghte (ModDu. jacht), fr. MLG. jacht, which is
short for jachtschiff, lit. 'hunting vessel', fr.
jacht, 'hunting, chase' (from the stem of jagen,
'to hunt'), and schiff, 'ship'. For the first element
see jaeger, 'sharpshooter', and cp. yager, yaw,
for the second see ship.

## yaffle
yaffle, yaffil, п., the green woodpecker (dial.) —
Of imitative origin.

## yager
yager, п., a jaeger. — Anglicized form of G. Jit·
ger, 'hunter'. See jaeger, 'sharpshooter', and cp.
yacht.

## yah
yah, interj. expressing derision. — Imitative.

## yahoo
yahoo, п., brute in human form. — A word
coined by Jonathan Swift (1667-1745) in Gulliver's
Tra vels.

## yahrzeit
yahrzeit, п., annual observance of the
anniversary of the death of a parent or near relative
(Jewish Religion). — Yiddish yortsayt, fr. MHG.
jdrzit, 'anniversary', lit. 'year's time', fr. jar,
'year', and zit, 'time'. See year and tide, п., and
cp. the first element in Zeitgeist.

## Yahweh
Yahweh, п., a modern attempt to transliterate the
Tetragrammaton, commonly rendered by
Jehovah. — This transliteration is based on the
supposition that the Tetragrammaton is the
imperfect Qal or Hiph'il of the Hebrew verb hdwah,
an earlier form of hayab, 'was', and lit. means
'the one who is, the existing', resp. 'He Who
calls into existence; the Eternal'. In reality,
however, the pronunciation of the Tetragrammaton
is unknown. Cp. Jehovah.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:863 COLUMN:2 -->
Υ
Derivatives: Yahw-ism, п., Yahw-ist, п., Yahw-
ist-ic, adj.

## Yajna
Yajna, п., sacrifice personified in Vedism as the
son of Ruchi and husband of Dakshina. — OI.
yajnah, 'sacrifice, worship', fr. yajati, 'he reveres
(a god) with sacrifices, he worships', which is rel.
to Avestic yazaite, of s.m., yasna-, 'sacrifice,
worship', and prob. cogn. with Gk. άγιος,
'holy', άγνύς, 'holy, chaste'. See hagio- and cp.
Yasna.

## yak
yak, п., wild ox of Tibet and Central Asia. —
Tibetan gyak.

## yaksha
yaksha, п., a class of divine beings, the gods of
wealth (Hindu mythol.) — OI. yaksdfi, rel. to
yaksati, 'he reveres, honors', which is prob. a
-ffl-enlargement of yajati, 'he worships'. See
Yajna.

## yam
yam, п., 1) the edible root of several tropical
climbing plants of the genus Dioscorea; 2) any
of these plants. — Port, inhame, lit. 'edible'
(with reference to the edible root), fr. Senegal
nyami, 'to eat'.

## Yauia
Yauia, п., the first of men that died, the judge of
the dead (Hindu mythol.) — OI. Yamah, of
uncertain origin. It means perh. lit. 'the restrainer',
fr. OI. yamah, 'rein, bridle', and is rel. to
yamati, yacchati, 'holds together, reins in, curbs'
and possibly cogn. with L. red-imio, -ire, 'to
wreathe round', redimiculum, 'band, fillet,
frontlet'. Cp. Yima.

## yamen
yamen, п., in China, official residence. — Chin.,
'office', lit. 'gate with flags', fr. ya, 'flag', and
men, 'gate'; so called from the flags placed
before official buildings. Cp. Tsung-li-yamen.

## yammer
yammer, intr. v., to lament (colloq.) — ME.
yameren, alteration of ME. yomeren, fr. OE.
geomerian, geomrian, 'to mourn, complain',
which is rel. to OE. geomor, OS. jdmar, 'sad,
sorrowful', OHG. jamar, 'sad, sorrowful',
whence the noun jamar, 'sadness, lamentation',
MHG. jdmer, G. Jammer, 'lamentation*, ON.
antra, OHG. amaron, MHG. (j)dmern, G. jam-
mem, 'to lament'; prob. of imitative origin.
Derivatives: yammer, п., yammer-er, n.

## yank
yank, tr. and intr. v., to pull, jerk (slang). — Of
uncertain origin.
Derivative: yank, п., a sudden pull.

## Yank
Yank, n. (slang). — Abbreviation of Yankee.

## Yankee
Yankee, п., a citizen of New England or of the
United States of America. — Perh. fr. Du.
Janke (dimin. of Jan, John), a name applied by
Dutch colonists of New York to the English of
Connecticut. See John.
Derivatives: Yankee-dom, п., Yankee-fied, adj.,
Yankee-ism, п., Yankee-ist, n.

## yap
yap, intr. v., to yelp; п., a yelp. — Of imitative
origin. Cp. yawp, yelp.
Derivatives: yapp-er, п., yapp-ing-ly, adv.,
yapp-y, adj.

## yapon
yapon, yaupon, п., a shrub, Ilex vomitoria. — Of
N. American Indian origin.

## yapp
yapp, п., name of a style of book-binding. — So
called after Yapp, a 19th cent, bookseller in
London.

## yard
yard, п., a unit of length. — ME. yarde, yerde, fr.
OE. gierd, geard, gerd, 'rod, stick, measure,
yard', rel. to OS. gerda, OFris. ierde, Du. gard,
'rod', OHG. garta, gartia, gerta, MHG., G.
gerte, 'switch, twig', ON. gaddr, 'spike, sting,
nail', OHG., MHG. gart, Goth, gazds, 'prickle,
goad', fr. I.-E. base 'ghasto-, 'ghazdho-, .'staff,
pole', whence also L. hasta, 'staff, shaft, spear',
Mir. gas, 'shoot, sprout', gat, 'willow twig'. Cp.
gad, 'goad'. Cp. also hastate.

## yard
yard, п., enclosure.—ME. yard, yerd, yerde, fr.OE.
geard, 'enclosure, piece of land, garden, yard',
rel. to OS. gardo, OFris. garda, Du. gaard(e),
OHG. garto, MHG. garte, G. Garten, 'garden',
OHG. gart, 'circle', ON. gardr, 'enclosure,
court, yard', Dan. guard, Swed. gard, 'yard,

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:863 COLUMN:3 -->
court, house', Goth, gards, 'house, family', and
cogn. with Gk. χόρτος, 'enclosed place, cattle
farm', L. hortus, 'garden', lit. 'an enclosed
place', co-hors, 'yard, enclosure; company;
crowd; cohort', Alb. gar&, gar&i, 'hedge', W.
garth, 'courtyard', Olr. gort, 'field', OSlav.
gradu, *a castle, city', Russ. gorod, 'town, city',
Lith. gafdas, 'fold, peftr-enclosure', OPruss.
surdis, 'hedge, fence', and prob. also with Hitt.
gurtush, 'fortress'. Cp. garden, garth, gird, 'to
encircle', and the second element in orchard. Cp.
also horticulture and words there referred to.
All these words derive fr. I.-E. *ghor-to-, *gkor-
dho-, dental enlargements of I.-E. base *gher-,
'to seize', whence Gk. χειρ, 'hand'. See chi-
ΓΟ-.
Derivatives: yard, tr. v., to enclose in a yard,
yard-age, n.

## yare
yare, adj., 1) ready, prepared; active (archaic or
dial.) — ME. yare, yarwe, fr. OE. geuro, gearu,
'eager, ready, prepared, complete'; rel. to OS.
garo, OHG. guro, garawer, MHG., G. gar, ON.
gdrr, of s.m., Du. gaar, 'done; clever'. See garb,
gear and cp. carouse.

## yarmuike
yarmuike, п., a skullcap worn esp. by observant
Jews. — Ukrainian and Pol. yarmulka, of
uncertain origin. It possibly derives fr. Turk.
yaimurluk, 'raincoat', fr. yaimur, 'rain'.

## yarn
yarn, n. — ME. yarn, yern, fr. OE. gearn; rel. to
ΟΝ., Dan., Swed., MLG., OHG., MHG., G.
garn, MDu. gaern, Du. garen, 'yarn', ON. gdrn,
'gut', and cogn. with OI. hiru, 'vein*, hirab,
'band', Gk. χορδή, 'intestine, string of gut', L.
herniu, 'rupture', hiru, 'empty gut', huru-spex,
'diviner inspecting entrails', Lith. farna, 'gut',
Lett, zafnu, of s.m. AH these words derive fr.
I.-E. base *gher-, 'intestine'. Cp. chord and
words there referred to.
Derivatives: yum, intr. v., yarn-er, n.

## yarrow
yarrow, п., the plant also called milfoil. — ME.
yurowe, yarwe, fr. OE. gearwe, rel. to MDu.
garwe, gerwe, Du. gerwe, OHG. gar(a)wa,
MHG. garwe, G. Garbe, 'yarrow'.

## yashmak
yashmak, п., a veil worn by Mohammedan
women. — Arab, yashmaq, 'veil worn by women'.

## Yasna
Yasna, п., one of the four divisions of the Avesta.
— Avestic yasna-, 'sacrifice, worship', rel. to OI.
yajna}), of s.m. See Yajna.

## yatagan
yatagan, п., a kind of Turkish sword. — Turk.
yatagan.

## yaw
yaw, intr. v., to fall away from the line of her
course (said of a ship). — Perh. ult. fr. ON.
jaga, 'to move to and fro', orig. 'to hunt', a
MLG. loan word. See jaeger, 'sharpshooter',
and cp. yacht, yager-
Derivative: yaw, п., the act of yawing.

## yawl
yawl, п., a small boat. — MLG. jolle or Du. jo!
(whence also Dan., G. jolle, Swed. julle, F. yole.
It. iole,Sp.yola, Russ. jar), 'yawi'; of unknown
origin. Cp. joily boat.
Derivative: yawl-er, n.

## yawl
yawl, intr. v., to howl (now dial.) — A var. of
yowl.

## yawn
yawn, intr. v. — ME. yanen, yanien, alteration of
ME. yenen, yOnen, yeonien (which derive fr. OE.
geonian, ginlan, 'to gape, yawn'), due to the
influence of ME. ganien, fr. OE. gSnian, of s.m.;
re^ to OE. ginan, 'to yawn', OS., ginon, ON.
gina, 'to yawn', ON. gin, 'mouth', MDu. ghenen,
Du. geeuwen, OHG. ginen, geinon, also glin,
MHG. genen, G. gdhnen, 'to yawn', and cogn.
with OSlav. zijajo, zijati, 'to gape', Lith. ϊίό-ju,
lia-ti, Czech ztvati, 'to yawn', Gk. χαίνειν, 'to
yawn, gape', L. hidre, of s.m., OI. vi-hd-, vijihite,
'to gape, be ajar'. All these words derive fr. I.-E.
base *ghe(i)-, *ghi-, 'to gape, yawn'. This base
is rel. to base *gho(u)-, *gheu-, 'to gape'. See
chaos and 1st gnm and cp. hiatus, dehisce. Cp.
also achene, Chama, chasm, Chauna, chela,
'claw', chemosis. Cp. also chori- and words there

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:864 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: 837 | -YL -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:864 COLUMN:1 -->
referred to.
Derivatives: yawn, п., the act of yawning, yawn-
er, п., yawn-ing, adj., yawn-ing-ly, adv.

## yawp
yawp, intr. v., to yelp; п., a yelp. — Of imitative
origin. Cp. ynp, yelp.

## yaws
yaws, h., a skin disease (med.) — A Caribbean
word.

## yclept
yclept, ycleped, adj., called, named {archaic). —
ME. icleped, fr. OE. gecleopod, geclypod, pp. of
(ge)clypian, 'to call'. See y-, 'with', and ciepe.

## ye
ye, pron. of the 2nd person (archaic and poet.) —
ME. ye, fr. OE. ge, 'ye', rel. to OS. gf, ge, ON.
er (prob. influenced in form by ON. ve~r),
Dan., Swed. /, 'ye, you', OFris. gi, MDu. gi,
ge, Du. gij, OHG., MHG. ir [prob. influenced
in form by OHG-, MHG. (= G.) wir, 'we'], G.
ihr, Goth, jus, and cogn. with OPruss. ious,
Lith. jus, Alb. ju, OI. уйуат, Avestic yuz m, Gk.
ύμεΐς, *ye, you'. Cp. you.

## ye
ye, def. art. — Archaic printed form of the
article the (OE. pe), due to a confusion of the
symbol p in OE. pe with the letter y. See the.

## yea
yea, adv., yes. — ME· ye, ya, fr. OE. gea, ge,
'yes', rel. to OS., ΟΝ., OHG., MHGJj, Dan.,
Swed. ja, OFris. je, DuJ, G. ja, Goth, ja, jai,
'yes\ Outside Teutonic cp. Gk. ή 'in truth,
verily', Bret, ye, ya, 'yes** Cp. yes.
Derivative: yea, n.

## yenn
yenn, tr. v., to bring forth; intr. v., to bring forth
(young); said of sheep or goat. — ME. yenen,
fr. OE. *ge-e~anian, fr. pref. ge- (see y-) and
eanian, 'to yean', which is rel. to Du. oonen;
prob. fr. I.-E. *agwh-nos, 'lamb', whence also
Gk. αμνός, 'lamb*, L. agnus, OSlav. (j)agne.,
Olr. йап, W. oen, OCo. oin, Bret, oan, 'lamb*,
Umbr. habina(f), 'ewe lambs' (ace.) Cp. ean.
Derivative: yean-ling, n.

## year
year, n. — ME. yere, fr. OE. gear, rel. to OS.,
OHG., MHG. jar, ON. ar, Dan. aar, Swed. ar,
OFris. gir, Du.jaar, G. Jahr, Goth, jer, 'year',
and cogn. with Avestic ydr , 'year*, Gk. ώρος,
'year*, ώρα, 'any limited time, the time of day,
hour, season spring, year' (whence L. h6ra,
'hour'), OSlav. jaruy 'spring', L. hornus (for *ko-
yor-inos), 'of this year' (from the abl. *ho yoro,
'in this year'). All these words possibly mean lit.
'that which goes or passes', and derive fr. I.-E.
*ye-ro, an enlargement of base *ye-, itself an
enlargement of base *еу-л Чо go', whence Gk.
εϊμι, Ιένκι, L. eo, ire, 'to go'. See itinerate and
cp. yore and the first element in yahrzeit. Cp.
also horary, hour.
Derivatives: year-ling, п., yearly (q.v.)

## yearly
yearly, adj. — ME. yerely, yeerly, fr. OE.
gearlic, formed fr. gear, 'year', with suff. -lie.
See year and adj. suff. -ly.

## yearly
yearly, adv. — ME. yerely, yerly, fr. OE. gearlice,
formed fr. gear, 'year', with suff. -lice. See year
and adv. suff. -ly.

## yearn
yearn, intr. v. — ME. yernen, fr. OE. geornan,
giernan, gernan, fr. georn, 'desirous', which is
rel. to OS., OHG. gem, ON. gjarn, 'desirous',
OS. gernean, girnean, ON. girna} OHG. gerdn,
geren, Goth, gairnjan, 'to desire',' MHG. gern,
be-gern, G. be-gehren, 'to desire', Du. gdarne>
OHG. gerno, MHG. gerne, G. gern, gerne,
'gladly, willingly', OHG. ger, 'desirous' (whence
OHG. girt, MHG. gir, G. Gier), 'greed', Goth.

## falhu-galrns
falhu-galrns, 'greedy', fr. I.-E. base *gher-, 'to
desire', whence also OI. haryati, 'he likes, is
fond of, Toclj. A tsarw-, AB tsarw-, 'to rejoice',
Gk. χαίρειν, 'to rejoice', χάρις, 'grace, charm',
Oscan heriest, 'he will desire', L. horiri, 'to
urge, incite', hortdri, 'to urge, incite, encourage,
exhort*, Olr. gor, 'pious', goire, 'piety'. Cp.
lammergeier. Cp. also Charis, char ism, Charissa,
Aleochara, Eucharist, chervil, hortation, dehort,
exhort.

## yenrnful
yenrnful, adj. — ME. yeornful, fr. OE. geornfull,
'eager, zealous'. See yearn and fall, adj.
Derivatives: yearnful-ly, adv., yearnful-ness, n.

## yeast
yeast, n. — ME. yest, fr. OE. gist, giest, rel. to
ON. jastr, jostr, Swed. jast, Du. gist, 'yeast',
MHG. gestjest, G. Gisckt, 'foam, froth", OHG.

## jesan
jesan, MHG. jesen, jern, gern, 'to ferment', G.

## gdren
gdren, 'to ferment' (tr.), and cogn. with OI.

## ydsyati
ydsyati, 'it boils, seethes', Avestic yaeshyeiti,
'boils, seethes' (intr.), Toch. A. yds-, 'to seethe',

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:864 COLUMN:2 -->
Gk. ζεΐν, 'to boil', ζόη, 'foam', W. ias,
'seething, foaming' (n.) All these words derive fr. I.-E.
base *yes-, 'to boil, seethe'. Cp. eczema. Cp. also
guhr.
Derivatives: yeast-y, adj., yeast-i-ness, n.

## yell
yell, intr. and tr. v. — ME. yellen, fr. OE. giellan,
also gillan, 'to yell, shout', rel. to ON. gjalla,
Swed. gdlla, 'to resound', MDu. ghellen, Du.
gillen, OHG. gellan, MHG., G. gellen, 'to yell*,
OHG., OS., OE. galan, ON. gala, 'to sing', OS.,
OHG. galm, 'outcry', ON. hana-gal, 'cockcrow',
ON. galdr, OE. gealdor, OHG. galtar, 'song",
ON. galend, 'sorcerer', lit. 'singer'. All these
words derive from the I.-E. imitative base
*ghel-, 'to cry out, call, shout, sing'. Cp. yelp.
Cp. also celandine, gale, 'wind', nightingale.
Derivatives: yellt п., yell-er, п., yell-ing, adj.

## yellow
yellow, adj. — ME. yelwe, yelow, fr. OE. geolu,
rel. to OS., OHG. gelo, MDu. ghele, Du. geel,
MHG. gel, G. gelb, ON. gulr, Swed. gul,
'yellow', and cogn. with L. helvus, Gaul.-L. gilvus,
'light bay1, Gk. χλόος, 'greenish-yellow color',
χλόη, 'young green shoot, young verdure',
χλοάζειν, 'to be green', χλωρός, 'greenish
yellow, pale green, green, fresh', χολή, also χόλος,
'bile', χελυς, χελώνη, 'tortoise', lit. 'the
yellow animal', OSlav. ilutu, Russ. zeTtyj, 'yellow',
Lith. zelvas, zalvas, 'greenish', OSlav. zelenu,
Russ. zelenyj, 'green', OSlav. tely, 'tortoise*, lit.
'the yellow animal', OI. hdrih, 'yellowish*,
hlranyam, 'gold', Avestic zari, 'yellow'. AH these
words derive fr. I.-E. *ghel-, *ghel-, *ghle-,
*gklo-, 'to gleam, glimmer; to be green or
yellow', whence also OE. glowan, ON. gloa, 'to
glow'. Cp. arsenic, Caltha, Chelone, Chelonia,
Chiorella, chiorine, Chi oris, choler, gall, 'bile',
glass, glow, gold, gull, 'unfledged bird', Helvella,
helvite, oleraceous, olitory, the first element in
zermahbub and the second element in Archelon.
Derivatives: yellow, n. and tr. and intr. v.,
yellow-ish, adj., yellow-ish-ness, п., yellow-ly,
adv., yellow-ness, n.

## yeliowhammer
yeliowhammer, п., a species of bunting. — Fr.
earlier yelambre, fr. ME. *yelwambre, fr. yelwe,
'yellow', and *ambre, 'yeliowhammer', fr. OE.
amore, of s.m. For the first element see yeilow.
The second element is rel. to OS. amer, OHG.
amero, MHG. amery G. Ammer,
'yeliowhammer', and to OHG. amaro, 'spelt'. Accordingly
OE. amore, etc., prop, denoted a bird that feeds
on spelt. The change of yelambre to yellow-
hammer is due to a folk-etymological association
with hammer. Cp. Emberiza.

## yelp
yelp, intr. v., to cry or bark shrilly. — ME.
yelpen, fr. OE. gielpan, also gilpan, gylpan, 'to
boast, exult', rel. to OE. gielp, 'boasting, pride,
glory', OS. galpon, ON. gjalpa, 'to yelp', ON.
gjalp, 'boasting', OHG. gelph, 'outcry', MHG.
gelfen, 'to boast'; fr. Teut. *gkelp-,
corresponding to I. -E. *gkelb-, an extension of the
imitative base *ghel-, 'to cry out'. See yeli and
cp. gulp.
Derivative: yelp, п., a shrill cry or bark.

## Yemen
Yemen, п., a region forming the southwestern
part of Arabia. — Vulgar pronunciation of
Arab. Yaman, lit. 'the country of the South; the
happy country' (cp. its Latin name Arabia
Felix, 'Happy Arabia*), fr. yaman, 'right hand,
right side; south (i.e. the right side, if one faces
east*), whence ydmana, 'he was happy', lit. 'he
turned or went to the right' (the right side was
regarded as auspicious), yammana, 'he went to
the right; he blessed; he went to Yemen'. See
Benjamin and cp. words there referred to.
Derivatives: Yemen-ic, adj., Yemen-ite, adj. and
n.

## yen
yen, п., the unit of Japan, coinage. — Chin, yuen,
'round; dollar'.

## yen
yen, п., a craving {slang); intr. v., to crave {slang).
— Chin, yen, O]5ium', lit. 'smoke'.

## yeoman
yeoman, n. — ME. yoman, yuman, yeman,
'manservant*, of uncertain origin; perh. contractions
of ME. yongman, resp. yungman, yengman,
'young man'. See young and man.
Derivatives: yeoman-ly, adj. and adv.,
yeomanry, n.

## -yer
-yer, agential suff., now occurringly only in a few
words (as in bowyer, lawyer, sawyer). — A var.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:864 COLUMN:3 -->
of-ier; only used after'a vowel or w. Cp. -eer.

## yerba
yerba, п., the herb mate. — Sp., fr. L. herba,
'grass, herb'. See herb and cp. contrayerva.

## yercum
yercum, п., fiber of the plant mudar. — Tamil
yerkum.

## yes
yes, adv. — ME. yes, yis, fr. OE. gese, gise, prob.
compounded of gea, 'yea*, and si, 3rd person
sing, of the subj. pres. of beon, 'to be', or of gea,
'yea', and swd, 'so'. See yea and is, resp. so.
Derivatives: yes, n. and tr. and intr. v.

## Yeshibah
Yeshibah, Yeshivah, п., a school for Talmudic
studies. — Heb. yeskibhdh, 'a sitting, session,
academy', verbal noun of yashabh, 'he sat down,
was sitting, remained, dwelled', which is rel. to
Aram, у tkebh, *he sat; he dwelled', Akkad.
ashdbu, 'to sit, dwell', Ugar. ySb, of s.m., Arab.
wdthaba, 'he leapt, jumped', in South Arab., 'he
sat, dwelled*, Ethiop. ausaba, 'he married', lit.
'he caused to dwell'. Cp. moshav, moshava. Cp.
also marchpane.

## yester-
yester-, pref. — ME. yestren, fr. OE. geostran-,
also giestran-, gystran, rel. to- MLG. ghisteren,
Du. gister(en), OHG. gestaron, gesteren, MHG.
gester, gestern, G. gestern, 'yesterday', ΟΝ. ΐ
gxr, 'tomorrow, yesterday', Goth, gistradagis,
'tomorrow'. The orig. meaning of these words
was 'the other day* (reckoned from today, either
backward or forward). They are cogn. with OI.
hyah, 'yesterday', Avestic губ, Pers. di,
'yesterday', Toch. fesdr, 'tomorrow', Gk. χθ-ές,
'yesterday', Alb. dje, L. heri, 'yesterday', L. hesternus,
'of yesterday', Olr. indhe, W. doe, OCo. doy,
'yesterday*. Cp. hesternal.

## yesterday
yesterday, adv. and n. — ME. yisterdai, yesterdai,
fr. OE. geostran dxg, also giestran dveg, gystran
dxg, -n. and adv., 'yesterday'. See yester- and
day.
yesternight {archaic), adv., last night; п., the night
last past. — ME. yisternight, yesternight, fr. OE.
gystran niht. See yester- and night.

## yestreen
yestreen, adv. and n. (Scot.) — Contraction of
yester-even. See yester and even, n.

## yet
yet, adv. — ME. yet, yete, yit, fr. OE. giet, gieta,
gyt, 'still, yet', rel. to OFris. ieta, eta, MHG.
ieuzo, ieze, 'yet'.
Derivative: yet, conj.

## yew
yew, п., any tree of the genus Taxus. — ME. eu,
fr. OE. eow, lw, rel. to MLG., MDu. iwe, tewe,
Du. ijf, OHG. iwa, MHG. iwe, G. Eibe, ON. yr,
'yew', and cogn. with Gaul, ivos (whence F. if,
Sp., Port, iva), Olr. eo; W. ywen, Bret, ivin,
'yew*; prob. fr. I.-E. base *oiwd-, * iwa-, *iwd-,
'berry, grape', whence also Gk. οίη; δη, οα,
'service, tree*, L. uva, *grape\ Arm. aigi (for
oiwiyd), 'vine', and possibly also Lith. jievd,
ieva, 'black alder', Lett, ieva, of s.m., OSlav. iva,
'willow'. Cp. Iva, uva.

## Yggdrasill
Yggdrasill, п., the great tree of the universe (Norse
mythol.) — ON. yg(g)drasill, fr. Yggr, name of
Odin, and drasill, 'horse*.

## Yiddish
Yiddish, adj. and n. — G. judisch, 'Jewish', fr.
Jude, 'Jew', fr. OHG. judo, of s.m., fr. L. Ju-
daeus, fr. Gk. 'Ιουδαίος. See Jew and adj. suff.
-ish.
Derivatives: Yiddish-ism, п., Yiddish-ist, n.

## yield
yield, tr. and intr. v. — ME. yelden, yilden, fr.
OE. gieldan, gildan, geldan, 'to pay, give', rel. to
OS. geldan, 'to be worth', ON. gjalda, 'to repay,
return', Dan. gjxlde, 'to be worth, be of some
value, concern*, MDu. ghefden, Du. gelden, 'to
cost, be worth, concern', OHG. geltan, MHG.
gelten, *to pay, restore; to be worth', G. gelten,
'to be worth', Goth, fra-gildan, us-gildan, 'to
repay, requite', and to Du. geld, 'money', OHG.,
MHG. gelt, 'payment, contribution*, G. Geld,
'money'; fr. pre-Teutonic *ghel-to-, Ί pay*. Cp.
OSlav. zledo, ilesti, 'to pay', Lith. geliuoti, 'to be
worth', which are Teut. loan words. Cp. also
geld, 'payment, tax', guild, and the second
element in Danegeld.
Derivatives: yield, n.,yield-ing, adj., yield-ing-ly,
adv.

## Yima
Yima, п., the Avestic equivalent αϊ Υ ama (Persian
mythol.) — Avestic Yima-, rel. to OI. Yamdh.
See Yama.

## -yJ
-yJ, combining form used to form the names of
chemical radicals. — F. -yle, fr. G. -yl, fr. Gk.
υλη, 'wood, forest; material, matter', which is

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:865 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: YLANG-YLANG | 838 -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:865 COLUMN:1 -->
of uncertain origin; cp. hylo-, odyl. The term -yl
was introduced into chemistry by the German
chemists Justus Liebig (1803-73) and Friedrich
WShler (1800-82) in 1832, when they coined the
name benzoyle (q.v.)

## ylang-ylang
ylang-ylang, n. — See ilang-ilang.

## ylem
ylem, п., the hypothetical first substance from
which the chemical elements are supposed to
have been formed; proposed by the physicist
George Gamow, professor of the George
Washington University (born in Odessa, Russia,
in 1904). — ME., fr. MF. Hem, fr. Late L. hy-
lem, ace. of hyle, fr. Gk. υλη, 'material, matter'.
See hyle.

## -ylene
-ylene, combining form 1) denoting an
unsaturated hydrocarbon; 2) used to form names of
bivalent radicals (chem.) — Coined fr. -yl and
-ene.

## -ylidene
-ylidene, combining form used to form names of
bivalent radicals derived by the removal of two
hydrogen atoms from the same carbon atom of
a hydrocarbon (chem.) — Coined through the
insertion of -id- into -ylene.

## yodel
yodel, intr. v., to sing by suddenly changing to
and from falsetto; tr. v., to sing (a tone) by
yodeling. — G. jodeln, formed fr. *yo-, an
imitative base expressing joy. Cp. yowl. Cp. also
jubilate. The word yodel first occurs in Scott
(1830).
Derivatives: yodel, п., yodel-er, n.

## yodh
yodh, yod, п., name of the 10th letter of the
Hebrew alphabet. — Heb. yodh, rel. to yddh,
'hand'; so called in allusion to the ancient
Hebrew form of this letter. Cp. iota, jot.

## yoga
yoga, n. (Hindu philos.) — OI. yoga-, 'a yoking,
union', fr. yunakti, 'harnesses, yokes, joins'. See
yoke and cp. Yuga.

## yogh
yogh, п., name of the Middle English letter j. —
ME. yogh, yoc, 30gh, 30c, 30k, prob. identical
with ME. 30c, 'yoke' (see yoke), and so called
because the word 30c begins with the letter 3.

## yoghurt
yoghurt, yoghourt, yogurt, п., a food madefrom
milk fermented by a bacterium. — Turk.
yogurt.

## yogi
yogi, п., one who practices yoga. — Hind, yogi,
fr. OI. yoga-. See yoga.

## yogism
yogism, п., teachings of the yoga. — A hybrid
coined fr. yogi with -ism, a suff. of Greek origin.

## yogist
yogist, п., an adherent of yogism. — A hybrid
coined fr. yogi with -ist, a suff. of Greek origin.

## yo-heave-ho
yo-heave-ho, interj. (naar.) — Of imitative origin.

## yoho
yoho, interj. (naut.) — Of imitative origin.

## yoicks
yoicks, interj., a huntsman's cry to foxhounds. —
Of imitative origin. Cp. hoicks.

## yoke
yoke, n. — ME. yok, fr. OE. geoc, rel. to OS. juk,
ΟΝ., Swed. ok, Dan. aag, MDu. joe, juc, Du.
juk, OHG. job, MHG., G. joch, Goth, juk,
'yoke', and cogn. with OI. yugam, Hitt. jugan,
Arm. luc, Gk. ζυγόν, L. jugum, OSlav. igo (for
*jugo), Lith. jitngas (in which the η is due to the
influence of the verb jtingiu, Ί yoke, harness',
corresponding to L. jungo, Ί join'), Lett, jugs,
OW. iou, W. /он, OCo. ieu, 'yoke', and with OI.
yunakti, 'harnesses', Gk. ζευγνύνοα, 'to join,
link together, yoke, harness', L. jungere, 'to
join, unite'. See join and cp. words there referred
to. Cp. also syzygy, yoga, Yuga, zeugma, zygo-,
zygoma.
Derivatives: yoke, v. (q.v.), yoke-less, adj.

## yokel
yokel, п., rustic, countryman. — Of uncertain
origin. Perh. fr. dial. E. yokel, 'woodpecker',
which is prob. of imitative origin.

## yolk
yolk, п., the yellow part of the egg. — ME. yelke,
yolke, fr. OE. geoloca, geoleca, geolca, 'yolk', fr.
geolu, 'yellow'. See yellow.
Derivatives: yolk-ed, yolk-y, adjs.

## yom
yom, п., day, a Hebrew word occurring in the
names of feasts. — Heb. yom, 'a day', rel. to
Aram.-Syr. yom, Ugar. ym, Arab, yaum, Akkad.
йти, 'day', Ethiop. yom, 'today', Aram.
уётата, Syr. imama, 'day', in contradistinction
to 'night'.

## Yom Kippur
Yom Kippur, the day of Atonement (Jewish
Religion). — Mishnaic Heb. yom kippur (in Bibl.
Heb. yom kippurtm), 'day of atonement', fr.
yarn, 'day' (see yom), and kippur, 'atonement,
expiation', fr.Bibl. Heb. kipper,'lheymade
atonement, made propitiation, forgave, appeased,

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:865 COLUMN:2 -->
pacified', from whose stem derive kopher,
'ransom ; fine', kapporeth, 'seat of Mercy,
Propitiatory', Mishnaic Heb. kappard , 'atonement,
expiation, forgiveness'. The orig. meaning of
kipper was prob. 'he covered' (cp. kissd al'awSn,
'he covered iniquity', Neh. 3 : 37). It is rel. to
Aram, kapper, 'he wiped out, effaced, forgave,
atoned for', Arab, kdfara, 'he covered, hid'.
Some scholars connect. Heb. kipper with Akkad
kaparu, 'to wipe off', kuppuru, 'to wipe off; to
expiate', Aram. kephar, 'he washed away, wiped
off'. However, as shown by the'Aram, verbs
к phar and kapper, the meanings 'to wash away,
wipe off, cover, expiate', are interrelated, and,
accordingly, all the above words are etymolog-
ically connected. For sense development cp.
Arab, ghafara, 'he covered; he forgave', 'ά/'d, 'he
covered; he wiped out; he forgave'.

## yom tob
yom tob, yom tov, a Jewish holiday or festival. —
Heb. yom tobh, lit. 'a good day', fr. убт, 'day',
and tobh, 'good'. For the first word see prec.
word, for the second see Tobiah.

## yon
yon, adj. — ME. yong, fr. OE. geon, 'yon', rel. to
OFris. jen, ON. enn, OHG. ener, jener, MHG.
ener, jener, MLG. gene, MDu. ghens, G. jener,
Goth. Jains, 'that, yon', ON. enn, inn, 'the', fr.
I.-E. base *eno-, *ono-,-whence also Gk. εκείνος
(Ion. κείνος), 'that one' (which prob. stands
for έ-κέ-ενος or *"έ-κεί-ενος), ένη, 'the day after
tomorrow', ένιοι, 'some', L. enim, 'indeed',
Umbr. enom, 'then', OSlav. onu, 'he*, Lith. anas,
ans, 'that one', Hitt. eni-, anni-, Of s.m., annaz,
'once, in time past'. Cp. yonder, beyond. Cp. also
other.
Derivative: yon, adv.

## yond
yond, adv., yonder. — ME., fr. OE. geond,
'through, throughout (prep.); over, yonder'
(adv.); rel. to MLG. gent,jint, Du. ginds, Goth.
jaind, 'thither', and to OE. geon, 'yon'. See prec.
word.

## yonder
yonder, adv. — ME. yonder, formed fr. yond,
'yonder', with compar. suff. -er. Cp. MLG.
ginder, gender, MDu. gender, gonder, ginder, Du.
ginder, Goth, jaindre, 'over there', and see prec.
word.
Derivative: yonder, adj.

## yore
yore, adv., long ago. — ME. yore, fr. OE. geara,
geara, 'long ago, formerly', lit. 'of years', gen.
pi. of gear, 'year'. See year.
Derivative: yore, n.

## york
york, tr. v., to bowl out (a batsman) with a
yorker. — Back formation from next word.

## yorker
yorker, п., a bowled ball that pitches inside the
crease (cricket). — Prob. connected with the
place name York.

## Yorkist
Yorkist, п., an adherent of the house of York
(English hist.) — Formed from the English
place name York with suff. -ist.

## you
you, pron. — ME. eow, eou, you, yow, fr. OE.
eow, used as dat. and ace. of ge, 'ye'; rel. to ON.
ydr (used as dat. and ace. of er, 'ye'), OS. iu
(used as dat. and ace. of gi, ge, 'ye'), OFris.
iuwe, iwe (used as dat. and ace. of gi, 'ye'), MDu.
и (used as dat. and ace. of gi, ge, 'ye'), Du. и
(used as dat. and ace. of gij, 'ye'), OHG., MHG.
iu (used as dat. of <>, 'ye'), OHG. iuwih, MHG.
iuwich, iuch (used as ace. of ir, *ye'), G. each
(used as dat. and ace. of ihr, 'ye'), Goth, izwis
(used as dat. and ace. of jus, 'ye'). See ye, pron.,
and cp. your.

## young
young, adj. — ME. yung, yong, fr. OE. geong, rel.
to OS., OFris. jung, ON. ungr, Dan., Swed. ung,
MDu. jonc, Du. jong, OHG. jung, MHG. June,
G. jung, Goth, juggs, 'yong', and cogn. with L.
juvencus, 'a young bullock; a young man', ju-
venca, 'a young cow; a young woman', Umbr.
iveka [corresponding to L·. ju(v)e(n)ca], 'heifer',
OI. yuvasah, 'youthful; young man, youth', Olr.
бас, Mir. oc, W. ieuanc, Co. iouenc, tunc, Bret.
yaouank, 'young'; fr. I.-E. *yuwnkos, a
derivative of *yuwn-, which is an enlargement of base
*yeu-, 'young', whence OI. yiiva,yavan-, 'young;
young man, youth', Avestic yvan- (gen. уйп-б),
'young man', L. juvenis, 'young; young man',
Olr. δα, 5am, 'younger, youngest', MW. ieu,
Bret., iaou, 'younger', W. ieuaf, 'youngest',
OSlav. junu, Lith. jaunas, Lett, jauns, 'young'.
Cp. youngster, younker, youth, the first element

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:865 COLUMN:3 -->
in euphroe and the second element in galloglass.
Cp. also juvenile and words there referred
to.
Derivatives: young, п., young-ish, adj.

## youngling
youngling, n. — ME. yongling, fr. OE. geongling,
dimin. of geong, 'young'. Cp. OS. jungling, ON.
ynglingr, OFris. jongeling, Du. jongeling, OHG.
jungaling, MHG. jungeling, G. Jungling and see
young and -ling.

## youngster
youngster, n. — The same as youngling, the suff.
-ster having replaced the older suff. -ling. See
young and -ster and cp. younker.

## younker
younker, n. — Du. jonkheer, jonker, fr. MDu.
jonchere, lit. 'a young lord', fr. MOu.jonc (Du.
jong), 'young', and here (Du. heer), 'lord,
master'. See young and Herr and cp. the second
element in mynheer.

## your
your, pron. — ME., fr. OE. eower, prop. gen. of
ge, 'ye'; rel. to OS. iuwar, OFris. iuwer, ON.
ydvarr, ydarr, Du. uw, OHG. iuwer, MHG.
iuwer, G- euer, Goth, izwar, 'your'. See ye,
pron., and cp. you.
Derivative: your, adj.

## yours
yours, pron. — ME. youres, yours, fr. OE.
eowres, gen. sing. masc. and neut. of eower,
'your'. See prec. word and adv. suff. -s.

## youth
youth, n. — ME. viwethe, youthe, youhthe, fr. OE.
geogop, geogup (in ME. the g between two
vowels was changed into 3, which disappeared),
fr. OE. geong, 'young'; rel. to OS. juguth, OFris.
jogethe, MDu. joghet, joghet, Du. jeugd, OHG.
jugund, MHG. jugent, G. Jtigend, Goth, junda,
'fr. Teut. *jugunpi, corresponding to I.-E.
*yuwn-ti, 'youth', which is an enlargement of
I.-E. *yuwn-, 'young'. See young and subst. suff.
-th.
Derivatives: youth-en, tr. and intr. v., youth-ful,
adj., youth-ful-ly, adv., youth-ful-ness, n.

## yowl
yowl, intr. v., to howl, wail; п., a howl, wail. —
ME. yowlen, youlen, of imitative origin. Cp.
yodel.

## yo-yo
yo-yo, п., a spoollike toy. — Trade name.

## yperite
yperite, п., mustafd gas. — F. yperite, formed fr.
yper- (fr. Ypres, a town in Belgium, where it was
used in World War I) and subst. suff. -ite.

## ytterbia
ytterbia, п., ytterbium oxide (chem.) — ModL.
See next word and 1 st -ia.

## ytterbium
ytterbium, п., a metallic element, belonging to the
rare earth group (chem.) — ModL., coined by
the Swedish chemist Carl Gustaf Mosander
(1797-1858) fr. Ytterby, name of a town in
Sweden, place of its discovery. For the ending
see chem. suff. -ium. Cp. erbium and yttrium.
Derivative: ytterb-ic, adj.

## yttria
yttria, п., yttrium oxide (chem.) — ModL. See
yttrium and 1 st -la.

## yttriferous
yttriferous, adj., containing yttrium (chem.) —
Compounded of yttrium and -ferous.

## yttrium
yttrium, п., a metallic element of the rare earth
group (chem.) — ModL., coined by Mosander
from the abbreviation of Ytterby, name of a
town in Sweden, place of its discovery. See
ytterbium.
Derivatives: yttr-ic, adj., yttri-ous, adj.

## yttro-
yttro-, combining form meaning 'containing
yttrium'. — See prec. word.

## Yucca
Yucca, п., a genus of plants, the bear grass and
the Spanish bayonet (bot.) — ModL., ft. Sp.
yuca, a word of Haitian origin,

## yuga
yuga, п., one of the four ages of the world. — OI.
yugam, 'yoke; age'. See yoke.

## Yugoslav
Yugoslav, Jugoslav, п., inhabitant of Yugoslavia.
— Compounded of Serbo-Croatian jugo-,
'south-', fr. jug, 'south, south wind, noon', and
Slav. Serbo-Croatian jug derives fr. OSlav. jugu
(whence also OCzech, Slovak, etc., juh, Czech.

## jih)
jih), 'south', whence also OSlav. jutro, 'morning';

Derivatives: Yugoslav, Jugoslav, Yugoslav-ic,

## Jugoslav-ic
Jugoslav-ic, adjs.

## Yugoslavia
Yugoslavia, Jugoslavia, п., the country inhabited
by the Serbs, Croats and Slovenes. — See prec.
word.
Derivative: Yugoslav-ian, Jugoslav-ian, adj.

## Ynit
Ynit, п., one of the Asiatic Eskimos. — Native
name lit. meaning 'men'. Cp. Innuit.

## yule
yule, n. — ME. yol, yole, fr. OE. geohhol, gehhol,

geol, rel. to OE. giola, 'the Yule month', ON.

jol, 'Yule, Christmas', ylir, 'the Yule month',

zabeta, zabita, п., regulation (India). — Arab.

## zacaton
zacaton, п., any of various grasses, the broom-
root. — Amer. Sp. zacaton, augment, of zacate,

## Zachariah
Zachariah, Zacharias, Zachary, masc. PN.
(Bible). — Late L. Zacharias, fr. Gk. Ζαχαρίας,
fr. Heb. Zlkharyahu, Zikharyah, lit. 'the Lord
has remembered'. The first element of this
compound name derives fr. Heb. zdkhdr, 'he
remembered', whence also zekher, zikkdron,
'remembrance, memorial', azkard , 'memorial
offering; name'. Cp. Aram.-Syr. dekhar, Arab.
dhdkara, Ethiop. zakhara, 'he remembered',
Akkad. sakdru, zakdru, 'to say, name, swear',
zikru, 'name'. For the second element see Elijah
and cp. words there referred to. Cp. Zecha-
riah.

## Zacchaeus
Zacchaeus, Zaccheus, masc. PN. — Late L. Zac-
chaeus, fr. Gk. Ζακχαΐος, fr. Heb. Zakkdy, lit.
'pure, innocent', fr. zdkha , 'he was clean, was
pure; he was innocent', which is rel. to Arab.
dhdkd, 'he was pure', Aram.-Syr. d*khd, cfkhi,
'he was bright', Aram.-Syr. zekhd, zekhi, 'he was
pure, was innocent' (whence Arab, zakd, 'was
pure in a moral sense'), Akkad. zaku, 'to be
clean, be pure'. Cp. zdkkdkh, 'was clean, was
pure, was bright', a secondary form of zdkha ,
and zkhukhfth, 'glass', which is a derivative of
zdkkdkh.

## zaddik
zaddik, n. — See tzaddik.

## zaffer
zaffer, za№e, п., unrefined cobalt oxide. — F.
zafre, safre, prob. fr. L. sapphirus, 'sapphire'.
See sapphire.

## zain
zain, п., a horse of dark color. — F., fr. Sp. zaino,
'traitor, false; horse of dark color', fr. Arab.
khd'in, 'traitor'.

## Zalophus
Zalophus, п., a genus of eared seals (zooi.) —
ModL., formed fr. ζα-, Aeol. equivalent of Gk.
δια-, 'very' (fr. δια, 'through'), and fr. Gk.
λόφος, 'crest'. See dla- and lopbo-.

## zamarra
zamarra, zamarro, п., shepherd's dress made of
sheepskin. — Sp., fr. Arab, sammur, 'sable,
sable's skin'. Cp. zimarra.

## Zamenis
Zamenis, п., a genus of colubrid snakes (zool.) —
ModL., fr. Gk. ζαμενής, 'very strong, mighty,
raging', formed fr. pref. ζα- (see zalophus) and
μένος, 'might, force', which derives fr. I.-E.
base 'men-, 'to think, remember, have one's
mind aroused', whence also L. mens, 'mind,
understanding'. See mind and cp. mental,
'pertaining to the mind'.
zamindar. n. — See zemindar.

## zanja
zanja, п., ditch, trench, drain. — Sp-, fr. Arab.

## Zannlchellla
Zannlchellla, п., a genus of plants, the horned
pondweed (bot.) — ModL., named after the
Italian botanist Gian Giroiamo Zannichelli
(1662-1729). For the ending see 1st suff. -in.

## Zannichelliaceae
Zannichelliaceae, n. pi., a family of aquatic herbs
(bot.) — ModL., formed fr. prec. word with suff.
-aceae.

## Zanthorrhiza
Zanthorrhiza, п., a genus of plants, the yellow-
root (bot.) — ModL., lit. 'yellow root', fr. Gk.
ξανθός, 'yellow' and ρ4ζα, 'root'. See xantho-
and rhizo-.

## zany
zany, п., a buffoon. — F. zani, borrowed fr.

Zarathustra, п., the founder of the ancient Persian

## zarp
zarp, п., a member of the Boer police. — Formed

Element in the English Vocabulary, p. 614.

## zayin
zayin, п., name of the 7th letter of the Hebrew

zeta.

## Zea
Zea, п., a genus of grasses (йог.) — ModL.,

ydvah, Avestic yava-, 'corn, grain', Lith. javaT
(pi.), of s.m., Ir. eorna, 'barley',

ζήλος (Dor. ζάλος), 'jealousy, fervor, zeal',

## zealot
zealot, n. — Late L. zildtes, fr. Gk. ζηλωτής,

Ism, п., zealot-ist, п., zealot-ry, n.

zealous, adj. — ML. zeldsus, fr. Late L. zelus. See

## zebra
zebra, Q. — Port., fr. Amharic zebrd.

## zebra-
zebra-, combining form denoting stripiness. —

## zebrine
zebrine, adj., pertaining to, or resembling, a

-ine (representing L. -inus).

## zebu
zebu, п., an Asiatic ox, Bos indicus. — F. zebu. In

86), the name is of uncertain origin.

## Zebulun
Zebulun, п., son of Jacob by Leah; a tribe of

## zeccbin
zeccbin, п., sequin. — See 1st seqnin.

## Zechariah
Zechariah, п., in the Bible, 1) the eleventh in the
order of the Twelve Prophets; 2) the Book of

## zed
zed, п., name of the letter z. — F. zide, fr. L. zeta,
fr. Gk. ζήτα, name of the letter ζ. See zeta and
cp. izzard.

fr. VArab. zedwar (in Classical Arabic

## zein
zein, п., a simple protein occurring in maize (bio-

## Zeitgeist
Zeitgeist, п., the spirit of the time. — G., lit. 'time

## zemindar
zemindar, п., landholder. — Pers. zamindar,

## zemstvo
zemstvo, п., provincial council in Russia.—Russ.,

same, semme, of s.m.. and cogn. with L. humus,

there referred to.

## zenann
zenann, п., apartment in which the women are
secluded in India, harem. — Hind, zanana, fr.
Pers. zanana, 'of women', fr. zan, 'woman',
which is rel. to OI. jdnih, 'wife', Avestic jainish,

## Zend
Zend, п., I) the translation and exposition of the
Avesta (cp. next word); 2) the original language

zand, 'commentary'; in the sense of 'the
language of the Zend-Avesta' first used by Anquetil-

## Zend-Avesta
Zend-Avesta, п., the sacred books of the Parsees.
— Pers. Avistak va Zend, lit. 'text and
commentary'. See Zend and Avesta.

## zenith

-mita, 'path, way*. VArab. semt became senit,
zenit, owing to a misreading of the letter m as
hi. Cp. azimuth. L, semila prob. stands for *se-
-mita, fr. se~d-, se, 'aside', and 'mita, fr. medre,
'to go'. See se- and meatus.
Derivative: zenith-al, adj.

zeolit-iz-ation, n.

## Zephaniah
Zephaniah, 1) masc. PN.; 2) in the Bible, the
ninth in the order of the Twelve Prophets
(Bible). — Heb. Tzephanydh, lit. 'the Lord has
hidden'. The first element of this compound

## name derives fr. Heb. tzdphdn
name derives fr. Heb. tzdphdn, 'he has hidden',

## whence also tzdphon
whence also tzdphon, 'north', prop, 'the hidden
region'. For the second element see Elijah and
cp. words there referred to.

## zephyr
zephyr, n. — Earlier Zephyrus, fr. ME. Zephirus,

## fr. L. zephyrus
fr. L. zephyrus, fr. Gk. ζέφυρος, 'west wind',
which prob. stands in gradational relationship
to ζόφος, 'darkness, dark region, west'.
Derivatives: zephyr-ean, zephyr-Ian, zephyr-ous,
adjs.
j\ohyranthes, п., a genus of plants of the amaryl-
iis family (bot.) — MtodL., compounded of Gk.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:868 COLUMN:1 -->
ζέφυρος, 'west wind' and (2ν*ος, 'flower'. See
zephyr and anther.

## zeppelin
zeppelin, п., a large, dirigible airship. — Named
after its inventor. Count Ferdinand von
Zeppelin (1838-1917).

## Zeraim
Zeraim, n. pi., the first of the six orders of the
Mishnah. — Heb. z rtfim, 'seeds', pi. of zera\
from the stem of zara\ 'he sowed', which is rel.
to Ugar. al·', Aram.-Syr. zV, 'he sowed', zera\
'seed', Arab, zara'a, 'he sowed', zar', 'seed',
Ethiop. zara'a, more frequently zara'a, 'he
sowed', Akkad. zeru, 'seed', zaru, 'begetter'. Cp. the
first element in Zerubbabel.

## zermahbub
zermahbub, п., a former Turkish gold coin. —
Turkish, fr. Pers. zer, 'gold' (see arsenic), and
Arab, mahbub, 'beloved', pass. part, of habba,
'he loved', which is rel. to Heb. habhabh, Aram.-
Syr. habbebh, 'he loved'.

## zero
zero, n. — F. zero, fr. It. zero, earlier zefiro, fr.
ML. zephirum, fr. Arab, sifr, 'empty; zero'. See
cipher.

## zeroize
zeroize, tr. v., to put (the dial, etc.) back to zero.
— A hybrid coined from prec. word and -Ize, a
suff. of Greek origin.

## Zerubbabel
Zerubbabel, п., the leader of the Babylonian exiles
back to Jerusalem {Bible). — Heb. Zerubbdbhel.
The name prob. means 'begotten in Babylon',
fr. ζ raat babhel, fr. passive part, of zara\ 'he
sowed', and Babhel, the Hebrew name of
Babylon. See Zeraim and Babel.

## zerumbet
zerumbet, п., a drug. — Sp, or Port., fr. Pers.
zarunbdd, fr. Hind, zarunbad.

## zest
zest, п., 1) something that gives flavor or relish;
2) keen enjoyment. — Early ModF. zest (F.
zeste), Orange or lemon peel', of uncertain
origin.
Derivatives: zest-y, adj., zest-ful, adj.,
zest-fully, adv., zest-ful-ness, n.

## zeta
zeta, п., name of the sixth letter of the Greek
alphabet: — L. zeta, fr. Gk. ζήτα, which prob.
derives fr. Heb. zayith (construct state: zith), or
Aram, zetha, 'olive'. See H. Lewy, Die semiti-
schen Fremdworter im Griechischen, 1895, pp.
169 f. and cp. cedilla. — Many scholars derive
Gk. ζήτα fr. zayin, name of the seventh letter
of the Hebrew alphabet (see zayin), and explain
the form ζήτα as based on the analogy of
ήτα, &ήτα, names of the letters following ζήτα.
See E. Boisacq, DELG., p. 309.

## zetetic
zetetic, adj., proceeding by inquiry. — Gk.
ζητητικός, 'searching, inquiring', fr. ζητητάς,
verbal adj. of ζητέω, Ί seek for, inquire into'.
See zeal and adj. suff. -ic.

## zeugma
zeugma, п., a figure of speech in which a word
(usually a verb or adjective) is used to modify
two words, to only one of which it is logically
applicable (gram, and rhet.) — L., fr. Gk.
ζεϋγμα, 'yoke, bond', from the stem of ζευ-
γνύναι, 'to join, link together, yoke, harness'
(whence also ζεϋγος, 'harness'), which is rel. to
ζυγον, ζυγός, 'yoke'. See yoke and cp. zeuxlte,
zygo-. For the ending see suff. -ma.

## zeunerite
zeunerite, п., a hydrous copper uranium arsenate
(mineral.) — G. Zeunerit, hamed after the
German physicist Gustav Zeuner (182g-I907).
The ending -it goes back to Gk. -ΐτης; see
subst. suff. -ire.

## Zeus
Zeus, п., the supreme god of the ancient Greeks.
— Gk. Ζευς [gen. ·Δι(/")6ς], cogn. with the
first element in L. Diespiter, Jupiter, 'Jupiter'.
See deity and cp. words there referred to. Cp.
also the first element in Diomedes, Dione,
Dioscuri, Diospyros, Zenobin.

## zeuxlte
zeuxlte, п., a kind of brown tourmaline.—
Formed with subst suff. -ite fr. Gk. ζεΰξις, 'a
joining', from the stem of ζευγνύναι, 'to join'. See
zeugma and cp. epizeuxis. The name ζεϋξις
was chosen to render 'Unity' in Huel Unity,
name of a place In Cornwall, where it was
found.

## zho
zho, also dzo, п., hybrid between a yak and a
common cow. — Tibetan wdzo.

## sibeiine
sibeiine, sibelline, adj., referring to sables. —
MF. (= F.) zibeline, fr. It. zibellino, 'pertaining
to sables'. See sable, 'a small animal', and adj.
suff. -ine.

## zibet
zibet, also zlbeth, п., the Asiatic or Indian civet.
— It. zibetto, fr. Gk. ζαπέτιον, fr. Arab, zabad.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:868 COLUMN:2 -->
'foam, froth', which is rel. to zubd, 'cream'. Cp.
civet.

## ziggurat
ziggurat, zikkurat, п., Babylonian temple in the
form of a tower. — Akkad. ziqquratu,
'pinnacle', fr. zaqaru, 'to be high*.

## zigzag
zigzag, п., one of a series of short turns in
alternate directions — F-, fr. G. Zickzack, which is
of doubtful, possibly imitative, origin. The
German word was orig. spelled sicsac; it was
first used during the siege of Landau in 1703 in
the military sense 'approaches' (pi.)
Derivatives: zigzag, adj. and intr. v., zigzagg-ed,
adj., zigzagg-ed-ly, adv., zigzagg-er, п., zigzagg-
y, adj.

## Zilla
Zilla, d., a genus of plants of the family Brassi-
caceae (bot.) — ModL., fr. Arab. si!!ah, 'thorn,
prickle', which is rel. to Arab, sulla', Aram.
stlwa, Heb. sillin, of s.m. See Immanuel L6w,
Aramaische Pflanzennamen, 150.

## zillah
zillah, п., a district in India. — Hind, dila', diV,
(pronounced zila', zil'), fr. Arab, φ!', 'rib, side,
part of land', which is rel. to Heb. tzeia', Akkad.
selu, Aram. 'aid', Ή'ά, Syr. el'd, 'rib'. The orig.
meaning of these words was 'something curved'.
They are rel. to Arab, ddla'a, 'declined
deviated', й*й7Г, curved'.

## zimarra
zimarra, п., soutane worn by priests. — It., dis-
similated fr. Sp. zamarra, fr. Arab, sammur,
'sable'. Cp. chimere, simar, zamarra.

## zimb
zimb, п., a kind of large fiy in Abyssinia. —
Amharic zimb, zemb, 'fly', rel. to Mahri debbet.
Heb. ζ bhubh, Arab, dhubab, Akkad, zumbu;
prob. of imitative origin. Cp. the second
element in Beelzebub.

## Zimbabwe
Zimbabwe, п., capital of a native chief. — A
Bantu word, lit. 'houses of stone'; compounded*
of zimba, 'houses' (pi. of imba, 'house') and
mabgi, 'stones'.

## zinc
zinc, n. — G. Zink, prop, the same as Zinke,
Zinken, 'spike, prong of a fork, jagged
projection, tooth of a comb', so called because of the
shape in which this metal settles in the furnace.
G. Zinken represents an enlargement of the
base seen in OHG. zina (MHG., G. zinne),
'pinnacle', which is rel. to OHG. zint, 'point,
spike', ON. tindr, 'point, top, summit', OE. tind,
'prong, spike', and cogn. with Mir. dind, dinn,
'hill'. Cp. zinke. Cp. also tine.
Derivative: zinc-ic, adj.

## zinciferous
zinciferous, adj., yielding zinc. — A hybrid
coined fr. Gk. Zink and L.ferre, 'to bear, carry*. See
zinc and -ferous.

## zinciflcation
zinciflcation, n. — A hybrid coined fr. G. Zink
(see zinc) and -ficarion, a suff. of Latin origin.

## zincify
zincify, tr. v., to coat with zinc. — A hybrid
coined fr. G. Zink (see zinc) and -fy, a suff. of
Latin origin.

## zinco
zinco, n. — Abbreviation of zincograph.

## zinco-
zinco-, combining form meaning 'zinc'. — Fr.
zinc.

## zincograph
zincograph, n. — A hybrid coined fr. G. Zink and
Gk. -γράφος, fr. γφάφειν, 'to write'. See zinc
and -graph.
Derivatives: zincograph, intr. and tr. v., zinco-
graph-er, п., zincograph-ic, adj., zincograpk-y, n.

## zincoid
zincoid, adj., resembling zinc. — A hybrid coined
fr. G. Zink (see zinc) and Gk. -οειϊής, 'like', fr.
είδος, 'form, shape'. See -oid.

## zincous
zincous, adj. — A hybrid coined fr. G. Zink (see
zinc) and -ous, a suff. of Latin origin.

## zlngaro
zlngaro, п., a gypsy. — It-, prob. an Iranian loan
word meaning 'blacksmith'. Cp. Pahlavi asinkttr,
'blacksmith'.

## zingerone
zingerone, п., a pungent ketone, ΰ,,Η^Ο, (chem.)
— Coined from the contraction of Zingiber and
-one, a suff. denoting a ketone.

## Zingiber
Zingiber, п., a genus of plants (бог.) — L.
zingiber, 'ginger'. See ginger.

## Zingiberaceae
Zingiberaceae, n. pi., a family of plants {hotл —
ModL., formed fr. Zingiber, with suff. -nceae.

## zingiberaceous
zingiberaceous, adj. — See prec. word and -ace-
ous.

## zingiberene
zingiberene, п., a sesquiterpene hydrocarbon,
C^H^ (chem.) — Coined fr. L. zingiber (see
Zingiber) and suff. -ene.

## zinke
zinke, п., a cornet. — G. Zinke, 'spike, tooth (of
a comb); cornet', rel to Zinken, 'prong of a fork,
jagged projection', and to Zink. See zinc.

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:868 COLUMN:3 -->

## Zinnia
Zinnia, п., genus of herbs,of the aster family. —
Named after the German botanist Johann
Gottfried Zinn (1727-59). For the ending see 1st
suff. -ia.

## zirmwnldite
zirmwnldite, п., a variety of mica (mineral.) — G.
Zinnwaldit, named- after Zinnwald in the Erz-
gebirge, Bohemia. The ending -it goes back to
Gk. -ΐτης; see subst. suff. -ite.

## Zion
Zion, п., name of one of the hills of Jerusalem.
Heb. TziyySn; the name is often used to denote
Jerusalem and the Land Israel.

## Zionism
Zionism, п., movement for the colonization of
the Jews in the Land of Israel. — G. Zionismus,
lit. 'movement for Zion', formed fr. Zion (see
Zion) with suff.- -ismus (fr. L. -ismus, see -ism).
The term Zionism appears for the first time in
Matthias Acher's Selbstemancipation ('Self-
emancipation'), published in 1886. — Matthias
Acher is the pseudonym of the writer and
publicist Nathan Birnbaum (1864-1937).

## Zionist
Zionist, п., an adherent of Zionism, — G. See
prec. word and -ist.
Derivatives: Zionist, adj., Zionist-ic, adj.

## Zionward
Zionward, Zionwards, adv., heavenward. — Lit.
'toward Zion'. See Zion and adv. suff. -ward,
resp. -wards.

## zip
zip, п., a sharp hissing sound; intr. v., to move
with a zip; to move with speed or vigor. — Of
imitative origin.
Derivatives: zipp-er, п., zipp-ing, adji, zipp-ing-
ly, adv.

## zip
zip, tr. v., to close or fasten with a zipper. —
Back formation fr. zipper.

## Ziphius
Ziphius, п., a genus of beaked whales (zool.) —
ModL., altered fr. Xiphius, fr. Gk. ξιφιός,
'swordfish', fr. ξίφος, 'sword'. See xipho- and
cp. Xiphias.

## Zipper
Zipper, п., a slide fastener. — Fr. Zipper, a trade
mark, formed from sip, п., with agential suff.
-er. 1

## zircon
zircon, n. — F., a var. of jargon, 'a variety of

Derivatives: zirconate (q.v.), zirconia (q.v.),
zircon-ic, adj., zirconium (q.v.)

## zirconate
zirconate, п., salt of zirconic acid (chem.) —
Formed with chem. suff. -ate fr. zircon (q.v.)

## zirconia
zirconia, п., zirconium dioxide (chem.) — ModL.,
formed fr. zirconium. See next word and 1st -ia.

## zirconium
zirconium, п., name of a metallic chemical
element. — ModL., coined by the German
chemist Martin Heinrich Klaproth (1743-1817) in
1789 (on analogy of many other element names
ending in -ium) fr. zircon (q.v.); so called by
him because it is found in the mineral zircon.

## sithar
sithar, п., a musical instrument with twenty-five
to forty strings, plucked with a plectrum. — G.,
fr. OHG. zitara, fr. L. cithara, fr. Gk. κι*άρα,
fr. Pers. sihtar. See cither(n) and cp. guitar and
glttern.

## zitherist
zitherist, п., a player on the zither. — Formed
from prec. word with suff. -ist.

## Zizania
Zizania, п., a genus of plants, the water or Indian
rice. — ModL., fr. Late L. zizanium, 'darnel,
cockle', fr. Gk. ζιζάνιον, fr. Syr. zlzon, which is
rel. to Heb. zun, pi. zunim, of s.m. Arab, ziw&n
is a Syriac loan word. Cp. Lagarde, Symmicta,
I, 63, Armenische Studien, § 1360, and Immanuel
Low, Aramaische Pflanzennamen, p. 132.

## Zizia
Zizia, п., a genus of plants of the carrot family
(bot.) — ModL., named after the German
botanist Johann Baptist Ziz (1779-1829). For the
ending see 1st suff. -ia.

## zizith
zizith, п., the tassel on the corners of garments
(Jewish religion). — Heb. tzitzith, 'tassel, lock',
rel. to Aram, tzitzitha, Syr. tzutzitha, of s.m.,
prob. also to Arab, nasiyj', 'hair on the
forehead'.

## Zizyphus
Zizyphus, also Ziziphus, п., a genus of plants of
the buckthorn family (bot.) Late L. zizyphus,
'the jujube tree'. See jujube.

## zloty
zloty, п., the monetary unit of Poland. — Pol.
zloty, lit. 'of gold',.fr. zYoro.'gold', rel. to Russ.
zoloto, Czech and Slovak zlato, Lett, ze-lts,
'gold', and cogn. with Go.th. gulp, OE. gold, etc.,
'gold'. See gold.

## zo-
zo-, combining form. — See zoo-.

## -zoa
-zoa, combining form denoting zoological
groups, as in Anthozoa, Bryozoa. — ModL. -zoa,
