<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: ZOANTHUS | 842 -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:869 COLUMN:1 -->
fr. Ok. ζώα, pi. of ζωον, 'animal'. See zoo- and
cp.-zoon.

## Zoanthus
Zoanthus, п., a genus of Anthozoa (zool.) —
ModL., compounded of Gk. ζωον, 'animal',
and ίίν*ος, 'flower'. See zoo- and anther and cp.
Anthozoa.

## Zoar
Zoar, п., name of a town situated on the East
side of the Dead Sea; used as a metonymy for
'place of refuge'. — Heb. Tzo'ar, 'name of a
town where Lot found refuge, lit. 'smallness,
insignificance', rel. to tzd'ir, 'little, young'. See
Gen. 19:20-22. Heb. tza'ir and Tzo'ar derive
from the root tz-'-r, 'to be small'. Cp. Syr.
tze'ar, 'was insignificant', Arab, saghura, 'was
small', Akkad. sefreru, 'to be small'. Cp. also
the parallel base z-'-r appearing in Heb. ζ 'er,
'little'; Aram. ze'ar, 'was or became small',
Arab, zd'ira, 'was scanty'.

## zoarial
zoarial, adj., pertaining to a zoarium. — Formed
fr. ModL. zoarium (see next word) with adj.
suff. -a].

## zoarium
zoarium, п., the aggregate of individuals m a
compound animal (zool.) — ModL., zoarium,
fr. Gk. ζωάριον, dimin. of ζφον, 'animal'. See
zoo- and -nrium.

## zodiac
zodiac, п., an imaginary belt in the heavens,
containing the twelve signs. — ME., fr. MF. (= F.)
zodiaque, fr. OF., fr. L. zddiacus, fr. Gk.
ζωδιακός (scil. κύκλος), 'the Zodiac', lit. '(the circle)
containing animals', fr. ζώδιον, 'small painted
or carved figure; sign of the Zodiac', dimin. of
ζωον, 'animal'. See zoo-.
Derivative: zodiac-al, adj.

## Zoe
Zoe, п., fem. PN. — Gk. Ζωή, lit. 'life' (see
zoo-), prop, loan translation of Heb. Hawwd ,
'Eve'. See Eve.

## zoea
zoea, п., the larva of some crustaceans. — ModL.,
fr. Gk. ζόη, 'life'. See zoo-.

## zoetic
zoetic, adj., pertaining to life (biol.) — Formed
with adj. suff. -ic fr. Gk. ζωή, 'life'. See zoo- and
cp. Zoe.

## zoetrope
zoetrope, п., a toy consisting of a revolving,
cylinder showing figures. — Compounded of Gk
ζωή, 'life', and τρόπος, 'turn'. See zoo- and -trope.
Derivative: zoetrop-ic, adj.

## Zohar
Zohar, п., name of a Jewish mystical commentary
on the Pentateuch written in Aramaic and in
Hebrew, the fundamental work of cabbalah. —
Heb. zohar, 'splendor, brightness', fr. stem z-h-r,
'to shine, give light', whence yazhiru (Dan. 12:3),
'they shall shine'; re], to Aram, ζ har, Arab.
zahara, 'it shone'.

## zoic
zoic, adj., pertaining to animal life. — Gk.
ζωικός, 'proper to animals', fr. ζωον, 'animal'.
See zoo- and adj. suff. -ic.

## -zoic
-zoic, combining form meaning 'living in', as in
hylozoic {biol.) — Formed with adj. suff. -ic fr.
Gk. ζωή, 'life'. See zoo-.

## zoisite
zoisite, п., a mineral allied to epidote. — G.
Zoisit, named after Baron Sigismund Zois von
Edelstein (1747-1819), who first observed this
mineral. The ending -// goes back to Gk. -ϊτης;
see subs't. suff. -ite.

## Zolaesque
Zolaesque, adj., characteristic of the style of Zola.
— Formed with suff. -esque from the name of
Zola. See next word.

## Zolaism
Zolaism, п., style characteristic of Zola. —
Formed with suff. -ism from the name of the
French novelist Emile Zola (1840-1902). For
the ending see suff. -ism.

## Zolaist
Zolaist, n. — See prec. word and -ist.
Derivative: Zolaist-ic, adj.

## zollverein
zollverein, п., a customs union. — G., 'customs
union', compounded of Zoll, 'tax, custom, toll'
and Verein, 'union'. See toll, 'tax', and verein.

## zombi
zombi, п., 1) in West African voodoo cults, the
python deity; 2) any voodo snake deity; 3) the
supernatural power by which, according to
voodoo belief, a dead body may be reanimated.
— Of African origin. Cp. Kongo zumbi, fetish'.
Derivative: zomb-ism, n.

## zonal
zonal, adj., pertaining to a zone. — Late L. zona-
lis, fr. L. zona. See zone and adj. suff. -a].
Derivative: zonal-ly, adv.

## zonar
zonar, п., a girdle. — ModGk. ζωνάρι, 'a girdle',
fr. Gk. ζωνάριον, dimin. of ζώνη. See zone,

## zone
zone, п., 1) a belt; 2) a region, area; 3) any of the
five great divisions of the earth's surface. — F.,

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:869 COLUMN:2 -->
fr. L. zona, fr. Gk. ζώνη, whence ζωννύναι, 'to
gird', ζωστός, 'girt', fr. I.-E. base *yos-, 'to
gird; girdle', whence also Avestic yasta-; 'girt',
Lith. juosiu, juosti, 'to gird', OSlav. po-jasu,
'girdle', Alb. n-geS, Ί gird'. Cp. zonar, Zostera,
azonic.
Derivatives: zone, tr. v., zonal (q.v.), zon-ary,
zon-ate, adjs., zonule (q.v.)

## zonule
zonule, п., small belt. — L. zonula, dimin. of zona,
'belt, girdle'. See prec. word and -ule.
Derivative: zonul-ar, adj.

## Zonuridae
Zonuridae, n. pi., a family of lizards (zool.) —
ModL., formed with suff. -idae fr. Gk. ζώνη,
'zone', and ούρα, 'tail'. See zone and uro-, 'tail'.

## Zoo
Zoo, n. — Abbreviation οι Zoological garden.

## zoo-
zoo-, also zo-, combining form denoting animals
or animal life. — Gk. ζωο-, ζω-, fr. ζωον,
'animal', lit. 'a living being', rel. to ζωή (Dor.
ζωα, also ζόά, Ion. ζόη), 'life', ζωός, 'living',
ζάω, ζην, 'to live', for I.-E. *gwei-, 'to live,
life', whence also Gk. βίος, 'life', Goth. *quius,
'elive', OE. cwicu, 'living'. See quick and cp.
bio- and vita]. Cp. also zoarium, zodiac, zoic,
zoology, zoon, azoic, azote, Cenozoic, entozoa,
enzootic, epizootic, hylozoism, Mesozolc, Me·
tazoa, Neozoic, Paleozoic. For the sense
development of Gk. ζφον, 'animal', lit. 'a living
being', cp. L. animal, 'animal', lit. 'a living
being' (see animal).

## zooblast
zooblast, п., an animal cell. — Compounded of
zoo- and Gk. βλαστός, 'bud, sprout, shoot'.
See -blast.

## zoochemistry
zoochemistry, п., chemistry of the consituents of
the animal body. — Compounded of zoo- and
chemistry.

## zoodynamics
zoodynamics, п., the science that deals with the
vital force of animals. — Compounded of zoo-
and dynamics.

## zoogamy
zoogamy, п., the sexual reproduction of animals.
— Compounded of zoo- and Gk. -γαμία, fr.
γάμος, 'marriage'. See -gamy.

## zoogeny
zoogeny, п., the origin of animals. —
Compounded of zoo- and Gk. -γένεια, fr. -γενής, 'born of,
produced by'. See -geny.

## zoogeography
zoogeography, п., the geographical distribution
of animals. — Compounded of zoo- and
geography.
Derivatives: zoogeograph-ic, zoogeograph-ic-al,
adjs.

## zoography
zoography, п., descriptive zoology. —
Compounded of zoo- and Gk. -γραφιά, fr. γράφειν,
'to write'. See -graphy.
Derivatives: zoograph-ic, zoograpn-ic-al, adjs.,
zoograph-ic-al-ly, adv.

## zooid
zooid, adj., resembling, but not identical with, an
animal. — Gk. ζωοειδής, compounded of ζωον,
'animal', and -οειδής, 'like', fr. είδος, 'form,
shape'. See zoo- and -oid.

## zooid
zooid, п., an organic body capable of
spontaneous movement. — Fr. prec. word.

## zooiatrons
zooiatrons, adj., pertaining to zoolatry. — A
hybrid coined from next word and -ous, a suff.
of French, ult. Latin, origin.

## zoolatry
zoolatry, п., the worship of animals. —
Compounded of zoo- and Gk. -λατρεία, -λατρίά,
fr. λατρεία, 'hired labor, service, worship'. See
-la try.

## zoollte
zoollte, zoolith, п., a fossil
animal.—Compounded of zoo- and -lite, resp. -lith.

## zoology
zoology, n. — ModL. zoologia, fr. Modern Gk.
ζωολογία, which is formed fr. Gk. ζωον (see
zoo-) and -λογία, fr. -λόγος, 'one who speaks
(in a certain manner); one who deals (with a
certain topic)'. See -logy.
Derivatives: zoolog-ic, zoolog-ic-al, adjs., zoolog·
ic-al-ly, adv., zoolog-ist, п., zoolog-ize, intr. and
tr. v.

## zoom
zoom, intr. and tr. v. and n. — Of imitative origin.

## zoomagnerism
zoomagnerism, п., animal magnetism. —
Compounded of zoo- and magnetism.

## zoometry
zoometry, п., measurement of animals. —
Compounded of zoo- and Gk. -μετρία, 'a
measuring of, fr. μέτρον, 'measure'. See -metry.

## zoomorphic
zoomorphic, adj., pertaining to zoomorphism. —
See next word and adj. suff. -ic.

## zoomorphism
zoomorphism, п., the representation of gods in
the form of animals. — Compounded of zoo-
and Gk. μορφή, 'form, shape'. See morpho-

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:869 COLUMN:3 -->
and -ism.

## zoon
zoon, п., any of the individuals of a compound
animal. — ModL., fr. Gk. ζωον, 'animal'. See
zoo-,

## -zoon
-zoon, combining form denoting an animal. —
ModL. -zoon, fr. Gk, ζωον. See prec. word,

## zoopathology
zoopathology, п., the study of the diseases of
animals. — Compounded of zoo- and pathology.
Derivatives: zoopatnolog-ical, adj., zoopatholog-
ist, n.

## zoophysics
zoophysics, п., the study of the physical structure
of animals. — Compounded of zoo- and physics,

## zoophyte
zoophyte, п., an invertebrate animal resembling a
plant. — ModL. zdophyton, lit. 'animal-plant',
fr. Gk. ζωον, 'animal', and φυτόν, 'plant'. See
zoo- and -phyte.
Derivative: zoopkyt-ic, adj.

## zoophytology
zoophytology, п., the study of zoophytes. —
Compounded of prec. word and -logy.
Derivatives: zoophytolog-ical, adj., zoophytolog-
ist, n.

## zooplasty
zooplasty, п., the transplantation of animal tissue
into the human body. — Compounded of zoo-
and -plasty.
Derivative: zooplast-ic, adj.

## zoopsychology
zoopsychology, п., the psychology of animals. —
Compounded of zoo- and psychology,

## zoosperm
zoosperm, п., 1) a spermatozoon; 2) a zoospore.
— Compounded of zoo- and Gk. σπέρμα,
'seed, germ, sperm'. See sperm and cp. sperato-
zoon.

## zoospore
zoospore, п., an asexual spore capable of
independent motion. — Compounded of zoo- and
Gk. σπορά, 'a sowing, seed'. See spore.

## zoosterol
zoosterol, п., a sterol of animal origin (biochem.)
— Formed fr. zoo- and sterol.

## zootaxy
zootaxy, п., the classification of animals. —
Compounded of zoo- and Gk. τάξις,
'arrangement'. See taxis.

## zootheism
zootheism, п., the worship of animals. —
Compounded of zoo- and 1st theism.

## zootomy
zootomy, п., the dissection of animals. —
Compounded of zoo- and Gk. -τομίά, *a cutting
of, fr. τομή, 'a cutting'. See -tomy.

## zorgite
zorgite, п., a lead copper selenide (mineral.) —
G. Zorgit, named after Zorge in Harz
Mountains. The ending goes back to Gk. -ϊτης; see
subst- suff. -ite.

## zoril
zoril, п., a small African carnivorous mammal.
— F. zorille, fr. Sp. zorrilla, dimin. of zorra, fem.
of zorro, 'fox', which is a loan word fr. Basque
azari.

## zorilla
zorilla, п., a zoril. — Sp. zorrilla. See prec. word.

## Zoroaster
Zoroaster, п., the founder of the ancient Persian
religion. — L. Zoroastrls, fr. Gk. Ζωροάστρης,
corrupted fr. Avestic Zara&usntra, lit. 'whose
camels are old', fr. "zarant, 'old', and ushtra,
'camel'. OPers. *zarant is rel. to Ol.jdran, 'old',
and cogn. with Ossetic ziirond, Gk. γέρων, gen.
γέροντος, 'old man'; see geronto- and cp. Zara-
thustra,

## Zoroastrian
Zoroastrian, adj., pertaining to Zoroaster or his
religion. — Formed fr. prec. word with suff.
-ian.

## ZorOastrianism
ZorOastrianism, п., the religion of the ancient
Persians, based on dualism. — Formed from
prec. word with suff. -ism.

## Zostera
Zostera, п., a genus of plants, the grass wrack
and the eel grass {boi.) — ModL., fr. Gk. ζω-
στήρ, 'belt', which is rel. to ζωστός, 'girt', verbal
adj. of ζωννύναι, 'to Igird', ζώνη, 'belt, girdle'.
See zone.

## zouave
zouave, п., a member of a French body of
infantry orig. composed of Algerians. — F., fr. Arab.
Zwawa, name of a tribe of the Kabyles in
Algeria, from which the zouaves were originally
recruited (in 1831).

## zounds
zounds, interj. — Contraction of God's wounds.

## See wound
See wound, n.

## zucchetto
zucchetto, п., small round skull cap worn by
dignitaries of the Roman Catholic Church. — It.,
dimin. of zucca, 'gourd; head', fr. Late L. cu-
cutia, a kind of gourd, which is peril, a blend of
cucurbita, 'gourd', and cutis, 'skin, hide'. See
Walde-Hofmann, LEW., I. 300. For the
etymology of these two words see cucumber and
cutis. Cp. succade.

## znfolo
znfolo, zuffolo, п., a small flageolet. — It. zu/olo,

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:870 -->
<!-- PAGE_MARGIN: 843 | ZYTHUM -->
<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:870 COLUMN:1 -->
fr. zufolare, 'to hiss, whistle', fr. VL. 'subilare,
dissimilated fr. L. sibildre, 'to hiss, whistle'. See
sibilant and cp. siffle.

## zumbooruk
zumbooruk, п., a small gun mounted on a swivel,
usually carried on a camel. — Turk.-Arab. zan-
burak, fr. Pers. zanburah (read zambarah), fr.
zanbur (r. zambur), 'hornet', fr. Arab, zunbur, (r.
zumbur), 'hornet'. For sense development cp.
E. musket, which ult. derives fr. It. moschetio,
'musket', lit. 'a little fly' (see musket).

## zunyite
zunyite, п., a basic orthosilicate of aluminum
(mineral.) — Named after Zuni mine in Anvil
Mountain, San Juan County, Colorado. For
the ending see subst. suff. -Ite.

## zwieback
zwieback, п., a kind of rusk. — G. Zwieback, lit.
'twice baked', fr. zwie- (used in compounds for
zwei), 'two', and the stem of backen, 'to bake'.
The first element is rel. to OE., E., OFris. twi-,
ON. tve-, Ы-. See twi-. For the second element
see bake. G. Zwieback is prop, a loan
translation of It. biscotto or F. biscuit.

## Zwinglian
Zwinglian, I) adj., pertaining to Zwingli or to his
teachings; 2) п., a follower of Zwingli. —
Formed with suff. -an fr. the name of the Swiss
Protestant reformer Ulrich Zwingli (1484-1531).

## zyg-
zyg-, form of zygo- before a vowel.

## Zygadenus
Zygadenus, п., a genus of plants of the family
Melanthaceae (йог.) — ModL., fr. Gk. ζυγά-
δην, 'jointly, in pairs', fr. ζυγόν, 'yoke, pair'.
See zygo-.

## zygal
zygal, adj., H-shaped. — See zygo- and adj. suff.
-a).

## zygapophyis
zygapophyis, п., articular process of a vertebra
(anat.) — ModL., compounded of zyg- and Gk.
άπόφυσις, 'process of a bone'. See apophysis.

## zygo-
zygo-, before a vowel zyg-, combining form
meaning 'yoke; forming pairs'. — Gk. ζυγό-,
ζυγ-, fr. ζυγόν, 'yoke, pair', rel. to ζευγνυναι,
'to join, link together', and cogn. with L.jugum,
'yoke', Goth, juk, OE. geoc, 'yoke'. See yoke

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:870 COLUMN:2 -->
and cp. zeugma, syzygy, azygous, epizeuxis.

## zygodactyl
zygodactyl, adj., having the toes arranged in
pairs, two in front and two behind. — Lit. 'yoke-
toed', compounded of zygo- and Gk. δάκτυλος,
'finger, toe'. See dactyl.
Derivatives: zygodactyl, п., a zygodactyl bird,
zygodactyl-ous, adj.

## zygoma
zygoma, п., 1) zygomatic arch; 2) the cheekbone
(anat.) — Medical L., fr. Gk. ζύγωμα, 'yoke;
zygomatic arch', fr. ζυγοϋν, 'to yoke together',
fr. ζυγόν, 'yoke'; see zygo-. In the sense of
'zygomatic arch' ζύγωμα was introduced into
anatomy by Galen. Cp. zygote.

## zygomatic
zygomatic, adj. — Formed with adj. suff. -ic fr.
Gk ζύγωμα, gen. ζυγώματος. See prec. word.

## Zygophyceae
Zygophyceae, n. pi., a class of algae (bot.) —
ModL-, compounded of zygo- and Gk. φϋκος,
'seaweed, tangle; a red dye'. See fucus.

## Zygophyllaceae
Zygophyllaceae, n. pi., the bean-caper family
(bot.) — ModL., formed fr. Zygophyilum with
suff. -aceae.

## zygophyilaceous
zygophyilaceous, adj. — See prec. word and
-aceous.

## Zygophylium
Zygophylium, п., a genus of plants, the bean
caper (bot.) — ModL., compounded of zygo-
and Gk. φύλλον, 'leaf (see phyilo-); so called in
allusion to the opposite (or alternate) leaflets.

## zygophyte
zygophyte, п., a plant which is reproduced by the
union, of two cells (bot.) — Compounded of
zygo- and Gk. φυτόν, 'plant'. See -pbyte.

## zygosis
zygosis, п., the union of two similar cells (Wo/.)
— ModL., fr. Gk. ζύγωσις, 'a balancing', fr.
ζυγοϋν, 'to yoke together; to balance', fr. ζυγόν,
'yoke; beam of the balance'. See zygo- and -osis.

## zygospore
zygospore, п., a spore formed through the union
of two similar gametes. — Compounded of
zygo- and Gk. σπορά, 'a sowing, seed'. See
spore.

## zygote
zygote, п., a zygospore. — Gk. ζυγωτός, 'yoked',

<!-- SOURCE_PAGE:870 COLUMN:3 -->
verbal adj. of ζυγοϋν, 'to yoke together'. See
zygoma.

## zym-
zym-, form of zymo- before a vowel.

## zymase
zymase, п., an enzyme present in yeast (biockem.)
— Coined by the French physician and chemist
Pierre-Jacques Antoine (1816-1908) in 1875 fr.
Gk. ζύμη (see next word) and suff. -ase.

## zyme
zyme, п., ferment (med.) — Gk. ζύμη, 'leaven,
ferment', (for I.-E. 'yus-ma), rel. to Gk. ζωμός,
'broth' (prob. for I.-E. *yd(u)smos), fr. I.-E.
base *yus-, whence also 01. yus-, 'broth*, L.
jus, 'broth, soup'; see jnice and cp. zymosis,
zymurgy, azyme, enzyme. Gk. ζέείν, 'to boil',
is not rel. to Gk. ζΰμη.

## zymo-
zymo-, before a vowel zym-, combining form
denoting ferment or fermentation. — Gk. ζϋμο-,
ζϋμ-, fr. ζύμη, 'leaven, ferment'. See zyme.

## zymogen
zymogen, zymogen*, п., a substance prodocing
ferment (biol.)— Lit. 'ferment producer', coined
by the German physiologist Rudolf Peter Hein-
rich Heidenhain (1834-97) fr. zymo- and -gen.

## zymosis
zymosis, п., fermentation. — ModL., fr. Gk.
ζΰμωσις, 'fermentation', fr. ζϋμοΰν, 'to
ferment' fr. ζύμη. See zyme and -osis.

## zymosterol
zymosterol, п., a sterol occurring in yeast
(biockem.) — Formed fr. zymo- and sterol.

## zymotic
zymotic, adj., pertaining to, or causing,
fermentation. — Gk. ζϋμωτικός, 'causing to ferment',
fr. ζυμωτός, 'fermented', verbal adj. of ζϋμοΰν.
See prec. word and -otic.

## zymurgy
zymurgy, п., that branch of chemistry which
deals with wine making and brewing. —
Compounded of Gk. ζύμη, 'leaven', and -ουργία,
'a working'. Cp. ζϋμουργός, 'maker of leaven',
and see zymo- and -urgy.

## zythum
zythum, п., beer (Roman antiq.) — L., fr. Gk.
ζϋ&ος, 'beer', esp. 'Egyptian beer, b^er of the
northern nations', which is prob. of Egyptian
origin. See Frisk. GEW., I, p. 616 s.v. ζΰ*ος.
